Laws on Persons and Society · 22:16–17

If a man seduces a young woman who isn’t pledged to be married and sleeps with her, he must pay the bride-price and make her his wife. If her father absolutely refuses to give her to him, he must still pay silver equal to the bride-price for a young woman.
Capital Offenses · 22:18–20
You must not let a sorceress live.
Whoever has sex with an animal must be put to death.
Whoever sacrifices to any god other than YHWH alone must be devoted to destruction.
Protection of the Vulnerable · 22:21–27
You must not mistreat a foreigner or oppress him, for you were foreigners in the land of Egypt.

You must not take advantage of any widow or orphan. If you do take advantage of them, and they cry out to me, I will surely hear their cry. My anger will blaze, and I will kill you with the sword. Then your own wives will be widows, and your children orphans.

If you lend money to one of my people among you who is poor, don’t act like a moneylender toward him. Don’t charge him interest. If you take your neighbor’s cloak as a pledge, give it back to him before the sun goes down, because it is the only covering he has, the cloak for his body. What else will he sleep in? When he cries out to me, I will hear, because I am gracious.
Duties to God · 22:28–31
You must not curse God, or curse a leader of your people.

You must not hold back the best of your harvest or the juice of your presses. You must give me the firstborn of your sons. Do the same with your cattle and your sheep. Let the firstborn stay with its mother seven days, and on the eighth day give it to me.
You are to be holy people to me. So don’t eat the meat of an animal torn apart by wild beasts in the field. Throw it to the dogs.”
Laws on Justice and Truth · 23:1–9
“You must not spread a false rumor. Don’t join hands with the wicked by being a lying witness.
You must not follow the crowd in doing wrong. When you testify in a lawsuit, don’t side with the many to twist justice. And don’t show favor to a poor man in his lawsuit either.

If you come across your enemy’s ox or donkey wandering off, you must bring it back to him. If you see the donkey of someone who hates you lying under its load, don’t walk away from him. You must help him with it.
You must not twist justice against the poor among you in their lawsuits.
Stay far away from a false charge, and don’t put the innocent and the righteous to death, for I will not acquit the wicked.
You must not take a bribe, because a bribe blinds those who see clearly and twists the words of the righteous.
You must not oppress a foreigner. You know how a foreigner feels, because you were foreigners in the land of Egypt.
The Sabbath Year and the Sabbath Day · 23:10–13

For six years you are to sow your land and gather in its harvest, but in the seventh year let it go and leave it alone, so the poor among your people can eat from it, and the wild animals can eat what they leave. Do the same with your vineyard and your olive grove.
Six days you are to do your work, but on the seventh day you are to rest, so that your ox and your donkey can rest, and the son of your servant woman and the foreigner can catch their breath.
Pay attention to everything I have told you. Don’t call on the names of other gods. Don’t even let them be heard on your lips.
The Three Pilgrimage Feasts · 23:14–19

Three times a year you are to hold a festival for me. Keep the Festival of Unleavened Bread. For seven days eat bread made without yeast, as I commanded you, at the appointed time in the month of Abib, because in that month you came out of Egypt. No one is to appear before me empty-handed. Keep the Festival of Harvest, with the first fruits of the crops you sow in the field, and the Festival of Ingathering at the end of the year, when you gather in your crops from the field. Three times a year all your men are to appear before the Lord YHWH.

Don’t offer the blood of my sacrifice along with anything containing yeast. And don’t let the fat of my festival offering be left until morning. Bring the best of the first fruits of your ground to the house of YHWH your God. Don’t cook a young goat in its mother’s milk.
The Angel of the Way · 23:20–33

Look, I am sending a messenger ahead of you to guard you along the way and to bring you to the place I have prepared. Pay attention to him and listen to his voice. Don’t defy him, because he will not forgive your rebellion, for my name is in him. But if you truly listen to his voice and do everything I say, I will be an enemy to your enemies and a foe to your foes. My messenger will go ahead of you and bring you into the land of the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hivites, and Jebusites, and I will wipe them out. Don’t bow down to their gods or serve them or follow their ways. Tear them down and smash their sacred pillars to pieces. Serve YHWH your God, and he will bless your bread and your water. I will take sickness away from among you. No woman in your land will miscarry or be barren. I will give you a full span of days. I will send my terror ahead of you and throw into confusion every people you come against. I will make all your enemies turn their backs and run. I will send the hornet ahead of you to drive the Hivites, Canaanites, and Hittites out of your way. I won’t drive them out in a single year, or the land would become a wasteland and the wild animals would multiply against you. Little by little I will drive them out ahead of you, until you have grown numerous enough to take possession of the land. I will set your borders from the Red Sea to the Sea of the Philistines, and from the wilderness to the Euphrates River. I will hand the people living in the land over to you, and you will drive them out ahead of you. Don’t make any covenant with them or with their gods. They must not live in your land, or they will make you sin against me. If you serve their gods, it will surely be a trap for you.”
The Covenant Ratified · 24:1–8

Then YHWH says to Moses, “Come up to YHWH, you and Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel, and bow down in worship at a distance. Moses alone is to come near YHWH. The others must not come near, and the people must not come up with him.”
So Moses comes and tells the people all YHWH’s words and all the rulings. And all the people answer with one voice, “Everything YHWH has said, we will do!”

Then Moses writes down all YHWH’s words. He gets up early in the morning and builds an altar at the foot of the mountain, with twelve standing stones for the twelve tribes of Israel. He sends young men of Israel, and they offer burnt offerings and sacrifice young bulls as peace offerings to YHWH. Moses takes half the blood and puts it in bowls, and the other half he splashes against the altar. Then he takes the Book of the Covenant and reads it aloud to the people. And they say, “Everything YHWH has said, we will do, and we will listen!”
Then Moses takes the blood and sprinkles it on the people and says, “Look, this is the blood of the covenant YHWH has cut with you, on the terms of all these words.”
The Elders Behold God · 24:9–11

Then Moses and Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel go up, and they see the God of Israel. Under his feet is something like a pavement of sapphire stone, clear as the sky itself. But God does not lay a hand on these leaders of Israel. They see God, and they eat and drink.
Moses Ascends into the Cloud · 24:12–18
YHWH says to Moses, “Come up to me on the mountain and stay there, and I will give you the tablets of stone, with the teaching and the commands I have written for their instruction.”

So Moses sets out with his assistant Joshua, and Moses goes up the mountain of God. He tells the elders, “Wait here for us until we come back to you. Look, Aaron and Hur are with you. Anyone with a dispute can go to them.”

Then Moses goes up the mountain, and the cloud covers the mountain. The glory of YHWH settles on Mount Sinai, and the cloud covers it for six days. On the seventh day he calls to Moses from the middle of the cloud. In the eyes of the people of Israel, the glory of YHWH is like a fire blazing and devouring on the mountaintop. And Moses goes into the middle of the cloud and climbs the mountain. And Moses stays on the mountain forty days and forty nights.
The Contribution · 25:1–9

YHWH says to Moses, “Tell the people of Israel to bring me a gift. Take my gift from everyone whose heart moves them to give. These are the gifts you are to receive from them: gold, silver, and bronze; blue, purple, and scarlet yarn; fine linen; goats’ hair; rams’ skins dyed red; fine leather; acacia wood; oil for the light; spices for the anointing oil and for the fragrant incense; onyx stones, and other stones for setting in the ephod and the breastpiece. And let them make me a sanctuary, so that I may pitch my tent and live among them. Make it exactly like the pattern I show you, the pattern of the tabernacle and of all its furnishings.
The Ark · 25:10–22

Have them make an ark of acacia wood, two and a half cubits long, a cubit and a half wide, and a cubit and a half high, about forty-five inches by twenty-seven by twenty-seven. Cover it with pure gold, inside and out, and put a gold molding around it. Cast four gold rings for it and fasten them to its four feet, two rings on one side and two rings on the other. Make poles of acacia wood and cover them with gold. Slide the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark, to carry the ark with them. The poles are to stay in the rings of the ark. They are not to be taken out. And put inside the ark the Testimony I will give you. Make a mercy seat of pure gold, two and a half cubits long and a cubit and a half wide. Make two cherubim of hammered gold at the two ends of the mercy seat, one cherub at one end and one cherub at the other. Make the cherubim of one piece with the mercy seat, at its two ends. The cherubim are to spread their wings upward, sheltering the mercy seat with their wings. They are to face each other, looking down toward the mercy seat. Set the mercy seat on top of the ark, and put inside the ark the Testimony I will give you. There I will meet with you. From above the mercy seat, from between the two cherubim on the ark of the Testimony, I will speak with you about everything I command you for the people of Israel.
The Table · 25:23–30

Make a table of acacia wood, two cubits long, a cubit wide, and a cubit and a half high. Cover it with pure gold and put a gold molding around it. Make a rim around it a handbreadth wide, and put a gold molding around the rim. Make four gold rings for it and fasten the rings to the four corners at its four legs. The rings are to be close to the rim, to hold the poles for carrying the table. Make the poles of acacia wood and cover them with gold, and carry the table with them. Make its plates and dishes, its pitchers and bowls for pouring out offerings. Make them of pure gold. And set the bread of the Presence on the table before me always.
The Lampstand · 25:31–40

Make a lampstand of pure gold. The lampstand is to be hammered out, its base and its shaft. Its cups, its buds, and its blossoms are to be of one piece with it. Six branches are to come out from its sides, three branches on one side and three on the other. On one branch there are to be three cups shaped like almond blossoms, each with a bud and a blossom, and three cups shaped like almond blossoms on the next branch, each with a bud and a blossom. So for all six branches coming out of the lampstand. And on the lampstand itself there are to be four cups shaped like almond blossoms, with their buds and blossoms. There is to be a bud under the first pair of branches, a bud under the second pair, and a bud under the third pair, all of one piece with it, for the six branches coming out of the lampstand. The buds and branches are to be of one piece with it, the whole of it hammered out of a single piece of pure gold. Make its seven lamps, and set them up so they light the space in front of it. Its wick trimmers and trays are to be of pure gold. Make it and all these utensils from a talent of pure gold, about seventy-five pounds. And see that you make them by the pattern you were shown on the mountain.”
The Linen Curtains · 26:1–6

“Make the tabernacle with ten curtains of fine twisted linen and blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, with cherubim worked into them by a skilled weaver. Each curtain is to be twenty-eight cubits long and four cubits wide. All the curtains are to be the same size. Join five of the curtains to one another, and join the other five to one another. Make loops of blue yarn along the edge of the end curtain in the first set, and do the same on the edge of the end curtain in the second set. Make fifty loops on the one curtain and fifty loops on the edge of the curtain in the second set, with the loops facing each other. Make fifty gold clasps and join the curtains to each other with the clasps, so that the tabernacle is one whole.
The Goat-hair Tent · 26:7–14

Make curtains of goats’ hair for a tent over the tabernacle. Make eleven curtains. Each curtain is to be thirty cubits long and four cubits wide. All eleven curtains are to be the same size. Join five of the curtains into one set and six into another. Fold the sixth curtain double at the front of the tent. Make fifty loops along the edge of the end curtain in the first set, and fifty loops along the edge of the end curtain in the second set. Make fifty bronze clasps and put the clasps into the loops to join the tent together, so that it is one whole. The extra length of the tent curtains, the half curtain left over, is to hang down over the back of the tabernacle. The extra cubit on each side, left over from the length of the tent curtains, is to hang over the sides of the tabernacle to cover it. Make a covering for the tent of rams’ skins dyed red, and over that a covering of fine leather.
The Frames · 26:15–30

Make upright frames of acacia wood for the tabernacle. Each frame is to be ten cubits long and a cubit and a half wide, with two pegs joined to each other. Make all the frames of the tabernacle this way. Make twenty frames for the south side of the tabernacle. Make forty silver bases to go under the twenty frames, two bases under each frame for its two pegs. For the second side of the tabernacle, the north side, make twenty frames, with their forty silver bases, two bases under each frame. For the far end of the tabernacle, toward the west, make six frames. And make two frames for the corners of the tabernacle at the far end. At these two corners the frames are to be double from bottom to top, fitted into a single ring. Make both corners this way. So there will be eight frames with their silver bases, sixteen bases, two under each frame.

Make crossbars of acacia wood: five for the frames on one side of the tabernacle, five for the frames on the other side, and five for the frames on the far end, toward the west. The middle crossbar, halfway up the frames, is to run from one end to the other. Cover the frames with gold and make gold rings to hold the crossbars. Cover the crossbars with gold too. Set up the tabernacle according to the plan you were shown on the mountain.
The Inner Veil · 26:31–35

Make a veil of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and fine twisted linen, with cherubim worked into it by a skilled weaver. Hang it on four posts of acacia wood covered with gold, with gold hooks, set on four silver bases. Hang the veil from the clasps, and bring the ark of the Testimony in behind the veil. The veil will separate the holy place from the most holy place for you. Put the mercy seat on the ark of the Testimony in the most holy place. Set the table outside the veil on the north side of the tabernacle, and put the lampstand across from the table on the south side.
The Entrance Screen · 26:36–37

For the entrance of the tent make a screen of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and fine twisted linen, the work of an embroiderer. For the screen make five posts of acacia wood covered with gold, with gold hooks, and cast five bronze bases for them.”
The Altar of Burnt Offering · 27:1–8

“Make the altar of acacia wood, five cubits long and five cubits wide. The altar is to be square, and three cubits high. Make horns on its four corners, of one piece with it, and cover it with bronze. Make its pots for removing the ashes, its shovels, its basins, its meat forks, and its firepans. Make all its utensils of bronze. Make a grate for it of bronze mesh, and put four bronze rings on the four corners of the mesh. Set it under the ledge of the altar, so that the mesh reaches halfway up the altar. Make poles for the altar, poles of acacia wood, and cover them with bronze. The poles are to be put through the rings, so they are on the two sides of the altar when it is carried. Make it hollow, out of boards. Make it just as you were shown on the mountain.
The Court · 27:9–19

Make the courtyard of the tabernacle. On the south side the courtyard is to have hangings of fine twisted linen a hundred cubits long, about a hundred and fifty feet, with twenty posts and twenty bronze bases, and with silver hooks and bands on the posts. The north side is to be the same: hangings a hundred cubits long, with twenty posts and twenty bronze bases, and with silver hooks and bands on the posts. Across the west end of the courtyard there are to be hangings fifty cubits long, with ten posts and ten bases. The east end of the courtyard, toward the sunrise, is to be fifty cubits wide. On one side of the entrance there are to be hangings fifteen cubits long, with three posts and three bases, and on the other side hangings fifteen cubits long, with three posts and three bases. For the gate of the courtyard there is to be a screen twenty cubits long, of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and fine twisted linen, the work of an embroiderer, with four posts and four bases. All the posts around the courtyard are to have silver bands and silver hooks, with bronze bases. The courtyard is to be a hundred cubits long and fifty cubits wide, with hangings of fine twisted linen five cubits high, and with bronze bases. All the tools of the tabernacle for every use, all its tent pegs, and all the tent pegs of the courtyard are to be bronze.
The Perpetual Lamp · 27:20–21

Command the people of Israel to bring you pure oil of pressed olives for the light, so that a lamp can be kept burning always. In the Tent of Meeting, outside the veil that is in front of the Testimony, Aaron and his sons are to tend it from evening until morning before YHWH. This is a rule for all time, generation after generation, for the people of Israel.”
The Priestly Garments Commanded · 28:1–5

“Then bring near to you your brother Aaron and his sons with him, from among the people of Israel, to serve me as priests: Aaron and his sons Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar. Make holy garments for your brother Aaron, for glory and for beauty. Speak to all the skilled workers, whom I have filled with a spirit of wisdom, and have them make Aaron’s garments to set him apart to serve me as priest. These are the garments they are to make: a breastpiece, an ephod, a robe, a woven tunic, a turban, and a sash. They are to make these holy garments for your brother Aaron and his sons, so they can serve me as priests. They are to use gold, and blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and fine linen.
The Ephod · 28:6–14

They are to make the ephod of gold, and blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and fine twisted linen, the work of a skilled weaver. It is to have two shoulder pieces attached at its two corners, so it can be fastened together. The woven waistband on it is to be of the same workmanship and of one piece with it, of gold, and blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and fine twisted linen. Take two onyx stones and engrave on them the names of the sons of Israel, six of their names on one stone and the remaining six on the other, in the order of their birth. Engrave the names of the sons of Israel on the two stones the way a gem cutter engraves a seal. Then mount them in gold settings. Fasten the two stones on the shoulder pieces of the ephod as stones of remembrance for the people of Israel. Aaron is to carry their names before YHWH on his two shoulders, as a reminder. Make gold settings, and two chains of pure gold, braided like cords, and fasten the braided chains to the settings.
The Breastpiece · 28:15–30

Make a breastpiece for making decisions, the work of a skilled weaver. Make it like the ephod, of gold, and blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and fine twisted linen. It is to be square and folded double, a span long and a span wide, about nine inches each way. Mount four rows of precious stones on it. The first row is to be a ruby, a topaz, and a beryl; the second row a turquoise, a sapphire, and an emerald; the third row a jacinth, an agate, and an amethyst; and the fourth row a chrysolite, an onyx, and a jasper. Mount them in gold settings. There are to be twelve stones, one for each of the names of the sons of Israel, each engraved like a seal with the name of one of the twelve tribes. For the breastpiece make braided chains of pure gold, like cords. Make two gold rings for the breastpiece and fasten them to its two upper corners. Fasten the two gold chains to the two rings at the corners of the breastpiece, and fasten the other two ends of the chains to the two settings, attaching them to the shoulder pieces of the ephod at the front. Make two more gold rings and fasten them to the other two corners of the breastpiece, on the inside edge next to the ephod. Make two more gold rings and fasten them to the bottom of the shoulder pieces on the front of the ephod, near the seam just above the woven waistband of the ephod. They are to tie the rings of the breastpiece to the rings of the ephod with a blue cord, so that it sits above the waistband of the ephod and the breastpiece won’t swing loose from the ephod. So whenever Aaron goes into the holy place, he will carry the names of the sons of Israel over his heart on the breastpiece for making decisions, as a constant reminder before YHWH. And put the Urim and the Thummim in the breastpiece for making decisions, so that they are over Aaron’s heart whenever he goes in before YHWH. So Aaron will always carry the means of making decisions for the people of Israel over his heart before YHWH.
The Robe · 28:31–35

Make the robe of the ephod all of blue. It is to have an opening for the head in the middle, with a woven band around the opening, like the collar of a coat of armor, so that it won’t tear. Around its hem make pomegranates of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, with gold bells between them all around, a gold bell and a pomegranate, a gold bell and a pomegranate, all around the hem of the robe. Aaron is to wear it when he serves, and the sound of the bells will be heard when he goes into the holy place before YHWH and when he comes out, so that he won’t die.
The Golden Plate · 28:36–38

Make a plate of pure gold and engrave on it, the way a seal is engraved, HOLY TO YHWH. Fasten it with a blue cord to the turban. It is to be on the front of the turban. It will be on Aaron’s forehead, and Aaron will carry the guilt of any fault in the holy gifts the people of Israel set apart. It is to be on his forehead always, so that they will be accepted before YHWH.
The Tunic, Turban, and Sash · 28:39–43
Weave the tunic of fine linen, make the turban of fine linen, and make the sash, the work of an embroiderer.

For Aaron’s sons make tunics, sashes, and headbands, for glory and for beauty. Dress your brother Aaron and his sons in them. Anoint them, ordain them, and set them apart as holy, so they can serve me as priests. Make linen undergarments for them to cover their bare flesh, reaching from the waist to the thighs. Aaron and his sons are to wear them whenever they go into the Tent of Meeting, or come near the altar to serve in the holy place, so that they don’t incur guilt and die. This is a rule for all time, for him and his descendants after him.”
The Offerings for Consecration · 29:1–3

“This is what you are to do to set them apart as holy, to serve me as priests. Take a young bull and two rams without defect, and bread made without yeast, cakes without yeast mixed with oil, and wafers without yeast spread with oil. Make them of fine wheat flour. Put them in one basket and bring them in the basket, along with the bull and the two rams.
The Washing and the Robing · 29:4–9

Bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting and wash them with water. Take the garments and dress Aaron in the tunic, the robe of the ephod, the ephod, and the breastpiece, and tie the woven waistband of the ephod around him. Set the turban on his head and fasten the holy crown to the turban. Then take the anointing oil and pour it on his head to anoint him. Bring his sons and dress them in tunics. Tie sashes on them, Aaron and his sons, and put headbands on them. The priesthood is theirs by a rule for all time. In this way you are to ordain Aaron and his sons.
The Bull of Purification · 29:10–14

Bring the bull to the front of the Tent of Meeting, and Aaron and his sons are to lay their hands on its head. Slaughter the bull before YHWH at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting. Take some of the bull’s blood and put it on the horns of the altar with your finger, and pour out all the rest of the blood at the base of the altar. Take all the fat that covers the insides, the lobe of the liver, and the two kidneys with the fat on them, and burn them on the altar. But burn the bull’s meat, its hide, and its dung outside the camp. It is a sin offering.
The First Ram: Burnt Offering · 29:15–18

Then take one of the rams, and Aaron and his sons are to lay their hands on its head. Slaughter the ram, take its blood, and splash it against all sides of the altar. Cut the ram into pieces, wash its insides and legs, and put them with the pieces and the head. Then burn the whole ram on the altar. It is a burnt offering to YHWH, a soothing aroma, an offering made by fire to YHWH.
The Second Ram: Ordination · 29:19–28

Take the other ram, and Aaron and his sons are to lay their hands on its head. Slaughter the ram and take some of its blood. Put it on the lobe of Aaron’s right ear and on the lobes of his sons’ right ears, on the thumbs of their right hands, and on the big toes of their right feet. Then splash the rest of the blood against all sides of the altar. Take some of the blood on the altar and some of the anointing oil, and sprinkle it on Aaron and his garments, and on his sons and their garments. Then he and his garments, and his sons and their garments, will be holy. Take from the ram the fat, the fat tail, the fat covering the insides, the lobe of the liver, the two kidneys with the fat on them, and the right thigh, for it is the ram of ordination. And take one round loaf of bread, one cake made with oil, and one wafer from the basket of unleavened bread that is before YHWH. Put all of these in the hands of Aaron and his sons, and have them wave them before YHWH as a wave offering. Then take them from their hands and burn them on the altar on top of the burnt offering, as a soothing aroma before YHWH. It is an offering made by fire to YHWH.

Take the breast of the ram for Aaron’s ordination and wave it before YHWH as a wave offering. It will be your share. Set apart as holy the breast that is waved and the thigh that is lifted up from the ram of ordination, the portions belonging to Aaron and his sons. They will belong to Aaron and his sons as their share for all time from the people of Israel. It is a contribution, a contribution from the people of Israel out of their peace offerings, their gift to YHWH.
The Seven Days of Ordination · 29:29–37

Aaron’s holy garments will belong to his sons after him, so they can be anointed and ordained in them. The son who succeeds him as priest and comes into the Tent of Meeting to serve in the holy place is to wear them for seven days.

Take the ram of ordination and boil its meat in a holy place. Aaron and his sons are to eat the meat of the ram and the bread in the basket at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting. They are to eat the things by which atonement was made for them at their ordination and consecration. But no outsider may eat them, because they are holy. If any of the meat of the ordination or any of the bread is left over until morning, burn what is left. It must not be eaten, because it is holy.

Do all this for Aaron and his sons, just as I have commanded you. Take seven days to ordain them. Every day offer a bull as a sin offering to make atonement. Purify the altar by making atonement for it, and anoint it to make it holy. For seven days make atonement for the altar and make it holy. Then the altar will be most holy, and whatever touches the altar will become holy.
The Daily Burnt Offering · 29:38–46

This is what you are to offer on the altar regularly, every day: two lambs a year old. Offer one lamb in the morning and the other lamb at twilight. With the first lamb offer a tenth of an ephah of fine flour, about two quarts, mixed with a quarter of a hin of oil from pressed olives, about a quart, and a quarter of a hin of wine as a drink offering. Offer the other lamb at twilight, with the same grain offering and drink offering as in the morning, as a soothing aroma, an offering made by fire to YHWH. This is to be the regular burnt offering, generation after generation, at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting before YHWH. There I will meet with you and speak with you. There I will meet with the people of Israel, and the place will be made holy by my glory. I will make the Tent of Meeting and the altar holy, and I will make Aaron and his sons holy, to serve me as priests. I will live among the people of Israel, and I will be their God. And they will know that I am YHWH their God, who brought them out of the land of Egypt so that I could live among them. I am YHWH their God.”
The Altar of Incense · 30:1–10

“The Levites will lay their hands on the heads of the bulls, and you must offer the one for a sin offering, and the other for a burnt offering to YHWH, to make atonement for the Levites. You must set the Levites before Aaron, and before his sons, and offer them as a wave offering to YHWH. Thus you must separate the Levites from among the children of Israel, and the Levites will be mine.

“After that, the Levites will go in to do the service of the Tent of Meeting: and you must cleanse them, and offer them as a wave offering. For they are wholly given to me from among the children of Israel; instead of all who open the womb, even the firstborn of all the children of Israel, I have taken them to me. For all the firstborn among the children of Israel are mine, both man and animal. On the day that I struck all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, I sanctified them for myself. I have taken the Levites instead of all the firstborn among the children of Israel. I have given the Levites as a gift to Aaron and to his sons from among the children of Israel, to do the service of the children of Israel in the Tent of Meeting, and to make atonement for the children of Israel; that there be no plague among the children of Israel, when the children of Israel come near to the sanctuary.”

Moses, and Aaron, and all the congregation of the children of Israel do so to the Levites. According to all that YHWH command Moses concerning the Levites, so the children of Israel do to them. The Levites purify themselves from sin, and they wash their clothes; and Aaron offers them for a wave offering before YHWH; and Aaron makes atonement for them to cleanse them. After that, the Levites go in to do their service in the Tent of Meeting before Aaron, and before his sons: as YHWH has commanded Moses concerning the Levites, so they do to them.
The Age of Service · 8:23–26

YHWH speaks to Moses, saying, “This is that which belongs to the Levites: from twenty-five years old and upward they must go in to wait on the service in the work of the Tent of Meeting; and from the age of fifty years they must cease waiting on the work, and will serve no more, but will minister with their brothers in the Tent of Meeting, to perform the duty, and will perform no service. You must do thus to the Levites concerning their duties.”
The Second Passover · 9:1–14

YHWH speaks to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, in the first month of the second year after they have come out of the land of Egypt, saying, “Moreover let the children of Israel keep the Passover in its appointed season. On the fourteenth day of this month, at evening, you must keep it in its appointed season—according to all its statutes, and according to all its ordinances, you must keep it.”

Moses speaks to the children of Israel, that they should keep the Passover. They keep the Passover in the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, at evening, in the wilderness of Sinai. According to all that YHWH command Moses, so the children of Israel do. There are certain men, who are unclean because of the dead body of a man, so that they can not keep the Passover on that day, and they come before Moses and before Aaron on that day. Those men say to him, “We are unclean because of the dead body of a man. Why are we kept back, that we may not offer the offering of YHWH in its appointed season among the children of Israel?”
Moses answers them, “Wait, that I may hear what YHWH will command concerning you.”

YHWH speaks to Moses, saying, “Say to the children of Israel, ‘If any man of you or of your generations is unclean by reason of a dead body, or is on a journey far away, he must still keep the Passover to YHWH. In the second month, on the fourteenth day at evening they must keep it; they must eat it with unleavened bread and bitter herbs. They must leave none of it until the morning, nor break a bone of it. According to all the statute of the Passover they must keep it. But the man who is clean, and is not on a journey, and fails to keep the Passover, that soul will be cut off from his people. Because he didn’t offer the offering of YHWH in its appointed season, that man will bear his sin.

“‘If a foreigner lives among you, and desires to keep the Passover to YHWH; according to the statute of the Passover, and according to its ordinance, so will he do. You must have one statute, both for the foreigner, and for him who is born in the land.’”
The Cloud and the Fire · 9:15–23

On the day that the tabernacle is raised up, the cloud covers the tabernacle, even the Tent of the Testimony: and at evening it is over the tabernacle, as it were the appearance of fire, until morning. So it is continually. The cloud covers it, and the appearance of fire by night. Whenever the cloud is taken up from over the Tent, then after that the children of Israel travel; and in the place where the cloud remains, there the children of Israel encamp. At the commandment of YHWH, the children of Israel travel, and at the commandment of YHWH they encamp. As long as the cloud remains on the tabernacle they remain encamped. When the cloud stays on the tabernacle many days, then the children of Israel keep YHWH’s command, and don’t travel. Sometimes the cloud is a few days on the tabernacle; then according to the commandment of YHWH they remain encamped, and according to the commandment of YHWH they travel. Sometimes the cloud is from evening until morning; and when the cloud is taken up in the morning, they travel: or by day and by night, when the cloud is taken up, they travel. Whether it is two days, or a month, or a year that the cloud stays on the tabernacle, remaining on it, the children of Israel remain encamped, and don’t travel; but when it is taken up, they travel. At the commandment of YHWH they encamp, and at the commandment of YHWH they travel. They keep YHWH’s command, at the commandment of YHWH by Moses.
The Silver Trumpets · 10:1–10

YHWH speaks to Moses, saying, “Make two trumpets of silver. You must make them of beaten work. You must use them for the calling of the congregation, and for the journeying of the camps. When they blow them, all the congregation will gather themselves to you at the door of the Tent of Meeting. If they blow just one, then the princes, the heads of the thousands of Israel, will gather themselves to you. When you blow an alarm, the camps that lie on the east side will go forward. When you blow an alarm the second time, the camps that lie on the south side will go forward. They must blow an alarm for their journeys. But when the assembly is to be gathered together, you must blow, but you must not sound an alarm.

“The sons of Aaron, the priests, will blow the trumpets. This will be to you for a statute forever throughout your generations. When you go to war in your land against the adversary who oppresses you, then you must sound an alarm with the trumpets. Then you will be remembered before YHWH your God, and you will be saved from your enemies.

“Also in the day of your gladness, and in your set feasts, and in the beginnings of your months, you must blow the trumpets over your burnt offerings, and over the sacrifices of your peace offerings; and they will be to you for a memorial before your God. I am YHWH your God.”
The Departure from Sinai · 10:11–28

In the second year, in the second month, on the twentieth day of the month, the cloud is taken up from over the tabernacle of the testimony. The children of Israel go forward according to their journeys out of the wilderness of Sinai; and the cloud stays in the wilderness of Paran. They first go forward according to the commandment of YHWH by Moses.

First, the standard of the camp of the children of Judah goes forward according to their armies. Nahshon the son of Amminadab is over his army. Nethanel the son of Zuar is over the army of the tribe of the children of Issachar. Eliab the son of Helon is over the army of the tribe of the children of Zebulun. The tabernacle is taken down; and the sons of Gershon and the sons of Merari, who bears the tabernacle, go forward. The standard of the camp of Reuben goes forward according to their armies. Elizur the son of Shedeur is over his army. Shelumiel the son of Zurishaddai is over the army of the tribe of the children of Simeon. Eliasaph the son of Deuel is over the army of the tribe of the children of Gad.
The Kohathites set forward, bearing the sanctuary. The others set up the tabernacle before they arrive.

The standard of the camp of the children of Ephraim sets forward according to their armies. Elishama the son of Ammihud is over his army. Gamaliel the son of Pedahzur is over the army of the tribe of the children of Manasseh. Abidan the son of Gideoni is over the army of the tribe of the children of Benjamin.

The standard of the camp of the children of Dan, which is the rear guard of all the camps, set forward according to their armies. Ahiezer the son of Ammishaddai is over his army. Pagiel the son of Ochran is over the army of the tribe of the children of Asher. Ahira the son of Enan is over the army of the tribe of the children of Naphtali. Thus are the travels of the children of Israel according to their armies; and they go forward.
Moses and Hobab · 10:29–32

Moses says to Hobab, the son of Reuel the Midianite, Moses’ father-in-law, “We are journeying to the place of which YHWH said, ‘I will give it to you.’ Come with us, and we will treat you well; for YHWH has spoken good concerning Israel.”
He says to him, “I will not go; but I will depart to my own land, and to my relatives.”

He says, “Don’t leave us, please; because you know how we are to encamp in the wilderness, and you can be our eyes. It will be, if you go with us, yes, it will be, that whatever good YHWH does to us, we will do the same to you.”
The Ark Goes Before Them · 10:33–36

They set forward from the Mount of YHWH three days’ journey. The ark of YHWH’s covenant goes before them three days’ journey, to seek out a resting place for them. The cloud of YHWH is over them by day, when they set forward from the camp. When the ark goes forward, Moses says, “Rise up, YHWH, and let your enemies be scattered! Let those who hate you flee before you!” When it rests, he says, “Return, YHWH, to the ten thousands of the thousands of Israel.”
Fire at Taberah · 11:1–3

The people are complaining in the ears of YHWH. When YHWH hears it, his anger burns; and YHWH’s fire burned among them, and consumes some of the outskirts of the camp. The people cry to Moses; and Moses prays to YHWH, and the fire abates. The name of that place is called Taberah, because YHWH’s fire burns among them.
The Craving for Meat · 11:4–9

The mixed multitude that is among them lusts exceedingly: and the children of Israel also weep again, and say, “Who will give us meat to eat? We remember the fish, which we ate in Egypt for nothing; the cucumbers, and the melons, and the leeks, and the onions, and the garlic; but now we have lost our appetite. There is nothing at all except this manna to look at.” The manna is like coriander seed, and its appearance like the appearance of bdellium. The people go around, gather it, and grind it in mills, or beat it in mortars, and boil it in pots, and make cakes of it. Its taste is like the taste of fresh oil. When the dew falls on the camp in the night, the manna falls on it.
The Burden of Moses · 11:10–15

Moses hears the people weeping throughout their families, every man at the door of his tent; and YHWH’s anger burns greatly; and Moses is displeased. Moses says to YHWH, “Why have you treated your servant so badly? Why haven’t I found favor in your sight, that you lay the burden of all this people on me? Have I conceived all this people? Have I brought them out, that you should tell me, ‘Carry them in your bosom, as a nurse carries a nursing infant, to the land which you swore to their fathers?’ Where could I get meat to give all these people? For they weep before me, saying, ‘Give us meat, that we may eat.’ I am not able to bear all this people alone, because it is too heavy for me. If you treat me this way, please kill me right now, if I have found favor in your sight; and don’t let me see my wretchedness.”
The Seventy Elders · 11:16–25

YHWH says to Moses, “Gather to me seventy men of the elders of Israel, whom you know to be the elders of the people, and officers over them; and bring them to the Tent of Meeting, that they may stand there with you. I will come down and talk with you there. I will take of the Spirit which is on you, and will put it on them; and they must bear the burden of the people with you, that you don’t bear it yourself alone.

“Say to the people, ‘Sanctify yourselves in preparation for tomorrow, and you will eat meat; for you have wept in the ears of YHWH, saying, “Who will give us meat to eat? For it was well with us in Egypt.” Therefore YHWH will give you meat, and you will eat. You will not eat one day, nor two days, nor five days, neither ten days, nor twenty days, but a whole month, until it comes out at your nostrils, and it is loathsome to you; because you have rejected YHWH who is among you, and have wept before him, saying, “Why did we come out of Egypt?”’”

Moses says, “The people, among whom I am, are six hundred thousand men on foot; and you have said, ‘I will give them meat, that they may eat a whole month.’ Will flocks and herds be slaughtered for them, to be sufficient for them? Will all the fish of the sea be gathered together for them, to be sufficient for them?”
YHWH says to Moses, “Has YHWH’s hand grown short? Now you will see whether my word will happen to you or not.”

Moses goes out, and tells the people YHWH’s words; and he gathers seventy men of the elders of the people, and sets them around the Tent. YHWH comes down in the cloud, and speaks to him, and takes of the Spirit that is on him, and puts it on the seventy elders. When the Spirit rests on them, they prophesy, but they do so no more.
Eldad and Medad · 11:26–30

But two men remain in the camp. The name of one is Eldad, and the name of the other Medad: and the Spirit rests on them; and they are of those who are written, but have not gone out to the Tent; and they prophesy in the camp. A young man runs, and tells Moses, and says, “Eldad and Medad are prophesying in the camp!”
Joshua the son of Nun, the servant of Moses, one of his chosen men, answers, “My lord Moses, forbid them!”
Moses says to him, “Are you jealous for my sake? I wish that all YHWH’s people were prophets, that YHWH would put his Spirit on them!”
Moses goes into the camp, he and the elders of Israel.
The Quail and the Plague · 11:31–35

A wind from YHWH goes out and brings quails from the sea, and let them fall by the camp, about a day’s journey on this side, and a day’s journey on the other side, around the camp, and about two cubits above the surface of the earth. The people rise up all that day, and all of that night, and all the next day, and gather the quails. He who gathereds least gathered ten homers; and they spread them all out for themselves around the camp. While the meat is still between their teeth, before it is chewed, YHWH’s anger burns against the people, and YHWH strikes the people with a very great plague. The name of that place is called Kibroth Hattaavah, because there they bury the people who lust.
From Kibroth Hattaavah the people travel to Hazeroth; and they stay at Hazeroth.
Miriam and Aaron Challenge Moses · 12:1–3

Miriam and Aaron speak against Moses because of the Cushite woman whom he has married; for he has married a Cushite woman. They say, “Has YHWH indeed spoken only with Moses? Hasn’t he spoken also with us?” And YHWH hears it.
Now the man Moses is very humble, more than all the men who are on the surface of the earth.
The Lord Defends Moses · 12:4–9
YHWH speaks suddenly to Moses, to Aaron, and to Miriam, “You three come out to the Tent of Meeting!”

The three of them comes out. YHWH comes down in a pillar of cloud, and stands at the door of the Tent, and calls Aaron and Miriam; and they both come forward. He says, “Now hear my words. If there is a prophet among you, I, YHWH, will make myself known to him in a vision. I will speak with him in a dream. My servant Moses is not so. He is faithful in all my house. With him, I will speak mouth to mouth, even plainly, and not in riddles; and he will see YHWH’s form. Why then were you not afraid to speak against my servant, against Moses?” YHWH’s anger burns against them; and he departs.
Miriam’s Leprosy · 12:10–16
The cloud departs from over the Tent; and look, Miriam is leprous, as white as snow. Aaron looks at Miriam, and look, she is leprous.

Aaron says to Moses, “Oh, my lord, please don’t count this sin against us, in which we have done foolishly, and in which we have sinned. Let her not, I pray, be as one dead, of whom the flesh is half consumed when he comes out of his mother’s womb.”
Moses cries to YHWH, saying, “Heal her, God, I beg you!”
YHWH says to Moses, “If her father had but spit in her face, shouldn’t she be ashamed seven days? Let her be shut up outside of the camp seven days, and after that she will be brought in again.”
Miriam is shut up outside of the camp seven days, and the people doesn’t travel until Miriam is brought in again. Afterward the people travel from Hazeroth, and encamp in the wilderness of Paran.
The Twelve Scouts · 13:1–16

YHWH speaks to Moses, saying, “Send men, that they may spy out the land of Canaan, which I give to the children of Israel. Of every tribe of their fathers, you must send a man, every one a prince among them.”
Moses sends them from the wilderness of Paran according to the commandment of YHWH. All of them are men who are heads of the children of Israel. These are their names:
Of the tribe of Reuben, Shammua the son of Zaccur.
Of the tribe of Simeon, Shaphat the son of Hori.
Of the tribe of Judah, Caleb the son of Jephunneh.
Of the tribe of Issachar, Igal the son of Joseph.
Of the tribe of Ephraim, Hoshea the son of Nun.
Of the tribe of Benjamin, Palti the son of Raphu.
Of the tribe of Zebulun, Gaddiel the son of Sodi.
Of the tribe of Joseph, of the tribe of Manasseh, Gaddi the son of Susi.
Of the tribe of Dan, Ammiel the son of Gemalli.
Of the tribe of Asher, Sethur the son of Michael.
Of the tribe of Naphtali, Nahbi the son of Vophsi.
Of the tribe of Gad, Geuel the son of Machi.
These are the names of the men who Moses sends to spy out the land. Moses calls Hoshea the son of Nun Joshua.
Instructions for the Survey · 13:17–20

Moses sends them to spy out the land of Canaan, and says to them, “Go up this way by the South, and go up into the hill country. See the land, what it is; and the people who dwell therein, whether they are strong or weak, whether they are few or many; and what the land is that they dwell in, whether it is good or bad; and what cities they are that they dwell in, whether in camps, or in strongholds; and what the land is, whether it is fat or lean, whether there is wood therein, or not. Be courageous, and bring some of the fruit of the land.” Now the time is the time of the first-ripe grapes.
The Survey of the Land · 13:21–25

So they go up, and spy out the land from the wilderness of Zin to Rehob, to the entrance of Hamath. They go up by the South, and come to Hebron; and Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai, the children of Anak, are there. (Now Hebron is built seven years before Zoan in Egypt.) They come to the valley of Eshcol, and cut down from there a branch with one cluster of grapes, and they bear it on a staff between two. They also bring some of the pomegranates and figs. That place is called the valley of Eshcol, because of the cluster which the children of Israel cut down from there. They return from spying out the land at the end of forty days.
The Report · 13:26–33

They go and come to Moses, to Aaron, and to all the congregation of the children of Israel, to the wilderness of Paran, to Kadesh; and bring back word to them and to all the congregation. They show them the fruit of the land. They tell him, and say, “We came to the land where you sent us. Surely it flows with milk and honey, and this is its fruit. However the people who dwell in the land are strong, and the cities are fortified and very large. Moreover, we saw the children of Anak there. Amalek dwells in the land of the South. The Hittite, the Jebusite, and the Amorite dwell in the hill country. The Canaanite dwells by the sea, and along the side of the Jordan.”
Caleb stills the people before Moses, and says, “Let us go up at once, and possess it; for we are well able to overcome it!”

But the men who go up with him say, “We aren’t able to go up against the people; for they are stronger than we.” They bring up an evil report of the land which they have spied out to the children of Israel, saying, “The land, through which we have gone to spy it out, is a land that eats up its inhabitants; and all the people who we saw in it are men of great stature. There we saw the Nephilim, the sons of Anak, who come from the Nephilim. We were in our own sight as grasshoppers, and so we were in their sight.”
The Congregation Rebels · 14:1–10

All the congregation lifts up their voice, and cries; and the people weep that night. All the children of Israel murmur against Moses and against Aaron. The whole congregation says to them, “We wish that we had died in the land of Egypt, or that we had died in this wilderness! Why does YHWH bring us to this land, to fall by the sword? Our wives and our little ones will be captured or killed! Wouldn’t it be better for us to return into Egypt?” They say to one another, “Let us make a captain, and let us return into Egypt.”
Then Moses and Aaron fall on their faces before all the assembly of the congregation of the children of Israel.

Joshua the son of Nun and Caleb the son of Jephunneh, who are of those who spy out the land, tears their clothes. They speak to all the congregation of the children of Israel, saying, “The land, which we passed through to spy it out, is an exceeding good land. If YHWH delights in us, then he will bring us into this land, and give it to us; a land which flows with milk and honey. Only don’t rebel against YHWH, neither fear the people of the land; for they are bread for us. Their defense is removed from over them, and YHWH is with us. Don’t fear them.”
But all the congregation threatens to stone them with stones.
YHWH’s glory appears in the Tent of Meeting to all the children of Israel.
Moses Intercedes · 14:11–19

YHWH says to Moses, “How long will this people despise me? and how long will they not believe in me, for all the signs which I have worked among them? I will strike them with the pestilence, and disinherit them, and will make of you a nation greater and mightier than they.”

Moses says to YHWH, “Then the Egyptians will hear it; for you brought up this people in your might from among them. They will tell it to the inhabitants of this land. They have heard that you YHWH are among this people; for you YHWH are seen face to face, and your cloud stands over them, and you go before them, in a pillar of cloud by day, and in a pillar of fire by night. Now if you killed this people as one man, then the nations which have heard the fame of you will speak, saying, ‘Because YHWH was not able to bring this people into the land which he swore to them, therefore he has slain them in the wilderness.’ Now please let the power of the Lord be great, according as you have spoken, saying, ‘YHWH is slow to anger, and abundant in steadfast love, forgiving iniquity and disobedience; and he will by no means clear the guilty, visiting the iniquity of the fathers on the children, on the third and on the fourth generation.’ Please pardon the iniquity of this people according to the greatness of your steadfast love, and just as you have forgiven this people, from Egypt even until now.”
The Lord’s Judgment · 14:20–38

YHWH says, “I have pardoned according to your word: but in very deed, as I live, and as all the earth will be filled with YHWH’s glory; because all those men who have seen my glory, and my signs, which I worked in Egypt and in the wilderness, yet have tempted me these ten times, and have not listened to my voice; surely they must not see the land which I swore to their fathers, neither will any of those who despised me see it. But my servant Caleb, because he had another spirit with him, and has followed me fully, him I will bring into the land into which he went. His offspring will possess it. Since the Amalekite and the Canaanite dwell in the valley, tomorrow turn, and go into the wilderness by the way to the Red Sea.” YHWH speaks to Moses and to Aaron, saying, “How long should I bear with this evil congregation, that murmur against me? I have heard the murmurings of the children of Israel, which they murmur against me. Tell them, ‘As I live, says YHWH, surely as you have spoken in my ears, so will I do to you. Your dead bodies will fall in this wilderness; and all who were counted of you, according to your whole number, from twenty years old and upward, who have murmured against me, surely you must not come into the land, concerning which I swore that I would make you dwell therein, except Caleb the son of Jephunneh, and Joshua the son of Nun. But your little ones, that you said should be captured or killed, them I will bring in, and they will know the land which you have rejected. But as for you, your dead bodies will fall in this wilderness. Your children will be wanderers in the wilderness forty years, and will bear your prostitution, until your dead bodies are consumed in the wilderness. After the number of the days in which you spied out the land, even forty days, for every day a year, you will bear your iniquities, even forty years, and you will know my alienation.’ I, YHWH, have spoken. I will surely do this to all this evil congregation, who are gathered together against me. In this wilderness they will be consumed, and there they will die.”

The men, whom Moses sends to spy out the land, who returns, and make all the congregation to murmur against him, by bringing up an evil report against the land, even those men who bring up an evil report of the land, die by the plague before YHWH. But Joshua the son of Nun, and Caleb the son of Jephunneh, remain alive of those men who go to spy out the land.
The Failed Assault · 14:39–45

Moses tells these words to all the children of Israel, and the people mourn greatly. They rise up early in the morning, and go up to the top of the mountain, saying, “Look, we are here, and will go up to the place which YHWH has promised: for we have sinned.”

Moses says, “Why now do you disobey the commandment of YHWH, since it must not prosper? Don’t go up, for YHWH isn’t among you; that way you won’t be struck down before your enemies. For there the Amalekite and the Canaanite are before you, and you will fall by the sword, because you turned back from following YHWH, therefore YHWH will not be with you.”

But they presume to go up to the top of the mountain. Nevertheless, the ark of YHWH’s covenant and Moses doesn’t depart out of the camp. Then the Amalekites come down, and the Canaanites who live in that mountain, and strike them and beat them down, even to Hormah.
Offerings Accompanying Sacrifices · 15:1–16

YHWH speaks to Moses, saying, “Speak to the children of Israel, and tell them, ‘When you have come into the land of your habitations, which I give to you, and will make an offering by fire to YHWH, a burnt offering, or a sacrifice, to accomplish a vow, or as a freewill offering, or in your set feasts, to make a pleasant aroma to YHWH, of the herd, or of the flock; then he who offers his offering will offer to YHWH a meal offering of one tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with the fourth part of a hin of oil. You must prepare wine for the drink offering, the fourth part of a hin, with the burnt offering, or for the sacrifice, for each lamb.

“‘Or for a ram, you must prepare for a meal offering two tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with the third part of a hin of oil; and for the drink offering you must offer the third part of a hin of wine, of a pleasant aroma to YHWH. When you prepare a bull for a burnt offering, or for a sacrifice, to accomplish a vow, or for peace offerings to YHWH; then will he offer with the bull a meal offering of three tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with half a hin of oil: and you must offer for the drink offering half a hin of wine, for an offering made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to YHWH. Thus will it be done for each bull, or for each ram, or for each of the male lambs, or of the young goats. According to the number that you must prepare, so you must do to everyone according to their number.

“‘All who are native-born will do these things in this way, in offering an offering made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to YHWH. If a stranger lives as a foreigner with you, or whoever may be among you throughout your generations, and will offer an offering made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to YHWH; as you do, so he must do. For the assembly, there will be one statute for you and for the stranger who lives as a foreigner, a statute forever throughout your generations. As you are, so will the foreigner be before YHWH. One law and one ordinance will be for you, and for the stranger who lives as a foreigner with you.’”
The First of the Dough · 15:17–21

YHWH speaks to Moses, saying, “Speak to the children of Israel, and tell them, ‘When you come into the land where I bring you, then it will be that when you eat of the bread of the land, you must offer up a wave offering to YHWH. Of the first of your dough you must offer up a cake for a wave offering. As the wave offering of the threshing floor, so you must heave it. Of the first of your dough, you must give to YHWH a wave offering throughout your generations.
Unintentional and Defiant Sins · 15:22–31

“‘When you err, and don’t observe all these commandments, which YHWH has spoken to Moses, even all that YHWH has commanded you by Moses, from the day that YHWH gave commandment, and onward throughout your generations; then it will be, if it was done unwittingly, without the knowledge of the congregation, that all the congregation will offer one young bull for a burnt offering, for a pleasant aroma to YHWH, with its meal offering, and its drink offering, according to the ordinance, and one male goat for a sin offering. The priest will make atonement for all the congregation of the children of Israel, and they will be forgiven; for it was an error, and they have brought their offering, an offering made by fire to YHWH, and their sin offering before YHWH, for their error. All the congregation of the children of Israel will be forgiven, as well as the stranger who lives as a foreigner among them; for with regard to all the people, it was done unwittingly.

“‘If one person sins unwittingly, then he must offer a female goat a year old for a sin offering. The priest will make atonement for the soul who errs, when he sins unwittingly before YHWH, to make atonement for him; and he will be forgiven. You must have one law for him who does anything unwittingly, for him who is native-born among the children of Israel, and for the stranger who lives as a foreigner among them.

“‘But the soul who does anything with a high hand, whether he is native-born or a foreigner, the same blasphemes YHWH. That soul will be cut off from among his people. Because he has despised YHWH’s word, and has broken his commandment, that soul will utterly be cut off. His iniquity will be on him.’”
The Sabbath Wood-gatherer · 15:32–36

While the children of Israel are in the wilderness, they find a man gathering sticks on the Sabbath day. Those who find him gathering sticks bring him to Moses and Aaron, and to all the congregation. They put him in custody, because it has not been declared what should be done to him.

YHWH says to Moses, “The man will surely be put to death. All the congregation will stone him with stones outside of the camp.” All the congregation brings him outside of the camp, and stones him to death with stones, as YHWH commands Moses.
The Tassels of Remembrance · 15:37–41

YHWH speaks to Moses, saying, “Speak to the children of Israel, and tell them that they should make themselves fringes in the borders of their garments throughout their generations, and that they put on the fringe of each border a cord of blue: and it will be to you for a fringe, that you may look on it, and remember all YHWH’s commandments, and do them; and that you don’ t follow your own heart and your own eyes, after which you use to play the prostitute; so that you may remember and do all my commandments, and be holy to your God. I am YHWH your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, to be your God: I am YHWH your God.”
Korah’s Uprising · 16:1–15

Now Korah, the son of Izhar, the son of Kohath, the son of Levi, with Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, and On, the son of Peleth, sons of Reuben, take some men. They rise up before Moses, with some of the children of Israel, two hundred fifty princes of the congregation, call to the assembly, men of renown. They assemble themselves together against Moses and against Aaron, and say to them, “You take too much on yourself, since all the congregation are holy, everyone of them, and YHWH is among them! Why do you lift yourselves up above YHWH’s assembly?”

When Moses hears it, he falls on his face. He says to Korah and to all his company, “In the morning, YHWH will show who are his, and who is holy, and will cause him to come near to him. Even him whom he must choose, he will cause to come near to him. Do this: take censers, Korah, and all his company; and put fire in them, and put incense on them before YHWH tomorrow. It will be that the man whom YHWH chooses, he will be holy. You have gone too far, you sons of Levi!”

Moses says to Korah, “Hear now, you sons of Levi! Is it a small thing to you, that the God of Israel has separated you from the congregation of Israel, to bring you near to himself, to do the service of YHWH’s tabernacle, and to stand before the congregation to minister to them; and that he has brought you near, and all your brothers the sons of Levi with you? Do you seek the priesthood also? Therefore you and all your company have gathered together against YHWH! What is Aaron that you murmur against him?”

Moses sends to call Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab; and they say, “We won’t come up! Is it a small thing that you have brought us up out of a land flowing with milk and honey, to kill us in the wilderness, but you must also make yourself a prince over us? Moreover you haven’t brought us into a land flowing with milk and honey, nor given us inheritance of fields and vineyards. Will you put out the eyes of these men? We won’t come up.”
Moses is very angry, and says to YHWH, “Don’t respect their offering. I have not taken one donkey from them, neither have I hurt one of them.”
The Test of the Censers · 16:16–24

Moses says to Korah, “You and all your company go before YHWH, you, and they, and Aaron, tomorrow. Each man take his censer, and put incense on them, and each man bring before YHWH his censer, two hundred fifty censers; you also, and Aaron, each his censer.”

They each take his censer, and put fire in them, and lay incense on it, and stand at the door of the Tent of Meeting with Moses and Aaron. Korah assembles all the congregation opposite them to the door of the Tent of Meeting.
YHWH’s glory appears to all the congregation. YHWH speaks to Moses and to Aaron, saying, “Separate yourselves from among this congregation, that I may consume them in a moment!”
They fall on their faces, and say, “God, the God of the spirits of all flesh, will one man sin, and will you be angry with all the congregation?”
YHWH speaks to Moses, saying, “Speak to the congregation, saying, ‘Get away from around the tent of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram!’”
The Earth Opens, the Fire Falls · 16:25–35

Moses rises up and goes to Dathan and Abiram; and the elders of Israel follow him. He speaks to the congregation, saying, “Depart, please, from the tents of these wicked men, and touch nothing of theirs, lest you be consumed in all their sins!”
So they go away from the tent of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram, on every side. Dathan and Abiram come out, and stand at the door of their tents, with their wives, their sons, and their little ones.

Moses says, “Hereby you will know that YHWH has sent me to do all these works; for they are not from my own mind. If these men die the common death of all men, or if they experience what all men experience, then YHWH hasn’t sent me. But if YHWH makes a new thing, and the ground opens its mouth, and swallows them up, with all that belong to them, and they go down alive into Sheol; then you will understand that these men have despised YHWH.”

As he finishes speaking all these words, the ground that is under them splits apart. The earth opens its mouth and swallows them up, with their households, all of Korah’s men, and all their goods. So they, and all that belong to them go down alive into Sheol. The earth closes on them, and they perish from among the assembly. All Israel that are around them flees at their cry; for they say, “Lest the earth swallow us up!” Fire comes out from YHWH, and devours the two hundred fifty men who offer the incense.
The Bronze Plating and the Plague · 16:36–50

YHWH speaks to Moses, saying, “Speak to Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest, that he take up the censers out of the burning, and scatter the fire away from the camp; for they are holy, even the censers of those who sinned against their own lives. Let them be beaten into plates for a covering of the altar, for they offered them before YHWH. Therefore they are holy. They will be a sign to the children of Israel.”

Eleazar the priest takes the bronze censers, which those who are burned have offered; and they beat them out for a covering of the altar, to be a memorial to the children of Israel, to the end that no stranger, who isn’t of the offspring of Aaron, would come near to burn incense before YHWH, that he not be as Korah, and as his company; as YHWH speaks to him by Moses.
But on the next day all the congregation of the children of Israel murmurs against Moses and against Aaron, saying, “You have killed YHWH’s people!”

When the congregation is assembled against Moses and against Aaron, They look toward the Tent of Meeting. Look, the cloud covers it, and YHWH’s glory appears. Moses and Aaron come to the front of the Tent of Meeting. YHWH speaks to Moses, saying, “Get away from among this congregation, that I may consume them in a moment!” They fall on their faces.

Moses says to Aaron, “Take your censer, and put fire from off the altar in it, and lay incense on it, and carry it quickly to the congregation, and make atonement for them; for wrath has gone out from YHWH! The plague has begun.”

Aaron does as Moses says, and runs into the middle of the assembly. The plague has already begun among the people. He puts on the incense, and makes atonement for the people. He stands between the dead and the living; and the plague is stayed. Now those who die by the plague are fourteen thousand and seven hundred, besides those who die about the matter of Korah. Aaron returns to Moses to the door of the Tent of Meeting, and the plague is stopped.
The Staffs of the Leaders · 17:1–7

YHWH speaks to Moses, saying, “Speak to the children of Israel, and take rods from them, one for each fathers’ house, of all their princes according to their fathers’ houses, twelve rods. Write each man’s name on his rod. You must write Aaron’s name on the rod of Levi; for there will be one rod for each head of their fathers’ houses. You must lay them up in the Tent of Meeting before the testimony, where I meet with you. It must happen, that the rod of the man whom I will choose will bud. I will make the murmurings of the children of Israel, which they murmur against you, cease from me.”

Moses speaks to the children of Israel; and all their princes give him rods, for each prince one, according to their fathers’ houses, a total of twelve rods. Aaron’s rod is among their rods. Moses lays up the rods before YHWH in the Tent of the Testimony.
Aaron’s Staff Buds · 17:8–11

On the next day, Moses goes into the Tent of the Testimony; and look, Aaron’s rod for the house of Levi has sprouted, budded, produced blossoms, and bears ripe almonds. Moses brings out all the rods from before YHWH to all the children of Israel. They look, and each man takes his rod.

YHWH says to Moses, “Put back the rod of Aaron before the testimony, to be kept for a token against the children of rebellion; that you may make an end of their murmurings against me, that they not die.” Moses does so. As YHWH commands him, so he does.
The Fear of the People · 17:12–13
The children of Israel speak to Moses, saying, “Look, we perish! We are undone! We are all undone! Everyone who keeps approaching YHWH’s tabernacle, dies! Will we all perish?”
The Duties of Priests and Levites · 18:1–7

YHWH says to Aaron, “You and your sons and your fathers’ house with you must bear the iniquity of the sanctuary; and you and your sons with you must bear the iniquity of your priesthood. Bring your brothers also, the tribe of Levi, the tribe of your father, near with you, that they may be joined to you, and minister to you; but you and your sons with you will be before the Tent of the Testimony. They must keep your commands, and the duty of the whole Tent; only they must not come near to the vessels of the sanctuary and to the altar, that they not die, neither they, nor you. They will be joined to you, and keep the responsibility of the Tent of Meeting, for all the service of the Tent. A stranger will not come near to you.

“You must perform the duty of the sanctuary and the duty of the altar, that there be no more wrath on the children of Israel. Look, I myself have taken your brothers the Levites from among the children of Israel. They are a gift to you, dedicated to YHWH, to do the service of the Tent of Meeting. You and your sons with you must keep your priesthood for everything of the altar, and for that within the veil. You must serve. I give you the service of the priesthood as a gift. The stranger who comes near will be put to death.”
The Priests’ Portion · 18:8–20

YHWH speaks to Aaron, “Look, I myself have given you the command of my wave offerings, even all the holy things of the children of Israel. I have given them to you by reason of the anointing, and to your sons, as a portion forever. This will be yours of the most holy things from the fire: every offering of theirs, even every meal offering of theirs, and every sin offering of theirs, and every trespass offering of theirs, which they must render to me, will be most holy for you and for your sons. You must eat of it like the most holy things. Every male will eat of it. It will be holy to you.

“This is yours, too: the wave offering of their gift, even all the wave offerings of the children of Israel. I have given them to you, and to your sons and to your daughters with you, as a portion forever. Everyone who is clean in your house will eat of it.

“I have given to you all the best of the oil, and all the best of the vintage, and of the grain, the first fruits of them which they give to YHWH. The first-ripe fruits of all that is in their land, which they bring to YHWH, will be yours. Everyone who is clean in your house will eat of it.

“Everything devoted in Israel will be yours. Everything that opens the womb, of all flesh which they offer to YHWH, both of man and animal will be yours. Nevertheless, you will surely redeem the firstborn of man, and you must redeem the firstborn of unclean animals. You must redeem those who are to be redeemed of them from a month old, according to your estimation, for five shekels of money, after the shekel of the sanctuary, which weighs twenty gerahs.

“But you must not redeem the firstborn of a cow, or the firstborn of a sheep, or the firstborn of a goat. They are holy. You must sprinkle their blood on the altar, and will burn their fat for an offering made by fire, for a pleasant aroma to YHWH. Their meat will be yours, as the wave offering breast and as the right thigh, it will be yours. All the wave offerings of the holy things, which the children of Israel offer to YHWH, I have given you, and your sons and your daughters with you, as a portion forever. It is a covenant of salt forever before YHWH to you and to your offspring with you.”
YHWH says to Aaron, “You must have no inheritance in their land, neither will you have any portion among them. I am your portion and your inheritance among the children of Israel.
The Levites’ Tithe · 18:21–32

“To the children of Levi, look, I have given all the tithe in Israel for an inheritance, in return for their service which they serve, even the service of the Tent of Meeting. Henceforth the children of Israel will not come near the Tent of Meeting, lest they bear sin, and die. But the Levites will do the service of the Tent of Meeting, and they must bear their iniquity. It will be a statute forever throughout your generations. Among the children of Israel, they must have no inheritance. For the tithe of the children of Israel, which they offer as a wave offering to YHWH, I have given to the Levites for an inheritance. Therefore I have said to them, ‘Among the children of Israel they must have no inheritance.’”

YHWH speaks to Moses, saying, “Moreover you must speak to the Levites, and tell them, ‘When you take of the children of Israel the tithe which I have given you from them for your inheritance, then you must offer up a wave offering of it for YHWH, a tithe of the tithe. Your wave offering will be credited to you, as though it were the grain of the threshing floor, and as the fullness of the wine press. Thus you also will offer a wave offering to YHWH of all your tithes, which you receive of the children of Israel; and of it you must give YHWH’s wave offering to Aaron the priest. Out of all your gifts, you must offer every wave offering of YHWH, of all its best parts, even the holy part of it.’

“Therefore you must tell them, ‘When you heave its best from it, then it will be credited to the Levites as the increase of the threshing floor, and as the increase of the wine press. You may eat it anywhere, you and your households, for it is your reward in return for your service in the Tent of Meeting. You must bear no sin by reason of it, when you have heaved from it its best. You must not profane the holy things of the children of Israel, that you not die.’”
The Red Heifer Ritual · 19:1–10

YHWH speaks to Moses and to Aaron, saying, “This is the statute of the law which YHWH has commanded. Tell the children of Israel to bring you a red heifer without spot, in which is no defect, and which was never yoked. You must give her to Eleazar the priest, and he must bring her outside of the camp, and one will kill her before his face. Eleazar the priest will take some of her blood with his finger, and sprinkle her blood toward the front of the Tent of Meeting seven times. One will burn the heifer in his sight; her skin, and her meat, and her blood, with her dung, will he burn. The priest will take cedar wood, hyssop, and scarlet, and cast it into the middle of the burning of the heifer. Then the priest will wash his clothes, and he must bathe his flesh in water, and afterward he will come into the camp, and the priest will be unclean until the evening. He who burns her will wash his clothes in water, and bathe his flesh in water, and will be unclean until the evening.

“A man who is clean will gather up the ashes of the heifer, and lay them up outside of the camp in a clean place; and it will be kept for the congregation of the children of Israel for use in water for cleansing impurity. It is a sin offering. He who gathers the ashes of the heifer will wash his clothes, and be unclean until the evening. It will be to the children of Israel, and to the stranger who lives as a foreigner among them, for a statute forever.
The Law of Corpse Impurity · 19:11–16

“He who touches the dead body of any man will be unclean seven days. He must purify himself with water on the third day, and on the seventh day he will be clean; but if he doesn’t purify himself the third day, then the seventh day he must not be clean. Whoever touches a dead person, the body of a man who has died, and doesn’t purify himself, defiles YHWH’s tabernacle; and that soul will be cut off from Israel; because the water for impurity was not sprinkled on him, he will be unclean. His uncleanness is yet on him.

“This is the law when a man dies in a tent: everyone who comes into the tent, and everyone who is in the tent, will be unclean seven days. Every open vessel, which has no covering bound on it, is unclean.
“Whoever in the open field touches one who is slain with a sword, or a dead body, or a bone of a man, or a grave, will be unclean seven days.
The Purification Procedure · 19:17–22

“For the unclean, they must take of the ashes of the burning of the sin offering; and running water will be poured into a vessel. A clean person will take hyssop, dip it in the water, and sprinkle it on the tent, on all the vessels, on the persons who were there, and on him who touched the bone, or the slain, or the dead, or the grave. The clean person will sprinkle on the unclean on the third day, and on the seventh day. On the seventh day, he must purify him.
