He must wash his clothes and bathe himself in water, and will be clean at evening. But the man who will be unclean, and will not purify himself, that soul will be cut off from among the assembly, because he has defiled the sanctuary of YHWH. The water for impurity has not been sprinkled on him. He is unclean. It will be a perpetual statute to them. He who sprinkles the water for impurity will wash his clothes, and he who touches the water for impurity will be unclean until evening.
“Whatever the unclean person touches will be unclean; and the soul that touches it will be unclean until evening.”
The Death of Miriam · 20:1
The children of Israel, even the whole congregation, come into the wilderness of Zin in the first month. The people stay in Kadesh. Miriam dies there, and is buried there.
Water from the Rock at Meribah · 20:2–13

There is no water for the congregation; and they assemble themselves together against Moses and against Aaron. The people quarrel with Moses, and speak, saying, “We wish that we had died when our brothers died before YHWH! Why have you brought YHWH’s assembly into this wilderness, that we should die there, we and our animals? Why have you made us to come up out of Egypt, to bring us in to this evil place? It is no place of seed, or of figs, or of vines, or of pomegranates; neither is there any water to drink.”

Moses and Aaron go from the presence of the assembly to the door of the Tent of Meeting, and fall on their faces. YHWH’s glory appears to them. YHWH speaks to Moses, saying, “Take the rod, and assemble the congregation, you, and Aaron your brother, and speak to the rock before their eyes, that it pour out its water. You must bring water to them out of the rock; so you must give the congregation and their livestock drink.”

Moses takes the rod from before YHWH, as he commands him. Moses and Aaron gather the assembly together before the rock, and he says to them, “Hear now, you rebels! Should we bring water out of this rock for you?” Moses lifts up his hand, and strikes the rock with his rod twice, and water comes out abundantly. The congregation and their livestock drank.

YHWH says to Moses and Aaron, “Because you didn’t believe in me, to sanctify me in the eyes of the children of Israel, therefore you must not bring this assembly into the land which I have given them.”
These are the waters of Meribah; because the children of Israel strove with YHWH, and he is sanctified in them.
Edom Refuses Passage · 20:14–21
Moses sends messengers from Kadesh to the king of Edom, saying:

“Thus says your brother Israel: You know all the travail that has happened to us; how our fathers went down into Egypt, and we lived in Egypt a long time. The Egyptians mistreated us and our fathers. When we cried to YHWH, he heard our voice, sent an angel, and brought us out of Egypt. Look, we are in Kadesh, a city in the edge of your border.

“Please let us pass through your land. We will not pass through field or through vineyard, neither will we drink from the water of the wells. We will go along the king’s highway. We will not turn away to the right hand nor to the left, until we have passed your border.”
Edom says to him, “You must not pass through me, lest I come out with the sword against you.”

The children of Israel say to him, “We will go up by the highway; and if we drink your water, I and my livestock, then I will give its price. Only let me, without doing anything else, pass through on my feet.”
He says, “You must not pass through.” Edom comes out against him with many people, and with a strong hand. Thus Edom refuses to give Israel passage through his border, so Israel turns away from him.
The Death of Aaron · 20:22–29

They travel from Kadesh: and the children of Israel, even the whole congregation, come to Mount Hor. YHWH speaks to Moses and Aaron in Mount Hor, by the border of the land of Edom, saying, “Aaron will be gathered to his people; for he must not enter into the land which I have given to the children of Israel, because you rebelled against my word at the waters of Meribah. Take Aaron and Eleazar his son, and bring them up to Mount Hor; and strip Aaron of his garments, and put them on Eleazar his son. Aaron will be gathered, and will die there.”

Moses does as YHWH commands. They go up into Mount Hor in the sight of all the congregation. Moses strips Aaron of his garments, and puts them on Eleazar his son. Aaron dies there on the top of the mountain, and Moses and Eleazar come down from the mountain. When all the congregation sees that Aaron is dead, they weep for Aaron thirty days, even all the house of Israel.
Victory over Arad · 21:1–3

The Canaanite, the king of Arad, who lives in the South, hears that Israel comes by the way of Atharim. He fights against Israel, and takes some of them captive. Israel vows a vow to YHWH, and says, “If you will indeed deliver this people into my hand, then I will utterly destroy their cities.” YHWH listens to the voice of Israel, and delivers up the Canaanites; and they utterly destroy them and their cities. The name of the place is called Hormah.
The Bronze Serpent · 21:4–9

They travel from Mount Hor by the way to the Red Sea, to go around the land of Edom The soul of the people is very discouraged because of the journey. The people speak against God, and against Moses, “Why have you brought us up out of Egypt to die in the wilderness? For there is no bread, and there is no water; and our soul loathes this disgusting bread.”

YHWH sends venomous snakes among the people, and they bit the people. Many people of Israel die. The people come to Moses, and say, “We have sinned, because we have spoken against YHWH, and against you. Pray to YHWH, that he take away the serpents from us.” Moses prays for the people.

YHWH says to Moses, “Make a venomous snake, and set it on a pole. It must happen, that everyone who is bitten, when he sees it, will live.” Moses makes a serpent of brass, and sets it on the pole. If a serpent has bitten any man, when he looks at the serpent of brass, he lives.
The Journey North · 21:10–20

The children of Israel travel, and encamp in Oboth. They travel from Oboth, and encamp at Iyeabarim, in the wilderness which is before Moab, toward the sunrise. From there they travel, and encamp in the valley of Zered. From there they travel, and encamp on the other side of the Arnon, which is in the wilderness, that comes out of the border of the Amorites: for the Arnon is the border of Moab, between Moab and the Amorites. Therefore it is said in the book of the Wars of YHWH, “Vaheb in Suphah, the valleys of the Arnon, the slope of the valleys that incline toward the dwelling of Ar, leans on the border of Moab.”
From there they travel to Beer; that is the well of which YHWH says to Moses, “Gather the people together, and I will give them water.”
Then Israel sings this song:
“Spring up, well! Sing to it,
the well, which the princes dug,
which the nobles of the people dug,
with the scepter, and with their poles.”

From the wilderness they travel to Mattanah; and from Mattanah to Nahaliel; and from Nahaliel to Bamoth; and from Bamoth to the valley that is in the field of Moab, to the top of Pisgah, which looks down on the desert.
Victory over Sihon · 21:21–31

Israel sends messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites, saying, “Let me pass through your land. We will not turn away into field or vineyard. We will not drink of the water of the wells. We will go by the king’s highway, until we have passed your border.”

Sihon would not allow Israel to pass through his border, but Sihon gathers all his people together, and goes out against Israel into the wilderness, and comes to Jahaz. He fights against Israel. Israel strikes him with the edge of the sword, and possesses his land from the Arnon to the Jabbok, even to the children of Ammon; for the border of the children of Ammon is strong. Israel takes all these cities. Israel lives in all the cities of the Amorites, in Heshbon, and in all its villages. For Heshbon is the city of Sihon the king of the Amorites, who have fought against the former king of Moab, and take all his land out of his hand, even to the Arnon. Therefore those who speak in proverbs say,
“Come to Heshbon.
Let the city of Sihon be built and established;
for a fire has gone out of Heshbon,
a flame from the city of Sihon.
It has devoured Ar of Moab,
The lords of the high places of the Arnon.
Woe to you, Moab!
You are undone, people of Chemosh!
He has given his sons as fugitives,
and his daughters into captivity,
to Sihon king of the Amorites.
We have shot at them.
Heshbon has perished even to Dibon.
We have laid waste even to Nophah,
Which reaches to Medeba.”
Thus Israel lives in the land of the Amorites.
Victory over Og · 21:32–35

Moses sends to spy out Jazer. They take its villages, and drive out the Amorites who are there. They turn and go up by the way of Bashan. Og the king of Bashan goes out against them, he and all his people, to battle at Edrei.
YHWH says to Moses, “Don’t fear him, for I have delivered him into your hand, with all his people, and his land. You must do to him as you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived at Heshbon.”
So they strike him, with his sons and all his people, until there are no survivors; and they possess his land.
Balak Summons Balaam · 22:1–14

The children of Israel travel, and encamp in the plains of Moab beyond the Jordan at Jericho. Balak the son of Zippor sees all that Israel has done to the Amorites. Moab is very afraid of the people, because they are many. Moab is distressed because of the children of Israel. Moab says to the elders of Midian, “Now this multitude will lick up all that is around us, as the ox licks up the grass of the field.”

Balak the son of Zippor is king of Moab at that time. He sends messengers to Balaam the son of Beor, to Pethor, which is by the River, to the land of the children of his people, to call him, saying, “Look, there is a people who came out of Egypt. Look, they cover the surface of the earth, and they are staying opposite me. Please come now therefore curse me this people; for they are too mighty for me. Perhaps I will prevail, that we may strike them, and that I may drive them out of the land; for I know that he whom you bless is blessed, and he whom you curse is cursed.”
The elders of Moab and the elders of Midian depart with the rewards of divination in their hand. They come to Balaam, and speak to him the words of Balak.
He says to them, “Lodge here this night, and I will bring you word again, as YHWH will speak to me.” The princes of Moab stay with Balaam.
God comes to Balaam, and says, “Who are these men with you?”

Balaam says to God, “Balak the son of Zippor, king of Moab, has said to me, ‘Look, the people that has come out of Egypt covers the surface of the earth. Now, come curse me them. Perhaps I will be able to fight against them, and will drive them out.’”
God says to Balaam, “You must not go with them. You must not curse the people; for they are blessed.”
Balaam rises up in the morning, and says to the princes of Balak, “Go to your land; for YHWH refuses to permit me to go with you.”
The princes of Moab rise up, and they go to Balak, and say, “Balaam refuses to come with us.”
The Second Summons · 22:15–21

Balak again sends princes, more, and more honorable than they. They come to Balaam, and say to him, “Thus says Balak the son of Zippor, ‘Please let nothing hinder you from coming to me, for I will promote you to very great honor, and whatever you say to me I will do. Please come therefore, and curse this people for me.’”

Balaam answers the servants of Balak, “If Balak would give me his house full of silver and gold, I can’t go beyond the word of YHWH my God, to do less or more. Now therefore please stay here tonight as well, that I may know what else YHWH will speak to me.”
God comes to Balaam at night, and says to him, “If the men have come to call you, rise up, go with them; but only the word which I speak to you, that you must do.”
Balaam rises up in the morning, and saddles his donkey, and goes with the princes of Moab.
Balaam’s Donkey · 22:22–35

God’s anger burned because he goes; and YHWH’s angel places himself in the way for an adversary against him. Now he is riding on his donkey, and his two servants are with him. The donkey sees YHWH’s angel standing in the way, with his sword drawn in his hand; and the donkey turns out of the path, and goes into the field. Balaam strikes the donkey, to turn her into the path. Then YHWH’s angel stands in a narrow path between the vineyards, a wall being on this side, and a wall on that side. The donkey sees YHWH’s angel, and she thrusts herself to the wall, and crushes Balaam’s foot against the wall. He strikes her again.

YHWH’s angel goes further, and stands in a narrow place, where there is no way to turn either to the right hand or to the left. The donkey sees YHWH’s angel, and she lies down under Balaam. Balaam’s anger burns, and he strikes the donkey with his staff.
YHWH opens the mouth of the donkey, and she says to Balaam, “What have I done to you, that you have struck me these three times?”
Balaam says to the donkey, “Because you have mocked me, I wish there were a sword in my hand, for now I would have killed you.”
The donkey says to Balaam, “Am I not your donkey, on which you have ridden all your life long until today? Was I ever in the habit of doing so to you?”
He says, “No.”

Then YHWH opens the eyes of Balaam, and he sees YHWH’s angel standing in the way, with his sword drawn in his hand; and he bows his head, and falls on his face. YHWH’s angel says to him, “Why have you struck your donkey these three times? Look, I have come out as an adversary, because your way is perverse before me. The donkey saw me, and turned away before me these three times. Unless she had turned away from me, surely now I would have killed you, and saved her alive.”
Balaam says to YHWH’s angel, “I have sinned; for I didn’t know that you stood in the way against me. Now therefore, if it displeases you, I will go back again.”
YHWH’s angel says to Balaam, “Go with the men; but only the word that I will speak to you, that you must speak.”
So Balaam goes with the princes of Balak.
Balaam Arrives in Moab · 22:36–41

When Balak hears that Balaam has come, he goes out to meet him to the City of Moab, which is on the border of the Arnon, which is in the utmost part of the border. Balak says to Balaam, “Didn’t I earnestly send for you to summon you? Why didn’t you come to me? Am I not able indeed to promote you to honor?”
Balaam says to Balak, “Look, I have come to you. Have I now any power at all to speak anything? The word that God puts in my mouth, that should I speak.”

Balaam goes with Balak, and they come to Kiriath Huzoth. Balak sacrifices cattle and sheep, and sends to Balaam, and to the princes who are with him. In the morning, Balak takes Balaam, and brings him up into the high places of Baal; and he sees from there part of the people.
The First Oracle · 23:1–12
Balaam says to Balak, “Build here seven altars for me, and prepare here seven bulls and seven rams for me.”

Balak does as Balaam has spoken; and Balak and Balaam offer on every altar a bull and a ram. Balaam says to Balak, “Stand by your burnt offering, and I will go. Perhaps YHWH will come to meet me. Whatever he shows me I will tell you.”
He goes to a bare height. God meets Balaam, and he says to him, “I have prepared the seven altars, and I have offered up a bull and a ram on every altar.”
YHWH puts a word in Balaam’s mouth, and says, “Return to Balak, and thus you must speak.”
He returns to him, and look, he is standing by his burnt offering, he, and all the princes of Moab. He takes up his parable, and says,
“From Aram has Balak brought me,
the king of Moab from the mountains of the East.
Come, curse Jacob for me.
Come, defy Israel.
How should I curse whom God has not cursed?
How should I defy whom YHWH has not defied?
For from the top of the rocks I see him.
From the hills I see him.
Look, it is a people that dwells alone,
and will not be listed among the nations.
Who can count the dust of Jacob,
or count the fourth part of Israel?
Let me die the death of the righteous!
Let my last end be like his!”
Balak says to Balaam, “What have you done to me? I took you to curse my enemies, and look, you have blessed them altogether.”
He answers and says, “Must I not take heed to speak that which YHWH puts in my mouth?”
The Second Oracle · 23:13–26
Balak says to him, “Please come with me to another place, where you may see them. You will see just part of them, and will not see them all. Curse them from there for me.”

He takes him into the field of Zophim, to the top of Pisgah, and builds seven altars, and offers up a bull and a ram on every altar. He says to Balak, “Stand here by your burnt offering, while I meet God over there.”
YHWH meets Balaam, and puts a word in his mouth, and says, “Return to Balak, and say this.”
He comes to him, and look, he is standing by his burnt offering, and the princes of Moab with him. Balak says to him, “What has YHWH spoken?”
He takes up his parable, and says,
“Rise up, Balak, and hear!
Listen to me, you son of Zippor.
God is not a man, that he should lie,
nor a son of man, that he should repent.
Has he said, and will he not do it?
Or has he spoken, and will he not make it good?
Look, I have received a command to bless.
He has blessed, and I can’t reverse it.
He has not seen iniquity in Jacob.
Neither has he seen perverseness in Israel.
YHWH his God is with him.
The shout of a king is among them.
God brings them out of Egypt.
He has as it were the strength of the wild ox.
Surely there is no enchantment with Jacob;
Neither is there any divination with Israel.
Now it will be said of Jacob and of Israel,
‘What has God done!’
Look, the people rises up as a lioness.
As a lion he lifts himself up.
He must not lie down until he eats of the prey,
and drinks the blood of the slain.”
Balak says to Balaam, “Neither curse them at all, nor bless them at all.”
But Balaam answers Balak, “Didn’t I tell you, saying, ‘All that YHWH speaks, that I must do?’”
Toward a Third Vantage Point · 23:27–30
Balak says to Balaam, “Come now, I will take you to another place; perhaps it will please God that you may curse them for me from there.”
Balak takes Balaam to the top of Peor, that looks down on the desert. Balaam says to Balak, “Build seven altars for me here, and prepare seven bulls and seven rams for me here.”
Balak does as Balaam has said, and offers up a bull and a ram on every altar.
The Third Oracle · 24:1–9

When Balaam sees that it pleases YHWH to bless Israel, he doesn’t go, as at the other times, to meet with enchantments, but he sets his face toward the wilderness. Balaam lifts up his eyes, and he sees Israel dwelling according to their tribes; and the Spirit of God comes on him. He takes up his parable, and says,
“Balaam the son of Beor says,
the man whose eyes are open says;
he says, who hears the words of God,
who sees the vision of the Almighty,
falling down, and having his eyes open:
How goodly are your tents, Jacob,
and your tents, Israel!
As valleys they are spread out,
as gardens by the riverside,
as aloes which YHWH has planted,
as cedar trees beside the waters.
Water will flow from his buckets.
His seed will be in many waters.
His king will be higher than Agag.
His kingdom will be exalted.
God brings him out of Egypt.
He has as it were the strength of the wild ox.
He must eat up the nations his adversaries,
will break their bones in pieces,
and pierce them with his arrows.
He couched, he lay down as a lion,
as a lioness; who will rouse him up?
Everyone who blesses you is blessed.
Everyone who curses you is cursed.”
Balak’s Fury · 24:10–14

Balak’s anger burns against Balaam, and he strikes his hands together. Balak says to Balaam, “I called you to curse my enemies, and, look, you have altogether blessed them these three times. Therefore, flee to your place, now! I thought to promote you to great honor; but, look, YHWH has kept you back from honor.”

Balaam says to Balak, “Didn’t I also tell your messengers whom you sent to me, saying, ‘If Balak would give me his house full of silver and gold, I can’t go beyond YHWH’s word, to do either good or bad from my own mind. I will say what YHWH says’? Now, look, I go to my people. Come, I will inform you what this people will do to your people in the latter days.”
The Star Oracle · 24:15–19
He takes up his parable, and says,
“Balaam the son of Beor says,
the man whose eyes are open says;
he says, who hears the words of God,
knows the knowledge of the Most High,
and who sees the vision of the Almighty,
Falling down, and having his eyes open:
I see him, but not now.
I see him, but not near.
A star will come out of Jacob.
A scepter will rise out of Israel,
and will strike through the corners of Moab,
and break down all the sons of Sheth.
Edom will be a possession.
Seir, his enemies, also will be a possession,
while Israel does valiantly.
Out of Jacob will one have dominion,
and will destroy the remnant from the city.”
Three Final Words · 24:20–25
He looks at Amalek, and takes up his parable, and says,
“Amalek was the first of the nations,
But his latter end will come to destruction.”
He looks at the Kenite, and takes up his parable, and says,
“Your dwelling place is strong.
Your nest is set in the rock.
Nevertheless Kain will be wasted,
until Asshur carries you away captive.”
He takes up his parable, and says,
“Alas, who will live when God does this?
But ships will come from the coast of Kittim.
They must afflict Asshur, and will afflict Eber.
He also will come to destruction.”
Balaam rises up, and goes and returns to his place; and Balak also goes his way.
Israel Joins Baal of Peor · 25:1–5

Israel stays in Shittim; and the people begin to play the prostitute with the daughters of Moab; for they call the people to the sacrifices of their gods. The people eat and bow down to their gods. Israel joins himself to Baal Peor. YHWH’s anger burns against Israel. YHWH says to Moses, “Take all the chiefs of the people, and hang them up to YHWH before the sun, that the fierce anger of YHWH may turn away from Israel.”
Moses says to the judges of Israel, “Everyone kill his men who have joined themselves to Baal Peor.”
Phinehas and the Plague · 25:6–18

Look, one of the children of Israel comes and brings to his brothers a Midianite woman in the sight of Moses, and in the sight of all the congregation of the children of Israel, while they are weeping at the door of the Tent of Meeting. When Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, sees it, he rises up from the middle of the congregation, and takes a spear in his hand. He goes after the man of Israel into the pavilion, and thrusts both of them through, the man of Israel, and the woman through her body. So the plague is stayed from the children of Israel. Those who die by the plague are twenty-four thousand.

YHWH speaks to Moses, saying, “Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, has turned my wrath away from the children of Israel, in that he was jealous with my jealousy among them, so that I didn’t consume the children of Israel in my jealousy. Therefore say, ‘Look, I give to him my covenant of peace. It will be to him, and to his offspring after him, the covenant of an everlasting priesthood, because he was jealous for his God, and made atonement for the children of Israel.’”

Now the name of the man of Israel that is slain, who is slain with the Midianite woman, is Zimri, the son of Salu, a prince of a fathers’ house among the Simeonites. The name of the Midianite woman who is slain is Cozbi, the daughter of Zur. He is head of the people of a fathers’ house in Midian.

YHWH speaks to Moses, saying, “Harass the Midianites, and strike them, for they harassed you with their wiles, wherein they have deceived you in the matter of Peor, and in the incident regarding Cozbi, the daughter of the prince of Midian, their sister, who was slain on the day of the plague in the matter of Peor.”
The Second Census Commanded · 26:1–4

After the plague, YHWH speaks to Moses and to Eleazar the son of Aaron the priest, saying, “Take a census of all the congregation of the children of Israel, from twenty years old and upward, by their fathers’ houses, all who are able to go out to war in Israel.” Moses and Eleazar the priest speak with them in the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho, saying, “Take a census, from twenty years old and upward; as YHWH commanded Moses and the children of Israel.”
These are those that come out of the land of Egypt.
The Muster by Tribe · 26:5–51

Reuben, the firstborn of Israel; the sons of Reuben: of Hanoch, the family of the Hanochites; of Pallu, the family of the Palluites; of Hezron, the family of the Hezronites; of Carmi, the family of the Carmites. These are the families of the Reubenites; and those who are counted of them are forty-three thousand seven hundred thirty. The sons of Pallu: Eliab. The sons of Eliab: Nemuel, and Dathan, and Abiram. These are that Dathan and Abiram, who are called by the congregation, who rebels against Moses and against Aaron in the company of Korah, when they rebel against YHWH, and the earth opens its mouth, and swallows them up together with Korah, when that company dies; at the time the fire devours two hundred fifty men, and they become a sign. Notwithstanding, the sons of Korah don’t die. The sons of Simeon after their families: of Nemuel, the family of the Nemuelites; of Jamin, the family of the Jaminites; of Jachin, the family of the Jachinites; of Zerah, the family of the Zerahites; of Shaul, the family of the Shaulites. These are the families of the Simeonites, twenty-two thousand two hundred. The sons of Gad after their families: of Zephon, the family of the Zephonites; of Haggi, the family of the Haggites; of Shuni, the family of the Shunites; of Ozni, the family of the Oznites; of Eri, the family of the Erites; of Arod, the family of the Arodites; of Areli, the family of the Arelites. These are the families of the sons of Gad according to those who are counted of them, forty thousand and five hundred. The sons of Judah: Er and Onan. Er and Onan die in the land of Canaan. The sons of Judah after their families are: of Shelah, the family of the Shelanites; of Perez, the family of the Perezites; of Zerah, the family of the Zerahites. The sons of Perez are: of Hezron, the family of the Hezronites; of Hamul, the family of the Hamulites. These are the families of Judah according to those who are counted of them, seventy-six thousand five hundred. The sons of Issachar after their families: of Tola, the family of the Tolaites; of Puvah, the family of the Punites; of Jashub, the family of the Jashubites; of Shimron, the family of the Shimronites. These are the families of Issachar according to those who are counted of them, sixty-four thousand three hundred. The sons of Zebulun after their families: of Sered, the family of the Seredites; of Elon, the family of the Elonites; of Jahleel, the family of the Jahleelites. These are the families of the Zebulunites according to those who are counted of them, sixty thousand five hundred. The sons of Joseph after their families: Manasseh and Ephraim. The sons of Manasseh: of Machir, the family of the Machirites; and Machir become the father of Gilead; of Gilead, the family of the Gileadites. These are the sons of Gilead: of Iezer, the family of the Iezerites; of Helek, the family of the Helekites; and Asriel, the family of the Asrielites; and Shechem, the family of the Shechemites; and Shemida, the family of the Shemidaites; and Hepher, the family of the Hepherites. Zelophehad the son of Hepher has no sons, but daughters: and the names of the daughters of Zelophehad are Mahlah, and Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah. These are the families of Manasseh. Those who are counted of them are fifty-two thousand seven hundred. These are the sons of Ephraim after their families: of Shuthelah, the family of the Shuthelahites; of Becher, the family of the Becherites; of Tahan, the family of the Tahanites. These are the sons of Shuthelah: of Eran, the family of the Eranites. These are the families of the sons of Ephraim according to those who are counted of them, thirty-two thousand five hundred. These are the sons of Joseph after their families. The sons of Benjamin after their families: of Bela, the family of the Belaites; of Ashbel, the family of the Ashbelites; of Ahiram, the family of the Ahiramites; of Shephupham, the family of the Shuphamites; of Hupham, the family of the Huphamites. The sons of Bela are Ard and Naaman: the family of the Ardites; of Naaman, the family of the Naamites. These are the sons of Benjamin after their families; and those who are counted of them are forty-five thousand six hundred. These are the sons of Dan after their families: of Shuham, the family of the Shuhamites. These are the families of Dan after their families. All the families of the Shuhamites, according to those who are counted of them, are sixty-four thousand four hundred. The sons of Asher after their families: of Imnah, the family of the Imnites; of Ishvi, the family of the Ishvites; of Beriah, the family of the Berites. Of the sons of Beriah: of Heber, the family of the Heberites; of Malchiel, the family of the Malchielites. The name of the daughter of Asher is Serah. These are the families of the sons of Asher according to those who are counted of them, fifty-three thousand and four hundred. The sons of Naphtali after their families: of Jahzeel, the family of the Jahzeelites; of Guni, the family of the Gunites; of Jezer, the family of the Jezerites; of Shillem, the family of the Shillemites. These are the families of Naphtali according to their families; and those who are counted of them are forty-five thousand four hundred. These are those who are counted of the children of Israel, six hundred one thousand seven hundred thirty.
The Apportionment of the Land · 26:52–56

YHWH speaks to Moses, saying, “To these the land will be divided for an inheritance according to the number of names. To the more you must give the more inheritance, and to the fewer you must give the less inheritance. To everyone according to those who were counted of him will his inheritance be given. Notwithstanding, the land will be divided by lot. According to the names of the tribes of their fathers they will inherit. According to the lot will their inheritance be divided between the more and the fewer.”
The Levite Clans · 26:57–62

These are those who are counted of the Levites after their families: of Gershon, the family of the Gershonites; of Kohath, the family of the Kohathites; of Merari, the family of the Merarites. These are the families of Levi: the family of the Libnites, the family of the Hebronites, the family of the Mahlites, the family of the Mushites, the family of the Korahites. Kohath becomes the father of Amram. The name of Amram’s wife is Jochebed, the daughter of Levi, who is born to Levi in Egypt. She bears to Amram Aaron and Moses, and Miriam their sister. To Aaron are born Nadab and Abihu, Eleazar and Ithamar. Nadab and Abihu die when they offer strange fire before YHWH. Those who are counted of them are twenty-three thousand, every male from a month old and upward; for they are not counted among the children of Israel, because there is no inheritance given them among the children of Israel.
The Generation Passes · 26:63–65

These are those who are counted by Moses and Eleazar the priest, who count the children of Israel in the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho. But among these there is not a man of them who are counted by Moses and Aaron the priest, who count the children of Israel in the wilderness of Sinai. For YHWH have said of them, “They will surely die in the wilderness.” There is not a man left of them, except Caleb the son of Jephunneh, and Joshua the son of Nun.
The Daughters of Zelophehad · 27:1–11

Then the daughters of Zelophehad, the son of Hepher, the son of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh, of the families of Manasseh the son of Joseph come near. These are the names of his daughters: Mahlah, Noah, and Hoglah, and Milcah, and Tirzah. They stand before Moses, and before Eleazar the priest, and before the princes and all the congregation, at the door of the Tent of Meeting, saying, “Our father died in the wilderness. He was not among the company of those who gathered themselves together against YHWH in the company of Korah, but he died in his own sin. He had no sons. Why should the name of our father be taken away from among his family, because he had no son? Give to us a possession among the brothers of our father.”

Moses brings their cause before YHWH. YHWH speaks to Moses, saying, “The daughters of Zelophehad speak right. You will surely give them a possession of an inheritance among their father’s brothers. You must cause the inheritance of their father to pass to them. You must speak to the children of Israel, saying, ‘If a man dies, and has no son, then you must cause his inheritance to pass to his daughter. If he has no daughter, then you must give his inheritance to his brothers. If he has no brothers, then you must give his inheritance to his father’s brothers. If his father has no brothers, then you must give his inheritance to his kinsman who is next to him of his family, and he will possess it. This will be a statute and ordinance for the children of Israel, as YHWH commanded Moses.’”
Moses Views the Land · 27:12–17

YHWH says to Moses, “Go up into this mountain of Abarim, and see the land which I have given to the children of Israel. When you have seen it, you also will be gathered to your people, as Aaron your brother was gathered; because in the strife of the congregation, you rebelled against my word in the wilderness of Zin, to honor me as holy at the waters before their eyes.” (These are the waters of Meribah of Kadesh in the wilderness of Zin.)

Moses speaks to YHWH, saying, “Let YHWH, the God of the spirits of all flesh, appoint a man over the congregation, who may go out before them, and who may come in before them, and who may lead them out, and who may bring them in; that the congregation of YHWH may not be as sheep which have no shepherd.”
Joshua Commissioned · 27:18–23

YHWH says to Moses, “Take Joshua the son of Nun, a man in whom is the Spirit, and lay your hand on him. Set him before Eleazar the priest, and before all the congregation; and commission him in their sight. You must give authority to him, that all the congregation of the children of Israel may obey. He must stand before Eleazar the priest, who will inquire for him by the judgment of the Urim before YHWH. At his word they must go out, and at his word they will come in, both he, and all the children of Israel with him, even all the congregation.”
Moses does as YHWH commands him. He takes Joshua, and sets him before Eleazar the priest, and before all the congregation. He lays his hands on him, and commissions him, as YHWH speaks by Moses.
Daily and Sabbath Offerings · 28:1–10

YHWH speaks to Moses, saying, “Command the children of Israel, and tell them, ‘See that you present my offering, my food for my offerings made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to me, in their due season.’ You must tell them, ‘This is the offering made by fire which you must offer to YHWH: male lambs a year old without defect, two day by day, for a continual burnt offering. You must offer the one lamb in the morning, and you must offer the other lamb at evening; with one tenth of an ephah of fine flour for a meal offering, mixed with the fourth part of a hin of beaten oil. It is a continual burnt offering, which was ordained in Mount Sinai for a pleasant aroma, an offering made by fire to YHWH. Its drink offering will be the fourth part of a hin for the one lamb. You must pour out a drink offering of strong drink to YHWH in the holy place. The other lamb you must offer at evening. As the meal offering of the morning, and as its drink offering, you must offer it, an offering made by fire, for a pleasant aroma to YHWH.

“‘On the Sabbath day, you must offer two male lambs a year old without defect, and two tenths of an ephah of fine flour for a meal offering, mixed with oil, and its drink offering: this is the burnt offering of every Sabbath, besides the continual burnt offering, and its drink offering.
The Monthly Offering · 28:11–15

“‘In the beginnings of your months, you must offer a burnt offering to YHWH: two young bulls, and one ram, seven male lambs a year old without defect; and three tenths of an ephah of fine flour for a meal offering, mixed with oil, for each bull; and two tenth parts of fine flour for a meal offering, mixed with oil, for the one ram; and one tenth part of fine flour mixed with oil for a meal offering to every lamb; for a burnt offering of a pleasant aroma, an offering made by fire to YHWH. Their drink offerings will be half a hin of wine for a bull, and the third part of a hin for the ram, and the fourth part of a hin for a lamb. This is the burnt offering of every month throughout the months of the year. One male goat for a sin offering to YHWH; it will be offered besides the continual burnt offering, and its drink offering.
Passover and Unleavened Bread · 28:16–25

“‘In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, is YHWH’s Passover. On the fifteenth day of this month will be a feast. Unleavened bread will be eaten for seven days. In the first day will be a holy convocation. You must do no regular work; but you must offer an offering made by fire, a burnt offering to YHWH: two young bulls, and one ram, and seven male lambs a year old; they will be to you without defect; and their meal offering, fine flour mixed with oil. You must offer three tenths for a bull, and two tenths for the ram. You must offer one tenth for every lamb of the seven lambs; and one male goat for a sin offering, to make atonement for you. You must offer these besides the burnt offering of the morning, which is for a continual burnt offering. In this way you must offer daily, for seven days, the food of the offering made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to YHWH. It will be offered in addition to the continual burnt offering, and its drink offering. On the seventh day you must have a holy convocation. You must do no regular work.
The Festival of Weeks · 28:26–31

“‘Also in the day of the first fruits, when you offer a new meal offering to YHWH in your feast of weeks, you must have a holy convocation. You must do no regular work; but you must offer a burnt offering for a pleasant aroma to YHWH: two young bulls, one ram, seven male lambs a year old; and their meal offering, fine flour mixed with oil, three tenths for each bull, two tenths for the one ram, one tenth for every lamb of the seven lambs; one male goat, to make atonement for you. Besides the continual burnt offering, and its meal offering, you must offer them and their drink offerings. See that they are without defect.
The Day of Trumpet Blasts · 29:1–6

“‘In the seventh month, on the first day of the month, you must have a holy convocation; you must do no regular work: it is a day of blowing of trumpets to you. You must offer a burnt offering for a pleasant aroma to YHWH: one young bull, one ram, seven male lambs a year old without defect; and their meal offering, fine flour mixed with oil, three tenths for the bull, two tenths for the ram, and one tenth for every lamb of the seven lambs; and one male goat for a sin offering, to make atonement for you; besides the burnt offering of the new moon, and its meal offering, and the continual burnt offering and its meal offering, and their drink offerings, according to their ordinance, for a pleasant aroma, an offering made by fire to YHWH.
The Day of Atonement · 29:7–11

“‘On the tenth day of this seventh month you must have a holy convocation. You must afflict your souls. “‘So you must not pollute the land in which you are; for blood pollutes the land. No atonement can be made for the land for the blood that is shed in it, but by the blood of him who shed it. You must not defile the land which you inhabit, in the middle of which I dwell; for I, YHWH, dwell in the middle of the children of Israel.’”
The Concern of Zelophehad’s Clan · 36:1–4

The heads of the fathers’ households of the family of the children of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh, of the families of the sons of Joseph, come near, and speak before Moses, and before the princes, the heads of the fathers’ households of the children of Israel. They say, “YHWH commanded my lord to give the land for inheritance by lot to the children of Israel. My lord was commanded by YHWH to give the inheritance of Zelophehad our brother to his daughters. If they are married to any of the sons of the other tribes of the children of Israel, then will their inheritance be taken away from the inheritance of our fathers, and will be added to the inheritance of the tribe to which they must belong. So will it be taken away from the lot of our inheritance. When the jubilee of the children of Israel will be, then will their inheritance be added to the inheritance of the tribe to which they must belong. So their inheritance will be taken away from the inheritance of the tribe of our fathers.”
The Lord’s Ruling · 36:5–9

Moses commands the children of Israel according to YHWH’s word, saying, “The tribe of the sons of Joseph speaks right. This is the thing which YHWH does command concerning the daughters of Zelophehad, saying, ‘Let them be married to whom they think best; only they must marry into the family of the tribe of their father. So will no inheritance of the children of Israel move from tribe to tribe; for the children of Israel will all keep the inheritance of the tribe of his fathers. Every daughter who possesses an inheritance in any tribe of the children of Israel will be wife to one of the family of the tribe of her father, that the children of Israel may each possess the inheritance of his fathers. So will no inheritance move from one tribe to another tribe; for the tribes of the children of Israel will each keep his own inheritance.’”
The Daughters Obey · 36:10–13

The daughters of Zelophehad do as YHWH commands Moses: for Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Noah, the daughters of Zelophehad, are married to their father’s brothers’ sons. They are married into the families of the sons of Manasseh the son of Joseph. Their inheritance remains in the tribe of the family of their father. These are the commandments and the ordinances which YHWH commanded by Moses to the children of Israel in the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho.
Prologue · 1:1–5

These are the words which Moses speaks to all Israel beyond the Jordan in the wilderness, in the Arabah over against Suf, between Paran, Tophel, Laban, Hazeroth, and Dizahab. It is eleven days’ journey from Horeb by the way of Mount Seir to Kadesh Barnea. In the fortieth year, in the eleventh month, on the first day of the month, Moses speaks to the children of Israel, according to all that YHWH has given him in commandment to them; after he has struck Sihon the king of the Amorites, who live in Heshbon, and Og the king of Bashan, who lives in Ashtaroth, at Edrei. Beyond the Jordan, in the land of Moab, Moses begins to declare this law, saying,
The Command to Leave Horeb · 1:6–8

“YHWH our God spoke to us in Horeb, saying, ‘You have lived long enough at this mountain. Turn, and take your journey, and go to the hill country of the Amorites, and to all the places near there, in the Arabah, in the hill country, in the lowland, in the South, by the seashore, in the land of the Canaanites, and in Lebanon, as far as the great river, the river Euphrates. Look, I have set the land before you. Go in and possess the land which YHWH swore to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give to them and to their offspring after them.’”
Leaders Appointed · 1:9–18

I speak to you at that time, saying, “I am not able to bear you myself alone. YHWH your God has multiplied you, and look, you are today as the stars of the sky for multitude. YHWH, the God of your fathers, make you a thousand times as many as you are, and bless you, as he has promised you! How can I myself alone bear your problems, your burdens, and your strife? Take wise men of understanding and well known according to your tribes, and I will make them heads over you.”

You answer me, and say, “The thing which you have spoken is good to do.” So I take the heads of your tribes, wise men, and known, and make them heads over you, captains of thousands, and captains of hundreds, and captains of fifties, and captains of tens, and officers, according to your tribes. I command your judges at that time, saying, “Hear cases between your brothers, and judge righteously between a man and his brother, and the foreigner who is living with him. You must not show partiality in judgment; you will hear the small and the great alike. You must not be afraid of the face of man, for the judgment is God’s. The case that is too hard for you, you must bring to me, and I will hear it.” I command you at that time all the things which you should do.
Scouts Sent to Kadesh · 1:19–25

We travel from Horeb, and go through all that great and terrible wilderness which you see, by the way to the hill country of the Amorites, as YHWH our God commands us; and we come to Kadesh Barnea. I say to you, “You have come to the hill country of the Amorites, which YHWH our God gives to us. Look, YHWH your God has set the land before you. Go up, take possession, as YHWH, the God of your fathers, has spoken to you. Don’t be afraid, neither be dismayed.”

You come near to me, everyone of you, and say, “Let us send men before us, that they may search the land for us, and bring us word again of the way by which we must go up, and the cities to which we will come.”

The thing pleases me well. I take twelve men of you, one man for every tribe. They turn and go up into the hill country, and come to the valley of Eshcol, and spy it out. They take some of the fruit of the land in their hands, and bring it down to us, and bring us word again, and say, “It is a good land which YHWH our God gives to us.”
Israel Rebels · 1:26–33

Yet you wouldn’t go up, but rebelled against the commandment of YHWH your God. You murmur in your tents, and say, “Because YHWH hated us, he has brought us out of the land of Egypt, to deliver us into the hand of the Amorites, to destroy us. Where are we going up? Our brothers have made our heart melt, saying, ‘The people are greater and taller than we. The cities are great and fortified up to the sky. Moreover we have seen the sons of the Anakim there!’”

Then I say to you, “Don’t dread, neither be afraid of them. YHWH your God who goes before you, he will fight for you, according to all that he did for you in Egypt before your eyes, and in the wilderness, where you have seen how that YHWH your God bore you, as a man does bear his son, in all the way that you went, until you came to this place.”

Yet in this thing you don’t believe YHWH your God, who goes before you on the way, to seek out a place for you to pitch your tents in, in fire by night, to show you by what way you should go, and in the cloud by day.
YHWH's Judgment · 1:34–40

YHWH hears the voice of your words, and is angry, and swore, saying, “Surely not one of these men of this evil generation will see the good land, which I swore to give to your fathers, except Caleb the son of Jephunneh. He will see it. I will give the land that he has trodden on to him, and to his children, because he has wholly followed YHWH.”

Also YHWH is angry with me for your sakes, saying, “You also will not go in there. Joshua the son of Nun, who stands before you, will go in there. Encourage him, for he must cause Israel to inherit it. Moreover your little ones, whom you said would be captured or killed, and your children, who today have no knowledge of good or evil, will go in there. I will give it to them, and they will possess it. But as for you, turn, and take your journey into the wilderness by the way to the Red Sea.”
The Failed Attempt · 1:41–46

Then you answer and say to me, “We have sinned against YHWH, we will go up and fight, according to all that YHWH our God commanded us.” Every man of you put on his weapons of war, and presumes to go up into the hill country.
YHWH says to me, “Tell them, ‘Don’t go up and don’t fight; for I am not among you; lest you be struck before your enemies.’”

So I speak to you, and you don’t listen; but you rebel against the commandment of YHWH, and are presumptuous, and go up into the hill country. The Amorites, who live in that hill country, come out against you, and chase you, as bees do, and beat you down in Seir, even to Hormah. You return and weep before YHWH; but YHWH doesn’t listen to your voice, nor turn his ear to you. So you stay in Kadesh many days, according to the days that you remain.
Circling Seir · 2:1–8
Then we turn, and take our journey into the wilderness by the way to the Red Sea, as YHWH speaks to me; and we encircle Mount Seir many days.

YHWH speaks to me, saying, “You have encircled this mountain long enough. Turn northward. Command the people, saying, ‘You are to pass through the border of your brothers the children of Esau, who dwell in Seir; and they will be afraid of you. Therefore be careful. Don’t contend with them; for I will not give you any of their land, no, not so much as for the sole of the foot to tread on; because I have given Mount Seir to Esau for a possession. You must purchase food from them for money, that you may eat. You must also buy water from them for money, that you may drink.’”
For YHWH your God has blessed you in all the work of your hand. He has known your walking through this great wilderness. These forty years, YHWH your God has been with you. You have lacked nothing.
So we pass by from our brothers the children of Esau, who dwell in Seir, from the way of the Arabah from Elath and from Ezion Geber. We turn and passed by the way of the wilderness of Moab.
Past Moab · 2:9–15
YHWH says to me, “Don’t bother Moab, neither contend with them in battle; for I will not give you any of his land for a possession; because I have given Ar to the children of Lot for a possession.”

(The Emim lives therein before, a people great, and many, and tall, as the Anakim. These also are considered to be Rephaim, as the Anakim; but the Moabites call them Emim. The Horites also live in Seir before, but the children of Esau succeed them. They destroy them from before them, and live in their place; as Israel does to the land of his possession, which YHWH gives to them.)
“Now rise up, and cross over the brook Zered.” We go over the brook Zered.

The days in which we come from Kadesh Barnea, until we have come over the brook Zered, are thirty-eight years; until all the generation of the men of war are consumed from the middle of the camp, as YHWH swears to them. Moreover YHWH’s hand is against them, to destroy them from the middle of the camp, until they are consumed.
Past Ammon · 2:16–25

So, when all the men of war are consumed and dead from among the people, YHWH speaks to me, saying, “You are to pass over Ar, the border of Moab, today. When you come near the border of the children of Ammon, don’t bother them, nor contend with them; for I will not give you any of the land of the children of Ammon for a possession; because I have given it to the children of Lot for a possession.”

(That also is considered a land of Rephaim: Rephaim lives there before; but the Ammonites call them Zamzummim, a great people, many, and tall, as the Anakim; but YHWH destroy them before them; and they succeed them, and live in their place; as he does for the children of Esau, who dwell in Seir, when he destroys the Horites from before them; and they succeed them, and live in their place even to this day: and the Avvim, who lives in villages as far as Gaza, the Caphtorim, who comes out of Caphtor, destroys them, and lives in their place.)

“Rise up, take your journey, and pass over the valley of the Arnon: look, I have given into your hand Sihon the Amorite, king of Heshbon, and his land; begin to possess it, and contend with him in battle. Today I will begin to put the dread of you and the fear of you on the peoples who are under the whole sky, who will hear the report of you, and will tremble, and be in anguish because of you.”
Sihon Defeated · 2:26–37

I send messengers out of the wilderness of Kedemoth to Sihon king of Heshbon with words of peace, saying, “Let me pass through your land. I will go along by the highway, I will turn neither to the right hand nor to the left. You must sell me food for money, that I may eat; and give me water for money, that I may drink. Just let me pass through on my feet, as the children of Esau who dwell in Seir, and the Moabites who dwell in Ar, did to me; until I pass over the Jordan into the land which YHWH our God gives us.” But Sihon king of Heshbon would not let us pass by him; for YHWH your God hardens his spirit, and makes his heart obstinate, that he might deliver him into your hand, as it is today.

YHWH says to me, “Look, I have begun to deliver up Sihon and his land before you. Begin to possess, that you may inherit his land.” Then Sihon comes out against us, he and all his people, to battle at Jahaz. YHWH our God delivers him up before us; and we strike him, his sons, and all his people. We take all his cities at that time, and utterly destroy every inhabited city, with the women and the little ones. We leave no one remaining. Only the livestock we take for plunder for ourselves, with the plunder of the cities which we have taken. From Aroer, which is on the edge of the valley of the Arnon, and the city that is in the valley, even to Gilead, there is not a city too high for us. YHWH our God delivers up all before us. Only to the land of the children of Ammon you don’t come near; all the banks of the river Jabbok, and the cities of the hill country, and wherever YHWH our God forbid us.
Og Defeated · 3:1–11

Then we turn, and go up the way to Bashan. Og the king of Bashan comes out against us, he and all his people, to battle at Edrei. YHWH says to me, “Don’t fear him; for I have delivered him, with all his people, and his land, into your hand. You must do to him as you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived at Heshbon.”

So YHWH our God delivers into our hand Og also, the king of Bashan, and all his people. We strike him until no one is left to him remaining. We take all his cities at that time. There is not a city which we don’t take from them; sixty cities, all the region of Argob, the kingdom of Og in Bashan. All these are cities fortified with high walls, gates, and bars; besides a great many villages without walls. We utterly destroy them, as we do to Sihon king of Heshbon, utterly destroying every inhabited city, with the women and the little ones. But all the livestock, and the plunder of the cities, we take for plunder for ourselves. We take the land at that time out of the hand of the two kings of the Amorites who are beyond the Jordan, from the valley of the Arnon to Mount Hermon. (The Sidonians call Hermon Sirion, and the Amorites call it Senir.) We take all the cities of the plain, and all Gilead, and all Bashan, to Salecah and Edrei, cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan. (For only Og king of Bashan remains of the remnant of the Rephaim. Look, his bedstead is a bedstead of iron. Isn’t it in Rabbah of the children of Ammon? Nine cubits are its length, and four cubits its width, after the cubit of a man.)
The Land Distributed · 3:12–20

This land we take in possession at that time: from Aroer, which is by the valley of the Arnon, and half the hill country of Gilead, and its cities, I give to the Reubenites and to the Gadites: and the rest of Gilead, and all Bashan, the kingdom of Og, I give to the half-tribe of Manasseh; all the region of Argob, even all Bashan. (The same is called the land of Rephaim. Jair the son of Manasseh takes all the region of Argob, to the border of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and calls them, even Bashan, after his own name, Havvoth Jair, to this day.) I give Gilead to Machir. To the Reubenites and to the Gadites I give from Gilead even to the valley of the Arnon, the middle of the valley, and its border, even to the river Jabbok, which is the border of the children of Ammon; the Arabah also, and the Jordan and its border, from Chinnereth even to the sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea, under the slopes of Pisgah eastward.

I command you at that time, saying, “YHWH your God has given you this land to possess it. You must pass over armed before your brothers the children of Israel, all the men of valor. But your wives, and your little ones, and your livestock, (I know that you have much livestock), will live in your cities which I have given you, until YHWH gives rest to your brothers, as to you, and they also possess the land which YHWH your God gives them beyond the Jordan. Then you must each return to his own possession, which I have given you.”
Moses Cannot Enter · 3:21–29

I command Joshua at that time, saying, “Your eyes have seen all that YHWH your God has done to these two kings. So will YHWH do to all the kingdoms where you go over. You must not fear them; for YHWH your God himself fights for you.”

I beg YHWH at that time, saying, “Lord YHWH, you have begun to show your servant your greatness, and your strong hand. For what god is there in heaven or in earth that can do works like yours, and mighty acts like yours? Please let me go over and see the good land that is beyond the Jordan, that fine mountain, and Lebanon.”

But YHWH is angry with me for your sakes, and doesn’t listen to me. YHWH says to me, “Let this satisfy you. Speak no more to me of this matter. Go up to the top of Pisgah, and lift up your eyes westward, and northward, and southward, and eastward, and see with your eyes; for you must not go over this Jordan. But commission Joshua, and encourage him, and strengthen him; for he must go over before this people, and he must cause them to inherit the land which you will see.” So we stay in the valley near Beth Peor.
Do Not Add or Take Away · 4:1–8

Now, Israel, listen to the statutes and to the ordinances, which I teach you, to do them; that you may live, and go in and possess the land which YHWH, the God of your fathers, gives you. You must not add to the word which I command you, neither will you take away from it, that you may keep the commandments of YHWH your God which I command you. Your eyes have seen what YHWH does because of Baal Peor; for all the men who follow Baal Peor, YHWH your God has destroyed them from among you. But you who are faithful to YHWH your God are all alive today. Look, I have taught you statutes and ordinances, even as YHWH my God commands me, that you should do so in the middle of the land where you go in to possess it. Keep therefore and do them; for this is your wisdom and your understanding in the sight of the peoples who will hear all these statutes and say, “Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people.” For what great nation is there, that has a god so near to them, as YHWH our God is whenever we call on him? What great nation is there, that has statutes and ordinances so righteous as all this law, which I set before you today?
Remember What You Saw · 4:9–14

Only be careful, and keep your soul diligently, lest you forget the things which your eyes see, and lest they depart from your heart all the days of your life; but make them known to your children and your children’s children; the day that you stand before YHWH your God in Horeb, when YHWH says to me, “Assemble the people to me, and I will make them hear my words, that they may learn to fear me all the days that they live on the earth, and that they may teach their children.” You come near and stand under the mountain. The mountain burns with fire to the heart of the sky, with darkness, cloud, and thick darkness. YHWH speaks to you out of the middle of the fire: you hear the voice of words, but you see no form; you only hear a voice. He declares to you his covenant, which he commands you to perform, even the ten commandments. He writes them on two stone tablets. YHWH commands me at that time to teach you statutes and ordinances, that you might do them in the land where you go over to possess it.
The Danger of Idols · 4:15–24

Be very careful, for you see no kind of form on the day that YHWH speaks to you in Horeb out of the middle of the fire, lest you corrupt yourselves, and make yourself a carved image in the form of any figure, the likeness of male or female, the likeness of any animal that is on the earth, the likeness of any winged bird that flies in the sky, the likeness of anything that creeps on the ground, the likeness of any fish that is in the water under the earth; and lest you lift up your eyes to the sky, and when you see the sun and the moon and the stars, even all the army of the sky, you are drawn away and worship them, and serve them, which YHWH your God has allotted to all the peoples under the whole sky. But YHWH has taken you, and brings you out of the iron furnace, out of Egypt, to be to him a people of inheritance, as it is today. Furthermore YHWH is angry with me for your sakes, and swears that I should not go over the Jordan, and that I should not go in to that good land, which YHWH your God gives you for an inheritance; but I must die in this land. I must not go over the Jordan; but you must go over, and possess that good land. Be careful, lest you forget the covenant of YHWH your God, which he makes with you, and make yourselves a carved image in the form of anything which YHWH your God has forbidden you. For YHWH your God is a devouring fire, a jealous God.
Scattered Among the Nations · 4:25–31

When you must father children, and children’s children, and you must have been long in the land, and will corrupt yourselves, and make a carved image in the form of anything, and will do that which is evil in YHWH your God’s sight, to provoke him to anger; I call heaven and earth to witness against you today, that you will soon utterly perish from off the land which you go over the Jordan to possess it. You will not prolong your days on it, but will utterly be destroyed. YHWH will scatter you among the peoples, and you will be left few in number among the nations, where YHWH will lead you away. There you must serve gods, the work of men’s hands, wood and stone, which neither see, nor hear, nor eat, nor smell. But from there you must seek YHWH your God, and you will find him, when you search after him with all your heart and with all your soul. When you are in oppression, and all these things have come on you, in the latter days you will return to YHWH your God, and listen to his voice. For YHWH your God is a merciful God. He will not fail you, neither destroy you, nor forget the covenant of your fathers which he swears to them.
The Incomparable God · 4:32–40

For ask now of the days that are past, which are before you, since the day that God creates man on the earth, and from the one end of the sky to the other, whether there has been anything as this great thing is, or has been heard like it? Do a people ever hear the voice of God speaking out of the middle of the fire, as you have heard, and live? Or has God tried to go and take a nation for himself from among another nation, by trials, by signs, by wonders, by war, by a mighty hand, by an outstretched arm, and by great terrors, according to all that YHWH your God does for you in Egypt before your eyes? It is shown to you so that you might know that YHWH is God. There is no one else besides him. Out of heaven he makes you to hear his voice, that he might instruct you. On earth he makes you to see his great fire; and you hear his words out of the middle of the fire. Because he loves your fathers, therefore he chooses their offspring after them, and brings you out with his presence, with his great power, out of Egypt; to drive out nations from before you greater and mightier than you, to bring you in, to give you their land for an inheritance, as it is today. Know therefore today, and take it to heart, that YHWH himself is God in heaven above and on the earth beneath. There is no one else. You must keep his statutes, and his commandments, which I command you today, that it may go well with you, and with your children after you, and that you may prolong your days in the land, which YHWH your God gives you, forever.
Cities of Refuge East of the Jordan · 4:41–43

Then Moses sets apart three cities beyond the Jordan toward the sunrise; that the man slayer might flee there, who kills his neighbor unawares, and doesn’t hate him in time past; and that fleeing to one of these cities he might live: Bezer in the wilderness, in the plain country, for the Reubenites; and Ramoth in Gilead, for the Gadites; and Golan in Bashan, for the Manassites.
Introduction to the Second Address · 4:44–49

This is the law which Moses sets before the children of Israel. These are the testimonies, and the statutes, and the ordinances, which Moses speaks to the children of Israel, when they come out of Egypt, beyond the Jordan, in the valley over against Beth Peor, in the land of Sihon king of the Amorites, who live at Heshbon, whom Moses and the children of Israel strike, when they come out of Egypt. They take his land in possession, and the land of Og king of Bashan, the two kings of the Amorites, who are beyond the Jordan toward the sunrise; from Aroer, which is on the edge of the valley of the Arnon, even to Mount Sion (also called Hermon), and all the Arabah beyond the Jordan eastward, even to the sea of the Arabah, under the slopes of Pisgah.
The Covenant at Horeb · 5:1–5

Moses calls to all Israel, and says to them, “Hear, Israel, the statutes and the ordinances which I speak in your ears today, that you may learn them, and observe to do them.” YHWH our God makes a covenant with us in Horeb. YHWH doesn’t make this covenant with our fathers, but with us, even us, who are all of us here alive today. YHWH speaks with you face to face on the mountain out of the middle of the fire, (I stand between YHWH and you at that time, to show you YHWH’s word: for you are afraid because of the fire, and don’t go up onto the mountain;) saying,
The Ten Words · 5:6–21
“I am YHWH your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.
“You must have no other gods before me.

“You must not make a carved image for yourself, any likeness of what is in heaven above, or what is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth. You must not bow yourself down to them, nor serve them; for I, YHWH, your God, am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers on the children, and on the third and on the fourth generation of those who hate me; and showing steadfast love to thousands of those who love me and keep my commandments.
“You must not take the name of YHWH your God in vain: for YHWH will not hold him guiltless who takes his name in vain.

“Observe the Sabbath day, to keep it holy, as YHWH your God commanded you. You must labor six days, and do all your work; but the seventh day is a Sabbath to YHWH your God, in which you must not do any work, you, nor your son, nor your daughter, nor your male servant, nor your female servant, nor your ox, nor your donkey, nor any of your livestock, nor your stranger who is within your gates; that your male servant and your female servant may rest as well as you. You will remember that you were a servant in the land of Egypt, and YHWH your God brought you out of there by a mighty hand and by an outstretched arm. Therefore YHWH your God commanded you to keep the Sabbath day.
“Honor your father and your mother, as YHWH your God commanded you; that your days may be long, and that it may go well with you, in the land which YHWH your God gives you.
“You must not murder.
“You must not commit adultery.
“You must not steal.
“You must not give false testimony against your neighbor.

“You must not covet your neighbor’s wife. Neither will you desire your neighbor’s house, his field, or his male servant, or his female servant, his ox, or his donkey, or anything that is your neighbor’s.”
The People's Fear · 5:22–27

YHWH speaks these words to all your assembly on the mountain out of the middle of the fire, of the cloud, and of the thick darkness, with a great voice. He adds no more. He writes them on two stone tablets, and gives them to me. When you hear the voice out of the middle of the darkness, while the mountain is burning with fire, you come near to me, even all the heads of your tribes, and your elders; and you say, “Look, YHWH our God has shown us his glory and his greatness, and we have heard his voice out of the middle of the fire. We have seen today that God does speak with man, and he lives. Now therefore why should we die? For this great fire will consume us. If we hear YHWH our God’s voice any more, then we will die. For who is there of all flesh, that has heard the voice of the living God speaking out of the middle of the fire, as we have, and lived? Go near, and hear all that YHWH our God will say, and tell us all that YHWH our God tells you; and we will hear it, and do it.”
YHWH's Response · 5:28–33

YHWH hears the voice of your words, when you speak to me; and YHWH says to me, “I have heard the voice of the words of this people, which they have spoken to you. They have well said all that they have spoken. Oh that there were such a heart in them, that they would fear me, and keep all my commandments always, that it might be well with them, and with their children forever!

“Go tell them, ‘Return to your tents.’ But as for you, stand here by me, and I will tell you all the commandment, and the statutes, and the ordinances, which you must teach them, that they may do them in the land which I give them to possess it.”

You must observe to do therefore as YHWH your God has commanded you. You must not turn away to the right hand or to the left. You must walk in all the way which YHWH your God has commanded you, that you may live, and that it may be well with you, and that you may prolong your days in the land which you will possess.
The Great Commandment · 6:1–3

Now this is the commandment, the statutes, and the ordinances, which YHWH your God command to teach you, that you might do them in the land where you go over to possess it; that you might fear YHWH your God, to keep all his statutes and his commandments, which I command you; you, and your son, and your son’s son, all the days of your life; and that your days may be prolonged. Hear therefore, Israel, and observe to do it; that it may be well with you, and that you may increase mightily, as YHWH, the God of your fathers, has promised to you, in a land flowing with milk and honey.
The Shema · 6:4–9

Hear, Israel: YHWH is our God. YHWH is one. You must love YHWH your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your might. These words, which I command you today, will be on your heart; and you must teach them diligently to your children, and will talk of them when you sit in your house, and when you walk by the way, and when you lie down, and when you rise up. You must bind them for a sign on your hand, and they will be for frontlets between your eyes. You must write them on the door posts of your house, and on your gates.
Do Not Forget YHWH · 6:10–15

It will be, when YHWH your God brings you into the land which he swears to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give you, great and goodly cities, which you don’t build, and houses full of all good things, which you don’t fill, and cisterns dug out, which you don’t dig, vineyards and olive trees, which you don’t plant, and you must eat and be full; then beware lest you forget YHWH, who brings you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage. You must fear YHWH your God; and you must serve him, and will swear by his name. You must not go after other gods, of the gods of the peoples who are around you; for YHWH your God among you is a jealous God; lest the anger of YHWH your God be kindled against you, and he destroy you from off the face of the earth.
Do Not Test YHWH · 6:16–19

You must not tempt YHWH your God, as you tempt him in Massah. You must diligently keep the commandments of YHWH your God, and his testimonies, and his statutes, which he has commanded you. You must do that which is right and good in YHWH’s sight; that it may be well with you, and that you may go in and possess the good land which YHWH swears to your fathers, to thrust out all your enemies from before you, as YHWH has spoken.
Teaching the Next Generation · 6:20–25

When your son asks you in time to come, saying, “What do the testimonies, the statutes, and the ordinances, which YHWH our God has commanded you mean?” then you must tell your son, “We were Pharaoh’s slaves in Egypt. YHWH brought us out of Egypt with a mighty hand; and YHWH showed great and awesome signs and wonders on Egypt, on Pharaoh, and on all his house, before our eyes; and he brought us out from there, that he might bring us in, to give us the land which he swore to our fathers. YHWH commanded us to do all these statutes, to fear YHWH our God, for our good always, that he might preserve us alive, as we are today. It will be righteousness to us, if we observe to do all this commandment before YHWH our God, as he has commanded us.”
Drive Out the Nations · 7:1–5

When YHWH your God brings you into the land where you go to possess it, and casts out many nations before you, the Hittite, the Girgashite, the Amorite, the Canaanite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite, seven nations greater and mightier than you; and when YHWH your God delivers them up before you, and you strike them; then you must utterly destroy them. You must make no covenant with them, nor show mercy to them. You must not make marriages with them. You must not give your daughter to his son, nor will you take his daughter for your son. For he will turn away your son from following me, that they may serve other gods. So YHWH’s anger would be kindled against you, and he would destroy you quickly. But you must deal with them like this. You must break down their altars, dash their pillars in pieces, cut down their Asherah poles, and burn their engraved images with fire.
A Treasured People · 7:6–11

For you are a holy people to YHWH your God. YHWH your God has chosen you to be a people for his own possession, above all peoples who are on the face of the earth. YHWH doesn’t set his love on you, nor choose you, because you are more in number than any people; for you are the fewest of all peoples: but because YHWH loves you, and because he desires to keep the oath which he swears to your fathers, YHWH has brought you out with a mighty hand, and redeems you out of the house of bondage, from the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt. Know therefore that YHWH your God himself is God, the faithful God, who keeps covenant and steadfast love with them who love him and keep his commandments to a thousand generations, and repays those who hate him to their face, to destroy them. He will not be slack to him who hates him. He will repay him to his face. You must therefore keep the commandments, the statutes, and the ordinances, which I command you today, to do them.
The Blessings of Obedience · 7:12–16

It must happen, because you listen to these ordinances, and keep and do them, that YHWH your God will keep with you the covenant and the steadfast love which he swears to your fathers. He will love you, bless you, and multiply you. He will also bless the fruit of your body and the fruit of your ground, your grain and your new wine and your oil, the increase of your livestock and the young of your flock, in the land which he swears to your fathers to give you. You will be blessed above all peoples. There won’t be male or female barren among you, or among your livestock. YHWH will take away from you all sickness; and he will put none of the evil diseases of Egypt, which you know, on you, but will lay them on all those who hate you. You must consume all the peoples whom YHWH your God will deliver to you. Your eye will not pity them. You must not serve their gods; for that would be a snare to you.
Do Not Fear Them · 7:17–26

If you must say in your heart, “These nations are more than I; how can I dispossess them?” you must not be afraid of them. You will remember well what YHWH your God does to Pharaoh, and to all Egypt: the great trials which your eyes see, the signs, the wonders, the mighty hand, and the outstretched arm, by which YHWH your God bring you out. So will YHWH your God do to all the peoples of whom you are afraid. Moreover YHWH your God will send the hornet among them, until those who are left, and hide themselves, perish from before you. You must not be scared of them; for YHWH your God is among you, a great and awesome God. YHWH your God will cast out those nations before you little by little. You may not consume them at once, lest the animals of the field increase on you. But YHWH your God will deliver them up before you, and will confuse them with a great confusion, until they are destroyed. He will deliver their kings into your hand, and you must make their name perish from under the sky. No one will be able to stand before you, until you have destroyed them. You must burn the engraved images of their gods with fire. You must not covet the silver or the gold that is on them, nor take it for yourself, lest you be snared in it; for it is an abomination to YHWH your God. You must not bring an abomination into your house, and become a devoted thing like it. You must utterly detest it, and you must utterly abhor it; for it is a devoted thing.
Remember the Wilderness · 8:1–6

You must observe to do all the commandments which I command you today, that you may live, and multiply, and go in and possess the land which YHWH swears to your fathers. You will remember all the way which YHWH your God has led you these forty years in the wilderness, that he might humble you, to prove you, to know what is in your heart, whether you would keep his commandments, or not. He humbles you, and allows you to be hungry, and feeds you with manna, which you don’t know, neither do your fathers know; that he might teach you that man does not live by bread only, but man lives by every word that proceeds out of YHWH’s mouth. Your clothing doesn’t grow old on you, neither does your foot swell, these forty years. You must consider in your heart that as a man disciplines his son, so YHWH your God disciplines you. You must keep the commandments of YHWH your God, to walk in his ways, and to fear him.
The Good Land · 8:7–10

For YHWH your God brings you into a good land, a land of brooks of water, of springs, and underground water flowing into valleys and hills; a land of wheat and barley, and vines and fig trees and pomegranates; a land of olive trees and honey; a land in which you must eat bread without scarceness, you must not lack anything in it; a land whose stones are iron, and out of whose hills you may dig copper. You must eat and be full, and you must bless YHWH your God for the good land which he has given you.
Do Not Forget YHWH · 8:11–20
