YHWH will bring you into Egypt again with ships, by the way of which I tell to you that you would never see it again. There you will sell yourselves to your enemies for male and female slaves, and nobody will buy you.
The Covenant at Moab · 29:1–13

These are the words of the covenant which YHWH commands Moses to make with the children of Israel in the land of Moab, in addition to the covenant which he makes with them in Horeb. Moses calls to all Israel, and says to them:

Your eyes have seen all that YHWH do in the land of Egypt to Pharaoh, and to all his servants, and to all his land; the great trials which your eyes see, the signs, and those great wonders. But YHWH has not given you a heart to know, eyes to see, and ears to hear, to this day. I have led you forty years in the wilderness. Your clothes have not grown old on you, and your shoes have not grown old on your feet. You have not eaten bread, neither have you drunk wine or strong drink; that you may know that I am YHWH your God. When you come to this place, Sihon the king of Heshbon, and Og the king of Bashan, come out against us to battle, and we strike them. We take their land, and give it for an inheritance to the Reubenites, and to the Gadites, and to the half-tribe of the Manassites. Therefore keep the words of this covenant and do them, that you may prosper in all that you do. All of you stand today in the presence of YHWH your God; your heads, your tribes, your elders, and your officers, even all the men of Israel, your little ones, your wives, and the foreigners who are in the middle of your camps, from the one who cuts your wood to the one who draws your water; that you may enter into the covenant of YHWH your God, and into his oath, which YHWH your God makes with you today; that he may establish you today as his people, and that he may be your God, as he speaks to you, and as he swears to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.
Warning against Apostasy · 29:14–29

Neither do I make this covenant and this oath with you only, but with those who stand here with us today before YHWH our God, and also with those who are not here with us today (for you know how we live in the land of Egypt, and how we come through the middle of the nations through which you pass; and you have seen their abominations, and their idols, wood and stone, silver and gold, which are among them); lest there should be among you man, woman, family, or tribe whose heart turns away today from YHWH our God, to go to serve the gods of those nations; lest there should be among you a root that produces bitter poison; and it happen, when he hears the words of this curse, that he bless himself in his heart, saying, “I will have peace, though I walk in the stubbornness of my heart, to destroy the moist with the dry.” YHWH will not pardon him, but then YHWH’s anger and his jealousy will smoke against that man, and all the curse that is written in this book will fall on him, and YHWH will blot out his name from under the sky. YHWH will set him apart for evil out of all the tribes of Israel, according to all the curses of the covenant that is written in this book of the law.

The generation to come, your children who will rise up after you, and the foreigner who will come from a far land, will say, when they see the plagues of that land, and the sicknesses with which YHWH has made it sick; and that all of its land is sulfur, salt, and burning, that it is not sown, doesn’t produce, nor does any grass grow in it, like the overthrow of Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim, which YHWH overthrows in his anger, and in his wrath; even all the nations will say, “Why has YHWH done thus to this land? What does the heat of this great anger mean?”

Then men will say, “Because they abandoned the covenant of YHWH, the God of their fathers, which he made with them when he brought them out of the land of Egypt, and went and served other gods, and worshiped them, gods that they didn’t know, and that he had not given to them. Therefore YHWH’s anger burned against this land, to bring on it all the curses that are written in this book. YHWH rooted them out of their land in anger, in wrath, and in great indignation, and thrust them into another land, as it is today.”
The secret things belong to YHWH our God; but the things that are revealed belong to us and to our children forever, that we may do all the words of this law.
The Promise of Restoration · 30:1–10

It must happen, when all these things have come on you, the blessing and the curse, which I have set before you, and you must call them to mind among all the nations, where YHWH your God has driven you, and return to YHWH your God, and obey his voice according to all that I command you today, you and your children, with all your heart, and with all your soul; that then YHWH your God will release you from captivity, have compassion on you, and will return and gather you from all the peoples where YHWH your God has scattered you. If your outcasts are in the uttermost parts of the heavens, from there YHWH your God will gather you, and from there he will bring you back. YHWH your God will bring you into the land which your fathers possess, and you will possess it. He will do you good, and increase your numbers more than your fathers. YHWH your God will circumcise your heart, and the heart of your offspring, to love YHWH your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, that you may live. YHWH your God will put all these curses on your enemies, and on those who hate you, who persecute you. You will return and obey YHWH’s voice, and do all his commandments which I command you today. YHWH your God will make you plenteous in all the work of your hand, in the fruit of your body, in the fruit of your livestock, and in the fruit of your ground, for good; for YHWH will again rejoice over you for good, as he rejoices over your fathers; if you will obey YHWH your God’s voice, to keep his commandments and his statutes which are written in this book of the law; if you turn to YHWH your God with all your heart, and with all your soul.
The Word is Near You · 30:11–14

For this commandment which I command you today is not too hard for you or too distant. It is not in heaven, that you should say, “Who will go up for us to heaven, and bring it to us, and proclaim it to us, that we may do it?” Neither is it beyond the sea, that you should say, “Who will go over the sea for us, and bring it to us, and proclaim it to us, that we may do it?” But the word is very near to you, in your mouth and in your heart, that you may do it.
Life and Death · 30:15–20

Look, I have set before you today life and prosperity, and death and evil. For I command you today to love YHWH your God, to walk in his ways, and to keep his commandments, his statutes, and his ordinances, that you may live and multiply, and that YHWH your God may bless you in the land where you go in to possess it. But if your heart turns away, and you will not hear, but are drawn away, and worship other gods, and serve them; I denounce to you today, that you will surely perish. You will not prolong your days in the land where you pass over the Jordan to go in to possess it. I call heaven and earth to witness against you today, that I have set before you life and death, the blessing and the curse. Therefore choose life, that you may live, you and your descendants; to love YHWH your God, to obey his voice, and to cling to him; for he is your life, and the length of your days; that you may dwell in the land which YHWH swears to your fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give them.
Joshua Commissioned · 31:1–8

Moses goes and speaks these words to all Israel. He says to them, “I am one hundred twenty years old today. I can no more go out and come in. YHWH has said to me, ‘You must not go over this Jordan.’ YHWH your God himself will go over before you. He will destroy these nations from before you, and you must dispossess them. Joshua will go over before you, as YHWH has spoken. YHWH will do to them as he did to Sihon and to Og, the kings of the Amorites, and to their land; whom he destroyed. YHWH will deliver them up before you, and you must do to them according to all the commandment which I have commanded you. Be strong and courageous. Don’t be afraid or scared of them; for YHWH your God himself is who goes with you. He will not fail you nor forsake you.”

Moses calls to Joshua, and says to him in the sight of all Israel, “Be strong and courageous, for you must go with this people into the land which YHWH has sworn to their fathers to give them; and you must cause them to inherit it. YHWH himself is who goes before you. He will be with you. He will not fail you nor forsake you. Don’t be afraid. Don’t be discouraged.”
The Torah Written and Commanded · 31:9–13

Moses writes this law, and delivers it to the priests the sons of Levi, who bears the ark of YHWH’s covenant, and to all the elders of Israel. Moses commands them, saying, “At the end of every seven years, in the set time of the year of release, in the feast of tents, when all Israel has come to appear before YHWH your God in the place which he will choose, you must read this law before all Israel in their hearing. Assemble the people, the men and the women and the little ones, and the foreigners who are within your gates, that they may hear, and that they may learn, and fear YHWH your God, and observe to do all the words of this law; and that their children, who have not known, may hear, and learn to fear YHWH your God, as long as you live in the land where you go over the Jordan to possess it.”
The Song Commanded · 31:14–30
YHWH says to Moses, “Look, your days approach that you must die. Call Joshua, and present yourselves in the Tent of Meeting, that I may commission him.”
Moses and Joshua go, and present themselves in the Tent of Meeting.

YHWH appears in the Tent in a pillar of cloud, and the pillar of cloud stands over the Tent’s door. YHWH says to Moses, “Look, you must sleep with your fathers. This people will rise up, and play the prostitute after the strange gods of the land, where they go to be among them, and will forsake me, and break my covenant which I have made with them. Then my anger will be kindled against them in that day, and I will forsake them, and I will hide my face from them, and they will be devoured, and many evils and troubles will come on them; so that they will say in that day, ‘Haven’t these evils come on us because our God is not among us?’ I will surely hide my face in that day for all the evil which they have done, in that they have turned to other gods.

“Now therefore write this song for yourselves, and teach it to the children of Israel. Put it in their mouths, that this song may be a witness for me against the children of Israel. For when I have brought them into the land which I swore to their fathers, flowing with milk and honey, and they have eaten and filled themselves, and grown fat; then they will turn to other gods, and serve them, and despise me, and break my covenant. It will happen, when many evils and troubles have come on them, that this song will testify before them as a witness; for it will not be forgotten out of the mouths of their descendants; for I know their ways and what they are doing today, before I have brought them into the land which I swore.”
So Moses writes this song the same day, and teaches it to the children of Israel.
He commissions Joshua the son of Nun, and says, “Be strong and courageous; for you must bring the children of Israel into the land which I swore to them. I will be with you.”

When Moses has finished writing the words of this law in a book, until they are finished, Moses commands the Levites, who bear the ark of YHWH’s covenant, saying, “Take this book of the law, and put it by the side of the ark of YHWH your God’s covenant, that it may be there for a witness against you. For I know your rebellion, and your stiff neck. Look, while I am yet alive with you today, you have been rebellious against YHWH. How much more after my death? Assemble to me all the elders of your tribes, and your officers, that I may speak these words in their ears, and call heaven and earth to witness against them. For I know that after my death you will utterly corrupt yourselves, and turn away from the way which I have commanded you; and evil will happen to you in the latter days; because you will do that which is evil in YHWH’s sight, to provoke him to anger through the work of your hands.”
Moses speaks in the ears of all the assembly of Israel the words of this song, until they are finished.
The Opening Call · 32:1–4
Give ear, you heavens, and I will speak.
Let the earth hear the words of my mouth.
My doctrine will drop as the rain.
My speech will condense as the dew,
as the misty rain on the tender grass,
as the showers on the herb.
For I will proclaim YHWH’s name.
Ascribe greatness to our God!
The Rock, his work is perfect,
for all his ways are just.
A God of faithfulness who does no wrong,
just and right is he.
Israel's Unfaithfulness · 32:5–18
They have dealt corruptly with him.
They are not his children, because of their defect.
They are a perverse and crooked generation.
Is this the way you repay YHWH,
foolish and unwise people?
Isn’t he your father who has bought you?
He has made you and established you.
Remember the days of old.
Consider the years of many generations.
Ask your father, and he will show you;
your elders, and they will tell you.
When the Most High gave to the nations their inheritance,
when he separated the children of men,
he set the bounds of the peoples
according to the number of the children of Israel.
For YHWH’s portion is his people.
Jacob is the lot of his inheritance.
He found him in a desert land,
in the waste howling wilderness.
He surrounded him.
He cared for him.
He kept him as the apple of his eye.
As an eagle that stirs up her nest,
that flutters over her young,
he spread abroad his wings,
he took them,
he bore them on his feathers.
YHWH alone led him.
There was no foreign god with him.
He made him ride on the high places of the earth.
He ate the increase of the field.
He caused him to suck honey out of the rock,
oil out of the flinty rock;
butter from the herd, and milk from the flock,
with fat of lambs,
rams of the breed of Bashan, and goats,
with the finest of the wheat.
From the blood of the grape, you drank wine.
But Jeshurun grew fat, and kicked.
You have grown fat.
You have grown thick.
You have become sleek.
Then he abandoned God who made him,
and rejected the Rock of his salvation.
They moved him to jealousy with strange gods.
They provoked him to anger with abominations.
They sacrificed to demons, not God,
to gods that they didn’t know,
to new gods that came up recently,
which your fathers didn’t dread.
Of the Rock who became your father, you are unmindful,
and have forgotten God who gave you birth.
YHWH's Judgment · 32:19–33
YHWH saw and abhorred,
because of the provocation of his sons and his daughters.
He said, “I will hide my face from them.
I will see what their end will be;
for they are a very perverse generation,
children in whom is no faithfulness.
They have moved me to jealousy with that which is not God.
They have provoked me to anger with their vanities.
I will move them to jealousy with those who are not a people.
I will provoke them to anger with a foolish nation.
For a fire is kindled in my anger,
that burns to the lowest Sheol,
devours the earth with its increase,
and sets the foundations of the mountains on fire.
“I will heap evils on them.
I will spend my arrows on them.
They will be wasted with hunger,
and devoured with burning heat
and bitter destruction.
I will send the teeth of animals on them,
with the venom of vipers that glide in the dust.
Outside the sword will bereave,
and in the rooms, terror;
on both young man and virgin,
the nursing infant with the gray-haired man.
I said that I would scatter them afar.
I would make their memory to cease from among men;
were it not that I feared the provocation of the enemy,
lest their adversaries should judge wrongly,
lest they should say, ‘Our hand is exalted,
YHWH has not done all this.’”
For they are a nation void of counsel.
There is no understanding in them.
Oh that they were wise, that they understood this,
that they would consider their latter end!
How could one chase a thousand,
and two put ten thousand to flight,
unless their Rock had sold them,
and YHWH had delivered them up?
For their rock is not as our Rock,
even our enemies themselves concede.
For their vine is of the vine of Sodom,
of the fields of Gomorrah.
Their grapes are poison grapes.
Their clusters are bitter.
Their wine is the poison of serpents,
the cruel venom of asps.
YHWH's Vengeance and Compassion · 32:34–43
“Isn’t this laid up in store with me,
sealed up among my treasures?
Vengeance is mine, and recompense,
at the time when their foot slides;
for the day of their calamity is at hand.
Their doom rushes at them.”
For YHWH will judge his people,
and have compassion on his servants,
when he sees that their power is gone;
that there is no one remaining, shut up or left at large.
He will say, “Where are their gods,
the rock in which they took refuge;
which ate the fat of their sacrifices,
and drank the wine of their drink offering?
Let them rise up and help you!
Let them be your protection.
“See now that I myself am he.
There is no god with me.
I kill and I make alive.
I wound and I heal.
There is no one who can deliver out of my hand.
For I lift up my hand to heaven and declare,
as I live forever,
if I sharpen my glittering sword,
my hand grasps it in judgment;
I will take vengeance on my adversaries,
and will repay those who hate me.
I will make my arrows drunk with blood.
My sword will devour flesh with the blood of the slain and the captives,
from the head of the leaders of the enemy.”
Rejoice, you nations, with his people,
for he will avenge the blood of his servants.
He will take vengeance on his adversaries,
and will make atonement for his land and for his people.
The Song's Conclusion · 32:44–52

Moses comes and speaks all the words of this song in the ears of the people, he and Joshua the son of Nun. Moses finishes reciting all these words to all Israel. He says to them, “Set your heart to all the words which I testify to you today, which you must command your children to observe to do, all the words of this law. For it is no vain thing for you; because it is your life, and through this thing you must prolong your days in the land, where you go over the Jordan to possess it.”

YHWH speaks to Moses that same day, saying, “Go up into this mountain of Abarim, to Mount Nebo, which is in the land of Moab, that is across from Jericho; and see the land of Canaan, which I give to the children of Israel for a possession. Die on the mountain where you go up, and be gathered to your people, as Aaron your brother died on Mount Hor, and was gathered to his people; because you trespassed against me among the children of Israel at the waters of Meribah of Kadesh, in the wilderness of Zin; because you didn’t uphold my holiness among the children of Israel. For you will see the land from a distance; but you must not go there into the land which I give the children of Israel.”
The Introduction · 33:1–5
This is the blessing with which Moses the man of God blesses the children of Israel before his death. He says,
“YHWH came from Sinai,
and rose from Seir to them.
He shone from Mount Paran.
He came from the ten thousands of holy ones.
At his right hand was a fiery law for them.
Yes, he loves the people.
All his saints are in your hand.
They sat down at your feet.
Each receives your words.
Moses commanded us a law,
an inheritance for the assembly of Jacob.
He was king in Jeshurun,
when the heads of the people were gathered,
all the tribes of Israel together.
The Tribal Blessings · 33:6–25
“Let Reuben live, and not die;
Nor let his men be few.”
This is for Judah. He says,
“Hear, YHWH, the voice of Judah.
Bring him in to his people.
With his hands he contended for himself.
You will be a help against his adversaries.”
About Levi he says,
“Your Thummim and your Urim are with your godly one,
whom you proved at Massah,
with whom you contended at the waters of Meribah.
He said of his father, and of his mother, ‘I have not seen him.’
He didn’t acknowledge his brothers,
nor did he know his own children;
for they have observed your word,
and keep your covenant.
They must teach Jacob your ordinances,
and Israel your law.
They must put incense before you,
and whole burnt offering on your altar.
YHWH, bless his skills.
Accept the work of his hands.
Strike through the hips of those who rise up against him,
of those who hate him, that they not rise again.”
About Benjamin he says,
“The beloved of YHWH will dwell in safety by him.
He covers him all day long.
He dwells between his shoulders.”
About Joseph he says,
“His land is blessed by YHWH,
for the precious things of the heavens, for the dew,
for the deep that couches beneath,
for the precious things of the fruits of the sun,
for the precious things that the moon can yield,
for the best things of the ancient mountains,
for the precious things of the everlasting hills,
for the precious things of the earth and its fullness,
the good will of him who lived in the bush.
Let this come on the head of Joseph,
on the crown of the head of him who was separated from his brothers.
The firstborn of his herd, majesty is his.
His horns are the horns of the wild ox.
With them he will push all the peoples, to the ends of the earth.
They are the ten thousands of Ephraim.
They are the thousands of Manasseh.”
About Zebulun he says,
“Rejoice, Zebulun, in your going out;
and Issachar, in your tents.
They will call the peoples to the mountain.
There they will offer sacrifices of righteousness,
for they will draw out the abundance of the seas,
the hidden treasures of the sand.”
About Gad he says,
“He who enlarges Gad is blessed.
He dwells as a lioness,
and tears the arm, yes, the crown of the head.
He provided the first part for himself,
for the lawgiver’s portion reserved was reserved for him.
He came with the heads of the people.
He executed the righteousness of YHWH,
His ordinances with Israel.”
About Dan he says,
“Dan is a lion’s cub
that leaps out of Bashan.”
About Naphtali he says,
“Naphtali, satisfied with favor,
full of YHWH’s blessing,
Possess the west and the south.”
About Asher he says,
“Asher is blessed with children.
Let him be acceptable to his brothers.
Let him dip his foot in oil.
Your bars will be iron and brass.
As your days, so your strength will be.
The Closing Doxology · 33:26–29
“There is no one like God, Jeshurun,
who rides on the heavens for your help,
in his excellency on the skies.
The eternal God is your dwelling place.
Underneath are the everlasting arms.
He thrust out the enemy from before you,
and said, ‘Destroy!’
Israel dwells in safety;
the fountain of Jacob alone,
In a land of grain and new wine.
Yes, his heavens drop down dew.
You are happy, Israel!
Who is like you, a people saved by YHWH,
the shield of your help,
the sword of your excellency?
Your enemies will submit themselves to you.
You will tread on their high places.”
Moses Views the Land · 34:1–4

Moses goes up from the plains of Moab to Mount Nebo, to the top of Pisgah, that is over against Jericho. YHWH shows him all the land of Gilead, to Dan, and all Naphtali, and the land of Ephraim and Manasseh, and all the land of Judah, to the western sea, and the south, and the Plain of the valley of Jericho the city of palm trees, to Zoar. YHWH says to him, “This is the land which I swore to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, saying, ‘I will give it to your offspring.’ I have caused you to see it with your eyes, but you must not go over there.”
The Death of Moses · 34:5–8

So Moses the servant of YHWH dies there in the land of Moab, according to YHWH’s word. He buries him in the valley in the land of Moab opposite Beth Peor, but no man knows where his tomb is to this day. Moses is one hundred twenty years old when he dies. His eye is not dim, nor his strength gone. The children of Israel weep for Moses in the plains of Moab thirty days, until the days of weeping in the mourning for Moses are ended.
Joshua's Commission · 34:9
Joshua the son of Nun is full of the spirit of wisdom; for Moses has laid his hands on him. The children of Israel listen to him, and do as YHWH commands Moses.
The Unparalleled Prophet · 34:10–12

Since then, there has not arisen a prophet in Israel like Moses, whom YHWH knows face to face, in all the signs and the wonders, which YHWH sends him to do in the land of Egypt, to Pharaoh, and to all his servants, and to all his land, and in all the mighty hand, and in all the awesome deeds, which Moses does in the sight of all Israel.
YHWH's Commission to Joshua · 1:1–9

Now after the death of Moses the servant of YHWH, YHWH speaks to Joshua the son of Nun, Moses’ servant, saying, “Moses my servant is dead. Now therefore arise, go across this Jordan, you, and all these people, to the land which I am giving to them, even to the children of Israel. I have given you every place that the sole of your foot will tread on, as I told Moses. From the wilderness, and this Lebanon, even to the great river, the river Euphrates, all the land of the Hittites, and to the great sea toward the going down of the sun, will be your border. No man will be able to stand before you all the days of your life. As I was with Moses, so I will be with you. I will not fail you nor forsake you.

“Be strong and courageous; for you will cause this people to inherit the land which I swore to their fathers to give them. Only be strong and very courageous. Be careful to observe to do according to all the law, which Moses my servant commanded you. Don’t turn from it to the right hand or to the left, that you may have good success wherever you go. This book of the law will not depart from your mouth, but you will meditate on it day and night, that you may observe to do according to all that is written in it; for then you will make your way prosperous, and then you will have good success. Haven’t I commanded you? Be strong and courageous. Don’t be afraid. Don’t be dismayed, for YHWH your God is with you wherever you go.”
Joshua Commands the People · 1:10–18

Then Joshua commands the officers of the people, saying, “Pass through the middle of the camp, and command the people, saying, ‘Prepare food; for within three days you are to pass over this Jordan, to go in to possess the land, which YHWH your God gives you to possess it.’”

Joshua speaks to the Reubenites, and to the Gadites, and to the half-tribe of Manasseh, saying, “Remember the word which Moses the servant of YHWH commanded you, saying, ‘YHWH your God gives you rest, and will give you this land. Your wives, your little ones, and your livestock, will live in the land which Moses gave you beyond the Jordan; but you will pass over before your brothers armed, all the mighty men of valor, and will help them until YHWH has given your brothers rest, as he has given you, and they have also possessed the land which YHWH your God gives them. Then you will return to the land of your possession, and possess it, which Moses the servant of YHWH gave you beyond the Jordan toward the sunrise.’”

They answer Joshua, saying, “All that you have commanded us we will do, and wherever you send us we will go. Just as we listened to Moses in all things, so will we listen to you. Only may YHWH your God be with you, as he was with Moses. Whoever rebels against your commandment, and doesn’t listen to your words in all that you command him will himself be put to death. Only be strong and courageous.”
Rahab and the Spies · 2:1–7

Joshua the son of Nun secretly sends two men out of Shittim as spies, saying, “Go, view the land, including Jericho.” They go and come into the house of a prostitute whose name is Rahab, and sleep there.
The king of Jericho is told, “Look, men of the children of Israel came in here tonight to spy out the land.”
Jericho’s king sends to Rahab, saying, “Bring out the men who have come to you, who have entered into your house; for they have come to spy out all the land.”

The woman takes the two men and hides them. Then she says, “Yes, the men came to me, but I didn’t know where they came from. About the time of the shutting of the gate, when it was dark, the men went out. Where the men went, I don’t know. Pursue them quickly. You may catch up with them.” But she has brought them up to the roof, and hides them under the stalks of flax which she has laid in order on the roof. The men pursue them along the way to the fords of the Jordan River. As soon as those who pursue them have gone out, they shut the gate.
Rahab's Confession of Faith · 2:8–14

Before they have lain down, she comes up to them on the roof. She says to the men, “I know that YHWH has given you the land, and that the fear of you has fallen upon us, and that all the inhabitants of the land melt away before you. For we have heard how YHWH dried up the water of the Red Sea before you, when you came out of Egypt; and what you did to the two kings of the Amorites, who were beyond the Jordan, to Sihon and to Og, whom you utterly destroyed. As soon as we had heard it, our hearts melted, and there wasn’t any more spirit in any man, because of you: for YHWH your God, he is God in heaven above, and on earth beneath. Now therefore, please swear to me by YHWH, since I have dealt kindly with you, that you also will deal kindly with my father’s house, and give me a true sign; and that you will save alive my father, my mother, my brothers, and my sisters, and all that they have, and will deliver our lives from death.”
The men say to her, “Our life for yours, if you don’t talk about this business of ours; and it will be, when YHWH gives us the land, that we will deal kindly and truly with you.”
The Scarlet Cord · 2:15–24

Then she lets them down by a cord through the window; for her house is on the side of the wall, and she lives on the wall. She says to them, “Go to the mountain, lest the pursuers find you. Hide yourselves there three days, until the pursuers have returned. Afterward, you may go your way.”

The men say to her, “We will be guiltless of this your oath which you’ve made us to swear. Look, when we come into the land, tie this line of scarlet thread in the window which you used to let us down. Gather to yourself into the house your father, your mother, your brothers, and all your father’s household. It will be that whoever goes out of the doors of your house into the street, his blood will be on his head, and we will be guiltless. Whoever is with you in the house, his blood will be on our head, if any hand is on him. But if you talk about this business of ours, then we will be guiltless of your oath which you’ve made us to swear.”
She says, “Let it be as you have said.” She sends them away, and they depart. Then she ties the scarlet line in the window.

They go, and come to the mountain, and stay there three days, until the pursuers have returned. The pursuers seek them all along the way, but don’t find them. Then the two men return, descend from the mountain, cross the river, and come to Joshua the son of Nun. They tell him all that have happened to them. They say to Joshua, “Truly YHWH has delivered all the land into our hands. Moreover, all the inhabitants of the land melt away before us.”
Preparing to Cross · 3:1–6

Joshua gets up early in the morning; and they move from Shittim, and come to the Jordan, he and all the children of Israel. They camp there before they cross over. After three days, the officers go through the middle of the camp; and they command the people, saying, “When you see the ark of YHWH your God’s covenant, and the priests the Levites bearing it, then leave your place, and follow it. Yet there will be a space between you and it of about two thousand cubits by measure—don’t come closer to it—that you may know the way by which you must go; for you have not passed this way before.”
Joshua says to the people, “Sanctify yourselves; for tomorrow YHWH will do wonders among you.”
Joshua speaks to the priests, saying, “Take up the ark of the covenant, and cross over before the people.” They take up the ark of the covenant, and go before the people.
The Jordan Stops · 3:7–17

YHWH says to Joshua, “Today I will begin to magnify you in the sight of all Israel, that they may know that as I was with Moses, so I will be with you. You will command the priests who bear the ark of the covenant, saying, ‘When you come to the brink of the waters of the Jordan, you will stand still in the Jordan.’”

Joshua says to the children of Israel, “Come here, and hear the words of YHWH your God.” Joshua says, “By this you will know that the living God is among you, and that he will without fail drive the Canaanite, and the Hittite, and the Hivite, and the Perizzite, and the Girgashite, and the Amorite, and the Jebusite out from before you. Look, the ark of the covenant of the Lord of all the earth passes over before you into the Jordan. Now therefore take twelve men out of the tribes of Israel, for every tribe a man. It will be that when the soles of the feet of the priests who bear the ark of YHWH, the Lord of all the earth, rest in the waters of the Jordan, that the waters of the Jordan will be cut off. The waters that come down from above will stand in one heap.”

When the people move from their tents to pass over the Jordan, the priests who bear the ark of the covenant being before the people, and when those who bear the ark have come to the Jordan, and the feet of the priests who bear the ark have dipped in the edge of the water (for the Jordan overflows all its banks all the time of harvest), the waters which come down from above stood, and rise up in one heap, a great way off, at Adam, the city that is beside Zarethan; and those that go down toward the sea of the Arabah, even the Salt Sea, are wholly cut off. Then the people pass over near Jericho. The priests who bear the ark of YHWH’s covenant stand firm on dry ground in the middle of the Jordan; and all Israel crosses over on dry ground, until all the nation has passed completely over the Jordan.
Twelve Stones from the Jordan · 4:1–9

When all the nation has completely crossed over the Jordan, YHWH speaks to Joshua, saying, “Take twelve men out of the people, a man out of every tribe, and command them, saying, ‘Take from out of the middle of the Jordan, out of the place where the priests’ feet stood firm, twelve stones, and carry them over with you, and lay them down in the place where you’ll camp tonight.’”

Then Joshua calls the twelve men, whom he has prepared of the children of Israel, a man out of every tribe. Joshua says to them, “Cross before the ark of YHWH your God into the middle of the Jordan, and each of you pick up a stone and put it on your shoulder, according to the number of the tribes of the children of Israel; that this may be a sign among you, that when your children ask in the future, saying, ‘What do you mean by these stones?’ then you will tell them, ‘Because the waters of the Jordan were cut off before the ark of YHWH’s covenant. When it crossed over the Jordan, the waters of the Jordan were cut off. These stones will be for a memorial to the children of Israel forever.’”

The children of Israel do as Joshua commands, and take up twelve stones out of the middle of the Jordan, as YHWH speaks to Joshua, according to the number of the tribes of the children of Israel. They carry them over with them to the place where they camp, and lay them down there. Joshua sets up twelve stones in the middle of the Jordan, in the place where the feet of the priests who bear the ark of the covenant stand; and they are there to this day.
The Crossing Completed · 4:10–24

For the priests who bear the ark stand in the middle of the Jordan, until everything is finished that YHWH commands Joshua to speak to the people, according to all that Moses commands Joshua; and the people hurry and pass over. When all the people have completely crossed over, YHWH’s ark crosses over, with the priests, in the presence of the people.

The children of Reuben, and the children of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, cross over armed before the children of Israel, as Moses speaks to them. About forty thousand men, ready and armed for war passed over before YHWH to battle, to the plains of Jericho. On that day, YHWH magnifies Joshua in the sight of all Israel; and they fear him, as they fear Moses, all the days of his life.
YHWH speaks to Joshua, saying, “Command the priests who bear the ark of the testimony, that they come up out of the Jordan.”

Joshua therefore commands the priests, saying, “Come up out of the Jordan!” When the priests who bear the ark of YHWH’s covenant have come up out of the middle of the Jordan, and the soles of the priests’ feet have been lifted up to the dry ground, the waters of the Jordan return to their place, and go over all its banks, as before. The people come up out of the Jordan on the tenth day of the first month, and encamp in Gilgal, on the east border of Jericho.

Joshua sets up those twelve stones, which they take out of the Jordan, in Gilgal. He speaks to the children of Israel, saying, “When your children ask their fathers in time to come, saying, ‘What do these stones mean?’ Then you will let your children know, saying, ‘Israel came over this Jordan on dry land. For YHWH your God dried up the waters of the Jordan from before you, until you had crossed over, as YHWH your God did to the Red Sea, which he dried up from before us, until we had crossed over; that all the peoples of the earth may know that YHWH’s hand is mighty; that you may fear YHWH your God forever.’”
Circumcision at Gilgal · 5:1–9

When all the kings of the Amorites, who are beyond the Jordan westward, and all the kings of the Canaanites, who are by the sea, hear how YHWH has dried up the waters of the Jordan from before the children of Israel, until we have crossed over, their heart melts, and there is no more spirit in them, because of the children of Israel. At that time, YHWH says to Joshua, “Make flint knives, and circumcise again the sons of Israel the second time.” Joshua makes himself flint knives, and circumcises the sons of Israel at the hill of the foreskins. This is the reason Joshua circumcises them: all the people who come out of Egypt, who are males, even all the men of war, die in the wilderness along the way, after they come out of Egypt. For all the people who come out are circumcised; but all the people who are born in the wilderness along the way as they come out of Egypt have not been circumcised. For the children of Israel walk forty years in the wilderness, until all the nation, even the men of war who come out of Egypt, are consumed, because they don’t listen to YHWH’s voice. YHWH swears to them that he wouldn’t let them see the land which YHWH swears to their fathers that he would give us, a land flowing with milk and honey. Their children, whom he raises up in their place, are circumcised by Joshua; for they are uncircumcised, because they have not circumcised them on the way. When they are done circumcising the whole nation, they stay in their places in the camp until they are healed.
YHWH says to Joshua, “Today I have rolled away the reproach of Egypt from you.” Therefore the name of that place is called Gilgal, to this day.
The First Passover in the Land · 5:10–12

The children of Israel encamp in Gilgal. They keep the Passover on the fourteenth day of the month at evening in the plains of Jericho. They eat unleavened cakes and parch grain of the produce of the land on the next day after the Passover, in the same day. The manna ceases on the next day, after they have eaten of the produce of the land. The children of Israel don’t have manna any more; but they eat of the fruit of the land of Canaan that year.
The Commander of YHWH's Army · 5:13–15

When Joshua is by Jericho, he lifts up his eyes and looks, and look, a man stands in front of him with his sword drawn in his hand. Joshua goes to him and says to him, “Are you for us, or for our enemies?”
He says, “No; but I have come now as commander of YHWH’s army.”
Joshua falls on his face to the earth, and worships, and asks him, “What does my lord say to his servant?”
The prince of YHWH’s army says to Joshua, “Take off your shoes; for the place on which you stand is holy.” Joshua does so.
The Battle Instructions · 6:1–7

Now Jericho is tightly shut up because of the children of Israel. No one goes out, and no one comes in. YHWH says to Joshua, “Look, I have given Jericho into your hand, with its king and the mighty men of valor. All of your men of war will march around the city, going around the city once. You will do this six days. Seven priests will bear seven trumpets of rams’ horns before the ark. On the seventh day, you will march around the city seven times, and the priests will blow the trumpets. It will be that when they make a long blast with the ram’s horn, and when you hear the sound of the trumpet, all the people will shout with a great shout; and the city wall will fall down flat, and the people will go up, every man straight in front of him.”
Joshua the son of Nun calls the priests, and says to them, “Take up the ark of the covenant, and let seven priests bear seven trumpets of rams’ horns before YHWH’s ark.”
They say to the people, “Advance! March around the city, and let the armed men pass on before YHWH’s ark.”
Six Days of Marching · 6:8–14

It is so, that when Joshua has spoken to the people, the seven priests bearing the seven trumpets of rams’ horns before YHWH advances and blows the trumpets, and the ark of YHWH’s covenant follow them. The armed men go before the priests who blow the trumpets, and the ark goes after them. The trumpets sound as they go.

Joshua commands the people, saying, “You will not shout, nor let your voice be heard, neither will any word proceed out of your mouth, until the day I tell you to shout. Then you will shout.” So he causes YHWH’s ark to go around the city, going about it once. Then they come into the camp, and stay in the camp. Joshua rises early in the morning, and the priests take up YHWH’s ark. The seven priests bearing the seven trumpets of rams’ horns in front of YHWH’s ark go on continually, and blow the trumpets. The armed men go in front of them. The rear guard comes after YHWH’s ark. The trumpets sound as they go. The second day they march around the city once, and return into the camp. They do this six days.
The Seventh Day · 6:15–21

On the seventh day, they rise early at the dawning of the day, and march around the city in the same way seven times. Only on this day they march around the city seven times. At the seventh time, when the priests blow the trumpets, Joshua says to the people, “Shout, for YHWH has given you the city! The city will be devoted, even it and all that is in it, to YHWH. Only Rahab the prostitute will live, she and all who are with her in the house, because she hid the messengers that we sent. But as for you, only keep yourselves from what is devoted to destruction, lest when you have devoted it, you take of the devoted thing; so you would make the camp of Israel accursed, and trouble it. But all the silver, gold, and vessels of brass and iron, are holy to YHWH. They will come into YHWH’s treasury.”

So the people shout and the priests blow the trumpets. When the people hear the sound of the trumpet, the people shout with a great shout, and the wall falls down flat, so that the people go up into the city, every man straight in front of him, and they take the city. They utterly destroy all that are in the city, both man and woman, both young and old, and ox, sheep, and donkey, with the edge of the sword.
Rahab Saved · 6:22–27

Joshua says to the two men who have spied out the land, “Go into the prostitute’s house, and bring the woman and all that she has out from there, as you swore to her.” The young men who are spies go in, and bring out Rahab with her father, her mother, her brothers, and all that she has. They also bring out all of her relatives, and they set them outside of the camp of Israel. They burn the city with fire, and all that are in it. Only they put the silver, the gold, and the vessels of brass and of iron into the treasury of YHWH’s house. But Rahab the prostitute, her father’s household, and all that she has, Joshua saves alive. She lives in the middle of Israel to this day, because she hides the messengers, whom Joshua sends to spy out Jericho.

Joshua commands them with an oath at that time, saying, “Cursed is the man before YHWH, who rises up and builds this city Jericho. With the loss of his firstborn he will lay its foundation, and with the loss of his youngest son he will set up its gates.” So YHWH is with Joshua; and his fame is in all the land.
The Sin of Achan · 7:1–9

But the children of Israel commit a trespass in the devoted things; for Achan, the son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, take some of the devoted things. Therefore YHWH’s anger burns against the children of Israel. Joshua sends men from Jericho to Ai, which is beside Beth Aven, on the east side of Bethel, and speaks to them, saying, “Go up and spy out the land.”

The men go up and spy out Ai. They return to Joshua, and say to him, “Don’t let all the people go up; but let about two or three thousand men go up and strike Ai. Don’t make all the people to toil there, for there are only a few of them.” So about three thousand men of the people go up there, and they flee before the men of Ai. The men of Ai strike about thirty-six men of them, and they chase them from before the gate even to Shebarim, and strike them at the descent. The hearts of the people melted, and become like water. Joshua tears his clothes, and falls to the earth on his face before YHWH’s ark until the evening, he and the elders of Israel; and they put dust on their heads. Joshua says, “Alas, Lord YHWH, why have you brought this people over the Jordan at all, to deliver us into the hand of the Amorites, to cause us to perish? I wish that we had been content and lived beyond the Jordan! Oh, Lord, what should I say, after Israel has turned their backs before their enemies! For the Canaanites and all the inhabitants of the land will hear of it, and will surround us, and cut off our name from the earth. What will you do for your great name?”
YHWH's Answer and Achan's Discovery · 7:10–21

YHWH says to Joshua, “Get up! Why have you fallen on your face like that? Israel has sinned. Yes, they have even transgressed my covenant which I commanded them. Yes, they have even taken some of the devoted things, and have also stolen, and also deceived. They have even put it among their own stuff. Therefore the children of Israel can’t stand before their enemies. They turn their backs before their enemies, because they have become devoted for destruction. I will not be with you any more, unless you destroy the devoted things from among you.

“Get up! Sanctify the people, and say, ‘Sanctify yourselves for tomorrow, for YHWH, the God of Israel, says, “There is a devoted thing among you, Israel. You cannot stand before your enemies until you take away the devoted thing from among you.”

“‘In the morning therefore you will be brought near by your tribes. It will be that the tribe which YHWH selects will come near by families. The family which YHWH selects will come near by households. The household which YHWH selects will come near man by man. It will be, that he who is taken with the devoted thing will be burned with fire, he and all that he has, because he has transgressed YHWH’s covenant, and because he has done a disgraceful thing in Israel.’”

So Joshua rises up early in the morning and brings Israel near by their tribes. The tribe of Judah is selected. He brings near the family of Judah; and he selects the family of the Zerahites. He brings near the family of the Zerahites man by man, and Zabdi is selected. He brings near his household man by man, and Achan, the son of Carmi, the son of Zabdi, the son of Zerah, of the tribe of Judah, is selected. Joshua says to Achan, “My son, please give glory to YHWH, the God of Israel, and make confession to him. Tell me now what you have done! Don’t hide it from me!”

Achan answers Joshua, and says, “I have truly sinned against YHWH, the God of Israel, and this is what I have done. When I saw among the plunder a beautiful Babylonian robe, two hundred shekels of silver, and a wedge of gold weighing fifty shekels, then I coveted them and took them. Look, they are hidden in the ground in the middle of my tent, with the silver under it.”
The Judgment on Achan · 7:22–26

So Joshua sends messengers, and they run to the tent. Look, it is hidden in his tent, with the silver under it. They take them from the middle of the tent, and bring them to Joshua and to all the children of Israel. They lay them down before YHWH. Joshua, and all Israel with him, take Achan the son of Zerah, the silver, the robe, the wedge of gold, his sons, his daughters, his cattle, his donkeys, his sheep, his tent, and all that he has; and they bring them up to the valley of Achor. Joshua says, “Why have you troubled us? YHWH will trouble you today.” All Israel stones him with stones, and they burn them with fire and stone them with stones. They raise over him a great heap of stones that remains to this day. YHWH turns from the fierceness of his anger. Therefore the name of that place is called “The valley of Achor” to this day.
The Capture of Ai · 8:1–29

YHWH says to Joshua, “Don’t be afraid, and don’t be dismayed. Take all the warriors with you, and arise, go up to Ai. Look, I have given into your hand the king of Ai, with his people, his city, and his land. You will do to Ai and her king as you did to Jericho and her king, except you will take its goods and its livestock for yourselves. Set an ambush for the city behind it.”

So Joshua arises, with all the warriors, to go up to Ai. Joshua chooses thirty thousand men, the mighty men of valor, and sends them out by night. He commands them, saying, “Look, you will lie in ambush against the city, behind the city. Don’t go very far from the city, but all of you be ready. I and all the people who are with me will approach to the city. It will happen, when they come out against us, as at the first, that we will flee before them. They will come out after us, until we have drawn them away from the city; for they will say, ‘They flee before us, like the first time.’ So we will flee before them, and you will rise up from the ambush, and take possession of the city; for YHWH your God will deliver it into your hand. It will be, when you have seized the city, that you will set the city on fire. You will do this according to YHWH’s word. Look, I have commanded you.”

Joshua sends them out; and they go to set up the ambush, and stay between Bethel and Ai, on the west side of Ai; but Joshua stays among the people that night. Joshua rises up early in the morning, musters the people, and goes up, he and the elders of Israel, before the people to Ai. All the people, even the men of war who are with him, go up, and come near, and come before the city, and encamp on the north side of Ai. Now there is a valley between him and Ai. He takes about five thousand men, and sets them in ambush between Bethel and Ai, on the west side of the city. So they set the people, even all the army who are on the north of the city, and their ambush on the west of the city; and Joshua goes that night into the middle of the valley. When the king of Ai sees it, they hurry and rise up early, and the men of the city go out against Israel to battle, he and all his people, at the time appointed, before the Arabah; but he doesn’t know that there is an ambush against him behind the city. Joshua and all Israel make as if they are beaten before them, and flee by the way of the wilderness. All the people who are in the city are called together to pursue after them. They pursue Joshua, and are drawn away from the city. There is not a man left in Ai or Beth El who doesn’t go out after Israel. They leave the city open, and pursue Israel.
YHWH says to Joshua, “Stretch out the javelin that is in your hand toward Ai, for I will give it into your hand.”

Joshua stretches out the javelin that is in his hand toward the city. The ambush arises quickly out of their place, and they run as soon as he has stretched out his hand, and enter into the city, and take it. They hurry and set the city on fire. When the men of Ai look behind them, they see, and look, the smoke of the city ascends up to heaven, and they have no power to flee this way or that way. The people who flee to the wilderness turn back on the pursuers. When Joshua and all Israel see that the ambush has taken the city, and that the smoke of the city ascends, then they turn again, and kill the men of Ai. The others come out of the city against them, so they are in the middle of Israel, some on this side, and some on that side. They strike them, so that they let none of them remain or escape. They capture the king of Ai alive, and bring him to Joshua.

When Israel has finished killing all the inhabitants of Ai in the field, in the wilderness in which they pursue them, and they have all fallen by the edge of the sword, until they are consumed, all Israel returns to Ai, and strikes it with the edge of the sword. All that fall that day, both of men and women, are twelve thousand, even all the men of Ai. For Joshua don’t draw back his hand, with which he stretches out the javelin, until he has utterly destroyed all the inhabitants of Ai. Israel takes for themselves only the livestock and the goods of that city, according to YHWH’s word which he commands Joshua. So Joshua burns Ai, and makes it a heap forever, even a desolation, to this day. He hangs the king of Ai on a tree until the evening, and at sundown Joshua commands, and they take his body down from the tree, and throw it at the entrance of the gate of the city, and raise a great heap of stones on it that remains to this day.
The Law Read at Mount Ebal · 8:30–35

Then Joshua builds an altar to YHWH, the God of Israel, on Mount Ebal, as Moses the servant of YHWH commands the children of Israel, as it is written in the book of the law of Moses, an altar of uncut stones, on which no one has lifted up any iron. They offer burnt offerings on it to YHWH and sacrifice peace offerings. He writes there on the stones a copy of Moses’ law, which he writes in the presence of the children of Israel. All Israel, their elders and officers, and their judges, stand on both sides of the ark before the priests the Levites, who carry the ark of YHWH’s covenant, the foreigner as well as the native; half of them in front of Mount Gerizim, and half of them in front of Mount Ebal, as Moses the servant of YHWH has commanded at the first, that they should bless the people of Israel. Afterward he reads all the words of the law, the blessing and the curse, according to all that is written in the book of the law. There is not a word of all that Moses commands, which Joshua doesn’t read before all the assembly of Israel, with the women, the little ones, and the foreigners who are among them.
The Gibeonite Deception · 9:1–15

When all the kings who are beyond the Jordan, in the hill country, and in the lowland, and on all the shore of the great sea in front of Lebanon, the Hittite, the Amorite, the Canaanite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite, heard of it they gather themselves together to fight with Joshua and with Israel, with one accord. But when the inhabitants of Gibeon hear what Joshua has done to Jericho and to Ai, they also resort to a ruse, and go and make as if they have been ambassadors, and take old sacks on their donkeys, and old, torn-up and bind up wine skins, and old and patched shoes on their feet, and wear old garments. All the bread of their food supply is dry and moldy. They go to Joshua at the camp at Gilgal, and say to him and to the men of Israel, “We have come from a far country. Now therefore make a covenant with us.”
The men of Israel say to the Hivites, “What if you live among us? How could we make a covenant with you?”
They say to Joshua, “We are your servants.”
Joshua says to them, “Who are you? Where do you come from?”

They say to him, “Your servants have come from a very far country because of the name of YHWH your God; for we have heard of his fame, all that he did in Egypt, and all that he did to the two kings of the Amorites who were beyond the Jordan, to Sihon king of Heshbon and to Og king of Bashan, who was at Ashtaroth. Our elders and all the inhabitants of our country spoke to us, saying, ‘Take supplies in your hand for the journey, and go to meet them. Tell them, “We are your servants. Now make a covenant with us.”’ This our bread we take hot for our supplies out of our houses on the day we go out to go to you; but now, look, it is dry, and has become moldy. These wine skins, which we fill, are new; and look, they are torn. These our garments and our shoes have become old because of the very long journey.”

The men sample their provisions, and don’t ask counsel from YHWH’s mouth. Joshua makes peace with them, and makes a covenant with them, to let them live. The princes of the congregation swear to them.
The Deception Discovered · 9:16–27

At the end of three days after they have made a covenant with them, they hear that they are their neighbors, and that they live among them. The children of Israel travel and come to their cities on the third day. Now their cities are Gibeon, Chephirah, Beeroth, and Kiriath Jearim. The children of Israel don’t strike them, because the princes of the congregation have sworn to them by YHWH, the God of Israel. All the congregation murmurs against the princes. But all the princes say to all the congregation, “We have sworn to them by YHWH, the God of Israel. Now therefore we may not touch them. We will do this to them, and let them live; lest wrath be on us, because of the oath which we swore to them.” The princes say to them, “Let them live, so they became wood cutters and drawers of water for all the congregation, as the princes had spoken to them.”

Joshua calls for them, and he speaks to them, saying, “Why have you deceived us, saying, ‘We are very far from you,’ when you live among us? Now therefore you are cursed, and some of you will never fail to be slaves, both wood cutters and drawers of water for the house of my God.”

They answer Joshua, and say, “Because your servants were certainly told how YHWH your God commanded his servant Moses to give you all the land, and to destroy all the inhabitants of the land from before you. Therefore we were very afraid for our lives because of you, and have done this thing. Now, look, we are in your hand. Do to us as it seems good and right to you to do.”

He does so to them, and delivers them out of the hand of the children of Israel, so that they don’t kill them. That day Joshua makes them wood cutters and drawers of water for the congregation and for YHWH’s altar to this day, in the place which he should choose.
The Coalition against Gibeon · 10:1–15

Now when Adoni-Zedek king of Jerusalem hears how Joshua has taken Ai, and has utterly destroyed it; as he has done to Jericho and her king, so he has done to Ai and her king; and how the inhabitants of Gibeon have made peace with Israel, and are among them, they are very afraid, because Gibeon is a great city, as one of the royal cities, and because it is greater than Ai, and all its men are mighty. Therefore Adoni-Zedek king of Jerusalem sends to Hoham king of Hebron, Piram king of Jarmuth, Japhia king of Lachish, and Debir king of Eglon, saying, “Come up to me and help me. Let us strike Gibeon; for they have made peace with Joshua and with the children of Israel.” Therefore the five kings of the Amorites, the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, and the king of Eglon, gather themselves together and go up, they and all their armies, and encamp against Gibeon, and make war against it. The men of Gibeon send to Joshua at the camp at Gilgal, saying, “Don’t abandon your servants! Come up to us quickly and save us! Help us; for all the kings of the Amorites that dwell in the hill country have gathered together against us.”

So Joshua goes up from Gilgal, he, and the whole army with him, including all the mighty men of valor. YHWH says to Joshua, “Don’t fear them, for I have delivered them into your hands. Not a man of them will stand before you.”

Joshua therefore comes to them suddenly. He marches from Gilgal all night. YHWH confuses them before Israel. He kills them with a great slaughter at Gibeon, and chases them by the way of the ascent of Beth Horon, and strikes them to Azekah and to Makkedah. As they flee from before Israel, while they are at the descent of Beth Horon, YHWH hurls down great stones from the sky on them to Azekah, and they die. There are more who dies from the hailstones than those whom the children of Israel killed with the sword.

Then Joshua speaks to YHWH in the day when YHWH delivers up the Amorites before the children of Israel. He says in the sight of Israel, “Sun, stand still on Gibeon! You, moon, stop in the valley of Aijalon!”

The sun stands still, and the moon stays, until the nation has avenged themselves of their enemies. Isn’t this written in the book of Jashar? The sun stays in the middle of the sky, and doesn’t hurry to go down about a whole day. There is no day like that before it or after it, that YHWH listens to the voice of a man; for YHWH fights for Israel.
Joshua returns, and all Israel with him, to the camp to Gilgal.
The Five Kings Captured and Killed · 10:16–27
These five kings flee, and hide themselves in the cave at Makkedah. Joshua is told, saying, “The five kings have been found, hidden in the cave at Makkedah.”

Joshua says, “Roll large stones to cover the cave’s entrance, and set men by it to guard them; but don’t stay there. Pursue your enemies, and attack them from the rear. Don’t allow them to enter into their cities; for YHWH your God has delivered them into your hand.”

When Joshua and the children of Israel have finished killing them with a very great slaughter until they are consumed, and the remnant which remains of them has entered into the fortified cities, all the people return to the camp to Joshua at Makkedah in peace. None moves his tongue against any of the children of Israel. Then Joshua says, “Open the cave entrance, and bring those five kings out of the cave to me.”

They do so, and bring those five kings out of the cave to him: the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, and the king of Eglon. When they bring those kings out to Joshua, Joshua calls for all the men of Israel, and says to the chiefs of the men of war who go with him, “Come near. Put your feet on the necks of these kings.”
They come near, and put their feet on their necks.
Joshua says to them, “Don’t be afraid, nor be dismayed. Be strong and courageous, for YHWH will do this to all your enemies against whom you fight.”

Afterward Joshua strikes them, put them to death, and hangs them on five trees. They are hanging on the trees until the evening. At the time of the going down of the sun, Joshua commands, and they take them down off the trees, and throw them into the cave in which they have hidden themselves, and lay great stones on the mouth of the cave, which remain to this very day.
The Southern Campaign Completed · 10:28–43

Joshua takes Makkedah on that day, and strikes it with the edge of the sword, with its king. He utterly destroys it and all the souls who are in it. He leaves no one remaining. He does to the king of Makkedah as he has done to the king of Jericho.

Joshua passes from Makkedah, and all Israel with him, to Libnah, and fights against Libnah. YHWH delivers it also, with its king, into the hand of Israel. He strikes it with the edge of the sword, and all the souls who are in it. He leaves no one remaining in it. He does to its king as he has done to the king of Jericho.

Joshua passes from Libnah, and all Israel with him, to Lachish, and encamps against it, and fights against it. YHWH delivers Lachish into the hand of Israel. He takes it on the second day, and strikes it with the edge of the sword, with all the souls who are in it, according to all that he has done to Libnah. Then Horam king of Gezer comes up to help Lachish; and Joshua strikes him and his people, until he has left him no one remaining.

Joshua passes from Lachish, and all Israel with him, to Eglon; and they encamp against it and fight against it. They take it on that day, and strike it with the edge of the sword. He utterly destroys all the souls who are in it that day, according to all that he has done to Lachish.

Joshua goes up from Eglon, and all Israel with him, to Hebron; and they fight against it. They take it, and strike it with the edge of the sword, with its king and all its cities, and all the souls who are in it. He leaves no one remaining, according to all that he has done to Eglon; but he utterly destroys it, and all the souls who are in it.

Joshua returns, and all Israel with him, to Debir, and fights against it. He takes it, with its king and all its cities. They strike them with the edge of the sword, and utterly destroy all the souls who are in it. He leaves no one remaining. As he has done to Hebron, so he does to Debir, and to its king; as he has done also to Libnah, and to its king. So Joshua strikes all the land, the hill country, the South, the lowland, the slopes, and all their kings. He leaves no one remaining, but he utterly destroys all that breathe, as YHWH, the God of Israel, commanded. Joshua strikes them from Kadesh Barnea even to Gaza, and all the country of Goshen, even to Gibeon. Joshua takes all these kings and their land at one time because YHWH, the God of Israel, fights for Israel. Joshua returns, and all Israel with him, to the camp to Gilgal.
The Northern Campaign · 11:1–15

When Jabin king of Hazor hears of it, he sends to Jobab king of Madon, to the king of Shimron, to the king of Achshaph, and to the kings who are on the north, in the hill country, in the Arabah south of Chinneroth, in the lowland, and in the heights of Dor on the west, to the Canaanite on the east and on the west, the Amorite, the Hittite, the Perizzite, the Jebusite in the hill country, and the Hivite under Hermon in the land of Mizpah. They go out, they and all their armies with them, many people, even as the sand that is on the seashore in multitude, with very many horses and chariots. All these kings meet together; and they come and encamp together at the waters of Merom, to fight with Israel.
YHWH says to Joshua, “Don’t be afraid because of them; for tomorrow at this time, I will deliver them up all slain before Israel. You will hamstring their horses and burn their chariots with fire.”

So Joshua comes suddenly, with all the warriors, against them by the waters of Merom, and attacks them. YHWH delivers them into the hand of Israel, and they strike them, and chase them to great Sidon, and to Misrephoth Maim, and to the valley of Mizpah eastward. They strike them until they leave them no one remaining. Joshua does to them as YHWH tells him. He hamstrings their horses and burns their chariots with fire. Joshua turns back at that time, and takes Hazor, and strikes its king with the sword: for Hazor uses to be the head of all those kingdoms. They strike all the souls who are in it with the edge of the sword, utterly destroying them. There is no one left who breathes. He burns Hazor with fire. Joshua captures all the cities of those kings, with their kings, and he strikes them with the edge of the sword, and utterly destroys them; as Moses the servant of YHWH commanded. But as for the cities that stand on their mounds, Israel burns none of them, except Hazor only. Joshua burns that. The children of Israel take all the plunder of these cities, with the livestock, as plunder for themselves; but every man they strike with the edge of the sword, until they have destroyed them. They don’t leave any who breathes.
As YHWH commands Moses his servant, so Moses commands Joshua. Joshua does so. He leaves nothing undone of all that YHWH command Moses.
The Summary of the Conquest · 11:16–23

So Joshua captures all that land, the hill country, all the South, all the land of Goshen, the lowland, the Arabah, the hill country of Israel, and the lowland of the same; from Mount Halak, that goes up to Seir, even to Baal Gad in the valley of Lebanon under Mount Hermon. He takes all their kings, strikes them, and puts them to death. Joshua makes war a long time with all those kings. There is not a city that makes peace with the children of Israel, except the Hivites, the inhabitants of Gibeon. They take all in battle. For it is of YHWH to harden their hearts, to come against Israel in battle, that he might utterly destroy them, that they might have no favor, but that he might destroy them, as YHWH commands Moses. Joshua comes at that time, and cuts off the Anakim from the hill country, from Hebron, from Debir, from Anab, and from all the hill country of Judah, and from all the hill country of Israel: Joshua utterly destroys them with their cities. There are none of the Anakim leaves in the land of the children of Israel. Only in Gaza, in Gath, and in Ashdod, does some remain. So Joshua takes the whole land, according to all that YHWH speaks to Moses; and Joshua gives it for an inheritance to Israel according to their divisions by their tribes. The land has rest from war.
Kings Defeated by Moses · 12:1–6

Now these are the kings of the land, whom the children of Israel strike, and possess their land beyond the Jordan toward the sunrise, from the valley of the Arnon to Mount Hermon, and all the Arabah eastward: Sihon king of the Amorites, who live in Heshbon, and rule from Aroer, which is on the edge of the valley of the Arnon, and the middle of the valley, and half Gilead, even to the river Jabbok, the border of the children of Ammon; and the Arabah to the sea of Chinneroth, eastward, and to the sea of the Arabah, even the Salt Sea, eastward, the way to Beth Jeshimoth; and on the south, under the slopes of Pisgah: and the border of Og king of Bashan, of the remnant of the Rephaim, who lives at Ashtaroth and at Edrei, and rules in Mount Hermon, and in Salecah, and in all Bashan, to the border of the Geshurites and the Maacathites, and half Gilead, the border of Sihon king of Heshbon.
Moses the servant of YHWH and the children of Israel strikes them. Moses the servant of YHWH gives it for a possession to the Reubenites, and the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
Kings Defeated by Joshua · 12:7–24

These are the kings of the land whom Joshua and the children of Israel strike beyond the Jordan westward, from Baal Gad in the valley of Lebanon even to Mount Halak, that goes up to Seir. Joshua gives it to the tribes of Israel for a possession according to their divisions; in the hill country, and in the lowland, and in the Arabah, and in the slopes, and in the wilderness, and in the South; the Hittite, the Amorite, and the Canaanite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite:
the king of Jericho, one;
the king of Ai, which is beside Bethel, one;
the king of Jerusalem, one;
the king of Hebron, one;
the king of Jarmuth, one;
the king of Lachish, one;
the king of Eglon, one;
the king of Gezer, one;
the king of Debir, one;
the king of Geder, one;
the king of Hormah, one;
the king of Arad, one;
the king of Libnah, one;
the king of Adullam, one;
the king of Makkedah, one;
the king of Bethel, one;
the king of Tappuah, one;
the king of Hepher, one;
the king of Aphek, one;
the king of Lassharon, one;
the king of Madon, one;
the king of Hazor, one;
the king of Shimron Meron, one;
the king of Achshaph, one;
the king of Taanach, one;
the king of Megiddo, one;
the king of Kedesh, one;
the king of Jokneam in Carmel, one;
the king of Dor in the height of Dor, one;
the king of Goiim in Gilgal, one;
the king of Tirzah, one:
all the kings thirty-one.
Land Still to Be Taken · 13:1–7
Now Joshua is old and well advanced in years. YHWH says to him, “You are old and advanced in years, and there remains yet very much land to be possessed.

“This is the land that still remains: all the regions of the Philistines, and all the Geshurites; from the Shihor, which is before Egypt, even to the border of Ekron northward, which is counted as Canaanite; the five lords of the Philistines; the Gazites, and the Ashdodites, the Ashkelonites, the Gittites, and the Ekronites; also the Avvim, on the south; all the land of the Canaanites, and Mearah that belongs to the Sidonians, to Aphek, to the border of the Amorites; and the land of the Gebalites, and all Lebanon, toward the sunrise, from Baal Gad under Mount Hermon to the entrance of Hamath; all the inhabitants of the hill country from Lebanon to Misrephoth Maim, even all the Sidonians. I will drive them out from before the children of Israel. Just allocate it to Israel for an inheritance, as I have commanded you. Now therefore divide this land for an inheritance to the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh.”
The Eastern Allotments · 13:8–33

With him the Reubenites and the Gadites receive their inheritance, which Moses gives them, beyond the Jordan eastward, even as Moses the servant of YHWH gives them: from Aroer, that is on the edge of the valley of the Arnon, and the city that is in the middle of the valley, and all the plain of Medeba to Dibon; and all the cities of Sihon king of the Amorites, who reign in Heshbon, to the border of the children of Ammon; and Gilead, and the border of the Geshurites and Maacathites, and all Mount Hermon, and all Bashan to Salecah; all the kingdom of Og in Bashan, who reigns in Ashtaroth and in Edrei (the same is left of the remnant of the Rephaim); for Moses attacks these, and drives them out. Nevertheless the children of Israel don’t drive out the Geshurites, nor the Maacathites: but Geshur and Maacath live within Israel to this day. Only he gives no inheritance to the tribe of Levi. The offerings of YHWH, the God of Israel, made by fire are his inheritance, as he speaks to him. Moses gives to the tribe of the children of Reuben according to their families. Their border is from Aroer, that is on the edge of the valley of the Arnon, and the city that is in the middle of the valley, and all the plain by Medeba; Heshbon, and all its cities that are in the plain; Dibon, Bamoth Baal, Beth Baal Meon, Jahaz, Kedemoth, Mephaath, Kiriathaim, Sibmah, Zereth Shahar in the mount of the valley, Beth Peor, the slopes of Pisgah, Beth Jeshimoth, all the cities of the plain, and all the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites, who reign in Heshbon, whom Moses strikes with the chiefs of Midian, Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba, the princes of Sihon, who lives in the land. The children of Israel also kill Balaam the son of Beor, the soothsayer, with the sword, among the rest of their slain.
The border of the children of Reuben is the bank of the Jordan. This is the inheritance of the children of Reuben according to their families, the cities and its villages.

Moses gives to the tribe of Gad, to the children of Gad, according to their families. Their border is Jazer, and all the cities of Gilead, and half the land of the children of Ammon, to Aroer that is near Rabbah; and from Heshbon to Ramath Mizpeh, and Betonim; and from Mahanaim to the border of Debir; and in the valley, Beth Haram, Beth Nimrah, Succoth, and Zaphon, the rest of the kingdom of Sihon king of Heshbon, the Jordan’s bank, to the uttermost part of the sea of Chinnereth beyond the Jordan eastward. This is the inheritance of the children of Gad according to their families, the cities and its villages.

Moses gives an inheritance to the half-tribe of Manasseh. It is for the half-tribe of the children of Manasseh according to their families. Their border is from Mahanaim, all Bashan, all the kingdom of Og king of Bashan, and all the villages of Jair, which are in Bashan, sixty cities. Half Gilead, Ashtaroth, and Edrei, the cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan, are for the children of Machir the son of Manasseh, even for the half of the children of Machir according to their families.

These are the inheritances which Moses distributes in the plains of Moab, beyond the Jordan at Jericho, eastward. But Moses gives no inheritance to the tribe of Levi. YHWH, the God of Israel, is their inheritance, as he speaks to them.
The Western Allotments Begin · 14:1–5

These are the inheritances which the children of Israel take in the land of Canaan, which Eleazar the priest, Joshua the son of Nun, and the heads of the fathers’ houses of the tribes of the children of Israel, distributed to them, by the lot of their inheritance, as YHWH commanded by Moses, for the nine tribes, and for the half-tribe. For Moses have given the inheritance of the two tribes and the half-tribe beyond the Jordan; but to the Levites he gives no inheritance among them. For the children of Joseph are two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim. They give no portion to the Levites in the land, except cities to dwell in, with their suburbs for their livestock and for their property. The children of Israel do as YHWH commands Moses, and they divide the land.
Caleb's Inheritance · 14:6–15

Then the children of Judah come near to Joshua in Gilgal. Caleb the son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite says to him, “You know the thing that YHWH spoke to Moses the man of God concerning me and concerning you in Kadesh Barnea. I was forty years old when Moses the servant of YHWH sent me from Kadesh Barnea to spy out the land. I brought him word again as it was in my heart. Nevertheless, my brothers who went up with me made the heart of the people melt; but I wholly followed YHWH my God. Moses swore on that day, saying, ‘Surely the land where you walked will be an inheritance to you and to your children forever, because you have wholly followed YHWH my God.’

“Now, look, YHWH has kept me alive, as he spoke, these forty-five years, from the time that YHWH spoke this word to Moses, while Israel walked in the wilderness. Now, look, I am eighty-five years old, today. As yet I am as strong today as I was in the day that Moses sent me. As my strength was then, even so is my strength now for war, to go out and to come in. Now therefore give me this hill country, of which YHWH spoke in that day; for you heard in that day how the Anakim were there, and great and fortified cities. It may be that YHWH will be with me, and I will drive them out, as YHWH said.”

Joshua blesses him; and he gives Hebron to Caleb the son of Jephunneh for an inheritance. Therefore Hebron becomes the inheritance of Caleb the son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite to this day, because he follows YHWH, the God of Israel wholeheartedly. Now the name of Hebron before is Kiriath Arba, after the greatest man among the Anakim. Then the land has rest from war.
The Allotment of Judah · 15:1–12

The lot for the tribe of the children of Judah according to their families is to the border of Edom, even to the wilderness of Zin southward, at the uttermost part of the south.
