Their south border is from the uttermost part of the Salt Sea, from the bay that looks southward; and it goes out southward of the ascent of Akrabbim, and passes along to Zin, and goes up by the south of Kadesh Barnea, and passes along by Hezron, goes up to Addar, and turns towards Karka; and it passes along to Azmon, goes out at the brook of Egypt; and the border ends at the sea. This will be your south border. The east border is the Salt Sea, even to the end of the Jordan. The border of the north quarter is from the bay of the sea at the end of the Jordan. The border goes up to Beth Hoglah, and passes along by the north of Beth Arabah; and the border goes up to the stone of Bohan the son of Reuben. The border goes up to Debir from the valley of Achor, and so northward, looking toward Gilgal, that faces the ascent of Adummim, which is on the south side of the river. The border passes along to the waters of En Shemesh, and ends at En Rogel. The border goes up by the valley of the son of Hinnom to the side of the Jebusite (also called Jerusalem) southward; and the border goes up to the top of the mountain that lies before the valley of Hinnom westward, which is at the farthest part of the valley of Rephaim northward. The border extended from the top of the mountain to the spring of the waters of Nephtoah, and goes out to the cities of Mount Ephron; and the border extended to Baalah (also called Kiriath Jearim); and the border turns about from Baalah westward to Mount Seir, and passes along to the side of Mount Jearim (also called Chesalon) on the north, and goes down to Beth Shemesh, and passes along by Timnah; and the border goes out to the side of Ekron northward; and the border extended to Shikkeron, and passes along to Mount Baalah, and goes out at Jabneel; and the goings out of the border are at the sea. The west border is to the shore of the great sea. This is the border of the children of Judah according to their families.
Caleb Takes Hebron and Debir · 15:13–19

He gives to Caleb the son of Jephunneh a portion among the children of Judah, according to the commandment of YHWH to Joshua, even Kiriath Arba, named after the father of Anak (also called Hebron). Caleb drives out the three sons of Anak: Sheshai, and Ahiman, and Talmai, the children of Anak. He goes up against the inhabitants of Debir: now the name of Debir before is Kiriath Sepher. Caleb says, “He who strikes Kiriath Sepher, and takes it, to him I will give Achsah my daughter as wife.” Othniel the son of Kenaz, the brother of Caleb, takes it: and he gives him Achsah his daughter as wife. When she comes, she has him ask her father for a field. She gets off her donkey, and Caleb says, “What do you want?”
She says, “Give me a blessing. Because you have set me in the land of the South, give me also springs of water.”
So he gives her the upper springs and the lower springs.
The Cities of Judah · 15:20–63

This is the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Judah according to their families. The farthest cities of the tribe of the children of Judah toward the border of Edom in the South are Kabzeel, Eder, Jagur, Kinah, Dimonah, Adadah, Kedesh, Hazor, Ithnan, Ziph, Telem, Bealoth, Hazor Hadattah, Kerioth Hezron (also called Hazor), Amam, Shema, Moladah, Hazar Gaddah, Heshmon, Beth Pelet, Hazar Shual, Beersheba, Biziothiah, Baalah, Iim, Ezem, Eltolad, Chesil, Hormah, Ziklag, Madmannah, Sansannah, Lebaoth, Shilhim, Ain, and Rimmon. All the cities are twenty-nine, with their villages.
In the lowland, Eshtaol, Zorah, Ashnah, Zanoah, En Gannim, Tappuah, Enam, Jarmuth, Adullam, Socoh, Azekah, Shaaraim, Adithaim and Gederah (or Gederothaim); fourteen cities with their villages.
Zenan, Hadashah, Migdal Gad, Dilean, Mizpah, Joktheel, Lachish, Bozkath, Eglon, Cabbon, Lahmam, Chitlish, Gederoth, Beth Dagon, Naamah, and Makkedah; sixteen cities with their villages.
Libnah, Ether, Ashan, Iphtah, Ashnah, Nezib, Keilah, Achzib, and Mareshah; nine cities with their villages.

Ekron, with its towns and its villages; from Ekron even to the sea, all that are by the side of Ashdod, with their villages. Ashdod, its towns and its villages; Gaza, its towns and its villages; to the brook of Egypt, and the great sea with its coastline.
In the hill country, Shamir, Jattir, Socoh, Dannah, Kiriath Sannah (which is Debir), Anab, Eshtemoh, Anim, Goshen, Holon, and Giloh; eleven cities with their villages.
Arab, Dumah, Eshan, Janim, Beth Tappuah, Aphekah, Humtah, Kiriath Arba (also called Hebron), and Zior; nine cities with their villages.
Maon, Carmel, Ziph, Jutah, Jezreel, Jokdeam, Zanoah, Kain, Gibeah, and Timnah; ten cities with their villages.
Halhul, Beth Zur, Gedor, Maarath, Beth Anoth, and Eltekon; six cities with their villages. Kiriath Baal (also called Kiriath Jearim), and Rabbah; two cities with their villages.
In the wilderness, Beth Arabah, Middin, Secacah, Nibshan, the City of Salt, and En Gedi; six cities with their villages.
As for the Jebusites, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the children of Judah can’t drive them out; but the Jebusites live with the children of Judah at Jerusalem to this day.
The Allotment of Ephraim · 16:1–10

The lot comes out for the children of Joseph from the Jordan at Jericho, at the waters of Jericho on the east, even the wilderness, going up from Jericho through the hill country to Bethel. It goes out from Bethel to Luz, and passes along to the border of the Archites to Ataroth; and it goes down westward to the border of the Japhletites, to the border of Beth Horon the lower, and on to Gezer; and ends at the sea.

The children of Joseph, Manasseh and Ephraim, take their inheritance. This is the border of the children of Ephraim according to their families. The border of their inheritance eastward is Ataroth Addar, to Beth Horon the upper. The border goes out westward at Michmethath on the north. The border turns about eastward to Taanath Shiloh, and passes along it on the east of Janoah. It goes down from Janoah to Ataroth, to Naarah, reaches to Jericho, and goes out at the Jordan. From Tappuah the border goes along westward to the brook of Kanah; and ends at the sea. This is the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Ephraim according to their families; together with the cities which are set apart for the children of Ephraim in the middle of the inheritance of the children of Manasseh, all the cities with their villages. They don’t drive out the Canaanites who live in Gezer; but the Canaanites dwell in the territory of Ephraim to this day, and have become servants to do forced labor.
The Allotment of Manasseh · 17:1–13

This is the lot for the tribe of Manasseh, for he is the firstborn of Joseph. As for Machir the firstborn of Manasseh, the father of Gilead, because he is a man of war, therefore he has Gilead and Bashan. So this is for the rest of the children of Manasseh according to their families: for the children of Abiezer, for the children of Helek, for the children of Asriel, for the children of Shechem, for the children of Hepher, and for the children of Shemida. These are the male children of Manasseh the son of Joseph according to their families. But Zelophehad, the son of Hepher, the son of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh, has no sons, but daughters. These are the names of his daughters: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah. They come to Eleazar the priest, and to Joshua the son of Nun, and to the princes, saying, “YHWH commanded Moses to give us an inheritance among our brothers.” Therefore according to the commandment of YHWH he gives them an inheritance among the brothers of their father. Ten parts fall to Manasseh, besides the land of Gilead and Bashan, which is beyond the Jordan; because the daughters of Manasseh have an inheritance among his sons. The land of Gilead belongs to the rest of the sons of Manasseh. The border of Manasseh is from Asher to Michmethath, which is before Shechem. The border goes along to the right hand, to the inhabitants of En Tappuah. The land of Tappuah belongs to Manasseh; but Tappuah on the border of Manasseh belongs to the children of Ephraim. The border goes down to the brook of Kanah, southward of the brook. These cities belong to Ephraim among the cities of Manasseh. The border of Manasseh is on the north side of the brook, and ends at the sea. Southward it is Ephraim’s, and northward it is Manasseh’s, and the sea is his border. They reach to Asher on the north, and to Issachar on the east. Manasseh has three heights in Issachar, in Asher Beth Shean and its towns, and Ibleam and its towns, and the inhabitants of Dor and its towns, and the inhabitants of Endor and its towns, and the inhabitants of Taanach and its towns, and the inhabitants of Megiddo and its towns. Yet the children of Manasseh can’t drive out the inhabitants of those cities; but the Canaanites would dwell in that land.
When the children of Israel have grown strong, they put the Canaanites to forced labor, and don’t utterly drive them out.
Joseph's Complaint and Joshua's Response · 17:14–18
The children of Joseph speak to Joshua, saying, “Why have you given me just one lot and one part for an inheritance, since we are a numerous people, because YHWH has blessed us so far?”

Joshua says to them, “If you are a numerous people, go up to the forest, and clear land for yourself there in the land of the Perizzites and of the Rephaim; since the hill country of Ephraim is too narrow for you.”

The children of Joseph say, “The hill country is not enough for us. All the Canaanites who dwell in the land of the valley have chariots of iron, both those who are in Beth Shean and its towns, and those who are in the valley of Jezreel.”

Joshua speaks to the house of Joseph, that is, to Ephraim and to Manasseh, saying, “You are a numerous people, and have great power. You will not have one lot only; but the hill country will be yours. Although it is a forest, you will cut it down, and it’s farthest extent will be yours; for you will drive out the Canaanites, though they have chariots of iron, and though they are strong.”
The Tabernacle Set Up at Shiloh · 18:1–10

The whole congregation of the children of Israel assembles themselves together at Shiloh, and sets up the Tent of Meeting there. The land is subdued before them. Seven tribes remain among the children of Israel, which have not yet divided their inheritance. Joshua says to the children of Israel, “How long will you neglect to go in to possess the land, which YHWH, the God of your fathers, has given you? Appoint for yourselves three men from each tribe. I will send them, and they will arise, walk through the land, and describe it according to their inheritance; and they will come to me. They will divide it into seven portions. Judah will live in his borders on the south, and the house of Joseph will live in their borders on the north. You will survey the land into seven parts, and bring the description here to me; and I will cast lots for you here before YHWH our God. However, the Levites have no portion among you; for the priesthood of YHWH is their inheritance. Gad, Reuben, and the half-tribe of Manasseh have received their inheritance east of the Jordan, which Moses the servant of YHWH gave them.”
The men arise and go. Joshua commands those who go to survey the land, saying, “Go walk through the land, survey it, and come again to me. I will cast lots for you here before YHWH in Shiloh.”

The men go and pass through the land, and survey it by cities into seven portions in a book. They come to Joshua to the camp at Shiloh. Joshua casts lots for them in Shiloh before YHWH. There Joshua divides the land to the children of Israel according to their divisions.
The Allotment of Benjamin · 18:11–28

The lot of the tribe of the children of Benjamin comes up according to their families. The border of their lot goes out between the children of Judah and the children of Joseph. Their border on the north quarter is from the Jordan. The border goes up to the side of Jericho on the north, and goes up through the hill country westward. It ends at the wilderness of Beth Aven. The border passes along from there to Luz, to the side of Luz (also called Bethel), southward. The border goes down to Ataroth Addar, by the mountain that lies on the south of Beth Horon the lower. The border extends, and turns around on the west quarter southward, from the mountain that lies before Beth Horon southward; and ends at Kiriath Baal (also called Kiriath Jearim), a city of the children of Judah. This is the west quarter. The south quarter is from the farthest part of Kiriath Jearim. The border goes out westward, and goes out to the spring of the waters of Nephtoah. The border goes down to the farthest part of the mountain that lies before the valley of the son of Hinnom, which is in the valley of Rephaim northward. It goes down to the valley of Hinnom, to the side of the Jebusite southward, and goes down to En Rogel. It extends northward, goes out at En Shemesh, and goes out to Geliloth, which is over against the ascent of Adummim. It goes down to the stone of Bohan the son of Reuben. It passes along to the side over against the Arabah northward, and goes down to the Arabah. The border passes along to the side of Beth Hoglah northward; and the border ends at the north bay of the Salt Sea, at the south end of the Jordan. This is the south border. The Jordan is its border on the east quarter. This is the inheritance of the children of Benjamin, by the borders around it, according to their families. Now the cities of the tribe of the children of Benjamin according to their families are Jericho, Beth Hoglah, Emek Keziz, Beth Arabah, Zemaraim, Bethel, Avvim, Parah, Ophrah, Chephar Ammoni, Ophni, and Geba; twelve cities with their villages. Gibeon, Ramah, Beeroth, Mizpeh, Chephirah, Mozah, Rekem, Irpeel, Taralah, Zelah, Eleph, the Jebusite (also called Jerusalem), Gibeath, and Kiriath; fourteen cities with their villages. This is the inheritance of the children of Benjamin according to their families.
The Allotment of Simeon · 19:1–9

The second lot comes out for Simeon, even for the tribe of the children of Simeon according to their families. Their inheritance is in the middle of the inheritance of the children of Judah. They have for their inheritance Beersheba (or Sheba), Moladah, Hazar Shual, Balah, Ezem, Eltolad, Bethul, Hormah, Ziklag, Beth Marcaboth, Hazar Susah, Beth Lebaoth, and Sharuhen; thirteen cities with their villages; Ain, Rimmon, Ether, and Ashan; four cities with their villages; and all the villages that are around these cities to Baalath Beer, Ramah of the South. This is the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Simeon according to their families. Out of the part of the children of Judah are the inheritance of the children of Simeon; for the portion of the children of Judah are too much for them. Therefore the children of Simeon have inheritance in the middle of their inheritance.
The Allotment of Zebulun · 19:10–16

The third lot comes up for the children of Zebulun according to their families. The border of their inheritance is to Sarid. Their border goes up westward, even to Maralah, and reaches to Dabbesheth. It reaches to the brook that is before Jokneam. It turns from Sarid eastward toward the sunrise to the border of Chisloth Tabor. It goes out to Daberath, and goes up to Japhia. From there it passes along eastward to Gath Hepher, to Ethkazin; and it goes out at Rimmon which stretches to Neah. The border turns around it on the north to Hannathon; and it ends at the valley of Iphtah El; Kattath, Nahalal, Shimron, Idalah, and Bethlehem: twelve cities with their villages. This is the inheritance of the children of Zebulun according to their families, these cities with their villages.
The Allotment of Issachar · 19:17–23

The fourth lot comes out for Issachar, even for the children of Issachar according to their families. Their border is to Jezreel, Chesulloth, Shunem, Hapharaim, Shion, Anaharath, Rabbith, Kishion, Ebez, Remeth, Engannim, En Haddah, and Beth Pazzez. The border reaches to Tabor, Shahazumah, and Beth Shemesh. Their border ends at the Jordan: sixteen cities with their villages. This is the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Issachar according to their families, the cities with their villages.
The Allotment of Asher · 19:24–31

The fifth lot comes out for the tribe of the children of Asher according to their families. Their border is Helkath, Hali, Beten, Achshaph, Allammelech, Amad, Mishal. It reaches to Carmel westward, and to Shihorlibnath. It turns toward the sunrise to Beth Dagon, and reaches to Zebulun, and to the valley of Iphtah El northward to Beth Emek and Neiel. It goes out to Cabul on the left hand, and Ebron, Rehob, Hammon, and Kanah, even to great Sidon. The border turns to Ramah, to the fortified city of Tyre; and the border turns to Hosah. It ends at the sea by the region of Achzib; Ummah also, and Aphek, and Rehob: twenty-two cities with their villages. This is the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Asher according to their families, these cities with their villages.
The Allotment of Naphtali · 19:32–39

The sixth lot comes out for the children of Naphtali, even for the children of Naphtali according to their families. Their border is from Heleph, from the oak in Zaanannim, Adami-nekeb, and Jabneel, to Lakkum. It ends at the Jordan. The border turns westward to Aznoth Tabor, and goes out from there to Hukkok. It reaches to Zebulun on the south, and reaches to Asher on the west, and to Judah at the Jordan toward the sunrise. The fortified cities are Ziddim, Zer, Hammath, Rakkath, Chinnereth, Adamah, Ramah, Hazor, Kedesh, Edrei, En Hazor, Iron, Migdal El, Horem, Beth Anath, and Beth Shemesh; nineteen cities with their villages. This is the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Naphtali according to their families, the cities with their villages.
The Allotment of Dan · 19:40–48

The seventh lot comes out for the tribe of the children of Dan according to their families. The border of their inheritance is Zorah, Eshtaol, Irshemesh, Shaalabbin, Aijalon, Ithlah, Elon, Timnah, Ekron, Eltekeh, Gibbethon, Baalath, Jehud, Bene Berak, Gath Rimmon, Me Jarkon, and Rakkon, with the border over against Joppa. The border of the children of Dan goes out beyond them; for the children of Dan goes up and fights against Leshem, and takes it, and strikes it with the edge of the sword, and possesses it, and lives therein, and calls Leshem, Dan, after the name of Dan their forefather. This is the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Dan according to their families, these cities with their villages.
Joshua's Own Inheritance · 19:49–51

So they finish distributing the land for inheritance by its borders. The children of Israel give an inheritance to Joshua the son of Nun among them. According to YHWH’s commandment, they give him the city which he asks, even Timnathserah in the hill country of Ephraim; and he builds the city, and lives there. These are the inheritances, which Eleazar the priest, Joshua the son of Nun, and the heads of the fathers’ houses of the tribes of the children of Israel, distributed for inheritance by lot in Shiloh before YHWH, at the door of the Tent of Meeting. So they finish dividing the land.
The Cities of Refuge · 20:1–9

YHWH speaks to Joshua, saying, “Speak to the children of Israel, saying, ‘Assign the cities of refuge, of which I spoke to you by Moses, that the man slayer who kills any person accidentally or unintentionally may flee there. They will be to you for a refuge from the avenger of blood. He will flee to one of those cities, and will stand at the entrance of the gate of the city, and declare his case in the ears of the elders of that city. They will take him into the city with them, and give him a place, that he may live among them. If the avenger of blood pursues him, then they will not deliver up the man slayer into his hand; because he struck his neighbor unintentionally, and didn’t hate him before. He will dwell in that city until he stands before the congregation for judgment, until the death of the high priest that will be in those days. Then the man slayer will return, and come to his own city, and to his own house, to the city he fled from.’”

They set apart Kedesh in Galilee in the hill country of Naphtali, Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim, and Kiriath Arba (also called Hebron) in the hill country of Judah. Beyond the Jordan at Jericho eastward, they assign Bezer in the wilderness in the plain out of the tribe of Reuben, Ramoth in Gilead out of the tribe of Gad, and Golan in Bashan out of the tribe of Manasseh. These are the appointed cities for all the children of Israel, and for the alien who lives among them, that whoever kills any person unintentionally might flee there, and not die by the hand of the avenger of blood, until he stands trial before the congregation.
The Levitical Cities · 21:1–42

Then the heads of fathers’ houses of the Levites come near to Eleazar the priest, and to Joshua the son of Nun, and to the heads of fathers’ houses of the tribes of the children of Israel. They speak to them at Shiloh in the land of Canaan, saying, “YHWH commanded through Moses to give us cities to dwell in, with their suburbs for our livestock.”

The children of Israel give to the Levites out of their inheritance, according to the commandment of YHWH, these cities with their suburbs. The lot comes out for the families of the Kohathites. The children of Aaron the priest, who are of the Levites, have thirteen cities by lot out of the tribe of Judah, out of the tribe of the Simeonites, and out of the tribe of Benjamin. The rest of the children of Kohath has ten cities by lot out of the families of the tribe of Ephraim, out of the tribe of Dan, and out of the half-tribe of Manasseh. The children of Gershon have thirteen cities by lot out of the families of the tribe of Issachar, out of the tribe of Asher, out of the tribe of Naphtali, and out of the half-tribe of Manasseh in Bashan. The children of Merari according to their families have twelve cities out of the tribe of Reuben, out of the tribe of Gad, and out of the tribe of Zebulun. The children of Israel give these cities with their suburbs by lot to the Levites, as YHWH commanded by Moses. They give out of the tribe of the children of Judah, and out of the tribe of the children of Simeon, these cities which are mentioned by name: and they are for the children of Aaron, of the families of the Kohathites, who are of the children of Levi; for theirs are the first lot. They give them Kiriath Arba, named after the father of Anak (also called Hebron), in the hill country of Judah, with its suburbs around it. But they give the fields of the city and its villages to Caleb the son of Jephunneh for his possession. To the children of Aaron the priest they give Hebron with its suburbs, the city of refuge for the man slayer, Libnah with its suburbs, Jattir with its suburbs, Eshtemoa with its suburbs, Holon with its suburbs, Debir with its suburbs, Ain with its suburbs, Juttah with its suburbs, and Beth Shemesh with its suburbs: nine cities out of those two tribes. Out of the tribe of Benjamin, Gibeon with its suburbs, Geba with its suburbs, Anathoth with its suburbs, and Almon with its suburbs: four cities. All the cities of the children of Aaron, the priests, are thirteen cities with their suburbs.

The families of the children of Kohath, the Levites, even the rest of the children of Kohath, have the cities of their lot out of the tribe of Ephraim. They give them Shechem with its suburbs in the hill country of Ephraim, the city of refuge for the man slayer, and Gezer with its suburbs, Kibzaim with its suburbs, and Beth Horon with its suburbs: four cities. Out of the tribe of Dan, Elteke with its suburbs, Gibbethon with its suburbs, Aijalon with its suburbs, Gath Rimmon with its suburbs: four cities. Out of the half-tribe of Manasseh, Taanach with its suburbs, and Gath Rimmon with its suburbs: two cities. All the cities of the families of the rest of the children of Kohath are ten with their suburbs.

They give to the children of Gershon, of the families of the Levites, out of the half-tribe of Manasseh Golan in Bashan with its suburbs, the city of refuge for the man slayer, and Be Eshterah with its suburbs: two cities. Out of the tribe of Issachar, Kishion with its suburbs, Daberath with its suburbs, Jarmuth with its suburbs, En Gannim with its suburbs: four cities. Out of the tribe of Asher, Mishal with its suburbs, Abdon with its suburbs, Helkath with its suburbs, and Rehob with its suburbs: four cities. Out of the tribe of Naphtali, Kedesh in Galilee with its suburbs, the city of refuge for the man slayer, Hammothdor with its suburbs, and Kartan with its suburbs: three cities. All the cities of the Gershonites according to their families are thirteen cities with their suburbs.

To the families of the children of Merari, the rest of the Levites, out of the tribe of Zebulun, Jokneam with its suburbs, Kartah with its suburbs, Dimnah with its suburbs, and Nahalal with its suburbs: four cities. Out of the tribe of Reuben, Bezer with its suburbs, Jahaz with its suburbs, Kedemoth with its suburbs, and Mephaath with its suburbs: four cities. Out of the tribe of Gad, Ramoth in Gilead with its suburbs, the city of refuge for the man slayer, and Mahanaim with its suburbs, Heshbon with its suburbs, Jazer with its suburbs: four cities in all. All these are the cities of the children of Merari according to their families, even the rest of the families of the Levites. Their lot is twelve cities.

All the cities of the Levites among the possessions of the children of Israel are forty-eight cities with their suburbs. Each of these cities includes their suburbs around them. It is this way with all these cities.
Not One Word Falls · 21:43–45

So YHWH gives to Israel all the land which he swears to give to their fathers. They possess it, and live in it. YHWH gives them rest all around, according to all that he swears to their fathers. Not a man of all their enemies stands before them. YHWH delivers all their enemies into their hand. Nothing fails of any good thing which YHWH has spoken to the house of Israel. All come to pass.
The Eastern Tribes Sent Home · 22:1–9

Then Joshua calls the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, and says to them, “You have kept all that Moses the servant of YHWH commanded you, and have listened to my voice in all that I commanded you. You have not left your brothers these many days to this day, but have performed the duty of the commandment of YHWH your God. Now YHWH your God has given rest to your brothers, as he spoke to them. Therefore now return and go to your tents, to the land of your possession, which Moses the servant of YHWH gave you beyond the Jordan. Only take diligent heed to do the commandment and the law which Moses the servant of YHWH commanded you, to love YHWH your God, to walk in all his ways, to keep his commandments, to hold fast to him, and to serve him with all your heart and with all your soul.”

So Joshua blesses them, and sends them away; and they go to their tents. Now to the one half-tribe of Manasseh Moses has given inheritance in Bashan; but to the other half gives Joshua among their brothers beyond the Jordan westward. Moreover when Joshua sends them away to their tents, he blesses them, and speaks to them, saying, “Return with much wealth to your tents, with very much livestock, with silver, with gold, with brass, with iron, and with very much clothing. Divide the plunder of your enemies with your brothers.”

The children of Reuben and the children of Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh return, and depart from the children of Israel out of Shiloh, which is in the land of Canaan, to go to the land of Gilead, to the land of their possession, which they own, according to the commandment of YHWH by Moses.
The Altar by the Jordan · 22:10–20

When they come to the region about the Jordan, that is in the land of Canaan, the children of Reuben and the children of Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh build there an altar by the Jordan, a great altar to look at. The children of Israel hear this, “Look, the children of Reuben and the children of Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh have built an altar in the border of the land of Canaan, in the region around the Jordan, on the side that belongs to the children of Israel.” When the children of Israel hear of it, the whole congregation of the children of Israel gathers themselves together at Shiloh, to go up against them to war. The children of Israel send to the children of Reuben, and to the children of Gad, and to the half-tribe of Manasseh, into the land of Gilead, Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest. With him are ten princes, one prince of a fathers’ house for each of the tribes of Israel; and they are each head of their fathers’ houses among the thousands of Israel. They come to the children of Reuben, and to the children of Gad, and to the half-tribe of Manasseh, to the land of Gilead, and they speak with them, saying, “Thus says the whole congregation of YHWH, ‘What trespass is this that you have committed against the God of Israel, to turn away today from following YHWH, in that you have built yourselves an altar, to rebel today against YHWH? Is the iniquity of Peor too little for us, from which we have not cleansed ourselves to this day, although there came a plague on the congregation of YHWH, that you must turn away today from following YHWH? It will be, since you rebel today against YHWH, that tomorrow he will be angry with the whole congregation of Israel. However, if the land of your possession is unclean, then pass over to the land of the possession of YHWH, in which YHWH’s tabernacle dwells, and take possession among us; but don’t rebel against YHWH, nor rebel against us, in building an altar other than YHWH our God’s altar. Didn’t Achan the son of Zerah commit a trespass in the devoted thing, and wrath fell on all the congregation of Israel? That man didn’t perish alone in his iniquity.’”
The Eastern Tribes' Defense · 22:21–29

Then the children of Reuben and the children of Gad and the half-tribe of Manasseh answer, and speak to the heads of the thousands of Israel, “The Mighty One, God, YHWH, the Mighty One, God, YHWH, he knows; and Israel will know: if it was in rebellion, or if in trespass against YHWH (don’t save us today), that we have built us an altar to turn away from following YHWH; or if to offer burnt offering or meal offering, or if to offer sacrifices of peace offerings, let YHWH himself require it.

“If we have not out of concern done this, and for a reason, saying, ‘In time to come your children might speak to our children, saying, “What have you to do with YHWH, the God of Israel? For YHWH has made the Jordan a border between us and you, you children of Reuben and children of Gad. You have no portion in YHWH.”’ So your children might make our children cease from fearing YHWH.

“Therefore we said, ‘Let’s now prepare to build ourselves an altar, not for burnt offering, nor for sacrifice; but it will be a witness between us and you, and between our generations after us, that we may perform the service of YHWH before him with our burnt offerings, with our sacrifices, and with our peace offerings;’ that your children may not tell our children in time to come, ‘You have no portion in YHWH.’

“Therefore we said, ‘It will be, when they tell us or our generations this in time to come, that we will say, “Look the pattern of YHWH’s altar, which our fathers made, not for burnt offering, nor for sacrifice; but it is a witness between us and you.”’

“Far be it from us that we should rebel against YHWH, and turn away today from following YHWH, to build an altar for burnt offering, for meal offering, or for sacrifice, besides YHWH our God’s altar that is before his tabernacle!”
The Altar Named Witness · 22:30–34

When Phinehas the priest, and the princes of the congregation, even the heads of the thousands of Israel that are with him, hear the words that the children of Reuben and the children of Gad and the children of Manasseh speak, it pleases them well. Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest says to the children of Reuben, to the children of Gad, and to the children of Manasseh, “Today we know that YHWH is among us, because you have not committed this trespass against YHWH. Now you have delivered the children of Israel out of YHWH’s hand.” Phinehas the son of Eleazar the priest, and the princes, returns from the children of Reuben, and from the children of Gad, out of the land of Gilead, to the land of Canaan, to the children of Israel, and brings them word again. The thing pleases the children of Israel; and the children of Israel bless God, and speak no more of going up against them to war, to destroy the land in which the children of Reuben and the children of Gad live. The children of Reuben and the children of Gad name the altar “A Witness Between Us that YHWH is God.”
Joshua Summons the Leaders · 23:1–5

After many days, when YHWH has given rest to Israel from their enemies all around, and Joshua is old and well advanced in years, Joshua calls for all Israel, for their elders and for their heads, and for their judges and for their officers, and says to them, “I am old and well advanced in years. You have seen all that YHWH your God has done to all these nations because of you; for it is YHWH your God who has fought for you. Look, I have allotted to you these nations that remain, to be an inheritance for your tribes, from the Jordan, with all the nations that I have cut off, even to the great sea toward the going down of the sun. YHWH your God will thrust them out from before you, and drive them from out of your sight. You will possess their land, as YHWH your God spoke to you.
The Charge to Obedience · 23:6–13

“Therefore be very courageous to keep and to do all that is written in the book of the law of Moses, that you not turn away from it to the right hand or to the left; that you not come among these nations, these that remain among you; neither make mention of the name of their gods, nor cause to swear by them, neither serve them, nor bow down yourselves to them; but hold fast to YHWH your God, as you have done to this day.

“For YHWH has driven great and strong nations out from before you. But as for you, no man has stood before you to this day. One man of you will chase a thousand; for it is YHWH your God who fights for you, as he spoke to you. Take good heed therefore to yourselves, that you love YHWH your God.

“But if you do at all go back, and hold fast to the remnant of these nations, even these who remain among you, and make marriages with them, and go in to them, and they to you; know for a certainty that YHWH your God will no longer drive these nations from out of your sight; but they will be a snare and a trap to you, a scourge in your sides, and thorns in your eyes, until you perish from off this good land which YHWH your God has given you.
The Way of All the Earth · 23:14–16

“Look, today I am going the way of all the earth. You know in all your hearts and in all your souls that not one thing has failed of all the good things which YHWH your God spoke concerning you. All have happened to you. Not one thing has failed of it. It will happen that as all the good things have come on you of which YHWH your God spoke to you, so YHWH will bring on you all the evil things, until he has destroyed you from off this good land which YHWH your God has given you, when you disobey the covenant of YHWH your God, which he commanded you, and go and serve other gods, and bow down yourselves to them. Then YHWH’s anger will be kindled against you, and you will perish quickly from off the good land which he has given to you.”
The Assembly at Shechem · 24:1–2

Joshua gathers all the tribes of Israel to Shechem, and calls for the elders of Israel, for their heads, for their judges, and for their officers; and they present themselves before God. Joshua says to all the people, “YHWH says, the God of Israel, ‘Your fathers lived of old time beyond the River, even Terah, the father of Abraham, and the father of Nahor: and they served other gods.
YHWH's Mighty Acts Recounted · 24:3–13

I took your father Abraham from beyond the River, and led him throughout all the land of Canaan, and multiplied his offspring, and gave him Isaac. I gave to Isaac Jacob and Esau: and I gave to Esau Mount Seir, to possess it. Jacob and his children went down into Egypt.

“‘I sent Moses and Aaron, and I plagued Egypt, according to that which I did among them: and afterward I brought you out. I brought your fathers out of Egypt: and you came to the sea. The Egyptians pursued your fathers with chariots and with horsemen to the Red Sea. When they cried out to YHWH, he put darkness between you and the Egyptians, and brought the sea on them, and covered them; and your eyes saw what I did in Egypt. You lived in the wilderness many days.

“‘I brought you into the land of the Amorites, that lived beyond the Jordan. They fought with you, and I gave them into your hand. You possessed their land, and I destroyed them from before you. Then Balak the son of Zippor, king of Moab, arose and fought against Israel. He sent and called Balaam the son of Beor to curse you, but I would not listen to Balaam; therefore he blessed you still. So I delivered you out of his hand.

“‘You went over the Jordan, and came to Jericho. The men of Jericho fought against you, the Amorite, the Perizzite, the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Girgashite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite; and I delivered them into your hand. I sent the hornet before you, which drove them out from before you, even the two kings of the Amorites; not with your sword, nor with your bow. I gave you a land whereon you had not labored, and cities which you didn’t build, and you live in them. You eat of vineyards and olive groves which you didn’t plant.’
Choose This Day · 24:14–18

“Now therefore fear YHWH, and serve him in sincerity and in truth. Put away the gods which your fathers served beyond the River, in Egypt; and serve YHWH. If it seems evil to you to serve YHWH, choose today whom you will serve; whether the gods which your fathers served that were beyond the River, or the gods of the Amorites, in whose land you dwell; but as for me and my house, we will serve YHWH.”

The people answer, “Far be it from us that we should forsake YHWH, to serve other gods; for it is YHWH our God who brought us and our fathers up out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage, and who did those great signs in our sight, and preserved us in all the way in which we went, and among all the peoples through the middle of whom we passed. YHWH drove out from before us all the peoples, even the Amorites who lived in the land. Therefore we also will serve YHWH; for he is our God.”
Joshua's Warning and the Renewed Pledge · 24:19–28

Joshua says to the people, “You can’t serve YHWH, for he is a holy God. He is a jealous God. He will not forgive your disobedience nor your sins. If you forsake YHWH, and serve foreign gods, then he will turn and do you evil, and consume you, after he has done you good.”
The people say to Joshua, “No, but we will serve YHWH.” Joshua says to the people, “You are witnesses against yourselves that you have chosen YHWH yourselves, to serve him.”
They say, “We are witnesses.”
“Now therefore put away the foreign gods which are among you, and incline your heart to YHWH, the God of Israel.”
The people say to Joshua, “We will serve YHWH our God, and we will listen to his voice.”

So Joshua makes a covenant with the people that day, and makes for them a statute and an ordinance in Shechem. Joshua writes these words in the book of the law of God; and he takes a great stone, and sets it up there under the oak that is by the sanctuary of YHWH. Joshua says to all the people, “Look, this stone will be a witness against us, for it has heard all YHWH’s words which he spoke to us. It will be therefore a witness against you, lest you deny your God.” So Joshua sends the people away, each to his own inheritance.
The Death of Joshua, the Burial of Joseph, the Death of Eleazar · 24:29–33

After these things, Joshua the son of Nun, the servant of YHWH, dies, being one hundred ten years old. They bury him in the border of his inheritance in Timnathserah, which is in the hill country of Ephraim, on the north of the mountain of Gaash. Israel serves YHWH all the days of Joshua, and all the days of the elders who outlive Joshua, and has known all the work of YHWH, that he has worked for Israel. They bury the bones of Joseph, which the children of Israel bring up out of Egypt, in Shechem, in the parcel of ground which Jacob buys from the sons of Hamor the father of Shechem for a hundred pieces of silver. They become the inheritance of the children of Joseph. Eleazar the son of Aaron dies. They bury him in the hill of Phinehas his son, which is given him in the hill country of Ephraim.
After Joshua · 1:1–7
After the death of Joshua, the children of Israel asks of YHWH, saying, “Who should go up for us first against the Canaanites, to fight against them?”
YHWH says, “Judah will go up. Look, I have delivered the land into his hand.”

Judah says to Simeon his brother, “Come up with me into my lot, that we may fight against the Canaanites; and I likewise will go with you into your lot.” So Simeon goes with him. Judah goes up, and YHWH delivers the Canaanites and the Perizzites into their hand. They strike ten thousand men in Bezek. They find Adoni-Bezek in Bezek, and they fight against him. They strike the Canaanites and the Perizzites. But Adoni-Bezek flees. They pursue him, catch him, and cut off his thumbs and his big toes. Adoni-Bezek says, “Seventy kings, having their thumbs and their big toes cut off, scavenged under my table. As I have done, so God has done to me.” They bring him to Jerusalem, and he dies there.
Judah Takes the Hill Country · 1:8–15
The children of Judah fight against Jerusalem, take it, strike it with the edge of the sword, and set the city on fire.

After that, the children of Judah go down to fight against the Canaanites who live in the hill country, and in the South, and in the lowland. Judah goes against the Canaanites who live in Hebron. (The name of Hebron before that is Kiriath Arba.) They strike Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai.

From there he goes against the inhabitants of Debir. (The name of Debir before that is Kiriath Sepher.) Caleb says, “I will give Achsah my daughter as wife to the man who strikes Kiriath Sepher, and takes it.” Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb’s younger brother, takes it, so he gives him Achsah his daughter as his wife.
When she comes, she gets him to ask her father for a field. She gets off her donkey; and Caleb says to her, “What would you like?”
She says to him, “Give me a blessing; because you have set me in the land of the South, give me also springs of water.” Then Caleb gives her the upper springs and the lower springs.
The Kenites · 1:16

They are left to test Israel by them, to know whether they would listen to YHWH’s commandments, which he commands their fathers by Moses. The children of Israel live among the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites. They take their daughters to be their wives, and give their own daughters to their sons and serve their gods.

The children of Israel do that which is evil in YHWH’s sight, and forget YHWH their God, and serve the Baals and the Asheroth. When the children of Israel cry to YHWH, YHWH raises up a savior to the children of Israel, who saves them, even Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb’s younger brother. YHWH’s Spirit comes on him, and he judges Israel; and he goes out to war, and YHWH delivers Cushan Rishathaim king of Mesopotamia into his hand. His hand prevails against Cushan Rishathaim. The land has rest forty years, then Othniel the son of Kenaz dies.
Ehud and Eglon · 3:12–30

The children of Israel again do that which is evil in YHWH’s sight, and YHWH strengthens Eglon the king of Moab against Israel, because they have done that which is evil in YHWH’s sight. He gathers the children of Ammon and Amalek to himself; and he goes and strikes Israel, and they possess the city of palm trees. The children of Israel serve Eglon the king of Moab eighteen years. But when the children of Israel cry to YHWH, YHWH raises up a savior for them, Ehud the son of Gera, the Benjamite, a left-handed man. The children of Israel send tribute by him to Eglon the king of Moab. Ehud makes himself a sword which has two edges, a cubit in length; and he wears it under his clothing on his right thigh. He offers the tribute to Eglon king of Moab. Now Eglon is a very fat man. When he has finished offering the tribute, he sends away the people who carry the tribute. But he himself turns back from the stone idols that are by Gilgal, and says, “I have a secret message for you, O king.”
The king says, “Keep silence!” All who stand by him leave him.

Ehud comes to him; and he is sitting by himself alone in the cool upper room. Ehud says, “I have a message from God to you.” He arises out of his seat. Ehud puts out his left hand, and takes the sword from his right thigh, and thrusts it into his body: and the handle also goes in after the blade; and the fat closes on the blade, for he doesn’t draw the sword out of his body; and it comes out behind. Then Ehud goes out onto the porch, and shuts the doors of the upper room on him, and locks them.

After he has gone, his servants come and see that the doors of the upper room are locked. They say, “Surely he is covering his feet in the upper room.” They wait until they are ashamed; and look, he doesn’t open the doors of the upper room. Therefore they take the key and open them, and look, their lord has fallen down dead on the floor.

Ehud escapes while they wait, passed beyond the stone idols, and escape to Seirah. When he has come, he blows a trumpet in the hill country of Ephraim; and the children of Israel go down with him from the hill country, and he leads them.

He says to them, “Follow me; for YHWH has delivered your enemies the Moabites into your hand.” They follow him, and take the fords of the Jordan against the Moabites, and don’t allow any man to pass over. After him is Shamgar the son of Anath, who strikes six hundred men of the Philistines with an ox goad. He also saves Israel.

The children of Israel again do that which is evil in YHWH’s sight, when Ehud is dead. YHWH sells them into the hand of Jabin king of Canaan, who reigns in Hazor; the captain of whose army is Sisera, who lives in Harosheth of the Gentiles. Now Deborah, a prophetess, the wife of Lappidoth, judges Israel at that time. She sends and calls Barak the son of Abinoam out of Kedesh Naphtali, and says to him, “Hasn’t YHWH, the God of Israel, commanded, ‘Go and lead the way to Mount Tabor, and take with you ten thousand men of the children of Naphtali and of the children of Zebulun? Barak says to her, “If you will go with me, then I will go; but if you will not go with me, I will not go.”
She says, “I will surely go with you. Nevertheless, the journey that you take won’t be for your honor; for YHWH will sell Sisera into a woman’s hand.” Deborah arises, and goes with Barak to Kedesh.
Barak calls Zebulun and Naphtali together to Kedesh; and ten thousand men follow him; and Deborah goes up with him.

Now Heber the Kenite has separated himself from the Kenites, even from the children of Hobab, Moses’ brother-in-law, and has pitched his tent as far as the oak in Zaanannim, which is by Kedesh.

They tell Sisera that Barak the son of Abinoam is gone up to Mount Tabor. Sisera gathers together all his chariots, even nine hundred chariots of iron, and all the people who are with him, from Harosheth of the Gentiles, to the river Kishon.

Deborah says to Barak, “Go; for this is the day in which YHWH has delivered Sisera into your hand. Hasn’t YHWH gone out before you?” So Barak goes down from Mount Tabor, and ten thousand men after him. YHWH confused Sisera, all his chariots, and all his army, with the edge of the sword before Barak. Sisera abandons his chariot and flees away on his feet. However Sisera flees away on his feet to the tent of Jael the wife of Heber the Kenite; for there is peace between Jabin the king of Hazor and the house of Heber the Kenite. Jael goes out to meet Sisera, and says to him, “Turn in, my lord, turn in to me; don’t be afraid.” He comes in to her into the tent, and she covers him with a rug.

YHWH’s angel comes, and sits under the oak which is in Ophrah, that belongs to Joash the Abiezrite. His son Gideon is beating out wheat in the wine press, to hide it from the Midianites. YHWH’s angel appears to him, and says to him, “YHWH is with you, you mighty man of valor!”

Gideon says to him, “Oh, my lord, if YHWH is with us, why then has all this happened to us? Where are all his wondrous works which our fathers told us of, saying, ‘Didn’t YHWH bring us up from Egypt?’ But now YHWH has cast us off, and delivered us into the hand of Midian.”
YHWH looks at him, and says, “Go in this your might, and save Israel from the hand of Midian. Haven’t I sent you?”
He says to him, “O Lord, how should I save Israel? Look, my family is the poorest in Manasseh, and I am the least in my father’s house.”
YHWH says to him, “Surely I will be with you, and you will strike the Midianites as one man.”

He says to him, “If now I have found favor in your sight, then show me a sign that it is you who talk with me. Please don’t go away, until I come to you, and bring out my present, and lay it before you.”
He says, “I will wait until you come back.”

Gideon goes in and prepares a young goat and unleavened cakes of an ephah of meal. He puts the meat in a basket and he puts the broth in a pot, and brings it out to him under the oak, and presents it.

He divides the three hundred men into three companies, and he puts into the hands of all them trumpets, and empty pitchers, with torches within the pitchers.

He says to them, “Watch me, and do likewise. Look, when I come to the outermost part of the camp, it will be that, as I do, so you will do. When I blow the trumpet, I and all who are with me, then blow the trumpets also on every side of all the camp, and shout, ‘For YHWH and for Gideon!’”

So Gideon, and the hundred men who are with him, come to the outermost part of the camp in the beginning of the middle watch, when they have but newly set the watch. Then they blow the trumpets, and break in pieces the pitchers that are in their hands. The three companies blow the trumpets, break the pitchers, and hold the torches in their left hands, and the trumpets in their right hands with which to blow; and they shout, “The sword of YHWH and of Gideon!” They each stand in his place around the camp; and all the army runs; and they shout, and put them to flight. They blow the three hundred trumpets, and YHWH sets every man’s sword against his fellow, and against all the army; and the army flees as far as Beth Shittah toward Zererah, as far as the border of Abel Meholah, by Tabbath.
Oreb and Zeeb · 7:23–25

The men of Israel are gathered together out of Naphtali, and out of Asher, and out of all Manasseh, and pursue Midian. Gideon sends messengers throughout all the hill country of Ephraim, saying, “Come down against Midian, and take before them the waters, as far as Beth Barah, even the Jordan!” So all the men of Ephraim are gathered together, and take the waters as far as Beth Barah, even the Jordan. They take the two princes of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb. They kill Oreb at Oreb’s rock, and Zeeb they kill at Zeeb’s wine press; and pursue Midian. Then they bring the heads of Oreb and Zeeb to Gideon beyond the Jordan.
Ephraim’s Complaint · 8:1–3

The men of Ephraim say to him, “Why have you treated us this way, that you didn’t call us when you went to fight with Midian?” They rebuke him sharply. He says to them, “What have I now done in comparison with you? Isn’t the gleaning of the grapes of Ephraim better than the vintage of Abiezer? God has delivered into your hand the princes of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb! What was I able to do in comparison with you?” Then their anger is abated toward him, when he has said that.
Succoth and Penuel · 8:4–9

Gideon comes to the Jordan, and passes over, he, and the three hundred men who are with him, faint, yet pursuing. He says to the men of Succoth, “Please give loaves of bread to the people who follow me; for they are faint, and I am pursuing after Zebah and Zalmunna, the kings of Midian.”
The princes of Succoth say, “Are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna now in your hand, that we should give bread to your army?”
Gideon says, “Therefore when YHWH has delivered Zebah and Zalmunna into my hand, then I will tear your flesh with the thorns of the wilderness and with briers.”

He goes up there to Penuel, and speaks to them in the same way; and the men of Penuel answer him as the men of Succoth have answered. He speaks also to the men of Penuel, saying, “When I come again in peace, I will break down this tower.”
Zebah and Zalmunna · 8:10–12

Now Zebah and Zalmunna are in Karkor, and their armies with them, about fifteen thousand men, all who are left of all the army of the children of the east; for there falls one hundred twenty thousand men who draw sword. Gideon goes up by the way of those who live in tents on the east of Nobah and Jogbehah, and strikes the army; for the army is secure. Zebah and Zalmunna flee; and he pursues them. He takes the two kings of Midian, Zebah and Zalmunna, and confuses all the army.
Reckoning at Succoth and Penuel · 8:13–17

Gideon the son of Joash returns from the battle from the ascent of Heres. He catches a young man of the men of Succoth, and inquires of him: and he describes for him the princes of Succoth, and its elders, seventy-seven men. He comes to the men of Succoth, and says, “See Zebah and Zalmunna, concerning whom you taunted me, saying, ‘Are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna now in your hand, that we should give bread to your men who are weary?’” He takes the elders of the city, and thorns of the wilderness and briers, and with them he teaches the men of Succoth. He breaks down the tower of Penuel, and kills the men of the city.
Brothers at Tabor · 8:18–21
Then he says to Zebah and Zalmunna, “What kind of men were they whom you killed at Tabor?”
They answer, “They were like you. Each one resembled the children of a king.”
He says, “They were my brothers, the sons of my mother. As YHWH lives, if you had saved them alive, I would not kill you.”
He says to Jether his firstborn, “Get up, and kill them!” But the youth doesn’t draw his sword; for he is afraid, because he is yet a youth.
Then Zebah and Zalmunna say, “Rise and fall on us; for as the man is, so is his strength.” Gideon arises, and kills Zebah and Zalmunna, and takes the crescents that are on their camels’ necks.
The Ephod · 8:22–27
Then the men of Israel say to Gideon, “Rule over us, both you, and your son, and your son’s son also; for you have saved us out of the hand of Midian.”

Gideon says to them, “I will not rule over you, neither will my son rule over you. YHWH will rule over you.” Gideon says to them, “I do have a request, that you would each give me the earrings of his plunder.” (For they have golden earrings, because they are Ishmaelites.)

They answer, “We will willingly give them.” They spread a garment, and every man throws the earrings of his plunder into it. The weight of the golden earrings that he requests is one thousand and seven hundred shekels of gold, besides the crescents, and the pendants, and the purple clothing that is on the kings of Midian, and besides the chains that are about their camels’ necks. Gideon makes an ephod out of it, and puts it in Ophrah, his city. Then all Israel plays the prostitute with it there; and it becomes a snare to Gideon, and to his house.
Rest, and the Death of Gideon · 8:28–32

So Midian is subdued before the children of Israel, and they lift up their heads no more. The land has rest forty years in the days of Gideon. Jerubbaal the son of Joash goes and lives in his own house. Gideon has seventy sons conceived from his body, for he has many wives. His concubine who is in Shechem also bears him a son, and he names him Abimelech. Gideon the son of Joash dies in a good old age, and is buried in the tomb of Joash his father, in Ophrah of the Abiezrites.
After Gideon · 8:33–35

As soon as Gideon is dead, the children of Israel turn again, and play the prostitute following the Baals, and make Baal Berith their god. The children of Israel don’t remember YHWH their God, who has delivered them out of the hand of all their enemies on every side; neither do they show kindness to the house of Jerubbaal, that is, Gideon, according to all the goodness which he has shown to Israel.
Abimelech Made King at Shechem · 9:1–6

Abimelech the son of Jerubbaal goes to Shechem to his mother’s brothers, and speaks with them, and with all the family of the house of his mother’s father, saying, “Please speak in the ears of all the men of Shechem, ‘Is it better for you that all the sons of Jerubbaal, who are seventy persons, rule over you, or that one rule over you?’ Remember also that I am your bone and your flesh.”

His mother’s brothers speak of him in the ears of all the men of Shechem all these words. Their hearts incline to follow Abimelech; for they say, “He is our brother.” They give him seventy pieces of silver out of the house of Baal Berith, with which Abimelech hires vain and light fellows, who follow him. He goes to his father’s house at Ophrah, and kills his brothers the sons of Jerubbaal, being seventy persons, on one stone: but Jotham the youngest son of Jerubbaal is left; for he hides himself. All the men of Shechem assemble themselves together, and all the house of Millo, and go and make Abimelech king, by the oak of the pillar that is in Shechem.
Jotham’s Parable of the Trees · 9:7–15

When they tell it to Jotham, he goes and stands on the top of Mount Gerizim, and lifts up his voice, cries out, and says to them, “Listen to me, you men of Shechem, that God may listen to you. The trees set out to anoint a king over themselves. They said to the olive tree, ‘Reign over us.’
“But the olive tree said to them, ‘Should I stop producing my oil, with which they honor God and man by me, and go to wave back and forth over the trees?’
“The trees said to the fig tree, ‘Come and reign over us.’
“But the fig tree said to them, ‘Should I leave my sweetness, and my good fruit, and go to wave back and forth over the trees?’
“The trees said to the vine, ‘Come and reign over us.’
“The vine said to them, ‘Should I leave my new wine, which cheers God and man, and go to wave back and forth over the trees?’
“Then all the trees said to the bramble, ‘Come and reign over us.’
“The bramble said to the trees, ‘If in truth you anoint me king over you, then come and take refuge in my shade; and if not, let fire come out of the bramble, and devour the cedars of Lebanon.’
Jotham’s Curse · 9:16–21

“Now therefore, if you have dealt truly and righteously, in that you have made Abimelech king, and if you have dealt well with Jerubbaal and his house, and have done to him according to the deserving of his hands (for my father fought for you, and risked his life, and delivered you out of the hand of Midian; and you have risen up against my father’s house today, and have slain his sons, seventy persons, on one stone, and have made Abimelech, the son of his female servant, king over the men of Shechem, because he is your brother); if you then have dealt truly and righteously with Jerubbaal and with his house today, then rejoice in Abimelech, and let him also rejoice in you; but if not, let fire come out from Abimelech, and devour the men of Shechem, and the house of Millo; and let fire come out from the men of Shechem, and from the house of Millo, and devour Abimelech.”
Jotham runs away, and flees, and goes to Beer, and lives there, for fear of Abimelech his brother.
The Spirit Between Abimelech and Shechem · 9:22–25

Abimelech is prince over Israel three years. Then God sends an evil spirit between Abimelech and the men of Shechem; and the men of Shechem deal treacherously with Abimelech, that the violence done to the seventy sons of Jerubbaal might come, and that their blood might be laid on Abimelech their brother, who kills them, and on the men of Shechem, who strengthens his hands to kill his brothers. The men of Shechem set an ambush for him on the tops of the mountains, and they rob all who come along that way by them, and Abimelech is told about it.
Gaal Son of Ebed · 9:26–33

Gaal the son of Ebed comes with his brothers, and goes over to Shechem; and the men of Shechem put their trust in him. They go out into the field, harvest their vineyards, trod the grapes, held festival, and go into the house of their god, and eat and drank, and curse Abimelech. Gaal the son of Ebed says, “Who is Abimelech, and who is Shechem, that we should serve him? Isn’t he the son of Jerubbaal? Isn’t Zebul his officer? Serve the men of Hamor the father of Shechem, but why should we serve him? I wish that this people were under my hand! Then I would remove Abimelech.” He says to Abimelech, “Increase your army, and come out!”

When Zebul the ruler of the city hears the words of Gaal the son of Ebed, his anger burns. He sends messengers to Abimelech craftily, saying, “Look, Gaal the son of Ebed and his brothers have come to Shechem; and look, they incite the city against you. Now therefore, go up by night, you and the people who are with you, and lie in wait in the field. It will be that in the morning, as soon as the sun is up, you will rise early, and rush on the city. Look, when he and the people who are with him come out against you, then may you do to them as you will find occasion.”
The Battle for Shechem · 9:34–45

Abimelech rises up, and all the people who are with him, by night, and they lay wait against Shechem in four companies. Gaal the son of Ebed goes out, and stands in the entrance of the gate of the city. Abimelech rises up, and the people who are with him, from the ambush.
When Gaal sees the people, he says to Zebul, “Look, people are coming down from the tops of the mountains.”
Zebul says to him, “You see the shadow of the mountains as if they were men.”
Gaal speaks again and says, “Look, people are coming down by the middle of the land, and one company comes by the way of the oak of Meonenim.”
Then Zebul says to him, “Now where is your mouth, that you said, ‘Who is Abimelech, that we should serve him?’ Isn’t this the people that you have despised? Please go out now and fight with them.”

Gaal goes out before the men of Shechem, and fights with Abimelech. Abimelech chases him, and he flees before him, and many fall wounded, even to the entrance of the gate. Abimelech lives at Arumah; and Zebul drives out Gaal and his brothers, that they should not dwell in Shechem. On the next day, the people go out into the field; and they tell Abimelech. He takes the people, and divides them into three companies, and lays wait in the field; and he looks, and look, the people come out of the city. So, he rises up against them, and strikes them. Abimelech and the companies that are with him rush forward, and stand in the entrance of the gate of the city; and the two companies rush on all who are in the field, and strike them. Abimelech fights against the city all that day; and he takes the city, and kills the people in it. He beats down the city, and sows it with salt.
The Tower of Shechem · 9:46–49

When all the men of the tower of Shechem hear of it, they enter into the stronghold of the house of Elberith. Abimelech is told that all the men of the tower of Shechem are gathered together. Abimelech goes up to Mount Zalmon, he and all the people who are with him; and Abimelech takes an ax in his hand, and cuts down a bough from the trees, and takes it up, and lays it on his shoulder. Then he says to the people who are with him, “What you have seen me do, make haste, and do as I have done!” All the people likewise each cut down his bough, and follow Abimelech, and put them at the base of the stronghold, and set the stronghold on fire on them; so that all the people of the tower of Shechem die also, about a thousand men and women.
Thebez · 9:50–57

Then Abimelech goes to Thebez, and encamps against Thebez, and takes it. But there is a strong tower within the city, and all the men and women of the city flee there, and shut themselves in, and go up to the roof of the tower. Abimelech comes to the tower, and fights against it, and comes near to the door of the tower to burn it with fire. A certain woman casts an upper millstone on Abimelech’s head, and breaks his skull.
Then he calls hastily to the young man his armor bearer, and says to him, “Draw your sword, and kill me, that men not say of me, ‘A woman killed him.’ His young man thrust him through, and he died.”

When the men of Israel see that Abimelech is dead, they each depart to his place. Thus God repays the wickedness of Abimelech, which he does to his father, in killing his seventy brothers; and God repays all the wickedness of the men of Shechem on their heads; and the curse of Jotham the son of Jerubbaal comes on them.

After Abimelech, Tola the son of Puah, the son of Dodo, a man of Issachar, arise to save Israel. He lives in Shamir in the hill country of Ephraim. He judges Israel twenty-three years, and dies, and is buried in Shamir.

After him Jair, the Gileadite arises, and he judges Israel twenty-two years. He has thirty sons who ride on thirty donkey colts, and they have thirty cities, which are called Havvoth Jair to this day, which are in the land of Gilead. Jair dies, and is buried in Kamon.
Apostasy and Cry · 10:6–10

The children of Israel again do that which is evil in YHWH’s sight, and serves the Baals, the Ashtaroth, the gods of Syria, the gods of Sidon, the gods of Moab, the gods of the children of Ammon, and the gods of the Philistines. They abandon YHWH, and don’t serve him. YHWH’s anger burns against Israel, and he sells them into the hand of the Philistines, and into the hand of the children of Ammon. They trouble and oppress the children of Israel that year. For eighteen years, they oppress all the children of Israel that are beyond the Jordan in the land of the Amorites, which is in Gilead. The children of Ammon pass over the Jordan to fight also against Judah, and against Benjamin, and against the house of Ephraim, so that Israel is very distressed. The children of Israel cry to YHWH, saying, “We have sinned against you, even because we have forsaken our God, and have served the Baals.”
“i Will Save You No More” · 10:11–14

YHWH says to the children of Israel, “Didn’t I save you from the Egyptians, and from the Amorites, from the children of Ammon, and from the Philistines? The Sidonians also, and the Amalekites, and the Maonites, oppressed you; and you cried to me, and I saved you out of their hand. Yet you have forsaken me, and served other gods. Therefore I will save you no more. Go and cry to the gods which you have chosen. Let them save you in the time of your distress!”
Israel Turns Back · 10:15–18

The children of Israel say to YHWH, “We have sinned! Do you to us whatever seems good to you; only deliver us, please, today.” They put away the foreign gods from among them, and serve YHWH; and his soul is grieved for the misery of Israel.

Then the children of Ammon are gathered together and encamp in Gilead. The children of Israel assemble themselves together and encamp in Mizpah. The people, the princes of Gilead, say to one another, “Who is the man who will begin to fight against the children of Ammon? He will be head over all the inhabitants of Gilead.”
Jephthah the Outcast · 11:1–3

Now Jephthah the Gileadite is a mighty man of valor, and he is the son of a prostitute. Gilead becomes the father of Jephthah. Gilead’s wife bears him sons. When his wife’s sons grow up, they drive Jephthah out, and say to him, “You will not inherit in our father’s house, for you are the son of another woman.” Then Jephthah flees from his brothers, and lives in the land of Tob. Outlaws join up with Jephthah, and they go out with him.
The Elders Come Back · 11:4–11

After a while, the children of Ammon make war against Israel. When the children of Ammon make war against Israel, the elders of Gilead go to get Jephthah out of the land of Tob. They say to Jephthah, “Come and be our chief, that we may fight with the children of Ammon.”
Jephthah says to the elders of Gilead, “Didn’t you hate me, and drive me out of my father’s house? Why have you come to me now when you are in distress?”

The elders of Gilead say to Jephthah, “Therefore we have turned again to you now, that you may go with us, and fight with the children of Ammon. You will be our head over all the inhabitants of Gilead.”
Jephthah says to the elders of Gilead, “If you bring me home again to fight with the children of Ammon, and YHWH delivers them before me, will I be your head?”
The elders of Gilead say to Jephthah, “YHWH will be witness between us. Surely we will do what you say.”
Then Jephthah goes with the elders of Gilead, and the people make him head and chief over them. Jephthah speaks all his words before YHWH in Mizpah.
Messengers to the Ammonite King · 11:12–28
Jephthah sends messengers to the king of the children of Ammon, saying, “What have you to do with me, that you have come to me to fight against my land?”

The king of the children of Ammon answers to the messengers of Jephthah, “Because Israel took away my land, when he came up out of Egypt, from the Arnon even to the Jabbok, and to the Jordan. Now therefore restore that territory again peaceably.”

Jephthah sends messengers again to the king of the children of Ammon; and he says to him, “Thus says Jephthah: Israel didn’t take away the land of Moab, nor the land of the children of Ammon, but when they came up from Egypt, and Israel went through the wilderness to the Red Sea, and came to Kadesh; then Israel sent messengers to the king of Edom, saying, ‘Please let me pass through your land;’ but the king of Edom didn’t listen. In the same way, he sent to the king of Moab; but he would not: and Israel stayed in Kadesh. Then they went through the wilderness, and went around the land of Edom, and the land of Moab, and came by the east side of the land of Moab, and they encamped on the other side of the Arnon; but they didn’t come within the border of Moab, for the Arnon was the border of Moab. Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites, the king of Heshbon; and Israel said to him, ‘Please let us pass through your land to my place.’ But Sihon didn’t trust Israel to pass through his border; but Sihon gathered all his people together, and encamped in Jahaz, and fought against Israel. YHWH, the God of Israel, delivered Sihon and all his people into the hand of Israel, and they struck them. So Israel possessed all the land of the Amorites, the inhabitants of that country. They possessed all the border of the Amorites, from the Arnon even to the Jabbok, and from the wilderness even to the Jordan. So now YHWH, the God of Israel, has dispossessed the Amorites from before his people Israel, and should you possess them? Won’t you possess that which Chemosh your god gives you to possess? So whoever YHWH our God has dispossessed from before us, them will we possess. Now are you anything better than Balak the son of Zippor, king of Moab? Did he ever strive against Israel, or did he ever fight against them? While Israel lived in Heshbon and its towns, and in Aroer and its towns, and in all the cities that are along by the side of the Arnon, three hundred years; why didn’t you recover them within that time? I therefore have not sinned against you, but you do me wrong to war against me. May YHWH the Judge be judge today between the children of Israel and the children of Ammon.”
However the king of the children of Ammon doesn’t listen to the words of Jephthah which he sends him.
The Vow · 11:29–31
Then YHWH’s Spirit comes on Jephthah, and he passes over Gilead and Manasseh, and passes over Mizpah of Gilead, and from Mizpah of Gilead he passes over to the children of Ammon.

Jephthah vows a vow to YHWH, and says, “If you will indeed deliver the children of Ammon into my hand, then it will be, that whatever comes out of the doors of my house to meet me, when I return in peace from the children of Ammon, it will be YHWH’s, and I will offer it up for a burnt offering.”
Victory · 11:32–33

So Jephthah passes over to the children of Ammon to fight against them; and YHWH delivers them into his hand. He strikes them from Aroer until you come to Minnith, even twenty cities, and to Abelcheramim, with a very great slaughter. So the children of Ammon are subdued before the children of Israel.
The Daughter at the Door · 11:34–40

Jephthah comes to Mizpah to his house; and look, his daughter comes out to meet him with tambourines and with dances. She is his only child. Besides her he has neither son nor daughter. When he sees her, he tears his clothes, and says, “Alas, my daughter! You have brought me very low, and you are one of those who trouble me; for I have opened my mouth to YHWH, and I can’t go back.”

She says to him, “My father, you have opened your mouth to YHWH; do to me according to that which has proceeded out of your mouth, because YHWH has taken vengeance for you on your enemies, even on the children of Ammon.” She says to her father, “Let this thing be done for me. Leave me alone two months, that I may depart and go down on the mountains, and bewail my virginity, I and my companions.”

He says, “Go.” He sends her away for two months: and she departs, she and her companions, and mourns her virginity on the mountains. At the end of two months, she returns to her father, who does with her according to his vow which he has vowed. She is a virgin. It is a custom in Israel that the daughters of Israel go yearly to celebrate the daughter of Jephthah the Gileadite four days in a year.
Ephraim’s Threat · 12:1–3

The men of Ephraim are gathered together, and pass northward; and they say to Jephthah, “Why did you pass over to fight against the children of Ammon, and didn’t call us to go with you? We will burn your house around you with fire!”

Jephthah says to them, “I and my people were at great strife with the children of Ammon; and when I called you, you didn’t save me out of their hand. When I saw that you didn’t save me, I put my life in my hand, and passed over against the children of Ammon, and YHWH delivered them into my hand. Why then have you come up to me today, to fight against me?”
Shibboleth at the Fords · 12:4–6

Then Jephthah gathers together all the men of Gilead, and fights with Ephraim. The men of Gilead strike Ephraim, because they say, “You are fugitives of Ephraim, you Gileadites, in the middle of Ephraim, and in the middle of Manasseh.” The Gileadites take the fords of the Jordan against the Ephraimites. When the fugitives of Ephraim say, “Let me go over,” the men of Gilead say to him, “Are you an Ephraimite?” If he says, “No”; then they say to him, “Now say ‘Shibboleth;’” and he says “Sibboleth”; for he can’t manage to pronounce it right: then they seize him, and kill him at the fords of the Jordan. At that time, forty-two thousand of Ephraim falls.
The Death of Jephthah · 12:7
Jephthah judges Israel six years. Then Jephthah the Gileadite dies, and is buried in the cities of Gilead.

After him Ibzan of Bethlehem judges Israel. He has thirty sons; and thirty daughters he sends outside his clan, and thirty daughters he brings in from outside his clan for his sons. He judges Israel seven years. Ibzan dies, and is buried at Bethlehem.
After him Elon the Zebulunite judges Israel; and he judges Israel ten years. Elon the Zebulunite dies, and is buried in Aijalon in the land of Zebulun.

After him Abdon the son of Hillel the Pirathonite judges Israel. He has forty sons and thirty sons’ sons, who ride on seventy donkey colts. He judges Israel eight years. Abdon the son of Hillel the Pirathonite dies, and is buried in Pirathon in the land of Ephraim, in the hill country of the Amalekites.
Israel Under the Philistines · 13:1
The children of Israel again do that which is evil in YHWH’s sight; and YHWH delivers them into the hand of the Philistines forty years.
The Angel Comes to Manoah’s Wife · 13:2–7

There is a certain man of Zorah, of the family of the Danites, whose name is Manoah; and his wife is barren, and childless. YHWH’s angel appears to the woman, and says to her, “See now, you are barren and childless; but you will conceive, and bear a son. Now therefore please beware and drink no wine nor strong drink, and don’t eat any unclean thing: for, look, you will conceive, and give birth to a son. No razor will come on his head; for the child will be a Nazirite to God from the womb. He will begin to save Israel out of the hand of the Philistines.”

Then the woman comes and tells her husband, saying, “A man of God came to me, and his face was like the face of the angel of God, very awesome. I didn’t ask him where he was from, neither did he tell me his name; but he said to me, ‘Look, you will conceive, and bear a son; and now drink no wine nor strong drink. Don’t eat any unclean thing; for the child will be a Nazirite to God from the womb to the day of his death.’”
Manoah’s Prayer · 13:8–14
Then Manoah entreats YHWH, and says, “Oh, Lord, please let the man of God whom you sent come again to us, and teach us what we should do to the child who will be born.”

God listens to the voice of Manoah, and the angel of God comes again to the woman as she sits in the field, but Manoah, her husband, isn’t with her. The woman hurries and runs, and tells her husband, and says to him, “Look, the man who came to me that day has appeared to me,”
Manoah arises, and follows his wife, and comes to the man, and says to him, “Are you the man who spoke to my wife?”
He says, “I am.”
Manoah says, “Now let your words happen. What will the child’s way of life and mission be?”

YHWH’s angel says to Manoah, “Of all that I said to the woman let her beware. She may not eat of anything that comes of the vine, neither let her drink wine or strong drink, nor eat any unclean thing. Let her observe all that I commanded her.”
Manoah’s Offering and the Angel’s Name · 13:15–23
Manoah says to YHWH’s angel, “Please stay with us, that we may make a young goat ready for you.”
YHWH’s angel says to Manoah, “Though you detain me, I won’t eat your bread. If you will prepare a burnt offering, you must offer it to YHWH.” For Manoah doesn’t know that he is YHWH’s angel.
Manoah says to YHWH’s angel, “What is your name, that when your words happen, we may honor you?”
YHWH’s angel says to him, “Why do you ask about my name, since it is incomprehensible?”

So Manoah takes the young goat with the meal offering, and offers it on the rock to YHWH. Then the angel does an amazing thing as Manoah and his wife watch. For when the flame goes up toward the sky from off the altar, YHWH’s angel ascends in the flame of the altar. Manoah and his wife watch; and they fall on their faces to the ground. But YHWH’s angel doesn’t appear to Manoah or to his wife any more. Then Manoah knows that he is YHWH’s angel. Manoah says to his wife, “We will surely die, because we have seen God.”
