Yet have respect for the prayer of your servant, and for his supplication, YHWH my God, to listen to the cry and to the prayer which your servant prays before you today; that your eyes may be open toward this house night and day, even toward the place of which you have said, ‘My name will be there;’ to listen to the prayer which your servant prays toward this place. Listen to the supplication of your servant, and of your people Israel, when they pray toward this place. Yes, hear in heaven, your dwelling place; and when you hear, forgive.

“If a man sins against his neighbor, and an oath is laid on him to cause him to swear, and he comes and swears before your altar in this house; then hear in heaven, and act, and judge your servants, condemning the wicked, to bring his way on his own head, and justifying the righteous, to give him according to his righteousness.

“When your people Israel are struck down before the enemy, because they have sinned against you; if they turn again to you, and confess your name, and pray and make supplication to you in this house; then hear in heaven, and forgive the sin of your people Israel, and bring them again to the land which you gave to their fathers.

“When the sky is shut up, and there is no rain, because they have sinned against you; if they pray toward this place, and confess your name, and turn from their sin, when you afflict them, then hear in heaven, and forgive the sin of your servants, and of your people Israel, when you teach them the good way in which they should walk; and send rain on your land, which you have given to your people for an inheritance.

“If there is famine in the land, if there is pestilence, if there is blight, mildew, locust or caterpillar; if their enemy besieges them in the land of their cities; whatever plague, whatever sickness there is; whatever prayer and supplication is made by any man, or by all your people Israel, who will each know the plague of his own heart, and spread out his hands toward this house, then hear in heaven, your dwelling place, and forgive, and act, and give to every man according to all his ways, whose heart you know (for you, even you only, know the hearts of all the children of men); that they may fear you all the days that they live in the land which you gave to our fathers.

“Moreover concerning the foreigner, who is not of your people Israel, when he comes out of a far country for your name’s sake (for they will hear of your great name, and of your mighty hand, and of your outstretched arm); when he comes and prays toward this house; hear in heaven, your dwelling place, and do according to all that the foreigner calls to you for; that all the peoples of the earth may know your name, to fear you, as do your people Israel, and that they may know that this house which I have built is called by your name.

“If your people go out to battle against their enemy, by whatever way you will send them, and they pray to YHWH toward the city which you have chosen, and toward the house which I have built for your name; then hear in heaven their prayer and their supplication, and maintain their cause. If they sin against you (for there is no man who doesn’t sin), and you are angry with them, and deliver them to the enemy, so that they carry them away captive to the land of the enemy, far off or near; yet if they repent in the land where they are carried captive, and turn again, and make supplication to you in the land of those who carried them captive, saying, ‘We have sinned, and have done perversely; we have dealt wickedly;’ if they return to you with all their heart and with all their soul in the land of their enemies, who carried them captive, and pray to you toward their land, which you gave to their fathers, the city which you have chosen, and the house which I have built for your name; then hear their prayer and their supplication in heaven, your dwelling place, and maintain their cause; and forgive your people who have sinned against you, and all their transgressions in which they have transgressed against you; and give them compassion before those who carried them captive, that they may have compassion on them (for they are your people, and your inheritance, which you brought out of Egypt, from the middle of the iron furnace); that your eyes may be open to the supplication of your servant, and to the supplication of your people Israel, to listen to them whenever they cry to you. For you separated them from among all the peoples of the earth, to be your inheritance, as you spoke by Moses your servant, when you brought our fathers out of Egypt, Lord YHWH.”
The Blessing and the Charge · 8:54–61

It is so, that when Solomon has finished praying all this prayer and supplication to YHWH, he arises from before YHWH’s altar, from kneeling on his knees with his hands spread out toward heaven. He stands, and blesses all the assembly of Israel with a loud voice, saying, “Blessed be YHWH, who has given rest to his people Israel, according to all that he promised. There has not failed one word of all his good promise, which he promised by Moses his servant. May YHWH our God be with us, as he was with our fathers. Let him not leave us or forsake us; that he may incline our hearts to him, to walk in all his ways, and to keep his commandments, and his statutes, and his ordinances, which he commanded our fathers. Let these my words, with which I have made supplication before YHWH, be near to YHWH our God day and night, that he may maintain the cause of his servant, and the cause of his people Israel, as every day requires; that all the peoples of the earth may know that YHWH himself is God. There is no one else.
“Let your heart therefore be perfect with YHWH our God, to walk in his statutes, and to keep his commandments, as it is today.”
The Dedication Feast · 8:62–66

The king, and all Israel with him, offer sacrifice before YHWH. Solomon offers for the sacrifice of peace offerings, which he offers to YHWH, twenty two thousand head of cattle, and one hundred twenty thousand sheep. So the king and all the children of Israel dedicated YHWH’s house. The same day the king makes the middle of the court holy that is before YHWH’s house; for there he offers the burnt offering, and the meal offering, and the fat of the peace offerings, because the bronze altar that is before YHWH is too little to receive the burnt offering, the meal offering, and the fat of the peace offerings. So Solomon holds the feast at that time, and all Israel with him, a great assembly, from the entrance of Hamath to the brook of Egypt, before YHWH our God, seven days and seven more days, even fourteen days. On the eighth day he sends the people away; and they bless the king, and go to their tents joyful and glad in their hearts for all the goodness that YHWH has shown to David his servant, and to Israel his people.
YHWH Appears to Solomon a Second Time · 9:1–9

When Solomon has finished the building of YHWH’s house, the king’s house, and all Solomon’s desire which he is pleased to do, YHWH appears to Solomon the second time, as he has appeared to him at Gibeon. YHWH says to him, “I have heard your prayer and your supplication, that you have made before me. I have made this house holy, which you have built, to put my name there forever; and my eyes and my heart will be there perpetually. As for you, if you will walk before me, as David your father walked, in integrity of heart, and in uprightness, to do according to all that I have commanded you, and will keep my statutes and my ordinances; then I will establish the throne of your kingdom over Israel forever, as I promised to David your father, saying, ‘There will not fail from you a man on the throne of Israel.’ But if you turn away from following me, you or your children, and not keep my commandments and my statutes which I have set before you, but go and serve other gods, and worship them; then I will cut off Israel out of the land which I have given them; and I will cast this house, which I have made holy for my name, out of my sight; and Israel will be a proverb and a byword among all peoples. Though this house is so high, yet everyone who passes by it will be astonished and hiss; and they will say, ‘Why has YHWH done this to this land, and to this house?’ and they will answer, ‘Because they abandoned YHWH their God, who brought their fathers out of the land of Egypt, and laid hold of other gods, and worshiped them, and served them. Therefore YHWH has brought all this evil on them.’”
Solomon's Other Works · 9:10–25

At the end of twenty years, in which Solomon has built the two houses, YHWH’s house and the king’s house (now Hiram the king of Tyre has furnished Solomon with cedar trees and cypress trees, and with gold, according to all his desire), King Solomon gives Hiram twenty cities in the land of Galilee. Hiram comes out of Tyre to see the cities which Solomon has given him; and they don’t please him. He says, “What cities are these which you have given me, my brother?” He calls them the land of Cabul to this day. Hiram sends to the king one hundred twenty talents of gold.

This is the reason of the levy which king Solomon raises, to build YHWH’s house, his own house, Millo, Jerusalem’s wall, Hazor, Megiddo, and Gezer. Pharaoh king of Egypt has gone up, taken Gezer, burns it with fire, kills the Canaanites who live in the city, and given it for a wedding gift to his daughter, Solomon’s wife. Solomon builds in the land Gezer, Beth Horon the lower, Baalath, Tamar in the wilderness, all the storage cities that Solomon has, the cities for his chariots, the cities for his horsemen, and that which Solomon desires to build for his pleasure in Jerusalem, and in Lebanon, and in all the land of his dominion. As for all the people who are left of the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites, who are not of the children of Israel; their children who are left after them in the land, whom the children of Israel are not able utterly to destroy, of them Solomon raise a levy of bondservants to this day. But of the children of Israel Solomon makes no bondservants; but they are the men of war, his servants, his princes, his captains, and rulers of his chariots and of his horsemen. These are the five hundred fifty chief officers who are over Solomon’s work, who rule over the people who labor in the work. But Pharaoh’s daughter comes up out of David’s city to her house which Solomon has built for her. Then he builds Millo. Solomon offers burnt offerings and peace offerings on the altar which he builds to YHWH three times per year, burning incense with them, on the altar that is before YHWH. So he finishes the house.
Solomon's Fleet at Ezion-geber · 9:26–28

King Solomon makes a fleet of ships in Ezion Geber, which is beside Eloth, on the shore of the Red Sea, in the land of Edom. Hiram sends in the fleet his servants, sailors who have knowledge of the sea, with the servants of Solomon. They come to Ophir, and fetched from there gold, four hundred and twenty talents, and bring it to king Solomon.
The Queen of Sheba · 10:1–13

When the queen of Sheba hears of the fame of Solomon concerning YHWH’s name, she comes to test him with hard questions. She comes to Jerusalem with a very great caravan, with camels that bear spices, very much gold, and precious stones; and when she has come to Solomon, she talks with him about all that are in her heart. Solomon answers all her questions. There is not anything hidden from the king which he doesn’t tell her. When the queen of Sheba has seen all the wisdom of Solomon, the house that he has built, the food of his table, the sitting of his servants, the attendance of his officials, their clothing, his cup bearers, and his ascent by which he goes up to YHWH’s house; there is no more spirit in her. She says to the king, “It was a true report that I heard in my own land of your acts, and of your wisdom. However I didn’t believe the words until I came and my eyes had seen it. Look, not even half was told me! Your wisdom and prosperity exceed the fame which I heard. Happy are your men, happy are these your servants, who stand continually before you, who hear your wisdom. Blessed is YHWH your God, who delighted in you, to set you on the throne of Israel. Because YHWH loved Israel forever, therefore he made you king, to do justice and righteousness.” She gives the king one hundred twenty talents of gold, and a very great quantity of spices, and precious stones. Never again is there such an abundance of spices as these which the queen of Sheba gives to king Solomon.

The fleet of Hiram that brings gold from Ophir, also brings in from Ophir great quantities of almug trees and precious stones. The king makes of the almug trees pillars for YHWH’s house, and for the king’s house, harps also and stringed instruments for the singers; no such almug trees come or are seen, to this day. King Solomon gives to the queen of Sheba all her desire, whatever she asks, besides that which Solomon gives her of his royal bounty. So she turns and goes to her own land, she and her servants.
Solomon's Wealth · 10:14–29

Now the weight of gold that comes to Solomon in one year is six hundred sixty-six talents of gold, besides that which the traders bring, and the traffic of the merchants, and of all the kings of the mixed people, and of the governors of the country. King Solomon makes two hundred bucklers of beaten gold; six hundred shekels of gold go to one buckler. he makes three hundred shields of beaten gold; three minas of gold go to one shield; and the king puts them in the House of the Forest of Lebanon. Moreover the king makes a great throne of ivory, and overlays it with the finest gold. There are six steps to the throne, and the top of the throne is round behind; and there are armrests on either side by the place of the seat, and two lions standing beside the armrests. Twelve lions stand there on the one side and on the other on the six steps. Nothing like it is made in any kingdom. All king Solomon’s drinking vessels are of gold, and all the vessels of the House of the Forest of Lebanon are of pure gold. None are of silver, because it is considered of little value in the days of Solomon. For the king has a fleet of Tarshish at sea with Hiram’s fleet. Once every three years the fleet of Tarshish comes, bringing gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks. So king Solomon exceeds all the kings of the earth in riches and in wisdom. All the earth seeks the presence of Solomon, to hear his wisdom, which God has put in his heart. Year after year, every man brings his tribute, vessels of silver, vessels of gold, clothing, armor, spices, horses, and mules. Solomon gathers together chariots and horsemen. He has one thousand four hundred chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen, that he keeps in the chariot cities and with the king at Jerusalem. The king makes silver as common as stones in Jerusalem, and cedars as common as the sycamore trees that are in the lowland. The horses which Solomon has are brought out of Egypt. The king’s merchants receive them in droves, each drives at a price. A chariot comes up and goes out of Egypt for six hundred shekels of silver, and a horse for one hundred fifty shekels; and so they export them to all the kings of the Hittites, and to the kings of Syria.
Solomon's Foreign Wives · 11:1–8

Now king Solomon loves many foreign women, together with the daughter of Pharaoh, women of the Moabites, Ammonites, Edomites, Sidonians, and Hittites; of the nations concerning which YHWH says to the children of Israel, “You will not go among them, neither will they come among you; for surely they will turn away your heart after their gods.” Solomon joins to these in love. He has seven hundred wives, princesses, and three hundred concubines; and his wives turn away his heart. When Solomon is old, his wives turn away his heart after other gods; and his heart is not perfect with YHWH his God, as the heart of David his father is. For Solomon goes after Ashtoreth the goddess of the Sidonians, and after Milcom the abomination of the Ammonites. Solomon does that which is evil in YHWH’s sight, and doesn’t go fully after YHWH, as David his father does. Then Solomon builds a high place for Chemosh the abomination of Moab, on the mountain that is before Jerusalem, and for Molech the abomination of the children of Ammon. So he does for all his foreign wives, who burn incense and sacrifice to their gods.
YHWH's Judgment on Solomon · 11:9–13

YHWH is angry with Solomon, because his heart is turned away from YHWH, the God of Israel, who has appeared to him twice, and has commanded him concerning this thing, that he should not go after other gods; but he doesn’t keep that which YHWH commands. Therefore YHWH says to Solomon, “Because this is done by you, and you have not kept my covenant and my statutes, which I have commanded you, I will surely tear the kingdom from you, and will give it to your servant. Nevertheless, I will not do it in your days, for David your father’s sake; but I will tear it out of your son’s hand. However I will not tear away all the kingdom; but I will give one tribe to your son, for David my servant’s sake, and for Jerusalem’s sake which I have chosen.”
Three Adversaries · 11:14–40

YHWH raises up an adversary to Solomon: Hadad the Edomite. He is one of the king’s offspring in Edom. For when David is in Edom, and Joab the captain of the army has gone up to bury the slain, and has struck every male in Edom (for Joab and all Israel remain there six months, until he has cut off every male in Edom); Hadad flees, he and certain Edomites of his father’s servants with him, to go into Egypt, when Hadad is still a little child. They arise out of Midian, and come to Paran; and they take men with them out of Paran, and they come to Egypt, to Pharaoh king of Egypt, who gives him a house, and appoint him food, and give him land. Hadad finds great favor in the sight of Pharaoh, so that he gives him as wife the sister of his own wife, the sister of Tahpenes the queen. The sister of Tahpenes bears him Genubath his son, whom Tahpenes weaned in Pharaoh’s house; and Genubath is in Pharaoh’s house among the sons of Pharaoh. When Hadad hears in Egypt that David sleeps with his fathers, and that Joab the captain of the army is dead, Hadad says to Pharaoh, “Let me depart, that I may go to my own country.”
Then Pharaoh says to him, “But what have you lacked with me, that look, you seek to go to your own country?”
He answers, “Nothing, however only let me depart.”

God raises up an adversary to him, Rezon the son of Eliada, who has fled from his lord Hadadezer king of Zobah. He gathers men to himself, and becomes captain over a troop, when David kills them of Zobah. They go to Damascus, and live there, and reigned in Damascus. He is an adversary to Israel all the days of Solomon, besides the mischief of Hadad. He abhors Israel, and reigns over Syria. Jeroboam the son of Nebat, an Ephraimite of Zeredah, a servant of Solomon, whose mother’s name is Zeruah, a widow, also lifts up his hand against the king. This is the reason why he lifts up his hand against the king: Solomon builds Millo, and repairs the breach of his father David’s city. The man Jeroboam is a mighty man of valor; and Solomon sees the young man that he is industrious, and he puts him in charge of all the labor of the house of Joseph. At that time, when Jeroboam goes out of Jerusalem, the prophet Ahijah the Shilonite finds him on the way; now Ahijah has clad himself with a new garment; and they two are alone in the field. Ahijah lays hold of the new garment that is on him, and tears it in twelve pieces. He says to Jeroboam, “Take ten pieces; for YHWH, the God of Israel, says, ‘Look, I will tear the kingdom out of the hand of Solomon, and will give ten tribes to you (but he will have one tribe, for my servant David’s sake and for Jerusalem’s sake, the city which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel); because that they have forsaken me, and have worshiped Ashtoreth the goddess of the Sidonians, Chemosh the god of Moab, and Milcom the god of the children of Ammon. They have not walked in my ways, to do that which is right in my eyes, and to keep my statutes and my ordinances, as David his father did.

“‘However I will not take the whole kingdom out of his hand; but I will make him prince all the days of his life, for David my servant’s sake whom I chose, who kept my commandments and my statutes; but I will take the kingdom out of his son’s hand, and will give it to you, even ten tribes. To his son will I give one tribe, that David my servant may have a lamp always before me in Jerusalem, the city which I have chosen for myself to put my name there. I will take you, and you will reign according to all that your soul desires, and will be king over Israel. It will be, if you will listen to all that I command you, and will walk in my ways, and do that which is right in my eyes, to keep my statutes and my commandments, as David my servant did; that I will be with you, and will build you a sure house, as I built for David, and will give Israel to you. I will afflict the offspring of David for this, but not forever.’”
Therefore Solomon seeks to kill Jeroboam; but Jeroboam arises, and flees into Egypt, to Shishak king of Egypt, and is in Egypt until the death of Solomon.
The Death of Solomon · 11:41–43

Now the rest of the acts of Solomon, and all that he does, and his wisdom, aren’t they write in the book of the acts of Solomon? The time that Solomon reigns in Jerusalem over all Israel is forty years. Solomon sleeps with his fathers, and is buried in his father David’s city; and Rehoboam his son reigns in his place.
Rehoboam and the Assembly at Shechem · 12:1–15

Rehoboam goes to Shechem, for all Israel has come to Shechem to make him king. When Jeroboam the son of Nebat hears of it (for he is yet in Egypt, where he has fled from the presence of king Solomon, and Jeroboam lives in Egypt, and they send and call him), Jeroboam and all the assembly of Israel come, and speak to Rehoboam, saying, “Your father made our yoke difficult. Now therefore make the hard service of your father, and his heavy yoke which he put on us, lighter, and we will serve you.”
He says to them, “Depart for three days, then come back to me.”
The people depart.
King Rehoboam takes counsel with the old men, who have stood before Solomon his father while he yet lives, saying, “What counsel do you give me to answer these people?”
They reply, “If you will be a servant to this people today, and will serve them, and answer them with good words, then they will be your servants forever.”

But he abandons the counsel of the old men which they have given him, and takes counsel with the young men who have grown up with him, who stand before him. He says to them, “What counsel do you give, that we may answer these people, who have spoken to me, saying, ‘Make the yoke that your father put on us lighter?’”

The young men who have grown up with him say to him, “Tell these people who spoke to you, saying, ‘Your father made our yoke heavy, but make it lighter to us;’ tell them, ‘My little finger is thicker than my father’s waist. Now my father burdened you with a heavy yoke, but I will add to your yoke. My father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.’”

So Jeroboam and all the people come to Rehoboam the third day, as the king asks, saying, “Come to me again the third day.” The king answers the people roughly, and abandons the counsel of the old men which they have given him, and speak to them according to the counsel of the young men, saying, “My father made your yoke heavy, but I will add to your yoke. My father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.”
So the king doesn’t listen to the people; for it is a thing brought about from YHWH, that he might establish his word, which YHWH speaks by Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam the son of Nebat.
The Kingdom Tears Apart · 12:16–24

When all Israel sees that the king doesn’t listen to them, the people answer the king, saying, “What portion have we in David? We don’t have an inheritance in the son of Jesse. To your tents, Israel! Now see to your own house, David.” So Israel departs to their tents.

But as for the children of Israel who live in the cities of Judah, Rehoboam reigns over them. Then king Rehoboam sends Adoram, who is over the men subject to forced labor; and all Israel stones him to death with stones. King Rehoboam hurries to get himself up to his chariot, to flee to Jerusalem. So Israel rebels against David’s house to this day. When all Israel hears that Jeroboam has returned, they send and call him to the congregation, and make him king over all Israel. There is no one who follows David’s house, except for the tribe of Judah only. When Rehoboam has come to Jerusalem, he assembles all the house of Judah and the tribe of Benjamin, a hundred and eighty thousand chosen men, who are warriors, to fight against the house of Israel, to bring the kingdom again to Rehoboam the son of Solomon. But the word of God comes to Shemaiah the man of God, saying, “Speak to Rehoboam the son of Solomon, king of Judah, and to all the house of Judah and Benjamin, and to the rest of the people, saying, ‘YHWH says, “You will not go up or fight against your brothers, the children of Israel. Everyone return to his house; for this thing is from me.”’” So they listen to YHWH’s word, and return and go their way, according to YHWH’s word.
Jeroboam's Golden Calves · 12:25–33

Then Jeroboam builds Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim, and lives in it; and he goes out from there, and builds Penuel. Jeroboam says in his heart, “Now the kingdom will return to David’s house. If this people goes up to offer sacrifices in YHWH’s house at Jerusalem, then the heart of this people will turn again to their lord, even to Rehoboam king of Judah; and they will kill me, and return to Rehoboam king of Judah.” So the king takes counsel, and makes two calves of gold; and he says to them, “It is too much for you to go up to Jerusalem. Look and look your gods, Israel, which brought you up out of the land of Egypt!” He sets the one in Bethel, and the other puts he in Dan. This thing becomes a sin; for the people go even as far as Dan to worship before the one there. He makes houses of high places, and makes priests from among all the people, who are not of the sons of Levi. Jeroboam ordains a feast in the eighth month, on the fifteenth day of the month, like the feast that is in Judah, and he goes up to the altar. He does so in Bethel, sacrificing to the calves that he has made, and he places in Bethel the priests of the high places that he has made. He goes up to the altar which he has made in Bethel on the fifteenth day in the eighth month, even in the month which he has devised of his own heart; and he ordains a feast for the children of Israel, and goes up to the altar, to burn incense.
The Man of God from Judah · 13:1–10

Look, a man of God comes out of Judah by YHWH’s word to Beth El; and Jeroboam is standing by the altar to burn incense. He cries against the altar by YHWH’s word, and says, “Altar! Altar! YHWH says: ‘Look, a son will be born to David’s house, Josiah by name. On you he will sacrifice the priests of the high places who burn incense on you, and they will burn men’s bones on you.’” He gives a sign the same day, saying, “This is the sign which YHWH has spoken: Look, the altar will be split apart, and the ashes that are on it will be poured out.”

When the king hears the saying of the man of God, which he cries against the altar in Bethel, Jeroboam puts out his hand from the altar, saying, “Seize him!” His hand, which he puts out against him, dried up, so that he can not draw it back again to himself. The altar is also split apart, and the ashes pour out from the altar, according to the sign which the man of God has given by YHWH’s word. The king answers the man of God, “Now intercede for the favor of YHWH your God, and pray for me, that my hand may be restored me again.”
The man of God interceded with YHWH, and the king’s hand is restored to him again, and becomes as it is before.
The king says to the man of God, “Come home with me, and refresh yourself, and I will give you a reward.”

The man of God says to the king, “Even if you gave me half of your house, I would not go in with you, neither would I eat bread nor drink water in this place; for so was it commanded me by YHWH’s word, saying, ‘You will eat no bread, drink no water, and don’t return by the way that you came.’” So he goes another way, and doesn’t return by the way that he comes to Bethel.
The Lying Prophet · 13:11–32

Now an old prophet lives in Bethel, and one of his sons comes and tells him all the works that the man of God has done that day in Bethel. They also tell their father the words which he has spoken to the king.

Their father says to them, “Which way did he go?” Now his sons have seen which way the man of God goes, who comes from Judah. He says to his sons, “Saddle the donkey for me.” So they saddle the donkey for him; and he rides on it. He goes after the man of God, and finds him sitting under an oak. He says to him, “Are you the man of God who came from Judah?”
He says, “I am.” Then he says to him, “Come home with me, and eat bread.”

He says, “I may not return with you, nor go in with you. I will not eat bread or drink water with you in this place. For it was said to me by YHWH’s word, ‘You will eat no bread or drink water there, and don’t turn again to go by the way that you came.’”
He says to him, “I also am a prophet as you are; and an angel spoke to me by YHWH’s word, saying, ‘Bring him back with you into your house, that he may eat bread and drink water.’” He lies to him.

So he goes back with him, eats bread in his house, and drank water. As they sit at the table, YHWH’s word comes to the prophet who brings him back; and he cries out to the man of God who comes from Judah, saying, “YHWH says, ‘Because you have been disobedient to YHWH’s mouth, and have not kept the commandment which YHWH your God commanded you, but came back, and have eaten bread and drank water in the place of which he said to you, “Eat no bread, and drink no water”; your body will not come to the tomb of your fathers.’”

After he has eaten bread, and after he drinks, he saddles the donkey for the prophet whom he has brought back. When he has gone, a lion meets him by the way and kills him. His body is thrown on the path, and the donkey stands by it. The lion also stands by the body. Look, men pass by, and see the body thrown on the path, and the lion standing by the body; and they come and tell it in the city where the old prophet lives. When the prophet who brings him back from the way heard of it, he says, “It is the man of God who was disobedient to YHWH’s mouth. Therefore YHWH has delivered him to the lion, which has mauled him and slain him, according to YHWH’s word, which he spoke to him.” He says to his sons, saying, “Saddle the donkey for me,” and they saddle it. He goes and finds his body thrown on the path, and the donkey and the lion standing by the body. The lion has not eaten the body, nor mauls the donkey. The prophet takes up the body of the man of God, and lays it on the donkey, and brings it back. He comes to the city of the old prophet to mourn, and to bury him. He lays his body in his own grave; and they mourn over him, saying, “Alas, my brother!”

After he has buried him, he speaks to his sons, saying, “When I am dead, bury me in the tomb in which the man of God is buried. Lay my bones beside his bones. For the saying which he cried by YHWH’s word against the altar in Bethel, and against all the houses of the high places which are in the cities of Samaria, will surely happen.”
Jeroboam's Persistent Sin · 13:33–34

After this thing Jeroboam doesn’t return from his evil way, but again makes priests of the high places from among all the people. Whoever wants to, he consecrates him, that there might be priests of the high places. This thing becomes sin to the house of Jeroboam, even to cut it off, and to destroy it from off the surface of the earth.
Jeroboam's Sick Son · 14:1–18

At that time Abijah the son of Jeroboam becomes sick. Jeroboam says to his wife, “Please get up and disguise yourself, so that you won’t be recognized as Jeroboam’s wife. Go to Shiloh. Look, Ahijah the prophet is there, who said that that I would be king over this people. Take with you ten loaves of bread, some cakes, and a jar of honey, and go to him. He will tell you what will become of the child.”

Jeroboam’s wife does so, and arises, and goes to Shiloh, and comes to Ahijah’s house. Now Ahijah can not see; for his eyes are set by reason of his age. YHWH says to Ahijah, “Look, Jeroboam’s wife is coming to inquire of you concerning her son; for he is sick. Tell her such and such; for it will be, when she comes in, that she will pretend to be another woman.”

So when Ahijah hears the sound of her feet as she comes in at the door, he says, “Come in, Jeroboam’s wife! Why do you pretend to be another? For I am sent to you with heavy news. Go, tell Jeroboam, ‘YHWH, the God of Israel, says: “Because I exalted you from among the people, and made you prince over my people Israel, and tore the kingdom away from David’s house, and gave it you; and yet you have not been as my servant David, who kept my commandments, and who followed me with all his heart, to do that only which was right in my eyes, but have done evil above all who were before you, and have gone and made for yourself other gods, molten images, to provoke me to anger, and have cast me behind your back; therefore, look, I will bring evil on the house of Jeroboam, and will cut off from Jeroboam everyone who urinates on a wall, he who is shut up and he who is left at large in Israel, and will utterly sweep away the house of Jeroboam, as a man sweeps away dung, until it is all gone. The dogs will eat he who belongs to Jeroboam who dies in the city; and the birds of the sky will eat he who dies in the field: for YHWH has spoken it.”’ Arise therefore, and go to your house. When your feet enter into the city, the child will die. All Israel will mourn for him and bury him; for he only of Jeroboam will come to the grave, because in him there is found some good thing toward YHWH, the God of Israel, in the house of Jeroboam. Moreover YHWH will raise up a king for himself over Israel, who will cut off the house of Jeroboam. This is the day! What? Even now. For YHWH will strike Israel, as a reed is shaken in the water; and he will root up Israel out of this good land which he gives to their fathers, and will scatter them beyond the River, because they have made their Asherah poles, provoking YHWH to anger. He will give Israel up because of the sins of Jeroboam, which he has sinned, and with which he has made Israel to sin.”

Jeroboam’s wife arises and departs, and comes to Tirzah. As she comes to the threshold of the house, the child dies. All Israel buries him and mourns for him, according to YHWH’s word, which he speaks by his servant Ahijah the prophet.
The End of Jeroboam · 14:19–20

The rest of the acts of Jeroboam, how he fights, and how he reigns, look, they are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel. The days which Jeroboam reigns are twenty two years, then he sleeps with his fathers, and Nadab his son reigns in his place.
Rehoboam King of Judah · 14:21–31

Rehoboam the son of Solomon reigns in Judah. Rehoboam is forty-one years old when he begins to reign, and he reigns seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city which YHWH has chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, to put his name there. His mother’s name is Naamah the Ammonitess. Judah does that which is evil in YHWH’s sight, and they provoke him to jealousy with their sins which they commit, above all that their fathers have done. For they also build for themselves high places, sacred pillars, and Asherah poles on every high hill and under every green tree. There are also sodomites in the land. They do according to all the abominations of the nations which YHWH drives out before the children of Israel. In the fifth year of king Rehoboam, Shishak king of Egypt comes up against Jerusalem, and he takes away the treasures of YHWH’s house, and the treasures of the king’s house. He even takes away all of it, including all the gold shields which Solomon has made. King Rehoboam makes shields of brass in their place, and commits them to the hands of the captains of the guard, who keep the door of the king’s house. It is so, that as often as the king goes into YHWH’s house, the guard bears them, and brings them back into the guard room.

Now the rest of the acts of Rehoboam, and all that he does, aren’t they write in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah? There is war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam continually. Rehoboam sleeps with his fathers, and is buried with his fathers in David’s city. His mother’s name is Naamah the Ammonitess. Abijam his son reigns in his place.
Abijam King of Judah · 15:1–8

Now in the eighteenth year of king Jeroboam the son of Nebat, Abijam begins to reign over Judah. He reigns three years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name is Maacah the daughter of Abishalom. He walks in all the sins of his father, which he has done before him; and his heart is not perfect with YHWH his God, as the heart of David his father. Nevertheless for David’s sake, YHWH his God gives him a lamp in Jerusalem, to set up his son after him, and to establish Jerusalem; because David does that which is right in YHWH’s eyes, and doesn’t turn away from anything that he commands him all the days of his life, except only in the matter of Uriah the Hittite. Now there is war between Rehoboam and Jeroboam all the days of his life. The rest of the acts of Abijam, and all that he does, aren’t they write in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah? There is war between Abijam and Jeroboam. Abijam sleeps with his fathers, and they bury him in David’s city; and Asa his son reigns in his place.
Asa King of Judah · 15:9–24

In the twentieth year of Jeroboam king of Israel, Asa begins to reign over Judah. He reigns forty-one years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name is Maacah the daughter of Abishalom. Asa does that which is right in YHWH’s eyes, as David his father does. He puts away the sodomites out of the land, and removes all the idols that his fathers have made. He also removes Maacah his mother from being queen, because she has made an abominable image for an Asherah. Asa cuts down her image and burns it at the brook Kidron. But the high places are not taken away. Nevertheless the heart of Asa is perfect with YHWH all his days. He brings into YHWH’s house the things that his father has dedicated, and the things that he himself has dedicated: silver, gold, and utensils. There is war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel all their days. Baasha king of Israel goes up against Judah, and builds Ramah, that he might not allow anyone to go out or come in to Asa king of Judah. Then Asa takes all the silver and the gold that is left in the treasures of YHWH’s house, and the treasures of the king’s house, and delivers it into the hand of his servants. Then King Asa sends them to Ben Hadad, the son of Tabrimmon, the son of Hezion, king of Syria, who lives at Damascus, saying, “There is a treaty between me and you, between my father and your father. Look, I have sent to you a present of silver and gold. Go, break your treaty with Baasha king of Israel, that he may depart from me.”

Ben Hadad listens to king Asa, and sends the captains of his armies against the cities of Israel, and strikes Ijon, and Dan, and Abel Beth Maacah, and all Chinneroth, with all the land of Naphtali. When Baasha hears of it, he stops building Ramah, and lives in Tirzah. Then king Asa makes a proclamation to all Judah. No one is exempted. They carry away the stones of Ramah, and its timber, with which Baasha has built; and king Asa uses it to build Geba of Benjamin, and Mizpah. Now the rest of all the acts of Asa, and all his might, and all that he does, and the cities which he builds, aren’t they write in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah? But in the time of his old age he is diseased in his feet. Asa sleeps with his fathers, and is buried with his fathers in his father David’s city; and Jehoshaphat his son reigns in his place.
Nadab King of Israel · 15:25–32

Nadab the son of Jeroboam begins to reign over Israel in the second year of Asa king of Judah; and he reigns over Israel two years. He does that which is evil in YHWH’s sight, and walks in the way of his father, and in his sin with which he makes Israel to sin. Baasha the son of Ahijah, of the house of Issachar, conspires against him; and Baasha strikes him at Gibbethon, which belongs to the Philistines; for Nadab and all Israel are besieging Gibbethon. Even in the third year of Asa king of Judah, Baasha kills him, and reigns in his place. As soon as he is king, he strikes all the house of Jeroboam. He doesn’t leave to Jeroboam any who breathes, until he has destroyed him; according to the saying of YHWH, which he speaks by his servant Ahijah the Shilonite; for the sins of Jeroboam which he sins, and with which he makes Israel to sin, because of his provocation with which he provokes YHWH, the God of Israel, to anger. Now the rest of the acts of Nadab, and all that he does, aren’t they write in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel? There is war between Asa and Baasha king of Israel all their days.
Baasha King of Israel · 15:33–34

In the third year of Asa king of Judah, Baasha the son of Ahijah begin to reign over all Israel in Tirzah for twenty-four years. He does that which is evil in YHWH’s sight, and walks in the way of Jeroboam, and in his sin with which he makes Israel to sin.
The Word against Baasha · 16:1–7

YHWH’s word comes to Jehu the son of Hanani against Baasha, saying, “Because I exalted you out of the dust, and made you prince over my people Israel, and you have walked in the way of Jeroboam, and have made my people Israel to sin, to provoke me to anger with their sins; look, I will utterly sweep away Baasha and his house; and I will make your house like the house of Jeroboam the son of Nebat. The dogs will eat Baasha’s descendants who die in the city; and he who dies of his in the field, the birds of the sky will eat.”

Now the rest of the acts of Baasha, and what he does, and his might, aren’t they write in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel? Baasha sleeps with his fathers, and is buried in Tirzah; and Elah his son reigns in his place.

Moreover YHWH’s word comes by the prophet Jehu the son of Hanani against Baasha and against his house, both because of all the evil that he does in YHWH’s sight, to provoke him to anger with the work of his hands, in being like the house of Jeroboam, and because he strikes him.
Elah, Zimri, and the Fall of Baasha's House · 16:8–20

In the twenty-sixth year of Asa king of Judah, Elah the son of Baasha begins to reign over Israel in Tirzah for two years. His servant Zimri, captain of half his chariots, conspires against him. Now he is in Tirzah, drinking himself drunk in the house of Arza, who is over the household in Tirzah; and Zimri goes in and strikes him, and kills him, in the twenty-seventh year of Asa king of Judah, and reigns in his place.

When he begins to reign, as soon as he sits on his throne, he attacks all the house of Baasha. He doesn’t leave him a single one who urinates on a wall among his relatives or his friends. Thus Zimri destroys all the house of Baasha, according to YHWH’s word, which he speaks against Baasha by Jehu the prophet, for all the sins of Baasha, and the sins of Elah his son, which they sin, and with which they make Israel to sin, to provoke YHWH, the God of Israel, to anger with their vanities. Now the rest of the acts of Elah, and all that he does, aren’t they write in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel? In the twenty-seventh year of Asa king of Judah, Zimri reigns seven days in Tirzah. Now the people are encamped against Gibbethon, which belongs to the Philistines. The people who are encamped heard that Zimri has conspired, and have also killed the king. Therefore all Israel makes Omri, the captain of the army, king over Israel that day in the camp. Omri goes up from Gibbethon, and all Israel with him, and they besiege Tirzah. When Zimri sees that the city is taken, he goes into the fortified part of the king’s house, and burns the king’s house over him with fire, and dies, for his sins which he sins in doing that which is evil in YHWH’s sight, in walking in the way of Jeroboam, and in his sin which he does, to make Israel to sin. Now the rest of the acts of Zimri, and his treason that he commits, aren’t they write in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
Omri King of Israel · 16:21–28

Then the people of Israel are divided into two parts: half of the people follows Tibni the son of Ginath, to make him king; and half follows Omri. But the people who follow Omri prevail against the people who follow Tibni the son of Ginath; so Tibni dies, and Omri reigns. In the thirty-first year of Asa king of Judah, Omri begins to reign over Israel for twelve years. He reigns six years in Tirzah. He buys the hill Samaria of Shemer for two talents of silver; and he builds on the hill, and calls the name of the city which he builds Samaria, after the name of Shemer, the owner of the hill. Omri does that which is evil in YHWH’s sight, and deals wickedly above all who are before him. For he walks in all the way of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, and in his sins with which he makes Israel to sin, to provoke YHWH, the God of Israel, to anger with their vanities. Now the rest of the acts of Omri which he does, and his might that he shows, aren’t they write in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel? So Omri sleeps with his fathers, and is buried in Samaria; and Ahab his son reigns in his place.
Ahab King of Israel · 16:29–34

In the thirty-eighth year of Asa king of Judah, Ahab the son of Omri begins to reign over Israel. Ahab the son of Omri reigns over Israel in Samaria twenty-two years. Ahab the son of Omri does that which is evil in YHWH’s sight above all that are before him. As if it has been a light thing for him to walk in the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, he takes as wife Jezebel the daughter of Ethbaal king of the Sidonians, and goes and serves Baal, and worships him. He raises up an altar for Baal in the house of Baal, which he has built in Samaria. Ahab makes the Asherah; and Ahab does more yet to provoke YHWH, the God of Israel, to anger than all the kings of Israel who are before him. In his days Hiel the Bethelite builds Jericho. He lays its foundation with the loss of Abiram his firstborn, and sets up its gates with the loss of his youngest son Segub, according to YHWH’s word, which he speaks by Joshua the son of Nun.
Elijah Declares the Drought · 17:1

Elijah the Tishbite, who is one of the settlers of Gilead, says to Ahab, “As YHWH, the God of Israel, lives, before whom I stand, there will not be dew nor rain these years, but according to my word.”
By the Brook Cherith · 17:2–7

Then YHWH’s word comes to him, saying, “Go away from here, turn eastward, and hide yourself by the brook Cherith, that is before the Jordan. You will drink from the brook. I have commanded the ravens to feed you there.” So he goes and does according to YHWH’s word; for he goes and lives by the brook Cherith that is before the Jordan. The ravens bring him bread and meat in the morning, and bread and meat in the evening; and he drinks from the brook. After a while, the brook dries up, because there is no rain in the land.
The Widow of Zarephath · 17:8–24
YHWH’s word comes to him, saying, “Arise, go to Zarephath, which belongs to Sidon, and stay there. Look, I have commanded a widow there to sustain you.”

So he arises and goes to Zarephath; and when he comes to the gate of the city, look, a widow is there gathering sticks. He calls to her, and says, “Please get me a little water in a jar, that I may drink.”
As she is going to get it, he calls to her, and says, “Please bring me a morsel of bread in your hand.”

She says, “As YHWH your God lives, I don’t have a cake, but a handful of meal in a jar, and a little oil in a jar. Look, I am gathering two sticks, that I may go in and bake it for me and my son, that we may eat it, and die.”

Elijah says to her, “Don’t be afraid. Go and do as you have said; but make me a little cake from it first, and bring it out to me, and afterward make some for you and for your son. For YHWH, the God of Israel says, ‘The jar of meal will not run out, and the jar of oil will not fail, until the day that YHWH sends rain on the earth.’”

She goes and does according to the saying of Elijah; and she, and he, and her house, eats many days. The jar of meal doesn’t run out, and the jar of oil does not fail, according to YHWH’s word, which he speaks by Elijah. After these things, the son of the woman, the mistress of the house, becomes sick; and his sickness is so severe that there is no breath left in him. She says to Elijah, “What have I to do with you, you man of God? You have come to me to bring my sin to memory, and to kill my son!”

He says to her, “Give me your son.” He takes him out of her bosom, and carries him up into the room where he stays, and lays him on his own bed. He cries to YHWH, and says, “YHWH my God, have you also brought evil on the widow with whom I am staying, by killing her son?”
He stretches himself on the child three times, and cries to YHWH, and says, “YHWH my God, please let this child’s soul come into him again.”

YHWH listens to the voice of Elijah; and the soul of the child comes into him again, and he revives. Elijah takes the child, and brings him down out of the room into the house, and delivers him to his mother; and Elijah says, “Look, your son lives.”
The woman says to Elijah, “Now I know that you are a man of God, and that YHWH’s word in your mouth is truth.”
Elijah Meets Obadiah · 18:1–16
After many days, YHWH’s word comes to Elijah, in the third year, saying, “Go, show yourself to Ahab; and I will send rain on the earth.”

Elijah goes to show himself to Ahab. The famine is severe in Samaria. Ahab calls Obadiah, who is over the household. (Now Obadiah fears YHWH greatly; for when Jezebel cuts off YHWH’s prophets, Obadiah takes one hundred prophets, and hides them by fifty in a cave, and feeds them with bread and water.) Ahab says to Obadiah, “Go through the land, to all the springs of water, and to all the brooks. Perhaps we may find grass and save the horses and mules alive, that we not lose all the animals.”

So they divide the land between them to pass throughout it. Ahab goes one way by himself, and Obadiah goes another way by himself. As Obadiah is on the way, look, Elijah meets him. He recognizes him, and falls on his face, and says, “Is it you, my lord Elijah?”
He answers him, “It is I. Go, tell your lord, ‘Look, Elijah is here!’”

He says, “How have I sinned, that you would deliver your servant into the hand of Ahab, to kill me? As YHWH your God lives, there is no nation or kingdom where my lord has not sent to seek you. When they said, ‘He is not here,’ he took an oath of the kingdom and nation, that they didn’t find you. Now you say, ‘Go, tell your lord, “Look, Elijah is here.”’ It will happen, as soon as I leave you, that YHWH’s Spirit will carry you I don’t know where; and so when I come and tell Ahab, and he can’t find you, he will kill me. But I, your servant, have feared YHWH from my youth. Isn’t it tells my lord what I do when Jezebel kills YHWH’s prophets, how I hide one hundred men of YHWH’s prophets with fifty to a cave, and feed them with bread and water? Now you say, ‘Go, tell your lord, “Look, Elijah is here”.’ He will kill me.”
Elijah says, “As YHWH of hosts lives, before whom I stand, I will surely show myself to him today.” So Obadiah goes to meet Ahab, and tells him; and Ahab goes to meet Elijah.
Elijah and Ahab · 18:17–19
When Ahab sees Elijah, Ahab says to him, “Is that you, you troubler of Israel?”

He answers, “I have not troubled Israel; but you, and your father’s house, in that you have forsaken YHWH’s commandments, and you have followed the Baals. Now therefore send, and gather to me all Israel to Mount Carmel, and four hundred fifty of the prophets of Baal, and four hundred of the prophets of the Asherah, who eat at Jezebel’s table.”
The Contest on Carmel · 18:20–40

So Ahab sends to all the children of Israel, and gathers the prophets together to Mount Carmel. Elijah comes near to all the people, and says, “How long will you waver between the two sides? If YHWH is God, follow him; but if Baal, then follow him.”
The people don’t say a word.

Then Elijah says to the people, “I, even I only, am left as a prophet of YHWH; but Baal’s prophets are four hundred fifty men. Let them therefore give us two bulls; and let them choose one bull for themselves, and cut it in pieces, and lay it on the wood, and put no fire under; and I will dress the other bull, and lay it on the wood, and put no fire under it. You call on the name of your god, and I will call on YHWH’s name. The God who answers by fire, let him be God.”
All the people answer, “What you say is good.”
Elijah says to the prophets of Baal, “Choose one bull for yourselves, and dress it first; for you are many; and call on the name of your god, but put no fire under it.”

They take the bull which is given them, and they dress it, and call on the name of Baal from morning even until noon, saying, “Baal, hear us!” But there is no voice, and nobody answers. They leap about the altar which is made. At noon, Elijah mocks them, and says, “Cry aloud; for he is a god. Either he is deep in thought, or he has gone somewhere, or he is on a journey, or perhaps he sleeps and must be awakened.”

They cry aloud, and cut themselves in their way with knives and lances, until the blood gushes out on them. When midday is past, they prophesy until the time of the evening offering; but there is no voice, no answer, and nobody pays attention.

Elijah says to all the people, “Come near to me!”; and all the people come near to him. He repairs YHWH’s altar that has been thrown down. Elijah takes twelve stones, according to the number of the tribes of the sons of Jacob, to whom YHWH’s word comes, saying, “Israel will be your name.” With the stones he builds an altar in YHWH’s name. He makes a trench around the altar, large enough to contain two seahs of seed. He puts the wood in order, and cuts the bull in pieces, and lays it on the wood. He says, “Fill four jars with water, and pour it on the burnt offering, and on the wood.” He says, “Do it a second time”; and they do it the second time. He says, “Do it a third time”; and they do it the third time. The water runs around the altar; and he also fills the trench with water.

At the time of the evening offering, Elijah the prophet comes near, and says, “YHWH, the God of Abraham, of Isaac, and of Israel, let it be known today that you are God in Israel, and that I am your servant, and that I have done all these things at your word. Hear me, YHWH, hear me, that this people may know that you, YHWH, are God, and that you have turned their heart back again.”

Then YHWH’s fire falls, and consumes the burnt offering, the wood, the stones, and the dust, and licks up the water that is in the trench. When all the people see it, they fall on their faces. They say, “YHWH, he is God! YHWH, he is God!”
Elijah says to them, “Seize the prophets of Baal! Don’t let one of them escape!”
They seize them; and Elijah brings them down to the brook Kishon, and kills them there.
The Rain Returns · 18:41–46
Elijah says to Ahab, “Get up, eat and drink; for there is the sound of abundance of rain.”

So Ahab goes up to eat and to drink. Elijah goes up to the top of Carmel; and he bows himself down on the earth, and puts his face between his knees. He says to his servant, “Go up now, and look toward the sea.”
He goes up, and looks, and says, “There is nothing.”
He says, “Go again” seven times.
On the seventh time, he says, “Look, a small cloud, like a man’s hand, is rising out of the sea.”
He says, “Go up, tell Ahab, ‘Get ready and go down, so that the rain doesn’t stop you.’”

In a little while, the sky grows black with clouds and wind, and there is a great rain. Ahab rides, and goes to Jezreel. YHWH’s hand is on Elijah; and he tucks his cloak into his belt and runs before Ahab to the entrance of Jezreel.
Elijah Flees to Horeb · 19:1–8

Ahab tells Jezebel all that Elijah has done, and how he has killed all the prophets with the sword. Then Jezebel sends a messenger to Elijah, saying, “So let the gods do to me, and more also, if I don’t make your life as the life of one of them by tomorrow about this time!”

When he sees that, he arises, and runs for his life, and comes to Beersheba, which belongs to Judah, and leaves his servant there. But he himself goes a day’s journey into the wilderness, and comes and sits down under a juniper tree. Then he requests for himself that he might die, and says, “It is enough. Now, O YHWH, take away my life; for I am not better than my fathers.”
He lies down and sleeps under a juniper tree; and look, an angel touches him, and says to him, “Arise and eat!”

He looks, and look, there is at his head a cake baked on the coals, and a jar of water. He eats and drank, and lies down again. YHWH’s angel comes again the second time, and touches him, and says, “Arise and eat, because the journey is too great for you.”
He arises, and eats and drank, and goes in the strength of that food forty days and forty nights to Horeb, God’s Mountain.
The Still Small Voice · 19:9–18
He comes to a cave there, and camps there; and look, YHWH’s word comes to him, and he says to him, “What are you doing here, Elijah?”

He says, “I have been very jealous for YHWH, the God of Armies; for the children of Israel have forsaken your covenant, thrown down your altars, and killed your prophets with the sword. I, even I only, am left; and they seek my life, to take it away.”
He says, “Go out, and stand on the mountain before YHWH.”

Look, YHWH passes by, and a great and strong wind tears the mountains, and breaks in pieces the rocks before YHWH; but YHWH is not in the wind. After the wind there is an earthquake; but YHWH is not in the earthquake. After the earthquake a fire passes; but YHWH is not in the fire. After the fire, there is a still small voice. When Elijah hears it, he wraps his face in his mantle, goes out, and stands in the entrance of the cave. Look, a voice comes to him, and says, “What are you doing here, Elijah?”

He says, “I have been very jealous for YHWH, the God of Armies; for the children of Israel have forsaken your covenant, thrown down your altars, and killed your prophets with the sword. I, even I only, am left; and they seek my life, to take it away.”

YHWH says to him, “Go, return on your way to the wilderness of Damascus. When you arrive, anoint Hazael to be king over Syria. Anoint Jehu the son of Nimshi to be king over Israel; and anoint Elisha the son of Shaphat of Abel Meholah to be prophet in your place. He who escapes from the sword of Hazael, Jehu will kill; and he who escapes from the sword of Jehu, Elisha will kill. Yet I reserved seven thousand in Israel, all the knees of which have not bowed to Baal, and every mouth which has not kissed him.”
The Call of Elisha · 19:19–21

So he departs from there, and finds Elisha the son of Shaphat, who is plowing with twelve yoke of oxen before him, and he with the twelfth. Elijah goes over to him, and puts his mantle on him. Elisha leaves the oxen, and runs after Elijah, and says, “Let me please kiss my father and my mother, and then I will follow you.”
He says to him, “Go back again; for what have I done to you?”

He returns from following him, and takes the yoke of oxen, and kills them, and boils their meat with the instruments of the oxen, and gives to the people, and they eat. Then he arises, and goes after Elijah, and serves him.
Ben-hadad Besieges Samaria · 20:1–12

Ben Hadad the king of Syria gathers all his army together; and there are thirty-two kings with him, with horses and chariots. He goes up and besieges Samaria, and fights against it. He sends messengers to Ahab king of Israel, into the city, and says to him, “Thus says Ben Hadad, ‘Your silver and your gold is mine. Your wives also and your children, even the best, are mine.’”
The king of Israel answers, “It is according to your saying, my lord, O king. I am yours, and all that I have.”

The messengers come again, and say, “Ben Hadad says, ‘I sent indeed to you, saying, “You will deliver me your silver, and your gold, and your wives, and your children; but I will send my servants to you tomorrow about this time, and they will search your house, and the houses of your servants; whatever is pleasant in your eyes, they will put it in their hand, and take it away.”’”

Then the king of Israel calls all the elders of the land, and says, “Please notice how this man seeks mischief; for he sent to me for my wives, and for my children, and for my silver, and for my gold; and I didn’t deny him.”
All the elders and all the people say to him, “Don’t listen, and don’t consent.”
Therefore he says to the messengers of Ben Hadad, “Tell my lord the king, ‘All that you sent for to your servant at the first I will do; but this thing I cannot do.’”

The messengers depart, and bring him back the message. Ben Hadad sends to him, and says, “The gods do so to me, and more also, if the dust of Samaria will be enough for handfuls for all the people who follow me.”
The king of Israel answers, “Tell him, ‘Don’t let him who puts on his armor brag like he who takes it off.’”
When Ben Hadad hears this message, as he is drinking, he and the kings, in the pavilions, he says to his servants, “Prepare to attack!” They prepare to attack the city.
The Unnamed Prophet and the First Victory · 20:13–22
Look, a prophet comes near to Ahab king of Israel, and says, “YHWH says, ‘Have you seen all this great multitude? Look, I will deliver it into your hand today. Then you will know that I am YHWH.’”
Ahab says, “By whom?”
He says, “YHWH says, ‘By the young men of the princes of the provinces.’”
Then he says, “Who will begin the battle?”
He answers, “You.”

Then he musters the young men of the princes of the provinces, and they are two hundred and thirty-two. After them, he musters all the people, even all the children of Israel, being seven thousand. They go out at noon. But Ben Hadad is drinking himself drunk in the pavilions, he and the kings, the thirty-two kings who help him. The young men of the princes of the provinces go out first; and Ben Hadad sends out, and they tell him, saying, “Men are coming out from Samaria.”
He says, “If they have come out for peace, take them alive; or if they have come out for war, take them alive.”

So these go out of the city, the young men of the princes of the provinces, and the army which follows them. They each kill his man. The Syrians flee, and Israel pursues them. Ben Hadad the king of Syria escapes on a horse with horsemen. The king of Israel goes out, and strikes the horses and chariots, and kills the Syrians with a great slaughter. The prophet comes near to the king of Israel, and says to him, “Go, strengthen yourself, and mark, and see what you do; for at the return of the year the king of Syria will come up against you.”
The Second Campaign · 20:23–34

The servants of the king of Syria say to him, “Their god is a god of the hills; therefore they were stronger than we. But let us fight against them in the plain, and surely we will be stronger than they. Do this thing: take the kings away, every man out of his place, and put captains in their place. Muster an army, like the army that you have lost, horse for horse, and chariot for chariot. We will fight against them in the plain, and surely we will be stronger than them.”

He listens to their voice, and does so. At the return of the year, Ben Hadad musters the Syrians, and goes up to Aphek, to fight against Israel. The children of Israel are mustered and given provisions, and go against them. The children of Israel encamp before them like two little flocks of young goats; but the Syrians fill the country. A man of God comes near and speaks to the king of Israel, and says, “YHWH says, ‘Because the Syrians have said, “YHWH is a god of the hills, but he is not a god of the valleys”; therefore I will deliver all this great multitude into your hand, and you will know that I am YHWH.’”

They encamp opposite each other for seven days. So it is, that in the seventh day the battle is joined; and the children of Israel kill one hundred thousand footmen of the Syrians in one day. But the rest flees to Aphek, into the city; and the wall falls on twenty-seven thousand men who are left. Ben Hadad flees, and comes into the city, into an inner room. His servants say to him, “See now, we have heard that the kings of the house of Israel are merciful kings. Please let us put sackcloth on our bodies, and ropes on our heads, and go out to the king of Israel. Maybe he will save your life.”
So they put sackcloth on their bodies and ropes on their heads, and come to the king of Israel, and say, “Your servant Ben Hadad says, ‘Please let me live.’”
He says, “Is he still alive? He is my brother.”
Now the men observe diligently, and hurry to take this phrase; and they say, “Your brother Ben Hadad.”
Then he says, “Go, bring him.”

Then Ben Hadad comes out to him; and he causes him to come up into the chariot. Ben Hadad says to him, “The cities which my father took from your father I will restore. You will make streets for yourself in Damascus, as my father made in Samaria.”
“I”, say Ahab, “will let you go with this covenant.” So he makes a covenant with him, and let him go.
The Prophet's Rebuke · 20:35–43
A certain man of the sons of the prophets says to his fellow by YHWH’s word, “Please strike me!”

The man refuses to strike him. Then he says to him, “Because you have not obeyed YHWH’s voice, look, as soon as you have departed from me, a lion will kill you.” As soon as he has departed from him, a lion finds him and kills him.
Then he finds another man, and says, “Please strike me.”

The man strikes him and wounds him. So the prophet departs, and waits for the king by the way, and disguises himself with his headband over his eyes. As the king passes by, he cries to the king; and he says, “Your servant went out into the middle of the battle; and look, a man came over, and brought a man to me, and said, ‘Guard this man! If by any means he is missing, then your life will be for his life, or else you will pay a talent of silver.’ As your servant was busy here and there, he was gone.”
The king of Israel says to him, “So will your judgment be. You yourself have decided it.”

He hurries, and takes the headband away from his eyes; and the king of Israel recognizes that he is one of the prophets. He says to him, “YHWH says, ‘Because you have let go out of your hand the man whom I had devoted to destruction, therefore your life will take the place of his life, and your people take the place of his people.’”
The king of Israel goes to his house sullen and angry, and comes to Samaria.
Naboth's Vineyard · 21:1–16

After these things, Naboth the Jezreelite has a vineyard, which is in Jezreel, next to the palace of Ahab king of Samaria. Ahab speaks to Naboth, saying, “Give me your vineyard, that I may have it for a garden of herbs, because it is near my house; and I will give you for it a better vineyard than it. Or, if it seems good to you, I will give you its worth in money.”
Naboth says to Ahab, “May YHWH forbid me, that I should give the inheritance of my fathers to you!”

Ahab comes into his house sullen and angry because of the word which Naboth the Jezreelite has spoken to him; for he has said, “I will not give you the inheritance of my fathers.” He lays himself down on his bed, and turns away his face, and would eat no bread. But Jezebel his wife comes to him, and says to him, “Why is your spirit so sad, that you eat no bread?”

He says to her, “Because I spoke to Naboth the Jezreelite, and said to him, ‘Give me your vineyard for money; or else, if it pleases you, I will give you another vineyard for it.’ He answered, ‘I will not give you my vineyard.’”

Jezebel his wife says to him, “Do you now govern the kingdom of Israel? Arise, and eat bread, and let your heart be merry. I will give you the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite.” So she writes letters in Ahab’s name, and seals them with his seal, and sends the letters to the elders and to the nobles who are in his city, who lives with Naboth. She writes in the letters, saying, “Proclaim a fast, and set Naboth on high among the people. Set two men, wicked fellows, before him, and let them testify against him, saying, ‘You cursed God and the king!’ Then carry him out, and stone him to death.”

The men of his city, even the elders and the nobles who live in his city, do as Jezebel has instructed them in the letters which she has written and sent to them. They proclaim a fast, and set Naboth on high among the people. The two men, the wicked fellows, come in and sit before him. The wicked fellows testify against him, even against Naboth, in the presence of the people, saying, “Naboth cursed God and the king!” Then they carry him out of the city and stone him to death with stones. Then they send to Jezebel, saying, “Naboth has been stoned, and is dead.”

When Jezebel hears that Naboth has been stoned, and is dead, Jezebel says to Ahab, “Arise, take possession of the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, which he refused to give you for money; for Naboth is not alive, but dead.”
When Ahab hears that Naboth is dead, Ahab rises up to go down to the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, to take possession of it.
Elijah's Verdict · 21:17–26

YHWH’s word comes to Elijah the Tishbite, saying, “Arise, go down to meet Ahab king of Israel, who dwells in Samaria. Look, he is in the vineyard of Naboth, where he has gone down to take possession of it. You will speak to him, saying, ‘YHWH says, “Have you killed and also taken possession?”’ You will speak to him, saying, ‘YHWH says, “In the place where dogs licked the blood of Naboth, dogs will lick your blood, even yours.”’”
Ahab says to Elijah, “Have you found me, my enemy?”

He answers, “I have found you, because you have sold yourself to do that which is evil in YHWH’s sight. Look, I will bring evil on you, and will utterly sweep you away and will cut off from Ahab everyone who urinates against a wall, and him who is shut up and him who is left at large in Israel. I will make your house like the house of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, and like the house of Baasha the son of Ahijah for the provocation with which you have provoked me to anger, and have made Israel to sin.” YHWH also speaks of Jezebel, saying, “The dogs will eat Jezebel by the rampart of Jezreel. The dogs will eat he who dies of Ahab in the city; and the birds of the sky will eat he who dies in the field.”

But there is no one like Ahab, who sells himself to do that which is evil in YHWH’s sight, whom Jezebel his wife stirs up. He does very abominably in following idols, according to all that the Amorites do, whom YHWH casts out before the children of Israel.
Ahab Humbles Himself · 21:27–29
When Ahab hears those words, he tears his clothes, and puts sackcloth on his flesh, and fasts, and lies in sackcloth, and goes softly.

YHWH’s word comes to Elijah the Tishbite, saying, “See how Ahab humbles himself before me? Because he humbles himself before me, I will not bring the evil in his days; but I will bring the evil on his house in his son’s day.”
Jehoshaphat and the Campaign at Ramoth-gilead · 22:1–12

They continue three years without war between Syria and Israel. In the third year, Jehoshaphat the king of Judah comes down to the king of Israel. The king of Israel says to his servants, “You know that Ramoth Gilead is ours, and we do nothing, and don’t take it out of the hand of the king of Syria?” He says to Jehoshaphat, “Will you go with me to battle to Ramoth Gilead?”
Jehoshaphat says to the king of Israel, “I am as you are, my people as your people, my horses as your horses.” Jehoshaphat says to the king of Israel, “Please inquire first for YHWH’s word.”
Then the king of Israel gathers the prophets together, about four hundred men, and says to them, “Should I go against Ramoth Gilead to battle, or should I refrain?”
They say, “Go up; for the Lord will deliver it into the hand of the king.”
But Jehoshaphat says, “Isn’t there here a prophet of YHWH, that we may inquire of him?”
The king of Israel says to Jehoshaphat, “There is yet one man by whom we may inquire of YHWH, Micaiah the son of Imlah; but I hate him, for he does not prophesy good concerning me, but evil.”
Jehoshaphat says, “Don’t let the king say so.”
Then the king of Israel calls an officer, and says, “Quickly get Micaiah the son of Imlah.”

Now the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat the king of Judah are sitting each on his throne, arrayed in their robes, in an open place at the entrance of the gate of Samaria; and all the prophets are prophesying before them. Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah makes himself horns of iron, and says, “YHWH says, ‘With these you will push the Syrians, until they are consumed.’” All the prophets prophesy so, saying, “Go up to Ramoth Gilead, and prosper; for YHWH will deliver it into the hand of the king.”
Micaiah the Prophet · 22:13–28
The messenger who goes to call Micaiah speaks to him, saying, “See now, the prophets declare good to the king with one mouth. Please let your word be like the word of one of them, and speak good.”
Micaiah says, “As YHWH lives, what YHWH says to me, that I will speak.”
When he has come to the king, the king says to him, “Micaiah, should we go to Ramoth Gilead to battle, or should we forbear?”

He answers him, “Go up and prosper; and YHWH will deliver it into the hand of the king.” The king says to him, “How many times do I have to adjure you that you speak to me nothing but the truth in YHWH’s name?”
He says, “I saw all Israel scattered on the mountains, as sheep that have no shepherd. YHWH said, ‘These have no master. Let them each return to his house in peace.’”
The king of Israel says to Jehoshaphat, “Didn’t I tell you that he would not prophesy good concerning me, but evil?”

Micaiah says, “Therefore hear YHWH’s word. I saw YHWH sitting on his throne, and all the army of heaven standing by him on his right hand and on his left. YHWH said, ‘Who will entice Ahab, that he may go up and fall at Ramoth Gilead?’ One said one thing; and another said another.
A spirit came out and stood before YHWH, and said, ‘I will entice him.’
YHWH said to him, ‘How?’
He said, ‘I will go out and will be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets.’

He said, ‘You will entice him, and will also prevail. Go out and do so.’ Now therefore, look, YHWH has put a lying spirit in the mouth of all these your prophets; and YHWH has spoken evil concerning you.”
Then Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah comes near, and strikes Micaiah on the cheek, and says, “Which way did YHWH’s Spirit go from me to speak to you?”
Micaiah says, “Look, you will see on that day, when you go into an inner room to hide yourself.”

The king of Israel says, “Take Micaiah, and carry him back to Amon the governor of the city, and to Joash the king’s son. Say, ‘Thus says the king, “Put this fellow in the prison, and feed him with bread of affliction and with water of affliction, until I come in peace.”’”
Micaiah says, “If you return at all in peace, YHWH has not spoken by me.” He says, “Listen, all you people!”
The Death of Ahab · 22:29–40

So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat the king of Judah go up to Ramoth Gilead. The king of Israel says to Jehoshaphat, “I will disguise myself, and go into the battle; but you put on your robes.” The king of Israel disguises himself, and goes into the battle.
Now the king of Syria has commanded the thirty-two captains of his chariots, saying, “Don’t fight with small nor great, except only with the king of Israel.”

When the captains of the chariots see Jehoshaphat, they say, “Surely that is the king of Israel!” and they come over to fight against him. Jehoshaphat cries out. When the captains of the chariots see that it is not the king of Israel, they turn back from pursuing him. A certain man draws his bow at random, and strikes the king of Israel between the joints of the armor. Therefore he says to the driver of his chariot, “Turn your hand, and carry me out of the battle; for I am severely wounded.” The battle increases that day. The king is propped up in his chariot facing the Syrians, and dies at evening. The blood runs out of the wound into the bottom of the chariot. A cry goes throughout the army about the going down of the sun, saying, “Every man to his city, and every man to his country!”

So the king dies, and is brought to Samaria; and they bury the king in Samaria. They wash the chariot by the pool of Samaria; and the dogs lick up his blood where the prostitutes wash themselves; according to YHWH’s word which he speaks.

Now the rest of the acts of Ahab, and all that he does, and the ivory house which he builds, and all the cities that he builds, aren’t they write in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel? So Ahab sleeps with his fathers; and Ahaziah his son reigns in his place.
Jehoshaphat King of Judah · 22:41–50

Jehoshaphat the son of Asa begins to reign over Judah in the fourth year of Ahab king of Israel. Jehoshaphat is thirty-five years old when he begins to reign; and he reigns twenty-five years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name is Azubah the daughter of Shilhi. He walks in all the way of Asa his father. He doesn’t turn away from it, doing that which is right in YHWH’s eyes. However the high places are not taken away. The people still sacrifice and burn incense on the high places. Jehoshaphat makes peace with the king of Israel. Now the rest of the acts of Jehoshaphat, and his might that he shows, and how he fights, aren’t they write in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah? The remnant of the sodomites, that remains in the days of his father Asa, he puts away out of the land. There is no king in Edom. A deputy rules. Jehoshaphat makes ships of Tarshish to go to Ophir for gold, but they don’t go; for the ships wrecked at Ezion Geber. Then Ahaziah the son of Ahab says to Jehoshaphat, “Let my servants go with your servants in the ships.” But Jehoshaphat would not. Jehoshaphat sleeps with his fathers, and is buried with his fathers in his father David’s city. Jehoram his son reigns in his place.
Ahaziah King of Israel · 22:51–53

Ahaziah the son of Ahab begins to reign over Israel in Samaria in the seventeenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and he reigns two years over Israel. He does that which is evil in YHWH’s sight, and walks in the way of his father, and in the way of his mother, and in the way of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, in which he makes Israel to sin. He serves Baal and worships him, and provokes YHWH, the God of Israel, to anger, in all the ways that his father has done so.
Ahaziah Consults Baal-zebub · 1:1–8
