Moab rebels against Israel after the death of Ahab. Ahaziah falls down through the lattice in his upper room that is in Samaria, and is sick. So he sends messengers, and says to them, “Go, inquire of Baal Zebub, the god of Ekron, whether I will recover of this sickness.”

But YHWH’s angel says to Elijah the Tishbite, “Arise, go up to meet the messengers of the king of Samaria, and tell them, ‘Is it because there is no God in Israel, that you go to inquire of Baal Zebub, the god of Ekron? Now therefore YHWH says, “You will not come down from the bed where you have gone up, but you will surely die.”’” Then Elijah departs.
The messengers return to him, and he says to them, “Why is it that you have returned?”

They say to him, “A man came up to meet us, and said to us, ‘Go, return to the king who sent you, and tell him, “YHWH says, ‘Is it because there is no God in Israel, that you send to inquire of Baal Zebub, the god of Ekron? Therefore you will not come down from the bed where you have gone up, but you will surely die.’”’”
He says to them, “What kind of man was he who came up to meet you, and told you these words?”
They answer him, “He was a hairy man, and wearing a leather belt around his waist.”
He says, “It’s Elijah the Tishbite.”
Fire from Heaven · 1:9–16
Then the king sends a captain of fifty with his fifty to him. He goes up to him; and look, he is sitting on the top of the hill. He says to him, “Man of God, the king has said, ‘Come down!’”

Elijah answers to the captain of fifty, “If I am a man of God, then let fire come down from the sky, and consume you and your fifty!” Then fire comes down from the sky, and consumes him and his fifty.
Again he sends to him another captain of fifty with his fifty. He answers him, “Man of God, the king has said, ‘Come down quickly!’”
Elijah answers them, “If I am a man of God, then let fire come down from the sky, and consume you and your fifty!” Then God’s fire comes down from the sky, and consumes him and his fifty.

Again he sends the captain of a third fifty with his fifty. The third captain of fifty goes up, and comes and falls on his knees before Elijah, and begs him, and says to him, “Man of God, please let my life, and the life of these fifty of your servants, be precious in your sight. Look, fire came down from the sky, and consumed the last two captains of fifty with their fifties. But now let my life be precious in your sight.”
YHWH’s angel says to Elijah, “Go down with him. Don’t be afraid of him.”

Then he arises, and goes down with him to the king. He says to him, “YHWH says, ‘Because you have sent messengers to inquire of Baal Zebub, the god of Ekron, is it because there is no God in Israel to inquire of his word? Therefore you will not come down from the bed where you have gone up, but you will surely die.’”
The Death of Ahaziah · 1:17–18

So he dies according to YHWH’s word which Elijah has spoken. Jehoram begins to reign in his place in the second year of Jehoram the son of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, because he has no son. Now the rest of the acts of Ahaziah which he does, aren’t they write in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
Elijah Taken Up in the Whirlwind · 2:1–12
When YHWH is about to take Elijah up by a whirlwind into heaven, Elijah goes with Elisha from Gilgal. Elijah says to Elisha, “Please wait here, for YHWH has sent me as far as Bethel.”
Elisha says, “As YHWH lives, and as your soul lives, I will not leave you.” So they go down to Bethel.
The sons of the prophets who are at Bethel come out to Elisha, and say to him, “Do you know that YHWH will take away your master from your head today?”
He says, “Yes, I know it. Hold your peace.”
Elijah says to him, “Elisha, please wait here, for YHWH has sent me to Jericho.”
He says, “As YHWH lives, and as your soul lives, I will not leave you.” So they come to Jericho.
The sons of the prophets who are at Jericho come near to Elisha, and say to him, “Do you know that YHWH will take away your master from your head today?”
He answers, “Yes, I know it. Hold your peace.”
Elijah says to him, “Please wait here, for YHWH has sent me to the Jordan.”

He says, “As YHWH lives, and as your soul lives, I will not leave you.” Then they both go on. Fifty men of the sons of the prophets go, and stand opposite them at a distance; and they both stand by the Jordan. Elijah takes his mantle, and rolls it up, and strikes the waters, and they are divided here and there, so that they both go over on dry ground. When they have gone over, Elijah says to Elisha, “Ask what I will do for you, before I am taken from you.”
Elisha says, “Please let a double portion of your spirit be on me.”
He says, “You have asked a hard thing. If you see me when I am taken from you, it will be so for you; but if not, it will not be so.”

As they continue on and talk, look, a chariot of fire and horses of fire separate them, and Elijah goes up by a whirlwind into heaven. Elisha sees it, and he cries, “My father, my father, the chariots of Israel and its horsemen!”
He sees him no more. Then he takes hold of his own clothes, and tears them in two pieces.
Elisha Takes Up the Mantle · 2:13–18

He also takes up Elijah’s mantle that falls from him, and goes back, and stands by the bank of the Jordan. He takes Elijah’s mantle that falls from him, and strikes the waters, and says, “Where is YHWH, the God of Elijah?” When he also has struck the waters, they are divided apart, and Elisha goes over. When the sons of the prophets who are at Jericho over against him see him, they say, “The spirit of Elijah rests on Elisha.” They come to meet him, and bow themselves to the ground before him. They say to him, “See now, there are with your servants fifty strong men. Please let them go and seek your master. Perhaps YHWH’s Spirit has taken him up, and put him on some mountain, or into some valley.”
He says, “Don’t send them.”
When they urge him until he is ashamed, he says, “Send them.”
Therefore they send fifty men; and they search for three days, but don’t find him. They come back to him, while he stays at Jericho; and he says to them, “Didn’t I tell you, ‘Don’t go?’”
The Healing of the Water and the Bears · 2:19–25
The men of the city say to Elisha, “Look, please, the situation of this city is pleasant, as my lord sees; but the water is bad, and the land is barren.”

He says, “Bring me a new jar, and put salt in it.” Then they bring it to him. He goes out to the spring of the waters, and throws salt into it, and says, “YHWH says, ‘I have healed these waters. There will not be from there any more death or barren wasteland.’” So the waters are healed to this day, according to Elisha’s word which he speaks.

He goes up from there to Bethel. As he is going up by the way, some youths come out of the city and mock him, and say to him, “Go up, you baldy! Go up, you baldy!” He looks behind him and sees them, and curses them in YHWH’s name. Then two female bears come out of the woods, and maul forty-two of those youths. He goes from there to Mount Carmel, and from there he returns to Samaria.
Jehoram of Israel · 3:1–3

Now Jehoram the son of Ahab begins to reign over Israel in Samaria in the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and reigns twelve years. He does that which is evil in YHWH’s sight, but not like his father, and like his mother, for he puts away the pillar of Baal that his father has made. Nevertheless he holds to the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, with which he makes Israel to sin. He doesn’t depart from them.
The Moab Campaign · 3:4–27

Now Mesha king of Moab is a sheep breeder; and he supplies the king of Israel with the wool of one hundred thousand lambs, and of one hundred thousand rams. But when Ahab is dead, the king of Moab rebels against the king of Israel. King Jehoram goes out of Samaria at that time, and musters all Israel. He goes and sends to Jehoshaphat the king of Judah, saying, “The king of Moab has rebelled against me. Will you go with me against Moab to battle?”
He says, “I will go up. I am as you are, my people as your people, my horses as your horses.” He says, “Which way should we go up?”

He answers, “The way of the wilderness of Edom.” So the king of Israel goes with the king of Judah and the king of Edom, and they march for seven days along a circuitous route. There is no water for the army or for the animals that follow them. The king of Israel says, “Alas! For YHWH has called these three kings together to deliver them into the hand of Moab.”
But Jehoshaphat says, “Isn’t there a prophet of YHWH here, that we may inquire of YHWH by him?”
One of the king of Israel’s servants answers, “Elisha the son of Shaphat, who poured water on the hands of Elijah, is here.”
Jehoshaphat says, “YHWH’s word is with him.” So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat and the king of Edom go down to him.
Elisha says to the king of Israel, “What have I to do with you? Go to the prophets of your father, and to the prophets of your mother.”

The king of Israel says to him, “No, for YHWH has called these three kings together to deliver them into the hand of Moab.” Elisha says, “As YHWH of hosts lives, before whom I stand, surely, were it not that I respect the presence of Jehoshaphat the king of Judah, I would not look toward you, nor see you. But now bring me a musician.” When the musician plays, YHWH’s hand comes on him. He says, “YHWH says, ‘Make this valley full of trenches.’ For YHWH says, ‘You will not see wind, neither will you see rain, yet that valley will be filled with water, and you will drink, both you and your livestock and your other animals. This is an easy thing in YHWH’s sight. He will also deliver the Moabites into your hand. You will strike every fortified city, and every choice city, and will fell every good tree, and stop all springs of water, and mar every good piece of land with stones.’”
In the morning, about the time of offering the sacrifice, look, water comes by the way of Edom, and the country is filled with water.

Now when all the Moabites hear that the kings have come up to fight against them, they gather themselves together, all who are able to put on armor, young and old, and stand on the border. They rise up early in the morning, and the sun shines on the water, and the Moabites see the water opposite them as red as blood. They say, “This is blood. The kings are surely destroyed, and they have struck each other. Now therefore, Moab, to the plunder!”

When they come to the camp of Israel, the Israelites rise up and strike the Moabites, so that they flee before them; and they go forward into the land attacking the Moabites. They beat down the cities; and on every good piece of land each man casts his stone, and fills it. They also stop all the springs of water, and fell all the good trees, until in Kir Hareseth all they leave are its stones; however the men armed with slings go around it, and attack it. When the king of Moab sees that the battle is too severe for him, he takes with him seven hundred men who draw a sword, to break through to the king of Edom; but they can not. Then he takes his oldest son who would have reigned in his place, and offers him for a burnt offering on the wall. There is great wrath against Israel; and they depart from him, and return to their own land.
The Widow's Oil · 4:1–7

Now a certain woman of the wives of the sons of the prophets cries out to Elisha, saying, “Your servant my husband is dead. You know that your servant feared YHWH. Now the creditor has come to take for himself my two children to be slaves.”
Elisha says to her, “What should I do for you? Tell me: what do you have in the house?”
She says, “Your servant has nothing in the house, except a pot of oil.”

Then he says, “Go, borrow empty containers from of all your neighbors. Don’t borrow just a few containers. Go in and shut the door on you and on your sons, and pour oil into all those containers; and set aside those which are full.”

So she goes from him, and shuts the door on herself and on her sons. They bring the containers to her, and she pours oil. When the containers are full, she says to her son, “Bring me another container.”
He says to her, “There isn’t another container.” Then the oil stops flowing.
Then she comes and tells the man of God. He says, “Go, sell the oil, and pay your debt; and you and your sons live on the rest.”
The Shunammite's Son · 4:8–37

One day Elisha goes to Shunem, where there is a prominent woman; and she persuades him to eat bread. So it is, that as often as he passes by, he turns in there to eat bread. She says to her husband, “See now, I perceive that this is a holy man of God who passes by us continually. Please let us make a little room on the roof. Let us set for him there a bed, a table, a chair, and a lamp stand. When he comes to us, he can stay there.”

One day he comes there, and he goes to the room and lies there. He says to Gehazi his servant, “Call this Shunammite.” When he has called her, she stands before him. He says to him, “Say now to her, ‘Look, you have cared for us with all this care. What is to be done for you? Would you like to be spoken for to the king, or to the captain of the army?’”
She answers, “I dwell among my own people.”
He says, “What then is to be done for her?”
Gehazi answers, “Most certainly she has no son, and her husband is old.”
He says, “Call her.” When he has called her, she stands in the door. He says, “At this season, when the time comes around, you will embrace a son.”
She says, “No, my lord, you man of God, do not lie to your servant.”

The woman conceives, and bears a son at that season, when the time comes around, as Elisha has said to her. When the child is grown, one day he goes out to his father to the reapers. He says to his father, “My head! My head!”
He says to his servant, “Carry him to his mother.”

When he has taken him, and brings him to his mother, he sits on her knees until noon, and then dies. She goes up and lays him on the man of God’s bed, and shuts the door on him, and goes out. She calls to her husband, and says, “Please send me one of the servants, and one of the donkeys, that I may run to the man of God, and come again.”
He says, “Why would you want go to him today? It is not a new moon or a Sabbath.”
She says, “It’s alright.”
Then she saddles a donkey, and says to her servant, “Drive, and go forward! Don’t slow down for me, unless I ask you to.”

So she goes, and comes to the man of God to Mount Carmel. When the man of God sees her afar off, he says to Gehazi his servant, “Look, there is the Shunammite. Please run now to meet her, and ask her, ‘Is it well with you? Is it well with your husband? Is it well with your child?’”
She answers, “It is well.”

When she comes to the man of God to the hill, she catches hold of his feet. Gehazi comes near to thrust her away; but the man of God says, “Leave her alone; for her soul is troubled within her; and YHWH has hidden it from me, and has not told me.”
Then she says, “Did I ask you for a son, my lord? Didn’t I say, ‘Do not deceive me’?”

Then he says to Gehazi, “Tuck your cloak into your belt, take my staff in your hand, and go your way. If you meet any man, don’t greet him; and if anyone greets you, don’t answer him again. Then lay my staff on the child’s face.”
The child’s mother says, “As YHWH lives, and as your soul lives, I will not leave you.”
So he arises, and follows her.
Gehazi goes ahead of them, and lays the staff on the child’s face; but there is no voice and no hearing. Therefore he returns to meet him, and tells him, “The child has not awakened.”

When Elisha has come into the house, look, the child is dead, and lying on his bed. He goes in therefore, and shuts the door on them both, and prays to YHWH. He goes up, and lies on the child, and put his mouth on his mouth, and his eyes on his eyes, and his hands on his hands. He stretches himself on him; and the child’s flesh grows warm. Then he returns, and walks in the house once back and forth; and goes up, and stretches himself out on him. Then the child sneezes seven times, and the child opens his eyes. He calls Gehazi, and says, “Call this Shunammite!” So he calls her.
When she has come in to him, he says, “Take up your son.”
Then she goes in, falls at his feet, and bows herself to the ground; then she picks up her son, and goes out.
Elisha at Gilgal and Dothan · 4:38–44

Elisha comes again to Gilgal. There is a famine in the land; and the sons of the prophets are sitting before him; and he says to his servant, “Get the large pot, and boil stew for the sons of the prophets.”

One goes out into the field to gather herbs, and finds a wild vine, and gathers a lap full of wild gourds from it, and comes and cuts them up into the pot of stew; for they don’t recognize them. So they pour out for the men to eat. As they are eating some of the stew, they cry out, and say, “Man of God, there is death in the pot!” And they can not eat it.
But he says, “Then bring meal.” He throws it into the pot; and he says, “Serve it to the people, that they may eat.” And there is nothing harmful in the pot.

A man from Baal Shalishah comes, and brings the man of God some bread of the first fruits: twenty loaves of barley and fresh ears of grain in his sack. He says, “Give to the people, that they may eat.”
His servant says, “What, should I set this before a hundred men?”
But he says, “Give the people, that they may eat; for YHWH says, ‘They will eat, and will have some left over.’”
So he sets it before them, and they eat, and have some left over, according to YHWH’s word.
Naaman the Syrian · 5:1–14

Now Naaman, captain of the army of the king of Syria, is a great man with his master, and honorable, because by him YHWH has given victory to Syria: he is also a mighty man of valor, but he is a leper. The Syrians have gone out in bands, and have brought away captive out of the land of Israel a little maiden; and she waits on Naaman’s wife. She says to her mistress, “I wish that my lord were with the prophet who is in Samaria! Then he would heal him of his leprosy.”
Someone goes in, and tells his lord, saying, “The maiden who is from the land of Israel said this.”
The king of Syria says, “Go now, and I will send a letter to the king of Israel.”

He departs, and takes with him ten talents of silver, and six thousand pieces of gold, and ten changes of clothing. He brings the letter to the king of Israel, saying, “Now when this letter has come to you, look, I have sent Naaman my servant to you, that you may heal him of his leprosy.”

When the king of Israel has read the letter, he tears his clothes, and says, “Am I God, to kill and to make alive, that this man sends to me to heal a man of his leprosy? But please consider and see how he seeks a quarrel against me.”

It is so, when Elisha the man of God hears that the king of Israel has torn his clothes, that he sends to the king, saying, “Why have you torn your clothes? Let him come now to me, and he will know that there is a prophet in Israel.”

So Naaman comes with his horses and with his chariots, and stands at the door of the house of Elisha. Elisha sends a messenger to him, saying, “Go and wash in the Jordan seven times, and your flesh will come again to you, and you will be clean.”

But Naaman is angry, and goes away, and says, “Look, I thought, ‘He will surely come out to me, and stand, and call on the name of YHWH his God, and wave his hand over the place, and heal the leper.’ Aren’t Abanah and Pharpar, the rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel? Couldn’t I wash in them, and be clean?” So he turns and goes away in a rage.

His servants come near, and speak to him, and say, “My father, if the prophet had asked you do some great thing, wouldn’t you have done it? How much rather then, when he says to you, ‘Wash, and be clean?’”
Then goes he down, and dips himself seven times in the Jordan, according to the saying of the man of God; and his flesh is restored like the flesh of a little child, and he is clean.
Naaman's Confession and Gehazi's Greed · 5:15–27

He returns to the man of God, he and all his company, and comes, and stands before him; and he says, “See now, I know that there is no God in all the earth, but in Israel. Now therefore, please take a gift from your servant.”
But he says, “As YHWH lives, before whom I stand, I will receive none.”

He urges him to take it; but he refuses. Naaman says, “If not, then, please let two mules’ burden of earth be given to your servant; for your servant will from now on offer neither burnt offering nor sacrifice to other gods, but to YHWH. In this thing may YHWH pardon your servant: when my master goes into the house of Rimmon to worship there, and he leans on my hand, and I bow myself in the house of Rimmon. When I bow myself in the house of Rimmon, may YHWH pardon your servant in this thing.”
He says to him, “Go in peace.”

So he departs from him a little way. But Gehazi the servant of Elisha the man of God, says, “Look, my master has spared this Naaman the Syrian, in not receiving at his hands that which he brought. As YHWH lives, I will run after him, and take something from him.”
So Gehazi follows after Naaman. When Naaman sees one running after him, he comes down from the chariot to meet him, and says, “Is all well?”

He says, “All is well. My master has sent me, saying, ‘Look, even now two young men of the sons of the prophets have come to me from the hill country of Ephraim. Please give them a talent of silver and two changes of clothing.’”

Naaman says, “Be pleased to take two talents.” He urges him, and binds two talents of silver in two bags, with two changes of clothing, and lays them on two of his servants; and they carry them before him. When he comes to the hill, he takes them from their hand, and stores them in the house. Then he lets the men go, and they depart. But he goes in, and stands before his master. Elisha says to him, “Where did you come from, Gehazi?”
He says, “Your servant went nowhere.”

He says to him, “Didn’t my heart go with you, when the man turned from his chariot to meet you? Is it a time to receive money, and to receive garments, and olive groves and vineyards, and sheep and cattle, and male servants and female servants? Therefore the leprosy of Naaman will cling to you and to your offspring forever.”
He goes out from his presence a leper, as white as snow.
The Floating Axehead · 6:1–7

The sons of the prophets say to Elisha, “See now, the place where we live and meet with you is too small for us. Please let us go to the Jordan, and each man take a beam from there, and let us make us a place there, where we may live.”
He answers, “Go!”
One says, “Please be pleased to go with your servants.”

He answers, “I will go.” So he goes with them. When they come to the Jordan, they cut down wood. But as one is cutting down a tree, the ax head falls into the water. Then he cries, and says, “Alas, my master! For it was borrowed.”
The man of God asks, “Where did it fall?” He shows him the place. He cuts down a stick, throws it in there, and makes the iron float. He says, “Take it.” So he puts out his hand and takes it.
Elisha and the Syrian Army · 6:8–23
Now the king of Syria is at war against Israel; and he takes counsel with his servants, saying, “My camp will be in such and such a place.”

The man of God sends to the king of Israel, saying, “Beware that you not pass this place; for the Syrians are coming down there.” The king of Israel sends to the place which the man of God tells him and warns him of; and he saves himself there, not once or twice. The king of Syria’s heart is very troubled about this. He calls his servants, and says to them, “Won’t you show me which of us is for the king of Israel?”
One of his servants says, “No, my lord, O king; but Elisha, the prophet who is in Israel, tells the king of Israel the words that you speak in your bedroom.”
He says, “Go and see where he is, that I may send and get him.”
He is told, “Look, he is in Dothan.”

Therefore he sends horses, chariots, and a great army there. They come by night, and surround the city. When the servant of the man of God has risen early, and gone out, look, an army with horses and chariots is around the city. His servant says to him, “Alas, my master! What should we do?”

He answers, “Don’t be afraid; for those who are with us are more than those who are with them.” Elisha prays, and says, “YHWH, please open his eyes, that he may see.” YHWH opens the young man’s eyes; and he sees: and look, the mountain is full of horses and chariots of fire around Elisha. When they come down to him, Elisha prays to YHWH, and says, “Please strike this people with blindness.”

He strikes them with blindness according to Elishah’s word. Elisha says to them, “This is not the way, neither is this the city. Follow me, and I will bring you to the man whom you seek.” He leads them to Samaria. When they have come into Samaria, Elisha says, “YHWH, open these men’s eyes, that they may see.”
YHWH opens their eyes, and they see; and look, they are in the middle of Samaria. The king of Israel says to Elisha, when he sees them, “My father, should I strike them? Should I strike them?”

He answers, “You will not strike them. Would you strike those whom you have taken captive with your sword and with your bow? Set bread and water before them, that they may eat and drink, and go to their master.”
He prepares a great feast for them. When they have eaten and drunk, he sends them away, and they go to their master. So the bands of Syria stop raiding the land of Israel.
The Siege of Samaria · 6:24–33

After this, Benhadad king of Syria gathers all his army, and goes up and besieges Samaria. There is a great famine in Samaria. Look, they besiege it, until a donkey’s head is sold for eighty pieces of silver, and the fourth part of a kab of dove’s dung for five pieces of silver. As the king of Israel is passing by on the wall, a woman cries to him, saying, “Help, my lord, O king!”
He says, “If YHWH doesn’t help you, where could I get help for you? From of the threshing floor, or from the wine press?” The king says to her, “What is your problem?”

She answers, “This woman said to me, ‘Give your son, that we may eat him today, and we will eat my son tomorrow.’ So we boiled my son, and ate him: and I said to her on the next day, ‘Give your son, that we may eat him;’ and she has hidden her son.”

When the king hears the words of the woman, he tears his clothes. Now he is passing by on the wall, and the people look, and look, he has sackcloth underneath on his body. Then he says, “God do so to me, and more also, if the head of Elisha the son of Shaphat stays on him today.”

But Elisha is sitting in his house, and the elders are sitting with him. Then the king sends a man from before him; but before the messenger comes to him, he says to the elders, “Do you see how this son of a murderer has sent to take away my head? Look, when the messenger comes, shut the door, and hold the door shut against him. Isn’t the sound of his master’s feet behind him?”
While he is still talking with them, look, the messenger comes down to him. Then he says, “Look, this evil is from YHWH. Why should I wait for YHWH any longer?”
The Siege Broken by the Word · 7:1–20
Elisha says, “Hear YHWH’s word. YHWH says, ‘Tomorrow about this time a seah of fine flour will be sold for a shekel, and two seahs of barley for a shekel, in the gate of Samaria.’”
Then the captain on whose hand the king leans answers the man of God, and says, “Look, if YHWH made windows in heaven, could this thing be?”
He says, “Look, you will see it with your eyes, but will not eat of it.”

Now there are four leprous men at the entrance of the gate. They say to one another, “Why do we sit here until we die? If we say, ‘We will enter into the city,’ then the famine is in the city, and we will die there. If we sit still here, we also die. Now therefore come, and let us surrender to the army of the Syrians. If they save us alive, we will live; and if they kill us, we will only die.”

They rise up in the twilight, to go to the camp of the Syrians. When they have come to the outermost part of the camp of the Syrians, look, no man is there. For the Lord has made the army of the Syrians to hear the sound of chariots, and the sound of horses, even the noise of a great army; and they say to one another, “Look, the king of Israel has hired against us the kings of the Hittites and the kings of the Egyptians to attack us.” Therefore they arise and flee in the twilight, and leave their tents, and their horses, and their donkeys, even the camp as it is, and flee for their life. When these lepers come to the outermost part of the camp, they go into one tent, and eat and drink, and carry away silver, gold, and clothing, and go and hide it. Then they come back, and enter into another tent, and carry things from there also, and go and hide them. Then they say to one another, “We aren’t doing right. Today is a day of good news, and we keep silent. If we wait until the morning light, punishment will overtake us. Now therefore come, let’s go and tell the king’s household.”

So they come and call to the city gatekeepers; and they tell them, “We came to the camp of the Syrians, and, look, there was no man there, not even a man’s voice, but the horses tied, and the donkeys tied, and the tents as they were.”

He calls the gatekeepers; and they tell it to the king’s household within. The king arises in the night, and says to his servants, “I will now show you what the Syrians have done to us. They know that we are hungry. Therefore are they gone out of the camp to hide themselves in the field, saying, ‘When they come out of the city, we will take them alive, and get into the city.’”

One of his servants answers, “Please let some people take five of the horses that remain, which are left in the city. Look, they are like all the multitude of Israel who are left in it. Look, they are like all the multitude of Israel who are consumed. Let us send and see.”
Therefore they take two chariots with horses; and the king sends them out to the Syrian army, saying, “Go and see.”

They go after them to the Jordan; and look, all the path is full of garments and equipment which the Syrians have cast away in their haste. The messengers return, and tell the king. The people go out and plunder the camp of the Syrians. So a seah of fine flour is sold for a shekel, and two measures of barley for a shekel, according to YHWH’s word. The king appoints the captain on whose hand he leans to be in charge of the gate; and the people trample over him in the gate, and he dies as the man of God has said, who speaks when the king comes down to him. It happens as the man of God has spoken to the king, saying, “Two seahs of barley for a shekel, and a seah of fine flour for a shekel, will be tomorrow about this time in the gate of Samaria”; and that captain answers the man of God, and says, “Now, look, if YHWH made windows in heaven, might such a thing be?” and he says, “Look, you will see it with your eyes, but will not eat of it.” It happens like that to him; for the people trampled over him in the gate, and he dies.
The Shunammite's Land Restored · 8:1–6

Now Elisha has spoken to the woman whose son he has restored to life, saying, “Arise, and go, you and your household, and stay for a while wherever you can; for YHWH has called for a famine. It will also come on the land for seven years.”

The woman arises, and does according to the man of God’s word. She goes with her household, and lives in the land of the Philistines for seven years. At the end of seven years, the woman returns from the land of the Philistines. Then she goes out to beg the king for her house and for her land. Now the king is talking with Gehazi the servant of the man of God, saying, “Please tell me all the great things that Elisha has done.” As he is telling the king how he has restored to life him who is dead, look, the woman, whose son he has restored to life, begs the king for her house and for her land. Gehazi says, “My lord, O king, this is the woman, and this is her son, whom Elisha restored to life.”

When the king asks the woman, she tells him. So the king appoints to her a certain officer, saying, “Restore all that was hers, and all the fruits of the field since the day that she left the land, even until now.”
Elisha and Hazael · 8:7–15
Elisha comes to Damascus; and Benhadad the king of Syria is sick. He is told, “The man of God has come here.”
The king says to Hazael, “Take a present in your hand, and go, meet the man of God, and inquire of YHWH by him, saying, ‘Will I recover from this sickness?’”

So Hazael goes to meet him, and takes a present with him, even of every good thing of Damascus, forty camels’ burden, and comes and stands before him, and says, “Your son Benhadad king of Syria has sent me to you, saying, ‘Will I recover from this sickness?’”

Elisha says to him, “Go, tell him, ‘You will surely recover;’ however YHWH has shown me that he will surely die.” He settles his gaze steadfastly on him, until he is ashamed. Then the man of God weeps.
Hazael says, “Why do you weep, my lord?”

He answers, “Because I know the evil that you will do to the children of Israel. You will set their strongholds on fire, and you will kill their young men with the sword, and will dash their little ones in pieces, and rip up their pregnant women.”
Hazael says, “But what is your servant, who is but a dog, that he could do this great thing?”
Elisha answers, “YHWH has shown me that you will be king over Syria.”
Then he departs from Elisha, and comes to his master, who says to him, “What did Elisha say to you?”
He answers, “He told me that you would surely recover.”
On the next day, he takes a thick cloth, dips it in water, and spreads it on his face, so that he dies. Then Hazael reigns in his place.
Jehoram and Ahaziah of Judah · 8:16–29

In the fifth year of Joram the son of Ahab king of Israel, Jehoshaphat being king of Judah then, Jehoram the son of Jehoshaphat king of Judah begins to reign. He is thirty-two years old when he begins to reign. He reigns eight years in Jerusalem. He walks in the way of the kings of Israel, as does Ahab’s house; for he marries Ahab’s daughter. He does that which is evil in YHWH’s sight. However YHWH would not destroy Judah, for David his servant’s sake, as he promises him to give to him a lamp for his children always.

In his days Edom revolts from under the hand of Judah, and makes a king over themselves. Then Joram passes over to Zair, and all his chariots with him: and he rises up by night, and strikes the Edomites who surround him, and the captains of the chariots; and the people flee to their tents. So Edom revolts from under the hand of Judah to this day. Then Libnah revolts at the same time. The rest of the acts of Joram, and all that he does, aren’t they write in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah? Joram sleeps with his fathers, and is buried with his fathers in David’s city; and Ahaziah his son reigns in his place. In the twelfth year of Joram the son of Ahab king of Israel, Ahaziah the son of Jehoram king of Judah begins to reign. Ahaziah is twenty-two years old when he begins to reign; and he reigns one year in Jerusalem. His mother’s name is Athaliah the daughter of Omri king of Israel. He walks in the way of Ahab’s house, and does that which is evil in YHWH’s sight, as does Ahab’s house; for he is the son-in-law of Ahab’s house. He goes with Joram the son of Ahab to war against Hazael king of Syria at Ramoth Gilead, and the Syrians wound Joram. King Joram returns to be healed in Jezreel from the wounds which the Syrians have given him at Ramah, when he fights against Hazael king of Syria. Ahaziah the son of Jehoram king of Judah goes down to see Joram the son of Ahab in Jezreel, because he is sick.
Jehu Anointed King · 9:1–13

Elisha the prophet calls one of the sons of the prophets, and says to him, “Put your belt on your waist, take this vial of oil in your hand, and go to Ramoth Gilead. When you come there, find Jehu the son of Jehoshaphat the son of Nimshi, and go in, and make him rise up from among his brothers, and take him to an inner room. Then take the vial of oil, and pour it on his head, and say, ‘YHWH says, “I have anointed you king over Israel.”’ Then open the door, flee, and don’t wait.”
So the young man, even the young man, the prophet, goes to Ramoth Gilead. When he comes, look, the captains of the army are sitting. Then he says, “I have a message for you, captain.”
Jehu says, “To which of us all?”

He says, “To you, O captain.” He arises, and goes into the house. Then he pours the oil on his head, and says to him, “YHWH, the God of Israel, says, ‘I have anointed you king over the people of YHWH, even over Israel. You must strike your master Ahab’s house, that I may avenge the blood of my servants the prophets, and the blood of all the servants of YHWH, at the hand of Jezebel. For the whole house of Ahab will perish. I will cut off from Ahab everyone who urinates against a wall, both him who is shut up and him who is left at large in Israel. I will make Ahab’s house like the house of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, and like the house of Baasha the son of Ahijah. The dogs will eat Jezebel on the plot of ground of Jezreel, and there will be no one to bury her.’” Then he opens the door and flees.
When Jehu comes out to the servants of his lord, and one says to him, “Is all well? Why did this mad fellow come to you?”
He says to them, “You know the man and how he talks.” They say, “That is a lie. Tell us now.”
He says, “He said to me, ‘YHWH says, I have anointed you king over Israel.’”
Then they hurry, and each man takes his cloak, and puts it under him on the top of the stairs, and blows the trumpet, saying, “Jehu is king.”
Jehu Kills Joram and Ahaziah · 9:14–29

So Jehu the son of Jehoshaphat the son of Nimshi conspires against Joram. (Now Joram is keeping Ramoth Gilead, he and all Israel, because of Hazael king of Syria; but king Joram has returned to be healed in Jezreel of the wounds which the Syrians have given him, when he fights with Hazael king of Syria.) Jehu says, “If this is your thinking, then let no one escape and go out of the city, to go to tell it in Jezreel.” So Jehu rides in a chariot and goes to Jezreel, for Joram lies there. Ahaziah king of Judah has come down to see Joram. Now the watchman is standing on the tower in Jezreel, and he spies the company of Jehu as he comes, and says, “I see a company.”
Joram says, “Take a horseman, and send to meet them, and let him say, ‘Is it peace?’”
So one goes on horseback to meet him, and says, “Thus says the king, ‘Is it peace?’”
Jehu says, “What do you have to do with peace? Fall in behind me!”
The watchman says, “The messenger came to them, but he isn’t coming back.”
Then he sends out a second on horseback, who comes to them, and says, “Thus says the king, ‘Is it peace?’”
Jehu answers, “What do you have to do with peace? Fall in behind me!”
The watchman says, “He came to them, and isn’t coming back. The driving is like the driving of Jehu the son of Nimshi, for he drives furiously.”
Joram says, “Get ready!”

They get his chariot ready. Then Joram king of Israel and Ahaziah king of Judah goes out, each in his chariot, and they go out to meet Jehu, and find him on Naboth the Jezreelite’s land. When Joram sees Jehu, he says, “Is it peace, Jehu?”
He answers, “What peace, so long as the prostitution of your mother Jezebel and her witchcraft abound?”
Joram turns his hands, and flees, and says to Ahaziah, “This is treason, Ahaziah!”

Jehu draws his bow with his full strength, and strikes Joram between his arms; and the arrow goes out at his heart, and he sinks down in his chariot. Then Jehu says to Bidkar his captain, “Pick him up, and throw him in the plot of the field of Naboth the Jezreelite; for remember how, when you and I rode together after Ahab his father, YHWH laid this burden on him: ‘Surely I have seen yesterday the blood of Naboth, and the blood of his sons,’ says YHWH; ‘and I will repay you in this plot of ground,’ says YHWH. Now therefore take and cast him onto the plot of ground, according to YHWH’s word.”

But when Ahaziah the king of Judah sees this, he flees by the way of the garden house. Jehu follows after him, and says, “Strike him also in the chariot!” They strike him at the ascent of Gur, which is by Ibleam. He flees to Megiddo, and dies there. His servants carry him in a chariot to Jerusalem, and bury him in his tomb with his fathers in David’s city. In the eleventh year of Joram the son of Ahab, Ahaziah begins to reign over Judah.
The Death of Jezebel · 9:30–37

When Jehu has come to Jezreel, Jezebel hears of it; and she paints her eyes, and adorns her head, and looks out at the window. As Jehu enters in at the gate, she says, “Do you come in peace, Zimri, you murderer of your master?”
He lifts up his face to the window, and says, “Who is on my side? Who?”
Two or three eunuchs look out at him.
He says, “Throw her down!”

So they throw her down; and some of her blood is sprinkled on the wall, and on the horses. Then he tramples her under foot. When he has come in, he eats and drank. Then he says, “See now to this cursed woman, and bury her; for she is a king’s daughter.”
They go to bury her, but they find no more of her than the skull, the feet, and the palms of her hands. Therefore they come back, and tell him.

He says, “This is YHWH’s word, which he spoke by his servant Elijah the Tishbite, saying, ‘The dogs will eat the flesh of Jezebel on the plot of Jezreel, and the body of Jezebel will be as dung on the face of the field on Jezreel’s land, so that they won’t say, “This is Jezebel.”’”
Jehu Destroys the House of Ahab · 10:1–17

Now Ahab has seventy sons in Samaria. Jehu writes letters, and sends to Samaria, to the rulers of Jezreel, even the elders, and to those who bring up Ahab’s sons, saying, “Now as soon as this letter comes to you, since your master’s sons are with you, and you have chariots and horses, a fortified city also, and armor, Select the best and fittest of your master’s sons, set him on his father’s throne, and fight for your master’s house.”

But they are exceedingly afraid, and say, “Look, the two kings didn’t stand before him! How then should we stand?” He who is over the household, and he who is over the city, the elders also, and those who raise the children, sent to Jehu, saying, “We are your servants, and will do all that you ask us. We will not make any man king. You do that which is good in your eyes.”

Then he writes a letter the second time to them, saying, “If you are on my side, and if you will listen to my voice, take the heads of the men who are your master’s sons, and come to me to Jezreel by tomorrow this time.”

Now the king’s sons, being seventy persons, are with the great men of the city, who bring them up. When the letter comes to them, they take the king’s sons and kill them, even seventy people, and put their heads in baskets, and send them to him to Jezreel. A messenger comes and tells him, “They have brought the heads of the king’s sons.”

He says, “Lay them in two heaps at the entrance of the gate until the morning.” In the morning, he goes out, and stands, and says to all the people, “You are righteous. Look, I conspired against my master and killed him, but who killed all these? Know now that nothing will fall to the earth of YHWH’s word, which YHWH spoke concerning Ahab’s house. For YHWH has done that which he spoke by his servant Elijah.”
So Jehu strikes all that remain of Ahab’s house in Jezreel, with all his great men, his familiar friends, and his priests, until he leaves him no one remaining.
He arises and departs, and goes to Samaria. As he is at the shearing house of the shepherds on the way, Jehu meets with the brothers of Ahaziah king of Judah, and says, “Who are you?”
They answer, “We are the brothers of Ahaziah. We are going down to greet the children of the king and the children of the queen.”
He says, “Take them alive!”
They take them alive, and kill them at the pit of the shearing house, even forty-two men. He doesn’t leave any of them.
When he has departed from there, he meets Jehonadab the son of Rechab coming to meet him. He greets him, and says to him, “Is your heart right, as my heart is with your heart?”
Jehonadab answers, “It is.”

“If it is, give me your hand.” He gives him his hand; and he takes him up to him into the chariot. He says, “Come with me, and see my zeal for YHWH.” So they make him ride in his chariot. When he comes to Samaria, he strikes all who remain to Ahab in Samaria, until he has destroyed him, according to YHWH’s word, which he speaks to Elijah.
The End of Baal Worship · 10:18–28

Jehu gathers all the people together, and says to them, “Ahab served Baal a little; but Jehu will serve him much. Now therefore call to me all the prophets of Baal, all of his worshipers, and all of his priests. Let no one be absent; for I have a great sacrifice to Baal. Whoever is absent, he will not live.” But Jehu does deceptively, intending to destroy the worshipers of Baal.
Jehu says, “Sanctify a solemn assembly for Baal!”

So they proclaim it. Jehu sends through all Israel; and all the worshipers of Baal come, so that there is not a man left that doesn’t come. They come into the house of Baal; and the house of Baal is filled from one end to another. He says to him who keeps the wardrobe, “Bring out robes for all the worshipers of Baal!”

So he brings robes out to them. Jehu goes with Jehonadab the son of Rechab into the house of Baal. Then he says to the worshipers of Baal, “Search, and see that none of the servants of YHWH are here with you, but only the worshipers of Baal.”

So they go in to offer sacrifices and burnt offerings. Now Jehu has appointed for himself eighty men outside, and says, “If any of the men whom I bring into your hands escape, he who lets him go, his life will be for the life of him.”

As soon as he has finished offering the burnt offering, Jehu says to the guard and to the captains, “Go in and kill them! Let no one escape.” So they strike them with the edge of the sword. The guard and the captains throw the bodies out, and go to the inner shrine of the house of Baal. They bring out the pillars that are in the house of Baal, and burn them. They break down the pillar of Baal, and break down the house of Baal, and make it a latrine, to this day. Thus Jehu destroys Baal out of Israel.
Jehu's Verdict and Legacy · 10:29–36

However, Jehu doesn’t depart from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, with which he makes Israel to sin, the golden calves that are in Bethel and that are in Dan. YHWH says to Jehu, “Because you have done well in executing that which is right in my eyes, and have done to Ahab’s house according to all that was in my heart, your descendants will sit on the throne of Israel to the fourth generation.”

But Jehu takes no heed to walk in the law of YHWH, the God of Israel, with all his heart. He doesn’t depart from the sins of Jeroboam, with which he makes Israel to sin. In those days YHWH begins to cut away parts of Israel; and Hazael strikes them in all the borders of Israel; from the Jordan eastward, all the land of Gilead, the Gadites, and the Reubenites, and the Manassites, from Aroer, which is by the valley of the Arnon, even Gilead and Bashan. Now the rest of the acts of Jehu, and all that he does, and all his might, aren’t they write in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel? Jehu sleeps with his fathers; and they bury him in Samaria. Jehoahaz his son reigns in his place. The time that Jehu reigns over Israel in Samaria is twenty-eight years.
Athaliah Seizes the Throne · 11:1–3

Now when Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah sees that her son is dead, she arises and destroys all the royal offspring. But Jehosheba, the daughter of king Joram, sister of Ahaziah, takes Joash the son of Ahaziah, and steals him away from among the king’s sons who are slain, even him and his nurse, and puts them in the bedroom; and they hide him from Athaliah, so that he is not slain. He is with her hidden in YHWH’s house six years while Athaliah reigns over the land.
The Coup of Jehoiada · 11:4–21

In the seventh year Jehoiada sends and fetches the captains over hundreds of the Carites and of the guard, and brings them to him into YHWH’s house; and he makes a covenant with them, and makes a covenant with them in YHWH’s house, and shows them the king’s son. He commands them, saying, “This is what you must do: a third of you, who come in on the Sabbath, will be keepers of the watch of the king’s house; a third of you will be at the gate Sur; and a third of you at the gate behind the guard. So you will keep the watch of the house, and be a barrier. The two companies of you, even all who go out on the Sabbath, will keep the watch of YHWH’s house around the king. You will surround the king, every man with his weapons in his hand; and he who comes within the ranks, let him be slain. Be with the king when he goes out, and when he comes in.”

The captains over hundreds do according to all that Jehoiada the priest commands; and they each take his men, those who are to come in on the Sabbath, with those who are to go out on the Sabbath, and come to Jehoiada the priest. The priest delivers to the captains over hundreds the spears and shields that have been king David’s, which are in YHWH’s house. The guard stands, every man with his weapons in his hand, from the right side of the house to the left side of the house, along by the altar and the house, around the king. Then he brings out the king’s son, and puts the crown on him, and gives him the covenant; and they make him king, and anoint him; and they clap their hands, and say, “Long live the king!”

When Athaliah hears the noise of the guard and of the people, she comes to the people into YHWH’s house: and she looks, and look, the king stands by the pillar, as the tradition is, with the captains and the trumpets by the king; and all the people of the land rejoice, and blow trumpets. Then Athaliah tears her clothes, and cries, “Treason! Treason!”

Jehoiada the priest commands the captains of hundreds who are set over the army, and says to them, “Bring her out between the ranks. Kill anyone who follows her with the sword.” For the priest says, “Don’t let her be slain in YHWH’s house.” So they make way for her; and she goes by the way of the horses’ entry to the king’s house, and she is slain there. Jehoiada makes a covenant between YHWH and the king and the people, that they should be YHWH’s people; also between the king and the people. All the people of the land go to the house of Baal, and break it down; his altars and his images break they in pieces thoroughly, and kill Mattan the priest of Baal before the altars. The priest appoints officers over YHWH’s house. He takes the captains over hundreds, and the Carites, and the guard, and all the people of the land; and they bring down the king from YHWH’s house, and come by the way of the gate of the guard to the king’s house. He sits on the throne of the kings. So all the people of the land rejoice, and the city is quiet. They have slain Athaliah with the sword at the king’s house.
Jehoash is seven years old when he begins to reign.
Joash Repairs the Temple · 12:1–21

Jehoash begins to reign in the seventh year of Jehu, and he reigns forty years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name is Zibiah of Beersheba. Jehoash does that which is right in YHWH’s eyes all his days in which Jehoiada the priest instructs him. However the high places are not taken away. The people still sacrifice and burn incense in the high places. Jehoash says to the priests, “All the money of the holy things that is brought into YHWH’s house, in current money, the money of the people for whom each man is evaluated, and all the money that it comes into any man’s heart to bring into YHWH’s house, let the priests take it to them, each man from his donor; and they will repair the damage to the house, wherever any damage is found.”

But it is so, that in the twenty-third year of king Jehoash the priests has not repaired the damage to the house. Then king Jehoash calls for Jehoiada the priest, and for the other priests, and says to them, “Why don’t you repair the damage to the house? Now therefore take no more money from your treasurers, but deliver it for repair of the damage to the house.”

The priests consent that they should take no more money from the people, and not repair the damage to the house. But Jehoiada the priest takes a chest, and bores a hole in its lid, and sets it beside the altar, on the right side as one comes into YHWH’s house; and the priests who keep the threshold put all the money that is brought into YHWH’s house into it. When they see that there is much money in the chest, the king’s scribe and the high priest come up, and they put it in bags and count the money that is found in YHWH’s house. They give the money that is weighed out into the hands of those who do the work, who has the oversight of YHWH’s house; and they pay it out to the carpenters and the builders, who work on YHWH’s house, and to the masons and the stone cutters, and for buying timber and cut stone to repair the damage to YHWH’s house, and for all that are laid out for the house to repair it. But there are not made for YHWH’s house cups of silver, snuffers, basins, trumpets, any vessels of gold, or vessels of silver, of the money that is brought into YHWH’s house; for they give that to those who do the work, and repaired YHWH’s house with it. Moreover they don’t demand an accounting from the men into whose hand they deliver the money to give to those who do the work; for they deal faithfully. The money for the trespass offerings, and the money for the sin offerings is not brought into YHWH’s house. It is the priests’.

Then Hazael king of Syria goes up, and fights against Gath, and takes it; and Hazael sets his face to go up to Jerusalem. Jehoash king of Judah takes all the holy things that Jehoshaphat and Jehoram and Ahaziah, his fathers, kings of Judah, have dedicated, and his own holy things, and all the gold that is found in the treasures of YHWH’s house, and of the king’s house, and sends it to Hazael king of Syria; and he goes away from Jerusalem. Now the rest of the acts of Joash, and all that he does, aren’t they write in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah? His servants arise, and make a conspiracy, and strike Joash at the house of Millo, on the way that goes down to Silla. For Jozacar the son of Shimeath, and Jehozabad the son of Shomer, his servants, strikes him, and he dies; and they bury him with his fathers in David’s city; and Amaziah his son reigns in his place.
Jehoahaz of Israel · 13:1–9

In the twenty-third year of Joash the son of Ahaziah, king of Judah, Jehoahaz the son of Jehu begins to reign over Israel in Samaria for seventeen years. He does that which is evil in YHWH’s sight, and follows the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, with which he makes Israel to sin. He doesn’t depart from it. YHWH’s anger burns against Israel, and he delivers them into the hand of Hazael king of Syria, and into the hand of Benhadad the son of Hazael, continually. Jehoahaz begs YHWH, and YHWH listens to him; for he sees the oppression of Israel, how the king of Syria oppresses them. (YHWH gives Israel a savior, so that they go out from under the hand of the Syrians; and the children of Israel live in their tents as before. Nevertheless they don’t depart from the sins of the house of Jeroboam, with which he makes Israel to sin, but walk in them; and the Asherah also remains in Samaria.) For he doesn’t leave to Jehoahaz of the people any more than fifty horsemen, and ten chariots, and ten thousand footmen; for the king of Syria destroys them, and makes them like the dust in threshing. Now the rest of the acts of Jehoahaz, and all that he does, and his might, aren’t they write in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel? Jehoahaz sleeps with his fathers; and they bury him in Samaria; and Joash his son reigns in his place.
Joash of Israel and Elisha's Death · 13:10–21

In the thirty-seventh year of Joash king of Judah, Jehoash the son of Jehoahaz begins to reign over Israel in Samaria for sixteen years. He does that which is evil in YHWH’s sight. He doesn’t depart from all the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, with which he makes Israel to sin; but he walks in them. Now the rest of the acts of Joash, and all that he does, and his might with which he fights against Amaziah king of Judah, aren’t they write in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel? Joash sleeps with his fathers; and Jeroboam sits on his throne. Joash is buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel.

Now Elisha becomes sick with the illness of which he dies; and Joash the king of Israel comes down to him, and weeps over him, and says, “My father, my father, the chariots of Israel and its horsemen!”

Elisha says to him, “Take bow and arrows”; and he takes bow and arrows for himself. He says to the king of Israel, “Put your hand on the bow”; and he puts his hand on it. Elisha lays his hands on the king’s hands. He says, “Open the window eastward”; and he opens it. Then Elisha says, “Shoot!” and he shoots. He says, “YHWH’s arrow of victory, even the arrow of victory over Syria; for you will strike the Syrians in Aphek, until you have consumed them.”

He says, “Take the arrows”; and he takes them. He says to the king of Israel, “Strike the ground”; and he strikes three times, and stops. The man of God is angry with him, and says, “You should have struck five or six times. Then you would have struck Syria until you had consumed it; whereas now you will strike Syria just three times.”
Elisha dies, and they bury him.

Now the bands of the Moabites invade the land at the coming in of the year. As they are burying a man, look, they see a band of raiders; and they throw the man into Elisha’s tomb. As soon as the man touches Elisha’s bones, he revives, and stands up on his feet.
Israel Recovered · 13:22–25

Hazael king of Syria oppresses Israel all the days of Jehoahaz. But YHWH is gracious to them, and has compassion on them, and has respect for them, because of his covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and would not destroy them, and he doesn’t cast them from his presence as yet.

Hazael king of Syria dies; and Benhadad his son reigns in his place. Jehoash the son of Jehoahaz takes again out of the hand of Benhadad the son of Hazael the cities which he has taken out of the hand of Jehoahaz his father by war. Joash strikes him three times, and recovers the cities of Israel.
Amaziah of Judah · 14:1–22

In the second year of Joash son of Joahaz king of Israel Amaziah the son of Joash king of Judah begins to reign. He is twenty-five years old when he begins to reign; and he reigns twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name is Jehoaddin of Jerusalem. He does that which is right in YHWH’s eyes, yet not like David his father. He does according to all that Joash his father has done. However the high places are not taken away. The people still sacrifice and burn incense in the high places. As soon as the kingdom is established in his hand, he kills his servants who have slain the king his father, but the children of the murderers he doesn’t put to death; according to that which is written in the book of the law of Moses, as YHWH commands, saying, “The fathers will not be put to death for the children, nor the children be put to death for the fathers; but every man will die for his own sin.”

He kills ten thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt, and takes Sela by war, and calls its name Joktheel, to this day. Then Amaziah sends messengers to Jehoash, the son of Jehoahaz son of Jehu, king of Israel, saying, “Come, let us look one another in the face.”

Jehoash the king of Israel sends to Amaziah king of Judah, saying, “The thistle that was in Lebanon sent to the cedar that was in Lebanon, saying, ‘Give your daughter to my son as wife. Then a wild animal that was in Lebanon passed by, and trampled down the thistle. You have indeed struck Edom, and your heart has lifted you up. Enjoy the glory of it, and stay at home; for why should you meddle to your harm, that you fall, even you, and Judah with you?’” But Amaziah would not listen. So Jehoash king of Israel goes up; and he and Amaziah king of Judah looks one another in the face at Beth Shemesh, which belongs to Judah. Judah is defeated by Israel; and each man flees to his tent. Jehoash king of Israel takes Amaziah king of Judah, the son of Jehoash the son of Ahaziah, at Beth Shemesh, and comes to Jerusalem, and breaks down the wall of Jerusalem from the gate of Ephraim to the corner gate, four hundred cubits. He takes all the gold and silver, and all the vessels that are found in YHWH’s house and in the treasures of the king’s house, the hostages also, and returns to Samaria.

Now the rest of the acts of Jehoash which he does, and his might, and how he fights with Amaziah king of Judah, aren’t they write in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel? Jehoash sleeps with his fathers, and is buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel; and Jeroboam his son reigns in his place.

Amaziah the son of Joash king of Judah lives after the death of Jehoash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel fifteen years. Now the rest of the acts of Amaziah, aren’t they write in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah? They make a conspiracy against him in Jerusalem, and he flees to Lachish; but they send after him to Lachish, and kill him there. They bring him on horses, and he is buried at Jerusalem with his fathers in David’s city.

All the people of Judah take Azariah, who is sixteen years old, and make him king in the place of his father Amaziah. He builds Elath, and restores it to Judah. After that the king sleeps with his fathers.
Jeroboam II of Israel · 14:23–29

In the fifteenth year of Amaziah the son of Joash king of Judah, Jeroboam the son of Joash king of Israel begins to reign in Samaria for forty-one years. He does that which is evil in YHWH’s sight. He doesn’t depart from all the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, with which he makes Israel to sin. He restores the border of Israel from the entrance of Hamath to the sea of the Arabah, according to YHWH, the God of Israel’s word, which he speaks by his servant Jonah the son of Amittai, the prophet, who is from Gath Hepher. For YHWH sees the affliction of Israel, that it is very bitter; for all, slave and free, and there is no helper for Israel. YHWH doesn’t say that he would blot out the name of Israel from under the sky; but he saves them by the hand of Jeroboam the son of Joash. Now the rest of the acts of Jeroboam, and all that he does, and his might, how he fights, and how he recovers Damascus, and Hamath, which has belonged to Judah, for Israel, aren’t they write in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel? Jeroboam sleeps with his fathers, even with the kings of Israel; and Zechariah his son reigns in his place.
Azariah (uzziah) of Judah · 15:1–7

In the twenty-seventh year of Jeroboam king of Israel, Azariah son of Amaziah king of Judah begins to reign. He is sixteen years old when he begins to reign, and he reigns fifty-two years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name is Jecoliah of Jerusalem. He does that which is right in YHWH’s eyes, according to all that his father Amaziah has done. However the high places are not taken away. The people still sacrifice and burn incense in the high places. YHWH strikes the king, so that he is a leper to the day of his death, and lives in a separate house. Jotham, the king’s son is over the household, judging the people of the land. Now the rest of the acts of Azariah, and all that he does, aren’t they write in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah? Azariah sleeps with his fathers; and they bury him with his fathers in David’s city: and Jotham his son reigns in his place.
The Last Kings of Israel · 15:8–31

In the thirty-eighth year of Azariah king of Judah, Zechariah the son of Jeroboam reigns over Israel in Samaria six months. He does that which is evil in YHWH’s sight, as his fathers have done. He doesn’t depart from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, with which he makes Israel to sin. Shallum the son of Jabesh conspires against him, and strikes him before the people, and kills him, and reigns in his place. Now the rest of the acts of Zechariah, look, they are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel. This is YHWH’s word which he speaks to Jehu, saying, “Your sons to the fourth generation will sit on the throne of Israel.” So it comes to pass.

Shallum the son of Jabesh begins to reign in the thirty-ninth year of Uzziah king of Judah, and he reigns for a month in Samaria. Menahem the son of Gadi goes up from Tirzah, comes to Samaria, strikes Shallum the son of Jabesh in Samaria, kills him, and reigns in his place. Now the rest of the acts of Shallum, and his conspiracy which he makes, look, they are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.

Then Menahem attacks Tiphsah, and all who are in it, and its border areas, from Tirzah. He attacks it because they don’t open their gates to him, and he rips up all their women who are with child. In the thirty ninth year of Azariah king of Judah, Menahem the son of Gadi begins to reign over Israel for ten years in Samaria. He does that which is evil in YHWH’s sight. He doesn’t depart all his days from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, with which he makes Israel to sin. Pul the king of Assyria comes against the land, and Menahem gives Pul one thousand talents of silver, that his hand might be with him to confirm the kingdom in his hand. Menahem exacts the money from Israel, even from all the mighty men of wealth, from each man fifty shekels of silver, to give to the king of Assyria. So the king of Assyria turns back, and doesn’t stay there in the land. Now the rest of the acts of Menahem, and all that he does, aren’t they write in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel? Menahem sleeps with his fathers, and Pekahiah his son reigns in his place.

In the fiftieth year of Azariah king of Judah, Pekahiah the son of Menahem begins to reign over Israel in Samaria for two years. He does that which is evil in YHWH’s sight. He doesn’t depart from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, with which he makes Israel to sin. Pekah the son of Remaliah, his captain, conspires against him and attacks him in Samaria, in the fortress of the king’s house, with Argob and Arieh; and with him are fifty men of the Gileadites. He kills him, and reigns in his place. Now the rest of the acts of Pekahiah, and all that he does, look, they are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.

In the fifty-second year of Azariah king of Judah, Pekah the son of Remaliah begins to reign over Israel in Samaria for twenty years. He does that which is evil in YHWH’s sight. He doesn’t depart from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, with which he makes Israel to sin. In the days of Pekah king of Israel, Tiglath Pileser king of Assyria comes and takes Ijon, Abel Beth Maacah, Janoah, Kedesh, Hazor, Gilead, and Galilee, all the land of Naphtali; and he carries them captive to Assyria. Hoshea the son of Elah makes a conspiracy against Pekah the son of Remaliah, attacks him, kills him, and reigns in his place, in the twentieth year of Jotham the son of Uzziah. Now the rest of the acts of Pekah, and all that he does, look, they are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.
Jotham of Judah · 15:32–38

In the second year of Pekah the son of Remaliah king of Israel, Jotham the son of Uzziah king of Judah begins to reign. He is twenty-five years old when he begins to reign, and he reigns sixteen years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name is Jerusha the daughter of Zadok. He does that which is right in YHWH’s eyes. He does according to all that his father Uzziah has done. However the high places are not taken away. The people still sacrifice and burn incense in the high places. He builds the upper gate of YHWH’s house. Now the rest of the acts of Jotham, and all that he does, aren’t they write in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah? In those days, YHWH begins to send Rezin the king of Syria and Pekah the son of Remaliah against Judah. Jotham sleeps with his fathers, and is buried with his fathers in his father David’s city, and Ahaz his son reigns in his place.
Ahaz of Judah · 16:1–20

In the seventeenth year of Pekah the son of Remaliah, Ahaz the son of Jotham king of Judah begins to reign. Ahaz is twenty years old when he begins to reign, and he reigns sixteen years in Jerusalem. He doesn’t do that which is right in YHWH his God’s eyes, like David his father. But he walks in the way of the kings of Israel, yes, and makes his son to pass through the fire, according to the abominations of the nations whom YHWH casts out from before the children of Israel. He sacrifices and burns incense in the high places, on the hills, and under every green tree. Then Rezin king of Syria and Pekah son of Remaliah king of Israel comes up to Jerusalem to wage war. They besiege Ahaz, but can not overcome him. At that time Rezin king of Syria recovers Elath to Syria, and drives the Jews from Elath; and the Syrians come to Elath, and live there, to this day. So Ahaz sends messengers to Tiglath Pileser king of Assyria, saying, “I am your servant and your son. Come up and save me out of the hand of the king of Syria, and out of the hand of the king of Israel, who rise up against me.” Ahaz takes the silver and gold that are found in YHWH’s house, and in the treasures of the king’s house, and sends it for a present to the king of Assyria. The king of Assyria listens to him; and the king of Assyria goes up against Damascus, and takes it, and carries its people captive to Kir, and kills Rezin. King Ahaz goes to Damascus to meet Tiglath Pileser king of Assyria, and sees the altar that is at Damascus; and king Ahaz sends to Urijah the priest a drawing of the altar and plans to build it. Urijah the priest builds an altar. According to all that king Ahaz has sent from Damascus, so Urijah the priest makes it for the coming of king Ahaz from Damascus. When the king has come from Damascus, the king sees the altar; and the king comes near to the altar, and offers on it. He burns his burnt offering and his meal offering, pours his drink offering, and sprinkles the blood of his peace offerings on the altar. The bronze altar, which is before YHWH, he brings from the front of the house, from between his altar and YHWH’s house, and puts it on the north side of his altar. King Ahaz commands Urijah the priest, saying, “On the great altar burn the morning burnt offering, the evening meal offering, the king’s burnt offering, his meal offering, with the burnt offering of all the people of the land, their meal offering, and their drink offerings; and sprinkle on it all the blood of the burnt offering, and all the blood of the sacrifice; but the bronze altar will be for me to inquire by.” Urijah the priest does so, according to all that king Ahaz commands. King Ahaz cuts off the panels of the bases, and removes the basin from off them, and takes down the sea from off the bronze oxen that are under it, and puts it on a pavement of stone. He removes the covered way for the Sabbath that they have built in the house, and the king’s entry outside to YHWH’s house, because of the king of Assyria. Now the rest of the acts of Ahaz which he does, aren’t they write in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah? Ahaz sleeps with his fathers, and is buried with his fathers in David’s city, and Hezekiah his son reigns in his place.
Hoshea and the Fall of Samaria · 17:1–6

In the twelfth year of Ahaz king of Judah, Hoshea the son of Elah begins to reign in Samaria over Israel for nine years. He does that which is evil in YHWH’s sight, yet not as the kings of Israel who are before him. Shalmaneser king of Assyria comes up against him, and Hoshea becomes his servant, and brings him tribute. The king of Assyria finds conspiracy in Hoshea; for he has sent messengers to So king of Egypt, and offers no tribute to the king of Assyria, as he has done year by year. Therefore the king of Assyria seizes him, and binds him in prison. Then the king of Assyria comes up throughout all the land, goes up to Samaria, and besieges it three years. In the ninth year of Hoshea the king of Assyria takes Samaria, and carries Israel away to Assyria, and places them in Halah, and on the Habor, the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes.
The Narrator's Great Explanation · 17:7–23

It is so because the children of Israel have sinned against YHWH their God, who brings them up out of the land of Egypt from under the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and have feared other gods, and walk in the statutes of the nations whom YHWH casts out from before the children of Israel, and of the kings of Israel, which they make. The children of Israel secretly do things that are not right against YHWH their God; and they build high places for themselves in all their cities, from the tower of the watchmen to the fortified city; and they set up for themselves pillars and Asherah poles on every high hill, and under every green tree; and there they burn incense in all the high places, as the nations whom YHWH carries away before them do; and they do wicked things to provoke YHWH to anger; and they serve idols, of which YHWH has said to them, “You will not do this thing.” Yet YHWH testifies to Israel, and to Judah, by every prophet, and every seer, saying, “Turn from your evil ways, and keep my commandments and my statutes, according to all the law which I commanded your fathers, and which I sent to you by my servants the prophets.” Notwithstanding, they would not listen, but harden their neck, like the neck of their fathers, who doesn’t believe in YHWH their God. They reject his statutes, and his covenant that he makes with their fathers, and his testimonies which he testifies to them; and they follow vanity, and become vain, and follow the nations that are around them, concerning whom YHWH has commanded them that they should not do like them. They abandon all the commandments of YHWH their God, and make molten images for themselves, even two calves, and make an Asherah, and worship all the army of the sky, and serve Baal. They cause their sons and their daughters to pass through the fire, use divination and enchantments, and sell themselves to do that which is evil in YHWH’s sight, to provoke him to anger. Therefore YHWH is very angry with Israel, and removes them out of his sight. There is none left but the tribe of Judah only. Also Judah doesn’t keep the commandments of YHWH their God, but walks in the statutes of Israel which they make. YHWH rejects all the offspring of Israel, afflicts them, and delivers them into the hands of raiders, until he has cast them out of his sight. For he tears Israel from David’s house; and they make Jeroboam the son of Nebat king; and Jeroboam drives Israel from following YHWH, and makes them sin a great sin. The children of Israel walk in all the sins of Jeroboam which he does; they don’t depart from them until YHWH removes Israel out of his sight, as he says by all his servants the prophets. So Israel is carried away out of their own land to Assyria to this day.
The Resettlement of Samaria · 17:24–41

The king of Assyria brings men from Babylon, from Cuthah, from Avva, and from Hamath and Sepharvaim, and places them in the cities of Samaria instead of the children of Israel; and they possess Samaria, and live in its cities. So it is, at the beginning of their dwelling there, that they don’t fear YHWH. Therefore YHWH sends lions among them, which kill some of them. Therefore they speak to the king of Assyria, saying, “The nations which you have carried away and placed in the cities of Samaria don’t know the law of the god of the land. Therefore he has sent lions among them, and look, they kill them, because they don’t know the law of the god of the land.”
Then the king of Assyria commands, saying, “Carry there one of the priests whom you brought from there; and let them go and dwell there, and let him teach them the law of the god of the land.”

So one of the priests whom they have carried away from Samaria comes and lives in Bethel, and teaches them how they should fear YHWH. However every nation makes gods of their own, and puts them in the houses of the high places which the Samaritans have made, every nation in their cities in which they live. The men of Babylon make Succoth Benoth, and the men of Cuth make Nergal, and the men of Hamath make Ashima, and the Avvites make Nibhaz and Tartak; and the Sepharvites burn their children in the fire to Adrammelech and Anammelech, the gods of Sepharvaim. So they fear YHWH, and also made from among themselves priests of the high places for themselves, who sacrifices for them in the houses of the high places. They fear YHWH, and also serve their own gods, after the ways of the nations from among whom they have been carried away. To this day they do what they do before. They don’t fear YHWH, and they do not follow the statutes, or the ordinances, or the law, or the commandment which YHWH commands the children of Jacob, whom he names Israel; with whom YHWH has made a covenant, and commands them, saying, “You will not fear other gods, nor bow yourselves to them, nor serve them, nor sacrifice to them; but you will fear YHWH, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt with great power and with an outstretched arm, and you will bow yourselves to him, and you will sacrifice to him. The statutes and the ordinances, and the law and the commandment, which he wrote for you, you will observe to do forever more. You will not fear other gods. You will not forget the covenant that I have made with you. You will not fear other gods. But you will fear YHWH your God, and he will deliver you out of the hand of all your enemies.” However they do not listen, but they do what they do before. So these nations fear YHWH, and also serve their engraved images. Their children likewise, and their children’s children, as their fathers do, so they do to this day.
Hezekiah's Reforms · 18:1–8

Now in the third year of Hoshea son of Elah king of Israel, Hezekiah the son of Ahaz king of Judah begins to reign. He is twenty-five years old when he begins to reign, and he reigns twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name is Abi the daughter of Zechariah. He does that which is right in YHWH’s eyes, according to all that David his father has done. He removes the high places, and breaks the pillars, and cuts down the Asherah. He also breaks in pieces the bronze serpent that Moses has made, because in those days the children of Israel burn incense to it; and he calls it Nehushtan. He trusts in YHWH, the God of Israel; so that after him is no one like him among all the kings of Judah, nor among them that are before him. For he joins with YHWH. He doesn’t depart from following him, but keeps his commandments, which YHWH commands Moses. YHWH is with him. Wherever he goes, he prospers. He rebels against the king of Assyria, and doesn’t serve him. He strikes the Philistines to Gaza and its borders, from the tower of the watchmen to the fortified city.
The Fall of Samaria Recalled · 18:9–12

In the fourth year of king Hezekiah, which is the seventh year of Hoshea son of Elah king of Israel, Shalmaneser king of Assyria comes up against Samaria, and besieges it.
