At the end of three years they take it. In the sixth year of Hezekiah, which is the ninth year of Hoshea king of Israel, Samaria is taken. The king of Assyria carries Israel away to Assyria, and puts them in Halah, and on the Habor, the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes, because they don’t obey YHWH their God’s voice, but transgress his covenant, even all that Moses the servant of YHWH commanded, and would not hear it or do it.
Sennacherib Invades Judah · 18:13–37

Now in the fourteenth year of king Hezekiah, Sennacherib king of Assyria come up against all the fortified cities of Judah, and take them. Hezekiah king of Judah sends to the king of Assyria to Lachish, saying, “I have offended you. Return from me. That which you put on me, I will bear.” The king of Assyria appoints to Hezekiah king of Judah three hundred talents of silver and thirty talents of gold. Hezekiah gives him all the silver that is found in YHWH’s house, and in the treasures of the king’s house. At that time, Hezekiah cuts off the gold from the doors of YHWH’s temple, and from the pillars which Hezekiah king of Judah has overlaid, and gives it to the king of Assyria.

The king of Assyria sends Tartan and Rabsaris and Rabshakeh from Lachish to king Hezekiah with a great army to Jerusalem. They go up and come to Jerusalem. When they have come up, they come and stand by the conduit of the upper pool, which is in the highway of the fuller’s field. When they have called to the king, Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, who are over the household, and Shebnah the scribe, and Joah the son of Asaph the recorder come out to them. Rabshakeh says to them, “Say now to Hezekiah, ‘Thus says the great king, the king of Assyria, “What confidence is this in which you trust? You say (but they are but vain words), ‘There is counsel and strength for war.’ Now on whom do you trust, that you have rebelled against me? Now, look, you trust in the staff of this bruised reed, even in Egypt. If a man leans on it, it will go into his hand, and pierce it. So is Pharaoh king of Egypt to all who trust on him. But if you tell me, ‘We trust in YHWH our God;’ isn’t that he whose high places and whose altars Hezekiah has taken away, and has said to Judah and to Jerusalem, ‘You will worship before this altar in Jerusalem?’ Now therefore, please give pledges to my master the king of Assyria, and I will give you two thousand horses, if you are able on your part to set riders on them. How then can you turn away the face of one captain of the least of my master’s servants, and put your trust on Egypt for chariots and for horsemen? Have I now come up without YHWH against this place to destroy it? YHWH said to me, ‘Go up against this land, and destroy it.’”’”

Then Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, Shebnah, and Joah, says to Rabshakeh, “Please speak to your servants in the Syrian language, for we understand it. Don’t speak with us in the Jews’ language, in the hearing of the people who are on the wall.”

But Rabshakeh says to them, “Has my master sent me to your master and to you, to speak these words? Hasn’t he sent me to the men who sit on the wall, to eat their own dung, and to drink their own urine with you?” Then Rabshakeh stands, and cries with a loud voice in the Jews’ language, and speaks, saying, “Hear the word of the great king, the king of Assyria. Thus says the king, ‘Don’t let Hezekiah deceive you; for he will not be able to deliver you out of his hand. Don’t let Hezekiah make you trust in YHWH, saying, “YHWH will surely deliver us, and this city will not be given into the hand of the king of Assyria.” Don’t listen to Hezekiah.’ For thus says the king of Assyria, ‘Make your peace with me, and come out to me; and everyone of you eat from his own vine, and everyone from his own fig tree, and everyone drink water from his own cistern; until I come and take you away to a land like your own land, a land of grain and new wine, a land of bread and vineyards, a land of olive trees and of honey, that you may live, and not die. Don’t listen to Hezekiah, when he persuades you, saying, “YHWH will deliver us.” Has any of the gods of the nations ever delivers his land out of the hand of the king of Assyria? Where are the gods of Hamath, and of Arpad? Where are the gods of Sepharvaim, of Hena, and Ivvah? Have they delivered Samaria out of my hand? Who are they among all the gods of the countries, that have delivered their country out of my hand, that YHWH should deliver Jerusalem out of my hand?’”

But the people stay quiet, and answer him not a word; for the king’s commandment is, “Don’t answer him.” Then Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, who is over the household, comes with Shebna the scribe, and Joah the son of Asaph the recorder, to Hezekiah with their clothes torn, and tells him Rabshakeh’s words.
Hezekiah's Prayer · 19:1–19

When king Hezekiah hears it, he tears his clothes, covers himself with sackcloth, and goes into YHWH’s house. He sends Eliakim, who is over the household, Shebna the scribe, and the elders of the priests, covered with sackcloth, to Isaiah the prophet the son of Amoz. They say to him, “Thus says Hezekiah, ‘Today is a day of trouble, of rebuke, and of rejection; for the children have come to the point of birth, and there is no strength to deliver them. It may be YHWH your God will hear all the words of Rabshakeh, whom the king of Assyria his master has sent to defy the living God, and will rebuke the words which YHWH your God has heard. Therefore lift up your prayer for the remnant that is left.’”

So the servants of king Hezekiah come to Isaiah. Isaiah says to them, “Tell your master this: ‘YHWH says, “Don’t be afraid of the words that you have heard, with which the servants of the king of Assyria have blasphemed me. Look, I will put a spirit in him, and he will hear news, and will return to his own land. I will cause him to fall by the sword in his own land.”’”

So Rabshakeh returns and finds the king of Assyria warring against Libnah; for he has heard that he has departed from Lachish. When he hears it says of Tirhakah king of Ethiopia, “Look, he has come out to fight against you, he sent messengers again to Hezekiah, saying, ‘Tell Hezekiah king of Judah this: “Don’t let your God in whom you trust deceive you, saying, Jerusalem will not be given into the hand of the king of Assyria. Look, you have heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all lands, by destroying them utterly. Will you be delivered? Have the gods of the nations delivered them, which my fathers have destroyed, Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and the children of Eden who were in Telassar? Where is the king of Hamath, the king of Arpad, and the king of the city of Sepharvaim, of Hena, and Ivvah?”’”

Hezekiah receives the letter from the hand of the messengers and reads it. Then Hezekiah goes up to YHWH’s house, and spreads it before YHWH. Hezekiah prays before YHWH, and says, “YHWH, the God of Israel, who sit above the cherubim, you are the God, even you alone, of all the kingdoms of the earth. You have made heaven and earth. Incline your ear, YHWH, and hear. Open your eyes, YHWH, and see. Hear the words of Sennacherib, which he has sent to defy the living God. Truly, YHWH, the kings of Assyria have laid waste the nations and their lands, and have cast their gods into the fire; for they were no gods, but the work of men’s hands, wood and stone. Therefore they have destroyed them. Now therefore, YHWH our God, save us, I beg you, out of his hand, that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that you, YHWH, are God alone.”
Isaiah's Oracle against Sennacherib · 19:20–34

Then Isaiah the son of Amoz sent to Hezekiah, saying, “YHWH, the God of Israel, says ‘You have prayed to me against Sennacherib king of Assyria, and I have heard you. This is the word that YHWH has spoken concerning him: ‘The virgin daughter of Zion has despised you and ridiculed you. The daughter of Jerusalem has shaken her head at you. Whom have you defied and blasphemed? Against whom have you exalted your voice and lifted up your eyes on high? Against the Holy One of Israel! By your messengers, you have defied the Lord, and have said, “With the multitude of my chariots, I have come up to the height of the mountains, to the innermost parts of Lebanon, and I will cut down its tall cedars and its choice cypress trees; and I will enter into his farthest lodging place, the forest of his fruitful field. I have dug and drunk strange waters, and with the sole of my feet will I dry up all the rivers of Egypt.” Haven’t you hear how I have done it long ago, and form it of ancient times? Now I have brought it to pass, that it should be yours to lay waste fortifies cities into ruinous heaps. Therefore their inhabitants have little power. They are dismayed and confound. They are like the grass of the field, and like the green herb, like the grass on the housetops, and like grain blasted before it has grown up. But I know your sitting down, your going out, your coming in, and your raging against me. Because of your raging against me, and because your arrogance has come up into my ears, therefore I will put my hook in your nose, and my bridle in your lips, and I will turn you back by the way by which you come.’

“This will be the sign to you: This year, you will eat that which grows of itself, and in the second year that which springs of the same; and in the third year sow, and reap, and plant vineyards, and eat its fruit. The remnant that has escaped of the house of Judah will again take root downward, and bear fruit upward. For out of Jerusalem a remnant will go out, and out of Mount Zion those who will escape. YHWH’s zeal will perform this.

“Therefore YHWH says concerning the king of Assyria, ‘He will not come to this city, nor shoot an arrow there. He will not come before it with shield, nor cast up a mound against it. By the way that he came, by the same he will return, and he will not come to this city,’ says YHWH. ‘For I will defend this city to save it, for my own sake, and for my servant David’s sake.’”
The Angel Strikes the Assyrian Camp · 19:35–37

That night, YHWH’s angel goes out, and strikes one hundred eighty-five thousand in the camp of the Assyrians. When men arise early in the morning, look, these are all dead bodies. So Sennacherib king of Assyria departs, and goes and returns, and lives at Nineveh. As he is worshiping in the house of Nisroch his god, Adrammelech and Sharezer strike him with the sword; and they escape into the land of Ararat. Esar Haddon his son reigns in his place.
Hezekiah's Illness and Recovery · 20:1–11
In those days Hezekiah is sick and dying. Isaiah the prophet the son of Amoz comes to him, and says to him, “YHWH says, ‘Set your house in order; for you will die, and not live.’”

Then he turns his face to the wall, and prays to YHWH, saying, “Remember now, YHWH, I beg you, how I have walked before you in truth and with a perfect heart, and have done that which is good in your sight.” And Hezekiah weeps bitterly.

Before Isaiah has gone out into the middle part of the city, YHWH’s word comes to him, saying, “Turn back, and tell Hezekiah the prince of my people, ‘YHWH, the God of David your father, says, “I have heard your prayer. I have seen your tears. Look, I will heal you. On the third day, you will go up to YHWH’s house. I will add to your days fifteen years. I will deliver you and this city out of the hand of the king of Assyria. I will defend this city for my own sake, and for my servant David’s sake.”’”
Isaiah says, “Take a cake of figs.”
They take and lay it on the boil, and he recovers. Hezekiah says to Isaiah, “What will be the sign that YHWH will heal me, and that I will go up to YHWH’s house the third day?”
Isaiah says, “This will be the sign to you from YHWH, that YHWH will do the thing that he has spoken: should the shadow go forward ten steps, or go back ten steps?”
Hezekiah answers, “It is a light thing for the shadow to go forward ten steps. No, but let the shadow return backward ten steps.”
Isaiah the prophet cries to YHWH; and he brings the shadow ten steps backward, by which it has gone down on the sundial of Ahaz.
The Babylonian Envoys · 20:12–21

At that time Berodach Baladan the son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sends letters and a present to Hezekiah; for he has heard that Hezekiah has been sick. Hezekiah listens to them, and shows them all the storehouse of his precious things, the silver, the gold, the spices, and the precious oil, and the house of his armor, and all that are found in his treasures. There is nothing in his house, or in all his dominion, that Hezekiah doesn’t show them.
Then Isaiah the prophet comes to king Hezekiah, and says to him, “What did these men say? From where did they come to you?”
Hezekiah says, “They have come from a far country, even from Babylon.”
He says, “What have they seen in your house?”
Hezekiah answers, “They have seen all that is in my house. There is nothing among my treasures that I have not shown them.”

Isaiah says to Hezekiah, “Hear YHWH’s word. ‘Look, the days come that all that is in your house, and that which your fathers have laid up in store to this day, will be carried to Babylon. Nothing will be left,’ says YHWH. ‘They will take away some of your sons who will issue from you, whom you will father; and they will be eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon.’”
Then Hezekiah says to Isaiah, “YHWH’s word which you have spoken is good.” He says moreover, “Isn’t it so, if peace and truth will be in my days?”

Now the rest of the acts of Hezekiah, and all his might, and how he makes the pool, and the conduit, and brings water into the city, aren’t they write in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah? Hezekiah sleeps with his fathers, and Manasseh his son reigns in his place.
Manasseh's Fifty-five Year Reign · 21:1–18

Manasseh is twelve years old when he begins to reign, and he reigns fifty-five years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name is Hephzibah. He does that which is evil in YHWH’s sight, after the abominations of the nations whom YHWH casts out before the children of Israel. For he builds again the high places which Hezekiah his father has destroyed; and he raises up altars for Baal, and makes an Asherah, as Ahab king of Israel does, and worships all the army of the sky, and serves them. He builds altars in YHWH’s house, of which YHWH says, “I will put my name in Jerusalem.” He builds altars for all the army of the sky in the two courts of YHWH’s house. He makes his son to pass through the fire, practices sorcery, used enchantments, and deals with those who have familiar spirits, and with wizards. He does much evil in YHWH’s sight, to provoke him to anger. He sets the engraved image of Asherah that he has made in the house of which YHWH says to David and to Solomon his son, “In this house, and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, will I put my name forever; I will not cause the feet of Israel to wander any more out of the land which I gave their fathers, if only they will observe to do according to all that I have commanded them, and according to all the law that my servant Moses commanded them.” But they don’t listen, and Manasseh seduces them to do that which is evil more than the nations do whom YHWH destroys before the children of Israel. YHWH speaks by his servants the prophets, saying, “Because Manasseh king of Judah has done these abominations, and has done wickedly above all that the Amorites did, who were before him, and has also made Judah to sin with his idols; therefore YHWH the God of Israel says, ‘Look, I bring such evil on Jerusalem and Judah that whoever hears of it, both his ears will tingle. I will stretch over Jerusalem the line of Samaria, and the plummet of Ahab’s house; and I will wipe Jerusalem as a man wipes a dish, wiping it and turning it upside down. I will cast off the remnant of my inheritance, and deliver them into the hands of their enemies. They will become a prey and a plunder to all their enemies, because they have done that which is evil in my sight, and have provoked me to anger, since the day their fathers came out of Egypt, even to this day.’”

Moreover Manasseh sheds innocent blood very much, until he has filled Jerusalem from one end to another; besides his sin with which he makes Judah to sin, in doing that which is evil in YHWH’s sight. Now the rest of the acts of Manasseh, and all that he does, and his sin that he sins, aren’t they write in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah? Manasseh sleeps with his fathers, and is buried in the garden of his own house, in the garden of Uzza; and Amon his son reigns in his place.
Amon's Brief Reign · 21:19–26

Amon is twenty-two years old when he begins to reign; and he reigns two years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name is Meshullemeth the daughter of Haruz of Jotbah. He does that which is evil in YHWH’s sight, as Manasseh his father does. He walks in all the ways that his father walks in, and serves the idols that his father serves, and worships them; and he abandons YHWH, the God of his fathers, and doesn’t walk in the way of YHWH. The servants of Amon conspire against him, and put the king to death in his own house. But the people of the land kill all those who have conspired against king Amon; and the people of the land make Josiah his son king in his place. Now the rest of the acts of Amon which he does, aren’t they write in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah? He is buried in his tomb in the garden of Uzza, and Josiah his son reigns in his place.
Josiah and the Book of the Law · 22:1–20

Josiah is eight years old when he begins to reign, and he reigns thirty-one years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name is Jedidah the daughter of Adaiah of Bozkath. He does that which is right in YHWH’s eyes, and walks in all the way of David his father, and doesn’t turn away to the right hand or to the left. In the eighteenth year of king Josiah, the king sends Shaphan, the son of Azaliah the son of Meshullam, the scribe, to YHWH’s house, saying, “Go up to Hilkiah the high priest, that he may count the money which is brought into YHWH’s house, which the keepers of the threshold have gathered of the people. Let them deliver it into the hand of the workmen who have the oversight of YHWH’s house; and let them give it to the workmen who are in YHWH’s house, to repair the damage to the house, to the carpenters, and to the builders, and to the masons, and for buying timber and cut stone to repair the house. However there was no accounting made with them of the money that was delivered into their hand; for they dealt faithfully.”

Hilkiah the high priest says to Shaphan the scribe, “I have found the book of the law in YHWH’s house.” Hilkiah delivers the book to Shaphan, and he reads it. Shaphan the scribe comes to the king, and brings the king word again, and says, “Your servants have emptied out the money that was found in the house, and have delivered it into the hands of the workmen who have the oversight of YHWH’s house.” Shaphan the scribe tells the king, saying, “Hilkiah the priest has delivered a book to me.” Then Shaphan reads it before the king.

When the king has heard the words of the book of the law, he tears his clothes. The king commands Hilkiah the priest, Ahikam the son of Shaphan, Achbor the son of Micaiah, Shaphan the scribe, and Asaiah the king’s servant, saying, “Go inquire of YHWH for me, and for the people, and for all Judah, concerning the words of this book that is found; for great is YHWH’s wrath that is kindled against us, because our fathers have not listened to the words of this book, to do according to all that which is written concerning us.”

So Hilkiah the priest, Ahikam, Achbor, Shaphan, and Asaiah, goes to Huldah the prophetess, the wife of Shallum the son of Tikvah, the son of Harhas, keeper of the wardrobe (now she lives in Jerusalem in the second quarter); and they talk with her. She says to them, “YHWH the God of Israel says, ‘Tell the man who sent you to me, “YHWH says, ‘Look, I will bring evil on this place, and on its inhabitants, even all the words of the book which the king of Judah has read. Because they have forsaken me, and have burned incense to other gods, that they might provoke me to anger with all the work of their hands, therefore my wrath will be kindled against this place, and it will not be quenched.’” But to the king of Judah, who sends you to inquire of YHWH, tell him, “YHWH the God of Israel says, ‘Concerning the words which you have heard, because your heart was tender, and you humbled yourself before YHWH, when you heard what I spoke against this place, and against its inhabitants, that they should become a desolation and a curse, and have torn your clothes, and wept before me; I also have heard you,’ says YHWH. ‘Therefore look, I will gather you to your fathers, and you will be gathered to your grave in peace. Your eyes will not see all the evil which I will bring on this place.’”’” So they bring this message back to the king.
Josiah's Reform · 23:1–27

The king sends, and they gather to him all the elders of Judah and of Jerusalem. The king goes up to YHWH’s house, and all the men of Judah and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem with him, with the priests, the prophets, and all the people, both small and great; and he reads in their hearing all the words of the book of the covenant which is found in YHWH’s house. The king stands by the pillar, and makes a covenant before YHWH, to walk after YHWH, and to keep his commandments, his testimonies, and his statutes, with all his heart, and all his soul, to confirm the words of this covenant that are written in this book; and all the people agree to the covenant. The king commands Hilkiah the high priest, and the priests of the second order, and the keepers of the threshold, to bring out of YHWH’s temple all the vessels that are made for Baal, for the Asherah, and for all the army of the sky, and he burns them outside of Jerusalem in the fields of the Kidron, and carries their ashes to Bethel. He gets rid of the idolatrous priests, whom the kings of Judah have ordained to burn incense in the high places in the cities of Judah, and in the places around Jerusalem; those also who burn incense to Baal, to the sun, and to the moon, and to the planets, and to all the army of the sky. He brings out the Asherah from YHWH’s house, outside of Jerusalem, to the brook Kidron, and burns it at the brook Kidron, and beats it to dust, and casts its dust on the graves of the common people. He breaks down the houses of the male shrine prostitutes that are in YHWH’s house, where the women wove hangings for the Asherah. He brings all the priests out of the cities of Judah, and defiles the high places where the priests have burned incense, from Geba to Beersheba; and he breaks down the high places of the gates that are at the entrance of the gate of Joshua the governor of the city, which are on a man’s left hand at the gate of the city. Nevertheless the priests of the high places don’t come up to YHWH’s altar in Jerusalem, but they eat unleavened bread among their brothers. He defiles Topheth, which is in the valley of the children of Hinnom, that no man might make his son or his daughter to pass through the fire to Molech. He takes away the horses that the kings of Judah have given to the sun, at the entrance of YHWH’s house, by the room of Nathan Melech the officer, who is in the court; and he burns the chariots of the sun with fire. The king breaks down the altars that are on the roof of the upper room of Ahaz, which the kings of Judah have made, and the altars which Manasseh has made in the two courts of YHWH’s house, and beats them down from there, and casts their dust into the brook Kidron. The king defiles the high places that are before Jerusalem, which are on the right hand of the mountain of corruption, which Solomon the king of Israel has built for Ashtoreth the abomination of the Sidonians, and for Chemosh the abomination of Moab, and for Milcom the abomination of the children of Ammon. He breaks in pieces the pillars, cuts down the Asherah poles, and fills their places with men’s bones. Moreover the altar that are at Bethel, and the high place which Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who makes Israel to sin, has made, even that altar and the high place he breaks down; and he burns the high place and beat it to dust, and burn the Asherah. As Josiah turns himself, he spies the tombs that are there in the mountain; and he sends, and takes the bones out of the tombs, and burns them on the altar, and defiles it, according to YHWH’s word which the man of God proclaims, who proclaims these things. Then he says, “What monument is that which I see?”
The men of the city tell him, “It is the tomb of the man of God, who came from Judah, and proclaimed these things that you have done against the altar of Bethel.”

He says, “Let him be! Let no one move his bones.” So they let his bones alone, with the bones of the prophet who come out of Samaria. All the houses also of the high places that are in the cities of Samaria, which the kings of Israel have made to provoke YHWH to anger, Josiah takes away, and does to them according to all the acts that he has done in Bethel. He kills all the priests of the high places that are there, on the altars, and burns men’s bones on them; and he returns to Jerusalem.

The king commands all the people, saying, “Keep the Passover to YHWH your God, as it is written in this book of the covenant.” Surely there is not kept such a Passover from the days of the judges who judge Israel, nor in all the days of the kings of Israel, nor of the kings of Judah; but in the eighteenth year of king Josiah, this Passover is kept to YHWH in Jerusalem. Moreover Josiah removes those who have familiar spirits, the wizards, and the teraphim, and the idols, and all the abominations that are seen in the land of Judah and in Jerusalem, that he might confirm the words of the law which are written in the book that Hilkiah the priest finds in YHWH’s house. There is no king like him before him, who turns to YHWH with all his heart, and with all his soul, and with all his might, according to all the law of Moses; and there is none like him who arises after him. Notwithstanding, YHWH doesn’t turn from the fierceness of his great wrath, with which his anger burns against Judah, because of all the provocation with which Manasseh has provoked him. YHWH says, “I will also remove Judah out of my sight, as I have removed Israel, and I will cast off this city which I have chosen, even Jerusalem, and the house of which I said, ‘My name will be there.’”
The Death of Josiah · 23:28–37

Now the rest of the acts of Josiah, and all that he does, aren’t they write in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah? In his days Pharaoh Necoh king of Egypt goes up against the king of Assyria to the river Euphrates; and king Josiah goes against him; and Pharaoh Necoh kills him at Megiddo, when he has seen him. His servants carry him in a chariot dead from Megiddo, and bring him to Jerusalem, and bury him in his own tomb. The people of the land take Jehoahaz the son of Josiah, and anoint him, and make him king in his father’s place.

Jehoahaz is twenty-three years old when he begins to reign; and he reigns three months in Jerusalem. His mother’s name is Hamutal the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah. He does that which is evil in YHWH’s sight, according to all that his fathers have done. Pharaoh Necoh puts him in bonds at Riblah in the land of Hamath, that he might not reign in Jerusalem; and puts the land to a tribute of one hundred talents of silver, and a talent of gold. Pharaoh Necoh makes Eliakim the son of Josiah king in the place of Josiah his father, and changes his name to Jehoiakim; but he takes Jehoahaz away, and he comes to Egypt and dies there. Jehoiakim gives the silver and the gold to Pharaoh; but he taxes the land to give the money according to the commandment of Pharaoh. He exacts the silver and the gold of the people of the land, from everyone according to his assessment, to give it to Pharaoh Necoh. Jehoiakim is twenty-five years old when he begins to reign, and he reigns eleven years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name is Zebidah the daughter of Pedaiah of Rumah. He does that which is evil in YHWH’s sight, according to all that his fathers have done.
Jehoiakim and the First Deportation · 24:1–7

In his days Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon comes up, and Jehoiakim becomes his servant three years. Then he turns and rebels against him. YHWH sends against him bands of the Chaldeans, and bands of the Syrians, and bands of the Moabites, and bands of the children of Ammon, and sends them against Judah to destroy it, according to YHWH’s word, which he speaks by his servants the prophets. Surely at the commandment of YHWH this comes on Judah, to remove them out of his sight, for the sins of Manasseh, according to all that he does, and also for the innocent blood that he sheds; for he fills Jerusalem with innocent blood, and YHWH would not pardon. Now the rest of the acts of Jehoiakim, and all that he does, aren’t they write in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah? So Jehoiakim sleeps with his fathers, and Jehoiachin his son reigns in his place.
The king of Egypt doesn’t come out of his land any more; for the king of Babylon has taken, from the brook of Egypt to the river Euphrates, all that belong to the king of Egypt.
Jehoiachin and the Second Deportation · 24:8–17

Jehoiachin is eighteen years old when he begins to reign, and he reigns in Jerusalem three months. His mother’s name is Nehushta the daughter of Elnathan of Jerusalem. He does that which is evil in YHWH’s sight, according to all that his father has done. At that time the servants of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon come up to Jerusalem, and the city is besieged. Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon comes to the city while his servants are besieging it, and Jehoiachin the king of Judah goes out to the king of Babylon, he, and his mother, and his servants, and his princes, and his officers; and the king of Babylon captures him in the eighth year of his reign. He carries out from there all the treasures of YHWH’s house, and the treasures of the king’s house, and cuts in pieces all the vessels of gold, which Solomon king of Israel has made in YHWH’s temple, as YHWH has said. He carries away all Jerusalem, and all the princes, and all the mighty men of valor, even ten thousand captives, and all the craftsmen and the smiths. No one remains, except the poorest people of the land. He carries away Jehoiachin to Babylon, with the king’s mother, the king’s wives, his officers, and the chief men of the land. He carries them into captivity from Jerusalem to Babylon. All the men of might, even seven thousand, and the craftsmen and the smiths one thousand, all of them strong and fit for war, even them the king of Babylon bring captive to Babylon. The king of Babylon makes Mattaniah, Jehoiachin’s father’s brother, king in his place, and changes his name to Zedekiah.
Zedekiah's Reign · 24:18–20

Zedekiah is twenty-one years old when he begins to reign, and he reigns eleven years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name is Hamutal the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah. He does that which is evil in YHWH’s sight, according to all that Jehoiakim has done. For through the anger of YHWH, this happens in Jerusalem and Judah, until he has cast them out from his presence.
Then Zedekiah rebels against the king of Babylon.
The Siege and Fall of Jerusalem · 25:1–21

In the ninth year of Zedekiah’s reign, in the tenth month, on the tenth day of the month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon comes against Jerusalem — he and his whole army. He camps against the city and they build siege works all around it. The city stays under siege until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.

By the ninth day of the fourth month the famine in the city is so severe that there is no bread for the people of the land. Then the city wall is broken through. All the fighting men slip out by night through the gate between the two walls, near the king’s garden — though the Chaldeans are all around the city — and the king heads off toward the Arabah. But the Chaldean army pursues the king and overtakes him on the plains of Jericho, and his whole army scatters from him.

They seize the king and bring him up to the king of Babylon at Riblah, and there they pass sentence on him. They slaughter the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes — and put out Zedekiah’s eyes, bind him in bronze shackles, and take him to Babylon.

In the fifth month, on the seventh day of the month — in the nineteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon — Nebuzaradan, captain of the guard, a servant of the king of Babylon, comes to Jerusalem. He burns the house of YHWH, the king’s house, and all the houses of Jerusalem; every great house he burns with fire. And the whole Chaldean army with the captain of the guard tears down the walls around Jerusalem.

Nebuzaradan, captain of the guard, carries into exile the rest of the people left in the city, the deserters who have gone over to the king of Babylon, and the rest of the crowd. But the captain of the guard leaves some of the poorest of the land to tend the vineyards and work the fields.

The Chaldeans break up the bronze pillars in the house of YHWH, the stands, and the bronze Sea that are in the house of YHWH, and they carry the bronze to Babylon. They take the pots, the shovels, the wick trimmers, the dishes, and all the bronze utensils used in the temple service. The captain of the guard takes the firepans and the basins — whatever is made of gold, for the gold, and whatever is made of silver, for the silver. As for the two pillars, the one Sea, and the stands that Solomon made for the house of YHWH — the bronze of all these things is beyond weighing. Each pillar stands eighteen cubits high, with a bronze capital on top three cubits high, and a lattice and pomegranates all around the capital, all of bronze. The second pillar, with its lattice, is just like it.

The captain of the guard takes Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the second priest, and the three keepers of the threshold. From the city he takes an official who is in charge of the fighting men, five men of the king’s inner circle who are found in the city, the secretary of the army commander who musters the people of the land, and sixty men of the people of the land who are found in the city. Nebuzaradan, captain of the guard, takes them and brings them to the king of Babylon at Riblah. And the king of Babylon strikes them down and puts them to death at Riblah in the land of Hamath.
So Judah goes into exile, away from its own land.
Gedaliah’s Governorship and Assassination · 25:22–26

Over the people who remain in the land of Judah — those Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has left behind — he appoints Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, as governor. When all the army commanders and their men hear that the king of Babylon has made Gedaliah governor, they come to Gedaliah at Mizpah: Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan son of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth the Netophathite, and Jaazaniah son of the Maacathite, they and their men.
Gedaliah swears an oath to them and their men. “Do not be afraid of the Chaldean officials,” he tells them. “Settle in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it will go well with you.”

But in the seventh month Ishmael son of Nethaniah, son of Elishama, who is of royal blood, comes with ten men. They strike Gedaliah down and he dies — along with the Judeans and the Chaldeans who are with him at Mizpah. Then all the people, from the least to the greatest, along with the army commanders, get up and go to Egypt, for they are afraid of the Chaldeans.
Jehoiachin Released from Prison · 25:27–30

In the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, Evil-merodach king of Babylon — in the year he becomes king — lifts up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah and brings him out of prison. He speaks kindly to him and gives him a seat above the seats of the other kings who are with him in Babylon. So Jehoiachin puts off his prison clothes, and for the rest of his life he eats at the king’s table. And a regular allowance is given him by the king, a portion for each day, for as long as he lives.
From Adam to Abraham · 1:1–27

Adam, Seth, Enosh, Kenan, Mahalalel, Jared, Enoch, Methuselah, Lamech, Noah, Shem, Ham, and Japheth. The sons of Japheth: Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras. The sons of Gomer: Ashkenaz, Diphath, and Togarmah. The sons of Javan: Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Rodanim. The sons of Ham: Cush, Mizraim, Put, and Canaan. The sons of Cush: Seba, Havilah, Sabta, Raama, Sabteca. The sons of Raamah: Sheba and Dedan. Cush becomes the father of Nimrod. He begins to be a mighty one in the earth. Mizraim becomes the father of Ludim, Anamim, Lehabim, Naphtuhim, Pathrusim, Casluhim (where the Philistines comes from), and Caphtorim. Canaan becomes the father of Sidon his firstborn, Heth, the Jebusite, and the Amorite, the Girgashite, the Hivite, the Arkite, the Sinite, the Arvadite, the Zemarite, and the Hamathite. The sons of Shem: Elam, Asshur, Arpachshad, Lud, Aram, Uz, Hul, Gether, and Meshech. Arpachshad becomes the father of Shelah, and Shelah becomes the father of Eber. To Eber are born two sons: the name of the one is Peleg, for in his days the earth is divided; and his brother’s name is Joktan. Joktan becomes the father of Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah, Hadoram, Uzal, Diklah, Ebal, Abimael, Sheba, Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab. All these are the sons of Joktan. Shem, Arpachshad, Shelah, Eber, Peleg, Reu, Serug, Nahor, Terah, Abram (also called Abraham).
The Sons of Abraham · 1:28–34

The sons of Abraham: Isaac and Ishmael. These are their generations: the firstborn of Ishmael, Nebaioth; then Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam, Mishma, Dumah, Massa, Hadad, Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah. These are the sons of Ishmael. The sons of Keturah, Abraham’s concubine: she bears Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah. The sons of Jokshan: Sheba and Dedan. The sons of Midian: Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah. All these are the sons of Keturah. Abraham becomes the father of Isaac. The sons of Isaac: Esau and Israel.
The Sons of Esau and Seir · 1:35–54

The sons of Esau: Eliphaz, Reuel, Jeush, Jalam, and Korah. The sons of Eliphaz: Teman, Omar, Zephi, Gatam, Kenaz, Timna, and Amalek. The sons of Reuel: Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah. The sons of Seir: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah, Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan. The sons of Lotan: Hori and Homam; and Timna are Lotan’s sister. The sons of Shobal: Alian, Manahath, Ebal, Shephi, and Onam. The sons of Zibeon: Aiah and Anah. The son of Anah: Dishon. The sons of Dishon: Hamran, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran. The sons of Ezer: Bilhan, Zaavan, and Jaakan. The sons of Dishan: Uz and Aran.

Now these are the kings who reign in the land of Edom, before any king reigns over the children of Israel: Bela the son of Beor; and the name of his city are Dinhabah. Bela dies, and Jobab the son of Zerah of Bozrah reigns in his place. Jobab dies, and Husham of the land of the Temanites reigns in his place. Husham dies, and Hadad the son of Bedad, who strikes Midian in the field of Moab, reigns in his place; and the name of his city is Avith. Hadad dies, and Samlah of Masrekah reigns in his place. Samlah dies, and Shaul of Rehoboth by the River reigns in his place. Shaul dies, and Baal Hanan the son of Achbor reigns in his place. Baal Hanan dies, and Hadad reigns in his place; and the name of his city is Pai: and his wife’s name is Mehetabel, the daughter of Matred, the daughter of Mezahab. Then Hadad dies. The chiefs of Edom are: chief Timna, chief Aliah, chief Jetheth, chief Oholibamah, chief Elah, chief Pinon, chief Kenaz, chief Teman, chief Mibzar, chief Magdiel, and chief Iram. These are the chiefs of Edom.
The Sons of Israel · 2:1–2
These are the sons of Israel: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun, Dan, Joseph, Benjamin, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher.
The Line of Judah to David · 2:3–17

The sons of Judah: Er, Onan, and Shelah; which three are born to him of Shua’s daughter the Canaanitess. Er, Judah’s firstborn, is wicked in YHWH’s sight; and he kills him. Tamar his daughter-in-law bears him Perez and Zerah. All the sons of Judah are five. The sons of Perez: Hezron and Hamul. The sons of Zerah: Zimri, Ethan, Heman, Calcol, and Dara; five of them in all. The son of Carmi: Achar, the troubler of Israel, who commits a trespass in the devoted thing. The son of Ethan: Azariah. The sons also of Hezron, who are born to him: Jerahmeel, Ram, and Chelubai. Ram becomes the father of Amminadab, and Amminadab becomes the father of Nahshon, prince of the children of Judah; and Nahshon becomes the father of Salma, and Salma becomes the father of Boaz, and Boaz becomes the father of Obed, and Obed becomes the father of Jesse; and Jesse becomes the father of his firstborn Eliab, and Abinadab the second, and Shimea the third, Nethanel the fourth, Raddai the fifth, Ozem the sixth, David the seventh; and their sisters are Zeruiah and Abigail. The sons of Zeruiah: Abishai, Joab, and Asahel, three. Abigail bore Amasa; and the father of Amasa are Jether the Ishmaelite.
The Sons of Hezron: Caleb · 2:18–24

Caleb the son of Hezron becomes the father of children of Azubah his wife, and of Jerioth; and these are her sons: Jesher, Shobab, and Ardon. Azubah dies, and Caleb marries Ephrath, who bears him Hur. Hur becomes the father of Uri, and Uri becomes the father of Bezalel.

Afterward Hezron goes in to the daughter of Machir the father of Gilead, whom he takes as wife when he is sixty years old; and she bears him Segub. Segub becomes the father of Jair, who has twenty-three cities in the land of Gilead. Geshur and Aram take the towns of Jair from them, with Kenath, and its villages, even sixty cities. All these are the sons of Machir the father of Gilead. After Hezron dies in Caleb Ephrathah, Abijah Hezron’s wife bears him Ashhur the father of Tekoa.
The Sons of Jerahmeel · 2:25–41

The sons of Jerahmeel the firstborn of Hezron are Ram the firstborn, Bunah, Oren, Ozem, and Ahijah. Jerahmeel has another wife, whose name is Atarah. She is the mother of Onam. The sons of Ram the firstborn of Jerahmeel are Maaz, Jamin, and Eker. The sons of Onam are Shammai and Jada. The sons of Shammai: Nadab and Abishur. The name of the wife of Abishur is Abihail; and she bears him Ahban and Molid. The sons of Nadab: Seled and Appaim; but Seled die without children. The son of Appaim: Ishi. The son of Ishi: Sheshan. The son of Sheshan: Ahlai. The sons of Jada the brother of Shammai: Jether and Jonathan; and Jether die without children. The sons of Jonathan: Peleth and Zaza. These are the sons of Jerahmeel. Now Sheshan has no sons, but daughters. Sheshan has a servant, an Egyptian, whose name is Jarha. Sheshan gives his daughter to Jarha his servant as wife; and she bears him Attai. Attai becomes the father of Nathan, and Nathan becomes the father of Zabad, and Zabad becomes the father of Ephlal, and Ephlal becomes the father of Obed, and Obed becomes the father of Jehu, and Jehu becomes the father of Azariah, and Azariah becomes the father of Helez, and Helez becomes the father of Eleasah, and Eleasah becomes the father of Sismai, and Sismai becomes the father of Shallum, and Shallum becomes the father of Jekamiah, and Jekamiah becomes the father of Elishama.
The Sons of Caleb Son of Hezron · 2:42–55

The sons of Caleb the brother of Jerahmeel are Mesha his firstborn, who is the father of Ziph; and the sons of Mareshah the father of Hebron. The sons of Hebron: Korah, Tappuah, Rekem, and Shema. Shema becomes the father of Raham, the father of Jorkeam; and Rekem becomes the father of Shammai. The son of Shammai is Maon; and Maon is the father of Beth Zur. Ephah, Caleb’s concubine, bore Haran, Moza, and Gazez; and Haran become the father of Gazez. The sons of Jahdai: Regem, Jothan, Geshan, Pelet, Ephah, and Shaaph. Maacah, Caleb’s concubine, bore Sheber and Tirhanah. She bears also Shaaph the father of Madmannah, Sheva the father of Machbena, and the father of Gibea; and the daughter of Caleb is Achsah. These are the sons of Caleb, the son of Hur, the firstborn of Ephrathah: Shobal the father of Kiriath Jearim, Salma the father of Bethlehem, and Hareph the father of Beth Gader. Shobal the father of Kiriath Jearim has sons: Haroeh, half of the Menuhoth. The families of Kiriath Jearim: the Ithrites, the Puthites, the Shumathites, and the Mishraites; from them come the Zorathites and the Eshtaolites. The sons of Salma: Bethlehem, the Netophathites, Atroth Beth Joab, and half of the Manahathites, the Zorites. The families of scribes who live at Jabez: the Tirathites, the Shimeathites, and the Sucathites. These are the Kenites who come from Hammath, the father of the house of Rechab.
The Sons of David Born in Hebron · 3:1–4

Now these are the sons of David, who are born to him in Hebron: the firstborn, Amnon, of Ahinoam the Jezreelitess; the second, Daniel, of Abigail the Carmelitess; the third, Absalom the son of Maacah the daughter of Talmai king of Geshur; the fourth, Adonijah the son of Haggith; the fifth, Shephatiah of Abital; the sixth, Ithream by Eglah his wife: six are born to him in Hebron; and he reigns there seven years and six months. He reigns thirty-three years in Jerusalem;
The Sons of David Born in Jerusalem · 3:5–9

and these are born to him in Jerusalem: Shimea, Shobab, Nathan, and Solomon, four, of Bathshua the daughter of Ammiel; and Ibhar, Elishama, Eliphelet, Nogah, Nepheg, Japhia, Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet, nine. All these are the sons of David, besides the sons of the concubines; and Tamar is their sister.
The Kings of Judah · 3:10–16

Solomon’s son is Rehoboam, Abijah his son, Asa his son, Jehoshaphat his son, Joram his son, Ahaziah his son, Joash his son, Amaziah his son, Azariah his son, Jotham his son, Ahaz his son, Hezekiah his son, Manasseh his son, Amon his son, and Josiah his son. The sons of Josiah: the firstborn Johanan, the second Jehoiakim, the third Zedekiah, and the fourth Shallum. The sons of Jehoiakim: Jeconiah his son, and Zedekiah his son.
The Royal Line After the Exile · 3:17–24

The sons of Jeconiah, the captive: Shealtiel his son, Malchiram, Pedaiah, Shenazzar, Jekamiah, Hoshama, and Nedabiah. The sons of Pedaiah: Zerubbabel and Shimei. The sons of Zerubbabel: Meshullam and Hananiah; and Shelomith are their sister; and Hashubah, Ohel, Berechiah, Hasadiah, and Jushab Hesed, five. The sons of Hananiah: Pelatiah and Jeshaiah; the sons of Rephaiah, the sons of Arnan, the sons of Obadiah, the sons of Shecaniah. The son of Shecaniah: Shemaiah. The sons of Shemaiah: Hattush, Igal, Bariah, Neariah, and Shaphat, six. The sons of Neariah: Elioenai, Hizkiah, and Azrikam, three. The sons of Elioenai: Hodaviah, Eliashib, Pelaiah, Akkub, Johanan, Delaiah, and Anani, seven.
Further Sons of Judah · 4:1–23

The sons of Judah: Perez, Hezron, Carmi, Hur, and Shobal. Reaiah the son of Shobal becomes the father of Jahath; and Jahath becomes the father of Ahumai and Lahad. These are the families of the Zorathites. These are the sons of the father of Etam: Jezreel, Ishma, and Idbash. The name of their sister is Hazzelelponi. Penuel is the father of Gedor and Ezer the father of Hushah. These are the sons of Hur, the firstborn of Ephrathah, the father of Bethlehem. Ashhur the father of Tekoa has two wives, Helah and Naarah. Naarah bears him Ahuzzam, Hepher, Temeni, and Haahashtari. These are the sons of Naarah. The sons of Helah are Zereth, Izhar, and Ethnan. Hakkoz becomes the father of Anub, Zobebah, and the families of Aharhel the son of Harum.
Jabez is more honorable than his brothers. His mother names him Jabez, saying, “Because I bore him with sorrow.”
Jabez calls on the God of Israel, saying, “Oh that you would bless me indeed, and enlarge my border! May your hand be with me, and may you keep me from evil, that I may not cause pain!”

God grants him that which he requests. Chelub the brother of Shuhah becomes the father of Mehir, who is the father of Eshton. Eshton becomes the father of Beth Rapha, Paseah, and Tehinnah the father of Ir Nahash. These are the men of Recah. The sons of Kenaz: Othniel and Seraiah. The sons of Othniel: Hathath. Meonothai becomes the father of Ophrah: and Seraiah becomes the father of Joab the father of Ge Harashim; for they are craftsmen. The sons of Caleb the son of Jephunneh: Iru, Elah, and Naam. The son of Elah: Kenaz. The sons of Jehallelel: Ziph, Ziphah, Tiria, and Asarel. The sons of Ezrah: Jether, Mered, Epher, and Jalon; and she bears Miriam, Shammai, and Ishbah the father of Eshtemoa. His wife the Jewess bears Jered the father of Gedor, Heber the father of Soco, and Jekuthiel the father of Zanoah. These are the sons of Bithiah the daughter of Pharaoh, whom Mered takes. The sons of the wife of Hodiah, the sister of Naham, are the father of Keilah the Garmite, and Eshtemoa the Maacathite. The sons of Shimon: Amnon, Rinnah, Ben Hanan, and Tilon. The sons of Ishi: Zoheth, and Ben Zoheth. The sons of Shelah the son of Judah: Er the father of Lecah, Laadah the father of Mareshah, and the families of the house of those who work fine linen, of the house of Ashbea; and Jokim, and the men of Cozeba, and Joash, and Saraph, who have dominion in Moab, and Jashubilehem. These records are ancient. These are the potters, and the inhabitants of Netaim and Gederah: they live there with the king for his work.
The Sons of Simeon · 4:24–43

The sons of Simeon: Nemuel, Jamin, Jarib, Zerah, Shaul; Shallum his son, Mibsam his son, and Mishma his son. The sons of Mishma: Hammuel his son, Zaccur his son, Shimei his son. Shimei has sixteen sons and six daughters; but his brothers don’t have many children, and all their family does not multiply like the children of Judah. David Becomes King over All Israel · 11:1–3

Then all Israel gathers themselves to David to Hebron, saying, “Look, we are your bone and your flesh. In times past, even when Saul was king, it was you who led out and brought in Israel. YHWH your God said to you, ‘You will be shepherd of my people Israel, and you will be prince over my people Israel.’”
So all the elders of Israel come to the king to Hebron; and David makes a covenant with them in Hebron before YHWH; and they anoint David king over Israel, according to YHWH’s word by Samuel.
David Captures Jerusalem · 11:4–9

David and all Israel go to Jerusalem (also called Jebus); and the Jebusites, the inhabitants of the land, are there. The inhabitants of Jebus say to David, “You will not come in here.” Nevertheless David takes the stronghold of Zion. The same is David’s city. David says, “Whoever strikes the Jebusites first will be chief and captain.” Joab the son of Zeruiah goes up first, and is made chief. David lives in the stronghold; therefore they call it David’s city. He builds the city all around, from Millo even around; and Joab repairs the rest of the city. David grows greater and greater; for YHWH of hosts is with him.
The Three Warriors · 11:10–19
Now these are the chief of the mighty men whom David has, who show themselves strong with him in his kingdom, together with all Israel, to make him king, according to YHWH’s word concerning Israel.

This is the number of the mighty men whom David has: Jashobeam, the son of a Hachmonite, the chief of the thirty; he lifts up his spear against three hundred and kills them at one time. After him is Eleazar the son of Dodo, the Ahohite, who is one of the three mighty men. He is with David at Pasdammim, and there the Philistines are gathered together to battle, where there is a plot of ground full of barley; and the people flee from before the Philistines. They stand in the middle of the plot, defend it, and kill the Philistines; and YHWH saves them by a great victory. Three of the thirty chief men goes down to the rock to David, into the cave of Adullam; and the army of the Philistines are encamped in the valley of Rephaim. David is then in the stronghold, and the garrison of the Philistines is in Bethlehem at that time. David longs, and says, “Oh that one would give me water to drink from the well of Bethlehem, which is by the gate!”

The three breaks through the army of the Philistines, and draws water out of the well of Bethlehem, that is by the gate, and takes it, and brings it to David; but David would not drink any of it, but pours it out to YHWH, and says, “My God forbid me, that I should do this! Should I drink the blood of these men who have put their lives in jeopardy?” For they risk their lives to bring it. Therefore he would not drink it. The three mighty men do these things.
Abishai and Benaiah · 11:20–25

Abishai, the brother of Joab, he is chief of the three; for he lifts up his spear against three hundred and kills them, and has a name among the three. Of the three, he is more honorable than the two, and is made their captain; however he isn’t included in the three. Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, the son of a valiant man of Kabzeel, who has done mighty deeds, kills the two sons of Ariel of Moab. He also goes down and kills a lion in the middle of a pit on a snowy day. He kills an Egyptian, a man of great stature, five cubits high. In the Egyptian’s hand is a spear like a weaver’s beam; and he goes down to him with a staff, plucks the spear out of the Egyptian’s hand, and kills him with his own spear. Benaiah the son of Jehoiada does these things, and has a name among the three mighty men. Look, he is more honorable than the thirty, but he doesn’t attain to the three; and David sets him over his guard.
The List of David's Warriors · 11:26–47

The mighty men of the armies also include Asahel the brother of Joab, Elhanan the son of Dodo of Bethlehem, Shammoth the Harorite, Helez the Pelonite, Ira the son of Ikkesh the Tekoite, Abiezer the Anathothite, Sibbecai the Hushathite, Ilai the Ahohite, Maharai the Netophathite, Heled the son of Baanah the Netophathite, Ithai the son of Ribai of Gibeah of the children of Benjamin, Benaiah the Pirathonite, Hurai of the brooks of Gaash, Abiel the Arbathite, Azmaveth the Baharumite, Eliahba the Shaalbonite, the sons of Hashem the Gizonite, Jonathan the son of Shagee the Hararite, Ahiam the son of Sacar the Hararite, Eliphal the son of Ur, Hepher the Mecherathite, Ahijah the Pelonite, Hezro the Carmelite, Naarai the son of Ezbai, Joel the brother of Nathan, Mibhar the son of Hagri, Zelek the Ammonite, Naharai the Berothite, the armor bearer of Joab the son of Zeruiah, Ira the Ithrite, Gareb the Ithrite, Uriah the Hittite, Zabad the son of Ahlai, Adina the son of Shiza the Reubenite, a chief of the Reubenites, and thirty with him, Hanan the son of Maacah, and Joshaphat the Mithnite, Uzzia the Ashterathite, Shama and Jeiel the sons of Hotham the Aroerite, Jediael the son of Shimri, and Joha his brother, the Tizite, Eliel the Mahavite, and Jeribai, and Joshaviah, the sons of Elnaam, and Ithmah the Moabite, Eliel, and Obed, and Jaasiel the Mezobaite.
Warriors Who Join David at Ziklag · 12:1–7

Now these are those who come to David to Ziklag, while he is a fugitive from Saul the son of Kish. They are among the mighty men, his helpers in war. They are armed with bows, and can use both the right hand and the left in slinging stones and in shooting arrows from the bow. They are of Saul’s relatives of the tribe of Benjamin. The chief is Ahiezer, then Joash, the sons of Shemaah the Gibeathite; Jeziel and Pelet, the sons of Azmaveth; Beracah; Jehu the Anathothite; Ishmaiah the Gibeonite, a mighty man among the thirty and a leader of the thirty; Jeremiah; Jahaziel; Johanan; Jozabad the Gederathite; Eluzai; Jerimoth; Bealiah; Shemariah; Shephatiah the Haruphite; Elkanah, Isshiah Azarel, Joezer, and Jashobeam, the Korahites; and Joelah and Zebadiah, the sons of Jeroham of Gedor.
Gadites Who Join David in the Wilderness · 12:8–15

Some Gadites join David in the stronghold in the wilderness, mighty men of valor, men trained for war, who can handle shield and spear; whose faces are like the faces of lions, and they are as swift as the gazelles on the mountains: Ezer the chief, Obadiah the second, Eliab the third, Mishmannah the fourth, Jeremiah the fifth, Attai the sixth, Eliel the seventh, Johanan the eighth, Elzabad the ninth, Jeremiah the tenth, and Machbannai the eleventh. These of the sons of Gad are captains of the army: he who is least is equal to one hundred, and the greatest to one thousand. These are those who go over the Jordan in the first month, when it has overflowed all its banks; and they put to flight all who live in the valleys, both toward the east and toward the west.
Benjaminites and Judahites Who Come to David · 12:16–18

Some of the children of Benjamin and Judah comes to the stronghold to David. David goes out to meet them, and answers them, “If you have come peaceably to me to help me, my heart will be united with you; but if you have come to betray me to my adversaries, since there is no wrong in my hands, may the God of our fathers see this and rebuke it.” Then the Spirit comes on Amasai, who is chief of the thirty, and he says, “We are yours, David, and on your side, you son of Jesse. Peace, peace be to you, and peace be to your helpers; for your God helps you.” Then David receives them, and makes them captains of the band.
Manassites Who Defect to David · 12:19–22

Some of Manasseh also joins David, when he comes with the Philistines against Saul to battle; but they don’t help them; for the lords of the Philistines sends him away after consultation, saying, “He will desert to his master Saul to the jeopardy of our heads.”

As he goes to Ziklag, some from Manasseh joins him: Adnah, Jozabad, Jediael, Michael, Jozabad, Elihu, and Zillethai, captains of thousands who are of Manasseh. They help David against the band of rovers; for they are all mighty men of valor, and are captains in the army. For from day to day men come to David to help him, until there is a great army, like God’s army.
The Army That Comes to David at Hebron · 12:23–40

These are the numbers of the heads of those who are armed for war, who comes to David to Hebron, to turn the kingdom of Saul to him, according to YHWH’s word. The children of Judah who bear shield and spear are six thousand eight hundred, armed for war. Of the children of Simeon, mighty men of valor for the war, seven thousand one hundred. Of the children of Levi four thousand six hundred. Jehoiada is the leader of the household of Aaron; and with him are three thousand seven hundred, and Zadok, a young man mighty of valor, and of his father’s house twenty-two captains. Of the children of Benjamin, Saul’s relatives, three thousand: for until then, the greatest part of them has kept their allegiance to Saul’s house. Of the children of Ephraim twenty thousand eight hundred, mighty men of valor, famous men in their fathers’ houses. Of the half-tribe of Manasseh eighteen thousand, who are mentioned by name, to come and make David king. Of the children of Issachar, men who have understanding of the times, to know what Israel ought to do, their heads are two hundred; and all their brothers are at their command. Of Zebulun, such as were able to go out in the army, who can set the battle in array, with all kinds of instruments of war, fifty thousand, and who can command and are not of double heart. Of Naphtali one thousand captains, and with them with shield and spear thirty-seven thousand. Of the Danites who can set the battle in array, twenty-eight thousand six hundred. Of Asher, such as were able to go out in the army, who can set the battle in array, forty thousand. On the other side of the Jordan, of the Reubenites, the Gadites, and of the half-tribe of Manasseh, with all kinds of instruments of war for the battle, one hundred twenty thousand. All these are men of war, who can order the battle array, and come with a perfect heart to Hebron, to make David king over all Israel; and all the rest also of Israel are of one heart to make David king. They are there with David three days, eating and drinking; for their brothers have supplied provisions for them. Moreover those who are near to them, as far as Issachar, Zebulun, and Naphtali, bring bread on donkeys, on camels, on mules, and on oxen: supplies of flour, cakes of figs, clusters of raisins, wine, oil, cattle, and sheep in abundance; for there is joy in Israel.
David Proposes to Bring the Ark · 13:1–4

David consults with the captains of thousands and of hundreds, even with every leader. David says to all the assembly of Israel, “If it seems good to you, and if it is of YHWH our God, let us send word everywhere to our brothers who are left in all the land of Israel, with whom the priests and Levites are in their cities that have suburbs, that they may gather themselves to us. Also, let us again bring the ark of our God back to us; for we didn’t seek it in the days of Saul.”
All the assembly says that they would do so; for the thing is right in the eyes of all the people.
The Ark is Brought from Kiriath-jearim · 13:5–8
So David assembles all Israel together, from the Shihor the brook of Egypt even to the entrance of Hamath, to bring God’s ark from Kiriath Jearim.

David goes up with all Israel to Baalah, that is, to Kiriath Jearim, which belongs to Judah, to bring up from there God YHWH’s ark that sits above the cherubim, that is called by the Name. They carry God’s ark on a new cart, and bring it out of Abinadab’s house; and Uzza and Ahio drive the cart. David and all Israel play before God with all their might, even with songs, with harps, with stringed instruments, with tambourines, with cymbals, and with trumpets.
The Death of Uzzah · 13:9–14

When they come to Chidon’s threshing floor, Uzza puts out his hand to hold the ark; for the oxen stumbles. YHWH’s anger burned against Uzza, and he strikes him, because he puts his hand on the ark; and he dies there before God. David is displeased, because YHWH has broken out against Uzza. He calls that place Perez Uzza, to this day. David is afraid of God that day, saying, “How can I bring God’s ark home to me?” So David doesn’t move the ark with him into David’s city, but carries it aside into Obed-Edom the Gittite’s house. God’s ark remains with the family of Obed-Edom in his house three months; and YHWH blesses Obed-Edom’s house and all that he has.
David's Palace and Family · 14:1–7

Hiram king of Tyre sends messengers to David with cedar trees, masons, and carpenters, to build him a house. David perceives that YHWH has established him king over Israel; for his kingdom is exalted on high, for his people Israel’s sake. David takes more wives at Jerusalem, and David becomes the father of more sons and daughters. These are the names of the children whom he has in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon, Ibhar, Elishua, Elpelet, Nogah, Nepheg, Japhia, Elishama, Beeliada, and Eliphelet.
David Defeats the Philistines · 14:8–17

When the Philistines hears that David is anointed king over all Israel, all the Philistines goes up to seek David; and David hears of it, and goes out against them. Now the Philistines has come and makes a raid in the valley of Rephaim. David inquires of God, saying, “Should I go up against the Philistines? Will you deliver them into my hand?”
YHWH says to him, “Go up; for I will deliver them into your hand.”

So they come up to Baal Perazim, and David defeats them there. David says, God has broken my enemies by my hand, like waters breaking out. Therefore they call the name of that place Baal Perazim. They leave their gods there; and David gives a command, and they are burned with fire.

The Philistines makes a another raid in the valley. David inquires again of God; and God says to him, “You will not go up after them. Turn away from them, and come on them opposite the mulberry trees. When you hear the sound of marching in the tops of the mulberry trees, then go out to battle; for God has gone out before you to strike the army of the Philistines.”
David does as God commands him; and they attack the army of the Philistines from Gibeon even to Gezer. The fame of David goes out into all lands; and YHWH brings the fear of him on all nations.
David Prepares for the Ark · 15:1–15

David makes himself houses in David’s city; and he prepares a place for God’s ark, and pitches a tent for it. Then David says, “No one ought to carry God’s ark but the Levites. For YHWH has chosen them to carry God’s ark, and to minister to him forever.”

David assembles all Israel at Jerusalem, to bring up YHWH’s ark to its place, which he has prepared for it. David gathers together the sons of Aaron and the Levites: of the sons of Kohath, Uriel the chief, and his brothers one hundred twenty; of the sons of Merari, Asaiah the chief, and his brothers two hundred twenty; of the sons of Gershom, Joel the chief, and his brothers one hundred thirty; of the sons of Elizaphan, Shemaiah the chief, and his brothers two hundred; of the sons of Hebron, Eliel the chief, and his brothers eighty; of the sons of Uzziel, Amminadab the chief, and his brothers one hundred twelve. David calls for Zadok and Abiathar the priests, and for the Levites, for Uriel, Asaiah, Joel, Shemaiah, Eliel, and Amminadab, and says to them, “You are the heads of the fathers’ households of the Levites. Sanctify yourselves, both you and your brothers, that you may bring the ark of YHWH, the God of Israel, up to the place that I have prepared for it. For because you didn’t carry it at first, YHWH our God broke out in anger against us, because we didn’t seek him according to the ordinance.”

So the priests and the Levites sanctify themselves to bring up the ark of YHWH, the God of Israel. The children of the Levites bear God’s ark on their shoulders with its poles, as Moses commands according to YHWH’s word.
The Musicians Appointed · 15:16–24

David speaks to the chief of the Levites to appoint their brothers as singers with instruments of music, stringed instruments, harps, and cymbals, sounding aloud and lifting up their voices with joy. So the Levites appoint Heman the son of Joel; and of his brothers, Asaph the son of Berechiah; and of the sons of Merari their brothers, Ethan the son of Kushaiah; and with them their brothers of the second rank, Zechariah, Ben, Jaaziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattithiah, Eliphelehu, Mikneiah, Obed-Edom, and Jeiel, the doorkeepers. So the singers, Heman, Asaph, and Ethan, are given cymbals of brass to sound aloud; and Zechariah, Aziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Maaseiah, and Benaiah, with stringed instruments set to Alamoth; and Mattithiah, Eliphelehu, Mikneiah, Obed-Edom, Jeiel, and Azaziah, with harps tuned to the eight-stringed lyre, to lead. Chenaniah, chief of the Levites, is over the singing. He teaches the singers, because he is skillful. Berechiah and Elkanah are doorkeepers for the ark. Shebaniah, Joshaphat, Nethanel, Amasai, Zechariah, Benaiah, and Eliezer, the priests, blow the trumpets before God’s ark; and Obed-Edom and Jehiah are doorkeepers for the ark.
The Ark Brought to Jerusalem · 15:25–29

So David, the elders of Israel, and the captains over thousands, goes to bring the ark of YHWH’s covenant up out of the house of Obed-Edom with joy. When God helps the Levites who bear the ark of YHWH’s covenant, they sacrifice seven bulls and seven rams. David is clothed with a robe of fine linen, as were all the Levites who bear the ark, the singers, and Chenaniah the choir master with the singers; and David has an ephod of linen on him. Thus all Israel brings the ark of YHWH’s covenant up with shouting, with sound of the cornet, with trumpets, and with cymbals, sounding aloud with stringed instruments and harps. As the ark of YHWH’s covenant comes to David’s city, Michal the daughter of Saul looks out at the window, and sees king David dancing and playing; and she despises him in her heart.
The Ark Installed; Sacrifices Offered · 16:1–6

They bring in God’s ark, and set it in the middle of the tent that David has pitched for it; and they offer burnt offerings and peace offerings before God. When David has finished offering the burnt offering and the peace offerings, he blesses the people in YHWH’s name. He gives to everyone of Israel, both man and woman, to everyone a loaf of bread, a portion of meat, and a cake of raisins. He appoints some of the Levites to minister before YHWH’s ark, and to commemorate, to thank, and to praise YHWH, the God of Israel: Asaph the chief, and second to him Zechariah, then Jeiel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Mattithiah, Eliab, Benaiah, Obed-Edom, and Jeiel, with stringed instruments and with harps; and Asaph with cymbals, sounding aloud; with Benaiah and Jahaziel the priests with trumpets continually, before the ark of the covenant of God.
The Psalm of Thanksgiving · 16:7–36
Then on that day David first ordains to give thanks to YHWH, by the hand of Asaph and his brothers.
Oh give thanks to YHWH.
Call on his name.
Make what he has done known among the peoples.
Sing to him.
Sing praises to him.
Tell of all his marvelous works.
Glory in his holy name.
Let the heart of those who seek YHWH rejoice.
Seek YHWH and his strength.
Seek his face forever more.
Remember his marvelous works that he has done,
his wonders, and the judgments of his mouth,
you offspring of Israel his servant,
you children of Jacob, his chosen ones.
He is YHWH our God.
His judgments are in all the earth.
Remember his covenant forever,
the word which he commanded to a thousand generations,
the covenant which he made with Abraham,
his oath to Isaac.
He confirmed the same to Jacob for a statute,
and to Israel for an everlasting covenant,
saying, “I will give you the land of Canaan,
The lot of your inheritance,”
when you were but a few men in number,
yes, very few, and foreigners were in it.
They went about from nation to nation,
from one kingdom to another people.
He allowed no man to do them wrong.
Yes, he reproved kings for their sakes,
“Don’t touch my anointed ones!
Do my prophets no harm!”
Sing to YHWH, all the earth!
Display his salvation from day to day.
Declare his glory among the nations,
and his marvelous works among all the peoples.
For great is YHWH, and greatly to be praised.
He also is to be feared above all gods.
For all the gods of the peoples are idols,
but YHWH made the heavens.
Honor and majesty are before him.
Strength and gladness are in his place.
Ascribe to YHWH, you relatives of the peoples,
ascribe to YHWH glory and strength!
Ascribe to YHWH the glory due to his name.
Bring an offering, and come before him.
Worship YHWH in holy array.
Tremble before him, all the earth.
The world also is established that it can’t be moved.
Let the heavens be glad,
and let the earth rejoice!
Let them say among the nations, “YHWH reigns!”
Let the sea roar, and its fullness!
Let the field exult, and all that is in it!
Then the trees of the forest will sing for joy before YHWH,
for he comes to judge the earth.
Oh give thanks to YHWH, for he is good,
for his steadfast love endures forever.
Say, “Save us, God of our salvation!
Gather us together and deliver us from the nations,
to give thanks to your holy name,
to triumph in your praise.”
Blessed be YHWH, the God of Israel,
from everlasting even to everlasting.
All the people say, “Amen,” and praise YHWH.
The Ark's Ministers and the Tabernacle at Gibeon · 16:37–43

So he leaves Asaph and his brothers there before the ark of YHWH’s covenant, to minister before the ark continually, as every day’s work requires; and Obed-Edom with their brothers, sixty-eight; Obed-Edom also the son of Jeduthun and Hosah to be doorkeepers; and Zadok the priest, and his brothers the priests, before YHWH’s tabernacle in the high place that is at Gibeon, to offer burnt offerings to YHWH on the altar of burnt offering continually morning and evening, even according to all that is written in YHWH’s law, which he commands to Israel; and with them Heman and Jeduthun, and the rest who are chosen, who are mentioned by name, to give thanks to YHWH, because his steadfast love endures forever; and with them Heman and Jeduthun with trumpets and cymbals for those that should sound aloud, and with instruments for the songs of God; and the sons of Jeduthun to be at the gate. All the people depart, each man to his house; and David returns to bless his house.
David's Desire to Build the Temple · 17:1–2
When David lives in his house, David says to Nathan the prophet, “Look, I dwell in a house of cedar, but the ark of YHWH’s covenant is in a tent.”
Nathan says to David, “Do all that is in your heart; for God is with you.”
The Word of the Lord to Nathan · 17:3–15

That same night, the word of God comes to Nathan, saying, “Go and tell David my servant, ‘YHWH says, “You will not build me a house to dwell in; for I have not lived in a house since the day that I brought up Israel to this day, but have gone from tent to tent, and from one tent to another. In all places in which I have walked with all Israel, did I speak a word with any of the judges of Israel, whom I commanded to be shepherd of my people, saying, ‘Why have you not built me a house of cedar?’”’

“Now therefore, you will tell my servant David, ‘YHWH of hosts says, “I took you from the sheep pen, from following the sheep, to be prince over my people Israel. I have been with you wherever you have gone, and have cut off all your enemies from before you. I will make you a name, like the name of the great ones who are in the earth. I will appoint a place for my people Israel, and will plant them, that they may dwell in their own place, and be moved no more. The children of wickedness will not waste them any more, as at the first, and from the day that I commanded judges to be over my people Israel. I will subdue all your enemies. Moreover I tell you that YHWH will build you a house. It will happen, when your days are fulfilled that you must go to be with your fathers, that I will set up your offspring after you, who will be of your sons; and I will establish his kingdom. He will build me a house, and I will establish his throne forever. I will be his father, and he will be my son. I will not take my steadfast love away from him, as I took it from him that was before you; but I will settle him in my house and in my kingdom forever. His throne will be established forever.”’” According to all these words, and according to all this vision, so Nathan speaks to David.
David's Prayer · 17:16–27

Then David the king goes in, and sits before YHWH; and he says, “Who am I, YHWH God, and what is my house, that you have brought me this far? This was a small thing in your eyes, God; but you have spoken of your servant’s house for a great while to come, and have respected me according to the standard of a man of high degree, YHWH God. What can David say yet more to you concerning the honor which is done to your servant? For you know your servant. YHWH, for your servant’s sake, and according to your own heart, you have done all this greatness, to make known all these great things. YHWH, there is no one like you, neither is there any God besides you, according to all that we have heard with our ears. What one nation in the earth is like your people Israel, whom God went to redeem to himself for a people, to make you a name by great and awesome things, in driving out nations from before your people, whom you redeem out of Egypt? For you made your people Israel your own people forever; and you, YHWH, became their God. Now, YHWH, let the word that you have spoken concerning your servant, and concerning his house, be established forever, and do as you have spoken. Let your name be established and magnified forever, saying, ‘YHWH of hosts is the God of Israel, even a God to Israel. The house of David your servant is established before you.’ For you, my God, have revealed to your servant that you will build him a house. Therefore your servant has found courage to pray before you. Now, YHWH, you are God, and have promised this good thing to your servant. Now it has pleased you to bless the house of your servant, that it may continue forever before you; for you, YHWH, have blessed, and it is blessed forever.”
David's Wars and Administration · 18:1–17

After this, David defeats the Philistines and subdues them, and takes Gath and its towns out of the hand of the Philistines. He defeats Moab; and the Moabites become servants to David, and bring tribute. David defeats Hadadezer king of Zobah to Hamath, as he goes to establish his dominion by the river Euphrates. David takes from him one thousand chariots, seven thousand horsemen, and twenty thousand footmen; and David hamstrings all the chariot horses, but reserved of them enough for one hundred chariots. When the Syrians of Damascus come to help Hadadezer king of Zobah, David strikes twenty-two thousand men of the Syrians. Then David puts garrisons in Syria of Damascus; and the Syrians become servants to David, and bring tribute. YHWH gives victory to David wherever he goes. David takes the shields of gold that are on the servants of Hadadezer, and brings them to Jerusalem. From Tibhath and from Cun, cities of Hadadezer, David takes very much brass, with which Solomon makes the bronze sea, the pillars, and the vessels of brass.

When Tou king of Hamath hears that David has struck all the army of Hadadezer king of Zobah, he sends Hadoram his son to king David, to Greet him, and to bless him, because he has fought against Hadadezer and strikes him (for Hadadezer has wars with Tou); and he has with him all kinds of vessels of gold and silver and brass. King David also dedicates these to YHWH, with the silver and the gold that he carries away from all the nations; from Edom, from Moab, from the children of Ammon, from the Philistines, and from Amalek. Moreover Abishai the son of Zeruiah strikes eighteen thousand of the Edomites in the Valley of Salt. He puts garrisons in Edom; and all the Edomites become servants to David. YHWH gives victory to David wherever he goes.

David reigns over all Israel; and he executes justice and righteousness for all his people. Joab the son of Zeruiah is over the army; Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud is recorder; Zadok the son of Ahitub, and Abimelech the son of Abiathar, are priests; Shavsha is scribe; and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada is over the Cherethites and the Pelethites; and the sons of David are chief officials serving the king.
David's Envoys Humiliated by the Ammonites · 19:1–5
After this, Nahash the king of the children of Ammon dies, and his son reigns in his place. David says, “I will show kindness to Hanun the son of Nahash, because his father showed kindness to me.”

So David sends messengers to comfort him concerning his father. David’s servants come into the land of the children of Ammon to Hanun, to comfort him. But the princes of the children of Ammon say to Hanun, “Do you think that David honors your father, in that he has sent comforters to you? Haven’t his servants come to you to search, to overthrow, and to spy out the land?” So Hanun takes David’s servants, shaves them, and cuts off their garments in the middle at their buttocks, and sends them away. Then some people go and tell David how the men are treated. He sends to meet them; for the men are greatly humiliated. The king says, “Stay at Jericho until your beards have grown, and then return.”
War with the Ammonites and Syrians · 19:6–19
