When the children of Ammon see that they have made themselves odious to David, Hanun and the children of Ammon send one thousand talents of silver to hire chariots and horsemen out of Mesopotamia, out of Aram-maacah, and out of Zobah. So they hire for themselves thirty-two thousand chariots, and the king of Maacah with his people, who come and encamp near Medeba. The children of Ammon gather themselves together from their cities, and come to battle. When David hears of it, he sends Joab with all the army of the mighty men. The children of Ammon come out, and put the battle in array at the gate of the city; and the kings who have come are by themselves in the field. Now when Joab sees that the battle is set against him before and behind, he chooses some of all the choice men of Israel, and puts them in array against the Syrians. The rest of the people he commits into the hand of Abishai his brother; and they put themselves in array against the children of Ammon. He says, “If the Syrians are too strong for me, then you are to help me; but if the children of Ammon are too strong for you, then I will help you. Be courageous, and let us be strong for our people and for the cities of our God. May YHWH do that which seems good to him.”

So Joab and the people who are with him come near to the front of the Syrians to the battle; and they flee before him. When the children of Ammon see that the Syrians have fled, they likewise flee before Abishai his brother, and enter into the city. Then Joab comes to Jerusalem.

When the Syrians see that they are defeated by Israel, they send messengers, and call out the Syrians who are beyond the River, with Shophach the captain of the army of Hadadezer leading them. David is told that; so he gathers all Israel together, passes over the Jordan, comes to them, and sets the battle in array against them. So when David has put the battle in array against the Syrians, they fight with him. The Syrians flee before Israel; and David kills of the Syrian men seven thousand chariots, and forty thousand footmen, and also kills Shophach the captain of the army. When the servants of Hadadezer see that they are defeated by Israel, they make peace with David, and serve him. The Syrians would not help the children of Ammon any more.
The Capture of Rabbah · 20:1–3

At the time of the return of the year, at the time when kings go out, Joab leads out the army, and wastes the country of the children of Ammon, and comes and besieges Rabbah. But David stays at Jerusalem. Joab strikes Rabbah, and overthrows it. David takes the crown of their king from off his head, and finds it to weigh a talent of gold, and there are precious stones in it. It is set on David’s head, and he brings very much plunder out of the city. He brings out the people who are in it, and has them cut with saws, with iron picks, and with axes. David does so to all the cities of the children of Ammon. Then David and all the people return to Jerusalem.
Wars with the Philistine Giants · 20:4–8
After this, war arises at Gezer with the Philistines. Then Sibbecai the Hushathite kills Sippai, of the sons of the giant; and they are subdued.

Again there is war with the Philistines; and Elhanan the son of Jair kills Lahmi the brother of Goliath the Gittite, the staff of whose spear is like a weaver’s beam. There is again war at Gath, where there is a man of great stature, who has twenty-four fingers and toes, six on each hand, and six on each foot; and he also is born to the giant. When he defies Israel, Jonathan the son of Shimea David’s brother kills him. These are born to the giant in Gath; and they fall by the hand of David, and by the hand of his servants.
David's Census · 21:1–7

Satan stands up against Israel, and moves David to take a census of Israel. David says to Joab and to the princes of the people, “Go, count Israel from Beersheba even to Dan; and bring me word, that I may know how many there are.”

Joab says, “May YHWH make his people a hundred times as many as they are. But, my lord the king, aren’t they all my lord’s servants? Why does my lord require this thing? Why will he be a cause of guilt to Israel?”

Nevertheless the king’s word prevails against Joab. Therefore Joab departs, and goes throughout all Israel, then comes to Jerusalem. Joab gives up the sum of the census of the people to David. All those of Israel are one million one hundred thousand men who draw a sword; and in Judah are four hundred seventy thousand men who draw a sword. But he doesn’t count Levi and Benjamin among them; for the king’s word is abominable to Joab.
God is displeased with this thing; therefore he strikes Israel.
David's Confession and the Plague · 21:8–17
David says to God, “I have sinned greatly, in that I have done this thing. But now put away, I beg you, the iniquity of your servant; for I have done very foolishly.”
YHWH speaks to Gad, David’s seer, saying, “Go and speak to David, saying, ‘YHWH says, “I offer you three things. Choose one of them, that I may do it to you.”’”

So Gad comes to David, and says to him, “YHWH says, ‘Take your choice: either three years of famine; or three months to be consumed before your foes, while the sword of your enemies overtakes you; or else three days the sword of YHWH, even pestilence in the land, and YHWH’s angel destroying throughout all the borders of Israel. Now therefore consider what answer I will return to him who sent me.’”
David says to Gad, “I am in distress. Let me fall, I pray, into YHWH’s hand; for his mercies are very great. Don’t let me fall into man’s hand.”

So YHWH sends a pestilence on Israel, and seventy thousand men of Israel fall. God sends an angel to Jerusalem to destroy it. As he is about to destroy, YHWH sees, and he relents of the disaster, and says to the destroying angel, “It is enough. Now withdraw your hand.” YHWH’s angel is standing by the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite. David lifts up his eyes, and sees YHWH’s angel standing between earth and the sky, having a drawn sword in his hand stretched out over Jerusalem.

Then David and the elders, clothed in sackcloth, fall on their faces. David says to God, “Isn’t it I who commanded the people to be counted? It is even I who have sinned and done very wickedly; but these sheep, what have they done? Please let your hand, O YHWH my God, be against me, and against my father’s house; but not against your people, that they should be plagued.”
David Buys the Threshing Floor · 21:18–30

Then YHWH’s angel commands Gad to tell David that David should go up and raise an altar to YHWH on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite. David goes up at the saying of Gad, which he speaks in YHWH’s name.

Ornan turns back, and sees the angel; and his four sons who are with him hide themselves. Now Ornan is threshing wheat. As David comes to Ornan, Ornan looks and sees David, and goes out of the threshing floor, and bows himself to David with his face to the ground.

Then David says to Ornan, “Give me the place of this threshing floor, that I may build an altar to YHWH on it. You will sell it to me for the full price, that the plague may be stopped from afflicting the people.”

Ornan says to David, “Take it for yourself, and let my lord the king do that which is good in his eyes. Look, I give the oxen for burnt offerings, and the threshing instruments for wood, and the wheat for the meal offering. I give it all.”
King David says to Ornan, “No; but I will most certainly buy it for the full price. For I will not take that which is yours for YHWH, nor offer a burnt offering that costs me nothing.”

So David gives to Ornan six hundred shekels of gold by weight for the place. David builds an altar to YHWH there, and offers burnt offerings and peace offerings, and calls on YHWH; and he answers him from the sky by fire on the altar of burnt offering.

Then YHWH commands the angel, and he puts his sword back into its sheath. At that time, when David sees that YHWH has answered him in the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite, then he sacrifices there. For YHWH’s tabernacle, which Moses makes in the wilderness, and the altar of burnt offering, are at that time in the high place at Gibeon. But David can’t go before it to inquire of God; for he is afraid because of the sword of YHWH’s angel.
David Prepares the Temple Site · 22:1–5
Then David says, “This is the house of YHWH God, and this is the altar of burnt offering for Israel.”

David gives orders to gather together the foreigners who are in the land of Israel; and he sets masons to cut dressed stones to build God’s house. David prepares iron in abundance for the nails for the doors of the gates, and for the couplings; and brass in abundance without weight; and cedar trees without number, for the Sidonians and the people of Tyre bring cedar trees in abundance to David. David says, “Solomon my son is young and tender, and the house that is to be built for YHWH must be exceedingly magnificent, of fame and of glory throughout all countries. I will therefore make preparation for it.” So David prepares abundantly before his death.
David's Charge to Solomon · 22:6–16

Then he calls for Solomon his son, and commands him to build a house for YHWH, the God of Israel. David says to Solomon his son, “As for me, it was in my heart to build a house to the name of YHWH my God. But YHWH’s word came to me, saying, ‘You have shed blood abundantly, and have made great wars. You will not build a house to my name, because you have shed much blood on the earth in my sight. Look, a son will be born to you, who will be a man of peace. I will give him rest from all his enemies all around; for his name will be Solomon, and I will give peace and quietness to Israel in his days. He will build a house for my name; and he will be my son, and I will be his father; and I will establish the throne of his kingdom over Israel for ever.’ Now, my son, may YHWH be with you and prosper you, and build the house of YHWH your God, as he has spoken concerning you. May YHWH give you discretion and understanding, and put you in charge of Israel; that so you may keep the law of YHWH your God. Then you will prosper, if you observe to do the statutes and the ordinances which YHWH gave Moses concerning Israel. Be strong and courageous. Don’t be afraid, and don’t be dismayed. Now, look, in my affliction I have prepared for YHWH’s house one hundred thousand talents of gold, one million talents of silver, and brass and iron without weight; for it is in abundance. I have also prepared timber and stone; and you may add to them. There are also workmen with you in abundance, cutters and workers of stone and timber, and all kinds of men who are skillful in every kind of work; of the gold, the silver, the brass, and the iron, there is no number. Arise and be doing, and may YHWH be with you.”
David Charges the Leaders of Israel · 22:17–19

David also commands all the princes of Israel to help Solomon his son, saying, “Isn’t YHWH your God with you? Hasn’t he given you rest on every side? For he has delivered the inhabitants of the land into my hand; and the land is subdued before YHWH, and before his people. Now set your heart and your soul to follow YHWH your God. Arise therefore, and build the sanctuary of YHWH God, to bring the ark of YHWH’s covenant and the holy vessels of God into the house that is to be built for YHWH’s name.”
David Organizes the Levites · 23:1–6

Now David is old and full of days; and he makes Solomon his son king over Israel. He gathers together all the princes of Israel, with the priests and the Levites. The Levites are counted from thirty years old and upward; and their number by their polls, man by man, is thirty-eight thousand. David says, “Of these, twenty-four thousand were to oversee the work of YHWH’s house, six thousand were officers and judges, four thousand were doorkeepers, and four thousand praised YHWH with the instruments which I made for giving praise.”
David divides them into divisions according to the sons of Levi: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
The Sons of Gershon · 23:7–11

Of the Gershonites: Ladan and Shimei. The sons of Ladan: Jehiel the chief, Zetham, and Joel, three. The sons of Shimei: Shelomoth, Haziel, and Haran, three. These are the heads of the fathers’ households of Ladan. The sons of Shimei: Jahath, Zina, Jeush, and Beriah. These four are the sons of Shimei. Jahath is the chief, and Zizah the second; but Jeush and Beriah don’t have many sons; therefore they become a fathers’ house in one reckoning.
The Sons of Kohath · 23:12–20

The sons of Kohath: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel, four. The sons of Amram: Aaron and Moses; and Aaron are separated, that he should sanctify the most holy things, he and his sons, forever, to burn incense before YHWH, to minister to him, and to bless in his name, forever. But as for Moses the man of God, his sons are named among the tribe of Levi. The sons of Moses: Gershom and Eliezer. The sons of Gershom: Shebuel the chief. The sons of Eliezer are: Rehabiah the chief; and Eliezer has no other sons; but the sons of Rehabiah are very many. The sons of Izhar: Shelomith the chief. The sons of Hebron: Jeriah the chief, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, and Jekameam the fourth. The sons of Uzziel: Micah the chief, and Isshiah the second.
The Sons of Merari · 23:21–23

The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. The sons of Mahli: Eleazar and Kish. Eleazar dies, and has no sons, but daughters only: and their brothers the sons of Kish take them as wives. The sons of Mushi: Mahli, Eder, and Jeremoth, three.
The Levites' New Role in the Temple · 23:24–32

These are the sons of Levi after their fathers’ houses, even the heads of the fathers’ houses of those who are counted individually, in the number of names by their polls, who do the work for the service of YHWH’s house, from twenty years old and upward. For David says, “YHWH, the God of Israel, has given rest to his people; and he dwells in Jerusalem forever. Also the Levites will no longer need to carry the tabernacle and all its vessels for its service.” For by the last words of David the sons of Levi are counted, from twenty years old and upward. For their office is to wait on the sons of Aaron for the service of YHWH’s house, in the courts, and in the rooms, and in the purifying of all holy things, even the work of the service of God’s house; for the show bread also, and for the fine flour for a meal offering, whether of unleavened wafers, or of that which is baked in the pan, or of that which is soaked, and for all measurements of quantity and size; and to stand every morning to thank and praise YHWH, and likewise in the evening; and to offer all burnt offerings to YHWH, on the Sabbaths, on the new moons, and on the set feasts, in number according to the ordinance concerning them, continually before YHWH; and that they should keep the duty of the Tent of Meeting, the duty of the holy place, and the duty of the sons of Aaron their brothers, for the service of YHWH’s house.
The Twenty-four Priestly Divisions · 24:1–19

These are the divisions of the sons of Aaron. The sons of Aaron: Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar. But Nadab and Abihu die before their father, and have no children: therefore Eleazar and Ithamar execute the priest’s office. David with Zadok of the sons of Eleazar and Ahimelech of the sons of Ithamar, divides them according to their ordering in their service. There are more chief men found of the sons of Eleazar than of the sons of Ithamar; and they are divided like this: of the sons of Eleazar there are sixteen, heads of fathers’ houses; and of the sons of Ithamar, according to their fathers’ houses, eight. Thus are they divided impartially by drawing lots; for there are princes of the sanctuary, and princes of God, both of the sons of Eleazar, and of the sons of Ithamar. Shemaiah the son of Nethanel the scribe, who is of the Levites, writes them in the presence of the king, the princes, Zadok the priest, Ahimelech the son of Abiathar, and the heads of the fathers’ households of the priests and of the Levites; one fathers’ house being taken for Eleazar, and one taken for Ithamar. Now the first lot comes out to Jehoiarib, the second to Jedaiah, the third to Harim, the fourth to Seorim, the fifth to Malchijah, the sixth to Mijamin, the seventh to Hakkoz, the eighth to Abijah, the ninth to Jeshua, the tenth to Shecaniah, the eleventh to Eliashib, the twelfth to Jakim, the thirteenth to Huppah, the fourteenth to Jeshebeab, the fifteenth to Bilgah, the sixteenth to Immer, the seventeenth to Hezir, the eighteenth to Happizzez, the nineteenth to Pethahiah, the twentieth to Jehezkel, the twenty-first to Jachin, the twenty-second to Gamul, the twenty-third to Delaiah, and the twenty-fourth to Maaziah. This is their ordering in their service, to come into YHWH’s house according to the ordinance given to them by Aaron their father, as YHWH, the God of Israel, has commanded him.
Remaining Levites by Lot · 24:20–31

Of the rest of the sons of Levi: of the sons of Amram, Shubael; of the sons of Shubael, Jehdeiah. Of Rehabiah: of the sons of Rehabiah, Isshiah the chief. Of the Izharites, Shelomoth; of the sons of Shelomoth, Jahath. The sons of Hebron: Jeriah, Amariah the second, Jahaziel the third, and Jekameam the fourth. The sons of Uzziel: Micah; of the sons of Micah, Shamir. The brother of Micah: Isshiah; of the sons of Isshiah, Zechariah. The sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi. The son of Jaaziah: Beno. The sons of Merari: of Jaaziah, Beno, Shoham, Zaccur, and Ibri. Of Mahli: Eleazar, who has no sons. Of Kish, the son of Kish: Jerahmeel. The sons of Mushi: Mahli, Eder, and Jerimoth. These are the sons of the Levites after their fathers’ houses. These likewise cast lots even as their brothers the sons of Aaron in the presence of David the king, Zadok, Ahimelech, and the heads of the fathers’ households of the priests and of the Levites; the fathers’ households of the chief even as those of his younger brother.
The Divisions of the Temple Musicians · 25:1–8

Moreover, David and the captains of the army set apart for the service certain of the sons of Asaph, and of Heman, and of Jeduthun, who are to prophesy with harps, with stringed instruments, and with cymbals. The number of those who do the work according to their service is: of the sons of Asaph: Zaccur, Joseph, Nethaniah, and Asharelah. The sons of Asaph are under the hand of Asaph, who prophesies at the order of the king. Of Jeduthun; the sons of Jeduthun: Gedaliah, Zeri, Jeshaiah, Shimei, Hashabiah, and Mattithiah, six, under the hands of their father Jeduthun, who prophesies in giving thanks and praising YHWH with the harp. Of Heman; the sons of Heman: Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Uzziel, Shebuel, Jerimoth, Hananiah, Hanani, Eliathah, Giddalti, Romamti-Ezer, Joshbekashah, Mallothi, Hothir, and Mahazioth. All these are the sons of Heman the king’s seer in the words of God, to lift up the horn. God gives to Heman fourteen sons and three daughters. All these are under the hands of their father for song in YHWH’s house, with cymbals, stringed instruments, and harps, for the service of God’s house; Asaph, Jeduthun, and Heman being under the order of the king. The number of them, with their brothers who are instructed in singing to YHWH, even all who are skillful, is two hundred eighty-eight. They cast lots for their offices, all alike, the small as well as the great, the teacher as well as the student.
The Twenty-four Musical Divisions · 25:9–31

Now the first lot comes out for Asaph to Joseph; the second to Gedaliah, he and his brothers and sons are twelve; the third to Zaccur, his sons and his brothers, twelve; the fourth to Izri, his sons and his brothers, twelve; the fifth to Nethaniah, his sons and his brothers, twelve; the sixth to Bukkiah, his sons and his brothers, twelve; the seventh to Jesharelah, his sons and his brothers, twelve; the eighth to Jeshaiah, his sons and his brothers, twelve; the ninth to Mattaniah, his sons and his brothers, twelve; the tenth to Shimei, his sons and his brothers, twelve; the eleventh to Azarel, his sons and his brothers, twelve; the twelfth to Hashabiah, his sons and his brothers, twelve; for the thirteenth, Shubael, his sons and his brothers, twelve; for the fourteenth, Mattithiah, his sons and his brothers, twelve; for the fifteenth to Jeremoth, his sons and his brothers, twelve; for the sixteenth to Hananiah, his sons and his brothers, twelve; for the seventeenth to Joshbekashah, his sons and his brothers, twelve; for the eighteenth to Hanani, his sons and his brothers, twelve; for the nineteenth to Mallothi, his sons and his brothers, twelve; for the twentieth to Eliathah, his sons and his brothers, twelve; for the twenty-first to Hothir, his sons and his brothers, twelve; for the twenty-second to Giddalti, his sons and his brothers, twelve; for the twenty-third to Mahazioth, his sons and his brothers, twelve; for the twenty-fourth to Romamti-Ezer, his sons and his brothers, twelve.
The Gatekeepers · 26:1–19

For the divisions of the doorkeepers: of the Korahites, Meshelemiah the son of Kore, of the sons of Asaph. Meshelemiah has sons: Zechariah the firstborn, Jediael the second, Zebadiah the third, Jathniel the fourth, Elam the fifth, Jehohanan the sixth, and Eliehoenai the seventh. Obed-Edom has sons: Shemaiah the firstborn, Jehozabad the second, Joah the third, Sacar the fourth, Nethanel the fifth, Ammiel the sixth, Issachar the seventh, and Peullethai the eighth; for God blesses him. Sons are also born to Shemaiah his son, who rules over the house of their father; for they are mighty men of valor. The sons of Shemaiah: Othni, Rephael, Obed, and Elzabad, whose brothers are valiant men, Elihu, and Semachiah. All these are of the sons of Obed-Edom: they and their sons and their brothers, able men in strength for the service; sixty-two of Obed-Edom. Meshelemiah has sons and brothers, valiant men, eighteen. Also Hosah, of the children of Merari, has sons: Shimri the chief (for though he is not the firstborn, yet his father makes him chief), Hilkiah the second, Tebaliah the third, and Zechariah the fourth: all the sons and brothers of Hosah are thirteen. Of these are the divisions of the doorkeepers, even of the chief men, having offices like their brothers, to minister in YHWH’s house. They cast lots, the small as well as the great, according to their fathers’ houses, for every gate. The lot eastward falls to Shelemiah. Then for Zechariah his son, a wise counselor, they cast lots; and his lot comes out northward. To Obed-Edom southward; and to his sons the storehouse. To Shuppim and Hosah westward, by the gate of Shallecheth, at the causeway that goes up, watchman opposite watchman. Eastward are six Levites, northward four a day, southward four a day, and for the storehouse two and two. For Parbar westward, four at the causeway, and two at Parbar. These are the divisions of the doorkeepers; of the sons of the Korahites, and of the sons of Merari.
Levites over Treasuries and Outer Affairs · 26:20–32

Of the Levites, Ahijah is over the treasures of God’s house and over the treasures of the dedicated things. The sons of Ladan, the sons of the Gershonites belonging to Ladan, the heads of the fathers’ households belonging to Ladan the Gershonite: Jehieli. The sons of Jehieli: Zetham, and Joel his brother, over the treasures of YHWH’s house. Of the Amramites, of the Izharites, of the Hebronites, of the Uzzielites: and Shebuel the son of Gershom, the son of Moses, is ruler over the treasures. His brothers: of Eliezer, Rehabiah his son, and Jeshaiah his son, and Joram his son, and Zichri his son, and Shelomoth his son. This Shelomoth and his brothers are over all the treasures of the dedicated things, which David the king, and the heads of the fathers’ households, the captains over thousands and hundreds, and the captains of the army, have dedicated. They dedicate some of the plunder wins in battles to repair YHWH’s house. All that Samuel the seer, and Saul the son of Kish, and Abner the son of Ner, and Joab the son of Zeruiah, have dedicated, whoever has dedicated anything, it is under the hand of Shelomoth, and of his brothers. Of the Izharites, Chenaniah and his sons are for the outward business over Israel, for officers and judges. Of the Hebronites, Hashabiah and his brothers, men of valor, one thousand seven hundred, have the oversight of Israel beyond the Jordan westward, for all the business of YHWH, and for the service of the king. Of the Hebronites is Jerijah the chief, even of the Hebronites, according to their generations by fathers’ households. They are sought for in the fortieth year of the reign of David, and mighty men of valor are found among them at Jazer of Gilead. His brothers, men of valor, are two thousand seven hundred, heads of fathers’ households, whom king David makes overseers over the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of the Manassites, for every matter pertaining to God, and for the affairs of the king.
The Twelve Monthly Military Divisions · 27:1–15

Now the children of Israel after their number, the heads of fathers’ households and the captains of thousands and of hundreds, and their officers who serve the king, in any matter of the divisions which come in and go out month by month throughout all the months of the year—of every division are twenty-four thousand. Over the first division for the first month is Jashobeam the son of Zabdiel: and in his division are twenty-four thousand. He is of the children of Perez, the chief of all the captains of the army for the first month. Over the division of the second month is Dodai the Ahohite, and his division; and Mikloth the ruler: and in his division are twenty-four thousand. The third captain of the army for the third month is Benaiah, the son of Jehoiada the priest, chief: and in his division are twenty-four thousand. This is that Benaiah who are the mighty man of the thirty, and over the thirty: and of his division are Ammizabad his son. The fourth captain for the fourth month is Asahel the brother of Joab, and Zebadiah his son after him: and in his division are twenty-four thousand. The fifth captain for the fifth month is Shamhuth the Izrahite: and in his division are twenty-four thousand. The sixth captain for the sixth month is Ira the son of Ikkesh the Tekoite: and in his division are twenty-four thousand. The seventh captain for the seventh month is Helez the Pelonite, of the children of Ephraim: and in his division are twenty-four thousand. The eighth captain for the eighth month is Sibbecai the Hushathite, of the Zerahites: and in his division are twenty-four thousand. The ninth captain for the ninth month is Abiezer the Anathothite, of the Benjamites: and in his division are twenty-four thousand. The tenth captain for the tenth month is Maharai the Netophathite, of the Zerahites: and in his division are Twenty-four thousand. The eleventh captain for the eleventh month is Benaiah the Pirathonite, of the children of Ephraim: and in his division are twenty-four thousand. The twelfth captain for the twelfth month is Heldai the Netophathite, of Othniel: and in his division are twenty-four thousand.
Tribal Leaders and Royal Officials · 27:16–34

Furthermore over the tribes of Israel: of the Reubenites is Eliezer the son of Zichri the ruler; of the Simeonites, Shephatiah the son of Maacah; of Levi, Hashabiah the son of Kemuel; of Aaron, Zadok; of Judah, Elihu, one of the brothers of David; of Issachar, Omri the son of Michael; of Zebulun, Ishmaiah the son of Obadiah; of Naphtali, Jeremoth the son of Azriel; of the children of Ephraim, Hoshea the son of Azaziah; of the half-tribe of Manasseh, Joel the son of Pedaiah; of the half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead, Iddo the son of Zechariah; of Benjamin, Jaasiel the son of Abner; of Dan, Azarel the son of Jeroham. These are the captains of the tribes of Israel. But David doesn’t take the number of them from twenty years old and under, because YHWH has said he would increase Israel like the stars of the sky. Joab the son of Zeruiah begins to take a census, but doesn’t finish; and wrath comes on Israel for this. The number isn’t put into the account in the chronicles of king David.

Over the king’s treasures are Azmaveth the son of Adiel: and over the treasures in the fields, in the cities, and in the villages, and in the towers, is Jonathan the son of Uzziah; Over those who do the work of the field for tillage of the ground are Ezri the son of Chelub; and over the vineyards are Shimei the Ramathite; and over the increase of the vineyards for the wine cellars are Zabdi the Shiphmite; and over the olive trees and the sycamore trees that are in the lowland are Baal Hanan the Gederite; and over the cellars of oil are Joash; and over the herds that feed in Sharon are Shitrai the Sharonite; and over the herds that are in the valleys is Shaphat the son of Adlai; and over the camels is Obil the Ishmaelite; and over the donkeys is Jehdeiah the Meronothite; and over the flocks is Jaziz the Hagrite. All these are the rulers of the property which is king David’s.

Also Jonathan, David’s uncle, is a counselor, a man of understanding, and a scribe; and Jehiel the son of Hachmoni is with the king’s sons. Ahithophel is the king’s counselor: and Hushai the Archite is the king’s friend. After Ahithophel is Jehoiada the son of Benaiah, and Abiathar. Joab is the captain of the king’s army.
David's Final Assembly · 28:1–8

David assembles all the princes of Israel, the princes of the tribes, the captains of the companies who serve the king by division, the captains of thousands, the captains of hundreds, and the rulers over all the substance and possessions of the king and of his sons, with the officers and the mighty men, even all the mighty men of valor, to Jerusalem. Then David the king stands up on his feet, and says, “Hear me, my brothers, and my people! As for me, it was in my heart to build a house of rest for the ark of YHWH’s covenant, and for the footstool of our God; and I had prepared for the building. But God said to me, ‘You will not build a house for my name, because you are a man of war, and have shed blood.’ However YHWH, the God of Israel, chose me out of all the house of my father to be king over Israel forever. For he has chosen Judah to be prince; and in the house of Judah, the house of my father; and among the sons of my father he took pleasure in me to make me king over all Israel. Of all my sons (for YHWH has given me many sons), he has chosen Solomon my son to sit on the throne of YHWH’s kingdom over Israel. He said to me, ‘Solomon, your son, will build my house and my courts; for I have chosen him to be my son, and I will be his father. I will establish his kingdom forever if he continues to do my commandments and my ordinances, as it is today.’

Now therefore, in the sight of all Israel, YHWH’s assembly, and in the audience of our God, observe and seek out all the commandments of YHWH your God; that you may possess this good land, and leave it for an inheritance to your children after you forever.
David's Charge to Solomon Before All Israel · 28:9–21

You, Solomon my son, know the God of your father, and serve him with a perfect heart and with a willing mind; for YHWH searches all hearts, and understands all the imaginations of the thoughts. If you seek him, he will be found by you; but if you forsake him, he will cast you off forever. Take heed now; for YHWH has chosen you to build a house for the sanctuary. Be strong, and do it.”

Then David gives to Solomon his son the plans for the porch of the temple, for its houses, for its treasuries, for its upper rooms, for its inner rooms, for the place of the mercy seat; and the plans of all that he has by the Spirit, for the courts of YHWH’s house, for all the surrounding rooms, for the treasuries of God’s house, and for the treasuries of the dedicated things; also for the divisions of the priests and the Levites, for all the work of the service of YHWH’s house, and for all the vessels of service in YHWH’s house; of gold by weight for the gold, for all vessels of every kind of service; for all the vessels of silver by weight, for all vessels of every kind of service; by weight also for the lamp stands of gold, and for its lamps, of gold, by weight for every lamp stand and for its lamps; and for the lamp stands of silver, by weight for every lamp stand and for its lamps, according to the use of every lamp stand; and the gold by weight for the tables of show bread, for every table; and silver for the tables of silver; and the forks, the basins, and the cups, of pure gold; and for the golden bowls by weight for every bowl; and for the silver bowls by weight for every bowl; and for the altar of incense refined gold by weight; and gold for the plans for the chariot, and the cherubim that spreads out and cover the ark of YHWH’s covenant. “All this”, says David, “I have been made to understand in writing from YHWH’s hand, even all the works of this pattern.”

David says to Solomon his son, “Be strong and courageous, and do it. Don’t be afraid, nor be dismayed; for YHWH God, even my God, is with you. He will not fail you, nor forsake you, until all the work for the service of YHWH’s house is finished. Look, there are the divisions of the priests and the Levites, for all the service of God’s house. Every willing man who has skill, for any kind of service, will be with you in all kinds of work. Also the captains and all the people will be entirely at your command.”
The Freewill Offerings of the Assembly · 29:1–9

David the king says to all the assembly, “Solomon my son, whom alone God has chosen, is yet young and tender, and the work is great; for the palace is not for man, but for YHWH God. Now I have prepared with all my might for the house of my God the gold for the things of gold, the silver for the things of silver, the brass for the things of brass, iron for the things of iron, and wood for the things of wood; also onyx stones, stones to be set, stones for inlaid work, of various colors, all kinds of precious stones, and marble stones in abundance. In addition, because I have set my affection on the house of my God, since I have a treasure of my own of gold and silver, I give it to the house of my God, over and above all that I have prepared for the holy house, even three thousand talents of gold, of the gold of Ophir, and seven thousand talents of refined silver, with which to overlay the walls of the houses; of gold for the things of gold, and of silver for the things of silver, and for all kinds of work to be made by the hands of artisans. Who then offers willingly to consecrate himself today to YHWH?”

Then the princes of the fathers’ households, and the princes of the tribes of Israel, and the captains of thousands and of hundreds, with the rulers over the king’s work, offer willingly; and they give for the service of God’s house of gold five thousand talents and ten thousand darics, of silver ten thousand talents, of brass eighteen thousand talents, and of iron one hundred thousand talents. People with whom precious stones are found give them to the treasure of YHWH’s house, under the hand of Jehiel the Gershonite. Then the people rejoice, because they offer willingly, because with a perfect heart they offer willingly to YHWH; and David the king also rejoices with great joy.
David's Great Prayer of Thanksgiving · 29:10–20

Therefore David blesses YHWH before all the assembly; and David says, “You are blessed, YHWH, the God of Israel our father, forever and ever. Yours, YHWH, is the greatness, the power, the glory, the victory, and the majesty! For all that is in the heavens and in the earth is yours. Yours is the kingdom, YHWH, and you are exalted as head above all. Both riches and honor come from you, and you rule over all! In your hand is power and might! It is in your hand to make great, and to give strength to all! Now therefore, our God, we thank you, and praise your glorious name. But who am I, and what is my people, that we should be able to offer so willingly as this? For all things come from you, and of your own have we given you. For we are strangers before you, and foreigners, as all our fathers were. Our days on the earth are as a shadow, and there is no remaining. YHWH our God, all this store that we have prepared to build you a house for your holy name comes from your hand, and is all your own. I know also, my God, that you try the heart, and have pleasure in uprightness. As for me, in the uprightness of my heart I have willingly offered all these things. Now I have seen with joy your people, who are present here, offer willingly to you. YHWH, the God of Abraham, of Isaac, and of Israel, our fathers, keep this desire forever in the thoughts of the heart of your people, and prepare their heart for you; and give to Solomon my son a perfect heart, to keep your commandments, your testimonies, and your statutes, and to do all these things, and to build the palace, for which I have made provision.”
Then David says to all the assembly, “Now bless YHWH your God!”
All the assembly blesses YHWH, the God of their fathers, and bows down their heads and prostrates themselves before YHWH and the king.
Solomon Crowned; David's Death · 29:21–30

They sacrifice sacrifices to YHWH, and offer burnt offerings to YHWH, on the next day after that day, even one thousand bulls, one thousand rams, and one thousand lambs, with their drink offerings and sacrifices in abundance for all Israel, and eat and drink before YHWH on that day with great gladness. They make Solomon the son of David king the second time, and anoint him before YHWH to be prince, and Zadok to be priest.

Then Solomon sits on the throne of YHWH as king instead of David his father, and prospered; and all Israel obeys him. All the princes, the mighty men, and also all of the sons of king David submits themselves to Solomon the king. YHWH magnifies Solomon exceedingly in the sight of all Israel, and gives to him such royal majesty as has not been on any king before him in Israel. Now David the son of Jesse reigns over all Israel. The time that he reigns over Israel is forty years; he reigns seven years in Hebron, and he reigns thirty-three years in Jerusalem. He dies at a good old age, full of days, riches, and honor; and Solomon his son reigns in his place. Now the acts of David the king, first and last, look, they are written in the history of Samuel the seer, and in the history of Nathan the prophet, and in the history of Gad the seer, with all his reign and his might, and the times that go over him, and over Israel, and over all the kingdoms of the countries.
Solomon's Sacrifice at Gibeon · 1:1–6

Solomon the son of David is firmly established in his kingdom, and YHWH his God is with him, and makes him exceedingly great. Solomon speaks to all Israel, to the captains of thousands and of hundreds, to the judges, and to every prince in all Israel, the heads of the fathers’ households. So Solomon, and all the assembly with him, go to the high place that is at Gibeon; for God’s Tent of Meeting is there, which YHWH’s servant Moses has made in the wilderness. But David has brought God’s ark up from Kiriath Jearim to the place that David has prepared for it; for he has pitched a tent for it at Jerusalem. Moreover the bronze altar that Bezalel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, has made is there before YHWH’s tabernacle; and Solomon and the assembly are seeking counsel there. Solomon goes up there to the bronze altar before YHWH, which is at the Tent of Meeting, and offers one thousand burnt offerings on it.
The Dream at Gibeon: Solomon's Request · 1:7–13
That night, God appears to Solomon and says to him, “Ask for what you want me to give you.”

Solomon says to God, “You have shown great steadfast love to David my father, and have made me king in his place. Now, YHWH God, let your promise to David my father be established; for you have made me king over a people like the dust of the earth in multitude. Now give me wisdom and knowledge, that I may go out and come in before this people; for who can judge this great people of yours?”

God says to Solomon, “Because this was in your heart, and you have not asked riches, wealth, honor, or the life of those who hate you, nor yet have you asked for long life; but have asked for wisdom and knowledge for yourself, that you may judge my people, over whom I have made you king, therefore wisdom and knowledge is granted to you. I will give you riches, wealth, and honor, such as none of the kings have had who have been before you had, and none after you will have.”
So Solomon comes from the high place that is at Gibeon, from before the Tent of Meeting, to Jerusalem; and he reigns over Israel.
Solomon's Wealth and Power · 1:14–17

Solomon gathers chariots and horsemen. He has one thousand four hundred chariots and twelve thousand horsemen that he places in the chariot cities, and with the king at Jerusalem. The king makes silver and gold to be as common as stones in Jerusalem, and he makes cedars to be as common as the sycamore trees that are in the lowland. The horses which Solomon has are brought out of Egypt and from Kue. The king’s merchants purchase them from Kue. They bring up and brought out of Egypt a chariot for six hundred pieces of silver, and a horse for one hundred fifty. They also export them to the Hittite kings and the Syrian kings.
Solomon Prepares to Build · 2:1–2

Now Solomon decides to build a house for YHWH’s name, and a house for his kingdom. Solomon counts out seventy thousand men to bear burdens, eighty thousand men who are stone cutters in the mountains, and three thousand six hundred to oversee them.
Solomon's Letter to Huram of Tyre · 2:3–10

Solomon sends to Huram the king of Tyre, saying, “As you dealt with David my father, and sent him cedars to build him a house in which to dwell, so deal with me. Look, I am about to build a house for the name of YHWH my God, to dedicate it to him, to burn before him incense of sweet spices, for the continual show bread, and for the burnt offerings morning and evening, on the Sabbaths, on the new moons, and on the set feasts of YHWH our God. This is an ordinance forever to Israel.

“The house which I am building will be great; for our God is greater than all gods. But who is able to build him a house, since heaven and the heaven of heavens can’t contain him? Who am I then, that I should build him a house, except just to burn incense before him?

“Now therefore send me a man skillful to work in gold, in silver, in brass, in iron, and in purple, crimson, and blue, and who knows how to engrave engravings, to be with the skillful men who are with me in Judah and in Jerusalem, whom David my father provided.

“Send me also cedar trees, cypress trees, and algum trees out of Lebanon; for I know that your servants know how to cut timber in Lebanon. Look, my servants will be with your servants, even to prepare me timber in abundance; for the house which I am about to build will be great and wonderful. Look, I will give to your servants, the cutters who cut timber, twenty thousand cors of beaten wheat, twenty thousand baths of barley, twenty thousand baths of wine, and twenty thousand baths of oil.”
Huram's Reply · 2:11–16

Then Huram the king of Tyre answers in writing, which he sends to Solomon, “Because YHWH loves his people, he has made you king over them.” Huram continues, “Blessed be YHWH, the God of Israel, who made heaven and earth, who has given to David the king a wise son, endowed with discretion and understanding, who would build a house for YHWH, and a house for his kingdom. Now I have sent a skillful man, endowed with understanding, of Huram my father’s, the son of a woman of the daughters of Dan; and his father was a man of Tyre, skillful to work in gold, in silver, in brass, in iron, in stone, in timber, and in purple, in blue, in fine linen, and in crimson, also to engrave any kind of engraving and to devise any device; that there may be a place appointed to him with your skillful men, and with the skillful men of my lord David your father.

“Now therefore the wheat the barley, the oil and the wine, which my lord has spoken of, let him send to his servants; and we will cut wood out of Lebanon, as much as you need. We will bring it to you in floats by sea to Joppa; and you will carry it up to Jerusalem.”
The Workforce · 2:17–18

Solomon counts all the foreigners who are in the land of Israel, after the census with which David his father has counted them; and they find one hundred fifty-three thousand six hundred. He sets seventy thousand of them to bear burdens, eighty thousand who are stone cutters in the mountains, and three thousand six hundred overseers to assign the people their work.
The Temple's Location and Foundation · 3:1–2

Then Solomon begins to build YHWH’s house at Jerusalem on Mount Moriah, where YHWH appears to David his father, which he prepares in the place that David has appointed, on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite. He begins to build in the second day of the second month, in the fourth year of his reign.
The Temple's Dimensions and Construction · 3:3–9

Now these are the foundations which Solomon lays for the building of God’s house. The length by cubits after the first measure is sixty cubits, and the width twenty cubits. The porch that is in front, its length, according to the width of the house, is twenty cubits, and the height one hundred twenty; and he overlays it within with pure gold. He makes the larger room with a ceiling of cypress wood, which he overlays with fine gold, and ornaments it with palm trees and chains. He decorates the house with precious stones for beauty. The gold is gold from Parvaim. He also overlays the house, the beams, the thresholds, its walls, and its doors with gold; and engraves cherubim on the walls.

He makes the most holy place. Its length, according to the width of the house, is twenty cubits, and its width twenty cubits; and he overlays it with fine gold, amounting to six hundred talents. The weight of the nails is fifty shekels of gold. He overlays the upper rooms with gold.
The Cherubim and the Veil · 3:10–14

In the most holy place he makes two cherubim by carving; and they overlay them with gold. The wings of the cherubim are twenty cubits long: the wing of the one is five cubits, reaching to the wall of the house; and the other wing is five cubits, reaching to the wing of the other cherub. The wing of the other cherub is five cubits, reaching to the wall of the house; and the other wing is five cubits, joining to the wing of the other cherub. The wings of these cherubim spread themselves out twenty cubits. They stand on their feet, and their faces are toward the house. He makes the veil of blue, purple, crimson, and fine linen, and ornaments it with cherubim.
The Two Pillars · 3:15–17

Also he makes before the house two pillars of thirty-five cubits height, and the capital that is on the top of each of them are five cubits. He makes chains in the inner sanctuary, and puts them on the tops of the pillars; and he makes one hundred pomegranates, and puts them on the chains. He sets up the pillars before the temple, one on the right hand, and the other on the left; and calls the name of that on the right hand Jachin, and the name of that on the left Boaz.
The Bronze Altar and the Sea · 4:1–6

Then he makes an altar of brass, twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and ten cubits high. Also he makes the molten sea of ten cubits from brim to brim. It is round, five cubits high, and thirty cubits in circumference. Under it is the likeness of oxen, which encircles it, for ten cubits, encircling the sea. The oxen are in two rows, cast when it is cast. It stands on twelve oxen, three looking toward the north, and three looking toward the west, and three looking toward the south, and three looking toward the east; and the sea is set on them above, and all their hindquarters are inward. It is a handbreadth thick; and its brim is made like the brim of a cup, like the flower of a lily. It receives and holds three thousand baths. He also makes ten basins, and puts five on the right hand, and five on the left, to wash in them. The things that belong to the burnt offering are washed in them; but the sea is for the priests to wash in.
The Lampstands, Tables, and Courts · 4:7–10

He makes the ten lamp stands of gold according to the ordinance concerning them; and he sets them in the temple, five on the right hand, and five on the left. He makes also ten tables, and places them in the temple, five on the right side, and five on the left. He makes one hundred basins of gold. Furthermore he makes the court of the priests, the great court, and doors for the court, and overlays their doors with brass. He sets the sea on the right side of the house eastward, toward the south.
Huram-abi's Work · 4:11–18
Huram makes the pots, the shovels, and the basins.

So Huram finishes doing the work that he does for king Solomon in God’s house: the two pillars, the bowls, the two capitals which are on the top of the pillars, the two networks to cover the two bowls of the capitals that are on the top of the pillars, and the four hundred pomegranates for the two networks; two rows of pomegranates for each network, to cover the two bowls of the capitals that are on the pillars. He also makes the bases, and he makes the basins on the bases; one sea, and the twelve oxen under it. Huram his father also makes the pots, the shovels, the forks, and all its vessels for king Solomon, for YHWH’s house, of bright brass. The king casts them in the plain of the Jordan, in the clay ground between Succoth and Zeredah. Thus Solomon makes all these vessels in great abundance; for the weight of the brass can not be determined.
The Golden Vessels and the Ark's Final Resting Place · 4:19–22

Solomon makes all the vessels that are in God’s house, the golden altar also, and the tables with the show bread on them; and the lamp stands with their lamps, to burn according to the ordinance before the inner sanctuary, of pure gold; and the flowers, the lamps, and the tongs of gold that are perfect gold; and the snuffers, the basins, the spoons, and the fire pans of pure gold. As for the entry of the house, its inner doors for the most holy place and the doors of the main hall of the temple are of gold.
The Temple Treasuries and the Assembly · 5:1–3

Thus all the work that Solomon does for YHWH’s house is finished. Solomon brings in the things that David his father has dedicated, even the silver, the gold, and all the vessels, and puts them in the treasuries of God’s house.

Then Solomon assembles the elders of Israel, and all the heads of the tribes, the princes of the fathers’ households of the children of Israel, to Jerusalem, to bring up the ark of YHWH’s covenant out of David’s city, which is Zion. So all the men of Israel assemble themselves to the king at the feast, which is in the seventh month.
The Ark Brought into the Temple · 5:4–10

All the elders of Israel come. The Levites take up the ark; and they bring up the ark, the Tent of Meeting, and all the holy vessels that are in the Tent; these the priests the Levites bring up. King Solomon and all the congregation of Israel, who are assembled to him, are before the ark, sacrificing sheep and cattle that can not be counted or counted for multitude. The priests bring in the ark of YHWH’s covenant to its place, into the inner sanctuary of the house, to the most holy place, even under the wings of the cherubim. For the cherubim spread out their wings over the place of the ark, and the cherubim covers the ark and its poles above. The poles are so long that the ends of the poles are seen from the ark in front of the inner sanctuary; but they are not seen outside; and it is there to this day. There is nothing in the ark except the two tablets which Moses puts at Horeb, when YHWH makes a covenant with the children of Israel, when they come out of Egypt.
The Glory of the Lord Fills the Temple · 5:11–14

When the priests have come out of the holy place (for all the priests who are present have sanctified themselves, and don’t keep their divisions; also the Levites who are the singers, all of them, even Asaph, Heman, Jeduthun, and their sons and their brothers, arrayed in fine linen, with cymbals and stringed instruments and harps, stand at the east end of the altar, and with them one hundred twenty priests sounding with trumpets); when the trumpeters and singers are as one, to make one sound to be heard in praising and thanking YHWH; and when they lift up their voice with the trumpets and cymbals and instruments of music, and praise YHWH, saying,
“For he is good;
for his steadfast love endures forever!”
then the house is filled with a cloud, even YHWH’s house, so that the priests can not stand to minister by reason of the cloud; for YHWH’s glory fills God’s house.
Solomon's Declaration · 6:1–2
Then Solomon says, “YHWH has said that he would dwell in the thick darkness. But I have built you a house and home, a place for you to dwell in forever.”
Solomon Blesses the Assembly · 6:3–11
The king turns his face, and blesses all the assembly of Israel: and all the assembly of Israel stands.

He says, “Blessed be YHWH, the God of Israel, who spoke with his mouth to David my father, and has with his hands fulfilled it, saying, ‘Since the day that I brought my people out of the land of Egypt, I chose no city out of all the tribes of Israel to build a house in, that my name might be there and I chose no man to be prince over my people Israel; but now I have chosen Jerusalem, that my name might be there; and I have chosen David to be over my people Israel.’ Now it was in the heart of David my father to build a house for the name of YHWH, the God of Israel. But YHWH said to David my father, ‘Whereas it was in your heart to build a house for my name, you did well that it was in your heart; nevertheless you will not build the house; but your son who will come out of your body, he will build the house for my name.’

“YHWH has performed his word that he spoke; for I have risen up in the place of David my father, and sit on the throne of Israel, as YHWH promised, and have built the house for the name of YHWH, the God of Israel. There I have set the ark, in which is YHWH’s covenant, which he made with the children of Israel.”
Solomon's Great Prayer of Dedication · 6:12–42

He stands before YHWH’s altar in the presence of all the assembly of Israel, and spreads out his hands (for Solomon has made a bronze scaffold, five cubits long, and five cubits wide, and three cubits high, and has set it in the middle of the court; and he stands on it, and kneels down on his knees before all the assembly of Israel, and spreads out his hands toward heaven) and he says, “YHWH, the God of Israel, there is no God like you in heaven or on earth; you who keep covenant and steadfast love with your servants who walk before you with all their heart; who have kept with your servant David my father that which you promised him. Yes, you spoke with your mouth, and have fulfilled it with your hand, as it is today.

“Now therefore, YHWH, the God of Israel, keep with your servant David my father that which you have promised him, saying, ‘There will not fail you a man in my sight to sit on the throne of Israel, if only your children take heed to their way, to walk in my law as you have walked before me.’ Now therefore, YHWH, the God of Israel, let your word be verified, which you spoke to your servant David.

“But will God indeed dwell with men on the earth? Look, heaven and the heaven of heavens can’t contain you; how much less this house which I have built! Yet have respect for the prayer of your servant, and to his supplication, YHWH my God, to listen to the cry and to the prayer which your servant prays before you; that your eyes may be open toward this house day and night, even toward the place where you have said that you would put your name; to listen to the prayer which your servant will pray toward this place. Listen to the petitions of your servant, and of your people Israel, when they pray toward this place. Yes, hear from your dwelling place, even from heaven; and when you hear, forgive.

“If a man sins against his neighbor, and an oath is laid on him to cause him to swear, and he comes and swears before your altar in this house; then hear from heaven, act, and judge your servants, bringing retribution to the wicked, to bring his way on his own head; and justifying the righteous, to give him according to his righteousness.

“If your people Israel are struck down before the enemy because they have sinned against you, and they turn again and confess your name, and pray and make supplication before you in this house; then hear from heaven, and forgive the sin of your people Israel, and bring them again to the land which you gave to them and to their fathers.

“When the sky is shut up, and there is no rain, because they have sinned against you; if they pray toward this place, and confess your name, and turn from their sin, when you afflict them; then hear in heaven, and forgive the sin of your servants of your people Israel, when you teach them the good way in which they should walk; and send rain on your land, which you have given to your people for an inheritance.

“If there is famine in the land, if there is pestilence, if there is blight or mildew, locust or caterpillar; if their enemies besiege them in the land of their cities; whatever plague or whatever sickness there is; whatever prayer and supplication is made by any man, or by all your people Israel, who will each know his own plague and his own sorrow, and will spread out his hands toward this house; then hear from heaven your dwelling place and forgive, and render to every man according to all his ways, whose heart you know (for you, even you only, know the hearts of the children of men) that they may fear you, to walk in your ways, so long as they live in the land which you gave to our fathers.

“Moreover concerning the foreigner, who is not of your people Israel, when he comes from a far country for your great name’s sake, and your mighty hand, and your outstretched arm; when they come and pray toward this house; then hear from heaven, even from your dwelling place, and do according to all that the foreigner calls to you for; that all the peoples of the earth may know your name and fear you, as do your people Israel, and that they may know that this house which I have built is called by your name.

“If your people go out to battle against their enemies, by whatever way you send them, and they pray to you toward this city which you have chosen, and the house which I have built for your name; then hear from heaven their prayer and their supplication, and maintain their cause.

“If they sin against you (for there is no man who doesn’t sin), and you are angry with them, and deliver them to the enemy, so that they carry them away captive to a land far off or near; yet if they come to their senses in the land where they are carried captive, and turn again, and make supplication to you in the land of their captivity, saying, ‘We have sinned, we have done perversely, and have dealt wickedly;’ if they return to you with all their heart and with all their soul in the land of their captivity, where they have carried them captive, and pray toward their land, which you gave to their fathers, and the city which you have chosen, and toward the house which I have built for your name; then hear from heaven, even from your dwelling place, their prayer and their petitions, and maintain their cause, and forgive your people who have sinned against you.
“Now, my God, let, I beg you, your eyes be open, and let your ears be attentive, to the prayer that is made in this place.
“Now therefore arise, YHWH God, into your resting place, you, and the ark of your strength. Let your priests, YHWH God, be clothed with salvation, and let your saints rejoice in goodness.
“YHWH God, don’t turn away the face of your anointed. Remember your acts of steadfast love to David your servant.”
Fire from Heaven · 7:1–3

Now when Solomon has finished praying, fire comes down from heaven and consumes the burnt offering and the sacrifices; and YHWH’s glory fills the house. The priests can not enter into YHWH’s house, because YHWH’s glory filled YHWH’s house. All the children of Israel look on, when the fire comes down, and YHWH’s glory is on the house. They bow themselves with their faces to the ground on the pavement, worship, and give thanks to YHWH, saying,
“For he is good;
for his steadfast love endures for ever.”
The Dedication Feast · 7:4–10

Then the king and all the people offer sacrifices before YHWH. King Solomon offers a sacrifice of twenty-two thousand head of cattle and a hundred twenty thousand sheep. So the king and all the people dedicate God’s house. The priests stand, according to their positions; the Levites also with instruments of music of YHWH, which David the king has made to give thanks to YHWH, when David praises by their ministry, saying “For his steadfast love endures for ever.” The priests sound trumpets before them; and all Israel stands.

Moreover Solomon makes the middle of the court that is before YHWH’s house holy; for there he offers the burnt offerings, and the fat of the peace offerings, because the bronze altar which Solomon has made is not able to receive the burnt offering, the meal offering, and the fat.
So Solomon holds the feast at that time for seven days, and all Israel with him, a very great assembly, from the entrance of Hamath to the brook of Egypt.

On the eighth day, they hold a solemn assembly; for they keep the dedication of the altar seven days, and the feast seven days. On the twenty-third day of the seventh month, he sends the people away to their tents, joyful and glad of heart for the goodness that YHWH has shown to David, and to Solomon, and to Israel his people.
The Lord's Second Appearance to Solomon · 7:11–22
Thus Solomon finishes YHWH’s house and the king’s house; and he successfully completes all that come into Solomon’s heart to make in YHWH’s house and in his own house.
YHWH appears to Solomon by night, and says to him, “I have heard your prayer, and have chosen this place for myself for a house of sacrifice.

“If I shut up the sky so that there is no rain, or if I command the locust to devour the land, or if I send pestilence among my people; if my people, who are called by my name, will humble themselves, pray, seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then I will hear from heaven, will forgive their sin, and will heal their land. Now my eyes will be open my ears attentive to prayer that is made in this place. For now I have chosen and made this house holy, that my name may be there forever; and my eyes and my heart will be there perpetually.

“As for you, if you will walk before me as David your father walked, and do according to all that I have commanded you, and will keep my statutes and my ordinances; then I will establish the throne of your kingdom, according as I covenanted with David your father, saying, ‘There will not fail you a man to be ruler in Israel.’

But if you turn away, and forsake my statutes and my commandments which I have set before you, and will go and serve other gods, and worship them; then I will pluck them up by the roots out of my land which I have given them; and this house, which I have made holy for my name, I will cast out of my sight, and I will make it a proverb and a byword among all peoples. This house, which is so high, everyone who passes by it will be astonished, and will say, ‘Why has YHWH done this to this land and to this house?’ They will answer, ‘Because they abandoned YHWH, the God of their fathers, who brought them out of the land of Egypt, and took other gods, worshiped them, and served them. Therefore he has brought all this evil on them.’”
Solomon's Building Works · 8:1–11
At the end of twenty years, in which Solomon has built YHWH’s house and his own house, Solomon builds the cities which Huram has given to Solomon, and causes the children of Israel to dwell there.

Solomon goes to Hamath Zobah, and prevails against it. He builds Tadmor in the wilderness, and all the storage cities, which he builds in Hamath. Also he builds Beth Horon the upper and Beth Horon the lower, fortified cities, with walls, gates, and bars; and Baalath, and all the storage cities that Solomon has, and all the cities for his chariots, the cities for his horsemen, and all that Solomon desires to build for his pleasure in Jerusalem, in Lebanon, and in all the land of his dominion.

As for all the people who are left of the Hittites, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites, who are not of Israel; of their children who are left after them in the land, whom the children of Israel don’t consume, of them Solomon conscripts forced labor to this day. But of the children of Israel, Solomon makes no servants for his work; but they are men of war, and chief of his captains, and rulers of his chariots and of his horsemen. These are the chief officers of king Solomon, even two-hundred fifty, who rules over the people.

Solomon brings up Pharaoh’s daughter out of David’s city to the house that he has built for her; for he says, “My wife will not dwell in the house of David king of Israel, because the places where YHWH’s ark has come are holy.”
The Temple Services Established · 8:12–16

Then Solomon offers burnt offerings to YHWH on YHWH’s altar, which he has built before the porch, even as the duty of every day required, offering according to the commandment of Moses, on the Sabbaths, on the new moons, and on the set feasts, three times per year, during the feast of unleavened bread, during the feast of weeks, and during the feast of tents.

He appoints, according to the ordinance of David his father, the divisions of the priests to their service, and the Levites to their offices, to praise and to minister before the priests, as the duty of every day required; the doorkeepers also by their divisions at every gate, for David the man of God has so commanded. They don’t depart from the commandment of the king to the priests and Levites concerning any matter, or concerning the treasures.
Now all the work of Solomon is prepared from the day of the foundation of YHWH’s house until it is finished. So YHWH’s house is completed.
Solomon's Fleet and Ophir Gold · 8:17–18

Then Solomon goes to Ezion Geber and to Eloth, on the seashore in the land of Edom. Huram sends him ships and servants who have knowledge of the sea by the hands of his servants; and they come with the servants of Solomon to Ophir, and bring from there four hundred fifty talents of gold, and bring them to king Solomon.
The Queen of Sheba Visits Solomon · 9:1–12

When the queen of Sheba hears of the fame of Solomon, she comes to test Solomon with hard questions at Jerusalem, with a very great caravan, including camels that bear spices, gold in abundance, and precious stones. When she has come to Solomon, she talks with him about all that are in her heart. Solomon answers all her questions. There isn’t anything hidden from Solomon which he doesn’t tell her. When the queen of Sheba has seen the wisdom of Solomon, the house that he has built, the food of his table, the seating of his servants, the attendance of his ministers, their clothing, his cup bearers also, their clothing, and his ascent by which he goes up to YHWH’s house; there is no more spirit in her.

She says to the king, “It was a true report that I heard in my own land of your acts and of your wisdom. However I didn’t believe their words until I came, and my eyes had seen it; and look, the half of the greatness of your wisdom was not told me. You exceed the fame that I heard! Happy are your men, and happy are these your servants, who stand continually before you, and hear your wisdom. Blessed be YHWH your God, who delighted in you, to set you on his throne, to be king for YHWH your God; because your God loved Israel, to establish them forever. Therefore made he you king over them, to do justice and righteousness.”

She gives the king one hundred and twenty talents of gold, spices in great abundance, and precious stones. There is never before such spice as the queen of Sheba gives to king Solomon. The servants of Huram and the servants of Solomon, who brings gold from Ophir, also bring algum trees and precious stones. The king uses algum tree wood to make terraces for YHWH’s house and for the king’s house, and harps and stringed instruments for the singers. There are none like these seen before in the land of Judah. King Solomon gives to the queen of Sheba all her desire, whatever she asks, besides that which she has brought to the king. So she turns, and goes to her own land, she and her servants.
Solomon's Incomparable Wealth · 9:13–28

Now the weight of gold that comes to Solomon in one year is six hundred sixty-six talents of gold, besides that which the traders and merchants brought. All the kings of Arabia and the governors of the country bring gold and silver to Solomon. King Solomon makes two hundred bucklers of beaten gold. Six hundred shekels of beaten gold go to one buckler. He makes three hundred shields of beaten gold. Three hundred shekels of gold go to one shield. The king puts them in the House of the Forest of Lebanon. Moreover the king makes a great throne of ivory, and overlays it with pure gold. There are six steps to the throne, with a footstool of gold, which are fastened to the throne, and armrests on either side by the place of the seat, and two lions standing beside the armrests. Twelve lions stand there on the one side and on the other on the six steps. There is nothing like it makes in any other kingdom. All king Solomon’s drinking vessels are of gold, and all the vessels of the House of the Forest of Lebanon are of pure gold. Silver is not considered valuable in the days of Solomon. For the king has ships that go to Tarshish with Huram’s servants. Once every three years, the ships of Tarshish come bringing gold, silver, ivory, apes, and peacocks.

So king Solomon exceeds all the kings of the earth in riches and wisdom. All the kings of the earth seek the presence of Solomon, to hear his wisdom, which God has put in his heart. They each bring tribute, vessels of silver, vessels of gold, clothing, armor, spices, horses, and mules every year. Solomon has four thousand stalls for horses and chariots, and twelve thousand horsemen, that he stations in the chariot cities, and with the king at Jerusalem. He rules over all the kings from the River even to the land of the Philistines, and to the border of Egypt. The king makes silver as common in Jerusalem as stones, and he makes cedars to be as abundant as the sycamore trees that are in the lowland. They bring horses for Solomon out of Egypt and out of all lands.
Solomon's Death · 9:29–31

Now the rest of the acts of Solomon, first and last, aren’t they write in the history of Nathan the prophet, and in the prophecy of Ahijah the Shilonite, and in the visions of Iddo the seer concerning Jeroboam the son of Nebat? Solomon reigns in Jerusalem over all Israel forty years. Solomon sleeps with his fathers, and he is buried in his father David’s city: and Rehoboam his son reigns in his place.
Rehoboam Goes to Shechem · 10:1–5

Rehoboam goes to Shechem; for all Israel has come to Shechem to make him king. When Jeroboam the son of Nebat hears of it (for he is in Egypt, where he has fled from the presence of king Solomon), Jeroboam returns out of Egypt. They send and call him; and Jeroboam and all Israel come, and they speak to Rehoboam, saying, “Your father made our yoke grievous: now therefore make the grievous service of your father, and his heavy yoke which he put on us, lighter, and we will serve you.”
He says to them, “Come again to me after three days.”
So the people depart.
Rehoboam Rejects the Elders' Counsel · 10:6–15
King Rehoboam takes counsel with the old men, who have stood before Solomon his father while he yet lives, saying, “What counsel do you give me about how to answer these people?”
They speak to him, saying, “If you are kind to these people, please them, and speak good words to them, then they will be your servants forever.”

But he abandons the counsel of the old men which they have given him, and takes counsel with the young men who have grown up with him, who stand before him. He says to them, “What counsel do you give, that we may give an answer to these people, who have spoken to me, saying, ‘Make the yoke that your father put on us lighter?’”

The young men who have grown up with him speak to him, saying, “Thus you will tell the people who spoke to you, saying, ‘Your father made our yoke heavy, but make it lighter on us;’ thus you will say to them, ‘My little finger is thicker than my father’s waist. Now whereas my father burdened you with a heavy yoke, I will add to your yoke. My father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.’”

So Jeroboam and all the people come to Rehoboam the third day, as the king asks, saying, “Come to me again the third day.” The king answers them roughly; and king Rehoboam abandons the counsel of the old men, and speaks to them after the counsel of the young men, saying, “My father made your yoke heavy, but I will add to it. My father chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.”
So the king doesn’t listen to the people; for it is brought about by God, that YHWH might establish his word, which he speaks by Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam the son of Nebat.
The Kingdom Divides · 10:16–19

When all Israel sees that the king doesn’t listen to them, the people answer the king, saying, “What portion have we in David? We don’t have an inheritance in the son of Jesse! Every man to your tents, Israel! Now see to your own house, David.” So all Israel departs to their tents.

But as for the children of Israel who live in the cities of Judah, Rehoboam reigns over them. Then king Rehoboam sends Hadoram, who is over the men subject to forced labor; and the children of Israel stone him to death with stones. King Rehoboam hurries to get himself up to his chariot, to flee to Jerusalem. So Israel rebels against David’s house to this day.
The Word of Shemaiah · 11:1–4

When Rehoboam has come to Jerusalem, he assembles the house of Judah and Benjamin, one hundred eighty thousand chosen men who are warriors, to fight against Israel, to bring the kingdom again to Rehoboam. But YHWH’s word comes to Shemaiah the man of God, saying, “Speak to Rehoboam the son of Solomon, king of Judah, and to all Israel in Judah and Benjamin, saying, ‘YHWH says, “You will not go up, nor fight against your brothers! Every man return to his house; for this thing is of me.”’” So they listen to YHWH’s words, and return from going against Jeroboam.
Rehoboam Strengthens His Kingdom · 11:5–12

Rehoboam lives in Jerusalem, and builds cities for defense in Judah. He builds Bethlehem, Etam, Tekoa, Beth Zur, Soco, Adullam, Gath, Mareshah, Ziph, Adoraim, Lachish, Azekah, Zorah, Aijalon, and Hebron, which are fortified cities in Judah and in Benjamin. He fortifies the strongholds, and puts captains in them, and stores of food, oil and wine. He puts shields and spears in every city, and makes them exceedingly strong. Judah and Benjamin belong to him.
Priests and Levites Come to Jerusalem · 11:13–17

The priests and the Levites who are in all Israel stand with him out of all their territory. For the Levites leave their suburbs and their possession, and come to Judah and Jerusalem; for Jeroboam and his sons cast them off, that they should not execute the priest’s office to YHWH. He himself appoints priests for the high places, for the male goats, and for the calves which he has made. After them, out of all the tribes of Israel, those who set their hearts to seek YHWH, the God of Israel, come to Jerusalem to sacrifice to YHWH, the God of their fathers. So they strengthen the kingdom of Judah, and make Rehoboam the son of Solomon strong for three years; for they walk three years in the way of David and Solomon.
Rehoboam's Family · 11:18–23

Rehoboam takes a wife for himself, Mahalath the daughter of Jerimoth the son of David and of Abihail the daughter of Eliab the son of Jesse. She bears him sons: Jeush, Shemariah, and Zaham. After her, he takes Maacah the daughter of Absalom; and she bears him Abijah, Attai, Ziza, and Shelomith. Rehoboam loves Maacah the daughter of Absalom above all his wives and his concubines; for he takes eighteen wives and sixty concubines, and becomes the father of twenty-eight sons and sixty daughters. Rehoboam appoints Abijah the son of Maacah to be chief, the prince among his brothers; for he intends to make him king. He deals wisely, and dispersed of all his sons throughout all the lands of Judah and Benjamin, to every fortified city. He gives them food in abundance and he seeks many wives for them.
Rehoboam Abandons the Law; Shishak Invades · 12:1–12

When the kingdom of Rehoboam is established and he is strong, he abandons YHWH’s law, and all Israel with him. In the fifth year of king Rehoboam, Shishak king of Egypt comes up against Jerusalem, because they have trespassed against YHWH, with twelve hundred chariots, and sixty thousand horsemen. The people are without number who comes with him out of Egypt: the Lubim, the Sukkiim, and the Ethiopians. He takes the fortified cities which belong to Judah, and comes to Jerusalem. Now Shemaiah the prophet comes to Rehoboam, and to the princes of Judah, who are gathered together to Jerusalem because of Shishak, and says to them, “YHWH says, ‘You have forsaken me, therefore I have also left you in the hand of Shishak.’”
Then the princes of Israel and the king humble themselves; and they say, “YHWH is righteous.”

When YHWH sees that they humble themselves, YHWH’s word comes to Shemaiah, saying, “They have humbled themselves. I will not destroy them; but I will grant them some deliverance, and my wrath won’t be poured out on Jerusalem by the hand of Shishak. Nevertheless they will be his servants, that they may know my service, and the service of the kingdoms of the countries.”

So Shishak king of Egypt comes up against Jerusalem and takes away the treasures of YHWH’s house and the treasures of the king’s house. He takes it all away. He also takes away the shields of gold which Solomon has made. King Rehoboam makes shields of brass in their place, and commits them to the hands of the captains of the guard, who keep the door of the king’s house. As often as the king enters into YHWH’s house, the guard comes and bears them, then brings them back into the guard room. When he humbles himself, YHWH’s wrath turns from him, so as not to destroy him altogether. Moreover, there are good things found in Judah.
Rehoboam's Death · 12:13–16

So king Rehoboam strengthens himself in Jerusalem and reigns; for Rehoboam is forty-one years old when he begins to reign, and he reigns seventeen years in Jerusalem, the city which YHWH has chosen out of all the tribes of Israel to put his name there. His mother’s name is Naamah the Ammonitess. He does that which is evil, because he doesn’t set his heart to seek YHWH.

Now the acts of Rehoboam, first and last, aren’t they write in the histories of Shemaiah the prophet and of Iddo the seer, in the genealogies? There are wars between Rehoboam and Jeroboam continually. Rehoboam sleeps with his fathers, and is buried in David’s city; and Abijah his son reigns in his place.
