Abijah's War with Jeroboam · 13:1–3

In the eighteenth year of king Jeroboam, Abijah begins to reign over Judah. He reigns three years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name is Micaiah the daughter of Uriel of Gibeah. There is war between Abijah and Jeroboam. Abijah joins battle with an army of valiant men of war, even four hundred thousand chosen men; and Jeroboam sets the battle in array against him with eight hundred thousand chosen men, who are mighty men of valor.
Abijah's Speech on Mount Zemaraim · 13:4–12

Abijah stands up on Mount Zemaraim, which is in the hill country of Ephraim, and says, “Hear me, Jeroboam and all Israel: Ought you not to know that YHWH, the God of Israel, gave the kingdom over Israel to David forever, even to him and to his sons by a covenant of salt? Yet Jeroboam the son of Nebat, the servant of Solomon the son of David, rose up, and rebelled against his lord. Worthless men were gathered to him, wicked fellows who strengthened themselves against Rehoboam the son of Solomon, when Rehoboam was young and tender hearted, and could not withstand them.

“Now you intend to withstand the kingdom of YHWH in the hand of the sons of David. You are a great multitude, and the golden calves which Jeroboam made you for gods are with you. Haven’t you driven out the priests of YHWH, the sons of Aaron, and the Levites, and made priests for yourselves according to the ways of the peoples of other lands? Whoever comes to consecrate himself with a young bull and seven rams may be a priest of those who are no gods.

“But as for us, YHWH is our God, and we have not forsaken him. We have priests serving YHWH, the sons of Aaron, and the Levites in their work; and they burn to YHWH every morning and every evening burnt offerings and sweet incense. They also set the show bread in order on the pure table; and the lamp stand of gold with its lamps, to burn every evening; for we keep the instruction of YHWH our God, but you have forsaken him. Look, God is with us at our head, and his priests with the trumpets of alarm to sound an alarm against you. Children of Israel, don’t fight against YHWH, the God of your fathers; for you will not prosper.”
Judah's Victory · 13:13–20

But Jeroboam causes an ambush to come about behind them; so they are before Judah, and the ambush is behind them. When Judah looks back, look, the battle is before and behind them; and they cry to YHWH, and the priests sound with the trumpets. Then the men of Judah give a shout. As the men of Judah shout, God strikes Jeroboam and all Israel before Abijah and Judah. The children of Israel flee before Judah, and God delivers them into their hand. Abijah and his people kill them with a great slaughter, so five hundred thousand chosen men of Israel fall down slain. Thus the children of Israel are brought under at that time, and the children of Judah prevail, because they rely on YHWH, the God of their fathers. Abijah pursues Jeroboam, and takes cities from him, Bethel with its villages, Jeshanah with its villages, and Ephron with its villages.
Jeroboam doesn’t recover strength again in the days of Abijah. YHWH strikes him, and he dies.
Abijah's Death · 13:21–22

But Abijah grows mighty, and takes for himself fourteen wives, and becomes the father of twenty-two sons, and sixteen daughters. The rest of the acts of Abijah, his ways, and his sayings are written in the commentary of the prophet Iddo.
Asa's Reforms and Peace · 14:1–8

So Abijah sleeps with his fathers, and they bury him in David’s city; and Asa his son reigns in his place. In his days, the land is quiet ten years. Asa does that which is good and right in YHWH his God’s eyes; for he takes away the foreign altars and the high places, breaks down the pillars, cuts down the Asherah poles, and commands Judah to seek YHWH, the God of their fathers, and to obey his law and command. Also he takes away out of all the cities of Judah the high places and the sun images; and the kingdom is quiet before him. He builds fortified cities in Judah; for the land is quiet, and he has no war in those years, because YHWH has given him rest. For he says to Judah, “Let us build these cities, and make walls around them, with towers, gates, and bars. The land is yet before us, because we have sought YHWH our God. We have sought him, and he has given us rest on every side.” So they build and prospered.

Asa has an army of three hundred thousand out of Judah who bears bucklers and spears, and two hundred eighty thousand out of Benjamin who bears shields and draws bows. All these are mighty men of valor.
Victory over the Cushites · 14:9–15

Zerah the Ethiopian comes out against them with an army of a million troops and three hundred chariots, and he comes to Mareshah. Then Asa goes out to meet him, and they set the battle in array in the valley of Zephathah at Mareshah. Asa cries to YHWH his God, and says, “YHWH, there is no one besides you to help, between the mighty and him who has no strength. Help us, YHWH our God; for we rely on you, and in your name are we come against this multitude. YHWH, you are our God. Don’t let man prevail against you.”

So YHWH strikes the Ethiopians before Asa and before Judah; and the Ethiopians flee. Asa and the people who are with him pursue them to Gerar: and so many of the Ethiopians fall that they can not recover themselves; for they are destroyed before YHWH and before his army; and they carry away very much booty. They strike all the cities around Gerar; for the fear of YHWH come on them, and they plunder all the cities; for there is much plunder in them. They also strike the tents of livestock, and carry away sheep in abundance, and camels, and return to Jerusalem.
The Prophecy of Azariah · 15:1–7

The Spirit of God comes on Azariah the son of Oded: and he goes out to meet Asa, and says to him, “Hear me, Asa, and all Judah and Benjamin! YHWH is with you, while you are with him; and if you seek him, he will be found by you; but if you forsake him, he will forsake you. Now for a long time Israel was without the true God, without a teaching priest, and without law. But when in their distress they turned to YHWH, the God of Israel, and sought him, he was found by them. In those times there was no peace to him who went out, nor to him who came in; but great troubles were on all the inhabitants of the lands. They were broken in pieces, nation against nation, and city against city; for God troubled them with all adversity. But you be strong, and don’t let your hands be slack; for your work will be rewarded.”
Asa's Great Reformation · 15:8–15

When Asa hears these words, and the prophecy of Oded the prophet, he takes courage, and puts away the abominations out of all the land of Judah and Benjamin, and out of the cities which he has taken from the hill country of Ephraim; and he renews YHWH’s altar that is before YHWH’s porch. He gathers all Judah and Benjamin, and those who live with them out of Ephraim, Manasseh, and Simeon; for they come to him out of Israel in abundance when they see that YHWH his God is with him. So they gather themselves together at Jerusalem in the third month, in the fifteenth year of Asa’s reign. They sacrifice to YHWH in that day, of the plunder which they have brought, seven hundred head of cattle and seven thousand sheep. They enter into the covenant to seek YHWH, the God of their fathers, with all their heart and with all their soul; and that whoever would not seek YHWH, the God of Israel, should be put to death, whether small or great, whether man or woman. They swear to YHWH with a loud voice, with shouting, with trumpets, and with cornets. All Judah rejoices at the oath, for they have sworn with all their heart, and seek him with their whole desire; and he is found by them. Then YHWH gives them rest all around.
Asa Deposes His Mother · 15:16–19

Also Maacah, the mother of Asa the king, he removes from being queen, because she has made an abominable image for an Asherah; so Asa cuts down her image, grinds it into dust, and burns it at the brook Kidron. But the high places are not taken away out of Israel; nevertheless the heart of Asa is perfect all his days. He brings the things that his father has dedicated, and that he himself has dedicated, silver, gold, and vessels into God’s house. There is no more war to the thirty-fifth year of Asa’s reign.
Asa's Treaty with Aram and the Prophet Hanani · 16:1–10

In the thirty-sixth year of Asa’s reign, Baasha king of Israel goes up against Judah, and builds Ramah, that he might not allow anyone to go out or come in to Asa king of Judah. Then Asa brings out silver and gold out of the treasures of YHWH’s house and of the king’s house, and sends to Ben Hadad king of Syria, who lives at Damascus, saying, “Let there be a treaty between me and you, as there was between my father and your father. Look, I have sent you silver and gold. Go, break your treaty with Baasha king of Israel, that he may depart from me.”

Ben Hadad listens to king Asa, and sends the captains of his armies against the cities of Israel; and they strike Ijon, Dan, Abel Maim, and all the storage cities of Naphtali. When Baasha hears of it, he stops building Ramah, and let his work cease. Then Asa the king takes all Judah, and they carry away the stones of Rama, and its timber, with which Baasha has built; and he builds Geba and Mizpah with them.

At that time Hanani the seer comes to Asa king of Judah, and says to him, “Because you have relied on the king of Syria, and have not relied on YHWH your God, therefore the army of the king of Syria has escaped out of your hand. Weren’t the Ethiopians and the Lubim a huge army, with chariots and horsemen exceeding many? Yet, because you relied on YHWH, he delivered them into your hand. For YHWH’s eyes run back and forth throughout the whole earth, to show himself strong in the behalf of them whose heart is perfect toward him. You have done foolishly in this; for from now on you will have wars.”
Then Asa is angry with the seer, and puts him in the prison; for he is in a rage with him because of this thing. Asa oppresses some of the people at the same time.
Asa's Disease and Death · 16:11–14

Look, the acts of Asa, first and last, look, they are written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel. In the thirty-ninth year of his reign, Asa is diseased in his feet. His disease is exceedingly great: yet in his disease he doesn’t seek YHWH, but just the physicians. Asa sleeps with his fathers, and dies in the forty-first year of his reign. They bury him in his own tomb, which he has dug out for himself in David’s city, and lay him in the bed which is filled with sweet odors and various kinds of spices prepared by the perfumers’ art; and they make a very great fire for him.
Jehoshaphat's Faithful Reign · 17:1–6

Jehoshaphat his son reigns in his place, and strengthens himself against Israel. He places forces in all the fortified cities of Judah, and sets garrisons in the land of Judah, and in the cities of Ephraim, which Asa his father has taken. YHWH is with Jehoshaphat, because he walks in the first ways of his father David, and doesn’t seek the Baals, but seeks to the God of his father, and walks in his commandments, and not in the ways of Israel. Therefore YHWH establishes the kingdom in his hand. All Judah brings tribute to Jehoshaphat, and he has riches and honor in abundance. His heart is lifted up in the ways of YHWH. Furthermore, he takes away the high places and the Asherah poles out of Judah.
The Teaching Mission · 17:7–9

Also in the third year of his reign he sends his princes, even Ben Hail, Obadiah, Zechariah, Nethanel, and Micaiah, to teach in the cities of Judah; and with them the Levites, even Shemaiah, Nethaniah, Zebadiah, Asahel, Shemiramoth, Jehonathan, Adonijah, Tobijah, and Tobadonijah, the Levites; and with them Elishama and Jehoram, the priests. They teach in Judah, having the book of YHWH’s law with them. They go about throughout all the cities of Judah and teach among the people.
Jehoshaphat's Greatness · 17:10–19

The fear of YHWH falls on all the kingdoms of the lands that are around Judah, so that they make no war against Jehoshaphat. Some of the Philistines brings Jehoshaphat presents and silver for tribute. The Arabians also bring him flocks, seven thousand seven hundred rams, and seven thousand seven hundred male goats. Jehoshaphat grows great exceedingly; and he builds fortresses and store cities in Judah. He has many works in the cities of Judah; and men of war, mighty men of valor, in Jerusalem. This is the numbering of them according to their fathers’ houses: From Judah, the captains of thousands: Adnah the captain, and with him three hundred thousand mighty men of valor; and next to him Jehohanan the captain, and with him two hundred eighty thousand; and next to him Amasiah the son of Zichri, who willingly offers himself to YHWH, and with him two hundred thousand mighty men of valor. From Benjamin: Eliada, a mighty man of valor, and with him two hundred thousand armed with bow and shield; and next to him Jehozabad, and with him one hundred eighty thousand ready and prepared for war. These are those who wait on the king, besides those whom the king puts in the fortified cities throughout all Judah.
Jehoshaphat Allies with Ahab · 18:1–3

Now Jehoshaphat has riches and honor in abundance; and he allies himself with Ahab. After some years, he goes down to Ahab to Samaria. Ahab kills sheep and cattle for him in abundance, and for the people who are with him, and moves him to go up with him to Ramoth Gilead. Ahab king of Israel says to Jehoshaphat king of Judah, “Will you go with me to Ramoth Gilead?”
He answers him, “I am as you are, and my people as your people. We will be with you in the war.”
The Prophets of Ahab and Micaiah · 18:4–27
Jehoshaphat says to the king of Israel, “Please inquire first for YHWH’s word.”
Then the king of Israel gathers the prophets together, four hundred men, and says to them, “Should we go to Ramoth Gilead to battle, or should I forbear?”
They say, “Go up; for God will deliver it into the hand of the king.”
But Jehoshaphat says, “Isn’t there here a prophet of YHWH besides, that we may inquire of him?”

The king of Israel says to Jehoshaphat, “There is yet one man by whom we may inquire of YHWH; but I hate him, for he never prophesies good concerning me, but always evil. He is Micaiah the son of Imla.”
Jehoshaphat says, “Don’t let the king say so.”
Then the king of Israel calls an officer, and says, “Get Micaiah the son of Imla quickly.”

Now the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat the king of Judah each sit on his throne, arrayed in their robes, and they are sitting in an open place at the entrance of the gate of Samaria; and all the prophets are prophesying before them. Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah makes himself horns of iron and says, “YHWH says, ‘With these you will push the Syrians, until they are consumed.’”
All the prophets prophesy so, saying, “Go up to Ramoth Gilead, and prosper; for YHWH will deliver it into the hand of the king.”

The messenger who goes to call Micaiah speaks to him, saying, “Look, the words of the prophets declare good to the king with one mouth. Let your word therefore, please be like one of theirs, and speak good.”
Micaiah says, “As YHWH lives, what my God says, that will I speak.”
When he has come to the king, the king says to him, “Micaiah, should we go to Ramoth Gilead to battle, or should I forbear?”
He says, “Go up, and prosper. They will be delivered into your hand.”
The king says to him, “How many times should I adjure you that you speak to me nothing but the truth in YHWH’s name?”
He says, “I saw all Israel scattered on the mountains, as sheep that have no shepherd. YHWH said, ‘These have no master. Let them each return to his house in peace.’”
The king of Israel says to Jehoshaphat, “Didn’t I tell you that he would not prophesy good concerning me, but evil?”

Micaiah says, “Therefore hear YHWH’s word: I saw YHWH sitting on his throne, and all the army of heaven standing on his right hand and on his left. YHWH said, ‘Who will entice Ahab king of Israel, that he may go up and fall at Ramoth Gilead?’ One spoke saying in this way, and another saying in that way. A spirit came out, stood before YHWH, and said, ‘I will entice him.’
“YHWH said to him, ‘How?’
“He said, ‘I will go, and will be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets.’
“He said, ‘You will entice him, and will prevail also. Go and do so.’
“Now therefore, look, YHWH has put a lying spirit in the mouth of these your prophets; and YHWH has spoken evil concerning you.”
Then Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah comes near, and strikes Micaiah on the cheek, and says, “Which way did YHWH’s Spirit go from me to speak to you?”
Micaiah says, “Look, you will see on that day, when you go into an inner room to hide yourself.”

The king of Israel says, “Take Micaiah, and carry him back to Amon the governor of the city, and to Joash the king’s son; and say, ‘Thus says the king, “Put this fellow in the prison, and feed him with bread of affliction and with water of affliction, until I return in peace.”’”
Micaiah says, “If you return at all in peace, YHWH has not spoken by me.” He says, “Listen, you people, all of you!”
The Battle of Ramoth-gilead · 18:28–34

So the king of Israel and Jehoshaphat the king of Judah go up to Ramoth Gilead. The king of Israel says to Jehoshaphat, “I will disguise myself, and go into the battle; but you put on your robes.” So the king of Israel disguises himself; and they go into the battle. Now the king of Syria has commanded the captains of his chariots, saying, “Don’t fight with small nor great, except only with the king of Israel.”

When the captains of the chariots see Jehoshaphat, they say, “It is the king of Israel!” Therefore they turn around to fight against him. But Jehoshaphat cries out, and YHWH helps him; and God moves them to depart from him. When the captains of the chariots see that it is not the king of Israel, they turn back from pursuing him. A certain man draws his bow at random, and strikes the king of Israel between the joints of the armor. Therefore he says to the driver of the chariot, “Turn your hand, and carry me out of the army; for I am severely wounded.” The battle increases that day. However the king of Israel props himself up in his chariot against the Syrians until the evening; and at about sunset, he dies.
The Prophet Jehu Rebukes Jehoshaphat · 19:1–3

Jehoshaphat the king of Judah returns to his house in peace to Jerusalem. Jehu the son of Hanani the seer goes out to meet him, and says to king Jehoshaphat, “Should you help the wicked, and love those who hate YHWH? Because of this, wrath is on you from before YHWH. Nevertheless there are good things found in you, in that you have put away the Asheroth out of the land, and have set your heart to seek God.”
Jehoshaphat Appoints Judges · 19:4–11

Jehoshaphat lives at Jerusalem; and he goes out again among the people from Beersheba to the hill country of Ephraim, and brings them back to YHWH, the God of their fathers. He sets judges in the land throughout all the fortified cities of Judah, city by city, and says to the judges, “Consider what you do, for you don’t judge for man, but for YHWH; and he is with you in the judgment. Now therefore let the fear of YHWH be on you. Take heed and do it; for there is no iniquity with YHWH our God, nor respect of persons, nor taking of bribes.”

Moreover in Jerusalem Jehoshaphat appoints Levites and priests, and of the heads of the fathers’ households of Israel, for the judgment of YHWH, and for controversies. They return to Jerusalem. He commands them, saying, “You will do this in the fear of YHWH, faithfully, and with a perfect heart. Whenever any controversy comes to you from your brothers who dwell in their cities, between blood and blood, between law and commandment, statutes and ordinances, you must warn them, that they not be guilty towards YHWH, and so wrath come on you and on your brothers. Do this, and you will not be guilty. Look, Amariah the chief priest is over you in all matters of YHWH; and Zebadiah the son of Ishmael, the ruler of the house of Judah, in all the king’s matters. Also the Levites will be officers before you. Deal courageously, and may YHWH be with the good.”
The Vast Army Approaches · 20:1–4

After this, the children of Moab, the children of Ammon, and with them some of the Ammonites, come against Jehoshaphat to battle. Then some comes who tells Jehoshaphat, saying, “A great multitude is coming against you from beyond the sea from Syria. Look, they are in Hazazon Tamar” (that is, En Gedi). Jehoshaphat is alarmed, and sets himself to seek to YHWH. He proclaims a fast throughout all Judah. Judah gathers themselves together to seek help from YHWH. They come out of all the cities of Judah to seek YHWH.
Jehoshaphat's Prayer · 20:5–13

Jehoshaphat stands in the assembly of Judah and Jerusalem, in YHWH’s house, before the new court; and he says, “YHWH, the God of our fathers, aren’t you God in heaven? Aren’t you ruler over all the kingdoms of the nations? Power and might are in your hand, so that no one is able to withstand you. Didn’t you, our God, drive out the inhabitants of this land before your people Israel, and give it to the offspring of Abraham your friend forever? They lived in it, and have built you a sanctuary in it for your name, saying, ‘If evil comes on us—the sword, judgment, pestilence, or famine—we will stand before this house, and before you (for your name is in this house), and cry to you in our affliction, and you will hear and save.’ Now, look, the children of Ammon and Moab and Mount Seir, whom you would not let Israel invade when they came out of the land of Egypt, but they turned away from them, and didn’t destroy them; look, how they reward us, to come to cast us out of your possession, which you have given us to inherit. Our God, will you not judge them? For we have no might against this great company that comes against us. We don’t know what to do, but our eyes are on you.”
All Judah stands before YHWH, with their little ones, their wives, and their children.
The Spirit Speaks Through Jahaziel · 20:14–19

Then YHWH’s Spirit comes on Jahaziel the son of Zechariah, the son of Benaiah, the son of Jeiel, the son of Mattaniah, the Levite, of the sons of Asaph, in the middle of the assembly; and he says, “Listen, all Judah, and you inhabitants of Jerusalem, and you, king Jehoshaphat. YHWH says to you, ‘Don’t be afraid, and don’t be dismayed because of this great multitude; for the battle is not yours, but God’s. Tomorrow, go down against them. Look, they are coming up by the ascent of Ziz. You will find them at the end of the valley, before the wilderness of Jeruel. You will not need to fight this battle. Set yourselves, stand still, and see the salvation of YHWH with you, O Judah and Jerusalem. Don’t be afraid, nor be dismayed. Go out against them tomorrow, for YHWH is with you.’”

Jehoshaphat bows his head with his face to the ground; and all Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem fall down before YHWH, worshiping YHWH. The Levites, of the children of the Kohathites and of the children of the Korahites, stand up to praise YHWH, the God of Israel, with an exceeding loud voice.
The Battle Won by Praise · 20:20–30

They rise early in the morning, and go out into the wilderness of Tekoa. As they go out, Jehoshaphat stands and says, “Listen to me, Judah, and you inhabitants of Jerusalem! Believe in YHWH your God, so you will be established! Believe his prophets, so you will prosper.”

When he has taken counsel with the people, he appoints those who are to sing to YHWH, and give praise in holy array, as they go out before the army, and say, “Give thanks to YHWH; for his steadfast love endures forever.” When they begin to sing and to praise, YHWH sets ambushers against the children of Ammon, Moab, and Mount Seir, who has come against Judah; and they are struck. For the children of Ammon and Moab stand up against the inhabitants of Mount Seir to utterly kill and destroy them: and when they have finished the inhabitants of Seir, everyone helps to destroy another.

When Judah comes to the place overlooking the wilderness, they look at the multitude; and look, they are dead bodies fallen to the earth, and there are none who escapes. When Jehoshaphat and his people come to take their plunder, they find among them in abundance both riches and dead bodies, and precious jewels, which they strip off for themselves, more than they can carry away. They take plunder for three days, it is so much. On the fourth day, they assemble themselves in Beracah Valley, for there they bless YHWH. Therefore the name of that place is called “Beracah Valley” to this day. Then they return, every man of Judah and Jerusalem, with Jehoshaphat in front of them, to go again to Jerusalem with joy; for YHWH have made them to rejoice over their enemies. They come to Jerusalem with stringed instruments, harps, and trumpets to YHWH’s house. The fear of God is on all the kingdoms of the countries, when they hear that YHWH fights against the enemies of Israel. So the realm of Jehoshaphat is quiet, for his God gives him rest all around.
Jehoshaphat's Later Failures and Death · 20:31–37

Jehoshaphat reigns over Judah. He is thirty-five years old when he begins to reign; and he reigns twenty-five years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name is Azubah the daughter of Shilhi. He walks in the way of Asa his father, and doesn’t turn away from it, doing that which is right in YHWH’s eyes. However the high places are not taken away, and the people have still not set their hearts on the God of their fathers. Now the rest of the acts of Jehoshaphat, first and last, look, they are written in the history of Jehu the son of Hanani, which is included in the book of the kings of Israel. After this, Jehoshaphat king of Judah joins himself with Ahaziah king of Israel. The same does very wickedly. He joins himself with him to make ships to go to Tarshish. They make the ships in Ezion Geber. Then Eliezer the son of Dodavahu of Mareshah prophesy against Jehoshaphat, saying, “Because you have joined yourself with Ahaziah, YHWH has destroyed your works.” The ships are wrecked, so that they are not able to go to Tarshish.
Jehoram's Wicked Reign · 21:1–11

Jehoshaphat sleeps with his fathers, and is buried with his fathers in David’s city, and Jehoram his son reigns in his place. He has brothers, the sons of Jehoshaphat: Azariah, Jehiel, Zechariah, Azariah, Michael, and Shephatiah. All these are the sons of Jehoshaphat king of Israel. Their father gives them great gifts of silver, of gold, and of precious things, with fortified cities in Judah; but he gives the kingdom to Jehoram, because he is the firstborn. Now when Jehoram has risen up over the kingdom of his father, and has strengthened himself, he kills all his brothers with the sword, and also some of the princes of Israel. Jehoram is thirty-two years old when he begins to reign, and he reigns eight years in Jerusalem. He walks in the way of the kings of Israel, as does Ahab’s house; for he has Ahab’s daughter as his wife. He does that which is evil in YHWH’s sight. However YHWH would not destroy David’s house, because of the covenant that he has made with David, and as he promises to give a lamp to him and to his children always.

In his days Edom revolts from under the hand of Judah, and makes a king over themselves. Then Jehoram goes there with his captains and all his chariots with him. He rises up by night and strikes the Edomites who surround him, along with the captains of the chariots. So Edom revolts from under the hand of Judah to this day. Then Libnah revolts at the same time from under his hand, because he has forsaken YHWH, the God of his fathers.
Moreover he makes high places in the mountains of Judah, and makes the inhabitants of Jerusalem play the prostitute, and leads Judah astray.
Elijah's Letter and the Plagues · 21:12–20

A letter comes to him from Elijah the prophet, saying, “YHWH, the God of David your father, says, ‘Because you have not walked in the ways of Jehoshaphat your father, nor in the ways of Asa king of Judah, but have walked in the way of the kings of Israel, and have made Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem to play the prostitute like Ahab’s house did, and also have slain your brothers of your father’s house, who were better than yourself, look, YHWH will strike your people with a great plague, including your children, your wives, and all your posessions; and you will have great sickness with a disease of your bowels, until your bowels fall out by reason of the sickness, day by day.’”

YHWH stirs up against Jehoram the spirit of the Philistines, and of the Arabians who are beside the Ethiopians; and they come up against Judah, break into it, and carry away all the posessions that are found in the king’s house, including his sons and his wives; so that there is no son leaves him, except Jehoahaz, the youngest of his sons.

After all this YHWH strikes him in his bowels with an incurable disease. In process of time, at the end of two years, his bowels fall out by reason of his sickness, and he dies of severe diseases. His people make no burning for him, like the burning of his fathers. He is thirty-two years old when he begins to reign, and he reigns in Jerusalem eight years. He departs without being missed; and they bury him in David’s city, but not in the tombs of the kings.
Ahaziah's Brief Reign · 22:1–9

The inhabitants of Jerusalem make Ahaziah his youngest son king in his place, because the band of men who come with the Arabians to the camp has slain all the oldest. So Ahaziah the son of Jehoram king of Judah reigns. Ahaziah is forty-two years old when he begins to reign, and he reigns one year in Jerusalem. His mother’s name is Athaliah the daughter of Omri. He also walks in the ways of Ahab’s house, because his mother is his counselor in acting wickedly. He does that which is evil in YHWH’s sight, as does Ahab’s house, for they are his counselors after the death of his father, to his destruction. He also follows their counsel, and goes with Jehoram the son of Ahab king of Israel to war against Hazael king of Syria at Ramoth Gilead, and the Syrians wound Joram. He returns to be healed in Jezreel of the wounds which they have given him at Ramah, when he fights against Hazael king of Syria. Azariah the son of Jehoram king of Judah goes down to see Jehoram the son of Ahab in Jezreel, because he is sick.

Now the destruction of Ahaziah is of God, in that he goes to Joram; for when he has come, he goes out with Jehoram against Jehu the son of Nimshi, whom YHWH has anointed to cut off Ahab’s house. When Jehu is executing judgment on Ahab’s house, he finds the princes of Judah and the sons of the brothers of Ahaziah, serving Ahaziah, and kills them. He seeks Ahaziah, and they catch him (now he is hiding in Samaria), and they bring him to Jehu, and kill him; and they bury him, for they say, “He is the son of Jehoshaphat, who sought YHWH with all his heart.” The house of Ahaziah has no power to hold the kingdom.
Athaliah Seizes Power; Joash Hidden · 22:10–12

Now when Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah sees that her son is dead, she arises and destroys all the royal offspring of the house of Judah. But Jehoshabeath, the king’s daughter, takes Joash the son of Ahaziah, and stealthily rescues him from among the king’s sons who are slain, and puts him and his nurse in the bedroom. So Jehoshabeath, the daughter of king Jehoram, the wife of Jehoiada the priest (for she is the sister of Ahaziah), hides him from Athaliah, so that she doesn’t kill him. He is with them hidden in God’s house six years while Athaliah reigns over the land.
The Coup against Athaliah · 23:1–11

In the seventh year, Jehoiada strengthens himself, and takes the captains of hundreds, Azariah the son of Jeroham, Ishmael the son of Jehohanan, Azariah the son of Obed, Maaseiah the son of Adaiah, and Elishaphat the son of Zichri, into a covenant with him. They go around in Judah, and gather the Levites out of all the cities of Judah, and the heads of fathers’ households of Israel, and they come to Jerusalem. All the assembly makes a covenant with the king in God’s house. He says to them, “Look, the king’s son must reign, as YHWH has spoken concerning the sons of David. This is the thing that you must do. A third part of you, who come in on the Sabbath, of the priests and of the Levites, will be gatekeepers of the thresholds. A third part will be at the king’s house; and a third part at the gate of the foundation. All the people will be in the courts of YHWH’s house. But let no one come into YHWH’s house, except the priests and those who minister of the Levites. They will come in, for they are holy, but all the people will follow YHWH’s instructions. The Levites will surround the king, every man with his weapons in his hand. Whoever comes into the house, let him be slain. Be with the king when he comes in, and when he goes out.”

So the Levites and all Judah do according to all that Jehoiada the priest commands: and they each take his men, those who are to come in on the Sabbath; with those who are to go out on the Sabbath; for Jehoiada the priest don’t dismiss the shift. Jehoiada the priest delivers to the captains of hundreds the spears, and bucklers, and shields, that has been king David’s, which are in God’s house. He sets all the people, every man with his weapon in his hand, from the right side of the house to the left side of the house, near the altar and the house, around the king. Then they bring out the king’s son, and put the crown on him, and give him the testimony, and make him king. Jehoiada and his sons anoint him, and they say, “Long live the king!”
Athaliah Executed; the Covenant Renewed · 23:12–21

When Athaliah hears the noise of the people running and praising the king, she comes to the people into YHWH’s house. Then she looks, and, look, the king stands by his pillar at the entrance, and the captains and the trumpets by the king. All the people of the land rejoice, and blow trumpets. The singers also play musical instruments, and lead the singing of praise. Then Athaliah tears her clothes, and says, “Treason! treason!”

Jehoiada the priest brings out the captains of hundreds who are set over the army, and says to them, “Bring her out between the ranks; and whoever follows her, let him be slain with the sword.” For the priest says, “Don’t kill her in YHWH’s house.” So they make way for her. She goes to the entrance of the horse gate to the king’s house; and they kill her there.

Jehoiada makes a covenant between himself, all the people, and the king, that they should be YHWH’s people. All the people go to the house of Baal, break it down, break his altars and his images in pieces, and kill Mattan the priest of Baal before the altars. Jehoiada appoints the officers of YHWH’s house under the hand of the priests the Levites, whom David has distributed in YHWH’s house, to offer the burnt offerings of YHWH, as it is written in the law of Moses, with rejoicing and with singing, as David has ordered. He sets the gatekeepers at the gates of YHWH’s house, that no one who is unclean in anything should enter in. He takes the captains of hundreds, the nobles, the governors of the people, and all the people of the land, and bring the king down from YHWH’s house. They come through the upper gate to the king’s house, and set the king on the throne of the kingdom. So all the people of the land rejoice, and the city is quiet. They have slain Athaliah with the sword.
Joash Repairs the Temple · 24:1–14

Joash is seven years old when he begins to reign, and he reigns forty years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name is Zibiah, of Beersheba. Joash does that which is right in YHWH’s eyes all the days of Jehoiada the priest. Jehoiada takes for him two wives, and he becomes the father of sons and daughters.

After this, Joash intends to restore YHWH’s house. He gathers together the priests and the Levites, and says to them, “Go out to the cities of Judah, and gather money to repair the house of your God from all Israel from year to year. See that you expedite this matter.” However the Levites don’t do it right away. The king calls for Jehoiada the chief, and says to him, “Why haven’t you required of the Levites to bring in the tax of Moses the servant of YHWH, and of the assembly of Israel, out of Judah and out of Jerusalem, for the Tent of the Testimony?” For the sons of Athaliah, that wicked woman, has broken up God’s house; and they also give all the dedicated things of YHWH’s house to the Baals.

So the king commands, and they make a chest, and set it outside at the gate of YHWH’s house. They make a proclamation through Judah and Jerusalem, to bring in for YHWH the tax that Moses the servant of God lays on Israel in the wilderness. All the princes and all the people rejoice, and bring in, and cast into the chest, until they have filled it. Whenever the chest is brought to the king’s officers by the hand of the Levites, and when they see that there is much money, the king’s scribe and the chief priest’s officer comes and empties the chest, and takes it, and carries it to its place again. Thus they do day by day, and gather money in abundance. The king and Jehoiada give it to those who do the work of the service of YHWH’s house. They hire masons and carpenters to restore YHWH’s house, and also those who work iron and brass to repair YHWH’s house. So the workmen work, and the work of repairing goes forward in their hands. They set up God’s house as it is designed, and strengthen it. When they have finished, they bring the rest of the money before the king and Jehoiada, from which are made vessels for YHWH’s house, even vessels with which to minister and to offer, including spoons and vessels of gold and silver. They offer burnt offerings in YHWH’s house continually all the days of Jehoiada.
Joash Turns After Jehoiada's Death · 24:15–22

But Jehoiada grows old and is full of days, and he dies. He is one hundred thirty years old when he dies. They bury him in David’s city among the kings, because he has done good in Israel, and toward God and his house.

Now after the death of Jehoiada, the princes of Judah comes, and bows down to the king. Then the king listens to them. They abandon the house of YHWH, the God of their fathers, and serve the Asherah poles and the idols, so wrath comes on Judah and Jerusalem for this their guiltiness. Yet he sends prophets to them, to bring them again to YHWH, and they testify against them; but they would not listen.

The Spirit of God comes on Zechariah the son of Jehoiada the priest; and he stands above the people, and says to them, “Thus says God, ‘Why do you disobey YHWH’s commandments, so that you can’t prosper? Because you have forsaken YHWH, he has also forsaken you.’”

They conspire against him, and stone him with stones at the commandment of the king in the court of YHWH’s house. Thus Joash the king doesn’t remember the kindness which Jehoiada his father has done to him, but kills his son. When he dies, he says, “May YHWH look at it, and repay it.”
Joash Punished; His Death · 24:23–27

At the end of the year, the army of the Syrians comes up against him: and they come to Judah and Jerusalem, and destroy all the princes of the people from among the people, and send all their plunder to the king of Damascus. For the army of the Syrians come with a small company of men; and YHWH delivers a very great army into their hand, because they have forsaken YHWH, the God of their fathers. So they execute judgment on Joash.

When they have departed from him (for they leave him very sick), his own servants conspire against him for the blood of the sons of Jehoiada the priest, and kill him on his bed, and he dies. They bury him in David’s city, but they don’t bury him in the tombs of the kings. These are those who conspire against him: Zabad the son of Shimeath the Ammonitess and Jehozabad the son of Shimrith the Moabitess. Now concerning his sons, the greatness of the burdens laid on him, and the rebuilding of God’s house, look, they are written in the commentary of the book of the kings. Amaziah his son reigns in his place.
Amaziah's Reign Begins Well · 25:1–4

Amaziah is twenty-five years old when he begins to reign, and he reigns twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name is Jehoaddan, of Jerusalem. He does that which is right in YHWH’s eyes, but not with a perfect heart. Now when the kingdom is established to him, he kills his servants who have killed his father the king. But he doesn’t put their children to death, but does according to that which is written in the law in the book of Moses, as YHWH commands, saying, “The fathers will not die for the children, neither will the children die for the fathers; but every man will die for his own sin.”
The War with Edom · 25:5–13

Moreover Amaziah gathers Judah together, and orders them according to their fathers’ houses, under captains of thousands and captains of hundreds, even all Judah and Benjamin. He counts them from twenty years old and upward, and finds that there are three hundred thousand chosen men, able to go out to war, who can handle spear and shield. He also hires one hundred thousand mighty men of valor out of Israel for one hundred talents of silver. A man of God comes to him, saying, “O king, don’t let the army of Israel go with you, for YHWH is not with Israel, with all the children of Ephraim. But if you will go, take action, and be strong for the battle. God will overthrow you before the enemy; for God has power to help, and to overthrow.”
Amaziah says to the man of God, “But what should we do for the hundred talents which I have given to the army of Israel?”
The man of God answers, “YHWH is able to give you much more than this.”

Then Amaziah separates them, the army that has come to him out of Ephraim, to go home again. Therefore their anger is greatly kindled against Judah, and they return home in fierce anger. Amaziah takes courage, and leads his people out, and goes to the Valley of Salt, and strikes ten thousand of the children of Seir. The children of Judah carry away ten thousand alive, and bring them to the top of the rock, and throw them down from the top of the rock, so that they all are broken in pieces. But the men of the army whom Amaziah sends back, that they should not go with him to battle, fall on the cities of Judah, from Samaria even to Beth Horon, and strike of them three thousand, and take much plunder.
Amaziah Follows Edomite Gods; His Downfall · 25:14–28

Now after Amaziah has come from the slaughter of the Edomites, he brings the gods of the children of Seir, and sets them up to be his gods, and bows down himself before them, and burns incense to them. Therefore YHWH’s anger burns against Amaziah, and he sends to him a prophet, who says to him, “Why have you sought after the gods of the people, which have not delivered their own people out of your hand?”
As he talks with him, the king says to him, “Have we made you one of the king’s counselors? Stop! Why should you be struck down?”
Then the prophet stops, and says, “I know that God has determined to destroy you, because you have done this, and have not listened to my counsel.”
Then Amaziah king of Judah consults his advisers, and sends to Joash, the son of Jehoahaz the son of Jehu, king of Israel, saying, “Come, let us look one another in the face.”

Joash king of Israel sends to Amaziah king of Judah, saying, “The thistle that was in Lebanon sent to the cedar that was in Lebanon, saying, ‘Give your daughter to my son as his wife. Then a wild animal that was in Lebanon passed by, and trampled down the thistle. You say to yourself that you have struck Edom; and your heart lifts you up to boast. Now stay at home. Why should you meddle with trouble, that you should fall, even you, and Judah with you?’”

But Amaziah would not listen; for it is of God, that he might deliver them into the hand of their enemies, because they have sought after the gods of Edom. So Joash king of Israel goes up, and he and Amaziah king of Judah looks one another in the face at Beth Shemesh, which belongs to Judah. Judah is defeated by Israel; and they every man flee to his tent.

Joash king of Israel takes Amaziah king of Judah, the son of Joash the son of Jehoahaz, at Beth Shemesh, and brings him to Jerusalem, and breaks down the wall of Jerusalem from the gate of Ephraim to the corner gate, four hundred cubits. He takes all the gold and silver, and all the vessels that are found in God’s house with Obed-Edom, and the treasures of the king’s house, the hostages also, and returns to Samaria.

Amaziah the son of Joash king of Judah lives for fifteen years after the death of Joash son of Jehoahaz king of Israel. Now the rest of the acts of Amaziah, first and last, look, aren’t they write in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel? Now from the time that Amaziah turns away from following YHWH, they make a conspiracy against him in Jerusalem. He flees to Lachish, but they send after him to Lachish, and kill him there. They bring him on horses, and bury him with his fathers in the City of Judah.
Uzziah's Prosperous Reign · 26:1–15

All the people of Judah take Uzziah, who is sixteen years old, and make him king in the place of his father Amaziah. He builds Eloth, and restores it to Judah, after that the king sleeps with his fathers. Uzziah is sixteen years old when he begins to reign; and he reigns fifty-two years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name is Jechiliah, of Jerusalem. He does that which is right in YHWH’s eyes, according to all that his father Amaziah has done. He sets himself to seek God in the days of Zechariah, who has understanding in the vision of God; and as long as he seeks YHWH, God makes him prosper.

He goes out and fights against the Philistines, and breaks down the wall of Gath, the wall of Jabneh, and the wall of Ashdod; and he builds cities in the country of Ashdod, and among the Philistines. God helps him against the Philistines, and against the Arabians who live in Gur Baal, and the Meunim. The Ammonites give tribute to Uzziah. His name spreads abroad even to the entrance of Egypt; for he grows exceedingly strong. Moreover Uzziah builds towers in Jerusalem at the corner gate, at the valley gate, and at the turning of the wall, and fortifies them. He builds towers in the wilderness, and digs out many cisterns, for he has much livestock; in the lowland also, and in the plain. He has farmers and vineyard keepers in the mountains and in the fruitful fields, for he loves farming. Moreover Uzziah has an army of fighting men, who go out to war by bands, according to the number of their reckoning made by Jeiel the scribe and Maaseiah the officer, under the hand of Hananiah, one of the king’s captains. The whole number of the heads of fathers’ households, even the mighty men of valor, is two thousand six hundred. Under their hand is an army, three hundred seven thousand five hundred, who makes war with mighty power, to help the king against the enemy. Uzziah prepares for them, even for all the army, shields, spears, helmets, coats of mail, bows, and stones for slinging. In Jerusalem, he makes devices, invented by skillful men, to be on the towers and on the battlements, with which to shoot arrows and great stones. His name spreads far abroad, because he is marvelously helped until he is strong.
Uzziah's Pride and Leprosy · 26:16–23

But when he is strong, his heart is lifted up, so that he does corruptly, and he trespasses against YHWH his God; for he goes into YHWH’s temple to burn incense on the altar of incense. Azariah the priest goes in after him, and with him eighty priests of YHWH, who are valiant men. They resist Uzziah the king, and say to him, “It isn’t for you, Uzziah, to burn incense to YHWH, but for the priests the sons of Aaron, who are consecrated to burn incense. Go out of the sanctuary, for you have trespassed. It will not be for your honor from YHWH God.”

Then Uzziah is angry. He has a censer in his hand to burn incense, and while he is angry with the priests, the leprosy breaks out on his forehead before the priests in YHWH’s house, beside the altar of incense. Azariah the chief priest, and all the priests, look at him, and look, he is leprous in his forehead, and they thrust him out quickly from there. Yes, he himself also hurries to go out, because YHWH has struck him. Uzziah the king is a leper to the day of his death, and lives in a separate house, being a leper; for he is cut off from YHWH’s house. Jotham his son is over the king’s house, judging the people of the land. Now the rest of the acts of Uzziah, first and last, Isaiah the prophet, the son of Amoz, writes. So Uzziah sleeps with his fathers; and they bury him with his fathers in the field of burial which belong to the kings, for they say, “He is a leper.” Jotham his son reigns in his place.
Jotham's Faithful Reign · 27:1–9

Jotham is twenty-five years old when he begins to reign, and he reigns sixteen years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name is Jerushah the daughter of Zadok. He does that which is right in YHWH’s eyes, according to all that his father Uzziah has done. However he doesn’t enter into YHWH’s temple. The people still act corruptly. He builds the upper gate of YHWH’s house, and he builds much on the wall of Ophel. Moreover he builds cities in the hill country of Judah, and in the forests he builds fortresses and towers. He also fights with the king of the children of Ammon, and prevails against them. The children of Ammon give him the same year one hundred talents of silver, ten thousand cors of wheat, and ten thousand cors of barley. The children of Ammon also give that much to him in the second year, and in the third. So Jotham becomes mighty, because he orders his ways before YHWH his God. Now the rest of the acts of Jotham, and all his wars, and his ways, look, they are written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah. He is five and twenty years old when he begins to reign, and reigns sixteen years in Jerusalem. Jotham sleeps with his fathers, and they bury him in David’s city; and Ahaz his son reigns in his place.
Ahaz's Wicked Reign · 28:1–8

Ahaz is twenty years old when he begins to reign, and he reigns sixteen years in Jerusalem. He doesn’t do that which is right in YHWH’s eyes, like David his father, but he walks in the ways of the kings of Israel, and also makes molten images for the Baals. Moreover he burns incense in the valley of the son of Hinnom, and burns his children in the fire, according to the abominations of the nations whom YHWH casts out before the children of Israel. He sacrifices and burns incense in the high places, and on the hills, and under every green tree.

Therefore YHWH his God delivers him into the hand of the king of Syria. They strike him, and carry away from him a great multitude of captives, and bring them to Damascus. He is also delivered into the hand of the king of Israel, who strikes him with a great slaughter. For Pekah the son of Remaliah killed in Judah one hundred twenty thousand in one day, all of them valiant men, because they have forsaken YHWH, the God of their fathers. Zichri, a mighty man of Ephraim, kills Maaseiah the king’s son, Azrikam the ruler of the house, and Elkanah who is next to the king. The children of Israel carry away captive of their brothers two hundred thousand, women, sons, and daughters, and take also away much plunder from them, and bring the plunder to Samaria.
The Prophet Oded and the Northern Captives · 28:9–15

But a prophet of YHWH is there, whose name is Oded; and he goes out to meet the army that comes to Samaria, and says to them, “Look, because YHWH, the God of your fathers, was angry with Judah, he has delivered them into your hand, and you have slain them in a rage which has reached up to heaven. Now you intend to degrade the children of Judah and Jerusalem as male and female slaves for yourselves. Aren’t there even with you trespasses of your own against YHWH your God? Now hear me therefore, and send back the captives that you have taken captive from your brothers, for the fierce wrath of YHWH is on you.” Then some of the heads of the children of Ephraim, Azariah the son of Johanan, Berechiah the son of Meshillemoth, Jehizkiah the son of Shallum, and Amasa the son of Hadlai, stands up against those who come from the war, and say to them, “You must not bring in the captives here, for you intend that which will bring on us a trespass against YHWH, to add to our sins and to our guilt; for our guilt is great, and there is fierce wrath against Israel.”

So the armed men leave the captives and the plunder before the princes and all the assembly. The men who have been mentioned by name rise up and take the captives, and with the plunder clothes all who are naked among them, dress them, give them sandals, and give them something to eat and to drink, anoint them, carry all the feeble of them on donkeys, and bring them to Jericho, the city of palm trees, to their brothers. Then they return to Samaria.
Ahaz Appeals to Assyria · 28:16–27

At that time king Ahaz sends to the kings of Assyria to help him. For again the Edomites have come and strike Judah, and carry away captives. The Philistines also has invaded the cities of the lowland, and of the South of Judah, and has taken Beth Shemesh, Aijalon, Gederoth, Soco with its villages, Timnah with its villages, and also Gimzo and its villages; and they live there. For YHWH bring Judah low because of Ahaz king of Israel, because he acts without restraint in Judah and trespasses severely against YHWH. Tilgath Pilneser king of Assyria comes to him, and gives him trouble, but doesn’t strengthen him. For Ahaz takes away a portion out of YHWH’s house, and out of the house of the king and of the princes, and gives it to the king of Assyria; but it doesn’t help him.

In the time of his distress, he trespasses yet more against YHWH, this same king Ahaz. For he sacrifices to the gods of Damascus, which strikes him. He says, “Because the gods of the kings of Syria helped them, so I will sacrifice to them, that they may help me.” But they are the ruin of him, and of all Israel. Ahaz gathers together the vessels of God’s house, and cuts the vessels of God’s house in pieces, and shuts up the doors of YHWH’s house; and he makes himself altars in every corner of Jerusalem. In every city of Judah he makes high places to burn incense to other gods, and provokes YHWH, the God of his fathers, to anger.

Now the rest of his acts, and all his ways, first and last, look, they are written in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel. Ahaz sleeps with his fathers, and they bury him in the city, even in Jerusalem, because they don’t bring him into the tombs of the kings of Israel; and Hezekiah his son reigns in his place.
Hezekiah Opens the Temple · 29:1–11

Hezekiah begins to reign when he is twenty-five years old, and he reigns twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name is Abijah, the daughter of Zechariah. He does that which is right in YHWH’s eyes, according to all that David his father has done. In the first year of his reign, in the first month, he opens the doors of YHWH’s house, and repairs them. He brings in the priests and the Levites, and gathers them together into the wide place on the east, and says to them, “Listen to me, you Levites! Now sanctify yourselves, and sanctify YHWH, the God of your fathers’ house, and carry the filthiness out of the holy place. For our fathers were unfaithful, and have done that which was evil in YHWH our God’s sight, and have forsaken him, and have turned away their faces from the habitation of YHWH, and turned their backs. Also they have shut up the doors of the porch, and put out the lamps, and have not burned incense nor offered burnt offerings in the holy place to the God of Israel. Therefore YHWH’s wrath was on Judah and Jerusalem, and he has delivered them to be tossed back and forth, to be an astonishment, and a hissing, as you see with your eyes. For, look, our fathers have fallen by the sword, and our sons and our daughters and our wives are in captivity for this. Now it is in my heart to make a covenant with YHWH, the God of Israel, that his fierce anger may turn away from us. My sons, don’t be negligent now; for YHWH has chosen you to stand before him, to minister to him, and that you should be his ministers, and burn incense.”
The Temple Cleansed · 29:12–19

Then the Levites arise, Mahath, the son of Amasai, and Joel the son of Azariah, of the sons of the Kohathites; and of the sons of Merari, Kish the son of Abdi, and Azariah the son of Jehallelel; and of the Gershonites, Joah the son of Zimmah, and Eden the son of Joah; and of the sons of Elizaphan, Shimri and Jeuel; and of the sons of Asaph, Zechariah and Mattaniah; and of the sons of Heman, Jehuel and Shimei; and of the sons of Jeduthun, Shemaiah and Uzziel. They gather their brothers, sanctify themselves, and go in, according to the commandment of the king by YHWH’s words, to cleanse YHWH’s house. The priests go into the inner part of YHWH’s house to cleanse it, and bring out all the uncleanness that they find in YHWH’s temple into the court of YHWH’s house. The Levites take it from there to carry it out to the brook Kidron. Now they begin on the first day of the first month to sanctify, and on the eighth day of the month they come to YHWH’s porch. They sanctify YHWH’s house in eight days, and on the sixteenth day of the first month they finish. Then they go in to Hezekiah the king within the palace, and say, “We have cleansed all YHWH’s house, including the altar of burnt offering with all its vessels, and the table of show bread with all its vessels. Moreover all the vessels, which king Ahaz in his reign threw away when he was unfaithful, have we prepared and sanctified. Look, they are before YHWH’s altar.”
The Great Offering of Restoration · 29:20–36

Then Hezekiah the king arises early, gathers the princes of the city, and goes up to YHWH’s house. They bring seven bulls, seven rams, seven lambs, and seven male goats, for a sin offering for the kingdom, for the sanctuary, and for Judah. He commands the priests the sons of Aaron to offer them on YHWH’s altar. So they kill the bulls, and the priests receive the blood, and sprinkle it on the altar. They kill the rams, and sprinkle the blood on the altar. They also kill the lambs, and sprinkle the blood on the altar. They bring near the male goats for the sin offering before the king and the assembly; and they lay their hands on them. Then the priests kill them, and they make a sin offering with their blood on the altar, to make atonement for all Israel; for the king commands that the burnt offering and the sin offering should be made for all Israel.

He sets the Levites in YHWH’s house with cymbals, with stringed instruments, and with harps, according to the commandment of David, of Gad the king’s seer, and Nathan the prophet; for the commandment is from YHWH by his prophets. The Levites stand with David’s instruments, and the priests with the trumpets. Hezekiah commands them to offer the burnt offering on the altar. When the burnt offering begins, YHWH’s song also begins, along with the trumpets and David king of Israel’s instruments. All the assembly worships, the singers sing, and the trumpeters sound. All this continues until the burnt offering is finished.

When they have finished offering, the king and all who are present with him bow themselves and worship. Moreover Hezekiah the king and the princes commands the Levites to sing praises to YHWH with the words of David, and of Asaph the seer. They sing praises with gladness, and they bow their heads and worship.

Then Hezekiah answers, “Now you have consecrated yourselves to YHWH. Come near and bring sacrifices and thank offerings into YHWH’s house.” The assembly brings in sacrifices and thank offerings, and as many as were of a willing heart brings burnt offerings. The number of the burnt offerings which the assembly brings is seventy bulls, one hundred rams, and two hundred lambs. All these are for a burnt offering to YHWH. The consecrated things are six hundred head of cattle and three thousand sheep. But the priests are too few, so that they can not flay all the burnt offerings. Therefore their brothers the Levites help them, until the work is ended, and until the priests have sanctified themselves; for the Levites are more upright in heart to sanctify themselves than the priests. Also the burnt offerings are in abundance, with the fat of the peace offerings, and with the drink offerings for every burnt offering. So the service of YHWH’s house is set in order. Hezekiah and all the people rejoice, because of that which God has prepared for the people; for the thing is done suddenly.
Hezekiah Summons Israel to the Passover · 30:1–12

Hezekiah sends to all Israel and Judah, and writes letters also to Ephraim and Manasseh, that they should come to YHWH’s house at Jerusalem, to keep the Passover to YHWH, the God of Israel. For the king has taken counsel with his princes and all the assembly in Jerusalem to keep the Passover in the second month. For they can not keep it at that time, because the priests have not sanctified themselves in sufficient number, and the people have not gathered themselves together to Jerusalem. The thing is right in the eyes of the king and of all the assembly. So they establish a decree to make proclamation throughout all Israel, from Beersheba even to Dan, that they should come to keep the Passover to YHWH, the God of Israel, at Jerusalem, for they have not kept it in great numbers in the way it is written.

So the couriers go with the letters from the king and his princes throughout all Israel and Judah, and according to the commandment of the king, saying, “You children of Israel, turn again to YHWH, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, that he may return to the remnant of you that have escaped out of the hand of the kings of Assyria. Don’t be like your fathers and like your brothers, who trespassed against YHWH, the God of their fathers, so that he gave them up to desolation, as you see. Now don’t be stiff-necked, as your fathers were, but yield yourselves to YHWH, and enter into his sanctuary, which he has sanctified forever, and serve YHWH your God, that his fierce anger may turn away from you. For if you turn again to YHWH, your brothers and your children will find compassion before those who led them captive, and will come again into this land, because YHWH your God is gracious and merciful, and will not turn away his face from you, if you return to him.”

So the couriers pass from city to city through the country of Ephraim and Manasseh, even to Zebulun, but people ridicule them and mock them. Nevertheless some men of Asher and Manasseh and of Zebulun humble themselves, and come to Jerusalem. Also the hand of God comes on Judah to give them one heart, to do the commandment of the king and of the princes by YHWH’s word.
The Passover Kept in the Second Month · 30:13–22

Many people assembled at Jerusalem to keep the feast of unleavened bread in the second month, a very great assembly. They arise and take away the altars that are in Jerusalem, and they take away all the altars for incense and throw them into the brook Kidron. Then they kill the Passover on the fourteenth day of the second month. The priests and the Levites are ashamed, and sanctify themselves, and bring burnt offerings into YHWH’s house. They stand in their place after their order, according to the law of Moses the man of God. The priests sprinkle the blood which they receive of the hand of the Levites. For there are many in the assembly who have not sanctified themselves: therefore the Levites are in charge of killing the Passovers for everyone who is not clean, to sanctify them to YHWH. For a multitude of the people, even many of Ephraim, Manasseh, Issachar, and Zebulun, have not cleansed themselves, yet they eat the Passover other than the way it is written. For Hezekiah has prayed for them, saying, “May the good YHWH pardon everyone who sets his heart to seek God, YHWH, the God of his fathers, even if they aren’t clean according to the purification of the sanctuary.”

YHWH listens to Hezekiah, and heals the people. The children of Israel who are present at Jerusalem keep the feast of unleavened bread seven days with great gladness. The Levites and the priests praise YHWH day by day, singing with loud instruments to YHWH. Hezekiah speaks encouragingly to all the Levites who have good understanding in the service of YHWH. So they eat throughout the feast for the seven days, offering sacrifices of peace offerings, and making confession to YHWH, the God of their fathers.
Seven Days More, and Great Joy · 30:23–27

The whole assembly takes counsel to keep another seven days, and they keep another seven days with gladness. For Hezekiah king of Judah gives to the assembly for offerings one thousand bulls and seven thousand sheep; and the princes give to the assembly a thousand bulls and ten thousand sheep: and a great number of priests sanctifies themselves. All the assembly of Judah, with the priests and the Levites, and all the assembly who come out of Israel, and the foreigners who come out of the land of Israel, and who lives in Judah, rejoices. So there is great joy in Jerusalem; for since the time of Solomon the son of David king of Israel there is nothing like this in Jerusalem. Then the priests the Levites arise and bless the people. Their voice is heard, and their prayer comes up to his holy habitation, even to heaven.
The Passover Aftermath: Destroying the High Places · 31:1

Now when all this is finished, all Israel who are present goes out to the cities of Judah, and breaks the pillars in pieces, cuts down the Asherah poles, and breaks down the high places and the altars out of all Judah and Benjamin, also in Ephraim and Manasseh, until they have destroyed them all. Then all the children of Israel return, every man to his possession, into their own cities.
Hezekiah Reorganises the Priests and Levites · 31:2–10

Hezekiah appoints the divisions of the priests and the Levites after their divisions, every man according to his service, both the priests and the Levites, for burnt offerings and for peace offerings, to minister, to give thanks, and to praise in the gates of YHWH’s camp. He also appoints the king’s portion of his possessions for the burnt offerings, for the morning and evening burnt offerings, and the burnt offerings for the Sabbaths, for the new moons, and for the set feasts, as it is written in YHWH’s law. Moreover he commands the people who live in Jerusalem to give the portion of the priests and the Levites, that they might give themselves to YHWH’s law. As soon as the commandment goes out, the children of Israel give in abundance the first fruits of grain, new wine, oil, honey, and of all the increase of the field; and they bring in the tithe of all things abundantly. The children of Israel and Judah, who live in the cities of Judah, also bring in the tithe of cattle and sheep, and the tithe of dedicated things which are consecrated to YHWH their God, and lay them in heaps.

In the third month they begin to lay the foundation of the heaps, and finish them in the seventh month. When Hezekiah and the princes come and see the heaps, they bless YHWH and his people Israel. Then Hezekiah questions the priests and the Levites about the heaps. Azariah the chief priest, of the house of Zadok, answers him and says, “Since people began to bring the offerings into YHWH’s house, we have eaten and had enough, and have plenty left over, for YHWH has blessed his people; and that which is left is this great store.”
The Distribution and Storehouses · 31:11–21

Then Hezekiah commands them to prepare rooms in YHWH’s house, and they prepare them. They bring in the offerings, the tithes, and the dedicated things faithfully. Conaniah the Levite is ruler over them, and Shimei his brother is second. Jehiel, Azaziah, Nahath, Asahel, Jerimoth, Jozabad, Eliel, Ismachiah, Mahath, and Benaiah are overseers under the hand of Conaniah and Shimei his brother, by the appointment of Hezekiah the king and Azariah the ruler of God’s house. Kore the son of Imnah the Levite, the gatekeeper at the east gate, is over the freewill offerings of God, to distribute YHWH’s offerings and the most holy things. Under him are Eden, Miniamin, Jeshua, Shemaiah, Amariah, and Shecaniah, in the cities of the priests, in their office of trust, to give to their brothers by divisions, to the great as well as to the small; besides those who are listed by genealogy of males, from three years old and upward, even everyone who enters into YHWH’s house, as the duty of every day required, for their service in their offices according to their divisions; and those who are listed by genealogy of the priests by their fathers’ houses, and the Levites from twenty years old and upward, in their offices by their divisions; and those who are listed by genealogy of all their little ones, their wives, their sons, and their daughters, through all the congregation; for in their office of trust they sanctify themselves in holiness. Also for the sons of Aaron the priests, who are in the fields of the suburbs of their cities, in every city, there are men who are mentioned by name, to give portions to all the males among the priests, and to all who are listed by genealogy among the Levites.

Hezekiah does so throughout all Judah; and he does that which is good, right, and faithful before YHWH his God. In every work that he begins in the service of God’s house, in the law, and in the commandments, to seek his God, he does it with all his heart, and prospered.
Sennacherib Invades Judah · 32:1–8

After these things and this faithfulness, Sennacherib king of Assyria comes, enters into Judah, and encamps against the fortified cities, and intends to win them for himself. When Hezekiah sees that Sennacherib has come, and that he is planning to fight against Jerusalem, he takes counsel with his princes and his mighty men to stop the waters of the springs which are outside of the city, and they help him. So, many people gather together and they stop all the springs and the brook that flows through the middle of the land, saying, “Why should the kings of Assyria come, and find abundant water?”

He takes courage, built up all the wall that is broken down, and raises it up to the towers, with the other wall outside, and strengthens Millo in David’s city, and makes weapons and shields in abundance. He sets captains of war over the people, and gathers them together to him in the wide place at the gate of the city, and speaks encouragingly to them, saying, “Be strong and courageous. Don’t be afraid or dismayed because of the king of Assyria, nor for all the multitude who is with him; for there is a greater one with us than with him. An arm of flesh is with him, but YHWH our God is with us to help us and to fight our battles.” The people rest themselves on the words of Hezekiah king of Judah.
Sennacherib's Taunt and Hezekiah's Prayer · 32:9–23

After this, Sennacherib king of Assyria sends his servants to Jerusalem, (now he is before Lachish, and all his power with him), to Hezekiah king of Judah, and to all Judah who are at Jerusalem, saying, Thus says Sennacherib king of Assyria, “In whom do you trust, that you remain under siege in Jerusalem? Doesn’t Hezekiah persuade you, to give you over to die by famine and by thirst, saying, ‘YHWH our God will deliver us out of the hand of the king of Assyria?’ Hasn’t the same Hezekiah taken away his high places and his altars, and commanded Judah and Jerusalem, saying, ‘You will worship before one altar, and you will burn incense on it?’ Don’t you know what I and my fathers have done to all the peoples of the lands? Were the gods of the nations of the lands in any way able to deliver their land out of my hand? Who was there among all the gods of those nations which my fathers utterly destroyed, that could deliver his people out of my hand, that your God should be able to deliver you out of my hand? Now therefore don’t let Hezekiah deceive you, nor persuade you in this way. Don’t believe him, for no god of any nation or kingdom was able to deliver his people out of my hand, and out of the hand of my fathers. How much less will your God deliver you out of my hand?”

His servants speak yet more against YHWH God, and against his servant Hezekiah. He also writes letters insulting YHWH, the God of Israel, and speaking against him, saying, “As the gods of the nations of the lands, which have not delivered their people out of my hand, so will the God of Hezekiah not deliver his people out of my hand.” They call out with a loud voice in the Jews’ language to the people of Jerusalem who are on the wall, to frighten them, and to trouble them; that they might take the city. They speak of the God of Jerusalem as of the gods of the peoples of the earth, which are the work of men’s hands.
Hezekiah the king and Isaiah the prophet the son of Amoz, prays because of this, and cries to heaven.

YHWH sends an angel, who cut off all the mighty men of valor, and the leaders and captains, in the camp of the king of Assyria. So he returns with shame of face to his own land. When he has come into the house of his god, those who come out of his own bowels kill him there with the sword. Thus YHWH saves Hezekiah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem from the hand of Sennacherib the king of Assyria and from the hand of all others, and guides them on every side. Many bring gifts to YHWH to Jerusalem, and precious things to Hezekiah king of Judah; so that he is exalted in the sight of all nations from then on.
Hezekiah's Pride and Humbling; His Death · 32:24–33

In those days Hezekiah is terminally ill, and he prays to YHWH; and he speaks to him, and gives him a sign. But Hezekiah doesn’t reciprocate appropriate to the benefit done for him, because his heart is lifted up. Therefore there is wrath on him, and on Judah and Jerusalem. Notwithstanding Hezekiah humbles himself for the pride of his heart, both he and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so that YHWH’s wrath doesn’t come on them in the days of Hezekiah.

Hezekiah has exceedingly much riches and honor. He provides himself with treasuries for silver, for gold, for precious stones, for spices, for shields, and for all kinds of valuable vessels; also storehouses for the increase of grain, new wine, and oil; and stalls for all kinds of animals, and flocks in folds. Moreover he provides for himself cities, and possessions of flocks and herds in abundance; for God has given him abundant posessions. This same Hezekiah also stops the upper spring of the waters of Gihon, and brings them straight down on the west side of David’s city. Hezekiah prospers in all his works.

However concerning the ambassadors of the princes of Babylon, who sends to him to inquire of the wonder that is done in the land, God leaves him, to try him, that he might know all that are in his heart.

Now the rest of the acts of Hezekiah, and his good deeds, look, they are written in the vision of Isaiah the prophet the son of Amoz, in the book of the kings of Judah and Israel. Hezekiah sleeps with his fathers, and they bury him in the ascent of the tombs of the sons of David. All Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem honor him at his death. Manasseh his son reigns in his place.
Manasseh's Wickedness · 33:1–9

Manasseh is twelve years old when he begins to reign, and he reigns fifty-five years in Jerusalem. He does that which is evil in YHWH’s sight, after the abominations of the nations whom YHWH casts out before the children of Israel. For he builds again the high places which Hezekiah his father has broken down; and he raises up altars for the Baals, made Asheroth, and worships all the army of the sky, and serves them. He builds altars in YHWH’s house, of which YHWH says, “My name will be in Jerusalem forever.” He builds altars for all the army of the sky in the two courts of YHWH’s house. He also makes his children to pass through the fire in the valley of the son of Hinnom. He practices sorcery, divination, and witchcraft, and deals with those who have familiar spirits, and with wizards. He does much evil in YHWH’s sight, to provoke him to anger. He sets the engraved image of the idol, which he has made, in God’s house, of which God says to David and to Solomon his son, “In this house, and in Jerusalem, which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel, will I put my name forever. I will not any more remove the foot of Israel from off the land which I have appointed for your fathers, if only they will observe to do all that I have commanded them, even all the law, the statutes, and the ordinances given by Moses.” Manasseh seduces Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so that they do more evil than do the nations whom YHWH destroys before the children of Israel.
Manasseh's Captivity and Repentance · 33:10–17

YHWH speaks to Manasseh, and to his people; but they don’t listen. Therefore YHWH brings on them the captains of the army of the king of Assyria, who take Manasseh in chains, binds him with fetters, and carries him to Babylon.

When he is in distress, he begs YHWH his God, and humbles himself greatly before the God of his fathers. He prays to him; and he is entreated by him, and hears his supplication, and brings him again to Jerusalem into his kingdom. Then Manasseh knows that YHWH is God.

Now after this, he builds an outer wall to David’s city, on the west side of Gihon, in the valley, even to the entrance at the fish gate. He encircles Ophel with it, and raises it up to a very great height; and he puts valiant captains in all the fortified cities of Judah. He takes away the foreign gods, and the idol out of YHWH’s house, and all the altars that he has built in the mountain of YHWH’s house, and in Jerusalem, and casts them out of the city. He builds up YHWH’s altar, and offers sacrifices of peace offerings and of thanksgiving on it, and commands Judah to serve YHWH, the God of Israel. Nevertheless the people sacrifice still in the high places, but only to YHWH their God.
Amon's Brief Wicked Reign · 33:18–25

Now the rest of the acts of Manasseh, and his prayer to his God, and the words of the seers who speak to him in the name of YHWH, the God of Israel, look, they are written among the acts of the kings of Israel. His prayer also, and how God is entreated of him, and all his sin and his trespass, and the places in which he builds high places, and sets up the Asherah poles and the engraved images, before he humbles himself: look, they are written in the history of Hozai. So Manasseh sleeps with his fathers, and they bury him in his own house; and Amon his son reigns in his place.

Amon is twenty-two years old when he begins to reign; and he reigns two years in Jerusalem. He does that which is evil in YHWH’s sight, as does Manasseh his father; and Amon sacrifices to all the engraved images which Manasseh his father has made, and serves them. He doesn’t humble himself before YHWH, as Manasseh his father has humbled himself; but this same Amon trespasses more and more. His servants conspire against him, and put him to death in his own house. But the people of the land kill all those who have conspired against king Amon; and the people of the land make Josiah his son king in his place.
Josiah's Early Reforms · 34:1–7

Josiah is eight years old when he begins to reign, and he reigns thirty-one years in Jerusalem.
