He does that which is right in YHWH’s eyes, and walks in the ways of David his father, and doesn’t turn away to the right hand or to the left. For in the eighth year of his reign, while he is yet young, he begins to seek after the God of David his father; and in the twelfth year he begins to purge Judah and Jerusalem from the high places, the Asherah poles, the engraved images, and the molten images. They break down the altars of the Baals in his presence; and he cuts down the incense altars that are on high above them. He breaks the Asherah poles, the engraved images, and the molten images in pieces, make dust of them, and scatter it on the graves of those who have sacrificed to them. He burns the bones of the priests on their altars, and purges Judah and Jerusalem. He does this in the cities of Manasseh, Ephraim, and Simeon, even to Naphtali, around in their ruins. He breaks down the altars, and beats the Asherah poles and the engraved images into powder, and cuts down all the incense altars throughout all the land of Israel, then returns to Jerusalem.
The Book of the Law Found · 34:8–21

Now in the eighteenth year of his reign, when he has purged the land and the house, he sends Shaphan the son of Azaliah, and Maaseiah the governor of the city, and Joah the son of Joahaz the recorder, to repair YHWH his God’s house. They come to Hilkiah the high priest, and deliver the money that is brought into God’s house, which the Levites, the keepers of the threshold, have gathered from the hands of Manasseh, Ephraim, of all the remnant of Israel, of all Judah and Benjamin, and of the inhabitants of Jerusalem. They deliver it into the hands of the workmen who have the oversight of YHWH’s house; and the workmen who labor in YHWH’s house give it to mend and repair the house. They give it to the carpenters and to the builders, to buy cut stone and timber for couplings, and to make beams for the houses which the kings of Judah have destroyed. The men do the work faithfully. Their overseers are Jahath and Obadiah, the Levites, of the sons of Merari; and Zechariah and Meshullam, of the sons of the Kohathites, to give direction; and others of the Levites, who are all skillful with musical instruments. Also they are over the bearers of burdens, and direct all who do the work in every kind of service. Of the Levites, there are scribes, officials, and gatekeepers.

When they bring out the money that is brought into YHWH’s house, Hilkiah the priest finds the book of YHWH’s law given by Moses. Hilkiah answers Shaphan the scribe, “I have found the book of the law in YHWH’s house.” So Hilkiah delivers the book to Shaphan.

Shaphan carries the book to the king, and moreover brings back word to the king, saying, “All that was committed to your servants, they are doing. They have emptied out the money that was found in YHWH’s house, and have delivered it into the hand of the overseers, and into the hand of the workmen.” Shaphan the scribe tells the king, saying, “Hilkiah the priest has delivered me a book.” Shaphan reads from it to the king.

When the king has heard the words of the law, he tears his clothes. The king commands Hilkiah, Ahikam the son of Shaphan, Abdon the son of Micah, Shaphan the scribe, and Asaiah the king’s servant, saying, “Go inquire of YHWH for me, and for those who are left in Israel and in Judah, concerning the words of the book that is found; for great is YHWH’s wrath that is poured out on us, because our fathers have not kept YHWH’s word, to do according to all that is written in this book.”
The Prophetess Huldah · 34:22–28

So Hilkiah, and they whom the king has commanded, go to Huldah the prophetess, the wife of Shallum the son of Tokhath, the son of Hasrah, keeper of the wardrobe (now she lives in Jerusalem in the second quarter), and they speak to her to that effect.

She says to them, “YHWH, the God of Israel says: ‘Tell the man who sent you to me, “YHWH says, ‘Look, I will bring evil on this place, and on its inhabitants, even all the curses that are written in the book which they have read before the king of Judah. Because they have forsaken me, and have burned incense to other gods, that they might provoke me to anger with all the works of their hands; therefore my wrath is poured out on this place, and it will not be quenched.’”’ But to the king of Judah, who sends you to inquire of YHWH, you will tell him this, ‘YHWH, the God of Israel says: “About the words which you have heard, because your heart was tender, and you humbled yourself before God, when you heard his words against this place, and against its inhabitants, and have humbled yourself before me, and have torn your clothes, and wept before me, I also have heard you,” says YHWH. “Look, I will gather you to your fathers, and you will be gathered to your grave in peace. Your eyes won’t see all the evil that I will bring on this place and on its inhabitants.”’”
They bring back word to the king.
Josiah's Covenant and Further Reform · 34:29–33

Then the king sends and gathers together all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem. The king goes up to YHWH’s house, with all the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the priests, the Levites, and all the people, both great and small; and he reads in their hearing all the words of the book of the covenant that is found in YHWH’s house. The king stands in his place, and makes a covenant before YHWH, to walk after YHWH, and to keep his commandments, and his testimonies, and his statutes, with all his heart, and with all his soul, to perform the words of the covenant that are written in this book. He causes all who are found in Jerusalem and Benjamin to stand. The inhabitants of Jerusalem do according to the covenant of God, the God of their fathers. Josiah takes away all the abominations out of all the countries that belong to the children of Israel, and makes all who are found in Israel to serve, even to serve YHWH their God. All his days they don’t depart from following YHWH, the God of their fathers.
Josiah's Great Passover · 35:1–19

Josiah keeps a Passover to YHWH in Jerusalem. They kill the Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month. He sets the priests in their offices, and encourages them in the service of YHWH’s house. He says to the Levites who teach all Israel, who are holy to YHWH, “Put the holy ark in the house which Solomon the son of David king of Israel built. It will no longer be a burden on your shoulders. Now serve YHWH your God, and his people Israel. Prepare yourselves after your fathers’ houses by your divisions, according to the writing of David king of Israel, and according to the writing of Solomon his son. Stand in the holy place according to the divisions of the fathers’ houses of your brothers the children of the people, and let there be for each a portion of a fathers’ house of the Levites. Kill the Passover, sanctify yourselves, and prepare for your brothers, to do according to YHWH’s word by Moses.”

Josiah gives to the children of the people, of the flock, lambs and young goats, all of them for the Passover offerings, to all who are present, to the number of thirty thousand, and three thousand bulls. These are of the king’s substance. His princes give for a freewill offering to the people, to the priests, and to the Levites. Hilkiah, Zechariah, and Jehiel, the rulers of God’s house, give to the priests for the Passover offerings two thousand six hundred small livestock, and three hundred head of cattle. Conaniah also, and Shemaiah and Nethanel, his brothers, and Hashabiah, Jeiel, and Jozabad, the chiefs of the Levites, give to the Levites for the Passover offerings five thousand small livestock and five hundred head of cattle.

So the service is prepared, and the priests stand in their place, and the Levites by their divisions, according to the king’s commandment. They kill the Passover, and the priests sprinkle the blood which they receive of their hand, and the Levites flay them. They remove the burnt offerings, that they might give them according to the divisions of the fathers’ houses of the children of the people, to offer to YHWH, as it is written in the book of Moses. They do the same with the cattle. They roast the Passover with fire according to the ordinance. They boil the holy offerings in pots, in cauldrons, and in pans, and carry them quickly to all the children of the people. Afterward they prepare for themselves and for the priests, because the priests the sons of Aaron are busy with offering the burnt offerings and the fat until night. Therefore the Levites prepare for themselves and for the priests the sons of Aaron. The singers the sons of Asaph are in their place, according to the commandment of David, Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun the king’s seer; and the gatekeepers are at every gate. They don’t need to depart from their service, because their brothers the Levites prepare for them.

So all the service of YHWH is prepared the same day, to keep the Passover, and to offer burnt offerings on YHWH’s altar, according to the commandment of king Josiah. The children of Israel who are present keep the Passover at that time, and the feast of unleavened bread seven days. There is no Passover like that keep in Israel from the days of Samuel the prophet, nor does any of the kings of Israel keep such a Passover as Josiah keeps, with the priests, the Levites, and all Judah and Israel who are present, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem. This passover is kept in the eighteenth year of the reign of Josiah.
The Death of Josiah · 35:20–27

After all this, when Josiah has prepared the temple, Neco king of Egypt goes up to fight against Carchemish by the Euphrates, and Josiah goes out against him. But he sends ambassadors to him, saying, “What have I to do with you, you king of Judah? I come not against you today, but against the house with which I have war. God has commanded me to make haste. Beware that it is God who is with me, that he not destroy you.”

Nevertheless Josiah would not turn his face from him, but disguises himself, that he might fight with him, and doesn’t listen to the words of Neco from the mouth of God, and comes to fight in the valley of Megiddo. The archers shoot at king Josiah; and the king says to his servants, “Take me away, because I am seriously wounded!”

So his servants take him out of the chariot, and put him in the second chariot that he has, and bring him to Jerusalem; and he dies, and is buried in the tombs of his fathers. All Judah and Jerusalem mourn for Josiah. Jeremiah laments for Josiah, and all the singing men and singing women speak of Josiah in their lamentations to this day; and they make them an ordinance in Israel. Look, they are written in the lamentations. Now the rest of the acts of Josiah, and his good deeds, according to that which is written in YHWH’s law, and his acts, first and last, look, they are written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah.
The Last Kings of Judah · 36:1–14

Then the people of the land take Jehoahaz the son of Josiah, and make him king in his father’s place in Jerusalem. Joahaz is twenty-three years old when he begins to reign; and he reigns three months in Jerusalem. The king of Egypt removes him from office at Jerusalem, and fins the land one hundred talents of silver and a talent of gold. The king of Egypt makes Eliakim his brother king over Judah and Jerusalem, and changes his name to Jehoiakim. Neco takes Joahaz his brother, and carries him to Egypt.

Jehoiakim is twenty-five years old when he begins to reign, and he reigns eleven years in Jerusalem. He does that which is evil in YHWH his God’s sight. Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon comes up against him, and binds him in fetters to carry him to Babylon. Nebuchadnezzar also carries some of the vessels of YHWH’s house to Babylon, and puts them in his temple at Babylon. Now the rest of the acts of Jehoiakim, and his abominations which he does, and that which is found in him, look, they are written in the book of the kings of Israel and Judah; and Jehoiachin his son reigns in his place.

Jehoiachin is eight years old when he begins to reign, and he reigns three months and ten days in Jerusalem. He does that which is evil in YHWH’s sight. At the return of the year, king Nebuchadnezzar sends and brings him to Babylon, with the valuable vessels of YHWH’s house, and makes Zedekiah his brother king over Judah and Jerusalem.

Zedekiah is twenty-one years old when he begins to reign, and he reigns eleven years in Jerusalem. He does that which is evil in YHWH his God’s sight. He doesn’t humble himself before Jeremiah the prophet speaking from YHWH’s mouth. He also rebels against king Nebuchadnezzar, who has made him swear by God; but he stiffens his neck, and hardens his heart against turning to YHWH, the God of Israel. Moreover all the chiefs of the priests, and the people, trespass very greatly after all the abominations of the nations; and they pollute YHWH’s house which he has made holy in Jerusalem.
The Fall of Jerusalem · 36:15–21

YHWH, the God of their fathers, sent to them by his messengers, rising up early and sending, because he has compassion on his people, and on his dwelling place; but they mock the messengers of God, and despise his words, and scoff at his prophets, until YHWH’s wrath arises against his people, until there is no remedy.

Therefore he brings on them the king of the Chaldeans, who kill their young men with the sword in the house of their sanctuary, and has no compassion on young man or virgin, old man or gray-headed. He gives them all into his hand. All the vessels of God’s house, great and small, and the treasures of YHWH’s house, and the treasures of the king, and of his princes, all these he brings to Babylon. They burn God’s house, and break down the wall of Jerusalem, and burn all its palaces with fire, and destroy all of its valuable vessels. He carries those who have escaped from the sword away to Babylon, and they are servants to him and his sons until the reign of the kingdom of Persia, to fulfill YHWH’s word by Jeremiah’s mouth, until the land has enjoyed its Sabbaths. As long as it lies desolate, it keeps Sabbath, to fulfill seventy years.
The Decree of Cyrus · 36:22–23

Now in the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, that YHWH’s word by the mouth of Jeremiah might be accomplished, YHWH stirs up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia, so that he makes a proclamation throughout all his kingdom, and puts it also in writing, saying, “Thus says Cyrus king of Persia, ‘YHWH, the God of heaven, has given all the kingdoms of the earth to me; and he has commanded me to build him a house in Jerusalem, which is in Judah. Whoever there is among you of all his people, YHWH his God be with him, and let him go up.’”
The Decree of Cyrus · 1:1–4

Now in the first year of Cyrus king of Persia, that YHWH’s word by Jeremiah’s mouth might be accomplished, YHWH stirs up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia, so that he makes a proclamation throughout all his kingdom, and puts it also in writing, saying, “Thus says Cyrus king of Persia, ‘YHWH, the God of heaven, has given me all the kingdoms of the earth; and he has commanded me to build him a house in Jerusalem, which is in Judah. Whoever there is among you of all his people, may his God be with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem, which is in Judah, and build the house of YHWH, the God of Israel (he is God), which is in Jerusalem. Whoever is left, in any place where he lives, let the men of his place help him with silver, with gold, with goods, and with animals, besides the freewill offering for God’s house which is in Jerusalem.’”
The Return of the Exiles · 1:5–11

Then the heads of fathers’ households of Judah and Benjamin, the priests, and the Levites, all whose spirit God has stirred to go up rise up to build YHWH’s house which is in Jerusalem. All those who are around them strengthen their hands with vessels of silver, with gold, with goods, with animals, and with precious things, besides all that are willingly offered. Also Cyrus the king brings out the vessels of YHWH’s house, which Nebuchadnezzar has brought out of Jerusalem, and has put in the house of his gods; even those, Cyrus king of Persia brings out by the hand of Mithredath the treasurer, and counts them out to Sheshbazzar, the prince of Judah. This is the number of them: thirty platters of gold, one thousand platters of silver, twenty-nine knives, thirty bowls of gold, four hundred ten silver bowls of a second sort, and one thousand other vessels. All the vessels of gold and of silver are five thousand four hundred. Sheshbazzar brings all these up when the captives are brought up from Babylon to Jerusalem.
The Register of Those Who Returned · 2:1–70

Now these are the children of the province, who goes up out of the captivity of those who have been carried away, whom Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon has carried away to Babylon, and who returns to Jerusalem and Judah, everyone to his city; who comes with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, Seraiah, Reelaiah, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispar, Bigvai, Rehum, and Baanah.

The number of the men of the people of Israel: The children of Parosh, two thousand one hundred seventy-two. The children of Shephatiah, three hundred seventy-two. The children of Arah, seven hundred seventy-five. The children of Pahathmoab, of the children of Jeshua and Joab, two thousand eight hundred twelve. The children of Elam, one thousand two hundred fifty-four. The children of Zattu, nine hundred forty-five. The children of Zaccai, seven hundred sixty. The children of Bani, six hundred forty-two. The children of Bebai, six hundred twenty-three. The children of Azgad, one thousand two hundred twenty-two. The children of Adonikam, six hundred sixty-six. The children of Bigvai, two thousand fifty-six. The children of Adin, four hundred fifty-four. The children of Ater, of Hezekiah, ninety-eight. The children of Bezai, three hundred twenty-three. The children of Jorah, one hundred twelve. The children of Hashum, two hundred twenty-three. The children of Gibbar, ninety-five. The children of Bethlehem, one hundred twenty-three. The men of Netophah, fifty-six. The men of Anathoth, one hundred twenty-eight. The children of Azmaveth, forty-two. The children of Kiriath Arim, Chephirah, and Beeroth, seven hundred forty-three. The children of Ramah and Geba, six hundred twenty-one. The men of Michmas, one hundred twenty-two. The men of Bethel and Ai, two hundred twenty-three. The children of Nebo, fifty-two. The children of Magbish, one hundred fifty-six. The children of the other Elam, one thousand two hundred fifty-four. The children of Harim, three hundred twenty. The children of Lod, Hadid, and Ono, seven hundred twenty-five. The children of Jericho, three hundred forty-five. The children of Senaah, three thousand six hundred thirty.

The priests: the children of Jedaiah, of the house of Jeshua, nine hundred seventy-three. The children of Immer, one thousand fifty-two. The children of Pashhur, one thousand two hundred forty-seven. The children of Harim, one thousand seventeen.

The Levites: the children of Jeshua and Kadmiel, of the children of Hodaviah, seventy-four. The singers: the children of Asaph, one hundred twenty-eight. The children of the gatekeepers: the children of Shallum, the children of Ater, the children of Talmon, the children of Akkub, the children of Hatita, the children of Shobai, in all one hundred thirty-nine.

The temple servants: the children of Ziha, the children of Hasupha, the children of Tabbaoth, the children of Keros, the children of Siaha, the children of Padon, the children of Lebanah, the children of Hagabah, the children of Akkub, the children of Hagab, the children of Shamlai, the children of Hanan, the children of Giddel, the children of Gahar, the children of Reaiah, the children of Rezin, the children of Nekoda, the children of Gazzam, the children of Uzza, the children of Paseah, the children of Besai, the children of Asnah, the children of Meunim, the children of Nephisim, the children of Bakbuk, the children of Hakupha, the children of Harhur, the children of Bazluth, the children of Mehida, the children of Harsha, the children of Barkos, the children of Sisera, the children of Temah, the children of Neziah, the children of Hatipha.

The children of Solomon’s servants: the children of Sotai, the children of Hassophereth, the children of Peruda, the children of Jaalah, the children of Darkon, the children of Giddel, the children of Shephatiah, the children of Hattil, the children of Pochereth Hazzebaim, the children of Ami. All the temple servants, and the children of Solomon’s servants, are three hundred ninety-two.

These are those who go up from Tel Melah, Tel Harsha, Cherub, Addan, and Immer; but they can not show their fathers’ houses, and their offspring, whether they are of Israel: the children of Delaiah, the children of Tobiah, the children of Nekoda, six hundred fifty-two. Of the children of the priests: the children of Habaiah, the children of Hakkoz, and the children of Barzillai, who takes a wife of the daughters of Barzillai the Gileadite, and are called after their name. These seek their place among those who are registered by genealogy, but they are not found: therefore are they deem disqualified and removed from the priesthood. The governor tells them that they should not eat of the most holy things until a priest stands up to serve with Urim and with Thummim.

The whole assembly together is forty-two thousand three hundred sixty, besides their male servants and their female servants, of whom there are seven thousand three hundred thirty-seven; and they have two hundred singing men and singing women. To King Artaxerxes,
From your servants the men beyond the River.

Be it known to the king that the Jews who come up from you have come to us to Jerusalem. They are building the rebellious and bad city, and have finished the walls, and repair the foundations. Be it known now to the king that if this city is built and the walls finish, they will not pay tribute, custom, or toll, and in the end it will be hurtful to the kings. Now because we eat the salt of the palace, and it is not appropriate for us to see the king’s dishonor, therefore we have sent and inform the king, that search may be made in the book of the records of your fathers. You will see in the book of the records, and know that this city is a rebellious city, and hurtful to kings and provinces, and that they have started rebellions within it in the past. Then the king sends an answer to Rehum the chancellor, and to Shimshai the scribe, and to the rest of their companions who live in Samaria, and in the rest of the country beyond the River:
Peace.

I decreed, and search has been made, and it is found that this city has made insurrection against kings in the past, and that rebellion and revolts have been made in it. There have also been mighty kings over Jerusalem, who have ruled over all the country beyond the River; and tribute, custom, and toll, are paid to them. In the month Nisan, in the twentieth year of Artaxerxes the king, when wine is before him, I pick up the wine, and gives it to the king. Now I have not been sad before in his presence. The king says to me, “Why is your face sad, since you are not sick? This is nothing else but sorrow of heart.”

Then I am very much afraid. I say to the king, “Let the king live forever! Why shouldn’t my face be sad, when the city, the place of my fathers’ tombs, lies waste, and its gates have been consumed with fire?”

So I pray to the God of heaven. I say to the king, “If it pleases the king, and if your servant has found favor in your sight, that you would send me to Judah, to the city of my fathers’ tombs, that I may build it.”

So it pleases the king to send me, and I set a time for him. For this deed of the queen will become known to all women, causing them to show contempt for their husbands, when it is reported, ‘King Ahasuerus commanded Vashti the queen to be brought in before him, but she didn’t come.’ Today, the princesses of Persia and Media who have heard of the queen’s deed will tell all the king’s princes. This will cause much contempt and wrath.

“If it pleases the king, let a royal commandment go from him, and let it be written among the laws of the Persians and the Medes, so that it cannot be altered, that Vashti may never again come before King Ahasuerus; and let the king give her royal estate to another who is better than she. This advice pleases the king and the princes, and the king does according to the word of Memucan: for he sends letters into all the king’s provinces, into every province according to its writing, and to every people in their language, that every man should rule his own house, speaking in the language of his own people.

After these things, when the wrath of King Ahasuerus is pacified, he remembers Vashti, and what she has done, and what is decreed against her. Let cosmetics be given them; and let the maiden who pleases the king be queen instead of Vashti.” The thing pleases the king, and he does so.

There is a certain Jew in the citadel of Susa, whose name is Mordecai, the son of Jair, the son of Shimei, the son of Kish, a Benjamite, who has been carried away from Jerusalem with the captives who have been carried away with Jeconiah king of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon has carried away. He brings up Hadassah, that is, Esther, his uncle’s daughter; for she has neither father nor mother. The maiden is fair and beautiful; and when her father and mother are dead, Mordecai takes her for his own daughter.

So, when the king’s commandment and his decree are heard, and when many maidens are gathered together to the citadel of Susa, to the custody of Hegai, Esther is taken into the king’s house, to the custody of Hegai, keeper of the women. The maiden pleases him, and she obtains kindness from him. He quickly gives her cosmetics and her portions of food, and the seven choice maidens who are to be given her out of the king’s house. He moves her and her maidens to the best place in the women’s house. Esther has not made known her people nor her relatives, because Mordecai has instructed her that she should not make it known. Mordecai walks every day in front of the court of the women’s house, to find out how Esther is doing, and what would become of her.

Each young woman’s turn comes to go in to King Ahasuerus after her purification for twelve months (for so are the days of their purification accomplished, six months with oil of myrrh, and six months with sweet fragrances and with preparations for beautifying women). The young woman then comes to the king like this: whatever she desires is given her to go with her out of the women’s house to the king’s house. In the evening she goes, and on the next day she returns into the second women’s house, to the custody of Shaashgaz, the king’s eunuch, who keeps the concubines. She comes in to the king no more, unless the king delights in her, and she is called by name.

Now when the turn of Esther, the daughter of Abihail the uncle of Mordecai, who has taken her for his daughter, comes to go in to the king, she requires nothing but what Hegai the king’s eunuch, the keeper of the women, advised. Esther obtains favor in the sight of all those who look at her.

So Esther is taken to King Ahasuerus into his royal house in the tenth month, which is the month Tebeth, in the seventh year of his reign. The king loves Esther more than all the women, and she obtains favor and kindness in his sight more than all the virgins; so that he sets the royal crown on her head, and makes her queen instead of Vashti.
Then the king makes a great feast for all his princes and his servants, even Esther’s feast; and he proclaims a holiday in the provinces, and gives gifts according to the king’s bounty.

When the virgins are gathered together the second time, Mordecai is sitting in the king’s gate. Esther has not yet made known her relatives nor her people, as Mordecai has commanded her; for Esther obeys Mordecai, like she does when she is brought up by him.

In those days, while Mordecai is sitting in the king’s gate, two of the king’s eunuchs, Bigthan and Teresh, who are doorkeepers, are angry, and seeks to lay hands on the King Ahasuerus. This thing became known to Mordecai, who informs Esther the queen; and Esther informs the king in Mordecai’s name. When this matter is investigated, and it is found to be so, they are both hanged on a tree; and it is written in the book of the chronicles in the king’s presence.

Then the king’s servants, who are in the king’s gate, say to Mordecai, “Why do you disobey the king’s commandment?” Now it comes to pass, when they speak daily to him, and he doesn’t listen to them, that they tell Haman, to see whether Mordecai’s reason would stand; for he has told them that he is a Jew. When Haman sees that Mordecai doesn’t bow down, nor pay him homage, Haman is full of wrath. But he scorns the thought of laying hands on Mordecai alone, for they have made known to him Mordecai’s people. Therefore Haman seeks to destroy all the Jews who are throughout the whole kingdom of Ahasuerus, even Mordecai’s people.

In the first month, which is the month Nisan, in the twelfth year of King Ahasuerus, they cast Pur, that is, the lot, before Haman from day to day, and from month to month, and choose the twelfth month, which is the month Adar. Haman says to King Ahasuerus, “There is a certain people scattered abroad and dispersed among the peoples in all the provinces of your kingdom, and their laws are different than other people’s. They don’t keep the king’s laws. Therefore it is not for the king’s profit to allow them to remain. If it pleases the king, let it be written that they be destroyed; and I will pay ten thousand talents of silver into the hands of those who are in charge of the king’s business, to bring it into the king’s treasuries.”

The king takes his ring from his hand, and gives it to Haman the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, the Jews’ enemy. The king says to Haman, “The silver is given to you, the people also, to do with them as it seems good to you.”

Then the king’s scribes are called in on the first month, on the thirteenth day of the month; and all that Haman commands are written to the king’s satraps, and to the governors who are over every province, and to the princes of every people, to every province according to its writing, and to every people in their language. It is written in the name of King Ahasuerus, and it is sealed with the king’s ring. Letters are sent by couriers into all the king’s provinces, to destroy, to kill, and to cause to perish, all Jews, both young and old, little children and women, in one day, even on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which is the month Adar, and to plunder their possessions. A copy of the letter, that the decree should be given out in every province, is published to all the peoples, that they should be ready against that day. The couriers go out in haste by the king’s commandment, and the decree is given out in the citadel of Susa. The king and Haman sit down to drink; but the city of Shushan is perplexed.

Now when Mordecai finds out all that are done, Mordecai tears his clothes, and puts on sackcloth with ashes, and goes out into the middle of the city, and wails loudly and bitterly. He comes even before the king’s gate, for no one is allowed inside the king’s gate clothed with sackcloth. In every province, wherever the king’s commandment and his decree come, there is great mourning among the Jews, and fasting, and weeping, and wailing; and many lay in sackcloth and ashes.

Esther’s maidens and her eunuchs come and tell her this, and the queen is exceedingly grieved. She sends clothing to Mordecai, to replace his sackcloth; but he doesn’t receive it. Then Esther calls for Hathach, one of the king’s eunuchs, whom he has appointed to attend her, and commands him to go to Mordecai, to find out what this is, and why it is. So Hathach goes out to Mordecai, to city square which is before the king’s gate. Mordecai tells him of all that have happened to him, and the exact sum of the money that Haman has promised to pay to the king’s treasuries for the destruction of the Jews. He also gives him the copy of the writing of the decree that is given out in Shushan to destroy them, to show it to Esther, and to declare it to her, and to urge her to go in to the king, to make supplication to him, and to make request before him, for her people.
Hathach comes and tells Esther the words of Mordecai.

Then Esther speaks to Hathach, and gives him a message to Mordecai: “All the king’s servants, and the people of the king’s provinces, know, that whoever, whether man or woman, comes to the king into the inner court without being called, there is one law for him, that he be put to death, except those to whom the king might hold out the golden scepter, that he may live. I have not been called to come in to the king these thirty days.”

They tell to Mordecai Esther’s words. Then Mordecai asks them to return this answer to Esther: “Don’t think to yourself that you will escape in the king’s house any more than all the Jews. For if you remain silent now, then relief and deliverance will come to the Jews from another place, but you and your father’s house will perish. Who knows if you haven’t come to the kingdom for such a time as this?”

Then Esther asks them to answer Mordecai, “Go, gather together all the Jews who are present in Shushan, and fast for me, and neither eat nor drink three days, night or day. I and my maidens will also fast the same way. Then I will go in to the king, which is against the law; and if I perish, I perish.” So Mordecai goes his way, and does according to all that Esther has commanded him.
Esther Before the King · 5:1–8

Now on the third day, Esther puts on her royal clothing, and stands in the inner court of the king’s house, next to the king’s house. The king sits on his royal throne in the royal house, next to the entrance of the house. When the king sees Esther the queen standing in the court, she obtains favor in his sight; and the king holds out to Esther the golden scepter that is in his hand. So Esther comes near, and touches the top of the scepter. Then the king asks her, “What would you like, queen Esther? What is your request? It will be given you even to the half of the kingdom.”
Esther says, “If it seems good to the king, let the king and Haman come today to the banquet that I have prepared for him.”
Then the king says, “Bring Haman quickly, so that it may be done as Esther has said.” So the king and Haman come to the banquet that Esther has prepared.
The king says to Esther at the banquet of wine, “What is your petition? It will be granted you. What is your request? Even to the half of the kingdom it will be performed.”

Then Esther answers and says, “My petition and my request is this. If I have found favor in the sight of the king, and if it pleases the king to grant my petition and to perform my request, let the king and Haman come to the banquet that I will prepare for them, and I will do tomorrow as the king has said.”

Then Haman goes out that day joyful and glad of heart, but when Haman sees Mordecai in the king’s gate, that he doesn’t stand up nor move for him, he is filled with wrath against Mordecai. Nevertheless Haman restrains himself, and goes home. There, he sends and calls for his friends and Zeresh his wife. Haman recounts to them the glory of his riches, the multitude of his children, all the things in which the king has promoted him, and how he has advanced him above the princes and servants of the king. Haman also says, “Yes, Esther the queen let no man come in with the king to the banquet that she had prepared but myself; and tomorrow I am also invited by her together with the king. Yet all this avails me nothing, so long as I see Mordecai the Jew sitting at the king’s gate.”

Then Zeresh his wife and all his friends says to him, “Let a gallows be made fifty cubits high, and in the morning speak to the king about hanging Mordecai on it. Then go in merrily with the king to the banquet.” This pleases Haman, so he has the gallows made.

On that night, the king can’t sleep. He commands the book of records of the chronicles to be brought, and they are read to the king. It is found written that Mordecai has told of Bigthana and Teresh, two of the king’s eunuchs, who are doorkeepers, who have tried to lay hands on the King Ahasuerus. The king says, “What honor and dignity has been given to Mordecai for this?”
Then the king’s servants who attend him say, “Nothing has been done for him.”
The king says, “Who is in the court?” Now Haman has come into the outer court of the king’s house, to speak to the king about hanging Mordecai on the gallows that he has prepared for him.
The king’s servants say to him, “Look, Haman stands in the court.”
The king says, “Let him come in.” So Haman comes in. The king says to him, “What will be done to the man whom the king delights to honor?”

Now Haman says in his heart, “Who would the king delight to honor more than myself?” Haman says to the king, “For the man whom the king delights to honor, let royal clothing be brought which the king uses to wear, and the horse that the king rides on, and on the head of which a crown royal is set. Let the clothing and the horse be delivered to the hand of one of the king’s most noble princes, that they may array the man whom the king delights to honor with them, and have him ride on horseback through the city square, and proclaim before him, ‘Thus will it be done to the man whom the king delights to honor!’”

Then the king says to Haman, “Hurry and take the clothing and the horse, as you have said, and do this for Mordecai the Jew, who sits at the king’s gate. Let nothing fail of all that you have spoken.”

Then Haman takes the clothing and the horse, and arrays Mordecai, and has him ride through the city square, and proclaims before him, “Thus will it be done to the man whom the king delights to honor!”

Mordecai comes back to the king’s gate, but Haman hurries to his house, mourning and having his head covered. Haman recounts to Zeresh his wife and all his friends everything that has happened to him. Then his wise men and Zeresh his wife say to him, “If Mordecai, before whom you have begun to fall, is of Jewish descent, you will not prevail against him, but you will surely fall before him.” While they are yet talking with him, the king’s eunuchs comes, and hurries to bring Haman to the banquet that Esther has prepared.

So the king and Haman come to banquet with Esther the queen. The king says again to Esther on the second day at the banquet of wine, “What is your petition, queen Esther? It will be granted you. What is your request? Even to the half of the kingdom it will be performed.”

Then Esther the queen answers, “If I have found favor in your sight, O king, and if it pleases the king, let my life be given me at my petition, and my people at my request. For we are sold, I and my people, to be destroyed, to be slain, and to perish. But if we had been sold for male and female slaves, I would have held my peace, although the adversary could not have compensated for the king’s loss.”
Then King Ahasuerus says to Esther the queen, “Who is he, and where is he who dared presume in his heart to do so?”
Esther says, “An adversary and an enemy, even this wicked Haman!”

Then Haman is afraid before the king and the queen. The king arises in his wrath from the banquet of wine and goes into the palace garden. Haman stands up to make request for his life to Esther the queen; for he sees that there is evil determined against him by the king. Then the king returns out of the palace garden into the place of the banquet of wine; and Haman has fallen on the couch where Esther is. Then the king says, “Will he even assault the queen in front of me in the house?” As the word goes out of the king’s mouth, they cover Haman’s face.
Then Harbonah, one of the eunuchs who are with the king says, “Look, the gallows fifty cubits high, which Haman has made for Mordecai, who spoke good for the king, is standing at Haman’s house.”
The king says, “Hang him on it!”
So they hang Haman on the gallows that he has prepared for Mordecai. Then is the king’s wrath pacifies.

On that day, King Ahasuerus gives the house of Haman, the Jews’ enemy, to Esther the queen. Mordecai comes before the king; for Esther has told what he is to her. The king takes off his ring, which he has taken from Haman, and gives it to Mordecai. Esther sets Mordecai over the house of Haman.

Esther speaks yet again before the king, and falls down at his feet, and begs him with tears to put away the mischief of Haman the Agagite, and his plan that he has planned against the Jews. Then the king holds out to Esther the golden scepter. So Esther arises, and stands before the king. She says, “If it pleases the king, and if I have found favor in his sight, and the thing seem right to the king, and I am pleasing in his eyes, let it be written to reverse the letters devised by Haman, the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, which he wrote to destroy the Jews who are in all the king’s provinces. For how can I endure to see the evil that would come to my people? How can I endure to see the destruction of my relatives?”

Then King Ahasuerus says to Esther the queen and to Mordecai the Jew, “See, I have given Esther the house of Haman, and him they have hanged on the gallows, because he laid his hand on the Jews. Write also to the Jews, as it pleases you, in the king’s name, and seal it with the king’s ring; for the writing which is written in the king’s name, and sealed with the king’s ring, may not be reversed by any man.”

Then the king’s scribes are called at that time, in the third month, which is the month Sivan, on the twenty-third day of the month; and it is written according to all that Mordecai commands to the Jews, and to the satraps, and the governors and princes of the provinces which are from India to Ethiopia, one hundred twenty-seven provinces, to every province according to its writing, and to every people in their language, and to the Jews in their writing, and in their language. He writes in the name of King Ahasuerus, and seals it with the king’s ring, and sends letters by courier on horseback, riding on royal horses that are bred from swift steeds. In those letters, the king grants the Jews who are in every city to gather themselves together, and to defend their life, to destroy, to kill, and to cause to perish, all the power of the people and province that would assault them, their little ones and women, and to plunder their possessions, on one day in all the provinces of King Ahasuerus, on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which is the month Adar. A copy of the letter, that the decree should be given out in every province, is published to all the peoples, that the Jews should be ready for that day to avenge themselves on their enemies. So the couriers who ride on royal horses go out, hastened and pressed on by the king’s commandment. The decree is given out in the citadel of Susa.

Mordecai goes out of the presence of the king in royal clothing of blue and white, and with a great crown of gold, and with a robe of fine linen and purple; and the city of Susa shouts and is glad. The Jews have light, gladness, joy, and honor. In every province, and in every city, wherever the king’s commandment and his decree come, the Jews have gladness, joy, a feast, and a good day. Many from among the peoples of the land become Jews; for the fear of the Jews are fallen on them.

Now in the twelfth month, which is the month Adar, on the thirteenth day of the month, when the king’s commandment and his decree come near to be put in execution, on the day that the enemies of the Jews hop to conquer them, (but it is turned out the opposite happens, that the Jews conquer those who hated them), the Jews gather themselves together in their cities throughout all the provinces of the King Ahasuerus, to lay hands on those who want to harm them. No one can withstand them, because the fear of them has fallen on all the people. All the princes of the provinces, the satraps, the governors, and those who do the king’s business help the Jews, because the fear of Mordecai has fallen on them. For Mordecai is great in the king’s house, and his fame goes out throughout all the provinces; for the man Mordecai grows greater and greater. The Jews strike all their enemies with the stroke of the sword, and with slaughter and destruction, and do what they want to those who hated them. In the citadel of Susa, the Jews kill and destroy five hundred men. They kill Parshandatha, Dalphon, Aspatha, Poratha, Adalia, Aridatha, Parmashta, Arisai, Aridai, and Vaizatha, the ten sons of Haman the son of Hammedatha, the Jews’ enemy, but they don’t lay their hand on the plunder.

Then Esther says, “If it pleases the king, let it be granted to the Jews who are in Shushan to do tomorrow also according to today’s decree, and let Haman’s ten sons be hanged on the gallows.”

This is done on the thirteenth day of the month Adar; and on the fourteenth day of that month they rest and make it a day of feasting and gladness. But the Jews who are in Shushan assembled together on the thirteenth and on the fourteenth days of the month; and on the fifteenth day of that month, they rest, and make it a day of feasting and gladness. Therefore the Jews of the villages, who live in the unwalled towns, make the fourteenth day of the month Adar a day of gladness and feasting, a good day, and a day of sending presents of food to one another.

Mordecai writes these things, and sends letters to all the Jews who are in all the provinces of the king Ahasuerus, both near and far, to enjoin them that they should keep the fourteenth and fifteenth days of the month Adar yearly, as the days in which the Jews have rest from their enemies, and the month which is turned to them from sorrow to gladness, and from mourning into a good day; that they should make them days of feasting and gladness, and of sending presents of food to one another, and gifts to the needy.
