The Cry: Faithfulness Has Vanished · 12:1–2
*For the music leader. On the Sheminith. A psalm of David.*
Save, YHWH! For the faithful are gone.
The trustworthy have vanished from among the children of Adam.
Everyone speaks emptiness to his neighbor.
With slippery lips and a double heart they talk.
The Divine Response · 12:3–6
May YHWH cut off all slippery lips,
the tongue that talks so big —
those who say, “With our tongues we will win.
Our lips are our own — who is master over us?”
“Because the poor are plundered,
because the needy are groaning,
now I will rise up,” says YHWH.
“I will set them in the safety they long for.”
The words of YHWH are pure words —
silver refined in a furnace in the ground,
purified seven times over.
Confidence and Perseverance · 12:7–8
You, YHWH, will keep them.
You will guard us from this generation forever.
The wicked strut around on every side
when what is vile is lifted high among the children of Adam.
The Four-fold Cry · 13:1–2
*For the music leader. A psalm of David.*
How long, YHWH? Will you forget me forever?
How long will you hide your face from me?
How long must I keep wrestling with plans in my soul,
with sorrow in my heart all day long?
How long will my enemy stand over me?
The Petition · 13:3–4
Look at me! Answer me, YHWH my God!
Light up my eyes,
or I will sleep the sleep of death,
and my enemy will say, “I have beaten him,”
and my foes will celebrate because I am shaken.
The Turn: Trust and Song · 13:5–6
But I — I trust in your steadfast love.
My heart will leap for joy in your rescue.
I will sing to YHWH,
for he has been good to me.
Universal Foolishness · 14:1–3
*For the music leader. Of David.*
The fool says in his heart, “There is no God.”
They are corrupt, their deeds are vile —
there is no one who does good.
YHWH looks down from heaven on the children of Adam
to see if there is anyone who understands,
anyone who seeks God.
They have all turned aside; together they have gone sour.
There is no one who does good — not even one.
The Indictment · 14:4–6
Do they know nothing, all these evildoers?
They eat up my people the way they eat bread,
and they never call on YHWH.
There they are, in sheer terror,
for God is with the generation of the righteous.
You would put to shame the plans of the poor,
but YHWH is his shelter.
The Hope · 14:7
Oh, that Israel’s rescue would come out of Zion!
When YHWH brings his people home again,
let Jacob leap for joy, let Israel be glad!
The Question and The Answer · 15:1–5
*A psalm of David.*
YHWH, who may stay as a guest in your tent?
Who may settle down on your holy mountain?
The one who walks with integrity and does what is right,
who speaks the truth from the heart,
who does not go around slandering with his tongue,
who does his friend no harm,
who heaps no insult on his neighbor;
in whose eyes the worthless one is despised,
but who honors those who fear YHWH;
who keeps his oath even when it costs him,
and does not change it;
who does not lend his money at interest,
and will not take a bribe against the innocent.
Whoever does these things will never be shaken.
Refuge in God Alone · 16:1–4
*A Miktam of David.*
Keep me safe, O God,
for I take shelter in you.
I say to YHWH, “You are my Lord.
I have nothing good apart from you.”
As for the holy ones in the land —
they are the noble ones,
and all my delight is in them.
But the sorrows of those who run after another god will multiply.
I will not pour out their offerings of blood,
I will not even let their names cross my lips.
The Lord as Inheritance · 16:5–8
YHWH, you are my share and my cup.
You hold my lot secure.
The boundary lines have fallen for me in lovely places.
Yes — my inheritance is beautiful to me.
I bless YHWH, who gives me counsel.
Even in the night my inmost being instructs me.
I keep YHWH before me always.
Because he is at my right hand,
I will not be shaken.
Joy in the Presence of God · 16:9–11
So my heart is glad, and my whole being rejoices.
Even my body rests secure,
for you will not abandon my soul to Sheol,
you will not let your faithful one see the pit.
You make known to me the path of life.
In your presence there is joy to the full;
at your right hand, delights forever.
The Claim of Innocence · 17:1–5
*A prayer of David.*
Hear what is right, YHWH!
Pay attention to my cry.
Lend your ear to my prayer —
it does not come from lying lips.
Let my verdict come from your presence.
Let your eyes see what is fair.
You have tested my heart,
you have visited me in the night,
you have put me through the fire —
and you find nothing.
I have resolved that my mouth will not cross the line.
As for what people do —
by the word of your lips
I have kept myself from the ways of the violent.
My steps have held to your tracks.
My feet have not slipped.
The Appeal for Protection · 17:6–12
I call on you, for you will answer me, O God.
Bend your ear to me; hear what I say.
Show the wonder of your steadfast love,
you who save by your right hand
those who take shelter from the ones who rise against them.
Guard me like the apple of your eye.
Hide me in the shadow of your wings,
from the wicked who are tearing me down,
from my deadly enemies who close in around me.
They have shut up their hearts, hard as fat.
Their mouths speak with swagger.
They track our steps — now they surround us.
They fix their eyes on us,
to throw us to the ground.
He is like a lion hungry for prey,
like a young lion crouching in hiding.
The Climax: to See God’s Face · 17:13–15
Rise up, YHWH! Confront him! Bring him to his knees!
Rescue my life from the wicked by your sword —
from men, by your hand, YHWH,
from men of this world, whose share is in this life.
You fill their bellies with what you have stored up;
their children have plenty,
and they leave what is left to their little ones.
But as for me — in righteousness I will see your face.
When I awake, I will be satisfied with seeing your likeness.
The God Who Delivers · 18:1–3
*For the music leader. Of David, the servant of YHWH, who speaks to YHWH the words of this song on the day YHWH rescues him from the hand of all his enemies and from the hand of Saul. He says:*
I love you, YHWH, my strength.
YHWH is my cliff, my fortress, the one who gets me out.
My God is my rock — I take shelter in him —
my shield, the horn that saves me, my high stronghold.
I call on YHWH, who is worthy of praise,
and I am saved from my enemies.
Death’s Grip and the Theophany · 18:4–19
The cords of death wrap around me.
The floods of destruction terrify me.
The cords of Sheol coil around me.
The snares of death lie in front of me.
In my distress I call on YHWH.
I cry to my God for help.
From his temple he hears my voice,
and my cry reaches his ears.
Then the earth heaves and quakes.
The foundations of the mountains shudder;
they rock back and forth, because he is angry.
Smoke goes up from his nostrils,
devouring fire from his mouth,
coals blazing out from him.
He bends the heavens and comes down,
thick darkness under his feet.
He rides on a cherub and flies;
he soars on the wings of the wind.
He makes darkness his hiding place,
his shelter all around him —
dark waters, thick clouds of the sky.
Out of the brightness before him
his clouds sweep past —
hail, and coals of fire.
YHWH thunders in the heavens.
The Most High lifts his voice —
hail, and coals of fire.
He sends out his arrows and scatters them,
lightning bolts in plenty, and throws them into panic.
The channels of the sea come into view,
the foundations of the world are laid bare,
at your rebuke, YHWH,
at the blast of breath from your nostrils.
He reaches down from on high and takes hold of me.
He draws me out of deep waters.
He rescues me from my strong enemy,
from those who hate me,
for they are too strong for me.
They confront me on the day of my disaster,
but YHWH is my support.
He brings me out into a wide-open place.
He rescues me — because he delights in me.
The Moral of The Deliverance · 18:20–30
YHWH deals with me according to my righteousness.
He repays me for the cleanness of my hands.
For I have kept the ways of YHWH,
and have not wickedly turned from my God.
All his judgments are before me.
I have not put his statutes away from me.
I have been whole-hearted with him,
and have kept myself from my guilt.
So YHWH has repaid me for my righteousness,
for the cleanness of my hands in his sight.
With the faithful you show yourself faithful.
With the blameless you show yourself blameless.
With the pure you show yourself pure,
but with the crooked you show yourself shrewd.
For you save a humble people,
but eyes held high — you bring them down.
You light my lamp, YHWH.
My God turns my darkness into light.
With you I can charge a troop.
With my God I can leap over a wall.
This God — his way is whole.
The word of YHWH has been tested by fire.
He is a shield to all who take shelter in him.
The King’s Victory · 18:31–50
For who is God besides YHWH?
And who is a rock except our God?
It is God who wraps me in strength
and makes my way whole.
He makes my feet like the feet of a deer
and sets me secure on the heights.
He trains my hands for battle,
so my arms can bend a bow of bronze.
You give me the shield of your rescue.
Your right hand holds me up.
Your gentleness makes me great.
You make a wide place for my steps,
and my ankles do not turn.
I chase my enemies and overtake them.
I do not turn back until they are finished.
I strike them down so they cannot rise.
They fall under my feet.
You wrap me in strength for the battle.
You bring down under me those who rise against me.
You make my enemies turn their backs to me,
and those who hate me — I put an end to them.
They cry for help, but there is no one to save —
to YHWH, but he does not answer them.
I grind them fine as dust before the wind.
I empty them out like mud in the streets.
You rescue me from the quarrels of the people.
You make me head of the nations.
A people I have never known serve me.
As soon as they hear of me, they obey me.
Foreigners come cringing before me.
Foreigners lose heart
and come trembling out of their strongholds.
YHWH lives! Blessed be my rock!
High be the God who saves me —
the God who gives me vengeance
and brings peoples down under me,
who rescues me from my enemies.
Yes, you lift me high above those who rise against me.
You rescue me from the man of violence.
So I will give you thanks among the nations, YHWH.
I will sing praise to your name.
He gives great victories to his king.
He shows steadfast love to his anointed one —
to David and to his descendants, forever.
The Heavens Declare · 19:1–6
*For the music leader. A psalm of David.*
The skies keep telling the glory of God;
the vault above announces what his hands have made.
Day after day pours out speech;
night after night makes knowledge known.
There is no speech, there are no words —
their voice is never heard —
and yet their call goes out through all the earth,
their words to the ends of the world.
In the heavens he has pitched a tent for the sun,
and the sun comes out like a bridegroom from his wedding chamber,
glad as a champion to run his course.
He rises at one end of the heavens
and makes his circuit to the other,
and nothing is hidden from his heat.
The Torah of YHWH · 19:7–11
The Torah of YHWH is whole —
it brings the soul back to life.
The testimony of YHWH is sure —
it makes the simple wise.
The precepts of YHWH are right —
they make the heart glad.
The commandment of YHWH is clear —
it brings light to the eyes.
The fear of YHWH is clean —
it stands forever.
The judgments of YHWH are true —
every one of them is righteous.
They are more to be wanted than gold,
than a hoard of fine gold,
sweeter than honey,
than honey dripping from the comb.
And by them your servant is warned.
In keeping them there is great reward.
The Prayer · 19:12–14
Who can see his own mistakes?
Clear me of the faults I cannot see.
Hold your servant back from willful sins, too.
Do not let them rule over me.
Then I will be whole,
and clean of great rebellion.
Let the words of my mouth
and the murmuring of my heart
be welcome before you,
YHWH, my rock and my redeemer.
The Priestly Blessing · 20:1–5
*For the music leader. A psalm of David.*
May YHWH answer you on the day of trouble.
May the name of the God of Jacob set you on high.
May he send you help from the sanctuary,
and hold you up out of Zion.
May he remember all your offerings,
and find your burnt offering rich. *Selah*
May he give you your heart’s desire,
and bring all your plans to pass.
We will shout for joy at your victory,
and raise our banners in the name of our God.
May YHWH grant all that you ask.
The Confidence of Trust · 20:6–9
Now I know that YHWH saves his anointed one.
He answers him from his holy heaven
with the saving strength of his right hand.
Some trust in chariots, some in horses —
but we call on the name of YHWH our God.
They buckle and fall,
but we rise up and stand firm.
YHWH, save the king!
Answer us on the day we call.
The King’s Joy · 21:1–7
*For the music leader. A psalm of David.*
YHWH, the king rejoices in your strength.
How greatly he exults in your rescue!
You have given him his heart’s desire.
You have not held back the request of his lips. *Selah*
For you come to meet him with rich blessings.
You set a crown of fine gold on his head.
He asks you for life, and you give it to him —
length of days, forever and ever.
His glory is great because of your rescue.
You lay splendor and majesty upon him.
For you make him a blessing forever.
You fill him with the joy of your presence.
For the king trusts in YHWH,
and through the steadfast love of the Most High
he will not be shaken.
The Enemies Defeated · 21:8–13
Your hand will find all your enemies.
Your right hand will find those who hate you.
You will make them like a blazing furnace
when you appear.
YHWH will swallow them up in his anger,
and fire will consume them.
You will wipe their offspring from the earth,
their descendants from among the children of Adam.
Though they aim evil at you,
though they dream up schemes,
they will not succeed.
For you will make them turn their backs
when you aim your bowstrings at their faces.
Be lifted high, YHWH, in your strength!
We will sing and make music to your might.
The Cry of Dereliction · 22:1–2
*For the music leader. On “The Doe of the Dawn.” A psalm of David.*
My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?
Why are you so far from saving me,
so far from the words of my groaning?
My God, I call by day, and you do not answer —
and by night, and there is no rest for me.
Trust Recalled: the Fathers Were Answered · 22:3–5
Yet you are holy,
enthroned on the praises of Israel.
Our fathers trusted in you.
They trusted, and you set them free.
They cried out to you, and they got away.
They trusted in you, and they were not put to shame.
The Worm: Scorned and Taunted · 22:6–8
But I am a worm, and not a man —
scorned by everyone, despised by the people.
All who see me make a joke of me.
They curl their lips, they shake their heads:
“He rolled it all onto YHWH — let YHWH get him out!
Let him rescue him, since he delights in him!”
The God Who Held from Birth · 22:9–11
Yet you are the one who drew me out of the womb,
who made me feel safe at my mother’s breast.
Onto you I was cast from birth.
From my mother’s womb, you have been my God.
Do not be far from me,
for trouble is near,
and there is no one to help.
The Bulls of Bashan · 22:12–18
Many bulls surround me.
The mighty bulls of Bashan close in on me.
They open their mouths wide at me,
like a lion tearing and roaring.
I am poured out like water.
All my bones are pulled out of joint.
My heart has turned to wax —
it melts away inside me.
My strength is dried up like a broken pot.
My tongue sticks to the roof of my mouth.
You lay me down in the dust of death.
For dogs surround me.
A pack of evildoers circles me.
They pierce my hands and my feet.
I can count every one of my bones.
They stare at me; they gloat over me.
They divide my clothes among them,
and for my garment they throw dice.
The Turn: Praise in The Assembly · 22:19–31
But you, YHWH — do not be far away!
My strength, hurry to help me!
Rescue my soul from the sword,
my only life from the power of the dog.
Save me from the lion’s mouth!
From the horns of the wild oxen —
you have answered me!
I will tell your name to my brothers.
In the middle of the assembly I will praise you.
You who fear YHWH, praise him!
All you descendants of Jacob, give him glory!
Stand in awe of him, all you descendants of Israel!
For he has not despised or turned away from
the suffering of the one who suffers.
He has not hidden his face from him —
when he cried to him for help, he heard.
From you comes my praise in the great assembly.
I will pay my vows before those who fear him.
The poor will eat and be satisfied.
Those who seek YHWH will praise him.
May your hearts live forever!
All the ends of the earth will remember and turn back to YHWH.
All the families of the nations
will bow down before you.
For the kingdom belongs to YHWH,
and he rules over the nations.
All the prosperous of the earth will eat and bow down.
All who go down to the dust will kneel before him —
even the one who cannot keep himself alive.
Descendants will serve him.
The Lord will be told of to the next generation.
They will come and tell of his righteousness
to a people not yet born —
that he has done it.
The Shepherd and His Sheep · 23:1–4
*A psalm of David.*
YHWH is my shepherd;
there is nothing I go without.
In meadows of fresh green grass he lets me lie down.
He leads me to waters where I can rest.
He brings my soul back.
He guides me along the right tracks,
for the sake of his name.
Even when I walk through the valley of deepest shadow,
I am not afraid of any harm,
for you are with me.
Your rod and your staff —
they give me comfort.
The Host and His Guest · 23:5–6
You spread a table before me
in full view of my enemies.
You soak my head with oil.
My cup runs over.
Surely goodness and steadfast love will chase after me
all the days of my life,
and I will make my home in the house of YHWH
for days without end.
The Earth Belongs to YHWH · 24:1–2
*A psalm of David.*
The earth belongs to YHWH, and everything in it —
the world, and all who live there.
For he laid its foundations on the seas,
and set it firm upon the rivers.
The Entrance Liturgy · 24:3–6
Who may climb the mountain of YHWH?
Who may stand in his holy place?
The one with clean hands and a pure heart,
who has not lifted up his soul to what is empty,
and has not sworn to deceive.
That one will carry away a blessing from YHWH,
and vindication from the God who saves him.
This is the generation of those who seek him,
who seek your face — O Jacob. *Selah*
The King of Glory · 24:7–10
Lift up your heads, you gates!
Be lifted up, you ancient doors,
so the King of glory may come in!
Who is this King of glory?
YHWH, strong and mighty!
YHWH, mighty in battle!
Lift up your heads, you gates!
Lift them up, you ancient doors,
so the King of glory may come in!
Who is he, this King of glory?
YHWH of hosts —
he is the King of glory! *Selah*
Trust and Guidance · 25:1–7
*Of David.*
To you, YHWH, I lift up my soul.
My God, in you I trust —
do not let me be put to shame.
Do not let my enemies gloat over me.
No one who waits for you will ever be put to shame.
Shame belongs to those who betray for nothing.
Make your ways known to me, YHWH.
Teach me your paths.
Lead me in your truth, and teach me,
for you are the God who saves me.
For you I wait all day long.
Remember your compassion, YHWH, and your steadfast love,
for they have been there from of old.
The sins of my youth and my rebellions — do not remember them.
Remember me by your steadfast love,
for the sake of your goodness, YHWH.
The God Who Teaches The Humble · 25:8–15
YHWH is good and upright.
That is why he shows sinners the road.
He leads the humble in what is right,
and teaches the humble his way.
All the paths of YHWH are steadfast love and faithfulness
for those who keep his covenant and his testimonies.
For the sake of your name, YHWH,
forgive my guilt — for it is great.
Who is the one who fears YHWH?
He will show him the road to choose.
His soul will spend the night in good things,
and his descendants will inherit the land.
The friendship of YHWH is for those who fear him;
he lets them know his covenant.
My eyes are always on YHWH,
for he is the one who pulls my feet out of the net.
Loneliness, Affliction, and Hope · 25:16–22
Turn to me and be kind to me,
for I am alone and afflicted.
The troubles of my heart keep growing.
Bring me out of my distress.
Look at my affliction and my hard labor,
and carry away all my sins.
Look at my enemies — how many they are,
and how violently they hate me.
Guard my soul and rescue me.
Do not let me be put to shame,
for I take shelter in you.
Let integrity and uprightness keep watch over me,
for I wait for you.
Redeem Israel, O God,
out of all their troubles.
The Appeal for Vindication · 26:1–3
*Of David.*
Vindicate me, YHWH,
for I have walked in my integrity.
I have trusted in YHWH without wavering.
Examine me, YHWH, and put me to the test.
Refine my inmost being and my heart.
For your steadfast love is before my eyes,
and I walk in your faithfulness.
Not Among the Wicked · 26:4–8
I do not sit with the worthless,
and I do not go in with the two-faced.
I hate the gathering of evildoers.
I will not sit down with the wicked.
I wash my hands in innocence
and go around your altar, YHWH,
to make the sound of thanksgiving heard
and to tell of all your wonders.
YHWH, I love the house where you live,
the place where your glory dwells.
The Appeal for Mercy · 26:9–12
Do not sweep my soul away with sinners,
nor my life with the bloodthirsty,
whose hands are full of schemes,
whose right hands are stuffed with bribes.
But as for me — I walk in my integrity.
Redeem me, and be kind to me.
My foot stands on level ground.
In the great congregations I will bless YHWH.
The Confidence of Trust · 27:1–6
*Of David.*
YHWH is my light and my rescue —
whom should I fear?
YHWH is the fortress of my life —
of whom should I be afraid?
When evildoers close in on me to eat up my flesh —
my foes and my enemies —
it is they who stumble and fall.
Though an army camps against me,
my heart will not be afraid.
Though war rises up against me,
even then I will be confident.
One thing I ask from YHWH —
this is what I am after:
to stay in YHWH's house
every day of my life,
to take in the loveliness of YHWH
and to seek him in his temple.
For on the day of trouble he will hide me in his shelter.
He will tuck me away in the secret place of his tent.
He will set me high upon a rock.
And now my head is lifted high
above my enemies all around me.
In his tent I will offer sacrifices with shouts of joy.
I will sing, I will make music to YHWH.
The Prayer for Presence · 27:7–12
Hear my voice, YHWH, when I call!
Be kind to me and answer me!
My heart says of you, “Seek his face.”
Your face, YHWH, I will seek.
Do not hide your face from me.
Do not turn your servant away in anger —
you have been my help.
Do not leave me, do not abandon me,
O God who saves me.
Even if my father and my mother abandon me,
YHWH will take me in.
Teach me your way, YHWH.
Lead me on a level path,
because of those who lie in wait for me.
Do not hand me over to the will of my foes,
for false witnesses have risen up against me,
breathing out violence.
The Final Word: Wait · 27:13–14
If I did not believe that I would see the goodness of YHWH
in the land of the living —
Wait for YHWH!
Hold firm, and let your heart be brave.
Wait for YHWH!
The Cry · 28:1–2
*Of David.*
To you, YHWH, I call.
My rock, do not turn a deaf ear to me —
for if you keep silent toward me,
I will be like those who go down to the pit.
Hear the sound of my pleading as I cry to you for help,
as I lift my hands toward your holy inner room.
Against the Wicked · 28:3–5
Do not drag me off with the wicked,
with those who do wrong,
who speak peace to their neighbors
while evil sits in their hearts.
Give them what their deeds deserve,
what their evil actions have earned.
Give them back what their hands have done.
Pay them what is coming to them.
For they pay no attention to the deeds of YHWH,
to the work of his hands.
He will tear them down and never build them up.
Praise for the Answer · 28:6–9
Blessed be YHWH,
for he has heard the sound of my pleading!
YHWH is my strength and my shield.
My heart trusts in him, and I am helped.
My heart leaps for joy,
and with my song I give him thanks.
YHWH is the strength of his people,
a fortress of rescue for his anointed one.
Save your people, and bless your inheritance.
Be their shepherd, and carry them forever.
The Call to Worship · 29:1–2
*A psalm of David.*
Give to YHWH, you sons of the mighty —
give to YHWH glory and strength.
Give to YHWH the glory his name deserves.
Bow down to YHWH in the splendor of holiness.
The Seven Thunders · 29:3–9
The voice of YHWH is over the waters.
The God of glory thunders —
YHWH, over the mighty waters.
The voice of YHWH — in power!
The voice of YHWH — in splendor!
The voice of YHWH breaks the cedars.
YHWH shatters the cedars of Lebanon.
He makes Lebanon skip like a calf,
and Sirion like a young wild ox.
The voice of YHWH splits flames of fire.
The voice of YHWH shakes the wilderness.
YHWH shakes the wilderness of Kadesh.
The voice of YHWH makes the deer give birth
and strips the forests bare.
And in his temple everyone cries, “Glory!”
The Enthroned King · 29:10–11
YHWH sat enthroned over the flood.
YHWH sits enthroned as King forever.
YHWH gives strength to his people.
YHWH blesses his people with peace.
Testimony of Deliverance · 30:1–5
*A psalm. A song for the dedication of the house. Of David.*
I lift you high, YHWH, for you have drawn me up,
and have not let my enemies celebrate over me.
YHWH my God, I cried to you for help,
and you healed me.
YHWH, you brought my soul up from Sheol.
You kept me alive, kept me from going down to the pit.
Sing praise to YHWH, you his faithful ones,
and give thanks at the remembrance of his holiness.
For his anger lasts only a moment,
but his favor, a lifetime.
Weeping may come to spend the night,
but in the morning — a shout of joy!
The Complacency and The Cry · 30:6–10
As for me, I said when things were easy,
“I will never be shaken.”
YHWH, by your favor you had made my mountain stand strong.
You hid your face — and I was terrified.
To you, YHWH, I call.
To the Lord I plead for mercy:
“What profit is there in my blood,
if I go down to the pit?
Will the dust give you thanks?
Will it tell of your faithfulness?
Hear, YHWH, and be kind to me!
YHWH, be my helper!”
The Turn: Mourning Into Dancing · 30:11–12
You have turned my mourning into dancing.
You have loosened my sackcloth
and wrapped me in joy,
so that my glory may sing your praise and not be silent.
YHWH my God, I will give you thanks forever.
Refuge and Appeal · 31:1–8
*For the music leader. A psalm of David.*
In you, YHWH, I take shelter.
Never let me be put to shame.
In your righteousness, set me free.
Bend your ear to me — rescue me quickly!
Be a rock of refuge for me,
a fortress to save me.
For you are my cliff and my fortress.
For the sake of your name, lead me and guide me.
Bring me out of the net they have hidden for me,
for you are my refuge.
Into your hand I entrust my spirit.
You have redeemed me, YHWH, God of truth.
I hate those who cling to worthless idols,
but as for me, I trust in YHWH.
I will leap for joy and be glad in your steadfast love,
because you have seen my affliction.
You have known the distress of my soul.
You have not handed me over to the enemy.
You have set my feet in a wide-open place.
The Depths of Anguish · 31:9–13
Be kind to me, YHWH, for I am in distress.
My eye is wasting away with grief —
my soul and my body too.
For my life is spent in sorrow,
and my years in groaning.
My strength gives way because of my guilt,
and my bones waste away.
Because of all my foes I have become a disgrace —
especially to my neighbors —
and a dread to those who know me.
Those who see me in the street run from me.
I have slipped from memory like someone dead.
I have become like a broken pot.
For I hear the whispering of many —
terror on every side! —
as they plot together against me,
scheming to take my life.
The Turn: Trust and Praise · 31:14–24
But I — I trust in you, YHWH.
I say, “You are my God.”
My times are in your hand.
Rescue me from the hand of my enemies,
from those who hunt me down.
Let your face shine on your servant.
Save me in your steadfast love.
YHWH, do not let me be put to shame, for I call on you.
Let the wicked be put to shame.
Let them be silent in Sheol.
Let the lying lips be struck dumb —
the ones that speak arrogantly against the righteous,
with pride and contempt.
Oh, how great is your goodness,
which you have stored up for those who fear you,
which you have worked for those who take shelter in you,
in full sight of the children of Adam!
You hide them in the secret place of your presence
from the plots of men.
You tuck them away in a shelter
from the quarrel of tongues.
Blessed be YHWH,
for he has shown me the wonder of his steadfast love
in a city under siege.
As for me, I said in my panic,
“I am cut off from your sight.”
But you heard the sound of my pleading
when I cried to you for help.
Love YHWH, all you his faithful ones!
YHWH guards the faithful,
and pays back the arrogant in full.
Be strong, and let your heart take courage,
all you who wait for YHWH.
The Beatitude of Forgiveness · 32:1–2
*Of David. A Maskil.*
Oh, how happy is the one whose rebellion is lifted away,
whose sin is covered over!
How happy is the one to whom YHWH counts no guilt,
and in whose spirit there is no deceit!
The Weight of Unconfessed Sin · 32:3–4
When I kept silent, my bones wore away
through my groaning all day long.
For day and night your hand was heavy on me.
My strength dried up as in the heat of summer. *Selah*
Confession and Forgiveness · 32:5
Then I made my sin known to you,
and did not cover up my guilt.
I said, “I will confess my rebellion to YHWH” —
and you lifted away the guilt of my sin. *Selah*
The Hiding Place · 32:6–7
So let every faithful one pray to you
while you may be found.
Surely, when the great waters flood in,
they will not reach him.
You are my hiding place.
You guard me from trouble.
You surround me with songs of rescue. *Selah*
Divine Instruction · 32:8–10
“I will teach you and show you the road you should walk.
I will give you counsel, with my eye upon you.
Do not be like the horse or the mule, without understanding,
whose eagerness must be reined in with bit and bridle,
or else it will not come near you.”
Many are the pains of the wicked,
but the one who trusts in YHWH —
steadfast love surrounds him.
The Shout · 32:11
Be glad in YHWH and rejoice, you righteous!
Shout for joy, all you upright in heart!
The Call to Praise · 33:1–3
Shout for joy in YHWH, you righteous!
Praise looks lovely on the upright.
Give thanks to YHWH with the lyre.
Make music to him on the ten-stringed harp.
Sing him a new song.
Play skillfully, with shouts of joy.
The Creative Word · 33:4–9
For the word of YHWH is upright,
and all his work is done in faithfulness.
He loves righteousness and justice.
The earth is full of the steadfast love of YHWH.
By the word of YHWH the heavens were made,
and all their host by the breath of his mouth.
He gathers the waters of the sea like a heap.
He puts the deeps away in storehouses.
Let all the earth fear YHWH.
Let everyone who lives in the world stand in awe of him.
For he spoke, and it came to be.
He commanded, and there it stood.
Nations and Their Plans · 33:10–15
YHWH breaks up the plans of the nations.
He frustrates the schemes of the peoples.
The plan of YHWH stands forever,
the purposes of his heart from generation to generation.
Happy is the nation whose God is YHWH,
the people he has chosen as his own inheritance!
From heaven YHWH looks down.
He sees all the children of Adam.
From the place where he sits enthroned
he watches all who live on the earth —
he who shapes the hearts of them all,
who understands everything they do.
The Only Reliable Hope · 33:16–22
No king is saved by the size of his army.
No warrior is rescued by his great strength.
A horse is a false hope for victory.
For all its great power, it cannot save.
Look — the eye of YHWH is on those who fear him,
on those who hope in his steadfast love,
to rescue their souls from death
and keep them alive in famine.
Our soul waits for YHWH.
He is our help and our shield.
For in him our heart is glad,
because we trust in his holy name.
Let your steadfast love, YHWH, rest upon us,
just as we hope in you.
Praise and Invitation · 34:1–3
*Of David, when he changes his behavior before Abimelech, who drives him out, and he goes away.*
I will bless YHWH at all times.
His praise will always be in my mouth.
My soul makes its boast in YHWH.
Let the humble hear it and be glad.
Make YHWH great with me!
Let us lift his name high together!
The Testimony · 34:4–7
I sought YHWH, and he answered me.
He rescued me from all my fears.
Those who look to him are radiant.
Their faces will never be ashamed.
This poor man cried out, and YHWH heard,
and saved him out of all his troubles.
The angel of YHWH camps around those who fear him,
and he sets them free.
The Wisdom Teaching · 34:8–22
Taste and see that YHWH is good!
Happy is the one who takes shelter in him.
Fear YHWH, you his holy ones,
for those who fear him lack nothing.
Young lions go needy and hungry,
but those who seek YHWH lack no good thing.
Come, children, listen to me.
I will teach you the fear of YHWH.
Who is the one who loves life,
who longs for many days to see good things?
Keep your tongue from evil,
and your lips from speaking lies.
Turn away from evil and do good.
Seek peace — and run after it.
The eyes of YHWH are on the righteous,
and his ears are open to their cry.
The face of YHWH is set against those who do evil,
to cut off the memory of them from the earth.
They cry out, and YHWH hears.
He rescues them out of all their troubles.
YHWH is near to the brokenhearted.
He saves those whose spirit is crushed.
Many are the troubles of the righteous one,
but YHWH rescues him out of them all.
He guards all his bones —
not one of them is broken.
Evil will kill the wicked,
and those who hate the righteous will be held guilty.
YHWH redeems the life of his servants.
None who take shelter in him will be held guilty.
The Appeal for Divine Combat · 35:1–10
*Of David.*
Take up my case, YHWH, against those who take me to court.
Fight against those who fight against me.
Take hold of shield and buckler,
and rise up to help me.
Draw out the spear and the battle-axe
to meet those who chase me.
Say to my soul,
“I am your rescue.”
Let those who seek my life be put to shame and disgraced.
Let those who plot my harm be turned back and humiliated.
Let them be like chaff before the wind,
with the angel of YHWH driving them on.
Let their road be dark and slippery,
with the angel of YHWH chasing them.
For without cause they hid their net for me;
without cause they dug a pit for my life.
Let ruin come on him when he does not expect it.
Let the net he hid catch him;
let him fall into it — to his ruin.
Then my soul will leap for joy in YHWH
and celebrate his rescue.
All my bones will say,
“YHWH, who is like you?
You rescue the poor from the one too strong for him,
the poor and needy from the one who robs him.”
The Treachery of False Witnesses · 35:11–18
Violent witnesses rise up.
They question me about things I know nothing of.
They pay me back evil for good.
My soul is left bereaved.
But I — when they were sick, I put on sackcloth.
I humbled my soul with fasting,
and my prayer kept coming back to my own chest.
I went about as though grieving a friend or a brother.
I bowed down in mourning,
like one weeping for his mother.
But when I stumble, they gather in glee.
They gather against me —
attackers I do not even know.
They tear at me without stopping.
Like godless mockers at a feast,
they grind their teeth at me.
Lord, how long will you look on?
Bring my soul back from their ruin,
my only life from the young lions.
I will give you thanks in the great assembly.
Among a mighty throng I will praise you.
Final Appeal and Praise · 35:19–28
Do not let those who are my enemies for no reason gloat over me.
Do not let those who hate me without cause wink their eyes.
For they do not speak peace.
Against the quiet ones of the land
they dream up words of deceit.
They open their mouths wide against me.
They say, “Aha! Aha!
Our eyes have seen it!”
You have seen it, YHWH — do not keep silent!
Lord, do not be far from me!
Wake up! Rouse yourself to my defense —
to my cause, my God and my Lord!
Vindicate me by your righteousness, YHWH my God.
Do not let them gloat over me.
Do not let them say in their hearts, “Aha — just what we wanted!”
Do not let them say, “We have swallowed him up.”
Let all who celebrate my trouble
be put to shame and humiliated together.
Let those who exalt themselves over me
be clothed with shame and disgrace.
Let those who delight in my vindication
shout for joy and be glad.
Let them say forever, “Great is YHWH,
who delights in the peace of his servant!”
Then my tongue will murmur your righteousness,
your praise all day long.
The Wicked and Their Self-deception · 36:1–4
*For the music leader. Of David, the servant of YHWH.*
Rebellion speaks to the wicked one
deep inside his heart.
There is no dread of God
before his eyes.
For he flatters himself in his own eyes
that his guilt will never be found out and hated.
The words of his mouth are trouble and deceit.
He has stopped being wise and doing good.
He plots trouble while lying on his bed.
He sets himself on a road that is not good.
He does not reject evil.
The Boundless Hesed of God · 36:5–9
YHWH, your steadfast love reaches to the heavens,
your faithfulness to the clouds.
Your righteousness is like the mighty mountains,
your judgments like the great deep.
Human and animal alike, you save, YHWH.
How precious is your steadfast love, O God!
The children of Adam take shelter in the shadow of your wings.
They drink their fill of the rich food of your house.
You give them drink from your river of delights.
For with you is the fountain of life.
In your light we see light.
The Prayer · 36:10–12
Keep on showing your steadfast love to those who know you,
and your righteousness to the upright in heart.
Do not let the foot of the proud come against me,
or the hand of the wicked drive me away.
There the evildoers lie fallen —
thrust down, and they cannot rise.
The Portion of the Righteous and the Wicked · 37:1–40
*Of David.*
א — Do not fume over evildoers.
Do not envy those who do wrong.
For like grass they will soon wither,
and like green growth they will fade.
ב — Trust in YHWH, and do good.
Settle in the land, and feed on faithfulness.
Take your delight in YHWH,
and he will give you what your heart asks for.
ג — Roll your way onto YHWH.
Trust in him — and he will act.
He will bring out your righteousness like the light,
your justice like the blaze of noon.
ד — Be still before YHWH, and wait for him with longing.
Do not fume over the one whose way prospers,
over the man who carries out his schemes.
ה — Let go of anger, and leave rage behind.
Do not fume — it leads only to evil.
For evildoers will be cut off,
but those who wait for YHWH —
they will inherit the land.
ו — Just a little while longer, and the wicked will be no more.
You will look carefully at his place,
and he will not be there.
But the humble will inherit the land,
and delight themselves in abundant peace.
ז — The wicked one plots against the righteous
and grinds his teeth at him.
But the Lord laughs at him,
for he sees that his day is coming.
ח — The wicked draw the sword and bend the bow
to bring down the poor and needy,
to slaughter those whose way is upright.
Their sword will go into their own hearts,
and their bows will be broken.
ט — Better is the little that the righteous one has
than the wealth of many wicked.
For the arms of the wicked will be broken,
but YHWH holds up the righteous.
י — YHWH knows the days of the blameless,
and their inheritance will last forever.
They will not be put to shame in evil times.
In days of famine they will have plenty.
כ — But the wicked will perish.
The enemies of YHWH are like the glory of the pastures —
they vanish; like smoke they vanish away.
ל — The wicked one borrows and does not pay back,
but the righteous one is generous and gives.
For those blessed by YHWH will inherit the land,
but those cursed by him will be cut off.
מ — By YHWH a man’s steps are made firm,
when he delights in his way.
Though he falls, he will not be thrown down,
for YHWH holds his hand.
נ — I have been young, and now I am old,
and I have never seen the righteous abandoned
or his children begging for bread.
All day long he is generous and lends,
and his children become a blessing.
ס — Turn away from evil, and do good,
and you will dwell secure forever.
For YHWH loves justice,
and he will not abandon his faithful ones.
ע — They are kept safe forever,
but the children of the wicked will be cut off.
The righteous will inherit the land
and live in it forever.
פ — The mouth of the righteous one murmurs wisdom,
and his tongue speaks what is just.
The Torah of his God is in his heart.
His steps do not slip.
צ — The wicked one watches for the righteous
and looks for a way to kill him.
YHWH will not leave him in his hand,
or let him be condemned when he is brought to trial.
ק — Wait for YHWH, and keep to his way,
and he will lift you up to inherit the land.
When the wicked are cut off, you will see it.
ר — I have seen a wicked man, ruthless,
spreading himself out like a lush native tree.
Then he passed away, and look — he was gone.
I searched for him, but he could not be found.
ש — Watch the blameless one, and look at the upright,
for there is a future for the man of peace.
But rebels will be destroyed together.
The future of the wicked is cut off.
ת — The rescue of the righteous comes from YHWH.
He is their fortress in the time of trouble.
YHWH helps them and sets them free.
He sets them free from the wicked and saves them,
because they take shelter in him.
The Prayer of a Penitent in Affliction · 38:1–22
*A psalm of David. For remembrance.*
YHWH, do not correct me in your fury.
Do not discipline me in your heat.
For your arrows have sunk into me,
and your hand has come down hard on me.
There is no soundness in my flesh because of your indignation.
There is no peace in my bones because of my sin.
For my guilt has gone over my head.
Like a heavy load, it is too heavy for me.
My wounds stink and fester
because of my foolishness.
I am bent over, bowed down to the ground.
All day long I go around in mourning.
For my loins are filled with burning,
and there is no soundness in my flesh.
I am numb and utterly crushed.
I groan from the turmoil of my heart.
Lord, all my longing is laid out before you.
My sighing is not hidden from you.
My heart pounds, my strength has left me,
and even the light of my eyes is gone.
My friends and companions stand back from my plague.
My neighbors keep their distance.
Those who seek my life set their traps.
Those who want me harmed speak of ruin.
All day long they murmur deceit.
But I am like a deaf man — I do not hear,
like a mute who does not open his mouth.
I have become like a man who cannot hear,
who has no answer in his mouth.
For I wait for you, YHWH.
You will answer, Lord my God.
For I said, “Do not let them gloat over me,
those who boast against me when my foot slips.”
For I am ready to fall,
and my pain is always before me.
I confess my guilt.
I am troubled by my sin.
But my enemies are full of life and strength.
Many are those who hate me for no reason.
Those who repay evil for good
accuse me because I pursue what is good.
Do not abandon me, YHWH.
My God, do not be far from me.
Hurry to help me,
Lord, my rescue!
The Brevity of Life · 39:1–13
*For the music leader. For Jeduthun. A psalm of David.*
I said, “I will guard my ways
so that I do not sin with my tongue.
I will keep a muzzle on my mouth
as long as the wicked are in front of me.”
I went silent, I said nothing.
I kept quiet even from good —
and my pain was stirred up.
My heart grew hot within me.
As I brooded, the fire burned.
Then I spoke with my tongue:
“Let me know my end, YHWH,
and what is the measure of my days.
Let me know how fleeting I am.
Look — you have made my days a few handbreadths,
and my lifetime is as nothing before you.
Every human being, standing tall, is only a breath. *Selah*
Each one walks about as a mere shadow.
They make their noise for nothing.
He piles up riches,
and does not know who will gather them in.
And now, Lord, what am I waiting for?
My hope is in you.
Rescue me from all my rebellions.
Do not make me the taunt of the fool.
I have gone silent; I do not open my mouth,
for you are the one who has done this.
Take your blow away from me.
I am worn out by the force of your hand.
With rebukes for guilt you discipline a man.
Like a moth you eat away what he treasures.
Every human being is only a breath. *Selah*
Hear my prayer, YHWH.
Give ear to my cry for help.
Do not be silent at my tears.
For I am a guest with you,
a passing stranger, like all my fathers.
Look away from me, so that I may smile again,
before I go away and am no more.”
Thanksgiving for Deliverance · 40:1–10
*For the music leader. Of David. A psalm.*
I waited and waited for YHWH,
and he bent down to me
and heard my cry for help.
He drew me up out of the roaring pit,
out of the muddy clay.
He set my feet on a rock
and made my steps steady.
He put a new song in my mouth,
a song of praise to our God.
Many will see and fear,
and put their trust in YHWH.
Happy is the man who makes YHWH his trust,
who does not turn to the proud,
or to those who wander off after lies.
Many are the wonders you have done, YHWH my God,
and your plans for us —
no one can compare with you!
If I were to tell them and speak of them,
they would be too many to count.
Sacrifice and offering you do not desire —
you have dug open my ears.
Burnt offering and sin offering you have not asked for.
Then I said, “Here I am — I have come.
In the scroll of the book it is written about me.
To do your will, my God, is my delight.
Your Torah is deep within me.”
I have told the good news of righteousness in the great assembly.
Look — I have not held back my lips,
as you know, YHWH.
I have not hidden your righteousness inside my heart.
I have spoken of your faithfulness and your rescue.
I have not concealed your steadfast love and your truth
from the great assembly.
A Prayer for Help · 40:11–17
You, YHWH — do not hold back your compassion from me.
Let your steadfast love and your truth always keep me safe.
For troubles beyond counting have surrounded me.
My guilt has caught up with me, and I cannot see.
They are more than the hairs of my head,
and my heart has failed me.
Be pleased, YHWH, to rescue me.
YHWH, hurry to help me!
Let those who seek to snatch away my life
be put to shame and humiliated together.
Let those who delight in my harm
be turned back and disgraced.
Let those who say to me, “Aha! Aha!”
be appalled at their own shame.
But let all who seek you
leap for joy and be glad in you.
Let those who love your rescue
always say, “YHWH is great!”
As for me, I am poor and needy,
but the Lord is thinking of me.
You are my help and the one who sets me free.
My God, do not delay!
Blessed Is the One Who Considers the Poor · 41:1–12
*For the music leader. A psalm of David.*
Happy is the one who pays attention to the weak!
On the day of trouble YHWH will set him free.
YHWH will guard him and keep him alive.
He will be called happy in the land.
You will not hand him over to the will of his enemies.
YHWH will hold him up on his sickbed.
In his illness you turn his whole bed around.
As for me, I said, “YHWH, be kind to me.
Heal my soul, for I have sinned against you.”
My enemies speak evil of me:
“When will he die, and his name perish?”
And if one comes to see me, he speaks emptiness.
His heart gathers trouble for itself;
he goes outside and tells it around.
All who hate me whisper together against me.
They plot the worst for me:
“Something deadly has been poured into him.
Now that he lies down, he will never get up again.”
Even my close friend, whom I trusted,
who ate my bread,
has lifted his heel against me.
But you, YHWH — be kind to me, and raise me up,
so that I may pay them back.
By this I know that you delight in me:
my enemy does not shout in triumph over me.
As for me, you hold me up in my integrity,
and set me in your presence forever.
Doxology: the End of Book One · 41:13
Blessed be YHWH, the God of Israel,
from everlasting to everlasting.
Amen and amen.
Longing for God · 42:1–11
*For the music leader. A Maskil of the sons of Korah.*
Like a deer that longs for streams of water,
so my soul longs for you, O God.
My soul is thirsty for God, for the living God.
When can I come and appear before the face of God?
My tears have been my bread day and night,
while all day long they say to me,
“Where is your God?”
These things I remember as I pour out my soul:
how I used to walk with the crowd,
leading them in procession to the house of God,
with shouts of joy and songs of thanks —
a throng keeping festival.
Why are you so low, my soul?
Why are you groaning inside me?
Wait for God —
for I will yet give him thanks,
the rescue of his face.
My God, my soul is low within me.
So I remember you from the land of the Jordan,
from the peaks of Hermon, from Mount Mizar.
Deep calls to deep
at the roar of your waterfalls.
All your breakers and your waves
have rolled over me.
By day YHWH sends out his steadfast love,
and in the night his song is with me —
a prayer to the God of my life.
I say to God, my rock,
“Why have you forgotten me?
Why must I go about in mourning,
pressed down by the enemy?”
Like a crushing in my bones,
my foes taunt me,
saying to me all day long,
“Where is your God?”
Why are you so low, my soul?
Why are you groaning inside me?
Wait for God —
for I will yet give him thanks,
the rescue of my face, and my God.
A Prayer for Vindication · 43:1–5
Vindicate me, O God, and take up my case
against a faithless nation.
From the man of deceit and wrong, set me free.
For you are the God of my stronghold —
why have you rejected me?
Why must I walk about in mourning,
pressed down by the enemy?
Send out your light and your truth —
let them lead me.
Let them bring me to your holy mountain,
to the places where you dwell.
Then I will go to the altar of God,
to God, the gladness of my joy,
and I will thank you on the lyre,
O God, my God.
Why are you so low, my soul?
Why are you groaning inside me?
Wait for God —
for I will yet give him thanks,
the rescue of my face, and my God.
What God Did in Days of Old · 44:1–8
*For the music leader. Of the sons of Korah. A Maskil.*
O God, we have heard it with our own ears.
Our fathers have told us
the work you did in their days,
in the days of long ago.
You, with your own hand, drove out the nations,
and planted our fathers.
You struck down the peoples,
and set our fathers free to spread out.
For it was not by their sword that they took the land,
and their own arm did not save them —
it was your right hand, and your arm,
and the light of your face,
because you delighted in them.
You are my King, O God.
Command victories for Jacob!
Through you we push back our foes.
Through your name we trample those who rise against us.
For I do not trust in my bow,
and my sword will not save me.
It is you who have saved us from our foes,
and put to shame those who hate us.
In God we have boasted all day long,
and we will give thanks to your name forever. *Selah*
Rejected, Yet Faithful · 44:9–26
But now you have rejected us and disgraced us.
You do not go out with our armies.
You make us turn back from the foe,
and those who hate us plunder us at will.
You hand us over like sheep for the slaughter.
You have scattered us among the nations.
You sell your people for a trifle.
You make no profit from the price.
You make us the scorn of our neighbors,
the mockery and ridicule of all around us.
You make us a byword among the nations,
a shaking of heads among the peoples.
All day long my disgrace is in front of me,
and shame has covered my face,
at the voice of the one who taunts and reviles,
at the sight of the enemy and the avenger.
All this has come upon us,
yet we have not forgotten you.
We have not been false to your covenant.
Our heart has not turned back,
nor have our steps strayed from your path —
yet you have crushed us in the haunt of jackals
and covered us over with the shadow of death.
If we had forgotten the name of our God,
or spread out our hands to a foreign god,
would God not search it out?
For he knows the secrets of the heart.
Yet for your sake we are being killed all day long.
We are counted as sheep for the slaughter.
Wake up! Why are you sleeping, Lord?
Rouse yourself! Do not reject us forever!
Why do you hide your face?
Why do you forget our affliction and our oppression?
For our soul is bowed down to the dust.
Our bodies cling to the ground.
Rise up — come help us!
Redeem us, for the sake of your steadfast love.
A Song for the King · 45:1–9
*For the music leader. On “The Lilies.” Of the sons of Korah. A Maskil. A love song.*
My heart is stirring with a good word.
I speak my verses to the king.
My tongue is the pen of a quick scribe.
You are the most handsome of the children of Adam.
Grace is poured out on your lips.
That is why God has blessed you forever.
Strap your sword on your thigh, O mighty one —
your splendor and your majesty!
In your majesty ride on to victory,
for the cause of truth, and humility, and righteousness.
Let your right hand teach you awesome deeds.
Your arrows are sharp —
peoples fall beneath you —
into the heart of the king’s enemies.
Your throne, O God, is forever and ever.
A scepter of uprightness is the scepter of your kingdom.
You love righteousness and hate wickedness.
That is why God, your God, has anointed you
with the oil of gladness above your companions.
All your robes are fragrant with myrrh and aloes and cassia.
From ivory palaces, stringed music makes you glad.
Daughters of kings are among your honored women.
At your right hand stands the queen
in gold of Ophir.
A Song for the Bride · 45:10–17
Listen, daughter — look, and bend your ear.
Forget your people and your father’s house,
and the king will long for your beauty.
He is your lord — bow down to him.
The daughter of Tyre comes with a gift.
The richest of the people seek your favor.
All glorious is the king’s daughter within.
Her gown is woven with gold.
In embroidered robes she is led to the king.
Her maiden companions follow behind her,
brought to you.
They are led in with gladness and joy.
They enter the palace of the king.
In place of your fathers will be your sons.
You will make them princes in all the earth.
I will make your name remembered in every generation.
So the peoples will praise you forever and ever.
God Is Our Refuge and Strength · 46:1–11
*For the music leader. Of the sons of Korah. On Alamoth. A song.*
God is our shelter and our strength,
a help in trouble, always found close by.
So we will not fear when the ground gives way,
though the mountains topple into the heart of the sea,
though its waters roar and foam,
though the mountains quake at its surging. *Selah*
There is a river — its channels bring joy to God's city,
the holy dwelling of the Most High.
God is in the middle of her — she will not be shaken.
God will help her as the morning breaks.
Nations roar, kingdoms totter.
He lifts his voice, and the earth melts.
YHWH of hosts is with us.
The God of Jacob is our high stronghold. *Selah*
Come and see the works of YHWH,
the desolations he has brought on the earth.
He makes wars stop to the ends of the earth.
He breaks the bow and snaps the spear.
He burns the chariots with fire.
“Let go, and know that I am God.
I will be lifted high among the nations.
I will be lifted high in the earth.”
YHWH of hosts is with us.
The God of Jacob is our high stronghold. *Selah*
God Is King over All the Earth · 47:1–9
*For the music leader. Of the sons of Korah. A psalm.*
All you peoples, clap your hands!
Shout to God with a ringing cry of joy!
For YHWH, the Most High, is awesome,
a great King over all the earth.
He brings peoples under us,
and nations under our feet.
He chooses our inheritance for us,
the pride of Jacob, whom he loves. *Selah*
God goes up with a shout,
YHWH with the blast of the shofar.
Sing praise to God — sing praise!
Sing praise to our King — sing praise!
For God is King of all the earth.
Sing praise with a skillful song!
God reigns over the nations.
God sits on his holy throne.
The nobles of the peoples gather
as the people of the God of Abraham.
For the shields of the earth belong to God —
he is lifted high above all.
The City of Our God · 48:1–14
*A song. A psalm of the sons of Korah.*
Great is YHWH, and greatly to be praised,
in the city of our God, his holy mountain.
Beautiful in its height, the joy of all the earth,
is Mount Zion, the heights of the north,
the city of the great King.
God, in her palaces,
has made himself known as a high stronghold.
For look — the kings joined forces.
They advanced together.
They saw — and they were stunned.
They panicked; they ran in terror.
Trembling took hold of them there,
pain like a woman in labor,
as when the east wind
shatters the ships of Tarshish.
Just as we have heard, so we have seen
in the city of YHWH of hosts, in the city of our God.
God makes her stand firm forever. *Selah*
We have pondered your steadfast love, O God,
in the middle of your temple.
Like your name, O God,
so your praise reaches to the ends of the earth.
Your right hand is full of righteousness.
Let Mount Zion be glad!
Let the daughters of Judah leap for joy
because of your judgments!
Walk around Zion, go all the way around her.
Count her towers.
Take note of her ramparts.
Go through her palaces,
so that you can tell the next generation
that this is God,
our God forever and ever.
He will guide us beyond death.
The Folly of Trusting in Riches · 49:1–20
*For the music leader. Of the sons of Korah. A psalm.*
Hear this, all you peoples!
Listen, all who live in this passing world —
low and high alike,
rich and poor together.
My mouth will speak wisdom,
and the murmuring of my heart, understanding.
I will bend my ear to a proverb.
I will open my riddle on the lyre.
Why should I be afraid in days of trouble,
when the guilt of those who dog my heels surrounds me —
those who trust in their wealth
and boast of their great riches?
No one can ever redeem his brother,
or pay God a ransom for him —
the redemption of a life costs too much,
and it can never be enough —
so that he could live on forever
and never see the pit.
For he sees that even the wise die.
The fool and the brute perish together,
and leave their wealth to others.
Their graves are their homes forever,
their dwelling places from generation to generation,
though they once named lands after themselves.
But a human being in his splendor does not stay the night.
He is like the beasts that perish.
This is the road of those who trust in themselves,
and of those who come after them, who approve their words. *Selah*
Like sheep they are herded into Sheol.
Death is their shepherd.
The upright will rule over them in the morning,
and their form will waste away in Sheol,
far from their lofty home.
But God will redeem my soul from the grip of Sheol,
for he will take me. *Selah*
Do not be afraid when someone grows rich,
when the glory of his house increases.
For when he dies he will take nothing with him.
His glory will not go down after him.
Though while he lives he blesses his own soul —
and people praise you when you do well for yourself —
he will go to the generation of his fathers,
who will never again see the light.
A human being in his splendor, without understanding,
is like the beasts that perish.
God the Righteous Judge · 50:1–15
*A psalm of Asaph.*
The Mighty One, God, YHWH, speaks
and summons the earth
from the rising of the sun to its setting.
Out of Zion, perfect in beauty,
God shines forth.
Our God comes, and he does not keep silent.
Fire devours in front of him,
and a storm rages all around him.
He calls to the heavens above,
and to the earth,
to judge his people:
“Gather to me my faithful ones,
who made a covenant with me by sacrifice!”
The heavens declare his righteousness,
for God himself is judge. *Selah*
“Listen, my people, and I will speak.
Israel, I will testify against you.
I am God, your God.
It is not for your sacrifices that I rebuke you —
your burnt offerings are always before me.
I will not take a bull from your house,
or goats from your pens.
For every animal of the forest is mine,
the cattle on a thousand hills.
I know every bird of the mountains,
and everything that moves in the field is mine.
If I were hungry, I would not tell you,
for the world is mine, and all that fills it.
Do I eat the flesh of bulls,
or drink the blood of goats?
Offer thanksgiving as your sacrifice to God,
and pay your vows to the Most High.
Call on me on the day of trouble.
I will rescue you, and you will honor me.”
The Rebuke of the Wicked · 50:16–23
But to the wicked God says:
“What right have you to recite my statutes,
or to take my covenant on your lips?
For you hate discipline,
and you throw my words behind you.
When you see a thief, you are pleased with him,
and you throw in your lot with adulterers.
You let your mouth loose for evil,
and your tongue harnesses deceit.
You sit and speak against your brother.
You slander your own mother’s son.
These things you have done, and I kept silent.
You thought I was just like you.
But now I rebuke you,
and lay it all out before your eyes.
Understand this, you who forget God,
or I will tear you apart, with no one to rescue.
The one who offers thanksgiving as his sacrifice honors me.
To the one who keeps to the road,
I will show the rescue of God.”
Have Mercy on Me, O God · 51:1–12
*For the music leader. A psalm of David, when Nathan the prophet comes to him after he has gone in to Bathsheba.*
Be kind to me, O God, as your steadfast love is kind.
As your compassion is vast,
wipe out my rebellions.
Wash me through and through from my guilt,
and make me clean from my sin.
For I know my rebellions,
and my sin is always in front of me.
It is you, you alone, I have wronged;
I did what you call evil, right before your eyes,
so that you are right when you speak
and blameless when you judge.
Look — I was born in guilt.
In sin my mother conceived me.
Look — you desire truth in the inner depths.
In the hidden place you teach me wisdom.
Scrub me with hyssop, and I will be clean.
Wash me, and I will be brighter than snow.
Let me hear joy and gladness.
Let the bones you have crushed dance again.
Hide your face from my sins,
and wipe out all my guilt.
Create a clean heart in me, O God,
and make a steady spirit new within me.
Do not throw me away from your presence.
Do not take your Holy Spirit from me.
Give me back the joy of your rescue,
and hold me up with a willing spirit.
The Sacrifices of God · 51:13–19
Then I will teach rebels your ways,
and sinners will turn back to you.
Rescue me from bloodguilt, O God,
God who saves me,
and my tongue will sing out your righteousness.
Lord, unseal my lips,
and my mouth will tell out your praise.
For you take no pleasure in sacrifice, or I would give it.
A burnt offering would not please you.
What God wants as sacrifice is a broken spirit.
A heart broken and ground down, O God,
you will never turn away.
Do good to Zion in your favor.
Build up the walls of Jerusalem.
Then you will delight in right sacrifices,
in burnt offerings and whole offerings.
Then bulls will go up on your altar.
The Judgment of the Boastful · 52:1–9
*For the music leader. A Maskil of David, when Doeg the Edomite comes and tells Saul, “David has gone to the house of Ahimelech.”*
Why do you boast of evil, you mighty man?
The steadfast love of God lasts all day long.
Your tongue plots ruin,
like a sharpened razor,
you worker of deceit.
You love evil more than good,
lying more than speaking what is right. *Selah*
You love every word that devours,
you deceitful tongue.
But God will tear you down forever.
He will snatch you up and pluck you from your tent.
He will uproot you from the land of the living. *Selah*
The righteous will see and be filled with awe,
and they will laugh at him:
“Look at the man who would not make God his stronghold,
but trusted in his great wealth
and grew strong in his ruin!”
But I am like a green olive tree in the house of God.
I trust in the steadfast love of God forever and ever.
I will give you thanks forever, for what you have done.
I will wait on your name, for it is good,
in the presence of your faithful ones.
The Fool Says There Is No God · 53:1–6
*For the music leader. On Mahalath. A Maskil of David.*
The fool says in his heart, “There is no God.”
They are corrupt, their wrongdoing is vile —
there is no one who does good.
God looks down from heaven on the children of Adam
to see if there is anyone who understands,
anyone who seeks God.
Every one of them has turned back; together they have gone sour.
There is no one who does good — not even one.
Do they know nothing, these evildoers?
They eat up my people the way they eat bread,
and they never call on God.
There they are, in sheer terror —
where there was nothing to fear.
For God scatters the bones of the one who camps against you.
You put them to shame, for God has rejected them.
Oh, that Israel’s rescue would come out of Zion!
When God brings his people home again,
let Jacob leap for joy, let Israel be glad!
God Is My Helper · 54:1–7
*For the music leader. With stringed instruments. A Maskil of David, when the Ziphites come and say to Saul, “Isn’t David hiding among us?”*
O God, save me by your name,
and defend my cause by your might.
O God, hear my prayer.
Give ear to the words of my mouth.
For strangers have risen against me,
and ruthless men seek my life.
They do not set God before them. *Selah*
Look — God is my helper.
The Lord is the one who holds up my life.
He will turn the evil back on those who lie in wait for me.
In your faithfulness, put an end to them.
With a freewill offering I will sacrifice to you.
I will give thanks to your name, YHWH, for it is good.
For he has rescued me from every trouble,
and my eye has looked in triumph on my enemies.
Cast Your Burden on YHWH · 55:1–11
*For the music leader. With stringed instruments. A Maskil of David.*
Give ear to my prayer, O God.
Do not hide yourself from my plea.
Pay attention to me, and answer me.
I am restless in my complaint, and I moan
at the voice of the enemy,
at the pressure of the wicked.
For they bring down trouble on me,
and in anger they hold a grudge against me.
My heart writhes within me.
The terrors of death have fallen on me.
Fear and trembling come over me,
and horror has covered me.
And I say, “Oh, that I had wings like a dove!
I would fly away and be at rest.
Look — I would wander far away.
I would spend the night in the wilderness. *Selah*
I would hurry to my place of escape,
away from the raging wind and the storm.”
Confuse them, Lord — split their tongues!
For I see violence and strife in the city.
Day and night they go around her on her walls,
and trouble and misery are inside her.
Ruin is in the middle of her.
Oppression and deceit never leave her square.
It Was Not an Enemy · 55:12–23
For it is not an enemy who taunts me —
that I could bear.
It is not one who hates me who lifts himself up against me —
I could hide from him.
But it is you, a man like myself,
my companion, my close friend.
We used to share sweet counsel together.
We walked with the throng into the house of God.
Let death come on them by surprise!
Let them go down to Sheol alive,
for evil is in their homes, in their very hearts.
As for me, I call on God,
and YHWH will save me.
Evening and morning and noon
I pour out my complaint and moan,
and he hears my voice.
He redeems my soul in peace
from the battle against me,
for many were arrayed against me.
God will hear and humble them —
he who sits enthroned from of old. *Selah*
For they do not change,
and they do not fear God.
He has stretched out his hand against his friends.
He has broken his covenant.
His mouth is smoother than butter,
but war is in his heart.
His words are softer than oil,
but they are drawn swords.
Throw your burden on YHWH,
and he will hold you up.
He will never let the righteous be shaken.
But you, O God, will bring them down
into the pit of destruction.
Men of blood and deceit
will not live out half their days.
But as for me, I will trust in you.
Trust in God When I Am Afraid · 56:1–13
*For the music leader. On “The Silent Dove of Far-Off Places.” Of David. A Miktam, when the Philistines seize him in Gath.*
Be kind to me, O God, for a man is panting after me.
All day long the attacker presses me hard.
My foes pant after me all day long,
for many are fighting against me, O Most High.
On the day I am afraid,
I put my trust in you.
In God, whose word I praise —
in God I trust; I am not afraid.
What can mere flesh do to me?
All day long they twist my words.
All their thoughts are bent on harming me.
They gather, they lie in hiding.
They watch my heels,
as they wait to take my life.
Because of their wickedness, will they escape?
In anger bring down the peoples, O God!
You have kept count of my wanderings.
Put my tears in your bottle.
Are they not in your book?
Then my enemies will turn back
on the day I call.
This I know — God is for me.
In God, whose word I praise,
in YHWH, whose word I praise —
in God I trust; I am not afraid.
What can a human being do to me?
Your vows are upon me, O God.
I will pay you thank offerings.
For you have rescued my soul from death —
yes, my feet from stumbling —
so that I may walk before God
in the light of the living.
My Heart Is Steadfast · 57:1–11
*For the music leader. On “Do Not Destroy.” Of David. A Miktam, when he runs from Saul into the cave.*
Be kind to me, O God, be kind to me,
for in you my soul takes shelter.
In the shadow of your wings I take shelter
until the storms of ruin pass by.
I cry out to God Most High,
to God, who finishes what he has begun for me.
He will send from heaven and save me.
He shames the one who pants after me. *Selah*
God will send out his steadfast love and his faithfulness.
My soul is in the middle of lions.
I lie down among those who breathe fire —
the children of Adam,
whose teeth are spears and arrows,
whose tongue is a sharp sword.
Be lifted high above the heavens, O God!
Let your glory be over all the earth!
They set a net for my steps.
My soul was bowed down.
They dug a pit in front of me —
and they have fallen into it themselves. *Selah*
My heart is steady, O God, my heart is steady!
I will sing and make music!
Wake up, my glory!
Wake up, harp and lyre!
I will wake up the dawn!
I will give you thanks among the peoples, Lord.
I will sing your praise among the nations.
For your steadfast love is great, reaching to the heavens,
and your faithfulness to the clouds.
Be lifted high above the heavens, O God!
Let your glory be over all the earth!
A Plea Against Unjust Rulers · 58:1–11
*For the music leader. On “Do Not Destroy.” Of David. A Miktam.*
Do you really speak justice, you mighty ones?
Do you judge the children of Adam fairly?
No — in your hearts you work out wrongs.
In the land you weigh out the violence of your hands.
The wicked go astray from the womb.
The liars wander off from birth.
They have venom like the venom of a snake,
like a deaf cobra that stops its ears,
that will not hear the voice of the charmers,
however skillful the spell-caster.
O God, break the teeth in their mouths!
Tear out the fangs of the young lions, YHWH!
Let them drain away like water that runs off.
When he aims his arrows, let them be as though cut off.
Let them be like a snail that melts away as it goes,
like a stillborn child that never sees the sun.
Before your pots can feel the heat of the thorns,
green or burning, he will sweep them away.
The righteous one will rejoice when he sees vengeance.
He will wash his feet in the blood of the wicked.
And people will say, “Surely there is fruit for the righteous!
Surely there is a God who judges on the earth!”
Deliver Me from My Enemies · 59:1–17
*For the music leader. On “Do Not Destroy.” Of David. A Miktam, when Saul sends men, and they watch the house in order to kill him.*
Rescue me from my enemies, my God.
Set me high above those who rise up against me.
Rescue me from those who do wrong.
Save me from men of blood.
For look — they lie in wait for my life.
Fierce men band together against me —
not for any rebellion or sin of mine, YHWH.
For no guilt of mine they run and take their positions.
Wake up to meet me, and see!
You, YHWH, God of Armies, God of Israel —
rouse yourself to punish all the nations!
Show no favor to any treacherous evildoer. *Selah*
They come back at evening,
snarling like dogs,
and prowl around the city.
Look — they spew from their mouths,
swords are on their lips —
for “Who is listening?”
But you, YHWH, laugh at them.
You hold all the nations in derision.
O my Strength, I will watch for you,
for God is my high stronghold.
My God, in his steadfast love, will come to meet me.
God will let me look in triumph on my foes.
Do not kill them, or my people may forget.
Make them stagger by your power, and bring them down,
O Lord, our shield.
For the sin of their mouths, the words of their lips,
let them be caught in their pride.
For the cursing and lies they tell,
finish them in your wrath — finish them, until they are no more.
Then let them know that God rules over Jacob
to the ends of the earth. *Selah*
They come back at evening,
snarling like dogs,
and prowl around the city.
They wander about looking for food,
and if they are not satisfied, they howl all night.
But I will sing of your strength.
I will shout for joy at your steadfast love in the morning.
For you have been a high stronghold for me,
a place to run on the day of my distress.
O my Strength, I will sing praise to you,
for God is my high stronghold,
the God of my steadfast love.
A Prayer After Defeat · 60:1–12

*For the music leader. On “The Lily of Testimony.” A Miktam of David, for teaching, when he fights Aram-naharaim and Aram-zobah, and Joab turns back and strikes down twelve thousand of Edom in the Valley of Salt.*
O God, you have rejected us. You have broken through our defenses.
You have been angry — now bring us back!
You have made the land quake; you have split it open.
Mend its cracks, for it is tottering.
You have made your people see hard things.
You have given us wine that makes us stagger.
You have raised a banner for those who fear you,
to rally to, out of reach of the bow. *Selah*
So that your beloved ones may be set free,
save with your right hand, and answer us!
God has spoken in his holiness:
“I will exult — I will divide up Shechem
and measure out the Valley of Succoth.
Gilead is mine, and Manasseh is mine.
Ephraim is the helmet on my head.
Judah is my scepter.
Moab is my washbasin.
On Edom I toss my sandal.
Over Philistia I raise my battle cry.”
Who will bring me into the fortified city?
Who will lead me to Edom?
Have you not rejected us, O God?
You do not go out, O God, with our armies.
Give us help against the foe,
for the help of human beings is worthless.
With God we will do mighty things,
and he will trample our foes.
The Rock That Is Higher Than I · 61:1–8
*For the music leader. On stringed instruments. Of David.*
Hear my cry, O God.
Listen to my prayer.
From the end of the earth I call to you
as my heart grows faint.
Lead me to the rock that is too high for me.
For you have been my shelter,
a strong tower against the enemy.
Let me stay as a guest in your tent forever.
Let me take shelter under the cover of your wings. *Selah*
For you, O God, have heard my vows.
You have given me the inheritance of those who fear your name.
Add days to the days of the king.
Let his years go on for generation after generation.
Let him sit enthroned before God forever.
Appoint steadfast love and faithfulness to watch over him.
So I will sing praise to your name forever,
as I pay my vows day after day.
My Soul Waits in Silence · 62:1–12
*For the music leader. For Jeduthun. A psalm of David.*
For God alone my soul waits in silence.
My rescue comes from him.
He alone is my rock and my rescue,
my high stronghold —
I will not be badly shaken.
How long will you all pile on one man
to batter him down,
like a leaning wall, a tottering fence?
They only plan to push him down from his high place.
They delight in lies.
With their mouths they bless,
but inside they curse. *Selah*
For God alone, my soul, wait in silence,
for my hope comes from him.
He alone is my rock and my rescue,
my high stronghold —
I will not be shaken.
My rescue and my glory rest on God.
My strong rock, my shelter, is in God.
Trust in him at all times, you people.
Pour out your hearts before him.
God is a shelter for us. *Selah*
The children of Adam are only a breath.
The sons of men are a lie.
Put them on the scales and they go up —
all of them together lighter than a breath.
Do not trust in extortion.
Do not set empty hopes on robbery.
If riches grow,
do not set your heart on them.
Once God has spoken —
twice I have heard it:
that strength belongs to God,
and that steadfast love is yours, Lord.
For you repay each one according to what he has done.
My Soul Thirsts for You · 63:1–11
*A psalm of David, when he is in the wilderness of Judah.*
O God, you are my God — I seek you at dawn.
My soul is thirsty for you.
My body faints with longing for you
in a dry and weary land with no water.
So I have looked for you in the sanctuary,
to see your power and your glory.
Because your steadfast love is better than life,
my lips will praise you.
So I will bless you as long as I live.
In your name I will lift up my hands.
My soul is satisfied as with the richest feast,
and with joyful lips my mouth praises you,
when I remember you on my bed,
and murmur of you through the watches of the night.
For you have been my help,
and in the shadow of your wings I sing for joy.
My soul clings close behind you.
Your right hand holds me up.
But those who seek my life to destroy it
will go down into the depths of the earth.
They will be given over to the power of the sword.
They will be food for jackals.
But the king will rejoice in God.
All who swear by him will glory,
for the mouths of liars will be shut.
Hide Me from the Secret Plots · 64:1–10
*For the music leader. A psalm of David.*
Hear my voice, O God, as I make my complaint.
Guard my life from the terror of the enemy.
Hide me from the secret counsel of evildoers,
from the noisy crowd of those who do wrong,
who sharpen their tongues like swords,
who aim bitter words like arrows,
shooting from hiding places at the blameless —
shooting suddenly, without fear.
They hold fast to their evil plan.
They talk about hiding their snares.
They say, “Who will see them?”
They search out wrongs:
“We have finished — a well-planned plan!”
The inner self and the heart of a man are deep.
But God shoots his arrow at them.
Suddenly they are struck down.
Their own tongues trip them up.
All who see them shake their heads.
Then everyone is afraid.
They tell what God has done,
and ponder his work.
Let the righteous one be glad in YHWH and take shelter in him.
Let all the upright in heart give praise!
Praise Awaits You in Zion · 65:1–8
*For the music leader. A psalm of David. A song.*
Praise waits in silence for you, O God, in Zion,
and to you vows will be paid.
You who hear prayer —
to you all flesh will come.
When our guilt is too much for me,
you cover over our rebellions.
Happy is the one you choose and bring near
to live in your courts!
We will be satisfied with the goodness of your house,
