the holiness of your temple.
With awesome deeds you answer us in righteousness,
O God who saves us,
the hope of all the ends of the earth
and of the farthest seas —
who sets the mountains firm by his strength,
wrapped in might,
who stills the roaring of the seas,
the roaring of their waves,
and the uproar of the peoples.
Those who live at the ends of the earth stand in awe of your signs.
You make the places where morning and evening begin
shout for joy.
The Bounty of the Year · 65:9–13
You visit the earth and water it.
You make it very rich.
The river of God is full of water.
You provide their grain,
for this is how you have prepared the land.
You soak its furrows and level its ridges.
You soften it with showers,
and bless its growth.
You crown the year with your goodness,
and your cart tracks drip with plenty.
The pastures of the wilderness drip,
and the hills are wrapped in joy.
The meadows are clothed with flocks.
The valleys are covered with grain.
They shout for joy — yes, they sing!
Come and See What God Has Done · 66:1–12
*For the music leader. A song. A psalm.*
Shout for joy to God, all the earth!
Sing out the glory of his name!
Make his praise glorious!
Say to God, “How awesome are your deeds!
Your power is so great
that your enemies come cringing to you.
All the earth bows down to you
and sings praise to you —
they sing praise to your name.” *Selah*
Come and see what God has done —
awesome in his deeds toward the children of Adam!
He turns the sea into dry land.
They cross the river on foot.
There we rejoice in him!
He rules by his might forever.
His eyes keep watch on the nations.
Let the rebellious not lift themselves up. *Selah*
Bless our God, you peoples!
Let the sound of his praise be heard!
He has kept our souls among the living,
and has not let our feet slip.
For you have tested us, O God.
You have refined us as silver is refined.
You brought us into the net.
You laid a crushing load on our backs.
You let men ride over our heads.
We went through fire and through water —
and you brought us out into abundance.
What God Has Done for Me · 66:13–20
I will come into your house with burnt offerings.
I will pay you my vows,
the ones my lips opened to make,
that my mouth spoke when I was in trouble.
I will offer you burnt offerings of fattened animals,
with the smoke of rams.
I will offer bulls and goats. *Selah*
Come and listen, all you who fear God,
and I will tell what he has done for my soul.
I cried out to him with my mouth,
and high praise was on my tongue.
If I had cherished wrong in my heart,
the Lord would not have listened.
But truly God has listened.
He has paid attention to the sound of my prayer.
Blessed be God,
who has not turned away my prayer,
or his steadfast love from me!
Let the Peoples Praise You · 67:1–7
*For the music leader. With stringed instruments. A psalm. A song.*
May God be kind to us and bless us.
May he make his face shine upon us, *Selah*
so that your way may be known on earth,
your rescue among all the nations.
Let the peoples give you thanks, O God.
Let all the peoples give you thanks!
Let the nations be glad and sing for joy,
for you judge the peoples fairly
and guide the nations on the earth. *Selah*
Let the peoples give you thanks, O God.
Let all the peoples give you thanks!
The earth has given its harvest.
God, our God, blesses us.
God blesses us —
and all the ends of the earth will fear him.
Let God Arise · 68:1–23
*For the music leader. Of David. A psalm. A song.*
God rises up — his enemies scatter!
Those who hate him run from his face!
As smoke is blown away, so you blow them away.
As wax melts before fire,
so the wicked perish before God.
But the righteous are glad.
They celebrate before God.
They are overjoyed with gladness.
Sing to God! Sing praise to his name!
Build a highway for the one who rides through the deserts —
Yah is his name — and celebrate before him!
A father to the fatherless, a defender of widows,
is God in his holy dwelling.
God gives the lonely a home to live in.
He leads prisoners out into prosperity,
but the rebellious live in a sun-scorched land.
O God, when you go out before your people,
when you march through the wasteland, *Selah*
the earth shakes, the heavens pour down rain,
before God, the One of Sinai,
before God, the God of Israel.
You shower down a generous rain, O God.
When your inheritance is weary, you make it strong again.
Your flock settles in it.
In your goodness, O God, you provide for the poor.
The Lord gives the word —
great is the company of women who bring the good news:
“The kings of armies flee — they flee!”
And she who stays at home divides the spoil.
Though you lie among the sheepfolds,
there are wings of a dove covered with silver,
its feathers with shimmering gold.
When the Almighty scatters kings there,
it is like snow falling on Zalmon.
A mountain of God is the mountain of Bashan,
a mountain of many peaks is the mountain of Bashan.
Why do you look on with envy, you many-peaked mountains,
at the mountain God has desired for his dwelling?
Yes, YHWH will dwell there forever.
The chariots of God are twice ten thousand,
thousands upon thousands.
The Lord is among them — Sinai is in the sanctuary.
You go up on high.
You lead captives in your train.
You receive gifts among people —
even among the rebellious —
that Yah God may dwell there.
Blessed be the Lord!
Day after day he carries us.
God is our rescue. *Selah*
Our God is a God who rescues.
To YHWH the Lord belong the ways out of death.
But God will crush the heads of his enemies,
the hairy crown of the one who walks on in his guilt.
The Lord says, “I will bring them back from Bashan.
I will bring them back from the depths of the sea,
so that your foot may wade in blood,
and the tongues of your dogs may have their share of the enemy.”
The Procession into the Sanctuary · 68:24–35
Your processions are seen, O God —
the processions of my God, my King, into the sanctuary.
The singers go first, the musicians follow,
in the middle of young women playing tambourines.
“In the great congregations bless God —
bless YHWH, you who come from the fountain of Israel!”
There is Benjamin, the youngest, leading them,
the princes of Judah in their throng,
the princes of Zebulun, the princes of Naphtali.
Your God has commanded your strength.
Show your strength, O God, as you have done for us before.
Because of your temple at Jerusalem,
kings will bring you gifts.
Rebuke the beast among the reeds,
the herd of bulls with the calves of the peoples.
Trample those who lust after silver.
Scatter the peoples who delight in war.
Envoys will come out of Egypt.
Cush will hurry to stretch out her hands to God.
Kingdoms of the earth, sing to God!
Sing praise to the Lord, *Selah*
to the one who rides through the heavens, the ancient heavens!
Listen — he sends out his voice, a mighty voice.
Give strength to God,
whose majesty is over Israel,
and whose strength is in the skies.
Awesome are you, O God, from your sanctuary.
The God of Israel — he gives strength and power to his people.
Blessed be God!
Save Me, O God · 69:1–12
*For the music leader. On “The Lilies.” Of David.*
Save me, O God,
for the waters have come up to my neck.
I am sinking in deep mud,
and there is no foothold.
I have come into deep waters,
and the flood sweeps over me.
I am worn out with crying.
My throat is parched.
My eyes fail
from waiting for my God.
More than the hairs of my head
are those who hate me without cause.
Mighty are those who would destroy me,
my enemies who lie about me.
What I did not steal
must I now give back?
O God, you know my foolishness.
My guilty deeds are not hidden from you.
Do not let those who wait for you be put to shame because of me,
Lord YHWH of hosts.
Do not let those who seek you be disgraced because of me,
O God of Israel.
For it is for your sake that I bear scorn,
that shame has covered my face.
I have become a stranger to my brothers,
a foreigner to my mother’s sons.
For zeal for your house has eaten me up,
and the insults of those who insult you have fallen on me.
When I wept and humbled my soul with fasting,
it only brought me scorn.
When I made sackcloth my clothing,
I became a byword to them.
Those who sit at the gate talk about me,
and the drunkards make songs about me.
A Prayer for Deliverance · 69:13–29
But as for me, my prayer is to you, YHWH,
at a time of your favor.
O God, in your great steadfast love,
answer me with your sure rescue.
Pull me out of the mud — do not let me sink!
Let me be rescued from those who hate me
and from the deep waters.
Do not let the flood sweep over me,
or the deep swallow me up,
or the pit close its mouth over me.
Answer me, YHWH, for your steadfast love is good.
In your great compassion, turn to me.
Do not hide your face from your servant,
for I am in distress — answer me quickly!
Come near to my soul, and redeem it.
Ransom me because of my enemies.
You know my scorn, my shame, and my disgrace.
All my foes are before you.
Scorn has broken my heart,
and I am sick.
I looked for sympathy, but there was none,
and for comforters, but I found none.
They gave me poison for my food,
and for my thirst they gave me sour wine to drink.
Let their table before them become a trap,
and their peace offerings a snare.
Let their eyes grow dark so they cannot see,
and make their loins tremble continually.
Pour out your indignation on them.
Let your burning anger overtake them.
Let their camp be desolate.
Let no one live in their tents.
For they hunt down the one you have struck,
and they talk about the pain of those you have wounded.
Add guilt to their guilt.
Do not let them come into your righteousness.
Let them be blotted out of the book of the living.
Let them not be written down with the righteous.
But I am afflicted and in pain.
Let your rescue, O God, set me up on high.
Praise and Hope for Zion · 69:30–36
I will praise the name of God with a song.
I will make him great with thanksgiving.
This will please YHWH more than an ox,
more than a bull with horns and hooves.
The humble see it and are glad.
You who seek God — let your hearts live!
For YHWH listens to the needy,
and does not despise his own who are prisoners.
Let heaven and earth praise him,
the seas and everything that moves in them.
For God will save Zion
and rebuild the cities of Judah.
They will live there and possess it.
The children of his servants will inherit it,
and those who love his name will dwell in it.
Make Haste to Help Me · 70:1–5
*For the music leader. Of David. For remembrance.*
O God, come rescue me!
YHWH, hurry to help me!
Let those who seek my life
be put to shame and humiliated.
Let those who delight in my harm
be turned back and disgraced.
Let those who say, “Aha! Aha!”
turn back because of their shame.
But let all who seek you
leap for joy and be glad in you.
Let those who love your rescue
always say, “God is great!”
As for me, I am poor and needy —
O God, hurry to me!
You are my help and the one who sets me free.
YHWH, do not delay!
Do Not Cast Me Off in Old Age · 71:1–24
In you, YHWH, I take shelter.
Never let me be put to shame.
In your righteousness rescue me and set me free.
Bend your ear to me, and save me.
Be a rock for me to live in,
where I can always come.
You have given the command to save me,
for you are my cliff and my fortress.
My God, set me free from the hand of the wicked,
from the grip of the unjust and the cruel.
For you are my hope, Lord YHWH,
my trust since I was young.
I have leaned on you since birth.
You are the one who brought me out of my mother’s womb.
My praise is always of you.
I have become a wonder to many,
but you are my strong shelter.
My mouth is full of your praise,
of your splendor all day long.
Do not throw me away when I am old.
When my strength runs out, do not abandon me.
For my enemies talk about me.
Those who watch for my life plot together.
They say, “God has abandoned him.
Chase him and seize him,
for there is no one to rescue him.”
O God, do not be far from me.
My God, hurry to help me!
Let those who accuse my soul
be put to shame and come to an end.
Let those who seek my harm
be wrapped in scorn and disgrace.
But as for me, I will always hope.
I will add to all your praise.
My mouth will tell of your righteousness,
of your rescue all day long —
though I do not know how to count it all.
I will come in the mighty deeds of the Lord YHWH.
I will make your righteousness remembered — yours alone.
O God, you have taught me since I was young,
and to this day I tell of your wonders.
So even when I am old and gray,
O God, do not abandon me,
until I tell of your strong arm to the next generation,
your might to all who are yet to come.
Your righteousness, O God, reaches to the heights.
You who have done great things —
O God, who is like you?
You who have made me see many troubles and hardships
will bring me back to life again.
From the depths of the earth
you will bring me up again.
You will increase my greatness,
and turn and comfort me again.
So I too will give you thanks with the harp
for your faithfulness, my God.
I will sing praise to you with the lyre,
O Holy One of Israel.
My lips will shout for joy when I sing praise to you —
and my soul, which you have redeemed.
My tongue too will murmur your righteousness all day long,
for those who sought my harm
have been put to shame and disgraced.
A Prayer for the King · 72:1–17
*Of Solomon.*
O God, give the king your judgments,
and the king’s son your righteousness.
May he judge your people with righteousness,
and your afflicted ones with justice.
Let the mountains bring peace to the people,
and the hills, righteousness.
May he defend the afflicted among the people,
save the children of the needy,
and crush the oppressor.
May they fear you as long as the sun endures,
as long as the moon, through all generations.
May he be like rain falling on the mown grass,
like showers that water the earth.
In his days may the righteous flourish,
and peace abound, until the moon is no more.
May he rule from sea to sea,
and from the River to the ends of the earth.
May the desert tribes bow down before him,
and his enemies lick the dust.
May the kings of Tarshish and of the coastlands bring tribute.
May the kings of Sheba and Seba offer gifts.
May all kings bow down to him,
and all nations serve him.
For he rescues the needy one who cries for help,
the afflicted one who has no helper.
He has pity on the weak and the needy,
and saves the lives of the needy.
From oppression and violence he redeems their lives,
and their blood is precious in his eyes.
Long may he live!
May gold of Sheba be given to him.
May prayer be made for him continually,
and blessings called down on him all day long.
May there be plenty of grain in the land,
waving on the tops of the mountains.
May its fruit rustle like Lebanon,
and may people flourish in the cities like the grass of the field.
May his name endure forever,
his name spread as long as the sun shines.
May all nations be blessed in him,
and call him happy.
Doxology: the End of Book Two · 72:18–20
Blessed be YHWH God, the God of Israel,
who alone does wonders.
Blessed be his glorious name forever.
May the whole earth be filled with his glory!
Amen and amen.
The prayers of David, son of Jesse, are ended.
The Prosperity of the Wicked · 73:1–14
*A psalm of Asaph.*
Surely God is good to Israel,
to those who are pure in heart.
But as for me, my feet had almost stumbled.
My steps had nearly slipped out from under me.
For I envied the boastful
when I saw the ease of the wicked.
For they have no pangs at their death.
Their bodies are sleek and well fed.
They are not in trouble as others are.
They are not struck down like the rest of mankind.
So pride is their necklace.
Violence wraps around them like a robe.
Their eyes bulge out from fatness.
The fancies of their hearts overflow.
They scoff, and speak with malice.
From on high they threaten oppression.
They set their mouths against the heavens,
and their tongues strut through the earth.
So his people turn back to them,
and drink up their words like water.
And they say, “How can God know?
Is there knowledge in the Most High?”
Look at them — these are the wicked.
Always at ease, they pile up wealth.
Surely for nothing I have kept my heart clean
and washed my hands in innocence.
For all day long I have been struck,
and corrected every morning.
Until I Entered the Sanctuary · 73:15–28
If I had said, “I will talk like that,”
I would have betrayed the generation of your children.
But when I tried to understand this,
it was a weary task in my eyes,
until I went into the sanctuary of God.
Then I understood their end.
Surely you set them on slippery ground.
You make them fall to ruin.
How suddenly they are made desolate!
They are swept away, finished off by terrors.
Like a dream when one wakes up,
so, Lord, when you rouse yourself,
you will despise their image.
When my heart was bitter,
when I was pierced to the core,
I was brutish and knew nothing.
I was like a beast before you.
Yet I am always with you.
You hold my right hand.
You guide me with your counsel,
and afterward you will take me into glory.
Whom do I have in heaven but you?
And there is nothing on earth I desire besides you.
My flesh and my heart may fail,
but God is the rock of my heart
and my portion forever.
For look — those who are far from you will perish.
You put an end to everyone who is unfaithful to you.
But as for me, to be near God is my good.
I have made the Lord YHWH my shelter,
so that I may tell of all your works.
Why Have You Cast Us Off Forever? · 74:1–17
*A Maskil of Asaph.*
O God, why have you rejected us forever?
Why does your anger smoke against the sheep of your pasture?
Remember your congregation, which you acquired long ago,
the tribe you redeemed to be your inheritance —
Mount Zion, where you have dwelt.
Lift up your steps toward the endless ruins.
The enemy has wrecked everything in the sanctuary.
Your foes have roared in the middle of your meeting place.
They have set up their own signs for signs.
They looked like men swinging axes
in a thicket of trees.
And now all its carved work
they smash with hatchets and hammers.
They set your sanctuary on fire.
They defiled the dwelling place of your name, down to the ground.
They said in their hearts, “We will crush them all together.”
They burned every meeting place of God in the land.
We do not see our signs.
There is no longer any prophet,
and none of us knows how long.
How long, O God, will the foe taunt?
Will the enemy spurn your name forever?
Why do you hold back your hand, your right hand?
Take it out from the fold of your robe, and finish them!
Yet God is my King from of old,
working rescue in the middle of the earth.
You split the sea by your strength.
You broke the heads of the sea monsters on the waters.
You crushed the heads of Leviathan.
You gave him as food to the creatures of the desert.
You split open springs and streams.
You dried up ever-flowing rivers.
Yours is the day, and yours the night.
You set the light and the sun in place.
You fixed all the boundaries of the earth.
Summer and winter — you formed them.
Remember Your Covenant · 74:18–23
Remember this: the enemy taunts, YHWH,
and a foolish people spurns your name.
Do not hand over the life of your dove to the wild beasts.
Do not forget the life of your afflicted ones forever.
Look to the covenant,
for the dark places of the land are full of the haunts of violence.
Do not let the oppressed turn back in shame.
Let the poor and needy praise your name.
Rise up, O God, take up your own cause!
Remember how the fool taunts you all day long.
Do not forget the clamor of your foes,
the uproar of those who rise against you,
which goes up continually.
God Is the Judge · 75:1–10
*For the music leader. On “Do Not Destroy.” A psalm of Asaph. A song.*
We give thanks to you, O God, we give thanks,
for your name is near.
People tell of your wonders.
“When I choose the appointed time,
I myself will judge with fairness.
When the earth and all who live in it are melting,
it is I who hold its pillars steady. *Selah*
I say to the boastful, ‘Do not boast,’
and to the wicked, ‘Do not lift up your horn.
Do not lift your horn on high,
or speak with an arrogant neck.’”
For not from the east or from the west,
and not from the wilderness, comes lifting up.
But it is God who judges,
putting one down and lifting another up.
For in the hand of YHWH there is a cup,
with foaming wine, well mixed.
He pours from it,
and all the wicked of the earth must drain it,
drinking down to the dregs.
But as for me, I will declare it forever.
I will sing praise to the God of Jacob.
All the horns of the wicked I will cut off,
but the horns of the righteous will be lifted high.
The God of Jacob Is Glorious · 76:1–12
*For the music leader. With stringed instruments. A psalm of Asaph. A song.*
God is known in Judah.
His name is great in Israel.
His shelter is in Salem,
his dwelling place in Zion.
There he broke the flaming arrows of the bow,
the shield and the sword and the weapons of war. *Selah*
You are radiant,
more majestic than the mountains full of prey.
The stout-hearted were stripped of their spoil.
They sank into sleep.
None of the warriors could lift a hand.
At your rebuke, O God of Jacob,
both rider and horse lay stunned.
You — you are to be feared!
Who can stand before you
once your anger flares?
From heaven you sounded out judgment.
The earth feared and was still,
when God rose up to judge,
to save all the humble of the earth. *Selah*
For even human wrath will praise you.
The last of that wrath you will wear like a belt.
Make vows to YHWH your God and keep them.
Let all around him bring gifts
to the One who is to be feared,
who cuts short the spirit of princes,
who is feared by the kings of the earth.
In the Day of Trouble I Sought the Lord · 77:1–9
*For the music leader. For Jeduthun. Of Asaph. A psalm.*
My voice goes up to God, and I cry out.
My voice goes up to God, and he will hear me.
On the day of my trouble I seek the Lord.
All night my hand is stretched out and does not grow tired.
My soul refuses to be comforted.
I remember God, and I groan.
I muse on it, and my spirit grows faint. *Selah*
You hold my eyelids open.
I am so troubled I cannot speak.
I think about the days of old,
the years long past.
I remember my song in the night.
I talk it over with my heart,
and my spirit searches:
“Will the Lord reject us forever?
Will he never show favor again?
Has his steadfast love come to an end for good?
Is his promise finished for all generations?
Has God forgotten to be kind?
Has he shut up his compassion in anger?” *Selah*
I Will Remember the Deeds of YHWH · 77:10–20
Then I say, “This is my wound.”
But I will think on the years of the right hand of the Most High.
I will remember the deeds of Yah.
Yes, I will remember your wonders of long ago.
I will murmur over all your work,
and ponder what you have done.
O God, your way is holy.
What god is great like our God?
You are the God who works wonders.
You have made your strength known among the peoples.
With your arm you redeemed your people,
the children of Jacob and Joseph. *Selah*
The waters see you, O God.
The waters see you, and they writhe.
The very deeps tremble.
The clouds pour down water.
The skies thunder.
Your arrows flash back and forth.
The sound of your thunder is in the whirlwind.
Lightning lights up the world.
The earth trembles and quakes.
Your way is through the sea,
your path through the mighty waters,
yet your footprints are not seen.
You lead your people like a flock
by the hand of Moses and Aaron.
What Our Fathers Told Us · 78:1–8
*A Maskil of Asaph.*
Listen to my teaching, my people.
Bend your ears to the words of my mouth.
I will open my mouth in a parable.
I will pour out riddles from of old,
things we have heard and known,
things our fathers have told us.
We will not hide them from their children.
We will tell the next generation
the praises of YHWH and his might,
and the wonders he has done.
He set up a testimony in Jacob,
and put a Torah in Israel,
which he commanded our fathers
to make known to their children,
so that the next generation would know them —
children yet to be born —
and they would rise up and tell their own children,
so that they would set their hope in God,
and not forget the deeds of God,
but keep his commandments,
and not be like their fathers,
a stubborn and rebellious generation,
a generation whose heart was not steady,
whose spirit was not faithful to God.
Ephraim Forgot His Works · 78:9–16
The sons of Ephraim, armed with bows,
turn back on the day of battle.
They do not keep the covenant of God.
They refuse to walk in his Torah.
They forget what he has done,
the wonders he has shown them.
In front of their fathers he works wonders
in the land of Egypt, in the fields of Zoan.
He splits the sea and lets them pass through.
He makes the waters stand up like a heap.
He leads them with the cloud by day,
and all night long with the light of fire.
He splits rocks in the wilderness
and gives them drink as if from the great deep.
He brings streams out of the rock
and makes waters run down like rivers.
They Tested God in the Desert · 78:17–39
Yet they go on sinning against him,
rebelling against the Most High in the dry land.
They test God in their hearts
by demanding the food they crave.
They speak against God.
They say, “Can God spread a table in the wilderness?
Yes, he struck the rock, and water gushed out,
and streams overflowed —
but can he give bread too?
Can he provide meat for his people?”
So YHWH hears, and he is furious.
A fire is kindled against Jacob,
and anger rises against Israel,
because they do not believe in God
or trust in his rescue.
Yet he commands the skies above
and opens the doors of heaven.
He rains down manna on them to eat,
and gives them the grain of heaven.
Each one eats the bread of the mighty.
He sends them food in abundance.
He sets the east wind blowing in the heavens,
and by his power he drives the south wind.
He rains down meat on them like dust,
winged birds like the sand of the seas.
He lets them fall in the middle of their camp,
all around their tents.
They eat and are well filled.
He gives them what they crave.
But before they have turned from their craving,
while the food is still in their mouths,
the anger of God rises against them.
He kills the strongest of them,
and lays low the young men of Israel.
In spite of all this, they keep on sinning.
They do not believe in his wonders.
So he makes their days vanish like a breath,
and their years in sudden terror.
When he kills them, they seek him.
They turn back and search eagerly for God.
They remember that God is their rock,
that God Most High is their redeemer.
But they flatter him with their mouths,
and lie to him with their tongues.
Their heart is not steady toward him.
They are not faithful to his covenant.
Yet he, being compassionate,
covers over their guilt and does not destroy them.
Again and again he holds back his anger
and does not stir up all his wrath.
He remembers that they are only flesh,
a wind that passes and does not come back.
How Often They Rebelled · 78:40–55
How often they rebel against him in the wilderness
and grieve him in the desert!
Again and again they test God
and provoke the Holy One of Israel.
They do not remember his hand,
the day he redeemed them from the foe,
when he worked his signs in Egypt,
his wonders in the fields of Zoan.
He turns their rivers to blood,
so they cannot drink from their streams.
He sends swarms of flies among them, which devour them,
and frogs, which bring them to ruin.
He gives their crops to the caterpillar,
and the fruit of their labor to the locust.
He kills their vines with hail,
and their sycamore-figs with frost.
He gives up their cattle to the hail,
and their flocks to bolts of lightning.
He lets loose on them his burning anger,
fury and indignation and distress,
a band of destroying messengers.
He clears a path for his anger.
He does not spare their souls from death,
but hands their lives over to the plague.
He strikes down every firstborn in Egypt,
the first fruits of their strength in the tents of Ham.
Then he leads out his people like sheep,
and guides them like a flock in the wilderness.
He leads them in safety, so they are not afraid,
but the sea covers their enemies.
He brings them to his holy border,
to this mountain his right hand has won.
He drives out nations before them.
He measures out their inheritance by line.
He settles the tribes of Israel in their tents.
They Tested the Most High · 78:56–64
Yet they test and rebel against God Most High,
and do not keep his testimonies.
They turn back and act faithlessly like their fathers.
They twist like a crooked bow.
They provoke him with their high places,
and stir his jealousy with their carved idols.
God hears, and he is furious,
and he utterly rejects Israel.
He abandons his dwelling at Shiloh,
the tent where he lived among mankind.
He gives up his strength to captivity,
his glory into the hand of the foe.
He hands his people over to the sword,
and is furious with his inheritance.
Fire devours their young men,
and their young women have no wedding songs.
Their priests fall by the sword,
and their widows cannot weep.
He Chose Judah and David · 78:65–72
Then the Lord wakes up as from sleep,
like a warrior shouting from wine.
He beats his foes back.
He puts them to everlasting shame.
He rejects the tent of Joseph.
He does not choose the tribe of Ephraim.
But he chooses the tribe of Judah,
Mount Zion, which he loves.
He builds his sanctuary like the heights,
like the earth, which he has founded forever.
He chooses David his servant
and takes him from the sheepfolds.
From following the nursing ewes he brings him
to shepherd Jacob his people,
Israel his inheritance.
And he shepherds them with an upright heart,
and guides them with skillful hands.
The Nations Have Defiled Your Temple · 79:1–13
*A psalm of Asaph.*
O God, the nations have come into your inheritance.
They have defiled your holy temple.
They have turned Jerusalem into heaps of rubble.
They have given the bodies of your servants
as food to the birds of the sky,
the flesh of your faithful ones to the beasts of the earth.
They have poured out their blood like water
all around Jerusalem,
and there is no one to bury them.
We have become the scorn of our neighbors,
the mockery and ridicule of all around us.
How long, YHWH? Will you be angry forever?
Will your jealousy burn like fire?
Pour out your wrath on the nations that do not know you,
on the kingdoms that do not call on your name.
For they have devoured Jacob
and laid waste his home.
Do not hold against us the guilt of those before us.
Let your compassion come quickly to meet us,
for we have been brought very low.
Help us, O God who saves us,
for the glory of your name.
Rescue us, and cover over our sins,
for the sake of your name.
Why should the nations say, “Where is their God?”
Let it be known among the nations, before our eyes,
that you avenge the poured-out blood of your servants.
Let the groaning of the prisoner come before you.
By the greatness of your arm,
keep alive those who are condemned to die.
Pay back our neighbors sevenfold, into their laps,
for the scorn with which they have scorned you, Lord.
Then we, your people, the sheep of your pasture,
will give you thanks forever.
From generation to generation
we will tell your praise.
Restore Us, O God · 80:1–7
*For the music leader. On “The Lilies of Testimony.” Of Asaph. A psalm.*
Shepherd of Israel, listen,
you who lead Joseph like a flock!
You who sit enthroned on the cherubim, shine out!
Before Ephraim and Benjamin and Manasseh,
stir up your might,
and come to save us!
O God, bring us back.
Let your face shine, and we will be saved.
YHWH God of Armies,
how long will you smolder against the prayers of your people?
You have fed them the bread of tears,
and given them tears to drink by the bowlful.
You make us a thing our neighbors fight over,
and our enemies laugh among themselves.
God of Armies, bring us back.
Let your face shine, and we will be saved.
The Vine Out of Egypt · 80:8–19
You brought a vine out of Egypt.
You drove out the nations and planted it.
You cleared the ground for it.
It took deep root and filled the land.
The mountains were covered with its shade,
the mighty cedars with its branches.
It sent out its shoots to the sea,
and its tendrils to the River.
Why have you broken down its walls,
so that all who pass by pick its fruit?
The boar from the forest gnaws at it,
and the creatures of the field feed on it.
God of Armies, turn back, we pray!
Look down from heaven and see.
Take care of this vine,
the stock your right hand planted,
the son you made strong for yourself.
It is burned with fire. It is cut down.
At the rebuke of your face they perish.
Let your hand rest on the man at your right hand,
on the son of Adam you made strong for yourself.
Then we will not turn back from you.
Give us life, and we will call on your name.
YHWH God of Armies, bring us back.
Let your face shine, and we will be saved.
Sing Aloud to God Our Strength · 81:1–7
*For the music leader. On the Gittith. Of Asaph.*
Sing for joy to God our strength!
Shout aloud to the God of Jacob!
Raise a song, and strike the tambourine,
the sweet lyre with the harp.
Blow the shofar at the new moon,
at the full moon, on our feast day.
For it is a statute for Israel,
a judgment of the God of Jacob.
He set it up as a testimony in Joseph
when he went out against the land of Egypt.
I hear a voice I had not known:
“I took the load off his shoulder.
His hands were freed from the basket.
In distress you called, and I rescued you.
I answered you from the hiding place of thunder.
I tested you at the waters of Meribah. *Selah*
If My People Would Listen · 81:8–16
Hear, my people, and I will warn you.
Israel, if only you would listen to me!
There shall be no strange god among you.
You shall not bow down to a foreign god.
I am YHWH your God,
who brought you up out of the land of Egypt.
Open your mouth wide, and I will fill it.
But my people would not listen to my voice.
Israel would have none of me.
So I let them go their way in the stubbornness of their hearts,
to walk by their own counsel.
Oh, if my people would only listen to me,
if Israel would walk in my ways,
how quickly I would bring their enemies down,
and turn my hand against their foes!
Those who hate YHWH would come cringing to him,
and their doom would last forever.
But he would feed you with the finest of the wheat,
and with honey from the rock I would satisfy you.”
God Stands in the Divine Council · 82:1–8
*A psalm of Asaph.*
God takes his stand in the council of God.
In the middle of the gods he gives judgment:
“How long will you judge unjustly,
and show favor to the wicked? *Selah*
Give justice to the weak and the orphan.
Do right by the afflicted and the poor.
Rescue the weak and the needy.
Set them free from the hand of the wicked.”
They do not know, they do not understand.
They walk about in darkness.
All the foundations of the earth are shaken.
“I said, ‘You are gods,
sons of the Most High, all of you.
Yet you will die like mortals,
and fall like any prince.’”
Rise up, O God, judge the earth!
For all the nations belong to you.
Do Not Keep Silence, O God · 83:1–18
*A song. A psalm of Asaph.*
O God, do not keep quiet.
Do not hold your peace or be still, O God.
For look — your enemies are in an uproar.
Those who hate you have raised their heads.
They lay crafty plans against your people.
They plot together against your treasured ones.
They say, “Come, let us wipe them out as a nation,
so that the name of Israel is remembered no more.”
For they have plotted together with one mind.
Against you they make a covenant:
the tents of Edom and the Ishmaelites,
Moab and the Hagrites,
Gebal and Ammon and Amalek,
Philistia with those who live in Tyre.
Even Assyria has joined them.
They are the strong arm of the children of Lot. *Selah*
Do to them as you did to Midian,
as to Sisera and Jabin at the brook Kishon,
who were destroyed at Endor,
who became dung for the ground.
Make their nobles like Oreb and Zeeb,
all their princes like Zebah and Zalmunna,
who said, “Let us take for ourselves
the pastures of God.”
My God, make them like whirling dust,
like chaff before the wind.
As fire burns up a forest,
as flame sets the mountains ablaze,
so chase them with your storm,
and terrify them with your whirlwind.
Fill their faces with shame,
so that they seek your name, YHWH.
Let them be ashamed and terrified forever.
Let them be disgraced and perish,
so that they may know that you alone,
whose name is YHWH,
are the Most High over all the earth.
How Lovely Is Your Dwelling Place · 84:1–12
*For the music leader. On the Gittith. Of the sons of Korah. A psalm.*
How lovely is the place where you dwell,
YHWH of hosts!
My soul longs, it even faints,
for the courts of YHWH.
My heart and my flesh cry out for joy
to the living God.
Even the sparrow has found a home,
and the swallow a nest for herself,
where she can lay her young —
near your altars, YHWH of hosts,
my King and my God.
Happy are those who live in your house!
They are always praising you. *Selah*
Happy are those whose strength is in you,
whose hearts are set on the highways to Zion.
As they pass through the Valley of Baca,
they make it a place of springs.
The early rain covers it with pools.
They go from strength to strength,
until each one appears before God in Zion.
YHWH God of Armies, hear my prayer.
Give ear, O God of Jacob. *Selah*
Look upon our shield, O God.
Look on the face of your anointed one.
For one day in your courts
is better than a thousand anywhere else.
I would rather stand at the threshold of the house of my God
than live in the tents of wickedness.
For YHWH God is a sun and a shield.
YHWH gives grace and glory.
He holds back no good thing
from those who walk with integrity.
YHWH of hosts,
happy is the one who trusts in you!
Restore Us Again · 85:1–7
*For the music leader. Of the sons of Korah. A psalm.*
YHWH, you showed favor to your land.
You brought Jacob home again.
You lifted away the guilt of your people.
You covered all their sin. *Selah*
You gathered up all your fury.
You turned back from your burning anger.
Bring us back, O God who saves us,
and put away your displeasure with us.
Will you be angry with us forever?
Will you draw out your anger through all generations?
Will you not give us life again,
so your people may be glad in you?
Show us your steadfast love, YHWH,
and give us your rescue.
Mercy and Truth Have Met · 85:8–13
Let me hear what God, YHWH, will speak,
for he will speak peace to his people, to his faithful ones.
Only let them not turn back to folly.
Surely his rescue is near to those who fear him,
so that glory may dwell in our land.
Steadfast love and faithfulness meet together.
Righteousness and peace kiss each other.
Faithfulness springs up from the ground,
and righteousness looks down from the sky.
Yes, YHWH will give what is good,
and our land will give its harvest.
Righteousness will go before him
and make a road for his steps.
Teach Me Your Way · 86:1–17
*A prayer of David.*
Bend your ear, YHWH, and answer me,
for I am poor and needy.
Guard my soul, for I am faithful to you.
You are my God — save your servant who trusts in you.
Be kind to me, Lord,
for to you I cry all day long.
Make the soul of your servant glad,
for to you, Lord, I lift up my soul.
For you, Lord, are good and forgiving,
rich in steadfast love to all who call on you.
Give ear to my prayer, YHWH.
Listen to the sound of my pleading.
On the day of my trouble I call on you,
for you will answer me.
There is no one like you among the gods, Lord,
and no works like yours.
All the nations you have made will come
and bow down before you, Lord,
and give glory to your name.
For you are great, and you do wonders.
You alone are God.
Teach me your way, YHWH,
so that I may walk in your truth.
Make my heart whole to fear your name.
I will thank you, Lord my God, with my whole heart,
and I will give glory to your name forever.
For great is your steadfast love toward me.
You have rescued my soul from the depths of Sheol.
O God, the arrogant have risen up against me.
A band of ruthless men seeks my life.
They do not set you before them.
But you, Lord, are a God compassionate and gracious,
slow to anger,
rich in steadfast love and faithfulness.
Turn to me and be kind to me.
Give your strength to your servant,
and save the son of your handmaid.
Show me a sign of your goodness,
so that those who hate me may see it and be ashamed,
because you, YHWH, have helped me and comforted me.
Zion, the City of God · 87:1–7
*Of the sons of Korah. A psalm. A song.*
His foundation is on the holy mountains.
YHWH loves the gates of Zion
more than all the dwellings of Jacob.
Glorious things are spoken of you,
O city of God. *Selah*
“I count Rahab and Babylon among those who know me.
Look — Philistia and Tyre, with Cush:
‘This one was born there.’”
And of Zion it will be said,
“This one and that one were born in her,”
and the Most High himself will establish her.
YHWH will record, as he registers the peoples,
“This one was born there.” *Selah*
Singers and dancers alike say,
“All my springs are in you.”
The Cry from the Darkness · 88:1–18
*A song. A psalm of the sons of Korah. For the music leader. On Mahalath Leannoth. A Maskil of Heman the Ezrahite.*
YHWH, God who saves me,
by day I cry out, and by night, before you.
Let my prayer come before you.
Bend your ear to my cry.
For my soul is full of troubles,
and my life has come close to Sheol.
I am counted among those who go down to the pit.
I am like a man with no strength left,
set loose among the dead,
like the slain who lie in the grave,
whom you remember no more,
who are cut off from your hand.
You have put me in the lowest pit,
in dark places, in the depths.
Your wrath lies heavy on me.
You overwhelm me with all your breakers. *Selah*
You have taken my friends far from me.
You have made me a horror to them.
I am shut in, and I cannot get out.
My eye grows dim with affliction.
I call on you, YHWH, every day.
I spread out my hands to you.
Do you work wonders for the dead?
Do the shades rise up to praise you? *Selah*
Is your steadfast love told of in the grave,
your faithfulness in Abaddon?
Are your wonders known in the darkness,
or your righteousness in the land of forgetting?
But I cry to you for help, YHWH.
In the morning my prayer comes to meet you.
Why, YHWH, do you reject my soul?
Why do you hide your face from me?
I have been afflicted and close to death since I was young.
I bear your terrors; I am at my wits’ end.
Your burning anger has swept over me.
Your terrors have destroyed me.
They surround me like water all day long.
They close in on me all together.
You have taken friend and neighbor far from me.
Darkness is my closest companion.
I Will Sing of Your Steadfast Love · 89:1–18
*A Maskil of Ethan the Ezrahite.*
I will sing of the steadfast love of YHWH forever.
With my mouth I will make your faithfulness known
to every generation.
For I say, “Steadfast love is built up forever.
In the heavens you establish your faithfulness.”
“I have made a covenant with my chosen one.
I have sworn to David my servant:
‘I will establish your offspring forever,
and build your throne for all generations.’” *Selah*
Let the heavens praise your wonders, YHWH,
your faithfulness in the assembly of the holy ones.
For who in the skies can compare with YHWH?
Who among the sons of the mighty is like YHWH,
a God feared in the council of the holy ones,
great and awesome above all who are around him?
YHWH God of Armies, who is like you?
Mighty Yah, your faithfulness surrounds you.
You rule over the swelling of the sea.
When its waves rise, you still them.
You crushed Rahab like a carcass.
With your strong arm you scattered your enemies.
The heavens are yours, and the earth is yours too.
The world and all that fills it — you founded them.
North and south — you created them.
Tabor and Hermon shout for joy at your name.
Yours is an arm full of might.
Your hand is strong; your right hand is lifted high.
Righteousness and justice are the foundation of your throne.
Steadfast love and faithfulness go before your face.
Happy are the people who know the festal shout,
who walk, YHWH, in the light of your face!
In your name they rejoice all day long,
and in your righteousness they are lifted up.
For you are the glory of their strength,
and by your favor our horn is lifted high.
For our shield belongs to YHWH,
our king to the Holy One of Israel.
The Covenant with David · 89:19–37
Once you spoke in a vision to your faithful ones, and said:
“I have given help to a mighty man.
I have raised up one chosen from among the people.
I have found David my servant.
With my holy oil I have anointed him.
My hand will hold him steady.
My arm will make him strong.
No enemy will get the better of him.
No son of wickedness will humble him.
I will crush his foes in front of him,
and strike down those who hate him.
My faithfulness and my steadfast love will be with him,
and in my name his horn will be lifted high.
I will set his hand on the sea,
and his right hand on the rivers.
He will call to me, ‘You are my Father,
my God, and the rock of my rescue.’
And I will make him the firstborn,
the highest of the kings of the earth.
I will keep my steadfast love for him forever,
and my covenant with him will stand firm.
I will establish his offspring forever,
and his throne as long as the heavens endure.
If his children abandon my Torah
and do not walk in my judgments,
if they profane my statutes
and do not keep my commandments,
then I will punish their rebellion with the rod,
and their guilt with blows.
But I will not take my steadfast love from him,
or betray my faithfulness.
I will not profane my covenant,
or change what has gone out from my lips.
Once and for all I have sworn by my holiness —
I will not lie to David.
His offspring will go on forever,
his throne like the sun before me.
Like the moon it will be established forever,
a faithful witness in the skies.” *Selah*
But Now You Have Cast Off · 89:38–51
But you have rejected and spurned him.
You are furious with your anointed one.
You have renounced the covenant with your servant.
You have thrown his crown in the dust.
You have broken down all his walls.
You have turned his strongholds into ruins.
All who pass by plunder him.
He has become the scorn of his neighbors.
You have lifted high the right hand of his foes.
You have made all his enemies glad.
You have turned back the edge of his sword,
and have not held him up in battle.
You have put an end to his splendor,
and thrown his throne to the ground.
You have cut short the days of his youth.
You have wrapped him in shame. *Selah*
How long, YHWH? Will you hide yourself forever?
How long will your wrath burn like fire?
Remember how short my life is!
For what emptiness have you created all the children of Adam?
What man can live and never see death?
Who can rescue his soul from the grip of Sheol? *Selah*
Lord, where is your steadfast love of old,
which you swore to David in your faithfulness?
Remember, Lord, how your servants are scorned,
how I carry in my heart the insults of all the many peoples,
with which your enemies have scorned, YHWH,
with which they have scorned the footsteps of your anointed one.
Doxology: the End of Book Three · 89:52
Blessed be YHWH forever!
Amen and amen.
Lord, You Have Been Our Dwelling Place · 90:1–11
*A prayer of Moses, the man of God.*
Lord, you have been our home
in every generation.
Before the mountains were born,
before you brought forth the earth and the world,
from forever back to forever ahead, you are God.
You turn mortals back to dust,
and say, “Return, children of Adam.”
A thousand years, as you see them,
are like yesterday once it has gone by,
like a few hours' watch in the night.
You sweep them away; they are like a sleep.
In the morning they are like grass that springs up —
in the morning it flowers and springs up,
by evening it withers and dries.
For we are consumed by your anger.
By your wrath we are terrified.
You have set our guilty deeds before you,
our secret sins in the light of your face.
For all our days slip away under your fury.
We finish our years like a sigh.
The days of our years are seventy,
or eighty, if we are strong.
Yet even their best is trouble and sorrow,
for they are soon gone, and we fly away.
Who knows the power of your anger?
Your fury is as great as the fear that is due you.
Teach Us to Number Our Days · 90:12–17
So teach us to count our days,
that we may bring home a heart of wisdom.
Turn back, YHWH! How long?
Have pity on your servants.
Fill us up each morning with your steadfast love,
and we will sing and celebrate all our days.
Make us glad for as many days as you have afflicted us,
for as many years as we have seen trouble.
Let your work be seen by your servants,
and your splendor by their children.
Let the kindness of the Lord our God rest on us,
make the work of our hands stand firm —
yes, make the work of our hands last.
He Who Dwells in the Shelter of the Most High · 91:1–13
Whoever makes a home in the hiding place of the Most High
spends the night under the Almighty's shadow.
I say to YHWH, “My shelter, my stronghold,
my God — I trust in him.”
He will pull you free from the bird-catcher's trap
and from the plague that kills.
He will cover you over with his pinions;
you will take shelter under his wings.
His faithfulness is a shield and a wall.
You will not be afraid of the night's terror
or the arrow that flies in daylight,
of the plague that prowls in the dark
or the ruin that rages at noon.
A thousand may drop beside you,
ten thousand at your right hand,
but it will not reach you.
You will only look on with your eyes
and see the payback of the wicked.
Because you have made YHWH your refuge,
the Most High your home,
no evil will be allowed to touch you,
no plague will come near your tent.
For he will give his angels orders about you,
to keep watch over you wherever you go.
They will carry you in their hands
so you don't stub your foot on a stone.
You will step on lion and cobra;
you will stamp on young lion and serpent.
Because He Holds Fast to Me · 91:14–16
“He clings to me in love, so I will get him out.
I will lift him out of reach, because he knows my name.
He calls to me, and I answer him;
I am right there with him in trouble.
I will rescue him and honor him.
I will fill him up with long life
and let him see my rescue.”
It Is Good to Give Thanks · 92:1–15
*A psalm. A song for the Sabbath day.*
It is good to give thanks to YHWH,
to sing praise to your name, O Most High,
to tell of your steadfast love in the morning,
and your faithfulness by night,
to the music of the ten-stringed lute and the harp,
to the murmur of the lyre.
For you have made me glad, YHWH, by what you have done.
At the works of your hands I sing for joy.
How great are your works, YHWH!
How deep are your thoughts!
The brutish man does not know,
the fool cannot understand this:
though the wicked sprout like grass
and all evildoers flourish,
they are doomed to be destroyed forever.
But you, YHWH, are on high forever.
For look, your enemies, YHWH —
look, your enemies will perish.
All evildoers will be scattered.
But you have lifted up my horn like that of the wild ox.
You have poured fresh oil over me.
My eyes have looked in triumph on those who lie in wait for me.
My ears have heard the doom of the evildoers who rise against me.
The righteous will flourish like the palm tree.
They will grow tall like a cedar in Lebanon.
Planted in the house of YHWH,
they will flourish in the courts of our God.
They will still bear fruit in old age.
They will stay full of sap and green,
to show that YHWH is upright.
He is my rock, and there is no wrong in him.
YHWH Reigns · 93:1–5
YHWH reigns! He is robed in majesty.
YHWH is robed; he has wrapped himself in strength.
Yes, the world stands firm; it cannot be shaken.
Your throne has stood firm from of old.
You are from everlasting.
The floods have lifted up, YHWH,
the floods have lifted up their voice.
The floods lift up their pounding waves.
Mightier than the thunder of the great waters,
mightier than the breakers of the sea,
is YHWH on high!
Your testimonies are very sure.
Holiness befits your house, YHWH,
for days without end.
O YHWH, God of Vengeance · 94:1–15
YHWH, God of vengeance,
God of vengeance, shine forth!
Rise up, Judge of the earth!
Pay back the proud what they deserve.
How long will the wicked, YHWH,
how long will the wicked celebrate?
They pour out arrogant words.
All the evildoers boast.
They crush your people, YHWH.
They afflict your inheritance.
They kill the widow and the stranger,
and murder the fatherless.
And they say, “Yah does not see.
The God of Jacob pays no attention.”
Pay attention yourselves, you brutish people!
You fools, when will you get wise?
Does the one who planted the ear not hear?
Does the one who formed the eye not see?
Does the one who disciplines nations not correct?
He is the one who teaches mankind knowledge.
YHWH knows the thoughts of mankind —
that they are only a breath.
Happy is the man you discipline, Yah,
the one you teach from your Torah,
to give him rest from days of trouble,
until a pit is dug for the wicked.
For YHWH will not abandon his people.
He will not forsake his inheritance.
For justice will return to righteousness,
and all the upright in heart will follow it.
YHWH Is My Stronghold · 94:16–23
Who will rise up for me against the evildoers?
Who will stand up for me against those who do wrong?
If YHWH had not been my help,
my soul would soon have lived in the land of silence.
When I said, “My foot is slipping,”
your steadfast love, YHWH, held me up.
When my anxious thoughts multiplied within me,
your comforts delighted my soul.
Can a throne of ruin be allied with you,
one that frames trouble by statute?
They band together against the life of the righteous,
and condemn innocent blood.
But YHWH has become my high stronghold,
and my God the rock of my refuge.
He will turn their own wickedness back on them,
and destroy them for their evil.
YHWH our God will destroy them.
Come, Let Us Sing to YHWH · 95:1–7
Come, let us sing for joy to YHWH!
Let us shout aloud to the rock of our rescue!
Let us come before his face with thanksgiving.
Let us shout to him with songs.
For YHWH is a great God,
a great King above all gods.
In his hand are the depths of the earth,
and the peaks of the mountains are his.
The sea is his, for he made it,
and his hands formed the dry land.
Come, let us bow down and kneel.
Let us kneel before YHWH, our Maker.
For he is our God,
and we are the people of his pasture,
the flock under his hand.
Today, if only you would hear his voice:
Do Not Harden Your Hearts · 95:8–11
“Do not harden your hearts as at Meribah,
as on the day at Massah in the wilderness,
when your fathers tested me.
They put me to the proof, though they had seen my work.
For forty years I loathed that generation,
and I said, ‘They are a people whose hearts go astray,
and they do not know my ways.’
So I swore in my anger,
‘They shall not enter my rest.’”
Sing to YHWH a New Song · 96:1–13
Sing to YHWH a new song!
Sing to YHWH, all the earth!
Sing to YHWH, bless his name!
Tell the good news of his rescue day after day!
Tell of his glory among the nations,
his wonders among all the peoples.
For great is YHWH, and greatly to be praised.
He is to be feared above all gods.
For all the gods of the peoples are idols,
but YHWH made the heavens.
Splendor and majesty are before him.
Strength and beauty are in his sanctuary.
Give to YHWH, you families of the peoples,
give to YHWH glory and strength.
Give to YHWH the glory his name deserves.
Bring an offering, and come into his courts.
Bow down to YHWH in the splendor of holiness.
Tremble before him, all the earth!
Say among the nations, “YHWH reigns!”
Yes, the world stands firm; it cannot be shaken.
He will judge the peoples fairly.
Let the heavens be glad, and let the earth rejoice!
Let the sea roar, and all that fills it!
Let the field exult, and everything in it!
Then all the trees of the forest will sing for joy
before YHWH, for he comes —
he comes to judge the earth.
He will judge the world in righteousness,
and the peoples in his faithfulness.
YHWH Reigns; Let the Earth Rejoice · 97:1–12
YHWH reigns! Let the earth rejoice!
Let the many coastlands be glad!
Clouds and thick darkness are all around him.
Righteousness and justice are the foundation of his throne.
Fire goes before him
and burns up his foes on every side.
His lightning lights up the world.
The earth sees it and trembles.
The mountains melt like wax before YHWH,
before the Lord of all the earth.
The heavens declare his righteousness,
and all the peoples see his glory.
All who serve carved images are put to shame,
those who boast in worthless idols.
Bow down to him, all you gods!
Zion hears and is glad,
and the daughters of Judah rejoice,
because of your judgments, YHWH.
For you, YHWH, are Most High over all the earth.
You are lifted far above all gods.
You who love YHWH, hate evil!
He guards the lives of his faithful ones.
He rescues them from the hand of the wicked.
Light is sown for the righteous,
and joy for the upright in heart.
Be glad in YHWH, you righteous,
and give thanks at the remembrance of his holiness!
He Has Done Marvelous Things · 98:1–9
*A psalm.*
Sing to YHWH a new song,
for he has done wonders!
His right hand and his holy arm
have won him the victory.
YHWH has made his rescue known.
He has uncovered his righteousness in the sight of the nations.
He has remembered his steadfast love and his faithfulness
to the house of Israel.
All the ends of the earth have seen
the rescue of our God.
Shout to YHWH, all the earth!
Break out in joyful song and sing praise!
Sing praise to YHWH with the lyre,
with the lyre and the sound of song!
With trumpets and the sound of the shofar
shout before the King, YHWH!
Let the sea roar, and all that fills it,
the world and those who live in it!
Let the rivers clap their hands!
Let the mountains sing for joy together
before YHWH, for he comes to judge the earth.
He will judge the world in righteousness,
and the peoples with fairness.
YHWH Reigns; Let the Peoples Tremble · 99:1–9
YHWH reigns — let the peoples tremble!
He sits enthroned on the cherubim — let the earth quake!
YHWH is great in Zion.
He is high above all the peoples.
Let them praise your great and awesome name.
Holy is he!
The strength of the King is that he loves justice.
You have established fairness.
You have done justice and righteousness in Jacob.
Lift high YHWH our God!
Bow down at his footstool!
Holy is he!
Moses and Aaron were among his priests,
and Samuel among those who called on his name.
They called on YHWH, and he answered them.
He spoke to them in the pillar of cloud.
They kept his testimonies and the statute he gave them.
YHWH our God, you answered them.
You were a forgiving God to them,
but one who avenged their wrongdoing.
Lift high YHWH our God,
and bow down at his holy mountain,
for YHWH our God is holy!
Make a Joyful Noise to YHWH · 100:1–5
*A psalm of thanksgiving.*
Raise a shout to YHWH, all the earth!
Serve YHWH gladly!
Come into his presence singing!
Be sure of this: YHWH is God.
He made us, and we are his —
his people, the flock he feeds.
March through his gates with thanks,
into his courtyards with praise!
Thank him; bless his name!
For YHWH is good;
his steadfast love never ends,
and his faithfulness goes on from generation to generation.
The Resolve of a King · 101:1–8
*Of David. A psalm.*
I will sing of steadfast love and justice.
To you, YHWH, I will sing praise.
I will pay careful attention to the way of integrity.
When will you come to me?
I will walk with a whole heart
inside my own house.
I will not set anything worthless before my eyes.
I hate the work of those who turn aside.
It will not cling to me.
A crooked heart will be far from me.
I will have nothing to do with evil.
Whoever slanders his neighbor in secret,
him I will silence.
Whoever has haughty eyes and a proud heart,
him I will not put up with.
My eyes will be on the faithful in the land,
so that they may live with me.
Whoever walks in the way of integrity
will serve me.
No one who practices deceit
will live in my house.
No one who tells lies
will stand before my eyes.
Morning by morning I will silence
all the wicked of the land,
cutting off all evildoers
from the city of YHWH.
The Prayer of the Afflicted · 102:1–11
*A prayer of one who is afflicted, when he grows faint and pours out his complaint before YHWH.*
YHWH, hear my prayer.
Let my cry for help come to you.
Do not hide your face from me
on the day of my distress.
Bend your ear to me.
On the day I call, answer me quickly!
For my days vanish like smoke,
and my bones burn like a furnace.
My heart is struck down and withered like grass.
I even forget to eat my bread.
Because of my loud groaning
my bones cling to my skin.
I am like a desert owl,
like a little owl among the ruins.
I lie awake.
I am like a lonely bird on the rooftop.
All day long my enemies taunt me.
Those who mock me use my name as a curse.
For I eat ashes like bread,
and mix my drink with tears,
because of your indignation and your anger.
For you have picked me up and thrown me away.
My days are like a lengthening shadow.
I wither away like grass.
But You, O YHWH, Are Enthroned Forever · 102:12–28
But you, YHWH, sit enthroned forever,
and your name endures through all generations.
You will rise up and have compassion on Zion,
for it is time to show her favor.
The appointed time has come.
For your servants hold her stones dear,
and have pity on her dust.
The nations will fear the name of YHWH,
and all the kings of the earth your glory.
For YHWH will build up Zion.
He will appear in his glory.
He will turn to the prayer of the destitute,
and will not despise their prayer.
Let this be written down for a generation to come,
so that a people yet to be created may praise Yah:
that he looked down from his holy height.
From heaven YHWH looked upon the earth,
to hear the groaning of the prisoner,
to set free those condemned to die,
so that the name of YHWH may be told in Zion,
and his praise in Jerusalem,
when peoples gather together,
and kingdoms, to serve YHWH.
He has broken my strength along the way.
He has cut short my days.
I say, “My God, do not take me away
in the middle of my days —
you whose years go on through all generations!”
Long ago you laid the foundation of the earth,
and the heavens are the work of your hands.
They will perish, but you will remain.
They will all wear out like a garment.
You will change them like clothing, and they will pass away.
But you are the same,
and your years have no end.
The children of your servants will live secure,
and their offspring will be established before you.
Bless YHWH, O My Soul · 103:1–12
*Of David.*
Bless YHWH, my soul!
All that is within me, bless his holy name!
Bless YHWH, my soul,
and do not forget all his kindnesses:
he forgives all your guilt,
he heals all your diseases,
he redeems your life from the pit,
he crowns you with steadfast love and compassion,
he satisfies you with good things all your life,
so that your youth is made new like the eagle’s.
YHWH works righteousness
and justice for all who are oppressed.
He made his ways known to Moses,
his deeds to the children of Israel.
YHWH is compassionate and gracious,
slow to anger and rich in steadfast love.
He will not always accuse,
nor will he hold his anger forever.
He does not handle us the way our sins have earned
or pay us back what our guilt is owed.
As high as the sky stands over the earth,
so huge is his steadfast love for those who fear him.
As far as sunrise is from sunset,
that far he has carried our rebellions away from us.
As a Father Shows Compassion · 103:13–19
The way a father aches with love for his children,
that is how YHWH aches with love for those who fear him.
For he knows what we are made of;
he keeps in mind that we are dust.
Human days are like grass;
we bloom like a wildflower.
A wind blows over it, and it is gone,
and the spot where it grew forgets it was there.
But YHWH's steadfast love
stretches from forever to forever over those who fear him,
and his righteousness to children’s children,
to those who keep his covenant
and remember to do his precepts.
YHWH has planted his throne in the heavens,
and his reign reaches over everything.
Bless YHWH, All His Works · 103:20–22
Bless YHWH, you his angels,
you mighty ones who do his word,
who listen to the voice of his word!
Bless YHWH, all his armies,
his servants who do his will!
Bless YHWH, all his works,
in every place where he rules!
Bless YHWH, my soul!
The Glory of God in Creation · 104:1–9
Bless YHWH, my soul!
YHWH my God, you are very great.
You are clothed with splendor and majesty,
wrapped in light as in a cloak.
You stretch out the heavens like a tent curtain.
You lay the beams of your upper rooms on the waters.
You make the clouds your chariot.
You walk on the wings of the wind.
You make the winds your messengers,
flames of fire your servants.
You set the earth on its foundations,
so that it will never be shaken.
You covered it with the deep like a garment.
The waters stood above the mountains.
At your rebuke they fled.
At the sound of your thunder they hurried away.
The mountains rose, the valleys sank down,
to the place you appointed for them.
You set a boundary they may not cross,
so they will never again cover the earth.
He Makes Springs Gush Forth · 104:10–23
You send springs gushing into the valleys.
They flow between the hills.
They give drink to every beast of the field.
The wild donkeys quench their thirst.
Beside them the birds of the sky make their homes.
They sing among the branches.
From your upper rooms you water the mountains.
The earth is satisfied with the fruit of your work.
You make grass grow for the cattle,
and plants for people to cultivate,
bringing bread out of the earth,
and wine to gladden the human heart,
oil to make the face shine,
and bread to strengthen the human heart.
The trees of YHWH drink their fill,
the cedars of Lebanon that he planted.
There the birds build their nests.
The stork makes her home in the pines.
The high mountains are for the wild goats.
The cliffs are a refuge for the rock badgers.
He made the moon to mark the seasons.
The sun knows the time of its setting.
You bring darkness, and it is night,
when all the beasts of the forest creep about.
The young lions roar for their prey,
seeking their food from God.
The sun rises, and they slip away
and lie down in their dens.
People go out to their work,
and to their labor until evening.
How Manifold Are Your Works · 104:24–35
How many are your works, YHWH!
In wisdom you have made them all.
The earth is full of your creatures.
There is the sea, great and wide,
teeming with creatures beyond counting,
living things both small and great.
There the ships go to and fro,
and Leviathan, which you formed to play in it.
All of them look to you
to give them their food in its season.
You give it to them, and they gather it up.
You open your hand, and they are filled with good things.
You hide your face, and they are terrified.
You take away their breath, and they die
and return to their dust.
You send out your Spirit, and they are created,
and you make the face of the ground new.
May the glory of YHWH last forever!
May YHWH rejoice in his works —
he who looks at the earth, and it trembles,
who touches the mountains, and they smoke!
I will sing to YHWH as long as I live.
I will sing praise to my God while I have breath.
May my musing be pleasing to him.
As for me, I rejoice in YHWH.
Let sinners vanish from the earth,
and let the wicked be no more.
Bless YHWH, my soul!
Hallelujah!
Remember His Wonderful Works · 105:1–7
Give thanks to YHWH, call on his name!
Make his deeds known among the peoples!
Sing to him, sing praise to him!
Tell of all his wonders!
Glory in his holy name!
Let the hearts of those who seek YHWH be glad!
Seek YHWH and his strength!
Seek his face always!
Remember the wonders he has done,
his signs, and the judgments he has spoken,
you offspring of Abraham his servant,
you children of Jacob, his chosen ones!
He is YHWH our God.
His judgments are in all the earth.
The Covenant with Abraham · 105:8–15
He remembers his covenant forever,
the word he commanded for a thousand generations,
the covenant he made with Abraham,
his oath to Isaac,
which he confirmed to Jacob as a statute,
to Israel as an everlasting covenant:
“To you I will give the land of Canaan
as the portion you will inherit.”
When they are few in number,
very few, and strangers in it,
wandering from nation to nation,
from one kingdom to another people,
he lets no one oppress them.
He rebukes kings on their account:
“Do not touch my anointed ones!
Do my prophets no harm!”
Joseph in Egypt · 105:16–25
He calls down a famine on the land.
He breaks every staff of bread.
He sends a man ahead of them —
Joseph, sold as a slave.
They hurt his feet with shackles.
His neck is put in iron,
until the time his word comes true.
The word of YHWH tests him.
The king sends and sets him free.
The ruler of peoples lets him go.
He makes him lord of his house,
ruler over all his possessions,
to bind his princes as he pleases
and teach his elders wisdom.
Then Israel comes into Egypt.
Jacob lives as a stranger in the land of Ham.
And YHWH makes his people very fruitful,
and makes them stronger than their foes.
He turns their hearts to hate his people,
to deal craftily with his servants.
The Plagues and the Exodus · 105:26–36
He sends Moses his servant,
and Aaron, whom he has chosen.
They work his signs among them,
his wonders in the land of Ham.
He sends darkness, and it grows dark,
and they do not rebel against his words.
He turns their waters into blood
and makes their fish die.
Their land swarms with frogs,
even in the chambers of their kings.
He speaks, and swarms of flies come,
and gnats throughout their country.
He gives them hail for rain,
and flaming fire throughout their land.
He strikes their vines and fig trees,
and shatters the trees of their country.
He speaks, and the locusts come,
young locusts without number.
They eat up every plant in their land,
and devour the fruit of their ground.
He strikes down every firstborn in their land,
the first fruits of all their strength.
He Brought Out His People with Joy · 105:37–45
Then he brings Israel out with silver and gold,
and not one among his tribes stumbles.
Egypt is glad when they leave,
for the dread of them has fallen on it.
He spreads out a cloud for a covering,
and fire to give light by night.
They ask, and he brings quail,
and satisfies them with the bread of heaven.
He opens the rock, and water gushes out.
It runs through the dry places like a river.
For he remembers his holy word
to Abraham his servant.
So he brings out his people with rejoicing,
his chosen ones with shouts of joy.
He gives them the lands of the nations,
and they take possession of what the peoples worked for,
so that they may keep his statutes
and observe his Torah.
Hallelujah!
Who Can Utter His Mighty Deeds? · 106:1–5
Hallelujah!
Give thanks to YHWH, for he is good,
for his steadfast love lasts forever!
Who can tell the mighty deeds of YHWH,
or make all his praise heard?
Happy are those who keep justice,
who do what is right at all times!
Remember me, YHWH, when you show favor to your people.
Visit me with your rescue,
so that I may see the good of your chosen ones,
rejoice in the gladness of your nation,
and glory with your inheritance.
Our Fathers Sinned in Egypt · 106:6–18
We have sinned, like our fathers.
We have done wrong; we have acted wickedly.
Our fathers in Egypt do not understand your wonders.
They do not remember your many acts of steadfast love,
but rebel by the sea, at the Sea of Reeds.
Yet he saves them for the sake of his name,
to make his might known.
He rebukes the Sea of Reeds, and it dries up.
He leads them through the deeps as through a desert.
He saves them from the hand of the one who hates them,
and redeems them from the hand of the enemy.
The waters cover their foes.
Not one of them is left.
Then they believe his words.
They sing his praise.
But they quickly forget what he has done.
They do not wait for his counsel.
They give way to craving in the wilderness,
and put God to the test in the desert.
He gives them what they ask,
but sends a wasting disease among them.
In the camp they envy Moses,
and Aaron, the holy one of YHWH.
The earth opens and swallows Dathan,
and covers the company of Abiram.
Fire blazes up among their company.
A flame burns up the wicked.
The Golden Calf · 106:19–31
They make a calf at Horeb
and bow down to a cast image.
They trade their Glory
for the image of an ox that eats grass.
They forget God, their savior,
who has done great things in Egypt,
wonders in the land of Ham,
awesome deeds by the Sea of Reeds.
So he says he will destroy them —
had not Moses, his chosen one,
stood in the breach before him
to turn his wrath away from destroying them.
Then they despise the pleasant land.
They do not believe his word.
They grumble in their tents.
They do not listen to the voice of YHWH.
So he raises his hand and swears to them
that he will make them fall in the wilderness,
and make their offspring fall among the nations,
and scatter them throughout the lands.
They yoke themselves to the Baal of Peor,
and eat sacrifices offered to the dead.
They provoke him with their deeds,
and a plague breaks out among them.
Then Phinehas stands up and intervenes,
and the plague is stopped.
And that is counted to him as righteousness
from generation to generation forever.
Rebellion at Meribah · 106:32–47
They anger him at the waters of Meribah,
and it goes badly for Moses because of them,
for they make his spirit bitter,
and he speaks rashly with his lips.
They do not destroy the peoples,
as YHWH commanded them,
but they mix with the nations
and learn their ways.
They serve their idols,
which become a snare to them.
They sacrifice their sons
and their daughters to demons.
They pour out innocent blood,
the blood of their sons and daughters,
whom they sacrifice to the idols of Canaan,
and the land is defiled with blood.
They make themselves unclean by what they do,
and are unfaithful in their deeds.
Then the anger of YHWH burns against his people,
and he abhors his inheritance.
He hands them over to the nations,
and those who hate them rule over them.
Their enemies oppress them,
and they are brought low under their power.
Many times he rescues them,
but they are rebellious in their plans,
and sink down in their guilt.
Yet he looks on their distress
when he hears their cry.
He remembers his covenant for their sake,
and relents according to his great steadfast love.
He causes them to be pitied
by all who hold them captive.
Save us, YHWH our God,
and gather us from among the nations,
so that we may give thanks to your holy name
and glory in your praise.
Doxology: the End of Book Four · 106:48
Blessed be YHWH, the God of Israel,
from everlasting to everlasting!
And let all the people say, “Amen!”
Hallelujah!
The Redeemed of YHWH · 107:1–9
Give thanks to YHWH, for he is good,
for his steadfast love lasts forever!
Let the redeemed of YHWH say so,
those he has redeemed from the hand of the foe,
and gathered in from the lands,
from the east and from the west,
from the north and from the sea.
Some wander in the wilderness, in the wasteland.
They find no road to a city to live in.
Hungry and thirsty,
their souls faint within them.
Then they cry out to YHWH in their trouble,
and he rescues them from their distress.
He leads them by a straight road
to a city where they can live.
Let them thank YHWH for his steadfast love,
for his wonders toward the children of Adam!
For he satisfies the thirsty soul,
and fills the hungry soul with good things.
Those Who Sat in Darkness · 107:10–16
Some sit in darkness and the shadow of death,
prisoners in misery and iron,
because they rebelled against the words of God
and spurned the counsel of the Most High.
So he humbles their hearts with hard labor.
They stumble, and there is no one to help.
Then they cry out to YHWH in their trouble,
and he saves them from their distress.
He brings them out of darkness and the shadow of death,
and snaps their chains apart.
Let them thank YHWH for his steadfast love,
for his wonders toward the children of Adam!
For he shatters the doors of bronze
and cuts through the bars of iron.
Fools Because of Their Sin · 107:17–22
Some are fools through their rebellious ways,
and suffer because of their guilt.
Their souls loathe every kind of food,
and they draw near to the gates of death.
Then they cry out to YHWH in their trouble,
and he saves them from their distress.
He sends out his word and heals them,
and rescues them from the pit.
Let them thank YHWH for his steadfast love,
for his wonders toward the children of Adam!
Let them offer sacrifices of thanksgiving,
and tell of his works with songs of joy!
Those Who Go Down to the Sea · 107:23–32
Some go down to the sea in ships,
doing business on the great waters.
They see the works of YHWH,
his wonders in the deep.
For he speaks, and raises a storm wind
that lifts up the waves of the sea.
They go up to the heavens, they go down to the depths.
Their courage melts away in their peril.
They reel and stagger like a drunkard,
and all their skill is swallowed up.
Then they cry out to YHWH in their trouble,
and he brings them out of their distress.
He hushes the storm to a whisper,
and the waves of the sea fall still.
They are glad because it grows quiet,
and he guides them to the harbor they long for.
Let them thank YHWH for his steadfast love,
for his wonders toward the children of Adam!
Let them lift him high in the assembly of the people,
and praise him in the council of the elders.
He Turns Rivers into a Desert · 107:33–43
He turns rivers into a desert,
springs of water into thirsty ground,
a fruitful land into a salt waste,
because of the wickedness of those who live there.
He turns a desert into pools of water,
a parched land into springs.
There he lets the hungry settle,
and they build a city to live in.
They sow fields and plant vineyards,
and gather a fruitful harvest.
He blesses them, and they multiply greatly,
and he does not let their cattle dwindle.
When they are diminished and brought low
through oppression, trouble, and sorrow,
he pours contempt on princes
and makes them wander in a trackless waste.
But he lifts the needy high out of affliction,
and makes their families like flocks.
The upright see it and are glad,
and all wickedness shuts its mouth.
Whoever is wise, let him pay attention to these things,
and consider the steadfast love of YHWH.
My Heart Is Steadfast, O God · 108:1–13
*A song. A psalm of David.*
My heart is steady, O God!
I will sing and make music with all my being!
Wake up, harp and lyre!
I will wake up the dawn!
I will give you thanks among the peoples, YHWH.
I will sing your praise among the nations.
For your steadfast love is great, higher than the heavens,
and your faithfulness reaches to the clouds.
Be lifted high above the heavens, O God!
Let your glory be over all the earth!
So that your beloved ones may be set free,
save with your right hand, and answer me!
God has spoken in his holiness:
“I will exult — I will divide up Shechem
and measure out the Valley of Succoth.
Gilead is mine; Manasseh is mine.
Ephraim is the helmet on my head.
Judah is my scepter.
Moab is my washbasin.
On Edom I toss my sandal.
Over Philistia I shout in triumph.”
Who will bring me into the fortified city?
Who will lead me to Edom?
Have you not rejected us, O God?
You do not go out, O God, with our armies.
Give us help against the foe,
for the help of human beings is worthless.
With God we will do mighty things,
and he will trample our foes.
The Prayer of the Accused · 109:1–20
*For the music leader. Of David. A psalm.*
