a time to be born,
and a time to die;
a time to plant,
and a time to pluck up that which is planted;
a time to kill,
and a time to heal;
a time to break down,
and a time to build up;
a time to weep,
and a time to laugh;
a time to mourn,
and a time to dance;
a time to cast away stones,
and a time to gather stones together;
a time to embrace,
and a time to refrain from embracing;
a time to seek,
and a time to lose;
a time to keep,
and a time to cast away;
a time to tear,
and a time to sew;
a time to keep silence,
and a time to speak;
a time to love,
and a time to hate;
a time for war,
and a time for peace.
Eternity in the Heart · 3:9–15

What profit has he who works in that in which he labors? I have seen the burden which God has given to the sons of men to be afflicted with. He has made everything beautiful in its time. He has also set eternity in their hearts, yet so that man can’t find out the work that God has done from the beginning even to the end. I know that there is nothing better for them than to rejoice, and to do good as long as they live. Also that every man should eat and drink, and enjoy good in all his labor, is the gift of God. I know that whatever God does, it will be forever. Nothing can be added to it, nor anything taken from it; and God has done it, that men should fear before him. That which is has been long ago, and that which is to be has been long ago: and God seeks again that which is passed away.
Injustice Under the Sun · 3:16–22

Moreover I saw under the sun, in the place of justice, that wickedness was there; and in the place of righteousness, that wickedness was there. I said in my heart, “God will judge the righteous and the wicked; for there is a time there for every purpose and for every work.” I said in my heart, “As for the sons of men, God tests them, so that they may see that they themselves are like animals. For that which happens to the sons of men happens to animals. Even one thing happens to them. As the one dies, so the other dies. Yes, they have all one breath; and man has no advantage over the animals: for all is vanity. All go to one place. All are from the dust, and all turn to dust again. Who knows the spirit of man, whether it goes upward, and the spirit of the animal, whether it goes downward to the earth?”
Therefore I saw that there is nothing better, than that a man should rejoice in his works; for that is his portion: for who can bring him to see what will be after him?
Oppression, Envy, and Toil · 4:1–8

Then I returned and saw all the oppressions that are done under the sun: and look, the tears of those who were oppressed, and they had no comforter; and on the side of their oppressors there was power; but they had no comforter. Therefore I praised the dead who have been long dead more than the living who are yet alive. Yes, better than them both is him who has not yet been, who has not seen the evil work that is done under the sun. Then I saw all the labor and achievement that is the envy of a man’s neighbor. This also is vanity and a striving after wind.
The fool folds his hands together and ruins himself. Better is a handful, with quietness, than two handfuls with labor and chasing after wind.

Then I returned and saw vanity under the sun. There is one who is alone, and he has neither son nor brother. There is no end to all of his labor, neither are his eyes satisfied with wealth. “For whom then, do I labor, and deprive my soul of enjoyment?” This also is vanity. Yes, it is a miserable business.
The Value of Companionship · 4:9–12

Two are better than one, because they have a good reward for their labor. For if they fall, the one will lift up his fellow; but woe to him who is alone when he falls, and doesn’t have another to lift him up. Again, if two lie together, then they have warmth; but how can one keep warm alone? If a man prevails against one who is alone, two will withstand him; and a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
The Vapor of Royal Ambition · 4:13–16

Better is a poor and wise youth than an old and foolish king who doesn’t know how to receive admonition any more. For out of prison he came out to be king; yes, even in his kingdom he was born poor. I saw all the living who walk under the sun, that they were with the youth, the other, who succeeded him. There was no end of all the people, even of all them over whom he was—yet those who come after will not rejoice in him. Surely this also is vanity and a chasing after wind.
Guard Your Steps Before God · 5:1–7

Guard your steps when you go to God’s house; for to draw near to listen is better than to give the sacrifice of fools, for they don’t know that they do evil. Don’t be rash with your mouth, and don’t let your heart be hasty to utter anything before God; for God is in heaven, and you on earth. Therefore let your words be few. For as a dream comes with a multitude of cares, so a fool’s speech with a multitude of words. When you vow a vow to God, don’t defer to pay it; for he has no pleasure in fools. Pay that which you vow. It is better that you should not vow, than that you should vow and not pay. Don’t allow your mouth to lead you into sin. Don’t protest before the messenger that this was a mistake. Why should God be angry at your voice, and destroy the work of your hands? For in the multitude of dreams there are vanities, as well as in many words: but you must fear God.
The Grievous Evil of Wealth · 5:8–17

If you see the oppression of the poor, and the violent taking away of justice and righteousness in a district, don’t marvel at the matter: for one official is eyed by a higher one; and there are officials over them. Moreover the profit of the earth is for all. The king profits from the field.

He who loves silver will not be satisfied with silver; nor he who loves abundance, with increase: this also is vanity. When goods increase, those who eat them are increased; and what advantage is there to its owner, except to feast on them with his eyes?
The sleep of a laboring man is sweet, whether he eats little or much; but the abundance of the rich will not allow him to sleep.

There is a grievous evil which I have seen under the sun: wealth kept by its owner to his harm. Those riches perish by misfortune, and if he has fathered a son, there is nothing in his hand. As he came out of his mother’s womb, naked will he go again as he came, and will take nothing for his labor, which he may carry away in his hand. This also is a grievous evil, that in all points as he came, so will he go. And what profit does he have who labors for the wind? All his days he also eats in darkness, he is frustrated, and has sickness and wrath.
The Gift of Enjoyment · 5:18–20

Look, that which I have seen to be good and proper is for one to eat and to drink, and to enjoy good in all his labor, in which he labors under the sun, all the days of his life which God has given him; for this is his portion. Every man also to whom God has given riches and wealth, and has given him power to eat of it, and to take his portion, and to rejoice in his labor—this is the gift of God. For he will not often reflect on the days of his life; because God occupies him with the joy of his heart.
The Man Who Cannot Enjoy · 6:1–9

There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, and it is heavy on men: a man to whom God gives riches, wealth, and honor, so that he lacks nothing for his soul of all that he desires, yet God gives him no power to eat of it, but an alien eats it. This is vanity, and it is an evil disease.

If a man fathers a hundred children, and lives many years, so that the days of his years are many, but his soul is not filled with good, and moreover he has no burial; I say, that a stillborn child is better than he: for it comes in vanity, and departs in darkness, and its name is covered with darkness. Moreover it has not seen the sun nor known it. This has rest rather than the other. Yes, though he live a thousand years twice told, and yet fails to enjoy good, don’t all go to one place? All the labor of man is for his mouth, and yet the appetite is not filled. For what advantage has the wise more than the fool? What has the poor man, that knows how to walk before the living? Better is the sight of the eyes than the wandering of the desire. This also is vanity and a chasing after wind.
The Limits of Human Knowledge · 6:10–12

Whatever has been, its name was given long ago; and it is known what man is; neither can he contend with him who is mightier than he. For there are many words that create vanity. What does that profit man? For who knows what is good for man in life, all the days of his vain life which he spends like a shadow? For who can tell a man what will be after him under the sun?
Better-than Proverbs · 7:1–14

A good name is better than fine perfume; and the day of death better than the day of one’s birth. It is better to go to the house of mourning than to go to the house of feasting: for that is the end of all men, and the living should take this to heart. Sorrow is better than laughter; for by the sadness of the face the heart is made good. The heart of the wise is in the house of mourning; but the heart of fools is in the house of mirth. It is better to hear the rebuke of the wise, than for a man to hear the song of fools. For as the crackling of thorns under a pot, so is the laughter of the fool. This also is vanity. Surely extortion makes the wise man foolish; and a bribe destroys the understanding. Better is the end of a thing than its beginning.

The patient in spirit is better than the proud in spirit. Don’t be hasty in your spirit to be angry, for anger rests in the bosom of fools. Don’t say, “Why were the former days better than these?” For you do not ask wisely about this.

Wisdom is as good as an inheritance. Yes, it is more excellent for those who see the sun. For wisdom is a defense, even as money is a defense; but the excellency of knowledge is that wisdom preserves the life of him who has it.

Consider the work of God, for who can make that straight, which he has made crooked? In the day of prosperity be joyful, and in the day of adversity consider; yes, God has made the one side by side with the other, to the end that man should not find out anything after him.
The Limits of Righteousness and Wisdom · 7:15–22

All this I have seen in my days of vanity: there is a righteous man who perishes in his righteousness, and there is a wicked man who lives long in his evildoing. Don’t be overly righteous, neither make yourself overly wise. Why should you destroy yourself? Don’t be too wicked, neither be foolish. Why should you die before your time? It is good that you should take hold of this. Yes, also from that don’t withdraw your hand; for he who fears God will come out of them all. Wisdom is a strength to the wise man more than ten rulers who are in a city. Surely there is not a righteous man on earth, who does good and doesn’t sin. Also don’t take heed to all words that are spoken, lest you hear your servant curse you; for often your own heart knows that you yourself have likewise cursed others.
The Search for Wisdom · 7:23–29

All this I have proved in wisdom. I said, “I will be wise”; but it was far from me. That which is, is far off and exceedingly deep. Who can find it out? I turned around, and my heart sought to know and to search out, and to seek wisdom and the scheme of things, and to know that wickedness is stupidity, and that foolishness is madness.
I find more bitter than death the woman whose heart is snares and traps, whose hands are chains. Whoever pleases God will escape from her; but the sinner will be ensnared by her.

“Look, I have found this,” says the Preacher, “to one another, to find out the scheme; which my soul still seeks; but I have not found. I have found one man among a thousand; but I have not found a woman among all those. Look, I have only found this: that God made man upright; but they search for many schemes.”
Wisdom and Royal Authority · 8:1–9

Who is like the wise man? And who knows the interpretation of a thing? A man’s wisdom makes his face shine, and the hardness of his face is changed. I say, “Keep the king’s command!” because of the oath to God. Don’t be hasty to go out of his presence. Don’t persist in an evil thing, for he does whatever pleases him, for the king’s word is supreme. Who can say to him, “What are you doing?” Whoever keeps the commandment will not come to harm, and his wise heart will know the time and procedure. For there is a time and procedure for every purpose, although the misery of man is heavy on him. For he doesn’t know that which will be; for who can tell him how it will be? There is no man who has power over the spirit to contain the spirit; neither does he have power over the day of death. There is no discharge in war; neither will wickedness deliver those who practice it.
All this I have seen, and applied my mind to every work that is done under the sun. There is a time in which one man has power over another to his hurt.
The Prosperity of the Wicked · 8:10–17

So I saw the wicked buried. Indeed they came also from holiness. They went and were forgotten in the city where they did this. This also is vanity. Because sentence against an evil work is not executed speedily, therefore the heart of the sons of men is fully set in them to do evil. Though a sinner commits crimes a hundred times, and lives long, yet surely I know that it will be better with those who fear God, who are reverent before him. But it will not be well with the wicked, neither will he lengthen days like a shadow; because he doesn’t fear God.

There is a vanity which is done on the earth, that there are righteous men to whom it happens according to the work of the wicked. Again, there are wicked men to whom it happens according to the work of the righteous. I said that this also is vanity. Then I commended mirth, because a man has no better thing under the sun, than to eat, and to drink, and to be joyful: for that will accompany him in his labor all the days of his life which God has given him under the sun.

When I applied my heart to know wisdom, and to see the business that is done on the earth (for also there is that neither day nor night sees sleep with his eyes), then I saw all the work of God, that man can’t find out the work that is done under the sun, because however much a man labors to seek it out, yet he won’t find it. Yes even though a wise man thinks he can comprehend it, he won’t be able to find it.
One Fate for All · 9:1–6

For all this I laid to my heart, even to explore all this: that the righteous, and the wise, and their works, are in the hand of God; whether it is love or hatred, man doesn’t know it; all is before them. All things come alike to all. There is one event to the righteous and to the wicked; to the good, to the clean, to the unclean, to him who sacrifices, and to him who doesn’t sacrifice. As is the good, so is the sinner; he who takes an oath, as he who fears an oath. This is an evil in all that is done under the sun, that there is one event to all: yes also, the heart of the sons of men is full of evil, and madness is in their heart while they live, and after that they go to the dead. For to him who is joined with all the living there is hope; for a living dog is better than a dead lion. For the living know that they will die, but the dead don’t know anything, neither do they have any more a reward; for their memory is forgotten. Also their love, their hatred, and their envy has perished long ago; neither have they any more a portion forever in anything that is done under the sun.
Eat, Drink, and Live with the Wife You Love · 9:7–10

Go your way—eat your bread with joy, and drink your wine with a merry heart; for God has already accepted your works. Let your garments be always white, and don’t let your head lack oil. Live joyfully with the wife whom you love all the days of your life of vanity, which he has given you under the sun, all your days of vanity: for that is your portion in life, and in your labor in which you labor under the sun. Whatever your hand finds to do, do it with your might; for there is no work, nor plan, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in Sheol, where you are going.
Time and Chance · 9:11–12

I returned, and saw under the sun, that the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, neither yet bread to the wise, nor yet riches to men of understanding, nor yet favor to men of skill; but time and chance happen to them all. For man also doesn’t know his time. As the fish that are taken in an evil net, and as the birds that are caught in the snare, even so are the sons of men snared in an evil time, when it falls suddenly on them.
The Poor Wise Man · 9:13–18

I have also seen wisdom under the sun in this way, and it seemed great to me. There was a little city, and few men within it; and a great king came against it, besieged it, and built great bulwarks against it. Now a poor wise man was found in it, and he by his wisdom delivered the city; yet no man remembered that same poor man. Then I said, “Wisdom is better than strength.” Nevertheless the poor man’s wisdom is despised, and his words are not heard. The words of the wise heard in quiet are better than the cry of him who rules among fools. Wisdom is better than weapons of war; but one sinner destroys much good.
Wisdom and Folly in Contrast · 10:1–20
Dead flies cause the oil of the perfumer to produce an evil odor;
so does a little folly outweigh wisdom and honor.
A wise man’s heart is at his right hand,
but a fool’s heart at his left.
Yes also, when the fool walks by the way, his understanding fails him, and he says to everyone that he is a fool.
If the spirit of the ruler rises up against you, don’t leave your place; for gentleness lays great offenses to rest.

There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, the sort of error which proceeds from the ruler. Folly is set in great dignity, and the rich sit in a low place. I have seen servants on horses, and princes walking like servants on the earth. He who digs a pit may fall into it; and whoever breaks through a wall may be bitten by a snake. Whoever carves out stones may be injured by them. Whoever splits wood may be endangered thereby. If the ax is blunt, and one doesn’t sharpen the edge, then he must use more strength; but skill brings success.

If the snake bites before it is charmed, then is there no profit for the charmer’s tongue. The words of a wise man’s mouth are gracious; but a fool is swallowed by his own lips. The beginning of the words of his mouth is foolishness; and the end of his talk is mischievous madness. A fool also multiplies words.
Man doesn’t know what will be; and that which will be after him, who can tell him? The labor of fools wearies every one of them; for he doesn’t know how to go to the city.
Woe to you, land, when your king is a child,
and your princes eat in the morning!
Happy are you, land, when your king is the son of nobles,
and your princes eat in due season,
for strength, and not for drunkenness!
By slothfulness the roof sinks in;
and through idleness of the hands the house leaks.
A feast is made for laughter,
and wine makes the life glad;
and money is the answer for all things.
Don’t curse the king, no, not in your thoughts;
and don’t curse the rich in your bedroom:
for a bird of the sky may carry your voice,
and that which has wings may tell the matter.
Cast Your Bread Upon the Waters · 11:1–6
Cast your bread on the waters;
for you will find it after many days.
Give a portion to seven, yes, even to eight;
for you don’t know what evil will be on the earth.
If the clouds are full of rain, they empty themselves on the earth;
and if a tree falls toward the south, or toward the north,
in the place where the tree falls, there will it be.
He who observes the wind won’t sow;
and he who regards the clouds won’t reap.
As you don’t know what is the way of the wind,
nor how the bones grow in the womb of her who is with child;
even so you don’t know the work of God who does all.
In the morning sow your seed,
and in the evening don’t withhold your hand;
for you don’t know which will prosper, whether this or that,
or whether they both will be equally good.
Rejoice, Young Man — and Remember · 11:7–10
Truly the light is sweet,
and a pleasant thing it is for the eyes to see the sun.
Yes, if a man lives many years, let him rejoice in them all;
but let him remember the days of darkness, for they will be many.
All that comes is vanity.
Rejoice, young man, in your youth,
and let your heart cheer you in the days of your youth,
and walk in the ways of your heart,
and in the sight of your eyes;
but know that for all these things God will bring you into judgment.
Therefore remove sorrow from your heart,
and put away evil from your flesh;
for youth and the dawn of life are vanity.
Remember Your Creator in Youth · 12:1–8
Remember also your Creator in the days of your youth,
before the evil days come, and the years draw near,
when you will say, “I have no pleasure in them”;
Before the sun, the light, the moon, and the stars are darkened,
and the clouds return after the rain;
in the day when the keepers of the house will tremble,
and the strong men will bow themselves,
and the grinders cease because they are few,
and those who look out of the windows are darkened,
and the doors will be shut in the street;
when the sound of the grinding is low,
and one will rise up at the voice of a bird,
and all the daughters of music will be brought low;
yes, they will be afraid of heights,
and terrors will be on the way;
and the almond tree will blossom,
and the grasshopper will be a burden,
and desire will fail;
because man goes to his everlasting home,
and the mourners go about the streets:
before the silver cord is severed,
or the golden bowl is broken,
or the pitcher is broken at the spring,
or the wheel broken at the cistern,
and the dust returns to the earth as it was,
and the spirit returns to God who gave it.
“Vanity of vanities,” says the Preacher.
“All is vanity!”
The Final Words · 12:9–14

Further, because the Preacher was wise, he still taught the people knowledge. Yes, he pondered, sought out, and set in order many proverbs. The Preacher sought to find out acceptable words, and that which was written blamelessly, words of truth. The words of the wise are like goads; and like nails well fastened are words from the masters of assemblies, which are given from one shepherd. Furthermore, my son, be admonished: of making many books there is no end; and much study is a weariness of the flesh.

This is the end of the matter. All has been heard. Fear God, and keep his commandments; for this is the whole duty of man. For God will bring every work into judgment, with every hidden thing, whether it is good, or whether it is evil.
Title · 1:1
The Song of songs, which is Solomon’s.
Opening Desire · 1:2–17
The Woman →
Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth;
for your love is better than wine.
Your oils have a pleasing fragrance.
Your name is oil poured out,
therefore the virgins love you.
Take me away with you.
Let us hurry.
The king has brought me into his rooms.
The Friends →
We will be glad and rejoice in you.
We will praise your love more than wine!
The Woman →
They are right to love you.
I am dark, but lovely,
you daughters of Jerusalem,
like Kedar’s tents,
like Solomon’s curtains.
Don’t stare at me because I am dark,
because the sun has scorched me.
My mother’s sons were angry with me.
They made me keeper of the vineyards.
I haven’t kept my own vineyard.
Tell me, you whom my soul loves,
where you graze your flock,
where you rest them at noon;
For why should I be as one who is veiled
beside the flocks of your companions?
The Man →
If you don’t know, most beautiful among women,
follow the tracks of the sheep.
Graze your young goats beside the shepherds’ tents.
I have compared you, my love,
to a steed in Pharaoh’s chariots.
Your cheeks are beautiful with earrings,
your neck with strings of jewels.
The Friends →
We will make you earrings of gold,
with studs of silver.
The Woman →
While the king sat at his table,
my perfume spread its fragrance.
My beloved is to me a sachet of myrrh,
that lies between my breasts.
My beloved is to me a cluster of henna blossoms
from the vineyards of En Gedi.
The Man →
Look, you are beautiful, my love.
Look, you are beautiful.
Your eyes are doves.
The Woman →
Look, you are beautiful, my beloved, yes, pleasant;
and our couch is verdant.
The Man →
The beams of our house are cedars.
Our rafters are firs.
The Rose of Sharon · 2:1–7
The Woman →
I am a rose of Sharon,
a lily of the valleys.
The Man →
As a lily among thorns,
so is my love among the daughters.
The Woman →
As the apple tree among the trees of the wood,
so is my beloved among the sons.
I sat down under his shadow with great delight,
his fruit was sweet to my taste.
He brought me to the banquet hall.
His banner over me is love.
Strengthen me with raisins,
refresh me with apples;
For I am faint with love.
His left hand is under my head.
His right hand embraces me.
I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem,
by the roes, or by the hinds of the field,
that you not stir up, nor awaken love,
until it so desires.
The Springtime Invitation · 2:8–17
The voice of my beloved!
Look, he comes,
leaping on the mountains,
skipping on the hills.
My beloved is like a roe or a young deer.
Look, he stands behind our wall!
He looks in at the windows.
He glances through the lattice.
My beloved spoke, and said to me,
“Rise up, my love, my beautiful one, and come away.
For, look, the winter is past.
The rain is over and gone.
The flowers appear on the earth.
The time of the singing has come,
and the voice of the turtledove is heard in our land.
The fig tree ripens her green figs.
The vines are in blossom.
They give out their fragrance.
Arise, my love, my beautiful one,
and come away.”
The Man →
My dove in the clefts of the rock,
In the hiding places of the mountainside,
Let me see your face.
Let me hear your voice;
for your voice is sweet, and your face is lovely.
Catch for us the foxes,
the little foxes that plunder the vineyards;
for our vineyards are in blossom.
The Woman →
My beloved is mine, and I am his.
He browses among the lilies.
Until the day is cool, and the shadows flee away,
turn, my beloved,
and be like a roe or a young deer on the mountains of Bether.
The Night Search · 3:1–5
By night on my bed,
I sought him whom my soul loves.
I sought him, but I didn’t find him.
I will get up now, and go about the city;
in the streets and in the squares I will seek him whom my soul loves.
I sought him, but I didn’t find him.
The watchmen who go about the city found me;
“Have you seen him whom my soul loves?”
I had scarcely passed from them,
when I found him whom my soul loves.
I held him, and would not let him go,
until I had brought him into my mother’s house,
into the room of her who conceived me.
I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem,
by the roes, or by the hinds of the field,
that you not stir up, nor awaken love,
until it so desires.
Solomon's Wedding Procession · 3:6–11
Who is this who comes up from the wilderness like pillars of smoke,
perfumed with myrrh and frankincense,
with all spices of the merchant?
Look, it is Solomon’s carriage!
Sixty mighty men are around it,
of the mighty men of Israel.
They all handle the sword, and are expert in war.
Every man has his sword on his thigh,
because of fear in the night.
King Solomon made himself a carriage
of the wood of Lebanon.
He made its pillars of silver,
its bottom of gold, its seat of purple,
the middle of it being paved with love,
from the daughters of Jerusalem.
Go out, you daughters of Zion, and see king Solomon,
with the crown with which his mother has crowned him,
in the day of his weddings,
in the day of the gladness of his heart.
The Man Praises His Beloved · 4:1–7
The Man →
Look, you are beautiful, my love.
Look, you are beautiful.
Your eyes are doves behind your veil.
Your hair is as a flock of goats,
that descend from Mount Gilead.
Your teeth are like a newly shorn flock,
which have come up from the washing,
where every one of them has twins.
None is bereaved among them.
Your lips are like scarlet thread.
Your mouth is lovely.
Your temples are like a piece of a pomegranate behind your veil.
Your neck is like David’s tower built for an armory,
whereon a thousand shields hang,
all the shields of the mighty men.
Your two breasts are like two fawns
that are twins of a roe,
which feed among the lilies.
Until the day is cool, and the shadows flee away,
I will go to the mountain of myrrh,
to the hill of frankincense.
You are all beautiful, my love.
There is no spot in you.
The Invitation · 4:8–16
Come with me from Lebanon, my bride,
with me from Lebanon.
Look from the top of Amana,
from the top of Senir and Hermon,
from the lions’ dens,
from the mountains of the leopards.
You have ravished my heart, my sister, my bride.
You have ravished my heart with one of your eyes,
with one chain of your neck.
How beautiful is your love, my sister, my bride!
How much better is your love than wine!
The fragrance of your perfumes than all kinds of spices!
Your lips, my bride, drip like the honeycomb.
Honey and milk are under your tongue.
The smell of your garments is like the smell of Lebanon.
A locked up garden is my sister, my bride;
a locked up spring,
a sealed fountain.
Your shoots are an orchard of pomegranates, with precious fruits:
henna with spikenard plants,
spikenard and saffron,
calamus and cinnamon, with every kind of incense tree;
myrrh and aloes, with all the best spices,
a fountain of gardens,

Title · 1:1
This is the vision Isaiah son of Amoz sees about Judah and Jerusalem, in the days when Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah are kings of Judah.
The Rebellious Nation · 1:2–9
Listen, you heavens! Earth, open your ears!
For YHWH is speaking:
“Children I have raised, children I have lifted high,
and they have broken away from me.
The ox knows its owner,
the donkey knows its master's feeding trough,
but Israel has no idea;
my people do not take it in.”
Oh, sinning nation,
a people weighed down with guilt,
a brood of evildoers,
children who ruin everything they touch!
They have walked away from YHWH.
They have scorned the Holy One of Israel.
They have turned their backs and gone.
Why keep asking to be struck?
Why go on rebelling?
The whole head is sick,
the whole heart is faint.
From the sole of the foot to the crown of the head
there is no sound spot left —
only bruises and welts and raw wounds,
never cleaned, never bandaged,
never soothed with oil.
Your land lies empty.
Your cities are burned to the ground.
Right before your eyes, strangers eat up your fields.
It is a wasteland, as if foreigners had torn it down.
And Daughter Zion is left
like a booth in a vineyard,
like a lean-to in a melon patch,
like a city under siege.
If YHWH of hosts had not left us
a handful of survivors,
we would be like Sodom;
we would look like Gomorrah.
Empty Religion · 1:10–20
Hear the word of YHWH,
you rulers of Sodom!
Open your ears to the teaching of our God,
you people of Gomorrah!
“What do I want with all your sacrifices?”
says YHWH.
“I am stuffed full of burnt rams
and the fat of fattened calves.
The blood of bulls and lambs and goats
gives me no pleasure.
When you come to appear before me,
who asked you for this,
this trampling through my courts?
Stop bringing me worthless offerings!
Your incense disgusts me.
New moons and Sabbaths and the calling of assemblies —
I cannot bear wickedness dressed up as worship.
Your new moons and your feasts
my whole soul hates.
They are a load on my back;
I am worn out from carrying them.
When you spread out your hands to pray,
I hide my eyes from you.
Even when you pile up prayer on prayer,
I am not listening.
Your hands are full of blood.
Wash yourselves! Scrub yourselves clean!
Get your evil deeds out of my sight.
Quit doing wrong.
Learn to do good.
Go looking for justice.
Set the oppressor straight.
Stand up for the orphan.
Plead the widow's case.”
“Come, let's settle this together,”
says YHWH.
“Though your sins are scarlet-dyed,
they will turn snow-white.
Though they are stained crimson-red,
they will become like fresh wool.
If you are willing and you listen,
you will eat the good things of the land.
But if you refuse and rebel,
the sword will eat you.”
The mouth of YHWH has spoken.
The Fallen City · 1:21–31
Oh, how she has become a prostitute,

She was full of justice;

and now — murderers.
Your silver has turned to slag.

Your princes are rebels
and partners with thieves.
Every one of them loves a bribe
and chases after payoffs.
They do not defend the orphan,
and the widow's case never even reaches them.
So hear what the Lord declares,
YHWH of hosts, the Mighty One of Israel:
“Ah! I will be rid of my foes.
I will pay back my enemies.
I will turn my hand against you.
I will smelt your slag away as if with lye
and pull out all your impurities.
I will give you back your judges as at the first
and your counselors as in the beginning.
After that you will be called
the City of Righteousness,
the Faithful Town.”
Zion will be redeemed by justice,
and those in her who turn back, by righteousness.
But rebels and sinners will be broken together,
and those who walk away from YHWH will come to an end.
You will be ashamed of the sacred oaks
you loved so much.
You will blush over the gardens
you chose for yourselves.
For you will be like an oak
whose leaves are withering,
like a garden with no water.
The strong man will become tinder,
and his work a spark.
The two will burn together,
and no one will put out the fire.

This is the word that Isaiah son of Amoz sees about Judah and Jerusalem.

For you have cast off your people,

My beloved has a vineyard

but all it grows is stinking fruit.

I will pull up its hedge,

For the vineyard of YHWH of hosts

and the people of Judah

Six Woes · 5:8–23
Woe to you who join house to house

Woe to those who get up early in the morning

who linger late into the evening

They have lyre and harp,

but they never look at what YHWH is doing;
they never see the work of his hands.
So my people go into exile

Their nobles are dying of hunger,
and their crowds are parched with thirst.

and stretches its mouth beyond all measure,
and down go Jerusalem's nobles and her crowds,
her noisy throngs and all who party in her.
So humanity is brought low,
everyone is humbled,
and the eyes of the proud are lowered.
But YHWH of hosts is lifted high in justice,
and the holy God shows himself holy in righteousness.
Then lambs will graze as in their own pasture,
and strangers will feed among the ruins of the rich.
Woe to those who haul guilt along with cords of falsehood
and drag sin behind them like a cart on ropes,
who say, “Let him hurry!
Let him get on with his work
so we can see it!

come close and arrive,
so we will know it!”
Woe to those who call evil good
and good evil,
who turn darkness into light
and light into darkness,
who turn bitter into sweet
and sweet into bitter!
Woe to those who are wise in their own eyes
and clever in their own sight!
Woe to those who are heroes at drinking wine
and champions at mixing liquor,
who let the guilty off for a bribe
and strip the innocent of their rights!
The Outstretched Hand · 5:24–30
So, as a tongue of fire licks up straw
and dry grass sinks down in the flame,
their root will rot away
and their blossom blow off like dust,
for they have rejected the teaching of YHWH of hosts
and scorned the word of the Holy One of Israel.
That is why the anger of YHWH burns against his people.
He stretches out his hand against them and strikes them down.
The mountains tremble,
and their corpses lie like garbage in the streets.
For all this, his anger has not turned away;
his hand is still stretched out.
He raises a signal flag for a far-off nation
and whistles for them from the ends of the earth —
and here they come, swift and fast!
Not one of them is weary, not one stumbles.
None of them dozes or sleeps.
Not a belt comes loose at the waist;
not a sandal strap snaps.
Their arrows are sharp,
and all their bows are bent.
Their horses' hooves are hard as flint,
their chariot wheels like a whirlwind.
Their roar is like a lion's;
they roar like young lions.
They growl and seize their prey
and carry it off,
and no one can rescue it.
In that day they will growl over it
like the roaring of the sea.
And if anyone looks out over the land —
darkness and distress!
Even the light is blotted out by its clouds.
The Throne-Room Vision · 6:1–7

In the year King Uzziah dies, I see the Lord sitting on a throne, high and lifted up, and the hem of his robe fills the temple. Seraphim stand above him, each with six wings. With two they cover their faces, with two they cover their feet, and with two they fly. They call out to one another: “Holy, holy, holy is YHWH of hosts! His glory fills the whole earth!” At the sound of their calling, the doorposts shake on their foundations, and the house fills with smoke.

And I say, “Oh no! I am done for! My lips are unclean, and I live among a people whose lips are unclean — and with my own eyes I have seen the King, YHWH of hosts!” Then one of the seraphim flies to me. In his hand is a glowing coal he has taken from the altar with tongs. He touches my mouth with it and says, “Look, this has touched your lips. Your guilt is gone, and your sin is covered.”
The Commission · 6:8–13

Then I hear the voice of the Lord saying, “Whom shall I send? Who will go for us?” And I say, “Here I am. Send me!” He says, “Go, and tell this people: ‘Keep on listening, but never understand. Keep on looking, but never perceive.’ Make the heart of this people fat, make their ears heavy, and shut their eyes, or else they might see with their eyes and hear with their ears and understand with their hearts, and turn back and be healed.”

Then I say, “How long, Lord?” And he answers, “Until the cities lie in ruins with no one living in them, the houses stand without people, and the land is utterly desolate, until YHWH sends the people far away and the land is left empty and abandoned. Even if a tenth remains in it, it will be burned again, like a terebinth or an oak that leaves a stump when it is cut down. The holy seed is its stump.”
The Syro-Ephraimite Crisis · 7:1–9

In the days of Ahaz son of Jotham, son of Uzziah, king of Judah, Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah, king of Israel, march up to make war on Jerusalem, but they cannot conquer it. Word comes to the house of David: “Aram has joined forces with Ephraim.” And the heart of the king and the hearts of his people shake like the trees of the forest shaking in the wind.

Then YHWH says to Isaiah, “Go out to meet Ahaz, you and your son Shear-jashub, at the end of the channel from the Upper Pool, on the road to the Launderer's Field. Say to him, ‘Be careful, and stay calm. Don't be afraid. Don't let your heart lose its nerve over these two smoldering stubs of firewood, over the burning anger of Rezin and Aram and the son of Remaliah. Aram, with Ephraim and the son of Remaliah, has plotted evil against you. They say, “Let's invade Judah and terrify it. Let's break it open for ourselves and set up the son of Tabeel as king inside it.” But this is what the Lord YHWH says: It will not stand. It will not happen. For the head of Aram is Damascus, and the head of Damascus is only Rezin. Within sixty-five years Ephraim will be too shattered to be a people. The head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is only Remaliah's son. If you will not stand firm in faith, you will not stand at all.’”
The Sign of Immanuel · 7:10–25
Again YHWH speaks to Ahaz: “Ask YHWH your God for a sign. Ask for one as deep as Sheol or as high as the heavens.” But Ahaz says, “I will not ask. I will not put YHWH to the test.”

Then Isaiah says, “Listen now, house of David! Is it not enough for you to wear out the patience of people? Must you wear out the patience of my God too? So the Lord himself will give you a sign. Look! The young woman is pregnant and will give birth to a son, and she will name him Immanuel. He will be eating curds and honey by the time he knows how to refuse what is evil and choose what is good. For before the boy knows how to refuse evil and choose good, the land of the two kings you dread will be deserted. YHWH will bring on you, on your people, and on your father's house days like none since the day Ephraim broke away from Judah. He will bring the king of Assyria.”

In that day YHWH will whistle for the fly from the far streams of the Nile in Egypt and for the bee in the land of Assyria. They will come and settle, all of them, in the steep ravines and the cracks of the rocks, on every thornbush and at every watering place. In that day the Lord will shave with a razor hired from beyond the River, the king of Assyria. He will shave the head and the hair of the legs, and it will sweep off the beard as well. In that day a man will keep alive one young cow and two sheep, and they will give so much milk that he will eat curds. Everyone left in the land will eat curds and honey. In that day every place where there used to be a thousand vines, worth a thousand pieces of silver, will be given over to briers and thorns. People will go there with bow and arrows, because the whole land will be briers and thorns. And the hills that used to be worked with the hoe — you will not go there for fear of the briers and thorns. They will become a place where cattle are turned loose and sheep trample.
Maher-shalal-hash-baz · 8:1–10

YHWH says to me, “Take a large tablet and write on it in ordinary letters: Belonging to Maher-shalal-hash-baz.” So I call in reliable witnesses to testify for me, Uriah the priest and Zechariah son of Jeberechiah. YHWH speaks to me again:
“Because this people has rejected
the gently flowing waters of Shiloah
and delights in Rezin and the son of Remaliah,
the Lord is about to bring up against them
the waters of the River, mighty and many:
the king of Assyria in all his glory.
It will rise over all its channels
and spill over all its banks.
It will sweep on into Judah,
flooding and pouring through,
reaching up to the neck,
and its outspread wings will fill
the whole breadth of your land, O Immanuel.”
Rage, you peoples, and be shattered!
Listen, all you distant lands!
Arm yourselves, and be shattered!
Arm yourselves, and be shattered!
Make your plans; they will come to nothing.
Give your orders; they will not stand.
For God is with us.
Fear YHWH Alone · 8:11–22
This is what YHWH says to me, with his strong hand upon me, warning me not to walk in the way of this people:
“Do not call conspiracy
everything this people calls conspiracy.
Do not fear what they fear,
and do not be terrified.
YHWH of hosts — he is the one you must treat as holy.
He is the one to fear;
he is the one to dread.
He will be a sanctuary,
but also a stone to strike against
and a rock to stumble over
for both houses of Israel,
a trap and a snare
for those who live in Jerusalem.
Many will stumble over them.
They will fall and be broken;
they will be snared and caught.”
Bind up the testimony.
Seal the teaching among my disciples.
I will wait for YHWH,
who is hiding his face from the house of Jacob.
I will put my hope in him.
Look, here I am with the children YHWH has given me.
We are signs and omens in Israel
from YHWH of hosts, who dwells on Mount Zion.

When people say to you, “Ask the mediums and the spiritists, who chirp and mutter,” shouldn't a people ask their own God? Why ask the dead on behalf of the living? To the teaching and to the testimony! If they do not speak by this word, there is no dawn for them. They will wander through the land, beaten down and hungry. When they are hungry, they will rage and curse their king and their God. They will look up toward heaven, then look down at the earth, and see only distress and darkness, the gloom of anguish, and they will be driven into thick darkness.
The Great Light · 9:1–7
But there will be no more gloom for the land that was in anguish.
In the past he humbled the land of Zebulun
and the land of Naphtali,
but in days to come he will bring glory
to the Way of the Sea, the land beyond the Jordan,
Galilee of the nations.
The people who walk in the dark
are seeing a great light.
Those living in the land of death's shadow —
on them the light is dawning.
You make the nation many;
you make its joy great.
They rejoice before you
as people rejoice at harvest,
as warriors celebrate when they divide the plunder.
For the yoke that weighed them down,
the bar across their shoulders,
the rod of their oppressor —
you shatter them all, as on the day of Midian.
Every boot that tramped in battle
and every cloak rolled in blood
will be burned,
fuel for the fire.
For a child is born to us,
a son is given to us,
and the right to rule rests on his shoulders.
And he is named
Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God,
Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.
His rule will keep growing,
and its peace will have no end,
on the throne of David and over his kingdom,
to establish it and hold it up
with justice and righteousness
from now on and forever.
YHWH of hosts will see it done, burning with zeal.
The Outstretched Hand Continues · 9:8–21
The Lord sends a word against Jacob,
and it falls on Israel.
All the people will know it,
Ephraim and those who live in Samaria,
who say in their pride
and arrogance of heart,
“The bricks have fallen,
but we will build with cut stone.
The sycamore figs are chopped down,
but we will put cedars in their place.”
So YHWH raises up Rezin's foes against him
and stirs up his enemies:
Arameans from the east and Philistines from the west,
and they devour Israel with open mouths.
For all this, his anger has not turned away;
his hand is still stretched out.
But the people do not turn back to the one who strikes them;
they do not seek YHWH of hosts.
So YHWH cuts off from Israel head and tail,
palm branch and reed, in a single day.
The elder and the man of rank are the head;
the prophet who teaches lies is the tail.
Those who guide this people lead them astray,
and those who are guided are swallowed up.
That is why the Lord takes no joy in their young men
and has no pity on their orphans and widows,
for every one of them is godless and evil,
and every mouth speaks foolishness.
For all this, his anger has not turned away;
his hand is still stretched out.
For wickedness burns like a fire;
it eats up briers and thorns.
It sets the forest thickets ablaze,
and they roll upward in a column of smoke.
By the fury of YHWH of hosts
the land is scorched,
and the people are like fuel for the fire.
No one spares his own brother.
They slice meat on the right, but are still hungry;
they eat on the left, but are not satisfied.
Each one devours the flesh of his own arm.
Manasseh devours Ephraim,
and Ephraim Manasseh,
and together they turn on Judah.
For all this, his anger has not turned away;
his hand is still stretched out.
Woe to Unjust Legislators · 10:1–4
Woe to those who write wicked laws
and keep drafting decrees that crush people,
to push the poor away from justice
and rob the needy among my people of their rights,
so that widows become their prey
and orphans their plunder!
What will you do on the day of reckoning,
when the storm comes from far away?
Who will you run to for help?
Where will you leave your riches?
Nothing is left but to crouch among the prisoners
or fall among the dead.
For all this, his anger has not turned away;
his hand is still stretched out.
The Assyrian Rod · 10:5–19
Woe to Assyria, the rod of my anger!
The club in their hand is my fury.
I send him against a godless nation;
I command him against the people who enrage me,
to grab the spoil and seize the plunder
and trample them down like mud in the streets.
But that is not what he has in mind;
that is not what he is planning.
His heart is set on destroying,
on wiping out nations, and not just a few.
For he says, “Aren't my commanders all kings?
Isn't Calno like Carchemish?
Isn't Hamath like Arpad?
Isn't Samaria like Damascus?
My hand has seized the kingdoms of the idols,
whose images outnumbered those of Jerusalem and Samaria.
Shall I not do to Jerusalem and her images
what I have done to Samaria and her idols?”
When the Lord finishes all his work
on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem,
he will punish the king of Assyria
for the fruit of his arrogant heart
and the haughty look in his eyes.
For he says:
“By the strength of my own hand I have done it,
and by my wisdom, because I am so clever.
I have erased the borders of nations
and looted their treasures.
Like a mighty bull I have brought down those on thrones.
My hand has found the wealth of the peoples like a nest.
As one gathers abandoned eggs,
I have gathered up the whole earth,
and not one wing fluttered,
not one beak opened to chirp.”
Does the axe brag over the one who swings it?
Does the saw lord it over the one who pulls it?
As if a rod could wave the one who lifts it,
or a club could lift up someone who is not wood!
So the Lord, YHWH of hosts,
will send a wasting sickness among his stout warriors,
and under his glory a fire will be kindled,
burning like a blazing fire.
The Light of Israel will become a fire,
and his Holy One a flame.
It will burn and devour his thorns and his briers
in a single day.
The glory of his forest and his orchard
he will destroy, body and soul,
as when a sick man wastes away.
The trees left in his forest will be so few
that a child could write them down.
The Remnant Returns · 10:20–34
In that day the remnant of Israel,
the survivors of the house of Jacob,
will no longer lean on the one who struck them.
They will lean in truth on YHWH,
the Holy One of Israel.
A remnant will return,
the remnant of Jacob,
to the Mighty God.
For though your people, Israel,
are like the sand of the sea,
only a remnant of them will return.
Destruction is decreed,
overflowing with righteousness.
For the Lord, YHWH of hosts,
will carry out the destruction he has decreed
in the midst of all the earth.
So this is what the Lord, YHWH of hosts, says:
“My people who live in Zion,
do not be afraid of Assyria,
though they beat you with a rod
and raise their club against you as Egypt did.
For in a very little while my fury will be over,
and my anger will turn to their destruction.”
YHWH of hosts will crack a whip against them,
as when he struck Midian at the rock of Oreb,
and he will raise his staff over the sea,
as he did in Egypt.
In that day their burden will be lifted from your shoulders
and their yoke from your neck.
The yoke will break because you have grown so strong.
He comes to Aiath.
He passes through Migron.
At Michmash he leaves his baggage.
They cross the pass:
“We camp tonight at Geba!”
Ramah trembles;
Gibeah of Saul runs away.
Cry out, Daughter Gallim!
Listen, Laishah!
Poor Anathoth!
Madmenah is on the run;
the people of Gebim take cover.
This very day he halts at Nob.
He shakes his fist
at the mountain of Daughter Zion,
the hill of Jerusalem.
Look! The Lord, YHWH of hosts,
lops off the branches with terrifying power.
The towering trees are cut down;
the lofty ones are laid low.
He hacks down the forest thickets with an axe,
and Lebanon falls before the Mighty One.
The Shoot from Jesse · 11:1–9
A green shoot will break out of Jesse's stump,
and a branch will grow from his roots and bear fruit.
The Spirit of YHWH will rest on him:
the Spirit of wisdom and understanding,
the Spirit of counsel and strength,
the Spirit of knowledge and the fear of YHWH.
His delight will be in the fear of YHWH.
He will not judge by what his eyes see
or decide by what his ears hear.
He will judge the poor with righteousness
and decide fairly for the humble of the earth.
He will strike the earth with the rod of his mouth
and kill the wicked with the breath of his lips.
Righteousness will be the belt around his waist,
and faithfulness the sash around his hips.
The wolf will be the lamb's houseguest,
the leopard will bed down beside the young goat,
calf and lion cub and fat ox will be together,
and a small boy will herd them along.
Cow and bear will graze together,
their young curled up side by side,
and the lion will munch straw like the ox.
The nursing baby will play over the cobra's hole,
and the toddler will put his hand
into the viper's den.
They will not hurt or destroy
anywhere on my holy mountain,
for the knowledge of YHWH will fill the earth
the way the waters cover the seabed.
The Second Exodus · 11:10–16
In that day the Root of Jesse
will stand as a banner for the peoples.
The nations will come looking for him,
and his resting place will be glorious.
In that day the Lord will reach out his hand a second time
to reclaim the remnant of his people
who are left in Assyria and Egypt,
in Pathros and Cush, in Elam and Shinar,
in Hamath and the islands of the sea.
He will raise a banner for the nations
and gather the outcasts of Israel.
He will bring together the scattered people of Judah
from the four corners of the earth.
Ephraim's jealousy will vanish,
and Judah's enemies will be cut off.
Ephraim will not envy Judah,
and Judah will not harass Ephraim.
They will swoop down on the slopes of Philistia to the west;
together they will plunder the people of the east.
They will lay their hands on Edom and Moab,
and the Ammonites will obey them.
YHWH will dry up
the tongue of the Egyptian sea.
He will wave his hand over the River
with his scorching wind
and split it into seven streams
so people can walk across in sandals.
There will be a highway for the remnant of his people
who are left in Assyria,
just as there was for Israel
on the day they came up out of the land of Egypt.

In that day you will say:
“I thank you, YHWH!
Though you were angry with me,
your anger has turned away,
and you comfort me.
Look! God is my salvation.
I will trust and not be afraid.
For Yah, YHWH, is my strength and my song,
and he has become my salvation.”
You will haul up water with joy
from the springs of salvation.
In that day you will say:
“Give thanks to YHWH!
Call on his name!
Make his deeds known among the peoples.
Tell them his name is lifted high.

let this be known in all the earth.

for great in your midst is the Holy One of Israel!”
The Oracle Against Babylon · 13:1–22
The oracle concerning Babylon that Isaiah son of Amoz sees.
On a bare hilltop raise a signal flag!
Shout to them;
wave them on
to march through the gates of the nobles.
I myself have commanded my consecrated ones.
I have called my warriors to carry out my anger,
my proud and exultant ones.
Listen! A roar on the mountains,
like a vast crowd!
Listen! An uproar of kingdoms,
of nations gathering!
YHWH of hosts is mustering
an army for battle.
They come from a distant land,
from the far edge of the sky:
YHWH and the weapons of his fury,
coming to wreck the whole land.
Wail, for the day of YHWH is near!
It comes like ruin from the Almighty.
So every hand goes limp,
and every human heart melts.
They are terrified.
Pangs and pains grip them;
they writhe like a woman in labor.
They stare aghast at one another,
their faces burning red.
Look, the day of YHWH is coming,
cruel, with fury and burning anger,
to make the land a desolation
and wipe its sinners out of it.
The stars of the sky and their constellations
will not give their light.
The sun will be dark when it rises,
and the moon will not shine.
I will punish the world for its evil
and the wicked for their guilt.
I will put an end to the pride of the arrogant
and bring down the haughtiness of tyrants.
I will make people scarcer than fine gold,
rarer than the gold of Ophir.
So I will make the heavens shudder,
and the earth will be shaken out of its place
at the fury of YHWH of hosts
on the day of his burning anger.
Like a hunted gazelle,
like sheep with no one to gather them,
each will turn back to his own people;
each will run to his own land.
Whoever is found will be stabbed,
and whoever is caught will fall by the sword.
Their little ones will be dashed to pieces before their eyes,
their houses looted,
their wives raped.
Look, I am stirring up the Medes against them,
who care nothing for silver
and take no delight in gold.
Their bows will cut down the young men.
They will have no pity on the fruit of the womb;
their eyes will not spare children.
And Babylon, the jewel of kingdoms,
the proud splendor of the Chaldeans,
will be like Sodom and Gomorrah
when God overthrew them.
She will never be lived in again
or settled from generation to generation.
No Arab will pitch his tent there;
no shepherds will rest their flocks there.
Desert creatures will lie down there,
and her houses will be full of howling things.
Ostriches will live there,
and wild goats will dance there.
Hyenas will cry in her strongholds,
and jackals in her luxurious palaces.
Her time is close at hand,
and her days will not be prolonged.
The Restoration of Israel · 14:1–3

YHWH will have compassion on Jacob. He will choose Israel once again and settle them in their own land, and foreigners will join them and attach themselves to the house of Jacob. The peoples will take them and bring them home, and the house of Israel will possess those peoples in YHWH's land as male and female servants. They will take captive those who took them captive and rule over those who oppressed them. YHWH will give you rest from your pain and turmoil and from the hard labor forced on you.
The Taunt Against the King of Babylon · 14:4–23
On that day you will take up this taunt against the king of Babylon:
How the oppressor has come to an end!
How his fury has ceased!
YHWH has broken the staff of the wicked,
the scepter of the rulers,
that struck down peoples in fury
with blow after blow,
that ruled the nations in anger
with relentless persecution.
The whole earth is at rest and quiet;
they break out into song.
Even the cypresses rejoice over you,
and the cedars of Lebanon:
“Since you were laid low,
no woodsman comes up to cut us down.”
Sheol below is stirred up
to meet you when you come.
It rouses the shades to greet you,
all who were leaders of the earth.
It raises from their thrones
all the kings of the nations.
All of them answer and say to you,
“You too have become weak like us!
You have become just like us!”
Your pomp is brought down to Sheol,
along with the music of your harps.
Maggots are spread out as your bed,
and worms are your blanket.
How you have fallen from heaven,
Shining One, son of the dawn!
How you are cut down to the ground,
you who laid the nations low!
You said in your heart,
“I will climb up to heaven.
Above the stars of God
I will set my throne on high.
I will sit on the mount of assembly
in the far reaches of the north.
I will climb above the tops of the clouds;
I will make myself like the Most High.”
But you are brought down to Sheol,
to the far depths of the pit.
Those who see you stare at you
and ponder what has become of you:
“Is this the man who made the earth tremble
and shook kingdoms,
who turned the world into a wilderness
and tore down its cities,
who never let his prisoners go home?”
All the kings of the nations lie in glory,
each in his own tomb.
But you are thrown out of your grave
like a rejected branch,
covered with the slain,
those pierced by the sword,
who go down to the stones of the pit,
like a corpse trampled underfoot.
You will not join them in burial,
because you have ruined your land
and killed your people.
May the offspring of evildoers
never be named again!
Prepare a place to slaughter his sons
for the guilt of their fathers,
so they never rise to take over the earth
and fill the face of the world with cities.
“I will rise against them,”
declares YHWH of hosts.
“I will cut off from Babylon name and remnant,
offspring and descendants,”
declares YHWH.
“I will make her a home for hedgehogs
and a land of swamps,
and I will sweep her with the broom of destruction,”

across the Brook of the Willows.

from a people tall and smooth-skinned,

and comes to Egypt.
The idols of Egypt tremble before him,
and the heart of Egypt melts within it.
“I will stir up Egyptian against Egyptian.
Brother will fight against brother,
neighbor against neighbor,
city against city,
kingdom against kingdom.
The spirit of Egypt will be drained out of it,
and I will confound its plans.
They will consult the idols and the spirits of the dead,
the mediums and the spiritists.
I will hand Egypt over
to a harsh master,
and a fierce king will rule over them,”
declares the Lord, YHWH of hosts.
The waters of the sea will dry up,
and the river will be parched and dry.
The canals will stink;
the streams of Egypt will dwindle and dry up;
reeds and rushes will rot away.
The meadows by the Nile, at the mouth of the Nile,
and every sown field along the Nile
will dry up, blow away, and be gone.
The fishermen will groan.
All who cast hooks in the Nile will mourn,
and those who spread nets on the water will waste away.
Those who work with combed flax will despair,
and the weavers of white cloth will lose hope.
The pillars of the land will be crushed,
and all who work for wages will be sick at heart.
The princes of Zoan are nothing but fools;
Pharaoh's wisest counselors give senseless advice.
How can you say to Pharaoh,
“I am a son of the wise,
a son of ancient kings”?
Where are your wise men now?
Let them tell you,
let them find out
what YHWH of hosts has planned against Egypt.
The princes of Zoan have become fools;
the princes of Memphis are deceived.
The cornerstones of her tribes
have led Egypt astray.
YHWH has poured into her
a spirit of confusion,
and they make Egypt stagger in everything she does,
like a drunkard staggering in his vomit.
There is nothing Egypt can do,
head or tail, palm branch or reed.

In that day Egypt will be like women. They will tremble with fear before the hand that YHWH of hosts raises against them. The land of Judah will become a terror to Egypt. Everyone who hears it mentioned will be afraid because of the plan YHWH of hosts is making against them.

In that day five cities in the land of Egypt will speak the language of Canaan and swear loyalty to YHWH of hosts. One of them will be called the City of Destruction. In that day there will be an altar to YHWH in the middle of the land of Egypt, and a pillar to YHWH at its border. It will be a sign and a witness to YHWH of hosts in the land of Egypt. When they cry out to YHWH because of their oppressors, he will send them a savior and defender, and he will rescue them. YHWH will make himself known to Egypt, and in that day the Egyptians will know YHWH. They will worship with sacrifices and offerings; they will make vows to YHWH and keep them. YHWH will strike Egypt, striking and healing, and they will turn back to YHWH. He will hear their prayers and heal them.

In that day there will be a highway from Egypt to Assyria. Assyrians will come into Egypt and Egyptians into Assyria, and Egypt will worship together with Assyria. In that day Israel will be the third, along with Egypt and Assyria, a blessing in the middle of the earth, whom YHWH of hosts has blessed, saying, “Blessed be Egypt my people, and Assyria the work of my hands, and Israel my inheritance.”
The Sign-Act Against Egypt and Cush · 20:1–6

In the year the field commander, sent by Sargon king of Assyria, comes to Ashdod and fights against it and captures it, at that time YHWH speaks through Isaiah son of Amoz: “Go, untie the sackcloth from your waist and take the sandals off your feet.” And he does so, walking around naked and barefoot.

Then YHWH says, “Just as my servant Isaiah has walked naked and barefoot for three years as a sign and an omen against Egypt and Cush, so the king of Assyria will lead away the captives of Egypt and the exiles of Cush, young and old, naked and barefoot, with their buttocks bared, to Egypt's shame. Then they will be dismayed and ashamed because of Cush, their hope, and Egypt, their pride. The Desert by the Sea · 21:1–10
The oracle concerning the desert by the sea.

from a land of terror.
A harsh vision has been shown to me:
the traitor betrays,
the destroyer destroys.
Go up, Elam! Lay siege, Media!
I am putting an end to all the groaning she has caused.
That is why my body is racked with pain.
Pangs have seized me,
like the pangs of a woman in labor.
I am bent double at what I hear;
I am dazed at what I see.
My heart staggers;
horror overwhelms me.
The twilight I longed for
has become a terror to me.
They set the table,
they spread the rugs,
they eat, they drink!
Get up, you officers!
Oil the shields!
For this is what the Lord says to me:
“Go, post a lookout.
Let him report what he sees.
When he sees riders,
horsemen in pairs,
riders on donkeys,
riders on camels,
let him listen closely,
very closely.”
Then the lookout shouts like a lion:
“Lord, I stand on the watchtower
all day long,
and I am stationed at my post
every night.
And look, here they come:
riders, horsemen in pairs!”
And he calls out,
“Fallen, fallen is Babylon!
All the carved images of her gods
he has smashed to the ground!”
My people, crushed on the threshing floor,
my grain beaten on the floor,
what I have heard from YHWH of hosts,
the God of Israel,
I have told you.
Oracle Concerning Dumah · 21:11–12
The oracle concerning Dumah.
Someone calls to me from Seir,
“Watchman, how much of the night is left?
Watchman, how much of the night is left?”
The watchman says,
“Morning is coming, but night as well.
If you want to ask, then ask.

Oracle Concerning Arabia · 21:13–17
The oracle concerning Arabia.

you caravans of Dedanites.

you who live in the land of Tema.

For they have fled from swords,
from the drawn sword,
from the bent bow,
and from the heat of battle.

For this is what the Lord says to me: “Within one year, counted like the years of a hired worker, all the glory of Kedar will come to an end. The archers who are left, the warriors of Kedar, will be few,” for YHWH, the God of Israel, has spoken.
The Oracle Concerning the Valley of Vision · 22:1–14
The oracle concerning the Valley of Vision.
What is wrong with you now,
that you have all gone up to the rooftops,
you town full of noise,
a city in uproar,
a reveling town?
Your dead were not killed by the sword;
they did not die in battle.
All your leaders ran away together;
they were captured without a bow being drawn.
All of you who were found were captured together,
though you had run far away.
So I say, “Look away from me;
let me weep bitterly.
Do not hurry to comfort me
over the ruin of the daughter of my people.”
For the Lord, YHWH of hosts, has a day
of panic and trampling and confusion
in the Valley of Vision,
of walls battered down
and cries ringing out to the mountains.
Elam takes up the quiver,
with chariots and riders and horsemen,
and Kir uncovers the shield.
Your choicest valleys are full of chariots,
and horsemen take their stand at the gates.
He strips away the covering of Judah.
In that day you look
to the weapons in the House of the Forest.
You see that the breaches in the city of David are many,
and you collect the waters of the Lower Pool.
You count the houses of Jerusalem
and tear houses down to strengthen the wall.
You make a reservoir between the two walls
for the water of the Old Pool.
But you do not look to the one who did this,
or see the one who planned it long ago.
In that day the Lord, YHWH of hosts,
calls for weeping and mourning,
for shaving heads and putting on sackcloth.
But look — joy and celebration,
killing cattle and slaughtering sheep,
eating meat and drinking wine!
“Let's eat and drink,
for tomorrow we die!”
YHWH of hosts has revealed this in my hearing:
“Surely this guilt will not be atoned for
until you die,”
says the Lord, YHWH of hosts.
The Oracle Concerning Shebna and Eliakim · 22:15–25

This is what the Lord, YHWH of hosts, says: “Go to this steward, to Shebna, who is in charge of the palace, and say: ‘What are you doing here, and who gave you the right to cut out a tomb for yourself here, carving your grave on the height, chiseling a resting place for yourself in the rock? Look, YHWH is about to hurl you away, mighty man. He will grab you firmly, wind you up tight, and throw you like a ball into a wide land. There you will die, and there your splendid chariots will stay, you disgrace to your master's house! I will push you out of your office, and you will be pulled down from your post.

In that day I will call my servant Eliakim son of Hilkiah. I will dress him in your robe and fasten your sash around him and hand your authority over to him. He will be a father to the people of Jerusalem and to the house of Judah. I will lay the key of the house of David on his shoulder. What he opens, no one will shut, and what he shuts, no one will open. I will drive him like a peg into a firm place, and he will become a throne of honor for his father's house. And they will hang on him the whole weight of his father's house, offspring and offshoots, every small vessel, from the bowls to all the jars.’ In that day,” declares YHWH of hosts, “the peg driven into a firm place will give way. It will be cut down and fall, and the load hanging on it will be cut off,” for YHWH has spoken.
The Oracle Against Tyre · 23:1–18
The oracle concerning Tyre.
Wail, you ships of Tarshish,
for Tyre is destroyed,
without house or harbor!
From the land of Cyprus
the news reaches them.
Be silent, you who live on the coast,
you merchants of Sidon,
whom the seafarers have made rich.
Over the great waters came the grain of Shihor;
the harvest of the Nile was her income,
and she became the marketplace of the nations.
Be ashamed, Sidon,
for the sea has spoken,
the stronghold of the sea:
“I have not been in labor or given birth.
I have not raised young men
or brought up young women.”
When the news reaches Egypt,
they will writhe in anguish at the report about Tyre.
Cross over to Tarshish!
Wail, you who live on the coast!
Is this your reveling city,
whose origin goes back to ancient days,
whose feet carried her
to settle in far-off lands?
Who has planned this against Tyre,
the giver of crowns,
whose merchants are princes,
whose traders are the honored of the earth?
YHWH of hosts has planned it,
to defile the pride of all glory,
to humble all the honored of the earth.
Overflow your land like the Nile,
Daughter Tarshish;
there is no harbor anymore.
He has stretched out his hand over the sea
and made kingdoms tremble.
YHWH has given command concerning Canaan
to destroy its strongholds.
He said, “You will celebrate no more,
you oppressed virgin daughter of Sidon.
Get up, cross over to Cyprus;
even there you will find no rest.”
Look at the land of the Chaldeans!
This people is no more.
Assyria has turned it over to desert creatures.
They set up their siege towers,
they stripped her palaces bare,
and they made her a ruin.
Wail, you ships of Tarshish,
for your stronghold is destroyed!
In that day Tyre will be forgotten for seventy years, the lifetime of one king. At the end of seventy years, it will happen to Tyre as in the song about the prostitute:
“Take up a harp,
go around the city,
you forgotten prostitute!
Play sweetly, sing many songs,
so you will be remembered.”

At the end of seventy years YHWH will visit Tyre, and she will go back to earning her wages and will sell herself to all the kingdoms of the world on the face of the earth. But her profits and her wages will be holy to YHWH. They will not be stored up or hoarded; her profits will go to those who live in the presence of YHWH, to give them plenty to eat and fine clothing.
The Earth Laid Waste · 24:1–13
Look! YHWH is emptying the earth
and stripping it bare.
He twists its face out of shape
and scatters the people who live on it.
It will be the same for the people as for the priest,
for the servant as for his master,
for the maid as for her mistress,
for the buyer as for the seller,
for the lender as for the borrower,
for the creditor as for the debtor.
The earth will be emptied out completely
and plundered completely,
for YHWH has spoken this word.
The earth mourns and withers;
the world wastes away and withers;
the heights of the earth's people waste away.
The earth is polluted
under the feet of those who live on it,
for they have broken the laws,
twisted the statutes,
and shattered the everlasting covenant.
So a curse devours the earth,
and those who live on it bear their guilt.
So the people of the earth are scorched,
and only a few are left.
The new wine mourns;
the vine withers;
all the merry-hearted groan.
The happy beat of the tambourines is stilled;
the noise of the revelers has stopped;
the joyful sound of the lyre is silent.
No one drinks wine with a song anymore;
strong drink is bitter to those who drink it.
The city of chaos is broken down;
every house is shut up so no one can enter.
In the streets they cry out for wine.
All joy has turned to gloom;
gladness is banished from the earth.
Desolation is left in the city,
and the gate is battered into ruins.
For this is how it will be on the earth
among the nations:
like an olive tree beaten bare,
like the gleanings when the grape harvest is done.
The Song of the Remnant · 24:14–20
They lift up their voices and shout for joy;
from the west they sing out the majesty of YHWH.
So in the east give glory to YHWH;
in the islands of the sea,
give glory to the name of YHWH, the God of Israel.
From the ends of the earth we hear songs:
“Glory to the Righteous One!”
But I say, “I waste away! I waste away!
Woe is me!
The traitors betray!
With treachery the traitors betray!”
Terror and the pit and the trap
are waiting for you, people of the earth!
Whoever runs from the sound of terror
will fall into the pit,
and whoever climbs out of the pit
will be caught in the trap.
For the floodgates of heaven are opened,
and the foundations of the earth shake.
The earth is utterly broken;
the earth is split wide open;
the earth is violently shaken.
The earth staggers like a drunkard;
it sways like a hut in the wind.
Its rebellion lies heavy on it,
and it falls and will never rise again.
YHWH Reigns on Mount Zion · 24:21–23
In that day YHWH will punish
the powers of heaven in the heavens
and the kings of the earth on the earth.
They will be herded together
like prisoners in a pit.
They will be locked up in a prison,
and after many days they will be punished.
Then the moon will blush
and the sun will be ashamed,
for YHWH of hosts will reign
on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem,
and his glory will shine before his elders.
A Song of Praise for Victory · 25:1–5
YHWH, you are my God!
I will lift you high; I will praise your name,
for you have done wonderful things,
plans formed long ago,
faithful and sure.
You have turned the city into a heap of rubble,
the fortified town into a ruin.
The foreigners' palace is a city no more;
it will never be rebuilt.
So a strong people will honor you;
cities of ruthless nations will fear you.
For you have been a stronghold for the poor,
a stronghold for the needy in their distress,
a shelter from the storm
and a shade from the heat.
For the breath of the ruthless
is like a storm beating against a wall,
like heat in a dry land.

so the song of the ruthless is hushed.

On this mountain YHWH of hosts will make
for all peoples a feast of rich food,
a feast of aged wine,
of rich food full of marrow,
of aged wine well refined.
And on this mountain he will swallow up
the shroud that covers all peoples,
the sheet spread over all nations.
He will swallow death up for good.
The Lord YHWH will wipe the tears
off every face,
and he will take away his people's disgrace
from all the earth,
for YHWH has spoken.
In that day they will say,
“Look, this is our God!
We waited for him, and he saved us.
This is YHWH; we waited for him.
Let's rejoice and be glad in his salvation!”
For the hand of YHWH will rest on this mountain,
but Moab will be trampled down where he stands,
as straw is trampled down in a manure pit.
He will spread out his hands in it
as a swimmer spreads his hands to swim,
but YHWH will bring down his pride
in spite of all the skill of his hands.
The high fortress of your walls
he will bring down, lay low,
and throw to the ground,
down into the dust.

In that day this song will be sung in the land of Judah:
“We have a strong city!
God sets up salvation
as its walls and ramparts.
Open the gates,
so the righteous nation may come in,
the nation that keeps faith.
You keep in peace, perfect peace,
the mind that leans on you,
because it trusts in you.
Trust in YHWH forever,
for Yah, YHWH, is an everlasting Rock.
For he brings down those who live on the heights;
he lays the lofty city low.
He lays it low to the ground
and throws it down into the dust.
The foot tramples it down,
the feet of the poor,
the steps of the needy.
The path of the righteous is level;
you make smooth the road of the righteous.
Yes, YHWH, walking in the path of your judgments,
we wait for you.
Your name and your renown
are the longing of our souls.

my spirit within me searches for you at dawn.
For when your judgments come to the earth,
the people of the world learn righteousness.

they do not learn righteousness.

and do not see the majesty of YHWH.
YHWH, your hand is raised high,
but they do not see it.
Let them see your zeal for your people and be ashamed;
let the fire meant for your enemies consume them.
YHWH, you will set peace in place for us,
for everything we have accomplished
you have done for us.

but your name alone is the one we call on.

the shades do not rise.
You have punished them and destroyed them
and wiped out all memory of them.

you have made the nation larger.
You have won glory for yourself;
you have pushed back all the borders of the land.
YHWH, in their distress they looked for you;
when your discipline fell on them,
they could barely whisper a prayer.
Like a pregnant woman about to give birth,
who writhes and cries out in her pains,
so were we before you, YHWH.
We were pregnant, we writhed,
but we gave birth only to wind.

and no people have been born into the world.
Your dead will live;
their bodies will rise.

Come, my people, go into your rooms
and shut your doors behind you.

to punish the people of the earth for their guilt.

and will no longer hide its slain.

sing about a lovely vineyard!

I am not angry.

I would march out against them
and burn them all up.
Or else let them take hold of my protection.
Let them make peace with me.
Yes, let them make peace with me.
In days to come Jacob will take root;
Israel will bud and blossom
and fill the whole world with fruit.
Has he struck Israel
as he struck those who struck him?
Has Israel been killed
as his killers were killed?
By driving her away, by sending her off, you contend with her.
He drives her out with his fierce wind
on the day the east wind blows.
So by this the guilt of Jacob will be atoned for,
and this will be the full fruit of taking away his sin:
when he makes all the altar stones
like chalk stones crushed to pieces,
and no Asherah poles or incense altars are left standing.
For the fortified city stands alone,
a settlement abandoned and deserted like the wilderness.
There the calves graze;
there they lie down
and strip its branches bare.

and women come and use them to light their fires.

so their Maker will not have compassion on them,
and the one who formed them will show them no favor.

from the flowing Euphrates to the Brook of Egypt,
and you, O children of Israel,
will be gathered up one by one.

and those who were lost in the land of Assyria
and those who were driven away to the land of Egypt
will come and worship YHWH
on the holy mountain in Jerusalem.

Woe to the proud crown of Ephraim's drunkards,
to the fading flower of its glorious beauty,
set on the head of the rich valley,
the city of those knocked flat by wine!
Look! The Lord has someone mighty and strong.
