He who dashes in pieces has come up against you. Keep the fortress! Watch the way! Strengthen your waist! Fortify your power mightily! For YHWH restores the excellency of Jacob, as the excellency of Israel; for the destroyers have destroyed them, and ruin their vine branches. The shield of his mighty men is made red. The valiant men are in scarlet. The chariots flash with steel in the day of his preparation, and the pine spears are brandished. The chariots rage in the streets. They rush back and forth in the wide ways. Their appearance is like torches. They run like the lightnings. He summons his picked troops. They stumble on their way. They dash to its wall, and the protective shield is put in place. The gates of the rivers are opened, and the palace is dissolved. It is decreed: she is uncovered, she is carried away; and her servants moan as with the voice of doves, beating on their breasts. But Nineveh has been from of old like a pool of water, yet they flee away. “Stop! Stop!” they cry, but no one looks back. Take the plunder of silver. Take the plunder of gold, for there is no end of the store, the glory of all goodly furniture. She is empty, void, and waste. The heart melts, the knees knock together, their bodies and faces have grown pale.
The Fallen Lion · 2:11–13

Where is the den of the lions, and the feeding place of the young lions, where the lion and the lioness walk, the lion’s cubs, and no one makes them afraid? The lion tears in pieces enough for his cubs, and strangles for his lionesses, and fills his caves with the kill, and his dens with prey. “Look, I am against you,” says YHWH of hosts, “and I will burn her chariots in the smoke, and the sword will devour your young lions; and I will cut off your prey from the earth, and the voice of your messengers will no longer be heard.”
Woe to the Bloody City · 3:1–7

Woe to the bloody city! It is all full of lies and robbery. The prey doesn’t depart. The noise of the whip, the noise of the rattling of wheels, prancing horses, and bounding chariots, the horseman mounting, and the flashing sword, the glittering spear, and a multitude of slain, and a great heap of corpses, and there is no end of the bodies. They stumble on their bodies, because of the multitude of the prostitution of the alluring prostitute, the mistress of witchcraft, who sells nations through her prostitution, and families through her witchcraft. “Look, I am against you,” says YHWH of hosts, “and I will lift your skirts over your face. I will show the nations your nakedness, and the kingdoms your shame. I will throw abominable filth on you, and make you vile, and will set you a spectacle. It will happen that all those who look at you will flee from you, and say, ‘Nineveh is laid waste! Who will mourn for her?’ Where will I seek comforters for you?”
Better Than Thebes? · 3:8–13

Are you better than No-Amon, who is situated among the rivers, who have the waters around her; whose rampart is the sea, and her wall is of the sea? Cush and Egypt are her boundless strength. Put and Libya are her helpers. Yet is she carried away. She goes into captivity. Her young children also are dashed in pieces at the head of all the streets, and they cast lots for her honorable men, and all her great men are bound in chains. You also will be drunken. You will be hidden. You also will seek a stronghold because of the enemy. All your fortresses will be like fig trees with the first-ripe figs: if they are shaken, they fall into the mouth of the eater. Look, your troops among you are women. The gates of your land are set wide open to your enemies. The fire has devoured your bars.
The Futility of Nineveh's Defenses · 3:14–17

Draw water for the siege. Strengthen your fortresses. Go into the clay, and tread the mortar. Make the brick kiln strong. There the fire will devour you. The sword will cut you off. It will devour you like the grasshopper. Multiply like grasshoppers. Multiply like the locust. You have increased your merchants more than the stars of the skies. The grasshopper strips, and flees away. Your guards are like the locusts, and your officials like the swarms of locusts, which settle on the walls on a cold day, but when the sun appears, they flee away, and their place is not known where they are.
The Final Elegy · 3:18–19

Your shepherds slumber, king of Assyria. Your nobles lie down. Your people are scattered on the mountains, and there is no one to gather them. There is no healing your wound, for your injury is fatal. All who hear the report of you clap their hands over you; for who hasn’t felt your endless cruelty?
Title · 1:1
The revelation which Habakkuk the prophet sees.
Habakkuk's First Complaint · 1:2–4

YHWH, how long will I cry, and you will not hear? I cry out to you “Violence!” and will you not save? Why do you show me iniquity, and look at perversity? For destruction and violence are before me. There is strife, and contention rises up. Therefore the law is paralyzed, and justice never prevails; for the wicked surround the righteous; therefore justice comes out perverts.
YHWH's First Response · 1:5–11

“Look among the nations, watch, and wonder marvelously; for I am working a work in your days, which you will not believe though it is told you. For, look, I raise up the Chaldeans, that bitter and hasty nation, that march through the width of the earth, to possess dwelling places that are not theirs. They are feared and dreaded. Their judgment and their dignity proceed from themselves. Their horses also are swifter than leopards, and are more fierce than the evening wolves. Their horsemen press proudly on. Yes, their horsemen come from afar. They fly as an eagle that hurries to devour. All of them come for violence. Their hordes face the desert. He gathers prisoners like sand. Yes, he scoffs at kings, and princes are a derision to him. He laughs at every stronghold, for he builds up an earthen ramp, and takes it. Then he sweeps by like the wind, and goes on. He is indeed guilty, whose strength is his god.”
Habakkuk's Second Complaint · 1:12–17

Aren’t you from everlasting, YHWH my God, my Holy One? We will not die. YHWH, you have appointed him for judgment. You, Rock, have established him to punish. You who have purer eyes than to see evil, and who cannot look on perversity, why do you tolerate those who deal treacherously, and keep silent when the wicked swallows up the man who is more righteous than he, and make men like the fish of the sea, like the creeping things, that have no ruler over them? He takes up all of them with the hook. He catches them in his net, and gathers them in his dragnet. Therefore he rejoices and is glad. Therefore he sacrifices to his net, and burns incense to his dragnet, because by them his life is luxurious, and his food is good. Will he therefore continually empty his net, and kill the nations without mercy?
The Watchman Waits · 2:1
I will stand at my watch, and set myself on the ramparts, and will look out to see what he will say to me, and what I will answer concerning my complaint.
YHWH's Second Response: the Vision · 2:2–5

YHWH answers me, “Write the vision, and make it plain on tablets, that he who runs may read it. For the vision is yet for the appointed time, and it hurries toward the end, and won’t prove false. Though it takes time, wait for it; because it will surely come. It won’t delay. Look, his soul is puffed up. It is not upright in him, but the righteous will live by his faith. Yes, moreover, wine is treacherous. A haughty man who doesn’t stay at home, who enlarges his desire as Sheol, and he is like death, and can’t be satisfied, but gathers to himself all nations, and heaps to himself all peoples.
Five Woes against the Aggressor · 2:6–20

Won’t all these take up a parable against him, and a taunting proverb against him, and say, ‘Woe to him who increases that which is not his, and who enriches himself by extortion! How long?’ Won’t your debtors rise up suddenly, and wake up those who make you tremble, and you will be their victim? Because you have plundered many nations, all the remnant of the peoples will plunder you, because of men’s blood, and for the violence done to the land, to the city and to all who dwell in it. Woe to him who gets an evil gain for his house, that he may set his nest on high, that he may be delivered from the hand of evil! You have devised shame to your house, by cutting off many peoples, and have sinned against your soul. For the stone will cry out of the wall, and the beam out of the woodwork will answer it. Woe to him who builds a town with blood, and establishes a city by iniquity! Look, isn’t it of YHWH of hosts that the peoples labor for the fire, and the nations weary themselves for vanity? For the earth will be filled with the knowledge of YHWH’s glory, as the waters cover the sea.

“Woe to him who gives his neighbor drink, pouring your inflaming wine until they are drunk, so that you may gaze at their naked bodies! You are filled with shame, and not glory. You will also drink, and be exposed! The cup of YHWH’s right hand will come around to you, and disgrace will cover your glory. For the violence done to Lebanon will overwhelm you, and the destruction of the animals, which made them afraid; because of men’s blood, and for the violence done to the land, to every city and to those who dwell in them.

“What value does the engraved image have, that its maker has engraved it; the molten image, even the teacher of lies, that he who fashions its form trusts in it, to make mute idols? Woe to him who says to the wood, ‘Awake!’ or to the mute stone, ‘Arise!’ Will this teach? Look, it is overlaid with gold and silver, and there is no breath at all within it. But YHWH is in his holy temple. Let all the earth be silent before him!”
Title and Prayer · 3:1–2
A prayer of Habakkuk, the prophet, set to victorious music.
YHWH, I have heard of your fame.
I stand in awe of your deeds, YHWH.
Renew your work in the middle of the years.
In the middle of the years make it known.
In wrath, you remember mercy.
The Theophanic Hymn · 3:3–15
God came from Teman,
the Holy One from Mount Paran. Selah.
His glory covered the heavens,
and his praise filled the earth.
His splendor is like the sunrise.
Rays shine from his hand, where his power is hidden.
Plague went before him,
and pestilence followed his feet.
He stood, and shook the earth.
He looked, and made the nations tremble.
The ancient mountains were crumbled.
The age-old hills collapsed.
His ways are eternal.
I saw the tents of Cushan in affliction.
The dwellings of the land of Midian trembled.
Was YHWH displeased with the rivers?
Was your anger against the rivers,
or your wrath against the sea,
that you rode on your horses,
on your chariots of salvation?
You uncovered your bow.
You called for your sworn arrows. Selah.
You split the earth with rivers.
The mountains saw you, and were afraid.
The storm of waters passed by.
The deep roared and lifted up its hands on high.
The sun and moon stood still in the sky,
at the light of your arrows as they went,
at the shining of your glittering spear.
You marched through the land in wrath.
You threshed the nations in anger.
You went out for the salvation of your people,
for the salvation of your anointed.
You crushed the head of the land of wickedness.
You stripped them head to foot. Selah.
You pierced the heads of his warriors with their own spears.
They came as a whirlwind to scatter me,
gloating as if to devour the wretched in secret.
You trampled the sea with your horses,
churning mighty waters.
Trembling, Yet Trust · 3:16–19
I heard, and my body trembled.
My lips quivered at the voice.
Rottenness enters into my bones, and I tremble in my place,
because I must wait quietly for the day of trouble,
for the coming up of the people who invade us.
For though the fig tree doesn’t flourish,
nor fruit be in the vines;
the labor of the olive fails,
the fields yield no food;
the flocks are cut off from the fold,
and there is no herd in the stalls:
yet I will rejoice in YHWH.
I will be joyful in the God of my salvation!
YHWH, the Lord, is my strength.
He makes my feet like deer’s feet,
and enables me to go in high places.
For the music director, on my stringed instruments.
Title · 1:1
YHWH’s word which comes to Zephaniah, the son of Cushi, the son of Gedaliah, the son of Amariah, the son of Hezekiah, in the days of Josiah, the son of Amon, king of Judah.
Universal Judgment · 1:2–6

I will utterly sweep away everything from the surface of the earth, says YHWH. I will sweep away man and animal. I will sweep away the birds of the sky, the fish of the sea, and the heaps of rubble with the wicked. I will cut off man from the surface of the earth, says YHWH. I will stretch out my hand against Judah, and against all the inhabitants of Jerusalem. I will cut off the remnant of Baal from this place: the name of the idolatrous and pagan priests, those who worship the army of the sky on the housetops, those who worship and swear by YHWH and also swear by Malcam, those who have turned back from following YHWH, and those who haven’t sought YHWH nor inquire after him.
The Day of YHWH for Jerusalem · 1:7–13

Be silent at the presence of the Lord YHWH, for the day of YHWH is at hand. For YHWH has prepared a sacrifice. He has consecrated his guests. It will happen in the day of YHWH’s sacrifice, that I will punish the princes, the king’s sons, and all those who are clothed with foreign clothing. In that day, I will punish all those who leap over the threshold, who fill their master’s house with violence and deceit. In that day, says YHWH, there will be the noise of a cry from the fish gate, a wailing from the second quarter, and a great crashing from the hills. Wail, you inhabitants of Maktesh, for all the people of Canaan are undone! All those who are loaded with silver are cut off. It will happen at that time, that I will search Jerusalem with lamps, and I will punish the men who are settled on their dregs, who say in their heart, “YHWH will not do good, neither will he do evil.” Their wealth will become a plunder, and their houses a desolation. Yes, they will build houses, but won’t inhabit them. They will plant vineyards, but won’t drink their wine.
The Great Day of YHWH · 1:14–18

The great day of YHWH is near. It is near, and hurries greatly, the voice of the day of YHWH. The mighty man cries there bitterly. That day is a day of wrath, a day of distress and anguish, a day of trouble and ruin, a day of darkness and gloom, a day of clouds and blackness, a day of the trumpet and alarm, against the fortified cities, and against the high battlements. I will bring distress on men, that they will walk like blind men, because they have sinned against YHWH, and their blood will be poured out like dust, and their flesh like dung. Neither their silver nor their gold will be able to deliver them in the day of YHWH’s wrath, but the whole land will be devoured by the fire of his jealousy; for he will make an end, yes, a terrible end, of all those who dwell in the land.
Seek YHWH · 2:1–3

Gather yourselves together, yes, gather together, you nation that has no shame, before the appointed time when the day passes as the chaff, before the fierce anger of YHWH comes on you, before the day of YHWH’s anger comes on you. Seek YHWH, all you humble of the land, who have kept his ordinances. Seek righteousness. Seek humility. It may be that you will be hidden in the day of YHWH’s anger.
Against the Nations · 2:4–15

For Gaza will be forsaken, and Ashkelon a desolation. They will drive out Ashdod at noonday, and Ekron will be rooted up. Woe to the inhabitants of the sea coast, the nation of the Cherethites! YHWH’s word is against you, Canaan, the land of the Philistines. I will destroy you, that there will be no inhabitant. The sea coast will be pastures, with cottages for shepherds and folds for flocks. The coast will be for the remnant of the house of Judah. They will find pasture. In the houses of Ashkelon, they will lie down in the evening, for YHWH, their God, will visit them, and restore them. I have heard the reproach of Moab, and the insults of the children of Ammon, with which they have reproached my people, and magnify themselves against their border. Therefore as I live, says YHWH of hosts, the God of Israel, surely Moab will be as Sodom, and the children of Ammon as Gomorrah, a possession of nettles, and salt pits, and a perpetual desolation. The remnant of my people will plunder them, and the survivors of my nation will inherit them. This they will have for their pride, because they have reproached and magnify themselves against the people of YHWH of hosts. YHWH will be awesome to them, for he will famish all the gods of the land. Men will worship him, everyone from his place, even all the shores of the nations. You Cushites also, you will be killed by my sword. He will stretch out his hand against the north, destroy Assyria, and will make Nineveh a desolation, as dry as the wilderness. Herds will lie down in the middle of her, all the animals of the nations. Both the pelican and the porcupine will lodge in its capitals. Their calls will echo through the windows. Desolation will be in the thresholds, for he has laid bare the cedar beams. This is the joyous city that lives carelessly, that says in her heart, “I am, and there is no one besides me.” How she has become a desolation, a place for animals to lie down in! Everyone who passes by her will hiss, and shake their fists.
Woe to Jerusalem · 3:1–8

Woe to her who is rebellious and polluted, the oppressing city! She doesn’t obey the voice. She doesn’t receive correction. She doesn’t trust in YHWH. She doesn’t draw near to her God. Her princes within her are roaring lions. Her judges are evening wolves. They leave nothing until the next day. Her prophets are arrogant and treacherous people. Her priests have profaned the sanctuary. They have done violence to the law. YHWH, within her, is righteous. He will do no wrong. Every morning he brings his justice to light. He doesn’t fail, but the unjust know no shame. I have cut off nations. Their battlements are desolate. I have made their streets waste, so that no one passes by. Their cities are destroyed, so that there is no man, so that there is no inhabitant. I say, “Just fear me. Receive correction, so that her dwelling won’t be cut off, according to all that I have appointed concerning her.” But they rise early and corrupt all their doings. “Therefore wait for me”, says YHWH, “until the day that I rise up to the prey, for my determination is to gather the nations, that I may assemble the kingdoms, to pour on them my indignation, even all my fierce anger, for all the earth will be devoured with the fire of my jealousy.
Purified Lips and a Purified People · 3:9–13

For then I will purify the lips of the peoples, that they may all call on YHWH’s name, to serve him shoulder to shoulder. From beyond the rivers of Cush, my worshipers, even the daughter of my dispersed people, will bring my offering. In that day you will not be disappointed for all your doings, in which you have transgressed against me; for then I will take away out from among you your proudly exulting ones, and you will no more be haughty in my holy mountain. But I will leave among you an afflicted and poor people, and they will take refuge in YHWH’s name. The remnant of Israel will not do iniquity, nor speak lies, neither will a deceitful tongue be found in their mouth, for they will feed and lie down, and no one will make them afraid.”
Sing, Daughter of Zion · 3:14–17

Sing, daughter of Zion! Shout, Israel! Be glad and rejoice with all your heart, daughter of Jerusalem. YHWH has taken away your judgments. He has thrown out your enemy. The King of Israel, YHWH, is among you. You will not be afraid of evil any more. In that day, it will be said to Jerusalem, “Don’t be afraid, Zion. Don’t let your hands be weak.” YHWH, your God, is among you, a mighty one who will save. He will rejoice over you with joy. He will calm you in his love. He will rejoice over you with singing.
The Final Restoration · 3:18–20

I will remove those who grieve about the appointed feasts from you. They are a burden and a reproach to you. Look, at that time I will deal with all those who afflict you, and I will save those who are lame, and gather those who are driven away. I will give them praise and honor, whose shame has been in all the earth. At that time will I bring you in, and at that time will I gather you; for I will give you honor and praise among all the peoples of the earth, when I restore your fortunes before your eyes, says YHWH.
First Oracle: is It Time? · 1:1–11

In the second year of Darius the king, in the sixth month, in the first day of the month, YHWH’s word comes by Haggai, the prophet, to Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and to Joshua, the son of Jehozadak, the high priest, saying, “This is what YHWH of hosts says: These people say, ‘The time hasn’t yet come, the time for YHWH’s house to be built.’”

Then YHWH’s word comes by Haggai, the prophet, saying, “Is it a time for you yourselves to dwell in your paneled houses, while this house lies waste? Now therefore this is what YHWH of hosts says: Consider your ways. You have sown much, and bring in little. You eat, but you don’t have enough. You drink, but you aren’t filled with drink. You clothe yourselves, but no one is warm, and he who earns wages earns wages to put them into a bag with holes in it.”

This is what YHWH of hosts says: “Consider your ways. Go up to the mountain, bring wood, and build the house. I will take pleasure in it, and I will be glorified,” says YHWH. “You looked for much, and, look, it came to little; and when you brought it home, I blew it away. Why?” says YHWH of hosts, “Because of my house that lies waste, while each of you is busy with his own house. Therefore for your sake the heavens withhold the dew, and the earth withholds its fruit. I called for a drought on the land, on the mountains, on the grain, on the new wine, on the oil, on that which the ground produces, on men, on livestock, and on all the labor of the hands.”
The People Obey · 1:12–15

Then Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, and Joshua, the son of Jehozadak, the high priest, with all the remnant of the people, obeyed YHWH, their God’s voice, and the words of Haggai, the prophet, as YHWH, their God, have sent him; and the people fear YHWH.
Then Haggai, YHWH’s messenger, speaks YHWH’s message to the people, saying, “I am with you,” says YHWH.

YHWH stirs up the spirit of Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and the spirit of Joshua, the son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and the spirit of all the remnant of the people; and they come and work on the house of YHWH of hosts, their God, in the twenty-fourth day of the month, in the sixth month, in the second year of Darius the king.
Second Oracle: the Glory to Come · 2:1–9

In the seventh month, in the twenty-first day of the month, YHWH’s word comes by Haggai the prophet, saying, “Speak now to Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and to Joshua, the son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and to the remnant of the people, saying, ‘Who is left among you who saw this house in its former glory? How do you see it now? Isn’t it in your eyes as nothing? Yet now be strong, Zerubbabel,’ says YHWH. ‘Be strong, Joshua, son of Jehozadak, the high priest. Be strong, all you people of the land,’ says YHWH, ‘and work, for I am with you,’ says YHWH of hosts. This is the word that I covenanted with you when you came out of Egypt, and my Spirit lived among you. ‘Don’t be afraid.’ For this is what YHWH of hosts says: ‘Yet once, it is a little while, and I will shake the heavens, the earth, the sea, and the dry land; and I will shake all nations. The precious things of all nations will come, and I will fill this house with glory, says YHWH of hosts. The silver is mine, and the gold is mine,’ says YHWH of hosts. ‘The latter glory of this house will be greater than the former,’ says YHWH of hosts; ‘and in this place will I give peace,’ says YHWH of hosts.”
Third Oracle: from This Day on · 2:10–19

In the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, in the second year of Darius, YHWH’s word comes by Haggai the prophet, saying, “YHWH of hosts says: Ask now the priests concerning the law, saying, ‘If someone carries holy meat in the fold of his garment, and with his fold touches bread, stew, wine, oil, or any food, will it become holy?’”
The priests answer, “No.”
Then Haggai says, “If one who is unclean by reason of a dead body touch any of these, will it be unclean?”
The priests answer, “It will be unclean.”

Then Haggai answers, “‘So is this people, and so is this nation before me,’ says YHWH; ‘and so is every work of their hands. That which they offer there is unclean. Now, please consider from this day and backward, before a stone was laid on a stone in YHWH’s temple. Through all that time, when one came to a heap of twenty measures, there were only ten. When one came to the wine vat to draw out fifty, there were only twenty. I struck you with blight, mildew, and hail in all the work of your hands; yet you didn’t turn to me,’ says YHWH. ‘Consider, please, from this day and backward, from the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, since the day that the foundation of YHWH’s temple was laid, consider it. Is the seed yet in the barn? Yes, the vine, the fig tree, the pomegranate, and the olive tree haven’t produced. From today I will bless you.’”
Fourth Oracle: Zerubbabel My Signet Ring · 2:20–23

YHWH’s word comes the second time to Haggai in the twenty-fourth day of the month, saying, “Speak to Zerubbabel, governor of Judah, saying, ‘I will shake the heavens and the earth. I will overthrow the throne of kingdoms. I will destroy the strength of the kingdoms of the nations. I will overthrow the chariots, and those who ride in them. The horses and their riders will come down, everyone by the sword of his brother. In that day, says YHWH of hosts, will I take you, Zerubbabel, my servant, the son of Shealtiel,’ says YHWH, ‘and will make you as a signet, for I have chosen you,’ says YHWH of hosts.”
Call to Return · 1:1–6

In the eighth month, in the second year of Darius, YHWH’s word comes to Zechariah the son of Berechiah, the son of Iddo, the prophet, saying, “YHWH was very displeased with your fathers. Therefore tell them: YHWH of hosts says: ‘Return to me,’ says YHWH of hosts, ‘and I will return to you,’ says YHWH of hosts. Don’t you be like your fathers, to whom the former prophets proclaimed, saying: YHWH of hosts says, ‘Return now from your evil ways, and from your evil doings;’ but they did not hear, nor listen to me, says YHWH. Your fathers, where are they? And the prophets, do they live forever? But my words and my decrees, which I commanded my servants the prophets, didn’t they overtake your fathers?
“Then they repented and said, ‘Just as YHWH of hosts determined to do to us, according to our ways, and according to our practices, so he has dealt with us.’”
First Vision: the Horseman Among the Myrtles · 1:7–17

On the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month, which is the month Shebat, in the second year of Darius, YHWH’s word comes to Zechariah the son of Berechiah, the son of Iddo, the prophet, saying, “I had a vision in the night, and look, a man riding on a red horse, and he stood among the myrtle trees that were in a ravine; and behind him there were red, brown, and white horses. Then I asked, ‘My lord, what are these?’”
The angel who talks with me says to me, “I will show you what these are.”
The man who stands among the myrtle trees answers, “They are the ones YHWH has sent to go back and forth through the earth.”
They report to YHWH’s angel who stands among the myrtle trees, and say, “We have walked back and forth through the earth, and look, all the earth is at rest and in peace.”
Then YHWH’s angel replies, “O YHWH of hosts, how long will you not have mercy on Jerusalem and on the cities of Judah, against which you have had indignation these seventy years?”

YHWH answers the angel who talks with me with kind and comforting words. So the angel who talks with me says to me, “Proclaim, saying, ‘YHWH of hosts says: “I am jealous for Jerusalem and for Zion with a great jealousy. I am very angry with the nations that are at ease; for I was but a little displeased, but they added to the calamity.” Therefore YHWH says: “I have returned to Jerusalem with mercy. My house will be built in it,” says YHWH of hosts, “and a line will be stretched out over Jerusalem.”’
“Proclaim further, saying, ‘YHWH of hosts says: “My cities will again overflow with prosperity, and YHWH will again comfort Zion, and will again choose Jerusalem.”’”
Second Vision: Four Horns and Four Craftsmen · 1:18–21
I lift up my eyes, and see, and look, four horns. I ask the angel who talks with me, “What are these?”
He answers me, “These are the horns which have scattered Judah, Israel, and Jerusalem.”
YHWH shows me four craftsmen. Then I ask, “What are these coming to do?”

He says, “These are the horns which scattered Judah, so that no man lifted up his head; but these have come to terrify them, to cast down the horns of the nations, which lifted up their horn against the land of Judah to scatter it.”
Third Vision: the Man with the Measuring Line · 2:1–13
I lift up my eyes, and see, and look, a man with a measuring line in his hand. Then I ask, “Where are you going?”
He says to me, “To measure Jerusalem, to see what is its width and what is its length.”

Look, the angel who talks with me goes out, and another angel goes out to meet him, and says to him, “Run, speak to this young man, saying, ‘Jerusalem will be inhabited as villages without walls, because of the multitude of men and livestock in it. For I,’ says YHWH, ‘will be to her a wall of fire around it, and I will be the glory in the middle of her. Come! Come! Flee from the land of the north,’ says YHWH; ‘for I have spread you abroad as the four winds of the sky,’ says YHWH. ‘Come, Zion! Escape, you who dwell with the daughter of Babylon.’ For YHWH of hosts says: ‘For honor he has sent me to the nations which plundered you; for he who touches you touches the apple of his eye. For, look, I will shake my hand over them, and they will be a plunder to those who served them; and you will know that YHWH of hosts has sent me. Sing and rejoice, daughter of Zion; for, look, I come, and I will dwell within you,’ says YHWH. Many nations will join themselves to YHWH in that day, and will be my people; and I will dwell among you, and you will know that YHWH of hosts has sent me to you. YHWH will inherit Judah as his portion in the holy land, and will again choose Jerusalem. Be silent, all flesh, before YHWH; for he has roused himself from his holy habitation!”
Fourth Vision: Joshua the High Priest · 3:1–10

He shows me Joshua the high priest standing before YHWH’s angel, and Satan standing at his right hand to be his adversary. YHWH says to Satan, “YHWH rebuke you, Satan! Yes, YHWH who has chosen Jerusalem rebuke you! Isn’t this a burning stick plucked out of the fire?”

Now Joshua is clothed with filthy garments, and is standing before the angel. He answers and speaks to those who stand before him, saying, “Take the filthy garments off him.” To him he says, “Look, I have caused your iniquity to pass from you, and I will clothe you with rich clothing.”
I say, “Let them set a clean turban on his head.”

So they set a clean turban on his head, and clothe him; and YHWH’s angel is standing by. YHWH’s angel protests to Joshua, saying, “YHWH of hosts says: ‘If you will walk in my ways, and if you will follow my instructions, then you also will judge my house, and will also keep my courts, and I will give you a place of access among these who stand by. Hear now, Joshua the high priest, you and your fellows who sit before you; for they are men who are a sign: for, look, I will bring out my servant, the Branch. For, look, the stone that I have set before Joshua; on one stone are seven eyes: look, I will engrave its engraving,’ says YHWH of hosts, ‘and I will remove the iniquity of that land in one day. In that day,’ says YHWH of hosts, ‘you will invite every man his neighbor under the vine and under the fig tree.’”
Fifth Vision: the Lampstand and Olive Trees · 4:1–14
The angel who talks with me comes again, and wakens me, as a man who is wakened out of his sleep. He says to me, “What do you see?”

I say, “I have seen, and look, a lamp stand all of gold, with its bowl on the top of it, and its seven lamps on it; there are seven pipes to each of the lamps, which are on the top of it; and two olive trees by it, one on the right side of the bowl, and the other on the left side of it.”
I answer and speak to the angel who talks with me, saying, “What are these, my lord?”
Then the angel who talks with me answers me, “Don’t you know what these are?”
I say, “No, my lord.”

Then he answers and speaks to me, saying, “This is YHWH’s word to Zerubbabel, saying, ‘Not by might, nor by power, but by my Spirit,’ says YHWH of hosts. Who are you, great mountain? Before Zerubbabel you are a plain; and he will bring out the capstone with shouts of ‘Grace, grace, to it!’”

Moreover YHWH’s word comes to me, saying, “The hands of Zerubbabel have laid the foundation of this house. His hands will also finish it; and you will know that YHWH of hosts has sent me to you. Indeed, who despises the day of small things? For these seven will rejoice, and will see the plumb line in the hand of Zerubbabel. These are YHWH’s eyes, which run back and forth through the whole earth.”
Then I ask him, “What are these two olive trees on the right side of the lamp stand and on the left side of it?”
I ask him the second time, “What are these two olive branches, which are beside the two golden spouts, that pour the golden oil out of themselves?”
He answers me, “Don’t you know what these are?”
I say, “No, my lord.”
Then he says, “These are the two anointed ones who stand by the Lord of the whole earth.”
Sixth Vision: the Flying Scroll · 5:1–4
Then again I lift up my eyes, and see, and look, a flying scroll. He says to me, “What do you see?”
I answer, “I see a flying scroll; its length is twenty cubits, and its width ten cubits.”

Then he says to me, “This is the curse that goes out over the surface of the whole land; for everyone who steals will be cut off according to it on the one side; and everyone who swears falsely will be cut off according to it on the other side. I will cause it to go out,” says YHWH of hosts, “and it will enter into the house of the thief, and into the house of him who swears falsely by my name; and it will remain in the middle of his house, and will destroy it with its timber and its stones.”
Seventh Vision: the Woman in the Basket · 5:5–11
Then the angel who talks with me comes forward, and says to me, “Lift up now your eyes, and see what is this that is appearing.”
I say, “What is it?”

He says, “This is the ephah basket that is appearing.” He says moreover, “This is their appearance in all the land (and look, a talent of lead was lifted up); and this is a woman sitting in the middle of the ephah basket.” He says, “This is Wickedness”; and he throws her down into the middle of the ephah basket; and he throws the weight of lead on its mouth.

Then lifts I up my eyes, and sees, and look, there are two women, and the wind is in their wings. Now they have wings like the wings of a stork, and they lift up the ephah basket between earth and the sky. Then I say to the angel who talks with me, “Where are these carrying the ephah basket?”
He says to me, “To build her a house in the land of Shinar. When it is prepared, she will be set there in her own place.”
Eighth Vision: Four Chariots · 6:1–8

Again I lift up my eyes, and see, and look, four chariots come out from between two mountains; and the mountains are mountains of brass. In the first chariot are red horses; in the second chariot black horses; in the third chariot white horses; and in the fourth chariot dapple horses, all of them powerful. Then I ask the angel who talks with me, “What are these, my lord?”

The angel answers me, “These are the four winds of the sky, which go out from standing before the Lord of all the earth. The one with the black horses goes out toward the north country; and the white went out after them; and the dappled went out toward the south country.” The strong goes out, and seeks to go that they might walk back and forth through the earth: and he says, “Go around and through the earth!” So they walk back and forth through the earth.
Then he calls to me, and speaks to me, saying, “Look, those who go toward the north country have quieted my spirit in the north country.”
The Crowning of Joshua · 6:9–15

YHWH’s word comes to me, saying, “Take of them of the captivity, even of Heldai, of Tobijah, and of Jedaiah; and come the same day, and go into the house of Josiah the son of Zephaniah, where they have come from Babylon. Yes, take silver and gold, and make crowns, and set them on the head of Joshua the son of Jehozadak, the high priest; and speak to him, saying, ‘YHWH of hosts says, “Look, the man whose name is the Branch: and he will grow up out of his place; and he will build YHWH’s temple; even he will build YHWH’s temple; and he will bear the glory, and will sit and rule on his throne; and he will be a priest on his throne; and the counsel of peace will be between them both. The crowns will be to Helem, and to Tobijah, and to Jedaiah, and to Hen the son of Zephaniah, for a memorial in YHWH’s temple. Those who are far off will come and build in YHWH’s temple; and you will know that YHWH of hosts has sent me to you. This will happen, if you will diligently obey YHWH your God’s voice.”’”
The Question About Fasting · 7:1–7

In the fourth year of king Darius, YHWH’s word comes to Zechariah in the fourth day of the ninth month, the month of Chislev. The people of Bethel send Sharezer and Regem Melech, and their men, to entreat YHWH’s favor, and to speak to the priests of the house of YHWH of hosts, and to the prophets, saying, “Should I weep in the fifth month, separating myself, as I have done these so many years?”

Then the word of YHWH of hosts comes to me, saying, “Speak to all the people of the land, and to the priests, saying, ‘When you fasted and mourned in the fifth and in the seventh month for these seventy years, did you at all fast to me, really to me? When you eat, and when you drink, don’t you eat for yourselves, and drink for yourselves? Aren’t these the words which YHWH proclaimed by the former prophets, when Jerusalem was inhabited and in prosperity, and its cities around her, and the South and the lowland were inhabited?’”
The Real Requirement · 7:8–14

YHWH’s word comes to Zechariah, saying, “Thus has YHWH of hosts spoken, saying, ‘Execute true judgment, and show kindness and compassion every man to his brother. Don’t oppress the widow, nor the fatherless, the foreigner, nor the poor; and let none of you devise evil against his brother in your heart.’ But they refused to listen, and turned their backs, and stopped their ears, that they might not hear. Yes, they made their hearts as hard as flint, lest they might hear the law, and the words which YHWH of hosts had sent by his Spirit by the former prophets. Therefore great wrath came from YHWH of hosts. It has come to pass that, as he called, and they refused to listen, so they will call, and I will not listen,” says YHWH of hosts; “but I will scatter them with a whirlwind among all the nations which they have not known. Thus the land was desolate after them, so that no man passed through nor returned: for they made the pleasant land desolate.”
Ten Promises of Restoration · 8:1–23
The word of YHWH of hosts comes to me. YHWH of hosts says: “I am jealous for Zion with great jealousy, and I am jealous for her with great wrath.”
YHWH says: “I have returned to Zion, and will dwell in the middle of Jerusalem. Jerusalem will be called ‘The City of Truth;’ and the mountain of YHWH of hosts, ‘The Holy Mountain.’”

YHWH of hosts says: “Old men and old women will again dwell in the streets of Jerusalem, every man with his staff in his hand for very age. The streets of the city will be full of boys and girls playing in its streets.”
YHWH of hosts says: “If it is marvelous in the eyes of the remnant of this people in those days, should it also be marvelous in my eyes?” says YHWH of hosts.

YHWH of hosts says: “Look, I will save my people from the east country, and from the west country; and I will bring them, and they will dwell within Jerusalem; and they will be my people, and I will be their God, in truth and in righteousness.”

YHWH of hosts says: “Let your hands be strong, you who hear in these days these words from the mouth of the prophets who were in the day that the foundation of the house of YHWH of hosts was laid, even the temple, that it might be built. For before those days there was no wages for man, nor any wages for an animal; neither was there any peace to him who went out or came in, because of the adversary. For I set all men everyone against his neighbor. But now I will not be to the remnant of this people as in the former days,” says YHWH of hosts. “For the seed of peace and the vine will yield its fruit, and the ground will give its increase, and the heavens will give their dew; and I will cause the remnant of this people to inherit all these things. It will come to pass that, as you were a curse among the nations, house of Judah and house of Israel, so will I save you, and you will be a blessing. Don’t be afraid. Let your hands be strong.”

For YHWH of hosts says: “As I thought to do evil to you, when your fathers provoked me to wrath,” says YHWH of hosts, “and I didn’t repent; so again I have thought in these days to do good to Jerusalem and to the house of Judah. Don’t be afraid. These are the things that you will do: speak every man the truth with his neighbor. Execute the judgment of truth and peace in your gates, and let none of you devise evil in your hearts against his neighbor, and love no false oath: for all these are things that I hate,” says YHWH.

The word of YHWH of hosts comes to me. YHWH of hosts says: “The fasts of the fourth, fifth, seventh, and tenth months will be for the house of Judah joy and gladness, and cheerful feasts. Therefore love truth and peace.”

YHWH of hosts says: “Many peoples, and the inhabitants of many cities will yet come; and the inhabitants of one will go to another, saying, ‘Let us go speedily to entreat the favor of YHWH, and to seek YHWH of hosts. I will go also.’ Yes, many peoples and strong nations will come to seek YHWH of hosts in Jerusalem, and to entreat the favor of YHWH.” YHWH of hosts says: “In those days, ten men will take hold, out of all the languages of the nations, they will take hold of the skirt of him who is a Jew, saying, ‘We will go with you, for we have heard that God is with you.’”
Judgment on the Nations · 9:1–8
A revelation.
YHWH’s word is against the land of Hadrach,
and will rest upon Damascus;
for the eye of man
and of all the tribes of Israel is toward YHWH;
and Hamath, also, which borders on it;
Tyre and Sidon, because they are very wise.
Tyre built herself a stronghold,
and heaped up silver like the dust,
and fine gold like the mire of the streets.
Look, the Lord will dispossess her,
and he will strike her power in the sea;
and she will be devoured with fire.
Ashkelon will see it, and fear;
Gaza also, and will writhe in agony;
as will Ekron, for her expectation will be disappointed;
and the king will perish from Gaza,
and Ashkelon will not be inhabited.
Foreigners will dwell in Ashdod,
and I will cut off the pride of the Philistines.
I will take away his blood out of his mouth,
and his abominations from between his teeth;
and he also will be a remnant for our God;
and he will be as a chieftain in Judah,
and Ekron as a Jebusite.
I will encamp around my house against the army,
that no one pass through or return;
and no oppressor will pass through them any more:
for now I have seen with my eyes.
The Coming King · 9:9–10
Rejoice greatly, daughter of Zion!
Shout, daughter of Jerusalem!
Look, your King comes to you!
He is righteous, and having salvation;
lowly, and riding on a donkey,
even on a colt, the foal of a donkey.
I will cut off the chariot from Ephraim,
and the horse from Jerusalem;
and the battle bow will be cut off;
and he will speak peace to the nations:
and his dominion will be from sea to sea,
and from the River to the ends of the earth.
Return of the Prisoners · 9:11–17
As for you also,
because of the blood of your covenant,
I have set free your prisoners from the pit in which is no water.
Turn to the stronghold, you prisoners of hope!
Even today I declare that I will restore double to you.
For indeed I bend Judah as a bow for me.
I have filled the bow with Ephraim;
and I will stir up your sons, Zion,
against your sons, Greece,
and will make you like the sword of a mighty man.
YHWH will be seen over them;
and his arrow will go flash like lightning;
and the Lord YHWH will blow the trumpet,
and will go with whirlwinds of the south.
YHWH of hosts will defend them;
and they will destroy and overcome with sling stones;
and they will drink, and roar as through wine;
and they will be filled like bowls,
like the corners of the altar.
YHWH their God will save them in that day as the flock of his people;
for they are like the jewels of a crown,
lifted on high over his land.
For how great is his goodness,
and how great is his beauty!
Grain will make the young men flourish,
and new wine the virgins.
YHWH Will Restore His People · 10:1–12
Ask of YHWH rain in the spring time,
YHWH who makes storm clouds,
and he gives rain showers to everyone for the plants in the field.
For the teraphim have spoken vanity,
and the diviners have seen a lie;
and they have told false dreams.
They comfort in vain.
Therefore they go their way like sheep.
They are oppressed, because there is no shepherd.
My anger is kindled against the shepherds,
and I will punish the male goats;
For YHWH of hosts has visited his flock, the house of Judah,
and will make them as his majestic horse in the battle.
From him will come the cornerstone,
from him the nail,
from him the battle bow,
from him every ruler together.
They will be as mighty men,
treading down muddy streets in the battle;
and they will fight, because YHWH is with them;
and the riders on horses will be confounded.
“I will strengthen the house of Judah,
and I will save the house of Joseph,
and I will bring them back;
for I have mercy on them;
and they will be as though I had not cast them off:
for I am YHWH their God, and I will hear them.
Ephraim will be like a mighty man,
and their heart will rejoice as through wine;
yes, their children will see it, and rejoice.
Their heart will be glad in YHWH.
I will signal for them, and gather them;
for I have redeemed them;
and they will increase as they have increased.
I will sow them among the peoples;
and they will remember me in far countries;
and they will live with their children, and will return.
I will bring them again also out of the land of Egypt,
and gather them out of Assyria;
and I will bring them into the land of Gilead and Lebanon;
and there won’t be room enough for them.
He will pass through the sea of affliction,
and will strike the waves in the sea,
and all the depths of the Nile will dry up;
and the pride of Assyria will be brought down,
and the scepter of Egypt will depart.
I will strengthen them in YHWH;
and they will walk up and down in his name,” says YHWH.
The Cedar and the Shepherds · 11:1–3
Open your doors, Lebanon,
that the fire may devour your cedars.
Wail, cypress tree, for the cedar has fallen,
because the stately ones are destroyed.
Wail, you oaks of Bashan,
for the strong forest has come down.
A voice of the wailing of the shepherds!
For their glory is destroyed: a voice of the roaring of young lions!
For the pride of the Jordan is ruined.
The Parable of the Two Staffs · 11:4–17

YHWH my God says: “Feed the flock of slaughter. Their buyers slaughter them, and go unpunished. Those who sell them say, ‘Blessed be YHWH, for I am rich;’ and their own shepherds don’t pity them. For I will no more pity the inhabitants of the land,” says YHWH; “but, look, I will deliver the men everyone into his neighbor’s hand, and into the hand of his king. They will strike the land, and out of their hand I will not deliver them.”

So I feed the flock of slaughter, especially the oppressed of the flock. I take for myself two staffs. The one I call “Favor”, and the other I call “Union”, and I feed the flock. I cut off the three shepherds in one month; for my soul is weary of them, and their soul also loathes me. Then I say, “I will not feed you. That which dies, let it die; and that which is to be cut off, let it be cut off; and let those who are left eat each other’s flesh.” I take my staff Favor, and cut it apart, that I might break my covenant that I have made with all the peoples. It is broken in that day; and thus the poor of the flock that listens to me knows that it is YHWH’s word. I say to them, “If you think it best, give me my wages; and if not, keep them.” So they weigh for my wages thirty pieces of silver. YHWH says to me, “Throw it to the potter, the handsome price that I was valued at by them!” I take the thirty pieces of silver, and throw them to the potter, in YHWH’s house. Then I cut apart my other staff, even Union, that I might break the brotherhood between Judah and Israel.

YHWH says to me, “Take for yourself yet again the equipment of a foolish shepherd. For, look, I will raise up a shepherd in the land, who will not visit those who are cut off, neither will seek those who are scattered, nor heal that which is broken, nor feed that which is sound; but he will eat the meat of the fat sheep, and will tear their hoofs in pieces. Woe to the worthless shepherd who leaves the flock! The sword will be on his arm, and on his right eye. His arm will be completely withered, and his right eye will be totally blinded!”
Jerusalem a Cup of Reeling · 12:1–9

A revelation, YHWH’s word concerning Israel. YHWH, who stretches out the heavens, and lays the foundation of the earth, and forms the spirit of man within him says: “Look, I will make Jerusalem a cup of reeling to all the surrounding peoples, and it will also be on Judah in the siege against Jerusalem. It will happen in that day, that I will make Jerusalem a burdensome stone for all the peoples. All who burden themselves with it will be severely wounded, and all the nations of the earth will be gathered together against it. In that day,” says YHWH, “I will strike every horse with terror, and his rider with madness; and I will open my eyes on the house of Judah, and will strike every horse of the peoples with blindness. The chieftains of Judah will say in their heart, ‘The inhabitants of Jerusalem are my strength in YHWH of hosts their God.’ In that day I will make the chieftains of Judah like a pan of fire among wood, and like a flaming torch among sheaves; and they will devour all the surrounding peoples, on the right hand and on the left; and Jerusalem will yet again dwell in their own place, even in Jerusalem. YHWH also will save the tents of Judah first, that the glory of David’s house and the glory of the inhabitants of Jerusalem not be magnified above Judah. In that day YHWH will defend the inhabitants of Jerusalem. He who is feeble among them at that day will be like David, and David’s house will be like God, like YHWH’s angel before them. It will happen in that day, that I will seek to destroy all the nations that come against Jerusalem.
Mourning for the One They Have Pierced · 12:10–14

I will pour on David’s house, and on the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the spirit of grace and of supplication; and they will look to me whom they have pierced; and they will mourn for him, as one mourns for his only son, and will grieve bitterly for him, as one grieves for his firstborn. In that day there will be a great mourning in Jerusalem, like the mourning of Hadadrimmon in the valley of Megiddon. The land will mourn, every family apart; the family of David’s house apart, and their wives apart; the family of the house of Nathan apart, and their wives apart; the family of the house of Levi apart, and their wives apart; the family of the Shimeites apart, and their wives apart; all the families who remain, every family apart, and their wives apart.
The Fountain Opened and False Prophecy Ended · 13:1–6

“In that day there will be a spring opened to David’s house and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, for sin and for uncleanness. It will come to pass in that day, says YHWH of hosts, that I will cut off the names of the idols out of the land, and they will be remembered no more. I will also cause the prophets and the spirit of impurity to pass out of the land. It will happen that, when anyone still prophesies, then his father and his mother who bore him will tell him, ‘You must die, because you speak lies in YHWH’s name;’ and his father and his mother who bore him will stab him when he prophesies. It will happen in that day, that the prophets will each be ashamed of his vision, when he prophesies; neither will they wear a hairy mantle to deceive: but he will say, ‘I am no prophet, I am a tiller of the ground; for I have been made a bondservant from my youth.’ One will say to him, ‘What are these wounds between your arms?’ Then he will answer, ‘Those with which I was wounded in the house of my friends.’
The Shepherd Struck · 13:7–9
“Awake, sword, against my shepherd,
and against the man who is close to me,” says YHWH of hosts.
“Strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered;
and I will turn my hand against the little ones.
It will happen that in all the land,” says YHWH,
“two parts in it will be cut off and die;
but the third will be left in it.
I will bring the third part into the fire,
and will refine them as silver is refined,
and will test them like gold is tested.
They will call on my name, and I will hear them.
I will say, ‘It is my people;’
and they will say, ‘YHWH is my God.’”
The Day of YHWH · 14:1–15

Look, a day of YHWH comes, when your plunder will be divided within you. For I will gather all nations against Jerusalem to battle; and the city will be taken, the houses rifle, and the women ravish. Half of the city will go out into captivity, and the rest of the people will not be cut off from the city. Then YHWH will go out and fight against those nations, as when he fights in the day of battle. His feet will stand in that day on the Mount of Olives, which is before Jerusalem on the east; and the Mount of Olives will be split in two, from east to west, making a very great valley. Half of the mountain will move toward the north, and half of it toward the south. You will flee by the valley of my mountains; for the valley of the mountains will reach to Azel; yes, you will flee, just like you flee from before the earthquake in the days of Uzziah king of Judah. YHWH my God will come, and all the holy ones with you. It will happen in that day, that there will not be light, cold, or frost. It will be a unique day which is known to YHWH; not day, and not night; but it will come to pass, that at evening time there will be light.
It will happen in that day, that living waters will go out from Jerusalem; half of them toward the eastern sea, and half of them toward the western sea; in summer and in winter will it be.

YHWH will be King over all the earth. In that day YHWH will be one, and his name one. All the land will be made like the Arabah, from Geba to Rimmon south of Jerusalem; and she will be lifted up, and will dwell in her place, from Benjamin’s gate to the place of the first gate, to the corner gate, and from the tower of Hananel to the king’s wine presses. Men will dwell therein, and there will be no more curse; but Jerusalem will dwell safely. This will be the plague with which YHWH will strike all the peoples who have fought against Jerusalem: their flesh will consume away while they stand on their feet, and their eyes will consume away in their sockets, and their tongue will consume away in their mouth. It will happen in that day, that a great panic from YHWH will be among them; and they will lay hold everyone on the hand of his neighbor, and his hand will rise up against the hand of his neighbor. Judah also will fight at Jerusalem; and the wealth of all the surrounding nations will be gathered together: gold, and silver, and clothing, in great abundance.
So will be the plague of the horse, of the mule, of the camel, and of the donkey, and of all the animals that will be in those camps, as that plague.
YHWH King over All the Earth · 14:16–21

It will happen that everyone who is left of all the nations that come against Jerusalem will go up from year to year to worship the King, YHWH of hosts, and to keep the feast of tents. It will be, that whoever of all the families of the earth doesn’t go up to Jerusalem to worship the King, YHWH of hosts, on them there will be no rain. If the family of Egypt doesn’t go up, and doesn’t come, neither will it rain on them. This will be the plague with which YHWH will strike the nations that don’t go up to keep the feast of tents. This will be the punishment of Egypt, and the punishment of all the nations that don’t go up to keep the feast of tents. In that day there will be on the bells of the horses, “HOLY TO YAHWEH”; and the pots in YHWH’s house will be like the bowls before the altar. Yes, every pot in Jerusalem and in Judah will be holy to YHWH of hosts; and all those who sacrifice will come and take of them, and cook in them. In that day there will no longer be a Canaanite in the house of YHWH of hosts.
Title · 1:1
A revelation, YHWH’s word to Israel by Malachi.
Disputation I: I Have Loved You · 1:2–5
“I have loved you,” says YHWH.
Yet you say, “How have you loved us?”

“Wasn’t Esau Jacob’s brother?” says YHWH, “Yet I loved Jacob; but Esau I hated, and made his mountains a desolation, and gave his heritage to the jackals of the wilderness.” Whereas Edom says, “We are beaten down, but we will return and build the waste places”; YHWH of hosts says, “They will build, but I will throw down; and men will call them ‘The Wicked Land,’ even the people against whom YHWH shows wrath forever.”
Your eyes will see, and you will say, “YHWH is great—even beyond the border of Israel!”
Disputation II: You Despise My Name · 1:6–14

When he comes into Jerusalem, the whole city is shaken. “Who is this?” people ask. And the crowds answer, “This is the prophet Jesus, from Nazareth in Galilee.”
A House of Prayer · 21:12–17

Jesus goes into the temple and drives out everyone who is buying and selling there. He knocks over the money changers’ tables and the dove sellers’ benches. “It is written,” he says to them, “‘My house will be called a house of prayer,’ but you are turning it into a hideout for robbers!”

The blind and the lame come to him in the temple, and he heals them. But the chief priests and the scribes see the wonderful things he is doing, and they hear the children shouting in the temple, “Hosanna to the Son of David!” And they are furious.
“Do you hear what they’re shouting?” they demand. “Yes,” Jesus answers. “Have you never read, ‘Out of the mouths of little children and nursing babies you have brought forth praise’?”
Then he walks away from them, out of the city, to Bethany, and stays the night there.
The Fig Tree · 21:18–22
At daybreak, on the way back into the city, Jesus is hungry.

He spots a fig tree by the road and walks over to it, but there is nothing on it, only leaves. “No fruit will ever grow on you again!” he tells it. And all at once the fig tree dries up. The disciples stare in amazement. “How could the fig tree dry up all at once?” they ask.

Jesus answers them, “Truly I tell you, if you have faith and don’t doubt, you will do more than what was done to this fig tree. You could even say to this mountain, ‘Pick yourself up and throw yourself into the sea,’ and it would happen. Anything you ask for in prayer, trusting God, will be yours.”
By What Authority? · 21:23–27
Jesus is back in the temple teaching when the chief priests and the elders of the people come up and confront him. “By what authority are you doing these things?” they ask. “Who gave you that right?”
Jesus answers them, “I have a question for you too. Answer it, and I’ll tell you where my authority comes from.

John’s baptism: where did it come from? From heaven, or from human beings?” They huddle together. “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ he’ll say, ‘So why didn’t you believe him?’ But if we say, ‘From human beings,’ we have the crowd to fear, because they all take John for a prophet.”
So they answer Jesus, “We don’t know.” And he says to them, “Then I’m not telling you where my authority comes from either.
Two Sons · 21:28–32

But tell me what you think. Once there was a man with two sons. He said to the older one, ‘Son, I need you out in the vineyard today.’ ‘No, I won’t,’ the boy said. But afterward he thought better of it and went. The father went to his second son and told him the same. ‘Yes, sir, right away,’ he said. And he never went.

Now which of those two did his father’s will?” “The first one,” they say. Jesus tells them, “Truly I tell you, tax collectors and prostitutes are getting into the kingdom of God before you are. John came and walked the road of righteousness right in front of you, and you wouldn’t believe him. The tax collectors and prostitutes believed him. And even when you saw that, you still wouldn’t change your minds and believe.
The Tenants Who Killed the Son · 21:33–46

Here is another parable. A landowner plants a vineyard. He hedges it all around, digs a pit for the winepress, and puts up a watchtower. Then he leases it to tenant farmers and goes off to another country. When the grapes are nearly ripe, he sends his servants to the tenants to collect his share of the harvest. But the tenants seize his servants. One they beat up, one they kill, one they stone. He sends a second group of servants, bigger than the first, and they get the same treatment. Finally he sends them his own son. ‘Surely they’ll show my son respect,’ he says. But when the tenants catch sight of the son, they put their heads together. ‘Here comes the heir! Let’s kill him, and the inheritance will be ours!’ So they seize him, drag him outside the vineyard, and kill him. So then, when the vineyard’s owner comes back, what is he going to do to those tenants?”
“He’ll destroy those evil men without mercy,” they say, “and he’ll lease the vineyard to other tenants who will hand over his fruit when it’s due.”
Jesus says to them, “Haven’t you ever read this Scripture: ‘The stone the builders threw away has become the cornerstone. This is the Lord’s doing, and it is a wonder in our eyes’?

So I tell you, the kingdom of God will be taken from you and handed to a nation that bears the fruit it should. Anyone who trips over this stone will be shattered, and anyone it lands on will be ground to dust.”
The chief priests and Pharisees listen to his parables, and they can tell he means them. They would like to seize him then and there, but they fear the crowds, who regard him as a prophet.
The Wedding Feast · 22:1–14

Jesus answers them by telling more parables. “The kingdom of heaven is like this. A king is giving a wedding feast for his son. He sends out his servants to call in the guests who have been invited to the wedding, but they refuse to come. So he sends out more servants. ‘Tell the invited guests,’ he says, ‘Look, my dinner is all prepared. My oxen and fattened calves have been slaughtered, and everything is ready. Come to the wedding!’ But the guests shrug it off and go their way, one to his farm, another to his business. And the others lay hands on his servants, beat them up, and kill them. The king is furious. He sends in his troops, and they destroy those murderers and set their city on fire.

Then he says to his servants, ‘Everything is set for the wedding, but the guests I invited weren’t worthy of it. So go out to the crossroads, where the streets run out of town, and invite everyone you find to the wedding.’ Out go the servants into the streets, and they gather everyone they come across, bad and good alike, and soon the wedding hall is packed. But when the king comes in to greet his guests, his eye falls on a man who has no wedding clothes on. ‘Friend,’ he says to him, ‘how is it you came in here dressed like that, with no wedding clothes?’ And the man is speechless. Then the king says to his servants, ‘Bind his hands and feet, and throw him out into the dark. There they will weep and grind their teeth.’ Many are called, you see, but few are chosen.”
Caesar’s Coin · 22:15–22

Then the Pharisees go off and work out a plan to trap Jesus with his own words. They send some of their disciples to him, along with some of Herod’s supporters. “Teacher,” they say, “we know you’re an honest man. You teach God’s way as it truly is, and you aren’t afraid of anybody, because you don’t look at a person’s rank. So tell us what you think. Is it lawful to pay the tax to Caesar, or not?”
But Jesus sees right through their malice. “You hypocrites,” he says, “why are you setting traps for me?
Show me the coin you pay the tax with.” They hand him a denarius.
“Whose face is this?” he asks them. “And whose name is written here?”
“Caesar’s,” they tell him. Then he says to them, “Well then, pay back to Caesar what belongs to Caesar, and pay back to God what belongs to God.”
That leaves them speechless with wonder, and they walk off and leave him be.
Whose Wife in the Resurrection? · 22:23–33

That same day some Sadducees come to him. The Sadducees say there is no resurrection, and they put a question to him. “Teacher,” they say, “Moses laid it down that if a man dies childless, his brother is to take the widow as his wife and give his dead brother children. Well, we had seven brothers here. The oldest got married, then died with no children, so his widow passed to the next brother. Then the second brother died the same way, and the third, and so on through all seven. Last of all, the woman died too. So in the resurrection, which of the seven will she be wife to? All of them had her.”

Jesus answers them, “You’re wandering off the path, and it’s because you understand neither the Scriptures nor the power of God. When the dead rise, they don’t marry, and they aren’t given in marriage. They are like the angels in heaven. And as for the dead being raised, haven’t you read what God himself said to you? ‘I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.’ He isn’t the God of the dead. He is the God of the living.”
The crowds listening are stunned by his teaching.
The Greatest Commandment · 22:34–40
Word reaches the Pharisees that Jesus has shut the Sadducees’ mouths, and they gather in a group. One of them, a lawyer, tries to test him. “Teacher, which commandment in the Law is the greatest?”

Jesus tells him, “‘Love the Lord your God with your whole heart, and with your whole soul, and with your whole mind.’ That is the greatest commandment, and the first. And there’s a second one just like it: ‘Love your neighbor as you love yourself.’ These two commandments hold up the whole Law and all the Prophets.”
David’s Son, David’s Lord · 22:41–46
While the Pharisees are still gathered there, Jesus puts a question to them.
“Tell me,” he says, “whose son is the Messiah?” “David’s,” they tell him.
He says to them, “Then why does David, moved by the Spirit, call him ‘Lord’? This is what he says:
The Lord said to my Lord,
Take your seat at my right hand
while I lay your enemies low
beneath your feet.
If David calls him ‘Lord,’ then how can he be just his son?”
Nobody can come up with a single word in reply. And from then on, not one of them has the nerve to question him anymore.
Moses’ Seat · 23:1–12

Then Jesus speaks to the crowds and to his disciples. “The scribes and the Pharisees have taken their seat in the chair of Moses,” he says. “So do what they tell you and keep it. But don’t copy what they do, because what they say and what they do are two different things. They tie up heavy loads, hard to carry, and pile them on people’s shoulders. But they won’t lift a finger to move them. Everything they do, they do so people will see it. They make their prayer boxes extra wide and the tassels on their cloaks extra long. They love the top places at dinners and the front seats in the synagogues. They love it when people bow to them in the market square and call them ‘Rabbi.’ But don’t you let anyone call you ‘Rabbi.’ There is only one who is your Teacher, and you are all family, brothers and sisters. And don’t give the name ‘father’ to anyone on earth. Your one Father is the Father in heaven. And don’t let anyone call you ‘leader,’ because you have one Leader, the Messiah. The one who is greatest among you will be the one who serves you. Whoever lifts himself up will be brought low, and whoever brings himself low will be lifted up.
Woe to You · 23:13–36

How terrible it will be for you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You lock up the kingdom of heaven and keep people out. You won’t go in yourselves, and when others are on their way in, you won’t let them enter.

How terrible for you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You’ll travel across sea and dry land to make one convert, and once you’ve got him, you turn him into a son of Gehenna twice over, worse than yourselves.

How terrible for you, blind guides! You say, ‘An oath sworn by the temple doesn’t count. But swear by the gold in the temple, and you have to keep it.’ Blind fools! What matters more, the gold, or the temple that makes the gold holy in the first place? And you say, ‘An oath sworn by the altar doesn’t count. But swear by the offering on it, and you have to keep it.’ You blind men! What matters more, the offering, or the altar that makes the offering holy? Swear by the altar, and you are swearing by the altar and everything lying on it. Swear by the temple, and you are swearing by the temple and by the One who lives there. Swear by heaven, and you are swearing by God’s throne and by the One seated on it.

How terrible for you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You give God a tenth of your mint and dill and cumin, the herbs from your garden. But you have walked right past the weightier things of the Law: justice and mercy and faithfulness. Those are what you should have been doing, without leaving the others undone. You blind guides! You strain a gnat out of your cup and gulp down a camel! (In the tongue Jesus speaks, a gnat is a galma and a camel is a gamla.)

How terrible for you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You wash the outside of the cup and the dish, but inside they are full of plunder and excess. You blind Pharisee! Clean out what’s inside the cup first, and the outside will come clean as well.

How terrible for you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You are like tombs painted white. On the outside they look lovely, but inside they are full of dead men’s bones and every kind of filth. That’s you exactly. People look at you and see righteous men, but underneath you are brimming with hypocrisy and lawlessness.

How terrible for you, scribes and Pharisees, you hypocrites! You put up tombs for the prophets and adorn the graves of righteous people. And you say, ‘If we had lived back in our ancestors’ days, we would never have helped them shed the prophets’ blood.’ So by your own words you admit you’re the sons of the men who murdered the prophets. Well then, fill your fathers’ cup to the brim! Snakes! Sons of vipers! How do you think you’ll escape the sentence of Gehenna?

That is why, look, I am sending you prophets and wise men and scribes. Some of them you will kill and crucify. Some of them you will flog in your synagogues and hunt down from town to town. And so it will all come down on you, all the innocent blood ever poured out on the earth, from the blood of Abel, that righteous man, all the way to the blood of Zechariah son of Berekiah, the one you killed between the sanctuary and the altar. Truly I tell you, all of this will come down on this generation.
O Jerusalem · 23:37–39

O Jerusalem, Jerusalem! You kill the prophets, and you stone the messengers sent to you. How many times I have wanted to gather your children close, the way a mother hen tucks her chicks under her wings! And you would not let me. Look, your house is left to you, deserted. I tell you, from now on you won’t lay eyes on me until the day you say, ‘Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord.’”
Not One Stone on Another · 24:1–3

As Jesus is leaving the temple grounds, his disciples come up and want him to look at the temple buildings. But he answers them, “You see all these things, don’t you? Truly I tell you, the day is coming when not one of these stones will be left on top of another. They will all be torn down.”

Later he is sitting on the Mount of Olives, and the disciples come to him when the others aren’t around. “When is all this going to happen?” they ask. “What sign will show that you are coming, and that the age is ending?”
The Beginning of Birth Pains · 24:4–14

Jesus answers them, “Watch out that nobody leads you astray. Many will come using my name and saying, ‘I am the Messiah,’ and they will lead many people astray. You are going to hear the noise of wars nearby and the news of wars far away. Don’t let it shake you. These things have to happen, but that isn’t the end yet. One nation will go to war against another, and one kingdom against another. In place after place there will be famine and earthquake. But all of this is only the first of the birth pains.

Then they will hand you over to be tortured, and they will kill you. All the nations will hate you because of my name. Then many will fall away. They will betray one another and hate one another. Many false prophets will spring up, and they will lead many astray. And because lawlessness will spread, most people’s love will grow cold. But the one who holds on to the end will be saved. And this good news of the kingdom will be announced all over the world, as a witness to all the nations. And then the end will come.
The Desolating Horror · 24:15–28

So when you see the desolating abomination that Daniel the prophet spoke about, standing where it has no right to stand, in the holy place (let whoever reads this understand), then the people in Judea must run for the mountains. Whoever is up on the roof must not go down to get anything out of the house. Whoever is out in the field must not turn back to get his cloak. How hard it will be in those days for women who are pregnant, and for mothers nursing their babies! Pray that you won’t have to run in winter, or on a Sabbath. Because then there will be great suffering, worse than anything since the world began, and nothing like it will ever happen again. Unless those days were cut short, nobody would come through alive. But for the sake of the chosen ones, those days will be cut short.

In those days, if someone says to you, ‘See, the Messiah is here!’ or, ‘He’s over there!’ don’t believe a word of it. Fake messiahs and fake prophets will show up, working great signs and wonders, enough to fool even God’s chosen ones, if that could be done. There. I’ve warned you in advance. So if they tell you, ‘Look, he’s out in the wilderness,’ don’t go out there. If they say, ‘Look, he’s hidden away in the back rooms,’ don’t believe it. The coming of the Son of Man will be like lightning that flashes out of the east and lights up the sky all the way to the west. Wherever there is a dead body, that’s where the vultures will flock.
The Son of Man on the Clouds · 24:29–31

Right after the suffering of those days, the sun will go dark, and the moon will give no light. The stars will fall from the sky, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken. Then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in the sky, and all the tribes of the earth will beat their breasts and mourn. They will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of the sky with power and great glory. And he will send out his angels with a mighty trumpet blast, and they will gather his chosen ones from the four winds, from one edge of the heavens to the other.
Learn from the Fig Tree · 24:32–44

Let the fig tree teach you something. As soon as its branches turn green and tender and it puts out leaves, you know summer is near. In the same way, when you see all these things happening, you can tell that he is close, standing at the very door. Truly I tell you, this generation won’t be gone before all these things take place. Heaven and earth will pass away. My words will not.
But when that day and that hour will come, nobody knows. The angels in heaven don’t know. The Son doesn’t know. Only the Father knows.

The coming of the Son of Man will be just like the days of Noah. Back then, before the flood, people carried on eating and drinking, getting married and marrying off their daughters, right up to the day Noah stepped into the ark. They didn’t see it coming until the flood rolled in and carried them all off. The coming of the Son of Man will be just like that. Two men will be working in a field. One is taken, and one is left. Two women will be grinding grain together. One is taken, and one is left. So keep awake. You can’t know the day your Lord will come. But think about this. If a homeowner knew which hour of the night the burglar would come, he’d stay up and keep watch, and he wouldn’t let anyone dig through his walls. So you have to be ready too. The Son of Man is coming at an hour you don’t expect.
The Servant Left in Charge · 24:45–51

Who, then, is the faithful and sensible servant, the one his master puts in charge of his household, to give the others their food at the right time? Blessed is that servant if his master finds him doing just that when he comes home. Truly I tell you, the master will put him in charge of everything he owns. But what if that servant is wicked, and he thinks to himself, ‘My master is taking his time.’ And he starts beating his fellow servants, and eating and drinking with the drunkards. Then his master will turn up on a day he isn’t looking for him, at an hour he doesn’t know. He will cut him in pieces and put him out with the hypocrites. There they will weep and grind their teeth.”
Ten Young Women with Lamps · 25:1–13

“When that day comes, the kingdom of heaven will be like this. Ten young women, bridesmaids, pick up their lamps and set out to meet the bridegroom. Five of them are foolish, and five are sensible. The foolish ones bring their lamps, but no spare oil. But the sensible ones bring jars of oil along with their lamps. The bridegroom is late, very late, and one by one they all nod off and sleep. In the middle of the night a cry goes up: ‘Look! The bridegroom! Go out and meet him!’ Up they all get, and they set to work trimming their lamps. ‘Let us have some of your oil,’ the foolish ones beg the sensible ones. ‘Our lamps are sputtering out!’ ‘We can’t,’ the sensible ones say. ‘There won’t be enough for all of us. You’d better go to the sellers and buy your own.’ So off they go to buy it. And while they’re gone, the bridegroom comes. The bridesmaids who are ready follow him in to the wedding feast, and the door swings shut. After a while the other bridesmaids come back. ‘Sir!
